text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: ELEGANCE / MAINTAINABILITY / SCOPE
Round: 2
Summary: All 21 Round 1 findings are materially addressed. Round 2 found 0 BLOCKER, 3 IMPORTANT, and 3 MINOR issues. Classification is advisory in this binary plan review; no Phase-10 severity tree was created. The structural RuntimeText design, one SkillDescriptor catalog, target-owned assets, flat default-depth topology, recoverable directory swap, Nix manifest derivation, and personal authority model are now proportionate and implementable.

IMPORTANT 1 — The exact CLI version still has a second stale source outside the declared version writer.
Evidence: Proposal 2 makes capabilities report the CLI version and makes the bundle require an exact compatible Pasture CLI release, while section 9 declares .claude-plugin/plugin.json the sole canonical version writer. Current cmd/pasture/root.go instead declares const version = "v0.1.0". Makefile and .github/workflows/release.yml attempt -X main.version injection, which applies to a string variable, not a compile-time constant. The proposal assigns plugin and bundle version derivation but never assigns repair and proof of the actual pasture binary version consumed by capabilities.
Consequence: A release can publish plugin and bundle version N while the downloaded CLI reports a stale hardcoded version. Fresh setup then rejects a compatible binary or, worse, accepts compatibility through another ad hoc comparison, recreating multiple version owners.
Exact correction: Add the pasture binary version projection to Release integration. Replace the hardcoded constant with one linker-injectable build variable whose production value is derived from the canonical release/tag; define the development value and rejection/override policy. Make capabilities read only that build value. Build the real binary with an injected non-default version and assert pasture --version, capabilities CLI version, bundle compatible release, release tag, and checksum artifact agree. Keep go/source fallback explicitly development-only unless it can provide equivalent immutable version provenance.

IMPORTANT 2 — Whole-directory uninstall and recovery do not yet protect unexpected unowned entries.
Evidence: The revised transaction moves CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed as a unit and later cleans its control-area backup. It explicitly protects modified managed content, but it does not say what happens when a user or another tool adds an unknown file, directory, or symlink under pasture-managed. Normative URD R16/R19 still requires unowned files to survive, and moving then cleaning the entire directory can delete such content.
Consequence: The simpler directory transaction can reintroduce silent user-data loss during upgrade, uninstall, or journal cleanup even though the former flat-file design refused unowned content.
Exact correction: Define pasture-managed as an exact ledger-owned generation and require authoritative recursive membership validation before every move or cleanup. Any extra entry, type change, or unknown symlink is an ownership conflict: status reports its exact path and upgrade/uninstall stop with zero mutation. Recovery must never delete a backup containing entries not proven ledger-owned; it must preserve it and report manual repair. Add unknown-file, unknown-subdirectory, post-PREPARED insertion, and interrupted-uninstall cases to the real subprocess suite.

IMPORTANT 3 — Collision-free slice ownership remains ambiguous at the only static target-registration seam.
Evidence: Foundation owns TargetHarness integration and target-aware protocol/install semantics with a promise that later slices never edit those files. Codex distribution later owns codex_* target files, protocol/install renderers, and plugin emitters. The current static harnessRegistry lives in internal/codegen/harness.go and must reference the Codex target; Foundation cannot produce a buildable registered target before later Codex types exist, while Codex distribution cannot wire the target without editing the Foundation-owned integration. Target-aware canonical semantics versus target-specific asset rendering is also not assigned precisely.
Consequence: Either the Foundation slice is intentionally unbuildable, a later slice crosses ownership, or the implementation invents global init registration to preserve nominal file separation. Any of those weakens slice-level review and creates the exact hidden integration edit the revision says it removed.
Exact correction: Name a buildable ownership handoff. The simplest option is: Foundation owns only target-neutral roots/catalog/RuntimeText and canonical InstallCLISpec/protocol sources; Codex distribution becomes final owner of harness.go plus codex_target and all Codex renderers while adding HarnessCodex and registry wiring in one reviewed integration leaf. Alternatively create an explicit supervisor-owned target-registration leaf after the emitters exist. State that Claude/OpenCode byte-baseline adjustments remain Foundation-owned and distinguish canonical install semantics from Codex asset rendering. Do not use init-time self-registration solely to avoid a shared-file handoff.

MINOR 1 — pkg/codexbundle exposes an unnecessary public Go API.
Evidence: The bundle-contract leaf freezes pkg/codexbundle, but its consumers are internal/codegen, internal/codexagents, and the same-repository CLI. Aura consumes manifest JSON, not the Go package. This repository reserves pkg for externally consumable contracts such as pkg/protocol.
Consequence: An internal serialization detail becomes a public import surface and acquires avoidable compatibility/documentation burden.
Exact correction: Put the Go contract in internal/codexbundle and freeze the external manifest wire schema with golden/schema tests. Promote a public package only when a real external Go consumer exists.

MINOR 2 — The updated research report still contains superseded recommendations.
Evidence: Its adversarial disposition correctly narrows authority to companion XOR Home Manager, but the numbered Recommended Architecture still says to make companion, Home Manager, and future project delivery mutually exclusive owners for a Codex home. That directly contradicts Proposal 2, URD R27, and the report own preceding correction. The report remains a frontmatter reference of Proposal 2.
Consequence: Implementation and future maintenance have two incompatible architecture summaries, undermining the one-source ownership cleanup.
Exact correction: Rewrite the numbered recommendations and validation bullets to match the managed-directory, personal-only authority, capabilities, exact-release bootstrap, structural RuntimeText, and target-owned-asset design; remove every stale flat/project-global claim.

MINOR 3 — Marketplace immutability still names a concept rather than the exact JSON source member.
Evidence: Round 1 requested exact sha versus ref representation. Proposal 2 specifies git-subdir plus an immutable 40-hex revision but does not name the field or provide the literal entry shape.
Consequence: Aura implementation must still choose a user-visible schema detail during a slice, and a value placed in ref instead of the immutable checksum member can weaken the stated pinning contract.
Exact correction: Include the exact schema-valid source object in the proposal and tests, with the 40-hex commit in source.sha, the precise HTTPS URL and plugins/pasture path, and any optional source.ref separately defined as informational or omitted. Assert the marketplace round-trips and the resolved installation commit equals source.sha.

Prior-finding verification: Round 1 delegation depth, CLI bootstrap, active verbatim assets, runtime identity, structural typing, catalog duplication, status truth, transaction threat model, project scope, Home Manager activation, deterministic loader observables, creator-validator provenance, output inventories, prerequisites, marketplace policy, and false parallelism are otherwise resolved by Proposal 2 and Amendment 2.

Required exit: issue Proposal 3 with these six corrections, synchronize the research report, and run a fresh three-axis round. ACCEPT still requires a fix-free round with zero findings.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 3 — normative resolution of Proposal 2 adversarial review

This amendment supersedes conflicting portions of Amendment 2, especially R25's statement that every command recovers, R28's unsupported debug-prompt agent observable, R30's marketplace path spelling, and any implication that CLI version or managed-directory membership may be inferred from mutable state.

R32 — Observer/mutator split and coherent recovery
`capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` are zero-write observers in every state. `plan` and `status` acquire a coherent read snapshot using the same cross-process lock discipline as mutations; they wait for an active mutation, inspect ledger, managed generation, and journal together, and report an interrupted transaction without repairing it. `capabilities` is static and never reads installer state. Add `pasture codex agents recover --format=text|json` as an explicit authorized mutator. `recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` take the exclusive lock; install/uninstall may recover first, but recovery invalidates the prior plan digest and therefore requires a fresh plan before a new requested generation is activated. Every journal state, concurrent reader/writer boundary, retry, and zero-write invariant is black-box tested.

R33 — Deterministic native-agent loader observable
Do not claim that app-server `skills/list`, plugin list/read, config/read, or `codex debug prompt-input` enumerates custom agent types in Codex 0.144.1. The hermetic pinned-Codex test starts a local fake Responses-compatible provider, invokes a fresh Codex process with isolated `CODEX_HOME`, captures the outbound model request's collaboration tool schema, and asserts the exact custom agent type enum before and after companion/Home Manager install and removal. App-server remains the deterministic skill/plugin observable. A separately labeled real network/model UAT proves the runtime can actually select each installed type.

R34 — Frozen release/checksum and activation contract
The supported release matrix is exactly linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64. A release publishes the 12 existing binary artifacts (pasture, pastured, pasture-release for all four tuples) plus `SHA256SUMS`. The checksum file is UTF-8, newline-terminated, lexicographically sorted, and contains exactly one line per expected basename in the grammar `<64 lowercase hex><two ASCII spaces><basename>`; basenames contain no slash. Bootstrap rejects missing, duplicate, extra, malformed, unsupported-platform, tag/version-mismatched, redirect-to-untrusted-origin, or hash-mismatched inputs. It downloads into a private same-filesystem stage, verifies the exact current-platform `pasture` artifact before rename or execution, fsyncs, and activates only the verified binary. Fake-release tests cover every negative case. A post-publish gate fetches the actual immutable tag and checksum roster and runs `pasture codex agents capabilities` for each supported tuple using native or declared emulated runners; Aura cannot change to AVAILABLE until that gate passes.

R35 — Executable clean-machine prerequisite matrix
The setup skill and CLI have isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME/PATH/repository tests for absent, incompatible, and compatible Codex; absent/incompatible Pasture; absent/present bd; absent/present Git; repository policy requiring present or missing `git agent-commit`; optional absent/present Claude-backed aura-swarm; no repository; and the fully provisioned path. Each case asserts the declared requirement, fallback, exact actionable error, and zero mutation of hooks, Git configuration, default home, unrelated task databases, or plugin caches.

R36 — One executable version projection
Change `cmd/pasture/root.go` from a non-injectable version constant to a linker-injectable variable with a development sentinel. The release build injects canonical `vX.Y.Z`; one parser projects both release tag and bare semver. CLI `--version`, `codex agents capabilities`, bundle compatibility, generated plugin/bundle versions, release tag, and checksum gate are tested for parity. `pasture-release` remains the sole canonical version writer and codegen remains a reader. The bundle wire implementation is internal (`internal/codexbundle`); its JSON schema, not a Go package API, is frozen.

R37 — Exact managed-generation membership and preservation
Before install, uninstall, or any destructive recovery move/cleanup, recursively compare the complete managed generation with the committed ledger: expected regular files, hashes, modes where relevant, directories, and no unknown entries or symlinks. Modified, missing, unknown, or type-changed content is TAMPERED and stops before mutation with preservation and repair guidance. Recovery may move/restore a whole previously validated generation; if either the loader-visible generation or transaction backup changed after journaling, preserve all candidates and stop rather than guessing or deleting. Cleanup removes only transaction-owned content whose recorded identity still matches. No flag silently adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown content in this feature.

R38 — Exact marketplace object
Aura's Codex marketplace entry uses exactly `source.source = "git-subdir"`, `source.url = "https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture.git"`, `source.sha = <40 lowercase hex commit>`, and `source.path = "./plugins/pasture"`. It does not use `ref`, `repo`, a mutable branch, or a path without `./`. The entry is appended; policy is installation NOT_AVAILABLE during stacked review, authentication ON_INSTALL, products omitted, category Productivity. Schema and exact-object tests freeze these keys. AVAILABLE remains a later release-backed change after R34 passes.

R39 — Buildable file ownership and integration
Canonical foundation owns roots, catalog, structural runtime semantics, and canonical assets, but not Codex target rendering or final registry integration. Codex distribution owns all Codex renderers/templates/UI overlays/bundle emission and the single final `harness.go` registration edit after its package compiles independently. CLI owns `internal/codexagents`, Cobra command files, and consumes the frozen `internal/codexbundle` schema. Release integration alone owns `cmd/pasture/root.go`, release workflow/checksums, Makefile/release packages, and version parity tests. Aura owns only its marketplace, Home Manager module/fixture, docs/input-lock, and Pasture gitlink. Any discovered shared file is reassigned in Beads before editing.

R40 — Research consistency
The committed Codex research report must describe target-owned support skills, the personal companion XOR Home Manager model with only explicit project checks, zero-write observers plus explicit recovery, the fake-provider agent-schema observable, and Aura-owned marketplace distribution. Drift back to recursive Codex verbatim copying, a global project ownership algebra, or debug-prompt agent enumeration fails documentation review.

REVIEW RESULT
Axis: elegance

Prior-round verification:
- RESOLVED: one linker-injectable CLI version projection and parity checks.

IMPORTANT — Zero-write observers have no defined lock bootstrap on pristine state
What: The proposal requires plan/status to acquire CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock without writing, but does not define how they obtain that lock before the persistent lock file and its parent exist.
Why: Opening the named lock with create semantics writes bytes/metadata and violates BDD 6; opening it without create fails. Reading pristine state without a linearization rule also cannot support the claimed coherent snapshot during a concurrent first install.
Where: Proposal 3 sections 5 and 6, and BDD 6; URD Amendment 3 R32.
When: The first plan/status call against a pristine CODEX_HOME, especially while the first install/recover/uninstall begins concurrently.
Caller impact: The implementation must either violate the explicit zero-write observer contract, fail on the supported first-run path, or return a snapshot whose coherence is unspecified.
Required correction: Add one explicit bootstrap/linearization protocol and deterministic race tests. A zero-write-compatible design is: mutators create the persistent lock before any other control or managed state; observers open-and-lock it only when present; when absent, observers verify all managed/control/journal paths are absent, lstat the lock again, and linearize a pristine result at that final absence; any state without a lock is TAMPERED/UNSUPPORTED. If the lock appears, retry through the locked path. Test pristine plan/status racing the first mutator and assert zero observer writes plus a coherent before-or-after result. Alternatively amend the zero-write requirement at the user gate and specify the sole permitted lock bootstrap write.

Decision: REVISE. This is not a fix-free 0/0/0 round, so Proposal 3 must not progress.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: TEST-QUALITY / FAILURE-MODEL, round 3

Result: 1 BLOCKER, 2 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR. Proposal 3 materially resolves the Round 2 checksum, release-gate, prerequisite-matrix, version, marketplace, build-ownership, and research-drift findings, but this is not a fix-free round.

BLOCKER B1 — A fresh Codex home cannot satisfy both the named lock protocol and the zero-write observer contract.
Evidence: Proposal section 5 says plan and status acquire the installer lock without writing. Section 6 fixes that lock at CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock. BDD 6 requires capabilities, plan, and status to write zero bytes, and the clean-machine matrix includes isolated fresh HOME/CODEX_HOME fixtures. On that first-run state neither CODEX_HOME/pasture nor agent-install.lock exists. A reader can open and advisory-lock an existing inode read-only, but opening the named missing file read-only fails with ENOENT; creating the parent or lock file violates the zero-write contract. The subprocess list covers a persistent unheld lock file, which assumes the inode already exists, but does not cover the absent-lock first-install race. Neither R32 nor Proposal 3 names a deterministic no-write coordination algorithm for that state.
Consequence: The primary setup flow calls plan before the first install, so an implementation must fail on a clean machine, mutate during observation, or read without synchronization while a first install creates the journal/ledger/generation. The current BDD cannot be implemented and a concurrent reader can report a synthetic mixed state.
Exact correction: Amend R32 and the proposal with an explicit zero-write pre-lock protocol. One workable contract is: when the lock exists, lstat every component without following symlinks, open the lock read-only, take a shared lock, and inspect the state. When it is absent, use a bounded double-collect of the exact control-tree/ledger/generation/journal identities and bytes, recheck lock absence and all collected identities before returning, and restart under the shared lock if the lock appears; changed observations retry and exhaustion returns a stable BUSY exit without writes. Mutators create/fsync the persistent lock before any other installer-state mutation and never remove it. An equally precise monotonic snapshot/epoch design is acceptable, but “acquire the lock without writing” is not an algorithm.
Required tests: Start with absent CODEX_HOME, absent control directory, and an existing control directory with no lock. Inject first-install creation at every observer boundary, plus interrupted-state and retry-exhaustion cases. Hash the complete tree before/after and allow only coherent old, interrupted, new, or BUSY reports. Keep the existing persistent-lock contention cases.

IMPORTANT I1 — The fake-provider assertion targets an enum that Codex 0.144.1 does not emit.
Evidence: Proposal section 10, BDD 12, and URD R33 require the fake Responses provider to assert an exact pasture_* agent-type enum. In pinned Codex rust-v0.144.1, codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_spec.rs constructs parameters.properties.agent_type with JsonSchema::string(Some(agent_type_description)) in both spawn_agent_common_properties_v1 and v2. codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs builds that description from turn_context.config.agent_roles. The role names are deterministic prose in agent_type.description, not a JSON enum. The local fake provider is a valid hermetic capture seam; the asserted shape is not.
Consequence: A correct pinned Codex request necessarily fails the proposed test, or the test must invent an enum and can falsely claim loader coverage.
Exact correction: Amend R33, Proposal section 10/BDD 12, and the research report to assert the actual pinned observable: spawn_agent exists; agent_type has type string; and its deterministic description advertises the exact expected built-ins plus the five pasture_* names in the pinned canonical order before/after companion and Home Manager install/removal. Golden the complete relevant tool fragment or parse the pinned description format explicitly. Add missing, duplicated, malformed, renamed, and built-in-shadowing fixtures. Keep actual selection as separately labeled network/model UAT.

IMPORTANT I2 — Recovery preconditions and tampered-journal tests are still not state-specific.
Evidence: Proposal section 6 names PREPARED, OLD_MOVED, NEW_ACTIVE, and COMMITTED and says recovery acts on an unambiguous state, but it does not freeze the journal schema, define the loader/stage/backup/ledger preconditions for each state and first-install versus upgrade/uninstall variants, or define how journal-referenced paths are derived and contained. Its subprocess list tests every valid journal state and tampered backups, not a tampered journal, despite this review record explicitly requiring tampered-journal tests. R37 protects managed generations and backups but does not close malformed/truncated/forged journal input.
Consequence: SIGKILL happy-state recovery can pass while a truncated or forged journal drives a move, restore, or cleanup against the wrong transaction or path. “Unambiguous” remains implementor judgment at the most destructive seam.
Exact correction: Freeze a versioned deny-unknown-fields journal wire contract and a state table. For each durable state and install/uninstall variant, specify the required existence, exact recorded identity/hash/membership, and permitted recovery transition for loader-visible generation, staged new generation, old backup, and ledger. Recompute transaction paths from a validated safe transaction ID; never trust arbitrary absolute or relative paths from journal data. Any malformed/truncated/unknown-version or state, invalid transition, mismatched transaction ID, path escape, symlink/type change, multiple active journals, or identity mismatch must return TAMPERED/AMBIGUOUS with zero mutation and preserve every candidate.
Required tests: After SIGKILL at every durable boundary, alter the journal independently of its content: truncation/bit flip, missing and extra fields, unknown version/state, traversal and absolute paths, swapped transaction IDs, duplicate/multiple journals, symlink/type replacement, and loader/stage/backup/ledger identity mismatches. Assert an external sentinel is untouched, all candidates remain, and diagnostics contain all six actionable-error fields. Then retain one clean explicit-recover case for every valid state/precondition row.

Round 2 I2 correctly moved to a fake Responses provider, but “enum” is not the pinned wire shape. Round 2 I3 and I4 are now executable: the exact 12-line SHA256SUMS grammar/roster, fake-release negatives, immutable actual-tag four-tuple capability gate, and isolated prerequisite matrix are explicit. Round 2 M1 research drift is materially corrected. Exact managed-generation membership and backup preservation are strong, but the journal itself still lacks the required corruption matrix.

VOTE: REVISE

Axis: adversarial correctness, security, and distribution.
Standard applied: fix-free means zero BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, and MINOR findings. This round is not clean.

Prior-finding verification:
- RESOLVED: Round 2 recovery/observer contradiction. Amendment 3 R32 and Proposal 3 Section 5 now make capabilities, plan, and status zero-write observers, add explicit recover, use coherent snapshots, and invalidate consent after recovery.
- RESOLVED: Round 2 marketplace defect. R38 and Section 9 freeze source.source, the exact HTTPS URL, source.sha, ./plugins/pasture, ordering, policy, category, and release availability.
- VERIFIED: the earlier root-depth, target-owned asset, structural compiler/catalog, exact bootstrap/prerequisite, personal ownership, Home Manager, artifact determinism, and build ownership corrections remain present.
- VERIFIED: pinned Codex 0.144.1 follows a directory symlink during recursive agent discovery because its executor read_directory classifies entries with metadata rather than symlink_metadata. The proposed one-link Home Manager generation is therefore a valid loader shape. No finding is raised on that surface.
- NOT RESOLVED TO A CLEAN ROUND: the deeper bootstrap-lock, interrupted-state identity, and pinned request-schema defects below remain.

BLOCKER B1 — A fresh zero-write observer cannot acquire the proposed persistent lock.

Evidence: Proposal 3 Section 5 says plan and status acquire the installer lock while writing zero bytes in every state. Section 6 places that persistent lock at CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock. On a fresh CODEX_HOME, both the control directory and lock file are absent. An advisory lock requires an open file descriptor: securely creating the parent and lock with O_CREAT is a filesystem mutation, while opening the absent file read-only fails with ENOENT. Taking an unlocked single snapshot is not equivalent because the first installer can create the lock and mutate state concurrently. Amendment 3 R32 and BDD 6 repeat the zero-write-plus-lock promise but specify no absent-lock bootstrap protocol.

Consequence: the primary fresh-user setup path cannot execute plan/status while satisfying its normative contract. An implementation must either mutate before consent, fail on pristine state, or race the first install, defeating zero-write evidence and coherent plan/status semantics.

Exact correction: define two observer paths and make the persistent lock identity non-replaceable after first creation. If a verified regular lock exists, observers open it read-only with no-follow semantics and acquire the shared/exclusive observer lock. If it is absent, observers perform a bounded optimistic double snapshot over lock identity, control directory, ledger, transaction tree, managed generation, and Home Manager ownership. Stable all-absent state is pristine; stable unowned content is reported as conflict; any appearance or identity change retries through the now-existing lock or returns a stable busy/interrupted result. Only an explicitly authorized mutator may securely create the control directory and persistent lock. Specify crash states before and after lock creation and never unlink/replace the lock. Add compiled-binary tests for absent CODEX_HOME, absent control directory, crash during lock bootstrap, first-mutator races at each snapshot boundary, symlink/type swaps, and proof that observer bytes and mtimes remain unchanged.

BLOCKER B2 — The tamper precondition makes legitimate OLD_MOVED and NEW_ACTIVE journals unrecoverable.

Evidence: Proposal 3 Section 6 says every mutation recursively compares the loader-visible managed generation against the committed ledger and classifies missing or modified content as TAMPERED. Amendment 3 R37 explicitly applies that committed-ledger comparison before any destructive recovery move or cleanup. In a valid OLD_MOVED crash state, the loader-visible generation is intentionally absent and the prior generation is in the transaction backup while the committed ledger still describes the prior generation. In a valid NEW_ACTIVE crash state, the loader-visible generation is intentionally the new staged generation while the committed ledger still describes the prior generation. Both valid states necessarily fail the stated comparison before recover can restore or complete them, contradicting Section 6, R32, R37, and BDD 8.

Consequence: SIGKILL at two mandatory durable boundaries can only yield TAMPERED preservation, never the promised unambiguous recovery. The core lifecycle would strand users after ordinary crashes even when every candidate is byte-exact.

Exact correction: replace the global ledger comparison with a normative state-aware identity table whose hashes, types, modes, and directory membership are durably journaled before each move. With no journal, active must match the committed ledger. PREPARED requires active-old to match the ledger and staged-new to match the journal. OLD_MOVED requires active absent, backup-old to match the ledger, and staged-new to match the journal. NEW_ACTIVE requires backup-old to match the prior ledger and active-new to match the journal. COMMITTED requires active-new to match the new ledger/journal before transaction-owned cleanup. Any candidate mismatch preserves all candidates and stops. Test both legitimate and independently tampered active, staged, backup, ledger, and journal variants at every durable state.

IMPORTANT I1 — The deterministic Codex test asserts an agent-type enum that pinned Codex does not emit.

Evidence: Amendment 3 R33, Proposal 3 Section 10, and BDD 12 require the fake Responses provider to observe an exact pasture_* type enum in the collaboration tool schema. In pinned Codex 0.144.1, core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_spec.rs constructs agent_type as JsonSchema::string(Some(agent_type_description)); it has no enum. core/src/agent/role.rs spawn_tool_spec::build formats custom and built-in role names into prose under Available roles in that description. See:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.144.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_spec.rs
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.144.1/codex-rs/core/src/agent/role.rs

Consequence: the mandatory hermetic test cannot pass as specified, or it can pass only by asserting a nonexistent field and therefore prove nothing about loaded native agents. This weakens the exact delivery evidence added specifically to replace the unsupported debug observable.

Exact correction: amend R33, Section 10, BDD 12, and the research report to assert the exact custom-role entries and descriptions inside the agent_type string schema description, including exact absence after companion/Home Manager removal and preservation of built-ins. If deterministic runtime resolution beyond discovery is required, script the fake provider to return an explicit spawn_agent call for each pasture_* role and assert the child request receives the expected generated developer instructions; retain network/model UAT only for behavioral selection. Freeze the pinned source/version and fail if the schema representation changes.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 4 — normative resolution of Proposal 3 adversarial review

This amendment supersedes conflicting portions of Amendments 2 and 3 concerning fresh-home observer locking, the native-agent schema observable, and recovery's use of the committed ledger as a universal identity source.

R41 — Zero-write lock bootstrap and observer linearization
The persistent lock is an empty regular mode-0600 file created only by an authorized mutator; an observer never creates the control directory or lock. A mutator may create `CODEX_HOME/pasture` and atomically create the lock with O_EXCL as its first owned file, then opens with no-follow/identity checks and takes the exclusive advisory lock before any ledger, journal, transaction, or managed-generation mutation. A race loser uses the same inode and lock. A crash after control-directory creation but before lock creation is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED; explicit recover may finish bootstrap only when the control directory is securely owned and empty and every other Pasture installer path is absent.

When a valid lock exists, plan/status open it read-only with no-follow, verify lstat/fstat identity, regular type, owner, link count, and restrictive mode, acquire a shared lock, and read one snapshot. Flock/open must leave bytes and mtimes unchanged. When the lock is absent, an observer takes two complete snapshots of lock identity, exact control-directory entries, ledger, transaction roots, and managed generation. If both snapshots are identical and every Pasture-owned path is absent, the result is pristine and linearizes before any later mutator. If a valid lock appears or any identity changes, retry through the locked path. Stable non-pristine state without a lock is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED or TAMPERED, never pristine. Bounded retry exhaustion is CONCURRENT_CHANGE with repair guidance. Tests cover fresh plan/status byte-and-mtime equality, two first mutators, observer at every mkdir/O_EXCL/flock boundary, creator crash, malformed/symlink/hardlinked lock, stable unowned state, retry exhaustion, and a mutator starting immediately after the second pristine snapshot.

R42 — Journal-recorded identities and state-specific recovery
The journal is the authority during an interrupted transaction. Before any rename it durably records operation, schema, transaction ID, contained candidate paths, prior identity (or ABSENT), desired identity (or ABSENT), prior-ledger digest (or ABSENT), desired-ledger digest (or ABSENT), and the complete staged-tree digest. Prior and desired identities include exact recursive membership, types, hashes, and relevant modes.

Recovery validates a state table, not a universal active-versus-committed-ledger rule. `P` is the recorded prior generation/ledger or ABSENT and `N` is the desired generation/ledger or ABSENT:

- healthy/no journal: active and ledger both match the same committed identity;
- PREPARED: active=P, backup absent, stage=N, ledger=P; it also recognizes the exact identity-equivalent immediate result of the old-directory rename if the crash preceded the OLD_MOVED journal write;
- OLD_MOVED: active absent, backup=P, stage=N, ledger=P; it also recognizes the exact immediate result of activating N if the crash preceded the NEW_ACTIVE journal write;
- NEW_ACTIVE: active=N, backup=P, stage absent, ledger=P; it also recognizes ledger=N if the crash preceded the COMMITTED journal write;
- COMMITTED: active=N, backup=P until cleanup, stage absent, ledger=N.

ABSENT handles first install and uninstall without invented files. PREPARED and OLD_MOVED recover by rolling back to P; an observed activation result, NEW_ACTIVE, and COMMITTED roll forward to N and then clean only recorded candidates. Directory and ledger renames are followed by directory fsync before the next journal checkpoint. Any state outside the exact checkpoint or its single identity-equivalent successor, any malformed/unknown journal field, path escape, duplicate candidate, impossible operation/state combination, hash mismatch, changed backup, unexpected ledger temp, or unknown transaction entry preserves all candidates and returns TAMPERED/INTERRUPTED with manual repair guidance. Tests cover baseline and successor crash shapes plus every tampered/corrupt/forged variant for first install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall.

R43 — Actual Codex custom-role observable
In pinned Codex 0.144.1, `spawn_agent`/collaboration `agent_type` is a plain JSON-schema string. Loaded custom roles are rendered as deterministic `Available roles:` prose in that property's description; there is no enum. The fake Responses-provider test parses the captured `spawn_agent` tool fragment and asserts the exact five names, descriptions, ordering, built-in preservation, and exact absence after removal. It then returns a deterministic tool call using each `pasture_*` string and verifies installed roles spawn while removed/unknown roles return the expected validation error; stubbed parent/child responses keep the test offline. App-server still observes skills/plugins, and real network/model UAT remains separate.

R44 — Research and proposal consistency
All research, plan, and acceptance prose must use the absent-lock double-snapshot algorithm, the journal identity table (including immediate successor crash shapes), and `agent_type.description` rather than an enum. A clean review must challenge these literal observables and recovery preconditions.

## Findings

### BLOCKER Issues

### IMPORTANT Issues
1. The generic P/N recovery table is not a function when uninstall sets N=ABSENT.

What: For uninstall, the `OLD_MOVED` row (`active=absent, backup=P, stage=absent, ledger=P`) and the `OLD_MOVED successor` row (`active=N=ABSENT, backup=P, stage=absent, ledger=P`) have the same journal value and identical observable identities, yet the table says the first restores P and the second rolls forward N.

Amendment 4 R41 and Proposal 4 Section 5 now define a mutator-only O_EXCL lock bootstrap, stable all-absent double snapshots for pristine zero-write observers, retry through the read-only locked path, explicit bootstrap-interrupted recovery, and bounded concurrent-change handling. The first-mutator, creator-crash, observer-linearization, inode, type, owner, link-count, mode, and mtime contracts are coherent under the stated threat model.
- RESOLVED: Round 3 B2 at the architectural level. R42 and Section 6 now make the journal, rather than the committed ledger alone, authoritative during interrupted transactions and validate prior, desired, active, stage, backup, and final-ledger identities per checkpoint.

The updated research matches R44.
- NOT RESOLVED TO A CLEAN ROUND: the generic P/N table is not state-specific enough for ABSENT operations, and its ledger commit omits a required transaction candidate.

BLOCKER B1 — ABSENT makes the claimed single exact successor ambiguous, with conflicting uninstall recovery actions.

Evidence: Section 6 and R42 say P or N may be ABSENT, every checkpoint has a single identity-equivalent successor, and recovery accepts only the named checkpoint or that successor. For uninstall, let P be the installed generation and N=ABSENT. The OLD_MOVED checkpoint is active absent, backup P, stage absent, ledger P and prescribes rollback by restoring P. Its claimed activation successor is active N=absent, backup P, stage absent, ledger P and prescribes roll-forward to N. These are exactly the same filesystem and ledger identity. NEW_ACTIVE has that same physical shape as well, distinguished only by the journal checkpoint. There is no activation rename when N is ABSENT, so an OLD_MOVED successor cannot be inferred from identity. For first install, P=ABSENT likewise makes PREPARED and its old-directory-rename successor identical even though no old directory can be renamed. This directly contradicts BDD 8, which requires exactly one checkpoint/successor identity.

Consequence: after a normal uninstall crash with an OLD_MOVED journal, the stated validator cannot decide whether to restore the owned installation or finish deleting it. Choosing either generic row violates the other; a test matrix cannot implement the promised exact classification without inventing an unstated tie-breaker.

Exact correction: replace the universal rows with operation-specific transition tables and mark impossible successors not applicable. For first install, omit the prior-directory move and define the direct PREPARED-to-active successor. For uninstall, OLD_MOVED always rolls back while that checkpoint is current; make the transition to roll-forward a separately durable journal commit-intent or NEW_ACTIVE checkpoint, with no identity-based OLD_MOVED successor when N=ABSENT. Keep upgrade and downgrade rows for present P and N. State how atomic journal replacement selects the old or new checkpoint after a crash, and test every operation-specific baseline, applicable successor, and impossible shape.

BLOCKER B2 — The exact recovery table has no identity or state for the next-ledger candidate required by atomic ledger replacement.

Evidence: R42 and Section 6 require an atomically written and fsynced ledger and recovery across the immediate ledger-commit successor. On supported Linux and macOS, installing a present desired ledger without mutating the committed ledger in place requires a same-directory or same-filesystem candidate: write and fsync the complete next ledger, rename it over the final ledger, then fsync the parent. Before rename that candidate exists; after rename it is absent. The journal mentions contained candidate paths and treats an unexpected ledger temp as an interruption, but the exact table has columns only for active generation, backup generation, generation stage, and final ledger. It says stage is absent throughout NEW_ACTIVE, where the next-ledger candidate must exist before commit. If the candidate is inside the generation stage, that row is false; if it is created after NEW_ACTIVE, a crash after candidate creation, write, or fsync yields a known transaction state that no row validates. Uninstall has the inverse issue: N=ABSENT requires an explicitly modeled, fsynced final-ledger removal rather than a present candidate.

Consequence: an ordinary crash around ledger commit can fall outside every accepted checkpoint/successor despite exact, untampered transaction content. Recovery must then either strand the user with manual repair, discard an unvalidated temp, or improvise a state transition, defeating the claimed recoverable transaction and exhaustive crash matrix.

Exact correction: freeze the next-ledger path and full identity or ABSENT in the journal, and add a next-ledger candidate column plus operation-specific rows. For install, upgrade, and downgrade, stage and fsync the desired ledger before the checkpoint that relies on it; while final ledger=P the exact candidate=N must exist, and after its rename final ledger=N while the candidate is absent. If staging can crash before that record is durable, add an explicit STAGING/publication protocol rather than treating an installer-created file as unknown. For uninstall, specify the no-candidate ledger-removal transition and its directory-fsynced successor. Corrupt, partial, missing, duplicate, and extra candidate cases must preserve all content, while exact candidates recover deterministically.

Round summary: 2 BLOCKER, 0 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR. VOTE: REVISE. Proposal 5 and a matching URD amendment must resolve both findings and receive a fresh independent three-axis review. This review record itself may now close.

Axis: TEST-QUALITY / FAILURE-MODEL, round 4

Result: 2 BLOCKER, 1 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR. The fresh observer and pinned Codex role-observable corrections are materially executable, but the transaction state table still cannot classify every promised crash state deterministically.

BLOCKER B1 — Substituting ABSENT makes the recovery table non-injective for uninstall.
Evidence: R42 and Proposal section 6 define OLD_MOVED as active=absent, backup=P, stage=N, ledger=P and require rollback to P. They define its immediate activation successor as active=N, backup=P, stage=absent, ledger=P and require roll-forward to N. For uninstall, N=ABSENT, so both rows reduce to the exact same observable tuple under the same OLD_MOVED journal: active absent, backup P, stage absent, ledger P. There is no activation rename because absence is already true after moving P to backup. The same physical state therefore requires opposite recovery actions. For first install, P=ABSENT also collapses PREPARED and its old-move successor, but both reduce to rollback/remove-stage, so that degeneracy is harmless; the uninstall one is not.
Consequence: Explicit recovery after an uninstall crash must guess whether to restore the installed agents or finish uninstalling them. Neither the baseline/successor test matrix nor a production implementation can meet the deterministic-preservation contract.
Exact correction: Specialize the state table by operation and make successor rows conditional on a real non-degenerate rename. One valid policy is: for uninstall, OLD_MOVED always rolls back; after that checkpoint, durably write a distinct NEW_ACTIVE/ABSENCE_ACTIVE journal state before absence becomes the roll-forward point, then remove the ledger. Alternatively define OLD_MOVED as uniformly roll-forward for uninstall and remove the contradictory successor. Generate the expanded first-install, upgrade/downgrade, and uninstall table after substituting P/N, and mechanically assert that no identical tuple of operation, journal, active, backup, generation-stage, ledger, and other recorded candidates maps to different recovery actions.

BLOCKER B2 — Legitimate ledger-commit and cleanup crash candidates are absent from the table.
Evidence: The table jumps from ledger=P to ledger=N and calls an unexpected ledger temp corrupt. A portable atomic ledger replacement on Linux/macOS requires creating, writing, and fsyncing a named same-filesystem desired-ledger candidate before its rename. SIGKILL after that fsync but before rename leaves a legitimate temp that has no table column or accepted row, so the current contract either misclassifies a normal crash as tampering or silently omits a promised durable boundary. Uninstall similarly needs an explicit ledger-unlink plus parent-fsync contract for N=ABSENT. Cleanup is also incomplete: after COMMITTED, removing backup P before removing the journal yields a valid backup-absent COMMITTED successor not listed; removing the in-directory journal before removing the transaction directory can leave an empty transaction directory with no authority, which the healthy/no-journal and unknown-member rules classify inconsistently.
Consequence: “SIGKILL after every durable boundary” cannot be implemented as a closed black-box matrix. Recovery or recovery-after-recovery can preserve false tamper states, leak permanent transaction residue, or delete a candidate whose ownership is no longer provable.
Exact correction: Freeze the ledger candidate as a journal-recorded safe path and identity, create/fsync it before PREPARED, and add a LedgerStage column to every applicable row. Rollback removes only that exact candidate; roll-forward renames it, fsyncs the ledger parent, and recognizes the exact post-rename successor. Give uninstall explicit pre-unlink/post-unlink/post-parent-fsync rows or a single documented durable linearization. Add cleanup checkpoint/successor states or an atomic tombstone layout that keeps authority until backup, journal, and transaction-directory cleanup is complete. Include crashes during explicit recovery itself.
Required tests: Barrier/SIGKILL before and after ledger-candidate create, file fsync, rename or uninstall unlink, parent fsync, COMMITTED write, backup deletion, journal deletion, transaction-directory removal, and every recovery retry. Assert each resulting tree matches exactly one row/action; unknown temps still preserve all candidates.

IMPORTANT I1 — The two-first-mutator bootstrap race has outcomes but no deterministic loser algorithm.
Evidence: R41 says the lock creator uses mkdir then O_EXCL, a race loser coordinates on the same inode, and a creator crash after mkdir but before O_EXCL requires explicit recover. If mutator B observes the secure empty directory after A mkdir but before A O_EXCL, B cannot distinguish a live delayed creator from the prescribed crash state. The proposal lists barriers at mkdir/O_EXCL/flock and “two first mutators” but does not say whether B may compete for O_EXCL, waits for A, times out, or returns BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED. Allowing B to create the inode contradicts explicit-recover-only stale bootstrap; forbidding it without a bounded wait does not guarantee coordination.
Consequence: Equivalent schedules can produce different public results or hang, so the promised concurrency test has no exact oracle.
Exact correction: Choose one algorithm. For example, only the process whose mkdir succeeded may O_EXCL; an EEXIST loser snapshots the empty directory identity and waits a bounded interval for the lock, then validates/opens/flocks it if it appears, retries on identity change, or returns BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED after a stable timeout. Explicit recover alone may create the lock in a pre-existing stable empty directory. Alternatively let all authorized mutators compete for O_EXCL and remove the explicit-recover-only distinction. Test both orderings, creator kill at each boundary, a deliberately paused creator, timeout, and prove exactly one state mutation while the loser has one specified result.

Resolved/retained contracts: The absent-lock double snapshot has a valid linearization point, covers mutation immediately after the second pristine snapshot, and explicitly tests zero bytes and mtimes. Existing-lock reads validate type/owner/link/mode and use read-only shared locking. The fake provider now targets the real pinned Codex shape: user roles are deterministic BTreeMap-ordered Available roles prose in agent_type.description; stubbed parent/child responses can exercise successful installed spawns and exact unknown/removed validation failures offline. The strict 12-line SHA256SUMS grammar and fake-release negatives, immutable actual-tag four-tuple capabilities gate, isolated prerequisite matrix, exact generation inventories, Home Manager enable/repeat/upgrade/conflict/disable plus pinned loader checks, version projection, marketplace object, and research wording remain executable as stated.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 5 — normative resolution of Proposal 4 adversarial review

This amendment supersedes Amendment 4's generic P/N successor table. Recovery is operation-specific and write-ahead: no two physically identical states may prescribe different actions, and every filesystem candidate created by ledger commit or cleanup is part of the journal contract.

R45 — Operation-specific write-ahead recovery automata
The journal uses durable intent checkpoints so a crash immediately before or after one filesystem operation has the same recovery direction. For install/upgrade (including explicit downgrade), P is optional and N is present:

1. CREATED/STAGING: active+ledger=P; only declared transaction candidates may be partial; rollback.
2. PREPARED: active+ledger=P, generation-stage=N, next-ledger=N, backup absent; rollback.
3. MOVE_OLD_INTENT (only when P exists): accepts either active=P/backup absent or active absent/backup=P; generation-stage and next-ledger remain N; rollback in both shapes.
4. OLD_MOVED (only when P exists): active absent, backup=P, stages=N, ledger=P; rollback.
5. ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT: accepts either active absent/generation-stage=N or active=N/generation-stage absent; backup=P or absent for first install, ledger=P, next-ledger=N; roll forward in both shapes.
6. NEW_ACTIVE: active=N, generation-stage absent, backup=P if any, ledger=P, next-ledger=N; roll forward.
7. COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT: accepts either ledger=P/next-ledger=N or ledger=N/next-ledger absent while active=N; roll forward in both shapes.
8. COMMITTED/CLEANUP: active+ledger=N; clean only exact recorded prior/candidate content.

First install has P=ABSENT and skips MOVE_OLD_INTENT/OLD_MOVED entirely. For uninstall, P is present and N is absent:

1. CREATED/PREPARED: active+ledger=P; rollback.
2. MOVE_OLD_INTENT: accepts active=P/backup absent or active absent/backup=P; rollback in both shapes.
3. OLD_MOVED: active absent, backup=P, ledger=P; rollback.
4. COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT: accepts ledger=P/retired-ledger absent or ledger absent/retired-ledger=P while active remains absent; roll forward in both shapes.
5. COMMITTED/CLEANUP: active+ledger absent; clean only exact backup/retired-ledger candidates.

Uninstall has no ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT or NEW_ACTIVE state. The durable intent checkpoint, not inference from an ABSENT desired generation, chooses rollback versus roll-forward. No-op install and no-op uninstall create no transaction.

R46 — Complete ledger, journal, and cleanup candidates
For install/upgrade, canonical `next-ledger.json` is generated, hashed, fsynced, and journaled inside the transaction before PREPARED; COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT atomically renames it over the control ledger and fsyncs the control directory. For uninstall, COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT atomically renames the validated control ledger to journaled `retired-ledger.json` rather than unlinking it. The state tables explicitly require each candidate's presence or absence.

The journal is an append-only framed log, not atomically replaced through an unmodeled temp. Each record has magic/schema, bounded length, canonical payload, monotonic sequence, previous-record hash, and SHA-256; every append and directory-changing operation is fsynced. Recovery uses the last complete hash-chained record. A partial tail is truncatable only when it is a prefix of the one canonical next record allowed by the observed physical state; otherwise all candidates are preserved as TAMPERED. A transaction directory with no complete first record is STAGING_INCOMPLETE and may be removed only when empty; partial or unknown content is preserved.

After COMMITTED, cleanup follows one fixed recorded order. The log records CLEANUP_INTENT and cleanup-prefix checkpoints; at each checkpoint recovery accepts only the recorded remaining suffix or the exact one-deletion successor and continues in the same direction. The journal remains until every other candidate is gone. A crash after journal unlink but before rmdir leaves only an empty, securely owned, well-formed transaction-ID directory; that exact terminal remnant may be removed, while any nonempty or malformed remnant is preserved. The transaction parent is fsynced after final rmdir. Tests inject crash/short-write at candidate creation, file fsync, every intent append, every rename, directory fsync, ledger replacement/retirement, each cleanup deletion/checkpoint, journal unlink, rmdir, and parent fsync for first install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall.

R47 — Deterministic first-mutator competition
After validating that no unknown control entry exists, every authorized mutator attempts the same secure mkdir plus lock O_EXCL bootstrap; there is no loser that merely waits on an absent inode. Exactly one creates the empty mode-0600 lock. EEXIST causes no-follow open/identity verification and blocking acquisition of that inode; transient ENOENT/identity replacement retries to the command deadline, then returns CONCURRENT_CHANGE. A creator crash after mkdir leaves an exact empty bootstrap namespace that explicit recover—or an install carrying a still-valid prior pristine plan digest—may finish without deleting content. The lock inode is coordination metadata and is excluded from the semantic plan digest; absent pristine state and a valid unheld lock with no installer state normalize to the same PRISTINE generation. Under the acquired lock, the first winner revalidates the digest and proceeds; later contenders observe the committed state and reject stale consent. Tests deterministically schedule two and three first mutators at mkdir, O_EXCL, open, flock, validation, and commit boundaries.

R48 — Documentation consistency
Research, proposal, and tests must show the two separate operation automata, all ledger candidates, append-only journal framing, cleanup-prefix states, and deterministic O_EXCL competition. The generic ABSENT successor table is forbidden because it is not a recovery function.

URD AMENDMENT 6 — normative resolution of Proposal 5 adversarial review

This amendment supersedes Amendment 5 wherever PREPARED or later states were assigned rollback. The transaction is monotone after a single durable semantic commit point, and both pre-commit abort and post-commit disposal use the same crash-resumable cleanup engine.

R49 — PREPARED is the roll-forward commit point
CREATED/STAGING performs no mutation outside the transaction directory. Once all bundle, prior-state, staged-generation, next-ledger, consent-digest, and path validations pass and every candidate is fsynced, appending/fsyncing PREPARED durably commits the already authorized requested semantic result. Every PREPARED-or-later install/upgrade/downgrade state rolls forward to N. Every PREPARED-or-later uninstall state rolls forward to ABSENT. MOVE_OLD_INTENT accepts pre/post rename and moves or keeps moving forward; OLD_MOVED proceeds to activation or ledger retirement. No recovery path renames backup P back into the loader tree and no post-PREPARED path deletes N candidates as a rollback.

If a PREPARED-or-later identity is missing, corrupt, modified, or ambiguous, recovery preserves all candidates and stops TAMPERED/INTERRUPTED; it never guesses or silently rolls back. The status/plan output states both the committed recovery direction and required repair.

R50 — One resumable cleanup engine for abort and commit
Only CREATED/STAGING may abort. Before deleting any pre-PREPARED transaction-local candidate, recover appends/fsyncs `CLEANUP_INTENT{kind:ABORT, terminal:P, ordered_candidates:[...]}`. The common cleanup engine then records `CLEANING{next_index}` checkpoints around a fixed candidate order. At each index it accepts the exact recorded remaining suffix or its exact one-deletion successor and continues in the same direction. `CLEANUP_COMPLETE` requires active+ledger still equal P and no candidate except the journal. It then uses the existing journal-unlink/empty-transaction-directory terminal protocol.

After semantic commit, the same engine receives `kind:COMMIT`, terminal N (or ABSENT for uninstall), and the exact backup/retired/transaction candidate order. It validates the terminal active+ledger identity at every resume point. Unknown entries, out-of-order missing candidates, changed identities, or nonempty terminal remnants preserve everything.

Journal states CREATED, STAGING, CLEANUP_INTENT, CLEANING, CLEANUP_COMPLETE, PREPARED, every forward intent/milestone, and COMMITTED therefore form one closed recovery automaton. Every state and accepted one-operation successor has one direction. Tests SIGKILL a recovery process before/after every cleanup intent append, each deletion, each cleanup checkpoint, journal unlink, and rmdir, then run recover again to a stable result. Exhaustive kill-recover-kill-recover tests cover partial generation/next-ledger staging, first install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, committed cleanup, and tampered variants.

R51 — Documentation consistency
Research and proposal text must call PREPARED the semantic roll-forward commit point and must not prescribe restore-old rollback after it. Abort cleanup is limited to transaction-local pre-PREPARED candidates and shares the prefix engine with committed cleanup.

URD AMENDMENT 7 — normative resolution of Proposal 6 adversarial test review

This amendment refines Amendment 6 at syscall granularity. A directory tree is never one cleanup candidate, and CREATED/STAGING never accepts an unexplained changed hash. Every partial file and every journal append has a deterministic oracle.

R52 — Journal-authorized staging and partial-write oracle
The first complete CREATED record contains base64-encoded canonical bytes, size, SHA-256, safe final relative path, and fixed transaction-temp path for every generated agent and next-ledger payload. Recovery must not depend on the plugin, bundle, network, or cache after CREATED is durable.

Staging uses only journaled steps. Directory creation has MKDIR_INTENT with absent/present pre/post shapes. Each file has WRITE_FILE_INTENT before temp creation; while that is the last complete record, the temp may be absent or a regular file whose length is at most expected and whose bytes equal the exact prefix of the journaled canonical payload. Full temp bytes must match size/hash and be fsynced. PUBLISH_FILE_INTENT then accepts full temp/final absent or temp absent/final exact around atomic rename and parent-directory fsync. A complete FILE_PUBLISHED checkpoint advances to the next deterministic path. `next-ledger.json` uses the same protocol.

CREATED/STAGING abort may delete only paths authorized by the last complete record and matching its absent/prefix/full/published shape. Oversize, non-prefix bytes, wrong type, wrong final bytes, unjournaled temp/final, symlink, or path replacement is TAMPERED and preserved. A partial first CREATED record has no byte oracle and remains STAGING_INCOMPLETE for manual repair; an empty transaction directory remains safely removable. PREPARED is appended only after every final stage payload is exact and all file/directory fsyncs pass.

R53 — Flattened atomic cleanup plan
No cleanup path calls recursive RemoveAll or treats a nonempty directory as one candidate. Before ABORT or COMMIT cleanup, derive and journal a fully flattened deterministic postorder `CleanupEntry[]` from journal-authorized paths: each regular/temp/retired file has one unlink entry with its permitted identity (exact or authorized prefix for abort), and each directory has one rmdir entry after all children. Entries are sorted by normalized relative path within the required postorder; symlinks and unknown types are never followed or deleted.

For each `CLEANING{next_index}` entry, recovery lstat-validates the exact path and parent identities, performs at most one unlink or rmdir, fsyncs the parent directory, then appends/fsyncs the next checkpoint. A crash may leave the current entry present or absent; both prescribe the same next action. Two or more uncheckpointed missing entries, a nonempty directory at rmdir, an out-of-order prefix, or any unknown/changed entry preserves all remaining content. Backup generations, staged generations, staging temps, next-ledger, retired-ledger, auxiliary empty directories, and committed/aborted transaction contents all flatten through this engine. Journal unlink and final empty transaction-directory rmdir retain their explicit terminal steps.

R54 — Exhaustive record and recovery fault matrix
All journal writes go through one framed append primitive with named fault points: before append, after every injected short-write offset, after complete bytes but before file fsync, after file fsync, and after parent-directory fsync when applicable. Tests enumerate every record kind: CREATED, MKDIR_INTENT, WRITE_FILE_INTENT, PUBLISH_FILE_INTENT, FILE_PUBLISHED, PREPARED, MOVE_OLD_INTENT, OLD_MOVED, ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT, NEW_ACTIVE, COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT, COMMITTED, CLEANUP_INTENT, every CLEANING index, and CLEANUP_COMPLETE. A full valid PREPARED record observed after restart is the commit point even if the prior process did not observe fsync return; absent/partial PREPARED leaves STAGING as the last complete state and aborts.

The matrix kills both the original mutator and every subsequent recovery process before/after each atomic unlink/rmdir/rename and each append/fsync, then repeats recovery to a stable terminal state. Tests include every byte-prefix staging length, wrong prefix at every position, oversize, temp/final dual presence, recursive-tree postorder, nonempty rmdir, cleanup one-deletion successor, two-deletion corruption, journal partial tails, and all first-install/upgrade/downgrade/uninstall paths.

R55 — Documentation consistency
Research and proposal text must name WRITE_FILE/PUBLISH intents, the self-contained prefix oracle, flattened postorder atomic cleanup entries, and the exhaustive record append/fsync matrix. “Recursive cleanup candidate” and unexplained partial-hash acceptance are forbidden.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URD AMENDMENT 8 — Plan UAT revision for unified harness installation

This amendment supersedes the Codex-agent-only delivery choice in Amendment 1 and Proposal 7 wherever they conflict. The transaction-safety, structural runtime compiler, plugin/agent truthfulness, release pinning, and clean-review requirements in Amendments 1–7 remain normative.

User feedback (verbatim):
How come the home-manager module wouldn't install the skills too? An installer is a good idea though. We would want a command that asks what the users want to install [hooks, agents, skills], and for what harnesses [claude code, opencode, codex]. This should be similar to our @~/dev/peasant-labs/peasant/develop kickstart TUI.

Disposition: proposed FIX-NOW for both the Home Manager skills gap and the interactive multi-harness installer. Explicit confirmation is required at the revised Plan UAT gate before ratification.

R56 — One harness/component delivery catalog
Pasture defines one typed catalog for harnesses {claude-code, opencode, codex} and components {skills, agents, hooks}. Each cell records support state, user-visible reason, delivery strategy, scope, destinations, prerequisites, immutable artifact membership, modes, hashes, and ownership unit. Role, command, skill-body, and lifecycle-hook semantics remain canonical Pasture data; plugins and Home Manager are projections, not parallel inventories. The TUI, noninteractive CLI, setup skill, release bundle, tests, and Aura Home Manager consume this catalog. Unsupported or degraded cells are visible and actionable, never silently dropped.

R57 — Kickstart-style interactive installer with machine parity
The shipped `pasture install` command (with `kickstart` alias) opens a Bubble Tea wizard only when no explicit selectors are supplied and stdin/stdout are suitable TTYs. Its central page is a row/column-toggleable harness × component matrix with available, installed, selected, disabled, conflict, and externally-managed states. It preserves answers on back-navigation, shows exact reasons for unavailable cells, renders a real plan with paths/create-update-remove-no-op actions/ownership/hook consent/external commands/recovery impact, then obtains one explicit confirmation before apply and shows cancellable per-unit progress plus actionable recovery guidance.

The same typed InstallRequest and immutable InstallPlan serve TUI input, Cobra flags, and versioned JSON. Explicit selectors never launch a TUI. Incomplete non-TTY input fails with what/why/where/when/impact/fix and exact corrective flags. `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` are zero-write observers. `apply`, `recover`, and `uninstall` are explicit mutators. TUI messages, flag requests, and fixture JSON that express the same selection must compile to byte-identical canonical plans and plan digests.

R58 — Component-explicit hook consent and no Git-hook mutation
Every reference to hooks means harness lifecycle hooks, not Git hooks. No path writes `.git/hooks`, changes `core.hooksPath`, or installs Beads hooks. Hook cells default disabled for every harness. Interactive hook selection plus final confirmation is explicit consent; noninteractive apply additionally requires an affirmative hook-consent flag; Home Manager requires `hooks` in the declared component set. Selecting skills or agents alone activates zero hook definitions. Errors name the exact hook unit and remediation.

R59 — Home Manager uses the same matrix
Aura exposes a typed `targets.<harness>.components` unique list over skills/agents/hooks. Empty disables a harness. Defaults preserve the live module: Claude Code and OpenCode skills+agents enabled; Codex disabled; all hooks disabled. Existing `commands.enable`, `agents.enable`, `opencode.skills.enable`, and `opencode.agents.enable` remain compatibility inputs with deprecation warnings; conflicting old/new declarations fail evaluation actionably. The global role filter remains one shared projection unless separately ratified.

Home Manager emits a versioned InstallIntent with authority=home-manager from the shared catalog. It never sources deprecated Aura skill/agent trees, reimplements protocol inventory, copies Codex plugin skills into an unnamespaced user skill directory, claims plugin-native Codex agents, or writes Codex’s private plugin cache directly. Aura’s Linux-only package support is either expanded before claiming Darwin Home Manager support or the module rejects unsupported systems before activation.

R60 — Codex plugin, agent, and Home Manager truthfulness
The primary generated Codex `pasture` plugin owns the complete namespaced skill set and carries the canonical native-agent bundle only as inert installer assets. A separately selectable `pasture-hooks` plugin owns lifecycle hooks so skills-only installation activates no hooks. Native custom agents remain standalone TOMLs under the supported personal agent tree and are installed only by an explicit mutator.

Codex Home Manager plugin mode uses a private pinned local marketplace plus the supported idempotent `codex plugin add` command, then verifies exact plugin ID/version/source and installed agent bytes. Before any mutation it detects a symlinked, read-only, or independently Home-Manager-owned `~/.codex/config.toml` and returns an actionable conflict. It never bypasses that conflict by editing cache internals. A separately generated standalone `$pasture-*` skill dialect is a possible pure-declarative alternative but is DEFERRED unless the user selects it at UAT; it must not be silently substituted.

R61 — Target-native OpenCode lifecycle hooks
Pasture adds an OpenCode-specific lifecycle plugin rather than copying Claude hook JSON or scripts. Against the pinned current OpenCode contract it projects Pasture’s system/session context, compaction context, and pre-shell discipline through target-native plugin events. Worker-only policy executes only when worker identity is proven from supported session/agent data; unknown identity does not block unrelated agents and is reported as degraded coverage. Tests pin the plugin API surface and fail on Claude event names, Claude plugin-root variables, or unsupported raw operations.

R62 — Release-complete immutable payload
The Pasture release must contain the complete generated installation payload, not only development-time repository files. Codegen emits a versioned delivery manifest and all exact payload bytes; the shipped `pasture` binary embeds or otherwise carries the same immutable bundle on every supported release platform. GitHub archives, Nix packages, setup skills, plugins, the CLI, and Home Manager agree on schema version, Pasture/plugin versions, base checksums, artifact hashes, modes, paths, and supported OS/architecture data. A release-installed CLI can plan and install without a source checkout or network after bundle acquisition.

R63 — Per-cell ownership and recoverable multi-unit apply
Ownership is exclusive per resolved `(home, scope, harness, component)`, not per whole home. Companion and Home Manager may coexist only on disjoint cells. Plan digests bind desired bundle bytes, all selected cells, current owners/generations/journals, destinations, collisions, external registry state, scope decisions, hook consent, and options.

Direct-file units use the Amendments 5–7 journal, PREPARED commit point, self-contained payload oracle, and flattened atomic cleanup. Harness registry adapters journal intent around supported idempotent CLI operations, may be safely re-entered after an unknown outcome, and verify exact postconditions. A multi-cell request applies deterministic ownership units; an interrupted or failed unit is classified and resumable, already committed units are never reported as an all-or-nothing rollback, and unrelated unselected cells are untouched. Preflight conflicts fail before the first unit commits.

R64 — Test and documentation contract
Fixture-based tests cover every 3×3 capability cell, row/column toggles, disabled/degraded reasons, prior selections, back/cancel/confirm, terminal resizing, non-TTY errors, hook consent, TUI/flags/JSON plan parity, repeated no-op apply, cross-authority conflicts, legacy Home Manager migration, immutable Codex config, missing harness CLIs, release-installed payload availability, external CLI unknown outcomes, and fault injection at every journal/syscall boundary. Black-box smoke tests load each selected component in the actual pinned harness and prove each unselected component absent. Research, proposal, CLI docs, Home Manager docs, and plugin metadata use the same catalog names and delivery claims.
