author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

## Severity totals

- BLOCKER: 0
- IMPORTANT: 1
- MINOR: 1

## Findings

### IMPORTANT

1. The transaction freezes the harness executable, but not the Pasture executable object that implements the detached runner and each start-gated wrapper.

Evidence:
- Proposal 11 correctly stages a byte-verified native Claude/Codex executable and makes that snapshot the eventual harness exec object.
- Each CLI step nevertheless requires a newly spawned Pasture-owned wrapper to read the authenticated gate and then exec that descriptor/path. The proposal does not define the wrapper binary source or bind its path, bytes, version, digest, inode, and schema to `EXT_CREATED`/`PREPARED`.
- The detached runner is likewise launched by the frontend without a frozen self-executable contract.
- Linux can often address the live image through `/proc/self/exe`, but Darwin has no equivalent descriptor-exec path for an arbitrary Go helper. A companion Pasture binary can be atomically upgraded or path-swapped while a committed transaction is still spawning later wrappers; Home Manager can also change generations.

Impact:
The authenticated channel proves that the process at the other end received exactly one durable release frame, but it does not prove that this process is the reviewed gate implementation. A changed or incompatible helper can bypass/fail the gate or make post-PREPARED recovery depend on the current Pasture installation, recreating the executable-identity ambiguity the harness snapshot was designed to remove.

Required fix:
Define one immutable, versioned Pasture runner/wrapper executable object. For example, stage a verified self/helper snapshot before `PREPARED`, record its bytes/digest/native format/gate-schema compatibility in the first complete journal contract, launch the detached runner and every wrapper only from that object, and retain it through terminal cleanup. An equivalent kernel-bound object is acceptable where proven, but Darwin must not fall back to a mutable current path. Add frontend-self, runner-helper, wrapper-helper, Pasture-upgrade, Nix-generation, path/inode/content swap, and recovery-with-a-different-current-binary fixtures. Distinguish the helper snapshot from the separately pinned harness snapshot in types and journal records.

### MINOR

1. The cited research file still declares a different external graph as exact.

Evidence:
- Proposal 11 freezes separate journaled `MARKETPLACE_LIST_*` and `PLUGIN_LIST_*` children followed by pure `ASSERT_*` steps.
- The research section titled as the exact step fixtures still states the shorter install/upgrade/uninstall graphs with opaque `VERIFY_*` nodes and its exact argv table omits both list operations.

Impact:
The proposal is implementable, but two cited sources claim different exact state machines, inviting a worker to collapse observers back into an opaque postcheck and weakening the no-parallel-truth guarantee.

Required fix:
Update the research exact argv table and all three graphs to the Proposal 11 list-child/assert form, or explicitly label the shorter notation as non-normative expansion shorthand and point to the single normative oracle. Add a drift assertion if both are generated from one schema.

## Verified clean areas

- `IntentMode` makes companion ensure-selected and Home Manager exact reconciliation distinct wire semantics; the separate 512-case suites avoid false cross-authority parity.
- Canonically sorted `ArtifactProjection{Harness, Artifact, Skill, Role}` removes Aura filename-prefix truth; direct packages prune and indivisible Codex skills reject narrowed roles honestly.
- Legacy matching projects only the Claude row, so an all-three Claude composite composes with every OpenCode/Codex subset.
- Transaction-local source/executable staging, durable `PREPARED`, then first-step `PUBLISH_N` gives external units one monotone commit direction.
- Closing the sole release writer after one `PIPE_BUF`-bounded frame and requiring wrapper EOF makes zero/short/extra versus exactly-one-frame execution coherent.
- Digest-qualified P/N sources, marketplaces, selectors, and explicit list/assert steps compose across install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, authorities, and unrelated registry entries.
- Pinned Claude 2.1.207 and Codex 0.144.1 help surfaces accept the proposed argv; OpenCode provenance now binds the actual `v1.17.18` tag commit.
- Linux descriptor execution and pure-Go Darwin snapshot/sysctl process identity remain feasible under the repository CGO prohibition.

## Conclusion

Proposal 11 removes the prior intent, role, Claude-row, source-commit, gate-frame, graph, and provenance ambiguities. The remaining helper-executable boundary is part of the same safety proof, not an implementation detail; the research graph must then be aligned to leave one exact lifecycle truth. REVISE.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: test quality and acceptance-plan falsification

Severity count: 0 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR.

Evidence reviewed: FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-11 aura-plugins-fmrw5 as amended through the canonical ArtifactProjection slice, one-write-and-EOF gate, and foreign-selector collision clarifications; URD aura-plugins-2hkz3 including Amendments 1-8; inherited Proposals 7-10; prior Round 10 test-quality vote aura-plugins-4mbfi; the updated research report; local Claude Code 2.1.207 and Codex 0.144.1 command help for every frozen argv; and git ls-remote resolution of OpenCode v1.17.18.

IMPORTANT 1 — the 32 role-subset claim has no input-presence oracle.

InstallRequest exposes EnabledRoles as a bare []RoleID, but Proposal 11 does not freeze the Cobra, TUI, JSON, or Home Manager grammar that distinguishes an omitted role filter from the explicit empty subset. Both matter: the normal default must retain all roles, while empty is one of the promised 32 subsets and retains only core skills for member-prunable packages. The current fixture sentence can be satisfied by constructing post-parse slices directly, so it cannot catch an adapter that collapses omitted, null, and [] or applies different defaults. It also does not establish which of the 32 cases make a selected indivisible Codex skills cell fail.

Required revision: freeze a presence-bearing role selection wire contract and exact defaults, including canonical flag syntax, TUI state, JSON omitted/null/empty behavior, and Home Manager normalization. Drive all 32 subsets through the actual adapters, including ordering, duplicates, unknown roles, omitted/default-all, and explicit empty. For every subset, assert the canonical ArtifactProjection, direct-package members/effects, the unchanged five-agent set, and Codex behavior: full roles succeeds while every truly narrowed projection fails before mutation with UNSUPPORTED_INDIVISIBLE_PROJECTION.

IMPORTANT 2 — the new lifecycle YAML oracle is not explicitly independent of production graph and argv tables.

Proposal 9 made internal/delivery/testdata/capabilities.yaml test-only and forbidden to production, but that fixture freezes nine capability rows, not the new Claude/Codex P/N lifecycle graphs. Proposal 11 says only that a checked-in YAML oracle freezes the vectors and separately calls the harness fixtures independent. It does not say that production cannot import or generate this new oracle, identify separate Claude and Codex expected data, or require a mutation to fail when a production command token, step order, intermediate vector, cleanup authorization, or unrelated-versus-colliding identity rule is wrong. Tests derived from the same runtime table can therefore pass a self-consistent but invalid graph.

Required revision: name checked-in test-only YAML lifecycle fixtures for Claude and Codex that are authored independently of runtime adapter tables and never imported or generated by production. Freeze exact argv token arrays, P/N and every known intermediate, retained sources, assertions, cleanup authority, unrelated-name preservation, and M_P/M_N/Q_P/Q_N collision rejection for install, upgrade, authorized downgrade, uninstall, and no-op. Add mutation tests proving each wrong token, omitted or reordered observer, wrong vector, premature cleanup, and cross-harness table substitution fails. Run the full record/fsync/gate/spawn/exit/recovery/cancellation matrix from those fixture expectations.

IMPORTANT 3 — the 7 x 64 legacy matrix omits the discovery-sensitive desired-empty exact-reconcile transition.

Section 3 correctly adds discovery when RECONCILE_EXACT touches an already Home-Manager-owned Claude cell, but its exhaustive matrix covers only seven nonempty desired Claude rows. A desired empty Claude row with one or more prior Home-Manager-owned Claude cells is a removal transition, unlike companion select-none and unlike an exact-reconcile empty row with no owned Claude cell. Neither the separate 512 desired-selection suite nor the 7 x 64 desired-row suite necessarily crosses that prior ownership with active/inactive/unknown/declined/stale/unavailable/apply-race legacy evidence.

Required revision: add an exact-reconcile transition matrix with desired Claude row empty, all seven nonempty prior Home-Manager-owned Claude subsets, all relevant other-harness selections, and every discovery state. Freeze when removal may proceed, when legacy state conflicts or is externally managed, and when unknown/declined/stale/unavailable/apply-changed evidence blocks before mutation. Pair it with controls proving companion select-none and an exact empty row with no owned Claude cells introduce no Claude discovery merely because other harnesses are selected.

IMPORTANT 4 — PUBLISH_N lacks the exact stage-plus-destination state required by existing-exact no-op.

Before PREPARED, STAGE_SOURCE is exact. If the digest-qualified persistent destination already exists exact, the post-PREPARED existing-exact branch is a no-op on the destination while the transaction stage still exists until authorized cleanup. The named fixture set includes stage-only, destination-only, and published-but-unrecorded, but not both exact stage and exact destination. Destination-only cannot exercise cleanup of the retained stage or the crash window around recording the no-op. A production implementation could leak the stage, replace an already exact destination, or classify the dual state as tampered while all listed fixtures pass.

Required revision: add the exact stage-plus-exact-destination state to the PUBLISH_N automaton and YAML oracle. Freeze its no-replacement postcondition, step-record/fsync successor, transaction-stage cleanup authorization, and recovery result. Fault-inject before and after existing-exact observation, no-op record/fsync, and each cleanup boundary; distinguish an identical destination from wrong-digest, prefix, symlink, and foreign destinations.

Positive evidence and passed falsifications: the two 512 suites now separate ENSURE_SELECTED from RECONCILE_EXACT and preserve their different empty semantics; the canonical sorted ArtifactProjection removes the map-order oracle and narrowed Codex projection fails honestly; the 7 x 64 nonempty desired-row matrix fixes the prior whole-request bug; STAGE_SOURCE followed by PREPARED then PUBLISH_N fixes the precommit persistent-write flaw; the immutable executable snapshot plus the sole PIPE_BUF-bounded writer closed immediately and wrapper read-through-EOF closes the runner-death gate ambiguity and defines zero/one process shapes; the exact Claude and Codex argv are accepted by the pinned local CLIs; unrelated registry identities are preserved while selector collisions fail foreign; and git ls-remote confirms OpenCode v1.17.18 resolves to b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c, making the discarded-pin mismatch-negative meaningful. Those improvements remain, but this round has findings.

Exit decision: do not close aura-plugins-iswju. Revise Proposal 11, then run a fresh three-axis review round and require a fix-free 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR consensus before Plan UAT.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: Round 11 correctness, security, and distribution

Severity totals: 2 BLOCKER, 3 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR.

Evidence reviewed: full Proposal 11 aura-plugins-fmrw5 including the amended one-write/EOF gate and sorted ArtifactProjection edge; URD aura-plugins-2hkz3 through Amendment 8; inherited Proposals 7-10; prior correctness finding aura-plugins-lfofi; updated research; current Aura Home Manager role and source topology; current Pasture CLI/codegen/release tests; local pinned Claude Code 2.1.207, Codex 0.144.1, and OpenCode 1.17.18 command surfaces; official Codex release metadata; official Apple execve contract; OpenCode tag resolution; and the actual Nix-provisioned Codex executable chain.

BLOCKER 1 — Darwin pathname execution is still not bound to the verified executable object.

Proposal 11 correctly copies and verifies a private harness snapshot, but explicitly executes that snapshot by path on Darwin. Apple execve takes a pathname. A final inode/hash check followed by execve(path) has a rename/unlink replacement window in which the directory entry can be switched before the kernel resolves it. Making the file non-writable and holding Pasture leases does not prevent the owning user or a fault-injection adversary from replacing a directory entry; those leases coordinate cooperating Pasture processes, not arbitrary same-user writers. Therefore the claim that path/inode swaps after PREPARED can never switch the exec object is stronger than the mechanism.

The trusted start-gate wrapper also has no frozen code-object provenance. If it is launched by a mutable Pasture pathname, a replaced wrapper can ignore the token protocol even though the harness snapshot itself is exact. If it is intended to execute in the already loaded runner image, that mechanism and its platform safety must be explicit.

Required revision: use a proven same-open-object execution mechanism on Darwin, or a platform primitive that starts suspended and verifies the actual process image/vnode before permitting any registry work. Bind the gate wrapper itself to an immutable verified object and protocol version. If neither is available, reject Darwin external cells and narrow the four-tuple claim. Fault tests must replace the wrapper and harness snapshot after every final check, at gate release, and immediately before the kernel exec boundary; a different inode must never run.

BLOCKER 2 — STAGE_EXECUTABLE has no self-contained partial-write oracle after runner death.

EXT_CREATED embeds the package ZIP but not the 100-400 MB harness executable bytes. Before PREPARED, STAGE_EXECUTABLE copies from a live descriptor into transaction state. If the runner dies after any short write, the descriptor is gone and a size plus final SHA-256 cannot prove whether the partial file is the exact canonical prefix or attacker-controlled bytes of the same length. URD R52/R54 requires journal-authorized prefix classification and forbids deleting a wrong-prefix candidate. Proposal 11 nevertheless calls the executable snapshot abortable transaction state and expects bounded recovery. Those claims cannot both hold without durable prefix material.

Required revision: journal authenticated executable chunks before each write, including exact chunk bytes or a construction that proves every possible partial final chunk, and give each chunk write/publish/fsync its own accepted predecessor/successor shapes. Embedding the full executable is another valid but large oracle. Otherwise classify any interrupted executable copy as preserved manual repair and narrow clean pre-PREPARED cancellation/recovery. Tests must kill at every byte/chunk boundary, replace/remove the original CLI after EXT_CREATED, distinguish every wrong prefix, and prove that abort never deletes unauthenticated bytes.

IMPORTANT 1 — rejecting wrappers contradicts the claimed Nix/Home Manager distribution path.

The locally supported Codex 0.144.1 entrypoint is /home/minttea/.nix-profile/bin/codex, a symlink to a Nix-store Bash wrapper. That wrapper adjusts PATH and execs a hidden patched .codex-wrapped native binary. Proposal 11 rejects scripts/wrappers, while also claiming Nix-generation swap coverage. Resolving directly to .codex-wrapped bypasses package behavior and its patched binary cannot be assumed to equal the official standalone extracted-executable digest. Thus the current Home Manager environment is classified incompatible despite being the exact pinned CLI version used by the research and review.

Required revision: either support a pinned executable-closure adapter that verifies the wrapper, interpreter, environment policy, native target, and package provenance as one immutable launch contract, or explicitly support only official standalone archives and remove Nix-profile compatibility claims. Add a real Nix-wrapped 0.144.1 fixture, not only a symlink-to-native fixture, and prove snapshot execution preserves required wrapper behavior.

IMPORTANT 2 — legacy Claude occupancy is not composed with role projection or empty exact reconciliation.

Proposal 11 marks an active legacy composite plus all three Claude cells EXTERNALLY_MANAGED regardless of EnabledRoles. The legacy all-in-one package exposes its full role-scoped skill set, so it cannot satisfy a narrowed role request; this is the same indivisible-projection truth already recognized for Codex skills. The 7 x 64 Claude-row suite does not cross the 32 role subsets.

There is a second omitted shape: RECONCILE_EXACT with an empty desired Claude row that touches currently Home-Manager-owned Claude cells correctly requires legacy discovery, but the outcome for an active legacy composite is not specified and the tests enumerate only seven nonempty desired rows. Removing modern links cannot achieve exact absence while the legacy composite remains active.

Required revision: include projection granularity and requested role effects in legacy effective-state comparison. An active legacy composite is externally managed only when its complete Claude effects, including full role exposure, exactly satisfy the request; narrowed roles conflict. Cross the Claude-row matrix with all 32 role subsets. Add empty desired-row/current-owner cases: active legacy must conflict before removing anything, inactive legacy may reconcile owned modern cells to absent, and unknown/stale observations block.

IMPORTANT 3 — the public request algebra does not reject invalid authority, mode, operation, or role-provenance combinations.

InstallRequest exposes Authority, Mode, Operation, and EnabledRoles, but the proposal states conventions rather than a closed validation table. A versioned JSON caller can construct home-manager plus ensure-selected, companion plus reconcile-exact, reconcile-exact uninstall, or another nonsensical tuple. It can also encode EnabledRoles as omitted/null versus an explicit empty list; empty is a real core-only role subset, while ordinary omission presumably means the historical all-role default. Without canonical presence rules those inputs can collapse to the same Go nil slice or digest differently across adapters.

Required revision: freeze and exhaustively validate the allowed authority x mode x operation table before discovery or mutation. Home Manager authority must require the immutable generated intent/executor prerequisites rather than being a caller-asserted label. Require a sorted unique role list in the canonical request, with adapters materializing the full default before encoding; reserve an explicit empty list for core-only direct skills and reject null/omitted if ambiguity would remain. Add malformed JSON and cross-authority negative fixtures proving zero mutation and actionable errors.

Verified closures and positive evidence:
- ENSURE_SELECTED and RECONCILE_EXACT now truthfully have separate exhaustive suites and digests.
- The sorted SkillDescriptor to ArtifactProjection edge removes filename-prefix role inference; direct pruning and indivisible Codex failure are coherent.
- Claude matching is correctly projected onto the Claude row for nonempty selections and preserves other harness actions.
- STAGE_SOURCE is transaction-local, PREPARED is unambiguous, and PUBLISH_N is the first postcommit source step.
- Closing the sole PIPE_BUF-bounded release writer and requiring read-through-EOF makes zero/short/extra/invalid gate streams fail closed; durable CHILD_ARMED precedes any valid release.
- Literal Claude and Codex argv in the lifecycle table match the local 2.1.207 and 0.144.1 help surfaces. The install/upgrade/downgrade/uninstall P/N graphs and collision rule are otherwise closed and preserve unrelated identities.
- OpenCode v1.17.18 now resolves to the correct tag commit b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c; the discarded commit is a useful negative.
- The independent oracle, semantic-discovery digest, embedded package source, shared authority lease, 81-state legacy option provenance, zero-write observers, and release bundle remain coherent.

Disposition: REVISE. Do not close aura-plugins-2amc6. A fresh proposal and three-axis round are required; ACCEPT remains reserved for a fix-free 0/0/0 review.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE
Reviewer: architecture/elegance
Severity totals: BLOCKER 1, IMPORTANT 1, MINOR 0

BLOCKER — The executable-provider algebra has no valid tuple for the Home Manager path. Home Manager invokes a Nix-built Pasture helper, but the closed provider set contains only `official-native` and `nix-wrapper-v1`; the latter models the wrapped Codex CLI, while the former requires an official release archive checksum. The helper therefore cannot satisfy the identity gate it is required to implement, and an embedded checksum of its own final binary would be recursive. Add a first-class direct Nix-native helper variant within the same provider schema, bound to immutable store/NAR/flake provenance and an independently supplied provider-specific digest. Do not add a parallel helper inventory.

IMPORTANT — `Digest` is still described as the canonical closure digest while `BoundObject` carries per-attempt image device/inode identity, and recovery claims a freshly created memfd/APFS clone is an identical closure. Fresh images necessarily have new physical identities. Define one stable semantic digest over provider/version/protocol/object bytes/environment/argv0, explicitly excluding descriptors and physical identities; journal per-attempt source/image identities separately and durably record a rebound before gate release.

Verified clean: BoundExecutableClosure replaces executable snapshots rather than layering them; Linux sealed-memfd/execveat and Darwin APFS-clone plus descriptor execution are pure-Go feasible and honestly conformance-gated; one helper descriptor binds frontend, runner, and wrappers; recovery narrows rather than substitutes; the request wire is a closed discriminated algebra; roles and legacy occupancy share one typed projection; and the research/proposal lifecycle graphs and independent lifecycle-oracle requirements are aligned.

Conclusion: REVISE. This is not a fix-free 0/0/0 round.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: test quality and acceptance-plan falsification

Severity count: 0 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR.

Evidence reviewed: full FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-12 aura-plugins-w2qbs; URD aura-plugins-2hkz3 through Amendment 8; inherited Proposals 7-11; all three Round 11 votes, especially test-quality comment 4116; the updated research report; the real local Nix Codex 0.144.1 wrapper, interpreter, PATH edit, and .codex-wrapped target; the current Pasture Nix build surface; Linux memfd and sealing documentation; and the frozen external lifecycle argv/graphs.

IMPORTANT 1 — closure semantic identity is not separated from per-launch descriptor identity.

BoundExecutableClosure has one canonical Digest while each BoundObject also carries source/image device and inode. Only descriptor numbers are explicitly excluded from serialization. The journal stores the closure digest plus those identities, and recovery is required to create a fresh identical sealed memfd or unlinked APFS image. A fresh memfd or clone necessarily has a new live image inode; restoring the same pinned Nix or native package can also recreate an exact source at a new inode. The proposal does not freeze whether these volatile identities participate in Digest or provide a repeat/mutation oracle. An implementation can therefore reject a valid exact restoration forever, or weaken equality until a different provider is accepted, while broad provider-loss tests still pass.

Required revision: define a stable ClosureSemanticDigest separately from LaunchImageIdentity. Freeze its canonical fields: provider, harness, version, helper protocol and bundle, ordered object purpose/content/provenance, image strategy, typed environment edits, and argv0 policy. Exclude process-local descriptors and fresh image device/inode; record those only in the launch/CHILD_ARMED identity. Tests must construct the same closure through two independent memfds and two APFS clones and require equal semantic digests but distinct launch identities; mutate every semantic field independently and require a digest change. Loss/restore tests must distinguish exact content plus provenance restored at a new inode from same bytes under the wrong provider/provenance and from any changed object.

IMPORTANT 2 — the Linux executable-memfd seal and failure oracle is still only an outcome sentence.

Proposal 12 names write, grow, shrink, and seal seals, but it does not require a test matrix around memfd creation flags, every copy offset, size/hash verification, each F_ADD_SEALS result, F_GET_SEALS, descriptor inheritance, final execveat, and cleanup on each failure. This matters because sealing is disabled unless MFD_ALLOW_SEALING is requested, and newer Linux kernels distinguish executable MFD_EXEC from MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL under vm.memfd_noexec policy. A test that merely executes one sealed happy-path image can miss a missing seal, an executable-policy failure, execution before sealing, an inherited writable descriptor/mapping, or a short-copy error.

Required revision: freeze the exact create flags and required final seal mask, and have the wrapper verify the mask as well as fstat identity before exec. On both supported Linux architectures, fault-inject before/after memfd_create, size allocation, every short-copy offset, hash, every seal operation, F_GET_SEALS, fd duplication/inheritance, CHILD_ARMED, and execveat. Negative fixtures cover missing MFD_ALLOW_SEALING, each missing seal, failed F_SEAL_WRITE due to a writable mapping, wrong size/content, fd-number collision/CLOEXEC mistakes, and executable-memfd policy modes including required MFD_EXEC behavior. Every negative must execute zero helper/harness code and leave no filesystem candidate.

Primary contract evidence: Linux kernel memfd execution policy is documented at https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/mfd_noexec.html and the sealing precondition/F_GET_SEALS contract at https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/memfd_create.2.html.

IMPORTANT 3 — helper handoff and provider-loss tests do not cover the deployed Pasture helper provider set.

The closure type includes Harness=pasture-helper and Provider official-native or nix-wrapper-v1, but section 2 freezes a real Nix provider only for Codex. The helper paragraph instead assumes the already-running Pasture object matches an official platform release checksum. Aura Home Manager execution comes from a Pasture/Nix integration path, and a Nix-built Pasture ELF can be immutable without being byte-identical to the official release archive. No fixture states whether that helper is supported, rejected before mutation, or bound as a distinct provider. The stated self-upgrade/removal test can pass using only an official helper and miss the Home Manager launch path.

Required revision: freeze the supported pasture-helper provider tuples independently from harness tuples. If Nix-built Pasture is supported, add a real Nix-built helper fixture with its own derivation/provenance/native digest and no comparison to official bytes; if not, make Home Manager supply the official helper and add an actionable rejection fixture for a Nix helper. For every supported helper provider, fault-test frontend-to-runner and runner-to-wrapper descriptor handoff at resolve/open/verify, CHILD_ARMED append/fsync, sole-writer release/EOF, exec, and provider disappearance. Then remove or replace the invocation path, helper package, each harness closure object, and the current Pasture installation independently; exact restoration must resume, wrong helper protocol/bundle/provider must remain RECOVERY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED, and no second runner/wrapper may start.

IMPORTANT 4 — the exhaustive legacy matrix is keyed by intent mode, not the three closed IntentKinds, leaving uninstall role semantics without an oracle.

companion-ensure and companion-uninstall share ensure-selected mode but have different desired transitions. InstallRequest nevertheless requires Roles for both, while section 3 never says whether an uninstall role subset is rejected, ignored/canonicalized, removes only projected skill members, or removes the whole selected cell. Section 4 then claims an exhaustive matrix over intent mode and prior Home Manager ownership only. It does not freeze companion-owned prior rows or active-legacy behavior when companion-uninstall selects one or all Claude cells. An implementation could treat an active full legacy composite as EXTERNALLY_MANAGED success for uninstall, silently ignore a role-dependent digest, or partially remove a cell and still satisfy the stated ensure-mode matrix.

Required revision: give Roles an exact per-IntentKind rule. Prefer either forbidding role flags for companion-uninstall and canonicalizing the wire to full roles, or explicitly defining and owning member-level partial removal; do not silently ignore a digest-bearing field. Make the legacy oracle cross all three IntentKinds rather than two modes, with the applicable prior companion and Home Manager ownership rows. Freeze that uninstall never adopts/removes the legacy composite, active legacy occupancy conflicts with a requested Claude absence before modern mutation, inactive state removes only exact Pasture-owned modern content, and unknown/declined/stale/unavailable/apply-changed evidence blocks. Run accepted/rejected JSON, Cobra, and TUI encodings for each kind with default roles plus all 32 explicit subsets according to that rule.

Positive evidence and passed falsifications: the Darwin fclonefileat design now has an explicit absent/exact/unlinked no-prefix state model and no unsafe stream fallback; descriptor execution has mandatory path/inode/content swap conformance on both Darwin architectures and no pathname fallback; the frontend runner and harness wrapper use the same one-frame/read-through-EOF gate; the actual Nix Codex wrapper grammar, interpreter, PATH edit, target, provider-specific digest, and behavioral equivalence are all mutation-tested; role input now distinguishes omitted default-all from explicit core-only and rejects malformed encodings; desired/prior/other/role/evidence legacy dimensions and exact-empty Home Manager removal are present; EXACT_STAGE_AND_DESTINATION closes the source reuse state; and separate manually authored test-only Claude/Codex YAML plus production mutation and reverse-parser tests prevent a shared wrong lifecycle table. These are substantial fixes, but the round is not fix-free.

Exit decision: do not close aura-plugins-o9xyb. Revise Proposal 12 and run a fresh three-axis review round; progression still requires 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR from all reviewers.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: Round 12 correctness, security, and distribution

Severity totals: 2 BLOCKER, 2 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR.

Evidence reviewed: frozen Proposal 12 aura-plugins-w2qbs; URD aura-plugins-2hkz3 through the inherited amendments; Proposals 7-11; all three Round 11 votes; the updated research report; current Aura Home Manager topology; the actual Nix Codex 0.144.1 wrapper and native target; golang.org/x/sys v0.44.0 source and CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-builds for linux amd64/arm64 and darwin amd64/arm64; Apple APFS cloning and execve documentation; XNU kern_exec.c at f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea; and pinned Codex 0.144.1 arg0/current_exe behavior.

BLOCKER 1 — the Darwin APFS clone is a stable snapshot of the source, but it is not an immutable execution image against the stated same-user writer.

fclonefileat creates a new copy-on-write filesystem object at a pathname. Proposal 12 opens that clone read-only, hashes it, unlinks it, and later relies on fstat device/inode identity. During the linked interval, another process with the same uid can discover the clone, chmod/open it for writing, retain that writable descriptor after unlink, and modify the inode after the accepted hash. The read-only ImageFD does not seal the inode, unlink does not revoke an already-open writer, and content writes do not change device/inode. Therefore the final re-fstat cannot detect the substitution. A rehash immediately before exec would merely introduce another hash-to-exec race. This directly contradicts the proposal claim that same-user in-place changes cannot alter a darwin-apfs-clone image.

Primary API evidence: Apple documents clonefile/fclonefileat as cloning APIs and COPYFILE_CLONE as a full data/metadata clone, not as a write seal: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/APFS_Guide/ToolsandAPIs/ToolsandAPIs.html

Required revision: either reject mutable Darwin executable sources and support only independently immutable/root-owned objects, or identify and prove a kernel-enforced, non-bypassable immutable-image primitive whose protection survives unlink and hostile same-uid descriptors. Tests must let an adversary open the brief clone for write before unlink, mutate it after the accepted hash and at the exec boundary, and prove that no changed bytes execute. Random names, permissions owned by the same uid, advisory locks, fstat, and code-signing assumptions are not sufficient substitutes for the seal.

BLOCKER 2 — an arbitrary immutable Nix-store file is not Home Manager authority.

Proposal 12 rejects ordinary JSON but grants home-manager-reconcile when the input is an immutable Nix-store intent containing generation/profile/digest/provenance fields. Nix explicitly lets a caller add an arbitrary file/path to the store (locally, nix store add-file is documented as adding caller-supplied content). Immutability proves that bytes do not change after import; it does not attest that Aura Home Manager generated those bytes or that the named generation/profile is active. All listed identity fields can therefore be copied or forged in another immutable store object. A companion caller can reach the hidden entrypoint with a fabricated exact-reconcile request and acquire removal authority over Home-Manager-owned cells, contradicting the promised spoofed-Home-Manager rejection.

Required revision: bind the Home Manager capability to a non-caller-selectable activation object, for example an exact validated reconciler wrapper/closure with its normalized intent embedded and fixed argv, plus an active-generation/profile proof checked independently of self-asserted intent fields. The public and hidden decoders must reject every arbitrary store path, including a byte-valid forged intent with copied generation/catalog values, before discovery. Add first-activation, generation-switch, stale-generation, copied-intent, manually added store-file, wrapper-substitution, and replay fixtures.

IMPORTANT 1 — the cited XNU source does not establish the claimed Darwin executable-descriptor contract.

The referenced kern_exec.c occurrence of /dev/fd creates an fd for a SUID/SGID interpreter script and passes /dev/fd/<n> as the script argument to its interpreter so the interpreter does not reopen the script pathname. It does not call execve on /dev/fd/<n> to load a Mach-O executable from the already-open descriptor. Apple public execve documentation remains pathname-based. Proposal 12 is fail-closed if a future conformance probe fails, which is good, but that future probe cannot serve as current proof for the claim that both Darwin architectures are supported tuples.

Primary evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea/bsd/kern/kern_exec.c and https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/execve.2.html

Required revision: correct the research/proposal description of the XNU code and provide pinned empirical Darwin amd64/arm64 evidence before claiming those tuples: native Mach-O execution from an open then unlinked fd, final source/path swaps, reserved-fd non-CLOEXEC lifetime, code-signing behavior, and exact failure classification. Freeze the supported macOS range. If that evidence is unavailable, narrow the Darwin external-cell support claim while retaining the no-path-fallback rule.

IMPORTANT 2 — the typed closure cannot represent the source identity, image identity, and recovery equality that the prose requires.

BoundObject has SourceFD and ImageFD but only one SHA256/Device/Inode tuple. For sealed memfd and APFS clone strategies the source and image are distinct objects with distinct device/inode identities; the prose nevertheless says the journal stores both source and image digest/device/inode. Recovery then creates a fresh memfd or clone with a necessarily new image inode while also requiring the exact recorded closure. If the closure digest binds image identity, exact recovery is impossible. If it excludes image identity, the proposal does not define the separate digest/record that CHILD_ARMED and the final re-fstat bind. The ambiguity is security-relevant because stable provider equality and per-attempt exec-object equality have different lifetimes.

Required revision: split stable SourceIdentity/ProviderIdentity from ephemeral ImageIdentity, define the exact fields and domain separator of each digest, state which record binds each, and specify recovery equality explicitly: the stable source/provider closure must match PREPARED while each new CHILD_ARMED binds its newly derived image identity. Add recovery tests proving a fresh image inode is accepted only with an exact stable closure and that any source or current-image mismatch is rejected.

Verified Round 11 closures that should be preserved:
- Removing streamed executable staging resolves the unauthenticated 100-400 MB partial-prefix oracle; the APFS clone operation now has its own absent/exact/unlinked crash vocabulary.
- The detached runner and wrappers are explicitly rebound to one Pasture helper closure, closing the prior mutable gate-code omission.
- official-native and nix-wrapper-v1 are separate provider tuples; the Nix wrapper/interpreter/PATH/native target and patched digest are no longer compared to official standalone bytes.
- The three IntentKinds, required explicit role array, default-all versus explicit empty grammar, legacy full-role/removal matrix, exact stage-plus-destination publication state, and separate test-only Claude/Codex lifecycle oracles address their Round 11 findings.
- x/sys v0.44.0 itself builds pure Go for all four target OS/architecture pairs and exposes MemfdCreate, Darwin Fclonefileat, sealing constants, and Linux SYS_EXECVEAT/AT_EMPTY_PATH. The repo will still need its own carefully tested execveat adapter because x/sys does not expose a high-level Execveat function.

Disposition: REVISE. This is not a fix-free 0/0/0 round. Keep aura-plugins-ajqw7 open; Proposal 13 and a fresh three-reviewer round are required.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Severity: 1 BLOCKER / 5 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR

Scope: FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-14 against canonical FOLLOWUP_URD-2 only, the cleaned research record, and current Pasture/Aura seams. This review does not treat superseded proposals as normative. The proposed test direction is much smaller and more honest, but the failure-model oracles are not yet complete enough for a 0/0/0 vote.

BLOCKER

B1 — The direct-file/tree recovery protocol is neither complete nor reachable through the public command contract.
Proposal §8 names useful shapes, but it omits at least: a create action with absent prior destination/ledger at PREPARED; create after destination publish but before ledger commit; file replacement after atomic rename without the tree backup shape; failures while atomically publishing PREPARING/PREPARED, the ledger, or record cleanup; pre-existing/colliding recorded stage/backup paths; and distinct file/tree uninstall boundaries. More fundamentally, §7 exposes recover dispositions accept-observed|retry|forget-aborted, which §9 defines for external commands, while §8 never says which command performs direct roll-forward/abort. Status is explicitly read-only, and a new plan/apply is not explicitly required to stop before overwriting a pending direct transaction. UR6 therefore has no finite executable recovery contract.

Exact correction: add a versioned DirectPending schema and one finite transition table covering {create, update, remove} × {file, tree} at every durable boundary. For each row specify prior destination/ledger, stage, backup, pending phase, allowed mutation, resulting ledger, and whether recovery resumes or aborts. Make status classification-only; make any pending direct record block planning/application; expose distinct direct recovery actions such as resume and abort-preparing with exact eligibility. Define pending/ledger publication themselves as temp-write + file fsync + rename + directory fsync. Test every table row and every state-publication/rename failpoint from independently hand-authored filesystem fixtures (including independently computed file/tree identity), and assert byte/mtime stability plus that no path other than the exact recorded candidates changes.

IMPORTANT

I1 — Config publication, TUI save/apply ordering, and parity still have an ambiguous fault boundary.
The proposal says any save failure prevents apply, but rename may have replaced config before the parent-directory fsync fails. It also calls one root Config both the persisted document and the CLI/env-resolved daemon view; an installer rewrite must not accidentally persist transient audit/provenance flag or environment overrides. Finally, the plan digest binds consent flags although InstallRequestV1 has no authorization field, so TUI checkbox, --allow-hooks, JSON request, and saved standing hook intent do not yet have one testable normalization boundary.

Exact correction: separate ConfigDocument (strict persisted YAML) from EffectiveConfig (CLI > env > file > defaults). The installer patches only ConfigDocument.Install. Specify ConfigPublishOutcome = unchanged | published | ambiguous and re-read/classify an exact candidate after any post-rename error; only confirmed publication may call the applier. Add one normalized PlanInput carrying proposed desired state and ephemeral hook authorization without serializing authorization as desired state. Freeze no-selector/non-TTY semantics. Use an injected filesystem and applier to cover every write/fsync/rename boundary, cancel-before-confirm, save failure with zero applier calls, published-config/apply-failure drift, CLI/env values not persisted, and one-field stale mutations of config, ledger, pending, direct destination, and external observation. Expected actions must be hand-authored, not captured from the production planner.

I2 — The external adapter recovery model leaves undefined outcomes and a shared-prerequisite uninstall hazard.
Section §9 does not distinguish a proven pre-spawn failure from a process that may have started, does not define the advertised forget-aborted disposition, and does not state fault behavior for external-record or external-ledger publication/cleanup. Codex skills and hooks are separate cells but may share one Aura marketplace registration; the proposal does not say whether that prerequisite is permanent, separately owned, or reference-counted, so install/remove order can invalidate the other cell.

Exact correction: publish a finite external transition table for NOT_STARTED, STARTED_UNKNOWN, OBSERVED_PRIOR, OBSERVED_DESIRED, and OBSERVED_OTHER across install/update/remove. Define exact eligibility and post-state for accept-observed, retry, and forget-aborted; make record/ledger writes use the same durable publication primitive and fault-test them. Give shared marketplace registration an explicit policy (for example, observe/add idempotently and never remove it automatically, or model separately with ownership). Test both Codex external cells in both install/remove orders. Drive a black-box fake CLI that records argv and independently changes observation state, including exec failure, bounded output, redaction, nonzero exit, hang/kill, postcondition mismatch, and process death; do not construct expected argv/postconditions from production adapter data.

I3 — Home Manager disable/rollback lacks the immutable executable and schema boundary required to implement or test it.
Current Aura hm-module.nix receives Pasture primarily as a source path, exposes no Pasture CLI package, and places all generated config behind mkIf cfg.enable. Proposal §10 requires an after-link pasture install hm-activate call and says cleanup is emitted on disable, but it does not bind an executable closure to the same catalog/intent, define behavior when cfg.enable becomes false or the module is later unimported, or define old-helper/new-ledger compatibility during rollback. An immutable intent alone is insufficient.

Exact correction: add a pinned Pasture package/helper option sourced from the same Pasture input; embed its Nix store executable path, intent schema, and catalog digest in each generation. Emit the cleanup/marker activation node even when enable=false while the module remains imported, and document that users must disable+activate before unimporting the module. Tamper one archive member, manifest path/mode/hash, base version, and Aura pin individually and require failure. After these contracts are added, the resulting suites remain finite: one explicit direct transition/failpoint table, one external transition table, one config publication table, a bounded Home Manager generation sequence, pinned conformance rows, and one black-box release matrix. A fresh review must find 0/0/0.

text:
VOTE: REVISE

Severity summary: 2 BLOCKER / 2 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR.

Normative baseline: FOLLOWUP_URD-2 (aura-plugins-iyd7j), Proposal 14, the cleaned research file, and current code seams only. I found no hidden inheritance from superseded Proposals 7-13.

BLOCKER 1 — The proposed catalog cannot represent its own direct-tree and dual-placement model without inference.

Where: Proposal 14 section 3.2 (ArtifactSpec, ResolvedArtifact, DeliveryUnit) versus sections 2, 3.3, and 8.

What/why: ArtifactSpec assigns one PackagePath directly to a payload, DeliveryUnit supplies only one DestinationRoot for a whole harness/component cell, and the direct reconciler commits one atomic ownership unit such as a skill directory. The model does not type (a) package-relative placement separately from destination-relative placement or (b) which files form one atomic direct ownership unit. The Codex agent bytes also have two placements: inert assets inside the skills plugin and standalone files under ~/.codex/agents. LogicalID and path-prefix inference are not an adequate placement/transaction contract. ResolvedArtifact.Bytes further makes the machine-readable catalog itself the payload store, duplicating/bloating the checked-in manifest instead of keeping catalog identity separate from the embedded archive. This contradicts UR3, which explicitly separates generated bytes, package membership, destination placement, and activation, and leaves section 8 unable to derive safe actions from typed data alone.

Smallest exact correction: split the contract into four explicit relations:
1. payload metadata/identity (artifact ID, logical owner, source, mode, digest, size; no serialized bytes);
2. package membership (package ID, artifact ID, package-relative path);
3. direct placement (cell ID, artifact ID, destination-relative path, atomic ownership-unit ID);
4. a validated tagged direct-versus-external delivery contract, so fields invalid for one strategy are not silently optional.
Keep exact bytes in a separately embedded deterministic payload archive keyed by artifact ID. State explicitly that a direct action is created per ownership-unit ID and never inferred from a filename or common prefix. Pin these relations in the independent catalog fixture.

BLOCKER 2 — Whole-profile authority is not race-free because Home Manager and the companion do not share an authority lock or marker ordering.

Where: sections 5, 6, and 10. The only defined lock is companion/lock; Home Manager has a separate external ledger. Section 10.1 says pre-link is zero-write validation, while section 10.2 says a generation writes an authority marker but does not define when, where, or under what shared exclusion.

What/why: A companion apply can pass its marker check and begin direct mutation while Home Manager independently validates and enters linkGeneration. On disable, a link-farm marker could disappear before external cleanup finishes, allowing companion mutation during the same activation. A persistent marker alone closes new starts only if it is published and removed under a lock both authorities obey. As written, Proposal 14 does not satisfy UR7: the two managers can concurrently mutate the same surface.

Smallest exact correction: add one profile-wide authority lock and activation-managed marker under the install state root; do not make the marker a home.file link. Companion apply must hold that authority lock for its complete mutation and recheck the marker under it. Home Manager enable/rollback-to-enabled must acquire the same lock, wait for companion mutation, verify zero companion ownership/pending state, and atomically publish the matching generation marker before linkGeneration. It may then release the lock because new companion applies reject the marker. Disable must retain the marker through direct-link removal and external-plugin cleanup, then remove it last under the shared lock. Amend the pre-link claim to “no artifact/harness mutation”; publishing the authority marker is required state mutation. Define actionable recovery for an activation that fails after marker publication.

IMPORTANT 1 — The Home Manager adapter boundary is not fully mapped to the current module.

Where: section 10 versus current Aura nix/hm-module.nix and flake.nix.

What/why: Current Home Manager has pasture.source, packages.enable, commands.extraCommands, agents.extraAgents, protocol.*, role filters, and the four legacy enable flags. Proposal 14 mentions only the enable flags and role filtering. It also invokes pasture install hm-activate without specifying the exact Pasture package in the activation closure. A local pasture.source override can therefore supply catalog/artifacts from one revision while an unspecified PATH binary or pinned input package applies another. Unmentioned extra/protocol/package options risk accidental deletion or collisions, violating the compatibility requirement and reintroducing hidden current-code assumptions.

Smallest exact correction: add a complete current-option disposition table. Keep extras/protocol/package behavior unchanged outside the generated matrix or deprecate each actionably; assert duplicate destinations between extras and catalog content. Add a typed pasture.package option/default for the exact store binary used by activation, invoke its absolute path, and bind its embedded catalog digest to the selected pasture.source catalog. If source is overridden without a matching package, allow direct links but make external cells unavailable with the exact correction.

IMPORTANT 2 — Section 14 calls horizontal layers “vertical slices” and centralizes cross-cutting tests in a collision-prone landing slice.

Where: section 14.

What/why: generation/catalog, configuration/planner, companion application, Home Manager/distribution, and conformance/landing are layer workstreams. The first three all feed the same Pasture command/dependency surface, while the last is expected to edit tests and release wiring owned by every earlier unit. Calling them vertical does not make them independently demonstrable or collision-safe, and a late conformance slice weakens the requirement that every implementation slice carry its own validation.

Smallest exact correction: rename these five items as architecture layers/integration contracts. Require Phase 8 to derive actual end-to-end slices with exclusive file/package ownership, dependency order, and slice-local tests. Contract/schema foundations can be prerequisite leaf tasks owned once; they are not parallel vertical slices. Keep only cross-repository smoke and final release parity in the landing slice.

Clean decisions retained:
- One versioned root config.yaml plus a separate XDG applied-state root is justified by the existing config path and UR4; a sibling install config would add another authority without user value.
- The desired config versus applied ledger split is clear and minimal.
- Home Manager direct links and companion direct reconciliation correctly remain separate mutation engines sharing catalog/selection semantics.
- Synchronous supported external CLIs with explicit ambiguous-result recovery are appropriately bounded; detached executable machinery is not needed.
- Whole-profile authority is a reasonable first-release proposal pending Plan-UAT confirmation once the shared exclusion protocol is complete.
- External/plugin cells and truthful Codex skill/agent/hook separation all trace to canonical requirements.

Required next action: revise only these four seams in a self-contained Proposal 15, then rerun all three review axes.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Severity: 1 BLOCKER / 8 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR.

The reset is substantially clearer and is self-contained with respect to Proposals 7-13, but the following correctness gaps remain.

## BLOCKER

### B1 — Post-crash external recovery can race the original harness command and can apply stale intent

Evidence: Section 9 writes the external record before spawn, then permits `recover ... retry` or `forget-aborted` after a Pasture process death based on a registry observation. A synchronous child does not necessarily die when its parent is killed; the original Claude/Codex CLI may still be running and may mutate the registry after the new observation. Adapter idempotence does not make two concurrent commands safe. The recovery contract also does not rebind the record to the current saved desired matrix/catalog before `accept-observed` or `retry`.

Impact: a retry/forget decision can race a late original command, commit a ledger that is immediately false, or reinstall a plugin that the user has since deselected. That violates UR6's requirement that an ambiguous third-party result is never guessed.

Exact correction: distinguish an in-process command completion from a post-controller-loss record. After controller loss, do not offer programmatic retry or forget based only on prior/desired observation. Require an adapter-specific, tested quiescence proof or route the cell to manual recovery with the exact process/CLI checks. Define `forget-aborted` only for a state that proves the spawn boundary was never crossed; otherwise remove it. Every recovery command must acquire the authority locks, reload the current config, catalog, external record, and observation, and refuse when the current desired identity differs. `accept-observed` may commit only the exact currently desired identity.

## IMPORTANT

### I1 — The config design does not separate the persisted document from the effective CLI/environment overlay

Evidence: Section 4 says the TUI loads the complete typed `Config` and preserves daemon/provenance values, while also retaining the existing CLI > environment > YAML > default resolver. Current `internal/config/viper.go` constructs only the effective `PasturedConfig` from all four tiers. The proposal does not define which representation the writer receives. If it receives the effective view, a temporary `PASTURE_AUDIT_*` value or daemon flag can be serialized into YAML during an installer update.

The publication contract also leaves the config-lock path and lock ownership API undefined: the writer takes the lock, while apply already takes the same lock before calling publication. Literal implementations can double-lock/deadlock. “Uses a mode-0700 parent” is unsafe for an explicit path whose existing parent is the user's home or another valid 0755 directory. Finally, the proposal promises an exact migration command for hybrid/unknown input, but no such public command exists in Section 7.

Impact: installer selection can silently change supported daemon settings, deadlock, chmod/reject a valid explicit path incorrectly, or emit a non-actionable migration error, contrary to UR4.

Exact correction: define separate APIs such as `LoadConfigDocument(path) -> raw document + digest` and `ResolveRuntimeConfig(document, flags, env) -> effective view`; only the raw document is updated and published. Define a canonical lock identity and a lock token/locked-writer API so apply acquires it once. Create a missing dedicated leaf directory as 0700 but never chmod arbitrary existing ancestors; validate their ownership/safety instead. Add the promised `pasture config migrate --config PATH` surface, or replace the promise with complete manual remediation and test it.

### I2 — The direct ledger/journal contract is not closed over its own crash states

Evidence: Sections 5 and 8 do not define versioned `Ledger`, `Pending`, and destination-identity schemas, although recovery depends on exact prior/desired identities and Section 8 later relies on the ledger recording parent directories Pasture created. The enumerated recovery shapes omit a first-install crash after stage-to-destination rename but before ledger publication: desired destination exists, prior ledger has no entry, and neither stage nor backup exists. The “equivalent” file replacement algorithm is also unspecified; if it renames directly over the old file, desired destination + prior ledger + no backup is another omitted shape.

Impact: an ordinary crash at a documented transaction boundary falls into manual recovery despite having an exact safe roll-forward, and implementors cannot independently agree on the durable schema or file algorithm.

Exact correction: include strict, versioned `LedgerV1`, `PendingV1`, `DestinationIdentity`, and external-record schemas with prior-exists/absent, created-parent ownership, stage/backup identities, action/cell IDs, digests, and state enum. Specify one file algorithm (prefer the same recorded backup exchange as trees) and enumerate create/update/uninstall recovery for every persisted phase, including desired destination + prior-absent ledger after publish. Corrupt/newer state must preserve evidence and return actionable manual recovery.

### I3 — Home Manager disable/rollback cannot reliably run the cleanup it promises, and the adapter executable is not bound to the catalog source

Evidence: Section 10 says disable/rollback removes external plugins and the marker, but an activation script guarded by module enablement is absent from the disabled generation. The current module places all configuration under `mkIf cfg.enable` (`nix/hm-module.nix:200`) and installs only Aura's `aura-swarm` package (`nix/hm-module.nix:236-240`), not a pinned `pasture` executable. The proposal names `pasture install hm-activate` without specifying its immutable Nix store executable. Existing `pasture.source` can also be overridden locally, so blindly using the flake input's binary can give the adapter a different embedded catalog from the linked files.

Impact: direct disable can strand an external plugin and authority marker, deadlocking companion activation; or Home Manager can execute an ambient/mismatched Pasture binary against another catalog.

Exact correction: either emit a safe tombstone cleanup activation even in the disabled generation, or require and enforce a two-generation transition (enabled with empty targets, verify zero external ledger/marker, then disable). Bind the activation command to an explicit `pasture.package` store path whose catalog digest is asserted equal to `pasture.source`; when a local source override lacks a matching package, external cells must be unavailable with an exact fix. Test direct disable, empty-matrix cleanup, rollback, local override, and unsupported system.

### I4 — Legacy Home Manager options cannot be translated correctly from final values alone

Evidence: Section 10 gives both the new matrix and old booleans nonempty/true defaults, then says disagreements are actionable. Nix must distinguish an explicit new declaration from defaults; otherwise a user who explicitly empties a Claude component conflicts with an old option merely because that old option defaulted true, while a legacy-only user can be mistaken for a new-matrix user.

Impact: existing configurations may fail evaluation or silently retain components the user disabled, violating UR7 compatibility/default requirements.

Exact correction: make the new matrix nullable/unset at the compatibility boundary and derive it from legacy values only when it is unset, or specify an equivalent definition-priority mechanism that can distinguish explicit declarations. When the new matrix is explicit, define exactly which explicit legacy declarations conflict, with role-filter projection and tests for defaults, legacy-only, new-only, agreement, and disagreement.

### I5 — External plugin ownership/adoption is undefined for a pre-existing exact plugin

Evidence: Section 6 says a selected unowned cell installs if conflict-free; Section 9 can observe an exact desired plugin and commit the ledger after a command. It never states what happens when the exact Claude/Codex plugin was already installed manually and there is no companion/HM ledger. Section 16 defers legacy adoption, and UR6 permits mutation/removal only for proven Pasture ownership.

Impact: an “already installed” exit/postcondition can silently adopt a foreign plugin and later authorize update/removal, or two authorities can claim the same registry identity.

Exact correction: specify that any observed external identity without the matching authority ledger is `FOREIGN_EXTERNAL_CONFLICT`, even when name/version/source match. Do not invoke add/update/remove or create ownership. Give exact manual uninstall/reinstall guidance. Any future import/adoption must be a separately consented UAT feature, not an exit-code shortcut.

### I6 — The claimed canonical release version owner does not exist in the current model

Evidence: Section 3 maps release version to “canonical Pasture release metadata” and Section 11 relies on one base semver, but the repository currently has `VERSION ?= dev` in `Makefile`, a separate hard-coded `0.1.0` in `flake.nix`, and no checked-in canonical version document. `pkg/protocol/README.md` explicitly says the Go API is currently unversioned.

Impact: plugin manifests, bundle/catalog, CLI version, Nix package, and Aura pins can each be internally valid while referring to different releases, defeating UR8 parity and downgrade decisions.

Exact correction: introduce and name one checked-in version authority (for example a small JSON/Go metadata file readable by Go and Nix), define development versus release values, and make Makefile ldflags, flake packages, catalog, both plugin manifests, bundle, and marketplace validation derive from or fail against it. Define the immutable catalog release identity as semver plus content digest/commit.

### I7 — Claude hooks have no concrete new marketplace/package transition

Evidence: the support table requires an external `pasture-hooks` Claude plugin, while Aura's current `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` exposes the monolithic `pasture` plugin. Section 11 merely says the Claude marketplace remains separate/current-compatible. It does not define the generated hooks-only Claude package path, its marketplace identity/source pin, or what happens to the old entry. Legacy adoption/removal is deferred, so the adapter cannot safely reinterpret the old `pasture` identity as hooks-only.

Impact: the supported Claude hooks cell has no installable immutable artifact, or an upgrade can unexpectedly replace a monolithic plugin with a hooks-only package.

Exact correction: define a distinct generated Claude hooks package and `pasture-hooks` marketplace entry with an immutable Pasture subdirectory pin. Keep the old `pasture` entry explicitly deprecated/pinned or remove it only through a user-confirmed migration; the adapter must target only the new identity. Add marketplace/install/update/remove observations for both coexistence and legacy conflict.

### I8 — The source/output prerequisite breaks the proposal's stated self-containment

Evidence: Section 11 says “Adopt aura-plugins-oj7we generation roots” and Section 14 names `GenerationRoots`, but Proposal 14 never defines that contract and it is not in current code. The referenced Bead is still open and only says to separate source and output roots.

Impact: the supervisor must reconstruct an external design decision to decide which reads use source, which writes use output, how `fs.FS`/paths are represented, and how generation tests invoke it. That contradicts Section 0's reset contract.

Exact correction: inline the minimal contract in Proposal 14, e.g. a typed `GenerationRoots{SourceRoot/SourceFS, OutputRoot}` passed through the one generator entrypoint, with all canonical/verbatim reads confined to Source and every generated artifact confined to Output. State repo defaults, release defaults, path-containment validation, and the migration/test boundary. Keep the Bead as audit/dependency evidence, not normative design.

## Exit decision

REVISE. Proposal 14 must resolve B1 and I1-I8, then receive a fresh fix-free correctness review. No repository edits were made.

Evidence: Section 11 says “Adopt aura-plugins-oj7we generation roots” and Section 14 names `GenerationRoots`, but Proposal 14 never defines that contract and it is not in current code. The referenced Bead is still open and only says to separate source and output roots.

Impact: the supervisor must reconstruct an external design decision to decide which reads use source, which writes use output, how `fs.FS`/paths are represented, and how generation tests invoke it. That contradicts Section 0's reset contract.

Exact correction: inline the minimal contract in Proposal 14, e.g. a typed `GenerationRoots{SourceRoot/SourceFS, OutputRoot}` passed through the one generator entrypoint, with all canonical/verbatim reads confined to Source and every generated artifact confined to Output. State repo defaults, release defaults, path-containment validation, and the migration/test boundary. Keep the Bead as audit/dependency evidence, not normative design.

## Exit decision

REVISE. Proposal 14 must resolve B1 and I1-I8, then receive a fresh fix-free correctness review. No repository edits were made.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
URE research response — native plugin registration surfaces

User question (verbatim):
What does each harness expose, such that the `pasture install` would be able to interact with each native plugin manager? Typically I would expect there to be some plugin registry file that is managed, and otherwise would simply be registering to that.

Current local CLI verification:
- Codex 0.144.1: `codex plugin marketplace add`, `codex plugin add PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE --json`, list, remove, and marketplace upgrade/remove.
- Claude Code 2.1.208: `claude plugin marketplace add`, install, update, enable, disable, uninstall, list, and validate.
- OpenCode 1.17.18: `opencode plugin MODULE --global`, documented by CLI as installing the npm plugin and updating config.

Primary-documentation findings:
- Codex marketplace catalogs live at repo `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` or personal `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`; installed plugin state is stored in `~/.codex/config.toml` and payloads are cached below `~/.codex/plugins/cache`. Codex plugins natively expose skills and hooks, but not native custom agents. Custom agents are standalone TOML files below `~/.codex/agents/` or project `.codex/agents/`.
- Claude Code marketplaces use `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; its native CLI owns marketplace registration and plugin install/update state. A Claude plugin can natively bundle skills, agents, and hooks.
- OpenCode has no equivalent marketplace catalog. Npm plugin package names are registered in the `plugin` array of `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; OpenCode/Bun installs them into its cache. Local JS/TS plugins are discovered from `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. Skills and agents are separate discovered files under `~/.config/opencode/skills/` and `~/.config/opencode/agents/`.

Architecture consequence:
`pasture install` should invoke the native CLI where one exists rather than edit internal plugin state. Because plugin installation is bundle-level while the user selects skills, agents, and hooks independently, marketplace/plugin packages must be split by independently selectable native component. Standalone surfaces remain ordinary generated-file installation:
- Claude Code: separate skills, agents, and hooks plugin entries.
- Codex: skills and hooks plugin entries; agents installed as standalone TOML.
- OpenCode: hooks as an npm/local JS plugin; skills and agents installed as standalone discovered files.
No Pasture receipt, ledger, ownership database, or parallel plugin registry is required.

URE decision — fail-fast application errors

Question shown:
Without a transaction model, should pasture install continue applying independent harness/extension actions after one fails, then exit nonzero with a per-action failure summary? The saved YAML would remain the desired selection, and rerunning the installer would retry normal idempotent install/uninstall commands.

User response (verbatim):

Captured decision:

- Return a nonzero exit with an informative, explanatory, actionable error identifying the harness, extension, operation, failure reason, caller impact, and remediation.
- Do not roll back actions that already succeeded.
- Do not persist an intermediate-action journal or recovery state.
- A later run uses ordinary idempotent native operations to apply the saved desired selection.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Severity: 1 BLOCKER / 5 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR

Scope: FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-15 against canonical FOLLOWUP_URE-2 and FOLLOWUP_URD-3 only, plus the live Pasture/Aura seams and installed native CLIs. No superseded installer-state machinery is required by this review.

BLOCKER

B1 — The proposed “missing executable while disabling is a no-op” test oracle can report a failed uninstall as success.
Proposal §6.1 says a missing harness executable is a no-op for ensure-absent. If a Pasture Claude/Codex/OpenCode plugin was installed and its CLI is later absent, the adapter cannot observe or remove it through the required native surface; returning nil leaves the extension active while the saved selection and result claim false. The same ambiguity exists in §7, which only makes a missing CLI fatal for enabled plugin cells. This directly contradicts URD-3 R4/R7 and BDD 5/8; a test that expects nil would certify the wrong product behavior.

Exact correction: remove the blanket no-op. Ensure-absent may return success without the executable only when absence is independently provable through a documented public observation that does not inspect a private cache. Otherwise it must stop with an actionable “cannot verify/remove” error; direct-file not-found remains a no-op. Apply the same rule to Home Manager. Add black-box cases with (a) exact plugin installed then executable hidden, which must fail and leave an honest result, (b) documented/proven absence, which may no-op, and (c) executable restored and rerun, which must remove idempotently. If the desired all-disabled first-run experience requires a different rule, revise the canonical behavior explicitly rather than silently equating “cannot execute removal” with “absent.”

IMPORTANT

I1 — Config tests do not yet prove default overlay, semantic preservation, or safe save-before-apply.
LoadInstallConfig only specifies defaults for a wholly missing file/section. A present partial section will decode omitted skills/agents booleans as false unless the loader overlays onto DefaultInstallConfig first or rejects partial input. “Round-trip and audit survives” also does not prove preservation of all supported root nodes, exact command path routing, or behavior when writing fails after the old file has been opened/truncated. The TUI plan omits the required assertion that a successful save remains saved when apply later fails, with no rollback.

Exact correction: define partial-section behavior (recommended: initialize defaults, then overlay explicit booleans) and duplicate/unknown-key behavior. Keep the raw persisted document separate from Viper’s effective CLI/env values so transient overrides are never serialized. Publish via a same-directory temporary file and rename—an ephemeral file-write detail, not a receipt, journal, transaction state, or recovery system. Add hand-authored YAML fixtures for no file, no install, every partially specified branch, explicit false, malformed/duplicate/unknown keys, audit_trail/audit_db_path/provenance plus unrelated supported nodes, and a nondefault command path. Inject read/write/rename failures and assert zero adapter calls plus preservation of the prior file. Assert cancel changes nothing, save success + second-action failure leaves the new preferences and first action intact, and the rerun preloads those preferences.

I2 — Separate mock-runner and manifest tests do not independently prove the real installer/native command wiring or fail-fast boundary.
Section 8 asserts native argv with injected runners and separately validates packages in isolated homes. Both can pass while the Cobra command selects the wrong adapter, wrong package ID/marketplace, wrong HOME/config root, or wrong install/remove sequence. The proposal also tests only the first adapter error, not partial failure inside a multi-command adapter such as marketplace-add followed by plugin-install. `$skill-creator` and `$plugin-creator` are interactive development aids, not reproducible repository test commands.

Exact correction: check in test-only, hand-authored native-contract fixtures for all nine cells: strategy, package/marketplace identity or standalone destination, exact add/list/remove argv, and observable postcondition. Production adapter constants must be compared to these fixtures, never used to generate expected values. Add a black-box built `pasture install` test in isolated HOME/XDG roots using local Claude/Codex marketplaces and a local OpenCode package: install, unchanged rerun, disable/uninstall, and public list/discovery checks. Inject a failure at every command boundary; prove the first prior subcommand/action remains, later actions are absent, the structured error contains harness/extension/operation/cause/impact/remedy, and a normal rerun completes without rollback state. For OpenCode’s CLI-less uninstall, use independent JSON/JSONC fixtures proving only the exact package string is removed while unrelated plugins/settings survive.

I3 — Source-free installation is BDD prose, not a concrete release test.
The validation list never builds the released pasture binary and denies it access to the repository while exercising embedded OpenCode skills/agents and Codex TOMLs. Generate-twice and checked-in drift can both pass even if `generated/embed.go`, command wiring, or runtime path resolution still reaches into the source checkout.

Exact correction: build the release-form binary, copy only that binary plus independently prepared native-CLI/local-marketplace fixtures into a fresh directory, run with an isolated HOME/XDG environment and repository-unrelated cwd, and install/status-by-public-observation/uninstall representative standalone and plugin-backed cells. Compare installed standalone trees, filenames, modes, and bytes to a hand-authored inventory/golden fixture rather than enumerating the production embed table. Run once with the source/output checkout made unavailable to the child process and require no cwd-dependent path in argv or errors.

I4 — Runtime-dialect and native-manifest completeness can remain self-referential.
A completeness test that iterates the production RuntimeSnippet registry, RoleSpec maps, or generated package list only proves internal agreement. A foreign-token denylist also cannot prove that every semantically required operation was converted. Likewise parsing TOML/YAML/JSON with Pasture-owned schemas does not prove Claude, OpenCode, or Codex accepts the artifacts.

Exact correction: add test-only fixtures that independently enumerate the expected role/command/support skill inventory, five agents, plugin components, and required runtime scenarios (skill invocation, user input, initial agent spawn, follow-up, message, wait, and instruction source) with expected/forbidden target-specific fragments for each harness. Mutation tests must fail when one item, marker, target mapping, or package member is removed or when a Claude operation leaks into OpenCode/Codex. Use reproducible native validators/loaders: `claude plugin validate` plus isolated install/list, Codex local marketplace add/list with standalone agent loader coverage, and OpenCode package/import/discovery checks. Pin the exercised CLI versions in the test evidence rather than calling an unspecified “current” binary.

I5 — Home Manager tests are parallel to, not an independent parity proof, and the hook-negative oracle is too weak.
Nix option evaluation and stub-command activation can each pass while Home Manager derives a different effective cell, source path, package ID, or remove action than `pasture install`. “No code path writes Git hooks” is not a behavioral oracle, and no proposed paired test proves hooks=false leaves every harness hook package absent while skills/agents remain present.

Exact correction: create one test-only nine-cell expected-surface fixture not consumed by production Go or Nix. Exercise all 64 installer boolean selections, then map representative/all equivalent selections into Home Manager and compare public plugin observations plus standalone bytes/links cell-by-cell.
