author: David Huu Pham
text:
INDEPENDENT AXIS B — TEST QUALITY / VALIDATABILITY REVIEW

Scope: PROPOSAL-7 aura-plugins-rrv7f, UAT aura-plugins-q5ams, URD aura-plugins-hznvh, PROPOSAL-6 aura-plugins-49fsf and its disposition, prior Axis-B reviews aura-plugins-s3gn3 and aura-plugins-ejxci, fixture tasks aura-plugins-9umx1/aura-plugins-noqor, AGENTS.md, current production-path tests, and tracker/engine race tests. Plan review is binary; no severity tree.

VOTE: REVISE

BLOCKER 1 — The receipt contract still exposes the superseded occurrence replay result.
Evidence: PROPOSAL-7 §0 (bd description lines 39-41) and §17 (lines 1205-1208) correctly require append-every/no RecordReplayed, but §3.2 still defines `ReceiptResult{Occurrence, Replayed bool}` (lines 168-188). Exact operation retry is a valid Provenance concern, but this public receipt result does not distinguish it from native-delivery replay, and the plan never says that the field is forbidden on the host-occurrence path. The current tests encode precisely the behavior UAT deleted: `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder_test.go:104-134`, `internal/lifecycle/lower_test.go:335-377`, and `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:231-255`.
Fix: remove `Replayed`/`RecordReplayed`/`ReplayKey` from occurrence and receipt contracts. Keep operation-id idempotency internal to Journal.Apply (or expose only the original occurrence ID with no occurrence-replay discriminator); explicitly mark `CommittedTransition.Replayed` as control-operation retry metadata if it remains. Add the connected black-box assertion that two separate identical host processes produce two occurrence IDs and no replay status, while retrying one exact operation returns its original ID.

BLOCKER 2 — Per-hook activation is not specified, so the fixture gate is either all-or-nothing or can falsely claim catalogue support.
Evidence: §14.1 requires an independent manifest and authentic fixtures before “broad” registration (lines 647-655), §14.1/§15.1 C make the process milestone an authentic all-30 gate (lines 1051-1054 and 1123-1128), but no enabled/withheld hook set, withheld reason, or per-(contract, host-version, event) activation rule is defined. The current resolver deliberately derives recordable events from its own registration list rather than the pinned catalogue (`internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go:115-133`, `227-240`), while the current catalogue coverage test derives synthetic payloads from the SUT (`internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend_test.go:495-529`). Without the missing contract, implementers must either register zero hooks until all 30 fixtures exist (no progressive user value) or register the pinned table without authentic evidence (false support).
Fix: define an independent manifest plus raw fixture metadata for each exact contract/version/event, and generate a disjoint enabled/withheld report. A hook may be emitted only when its independent fixture and its real registration -> built binary/stdin -> T1 reader proof pass; no fixture means no registration, with a visible machine-readable/human-readable withheld reason. Add a non-vacuity test proving enabled ∪ withheld is exactly the independent 30-event manifest and no enabled event lacks its authentic fixture. Race the fixed-actor/manifest activation across separate processes as part of this gate.

BLOCKER 3 — The public bounded-reader contract is too incomplete to make the required black-box assertions non-substitutable.
Evidence: §7 only declares `PageRequest`, `LineageBounds`, and methods returning undefined `*Query`/`*Page` types (lines 597-622). It specifies neither page contents, next-cursor/has-more/truncation semantics, snapshot validation, nor zero/>maximum behavior. It also exposes no bounded reader for definitions, capability/phase state, or commits, although §4.3 and §14.3 require exact version propagation through those records and §14.1 #3 requires reading the committed phase (lines 294-308, 1035-1049, 1076-1086). Existing tests fall back to direct SQL/projection reads (`cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:132-195`, `internal/engine/control_test.go:112-124`, `internal/engine/projection.go:84-124`), so leaving this open permits a green implementation that never exercises the public path.
Fix: freeze the public page/query/result types, including snapshot token, exclusive continuation cursor, deterministic order, `HasMore`/next cursor, truncation reason, and typed errors for zero, over-limit, forged-future, stale/mismatched cursor, and snapshot mutations. Add bounded phase/commit/capability/definition reads (or explicitly route those assertions through a documented bounded `Journal().Facts()` API). Make the named M2/M3/M6 tests external black-box tests that use only those readers and fail if direct SQL or a test-only export is substituted.

IMPORTANT 1 — Retention/tombstone tests are deferred in prose rather than parameterized by the still-open UAT choice, and some bound edge semantics remain unnamed.
Evidence: §13 says a later content policy supplies its own tombstone matrix (lines 1028-1031), §14.3 repeats that it supplies the matrix later (lines 1091-1093), and §16 leaves retention choices open (lines 1189-1201). §5.3 names maxima (lines 416-433) but does not define invalid-zero/over-limit behavior for every public page/lineage bound. This is the unresolved part of prior B-mini Important 4.
Fix: make the canary corpus take a selected `RetentionMode`: metadata-only proves no raw object exists/no resurrection is possible; encrypted or external modes each provide explicit deletion, tombstone, permitted-metadata, replay, and no-resurrection cases. Freeze named bound constants and constructor/reader outcomes for zero and values above each maximum, then assert stable snapshot pagination at every boundary.

IMPORTANT 2 — Positive human-to-code lineage is not a named executable production-path proof.
Evidence: §14.3 names fan-out/cycle/cursor tests and path-only confidence cases (lines 1084-1095), and §17 gives the path-only negative (lines 1227-1229), but no named test creates an explicit human-signal -> turn/tool -> selected enrichment -> artifact/commit chain and queries it forward and backward. The current spine only reads legacy observation/session rows (`cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:132-195`), and lowering tests use a fake recorder (`internal/lifecycle/lower_test.go:304-333`).
Fix: add an M3 black-box fixture with explicit `PromptedBy`/`ExecutedTool`/`ProducedArtifact` (or the finalized typed link records), query human-to-code and code-to-human through the bounded reader, and separately test missing/contradictory enrichment returning ObservedPath plus the causal gap. Assert timestamp/session proximity never creates the link.

PRIOR AXIS-B MINI FINDINGS
- Prior blocker 1 (connected T1 -> T2/T3 production path): CLOSED in the proposal text by §14.1 named `TestClaudeGeneratedLifecycleToInterpretationReader` and `TestHookCandidateToEpochControl` (lines 1035-1049), plus the M2/M6 essential gates (§14.4, lines 1099-1107). The reader contract gap above is a new blocker about making that assertion non-substitutable.
- Prior blocker 2 (authority expiry/revocation/scope/retry/race/no partial writes): CLOSED by §14.2 (lines 1056-1074), which enumerates independent handles/processes, all scope axes, expiry, revoke-before/during commit, exact retry ordering, changed-input conflict, fresh-operation semantics, and delta snapshots.
- Prior Important 1 (invalid-delivery matrix): CLOSED by §5.4 (lines 440-454), which gives append/no-append and T2/T3/context outcomes for malformed, duplicate, UTF-8, truncation, over-limit, unsupported schema, mismatch, unknown payload-only event, and store failure; §14.1/14.2 place it on the process/file-backed path.
- Prior Important 2 (exact version propagation): CLOSED by §14.3 (lines 1076-1083), requiring two definitions/builds, every dependent output, modified-definition rejection, same-VCS/different-build, dirty, missing, and unresolved/no-control behavior.
- Prior Important 3 (disclosure negatives): CLOSED by §14.3 (lines 1087-1090), covering candidate-only, wrong recipient/scope, stale phase, expired/revoked capability, unauthorized acknowledgement, failed send, suppression/revocation, and immutable history.
- Prior Important 4 (privacy/tombstones/bounds): OPEN/PARTIAL; numeric values are now named in §5.3, but tombstone behavior is still “later policy supplies its matrix” and not a parameterized test contract (§13/§14.3); see Important 1 above.
- Prior Important 5 (large graph and milestone gates): CLOSED by §14.3 fan-out/cycle/cursor/snapshot/node/edge cases and §14.4’s essential/deferred table (lines 1097-1108).
- Prior Important 6 (generated-artifact negative guard): CLOSED by §12’s mechanical-only artifact boundary and compile/regeneration/subprocess guards (lines 993-1009), §14.3 mutation tests, and §15.4 replacement/deletion dispositions.

MINOR
None.

CHECKS RUN / SKIPPED
- Read full available UAT/URD/proposal/disposition/review/fixture task records, AGENTS.md, current lifecycle/codegen/handler/recorder/spine tests, and tracker/engine race/control/projection tests.
- PASS: `nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/codegen/...`.
- PASS: `nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/handlers/... ./internal/tasks/...`.
- PASS: `nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine/...`. These are current tests and intentionally pass the superseded digest/pre-parse/no-store/non-zero-refusal/direct-projection behavior; they are not acceptance evidence for PROPOSAL-7.
- Skipped full repository/Nix/build gates because this is a design-only review of an unratified proposal. No source, proposal fields, dependencies, commits, or pushes were changed.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
# PROPOSAL-7 mirrored review finding disposition

This comment dispositions every finding in the fresh mirrored review wave before
PROPOSAL-8 is created. `ACCEPT` adopts the finding and proposed outcome as
written. `MODIFY` adopts the required outcome while tightening or replacing the
suggested mechanism. `REJECT` would decline a finding; no finding is rejected.
Votes remain historical and do not transfer to PROPOSAL-8.

## Axis A general - aura-plugins-1pfty - VOTE: REVISE

1. **MODIFY - transaction-local capability expiry.** Adopt the preferred
   minimal upstream Provenance primitive rather than defer expiry. Add one closed
   `ConditionTransactionTimeBefore` arm to the pinned condition algebra. It is
   canonical operation input and is evaluated after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` acquires
   the write lock and after exact-operation replay lookup, but before any effect.
   The authoritative source is SQLite UTC Unix milliseconds; `now < deadline`
   passes and `now >= deadline` returns typed `ConditionTimeExpired` with zero
   writes. The same Apply also checks current Bound capability and current phase,
   then writes Consumed plus control effects. An upstream lock-spanning test must
   prove that a contender queued before the deadline but admitted after it loses,
   while an already committed exact retry still returns its original result.
2. **ACCEPT - immutable context-policy and build definitions.** Every policy,
   runtime, codebook, schema, interpreter, and build reference gains an immutable
   definition JournalID plus content identity. A disclosure plan identifies the
   exact policy/build definitions; later attempt/result facts cite the plan. Two
   policy versions over the same committed inputs remain independently
   resolvable, with no implicit latest selection.

## Axis A mini - aura-plugins-b9qkt - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - remove occurrence replay from the public model.** Delete
   `ReceiptResult.Replayed`, `RecordReplayed`, `ReplayKey`, payload-digest
   occurrence identity, and all occurrence-level replay/dedup vocabulary. A
   receipt exposes only the new occurrence identity, which is a typed view of
   its produced evidence JournalID. Exact operation idempotency remains internal
   to Provenance and never classifies a host delivery.
2. **MODIFY - expiry boundary.** Same disposition as Axis A general finding 1:
   add the closed transaction-time condition and database-time evaluator rather
   than perform a pre-Apply clock check or defer expiry.
3. **ACCEPT - canonical T2/context/reader contracts.** Define one immutable
   post-T1 `OccurrenceRecord`, complete interpretation/enrichment inputs and
   outputs, exact result-slot mapping, immutable policy/build definitions,
   complete disclosure plan/attempt/result correlation, and concrete bounded
   page/cursor/query/error contracts for all record families.
4. **ACCEPT - progressive activation.** Registration is gated independently per
   exact contract/event by an authentic fixture and real generated-hook to
   binary to journal to public-reader proof. Enabled and withheld entries form a
   complete disjoint activation manifest; all-30 remains a separate catalogue
   completeness milestone.
5. **ACCEPT - hard replay-prototype guard.** Delete or invert all prototype
   replay tests and symbols. A focused static source guard rejects
   `ReplayKey`, `RecordReplayed`, lifecycle receipt `Replayed`, and payload
   digest use as occurrence identity.
6. **ACCEPT - M4/M5/M6 ownership.** Add exact file owners, tests, migrations,
   integration points, and L1/L2/L3 leaves for context, response, upstream
   Provenance expiry, and control cutover.
7. **ACCEPT - exact definition resolver.** Add one bounded resolver/activation
   service for active and historical immutable definition JournalIDs. Retirement
   prevents new activation but never removes historical resolution.

## Axis B general - aura-plugins-xwiuk - VOTE: ACCEPT

1. **ACCEPT - vote and test strategy.** Preserve the independent exact-version
   host oracle; generated-registration to built binary/stdin to file-backed T1,
   T2, T3 and public-reader paths; append/invalid/version/authority/context/
   privacy/bounds/compiler/projection matrices; one journal; one FSM; and
   explicit old-test inversion.
2. **ACCEPT - progressive subset guardrail.** Support claims and generated
   registration advertise only independently fixture-backed enabled events.
   Enabled events cannot borrow proof from the catalogue or from another event.
3. **ACCEPT - concurrency guardrail.** Receipt and authority races use separate
   processes or independently opened handles against one file, never only
   goroutines sharing a tracker.
4. **ACCEPT - concrete M3 chain guardrail.** The named black-box proof is an
   actual Pasture-issued human signal -> host binding -> agent tool call ->
   selected VCS/tool/worktree enrichment -> artifact/commit chain queried both
   forward and reverse, plus missing and contradictory enrichment cases.

## Axis B mini - aura-plugins-0gvfe - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - no receipt replay discriminator.** Same as A-mini finding 1. Two
   separate byte-identical CLI invocations create distinct operation IDs,
   evidence JournalIDs, and occurrence IDs. A retry of one exact internal Apply
   returns its original journal result without a delivery-facing status.
2. **ACCEPT - per-event activation contract.** Same as A-mini finding 4. The
   independent expected 30-event manifest is a completeness oracle; the
   enabled/withheld activation manifest is separate and names typed reasons.
3. **ACCEPT - complete bounded reader.** Freeze opaque cursor encoding,
   snapshot and query-fingerprint checks, deterministic JournalID ordering,
   concrete pages, truncation reasons, lineage depth/node/edge limits, and typed
   invalid-size/mismatch/stale/tamper failures. Production acceptance tests may
   use only public readers, never direct SQL or projection internals.
4. **MODIFY - UAT-parameterized retention matrix.** Do not select an interim
   privacy mode. Specify blocking matrices now for metadata-only, encrypted
   local content, and external content-addressed content. The later UAT choice
   selects which complete matrix must pass before activation.
5. **ACCEPT - positive human-to-code proof.** Add the exact M3 production path
   preserved by the B-general guardrail, including forward/reverse reads and
   ObservedPath-only behavior when enrichment is missing or contradictory.

## Axis C general - aura-plugins-avkc0 - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - event-granular activation.** Verified events may deliver M1 value
   independently; missing fixtures visibly withhold only their own events.
   All-30 gates only the complete-catalogue claim.
2. **ACCEPT - one occurrence and complete disclosure write contract.** Private
   transport capture is not a second public occurrence. T2 consumes only the
   immutable `OccurrenceRecord`. Context policy evaluation is pure; plan,
   delivery attempt, delivered/acknowledged/failed/revoked/suppressed results
   are separate immutable operations with exact plan/attempt/operation/version
   correlation and injected clock ownership.
3. **ACCEPT - exclusive ownership.** Remove `R/C`, name every generated,
   migration, projection, wiring, test, prototype, and upstream file owner, and
   permit a wiring-file transfer only after the previous owner has merged and
   closed. No concurrent slice owns the same path.
4. **ACCEPT - remove lifecycle `Replayed`.** Operation retry remains an internal
   Journal behavior; lifecycle and control result models expose stable IDs only.
5. **MODIFY - latency budget.** Preserve the 12-second command and 15-second host
   ceilings, and require a measured per-enabled-event production-path budget
   before activation. The exact normal-operation SLO is fixture-derived and is
   not guessed in the proposal.
6. **ACCEPT - bounded Enricher only.** Keep one pure bounded enrichment seam; do
   not add a plugin registry or runtime-authored codebook DSL.
7. **ACCEPT - separate future owners.** Context, response, Provenance deadline,
   and control cutover are distinct slices; the engine/audit cutover is not an
   unnamed horizontal assignment.

## Axis C mini - aura-plugins-q85i6 - VOTE: REVISE

1. **ACCEPT - progressive activation.** Same as C-general finding 1.
2. **ACCEPT - canonical occurrence and context identity inputs.** Same as
   C-general finding 2, with complete T2 draft/enrichment/result types and no
   undefined names.
3. **ACCEPT - retire replay vocabulary.** Same as A-mini finding 1; no public
   lifecycle or control result has `Replayed` or an equivalent delivery flag.
4. **ACCEPT - exact historical definition service.** Same as A-mini finding 7.
5. **ACCEPT - M4/M5/M6 worker readiness.** Same as A-mini finding 6.
6. **ACCEPT - no second host descriptor table.** The private hostcontract
   descriptor is the sole typed event/name/field/identity/blocking/mutation/
   failure/stop source. It generates frontend payload descriptors and the
   registration candidate manifest. Runtime, frontend, and codegen consume only
   generated derivatives. Clean regeneration and a focused dependency/source
   ownership test reject another descriptor or event map outside the owner.
7. **ACCEPT - deep defensive copies.** Constructors reject zero/over-limit
   values; every nested collection is copied on construction and return,
   including phase transition slices and cursors.
8. **ACCEPT - opaque raw content.** `json.RawMessage` remains inside private
   envelope/retention codecs. Target-neutral occurrence, interpretation,
   context, and reader APIs expose only typed metadata and `EvidencePayloadRef`.
9. **ACCEPT - neutral response until UAT.** Keep only the mechanically encoded
   neutral result active. Delivery/ack channel and future verdict/process-health
   encoding remain explicit open UAT decisions.

## Preserved closed PROPOSAL-7 work

PROPOSAL-8 must not reopen the verified corrected 30-hook audit, one
Journal/Apply substrate, journal-native causal evidence, one immutable FSM and
cutover direction, fixed T1 actor/authority/operation/result path, versioned
envelope, compiler package boundary, malformed matrix, essential/deferred test
split, resource budgets, Claude 2.1.210 Elicitation safety boundary, or
prototype quarantine direction. The revision is limited to the accepted and
modified seams above.

author: David Huu Pham
text: Classification: (a) test-quality defect, not a production data race. Evidence: the reproduced full-tree race failure was TestSliceQueue_BackpressureAllEventuallyComplete reporting slice bp-03 missed SliceSubWorkflow's intentional 2s start-signal deadline (internal/engine/slice.go:65-76). The test launched 30 concurrent spin-polling signal senders (previous internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go:560-571); sendMockStartSignal retries SQLite-backed dbos.Send every 10ms (internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go:1346-1358 after this change). Under full-tree CPU/SQLite contention, one sender was starved past the workflow deadline even though its own helper allowed 90s. The engine package passed 5/5 isolation runs before the fix and the focused backpressure test passed count=3 at -cpu=1,2,4, supporting load-sensitive test scheduling rather than a race report. No Go race detector finding, SQLite lock error, DBOS queue starvation, or production-code failure was observed. SQLite/DBOS architecture finding: 30 test goroutines repeatedly writing the same DBOS SQLite notification store create avoidable contention and can delay delivery beyond a separate workflow deadline; pending shared-SQLite work should avoid retry storms and should monitor/serialize high-fanout writers where ordering does not require concurrent delivery. Change: internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go now sends mock start signals serially in both bounded-concurrency and 30-slice backpressure tests; queue execution remains concurrent, which is the behavior those tests assert. Proof: post-fix internal/engine race package 10/10 green; full-tree CGO race suite 5/5 green. Gates passed: gofmt -l . (empty), go vet ./..., CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./..., nix flake check --no-build, git diff --check. Commit 3cc3ca7 pushed. Files changed: internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go only. Blockers: none. Task intentionally left open for supervisor/review.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ARCHITECT DISPOSITION: (a) classification ACCEPTED, fix accepted, commit 3cc3ca7.

The evidence supports it: no race-detector finding, no SQLite lock error, no production-code failure, and the 30 concurrent spin-polling senders retrying dbos.Send every 10ms are test scaffolding rather than a shape any real caller produces. Signal-delivery concurrency was never the backpressure invariant under test, so serializing it removes contention noise without weakening the assertion. Isolation runs passing 5/5 before the fix and -cpu=1,2,4 passing after both point at load-sensitive scheduling. Ten engine runs and five full-tree runs is adequate proof for an intermittent failure.

Credit for recording the contention finding rather than quietly enlarging a timeout. That is the distinction the task asked for and it was respected.

HOWEVER - the fix closes the flake and leaves a production characteristic uncovered, which I am filing separately rather than letting it disappear into a green suite.

The deadline that expired is PRODUCTION code, not test code: internal/engine/slice.go:65 sets a 2s start-signal window, and on timeout SliceSubWorkflow returns an honest failure - 'the slice was enqueued but never started'. So the observed behaviour was a real production deadline being missed because writes to the DBOS SQLite notification store were contended. The test was provoking that, accidentally. Nothing provokes it now.

That is load-bearing for the architecture currently being planned. The lifecycle pivot will write to the SAME shared SQLite file on every tool call, and under multi-agent orchestration with subagents the fanout is genuinely high - which is exactly the condition that just starved this deadline. The pivot can therefore reintroduce this in production, where it manifests as spurious slice failures, with no test covering it.

PROPOSAL-8 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 1/2

## 12. Malformed ingress, retention boundary, and response

### 12.1 Invalid-delivery matrix

| Input | T1 | T2/T3/context | Process result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled generated registration gives known contract/event; malformed, duplicate, invalid UTF-8, truncated, or over-limit bytes | one bounded occurrence with exact capture disposition | none | neutral exit 0; redacted diagnostic if needed |
| Enabled known registration with unsupported schema | one `CaptureUnsupportedSchema` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Enabled registration and payload event mismatch | one `CaptureEventMismatch` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Withheld or unregistered event | no store open, no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; support report gives typed reason |
| Payload-only unknown event without trusted registration coordinate | no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; stderr explicitly says no receipt |
| Store/definition activation/T1 Apply failure | no false receipt claim | none | neutral exit 0; actionable redacted storage diagnostic |
| T1 succeeds and T2 fails | receipt remains | no partial T2/T3/context | neutral exit 0; internal diagnostic cites occurrence safely |

Host stdout contains only the mechanical native response. It never exposes
JournalID, rowid, ActivityID, database path, raw prompt/tool/transcript data, or
retention keys.

### 12.2 Response boundary

Target-independent interpretation cannot import host response internals.
Generated scripts register and forward only. M1-M4 expose only one mechanical
neutral response. `Stop` and `SubagentStop` are captured before the loop guard;
active loop state produces a suppressed fact and no recursive consultation.

Future allow/deny/ask/defer verdict and process-health encoding remains open UAT.
Generic CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny. A deliberate gate cannot
activate until its exact host fixture and future response UAT pass.

## 13. Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit: exactly 30 events

The source facts below are unchanged from the verified PROPOSAL-7 audit. The
private hostcontract becomes their sole production source; the independent
fixture manifest verifies them. All events require the common `session_id` and
may admit common `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`,
`hook_event_name`, `effort`, `agent_id`, and `agent_type` only where the pinned
descriptor allows. Common presence is not semantic identity.

Behavior abbreviations:

- `OBS`: nonblocking, no mutation, report-and-continue, no reconciliation.
- `GATE`: blocking, no mutation unless stated, exit-2-would-block,
  host-native reconciliation.
- `COND`: conditionally blocking; `config_source=policy_settings` is the pinned
  nonblocking matcher.
- `STOP`: blocking gate consulted only while `stop_hook_active=false`.
- `HUMAN`: blocking explicit-human-response classification, `MutationNone`.

The behavior column describes host capability, not Pasture authority. Only an
Enabled activation is registered; every audit row remains in the independent
catalogue whether Enabled or Withheld.

| # | Event; exact event-specific fields; identity additions; behavior | T2 evidence/candidate and bidirectional use |
|---:|---|---|

Candidate gate/tool policy; event alone has no control authority. M4 may supply tool context; future M5 may encode a typed gate response. |

The pin cannot prove original/effective values or an overrider. It remains evidence/candidate only and cannot commit a human decision for this contract. |

Completeness requires rows 1-30 exactly once and in this order. Activation is
orthogonal: a Withheld row remains part of catalogue truth but is absent from
host registration.

## 14. Retention and tombstone matrix, parameterized by UAT

This proposal does not select a retention mode. The selected mode becomes a
blocking UAT output and its entire matrix must pass before any event carrying
that capture class becomes Enabled.

| Mode | Required blocking tests |
|---|---|
| Metadata only | Raw prompt/tool/transcript/path/elicitation bytes never appear in journal, projections, readers, logs, stderr, temporary files, or replay. Missing policy-required content emits typed `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect. |
| Encrypted local payload | Keys are never journaled/logged; missing/wrong key fails closed; ciphertext is bounded and authenticated; deletion appends a tombstone and removes key/object according to policy; readers return tombstoned/missing without plaintext leakage; replay and projection rebuild cannot resurrect deleted content; key rotation preserves permitted refs and history. |
| External content-addressed payload | Store and object refs are typed and bounded; content identity verifies fetched bytes; missing/deleted object returns typed unresolved/tombstoned state; deletion appends a tombstone; journal/projection replay cannot re-upload or resurrect; logs/queries expose no content or credentials. |

All modes preserve occurrence identity, runtime/version envelope, policy-
permitted native binding metadata, causal links, disclosure history, capability
history, and commits. Tombstones never erase the fact that content existed or
rewrite prior JournalIDs. Raw JSON remains behind private retention-policy
accessors and never enters `OccurrenceRecord` or another target-neutral type.

## 15. Named production-path proofs and validation

### 15.1 Required black-box tests

1. `TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceReader`: for each Enabled event, generate
   the actual registration, invoke the built command with the authentic raw
   fixture against one file-backed database, and read `OccurrenceRecord` only
   through `LifecycleReader`. Two byte-identical process invocations yield two
   operation IDs and two occurrence JournalIDs with no replay field.
2. `TestWithheldClaudeEventIsNotRegistered`: every Withheld event is absent from
   host registration and present in the support report with the exact typed
   reason. Enabled union Withheld equals the independent 30-event oracle.
3. `TestClaudeLifecycleToInterpretationReader`: the same generated/binary path
   reaches T1, T2, exact definitions, stable slots, and public fact/link/
   candidate/unresolved pages. Direct interpreter/Apply tests cannot substitute.
4. `TestHumanSignalToCommitLineageBlackBox`: a Pasture-issued human signal is
   bound to the host session/request, followed by an agent tool call, selected
   VCS/tool/worktree enrichment, artifact and commit evidence, then queried
   human-to-code and code-to-human through the bounded reader. Missing and
   contradictory enrichment remain `ObservedPath` plus typed unresolved facts;
   no timestamp/session proximity promotes confidence.
5. `TestDisclosurePlanAttemptResultReader`: committed state enters the pure
   projector, then separate plan/attempt/result operations are read publicly;
   candidate/stale/wrong-recipient/unauthorized/unknown-policy cases write
   nothing and projection rebuild is identical.
6. `TestHookCandidateToEpochControl`: a real enabled hook produces a candidate;
   production services issue/bind capability and T3 commits through one FSM,
   then public capability/commit readers return the result. No direct projection
   writer or test-only export counts.
7. `TestTransactionTimeBeforeLockSpanningExpiry`: upstream Provenance holds the
   SQLite writer across the deadline; a fresh queued operation loses after lock
   acquisition with typed expiry and zero writes; an exact committed retry still
   returns its original result.

### 15.2 Definition, reader, privacy, and race matrices

- Activate two codebooks, interpreters, builds, and context policies over the
  same source facts; every dependent record resolves its exact definition
  JournalIDs and never silently selects latest.
- Retire a definition and prove historical resolution still works while new
  active resolution does not choose it.
- Test malformed/tampered/mismatched/future/stale cursors, zero/over-limit page
  and lineage bounds, stable snapshots, no duplicate/skip, continuation,
  explicit cycles, node/edge/depth truncation, and defensive copies.
- Race separate processes or independent handles on fixed actor activation,
  definition activation, distinct receipts, revocation versus consume, two
  consumers of one capability, and two capabilities for one current phase.
- Snapshot journal/capability/phase/decision/context/projection deltas before
  every losing operation and assert zero partial semantic writes.
- Parameterize privacy canaries by the UAT-selected retention mode and run them
  through generated process, journal, readers, logs, stderr, tombstone, and
  replay paths.
- Delete lifecycle/phase/lineage/disclosure projections and rebuild identical
  public results from the journal.

### 15.3 Static and generation guards

- Focused source guard rejects `ReplayKey`, `RecordReplayed`, lifecycle result
  `Replayed`, occurrence dedup/window/count code, and payload digest use as an
  occurrence key.
- Host descriptor ownership/dependency test rejects a second event/field/
  behavior table outside hostcontract and generated derivatives.
- Compile-fail imports prove model/codebook/lowering/context/control cannot
  import private host response/descriptor packages.
- Clean regeneration rejects drift or retired generated assets.
- Subprocess mutation proves argv/env cannot select semantics or authority and
  generic internal errors cannot produce deny.
- Phase parity proves runtime and generated surfaces derive from one immutable
  phase law.

All Go test commands use `-race`; no duplicate non-race wave counts. Commit
gates remain gofmt, go vet, race tests, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build`, Nix checks,
clean generation drift, and `git diff --check`.

| S6-RESPONSE | typed native response and process-health contract selected by UAT | exact host response fixtures, neutral/fault/deny isolation, timeout budget | mechanical encoder/service and handler wiring |
| S7-PROVENANCE-DEADLINE | closed time condition, canonical fields, typed expiry failure, private transaction-time source | canonical round trip/conflict, DBOS parity, equality boundary, fake-clock unit cases, lock-spanning race | transaction evaluator after replay/lock, public aliases, Pasture dependency pin |
| S8-CONTROL-CUTOVER | capability scope/state, commit input/result, phase evidence | issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix, independent-process races, exact retry/conflict, old-writer rejection, projection replay | control service, capability consumption + phase CAS, engine/handler/audit cutover |

### 17.4 Dependencies and merge timing

| Integration point | Exporter | Consumers | Merge gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| IP-0 immutable phase law | S0 | S3, S5, S8 | S0 L3 before candidate/context/control tests |
| IP-1 occurrence/definition/envelope/reader contracts | S1 | S2-S8 | S1 L1 before consumer L1; S1 L3 before enabled registration |
| IP-2 fixed actor, T1 appender, public occurrence reader | S1 | S2 | S1 L3 before first Enabled event |
| IP-3 hostcontract generated descriptors + activation manifest | S2 | codegen, S3, S6 | per-event fixture proof before that event becomes Enabled |
| IP-4 T2 result algebra and exact definitions | S3 | S4, S5, S8 | S3 L3 before lineage/context/control |
| IP-5 bounded explicit lineage | S4 | S5, S8, user queries | S4 L3 before lineage-dependent context/control rules |
| IP-6 disclosure plan/attempt/result contract | S5 | S6 and readers | UAT channel/ack and S5 L3 |
| IP-7 transaction-time condition | S7 | S8 | reviewed upstream release and Pasture pin before S8 L3 |
| IP-8 capability/phase control cutover | S8 | engine/handlers | S0, S3, S4, S7 merged; one cutover, no dual writer |

S0 and S7 may proceed in parallel with other prerequisite work after
ratification. S2 events activate independently as their fixture/run refs pass.
S3 waits for at least one Enabled T1 vertical, not all 30. Catalogue completion
continues independently and blocks only the complete-catalogue claim.

### 17.5 Prototype quarantine and exact disposition

The six stopped untracked files remain quarantined and cannot be committed as-is:

| Untracked file | Exclusive owner | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go` | S2, then conditional sequential transfer | rewrite as typed process composition; fresh delivery operation; no semantic selection |
| `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go` | S2 | rewrite as per-enabled authentic generated/binary/T1/public-reader proof |
| `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` | S2, then conditional sequential transfer | rewrite receipt-first; optional typed stages; mechanical response only |
| `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_test.go` | S2 | invert parse-before-store and nonzero-refusal assertions |
| `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go` | S1 | delete; replace with journal-native receipt package; no audit/activity direct writes |
| `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder_test.go` | S1 | delete; replace with result-slot, independent-process append tests |

Committed prototype disposition is also exclusive:

| Existing path | Owner | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/lifecycle/event.go`, `event_test.go` | S1 | replace with canonical model; remove digest and one-semantic event |
| `internal/lifecycle/key.go`, `key_test.go` | S1 | delete; static guard prevents replacement replay key |
| `internal/lifecycle/frontend.go`, `frontend_test.go`, `fixtures_test.go`, `verifier_internal_test.go` | S2 | replace with private capture and independent activation fixtures |
| `internal/lifecycle/backend.go`, `backend_test.go` | S2 | delete same-package host behavior side door |
| `internal/lifecycle/claude/**` | S2 | move/rewrite under ingress from generated descriptor; no duplicate table |
| `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, `lower_test.go`, `lower_internal_test.go` | S3 | replace with pure T2 canonicalization/effect mapping |
| `internal/runtime/lifecycle.go`, `lifecycle_profiles.go`, `lookup.go` | S2 | replace manual host behavior tables with generated derivatives/facade |
| `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go` and generated Claude hook assets | S2 | registration/support only; no parsing/semantics/authority |
| generated `pasture-lifecycle.py` and hidden env-selected lifecycle adapter path | S2 | delete when first replacement event is Enabled; no dual semantic path |
| `internal/engine/{control,workflow,projection,activities}.go` and direct transition audit writers | S8 | route through journal-backed control; projections/operational evidence only |

## 18. Open Plan UAT decisions

No option below is selected here. The open UAT records the final choice and
updates the URD before ratification and slicing.

### 18.1 Retention mode

- Metadata only: lowest privacy/operations cost, but unavailable content remains
  explicitly unresolved.
- Encrypted local payload: richer local reconstruction, but requires key,
  deletion, rotation, tombstone, and no-resurrection guarantees.
- External content-addressed payload: durable/shared evidence, but adds store,
  credential, availability, deletion, and privacy obligations.

### 18.2 First activated high-value hooks

UAT receives the current activation readiness report and may select only events
whose authentic exact-version fixture and production path already pass. Candidate
value groupings are session spine, human-signal ingress, tool/artifact lineage,
or multi-agent orchestration. No grouping overrides per-event proof, and this
proposal does not preselect an event.

### 18.3 Context delivery and acknowledgement

Delivery alternatives are generated start/compaction material, dynamic
per-contract host response, or explicit `pasture epoch context` pull.
Acknowledgement alternatives are positive host evidence, explicit agent receipt,
or unavailable acknowledgement (record delivery/unknown only). UAT selects one
compatible pair and its failure/retry semantics.

### 18.4 Future verdict and process-health encoding

Alternatives are a typed host-native verdict separated from process health,
exact native exit/status semantics where the pinned contract proves them, or
continued neutral-only behavior. No deny/ask/defer value becomes reachable until
this UAT and exact response fixture pass.

### 18.5 Artifact enrichment depth and storage

Alternatives are commit/path metadata only, encrypted local diff/snapshot, or
external content-addressed evidence. This decision is orthogonal to occurrence
identity and must be compatible with the selected retention mode. Missing depth
never promotes an observation beyond `ObservedPath`.

PROPOSAL-8 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 2/2

## 19. Validation checklist

- [ ] Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit remains exactly 30 events in pinned order.
- [ ] Hostcontract is the sole production event/name/field/identity/behavior source.
- [ ] Enabled and Withheld are disjoint, complete, typed, and independently proved.
- [ ] At least one UAT-selected fixture-ready event can deliver M1 without all 30.
- [ ] Every separate delivery has a fresh operation ID and occurrence JournalID.
- [ ] No lifecycle/public symbol exposes replay, dedup, repeat count, or payload occurrence identity.
- [ ] `OccurrenceRecord` is the only public post-T1 occurrence type and is deeply immutable.
- [ ] Raw JSON is confined to private ingress/retention code.
- [ ] T2 defines every input/output, exact definition, operation, clock, effect, and slot.
- [ ] Enrichment snapshots are immutable, snapshot-bound, and bounded.
- [ ] Missing/contradictory enrichment is typed unresolved evidence.
- [ ] Context projection is pure and plan/attempt/result facts correlate exactly.
- [ ] Disclosure current state rebuilds identically from immutable journal history.
- [ ] Definitions resolve by immutable JournalID; retirement never erases history.
- [ ] Transaction time is checked after SQLite lock acquisition and exact replay.
- [ ] Capability Bound->Consumed, expiry, and phase CAS share one Apply.
- [ ] Readers define concrete typed filters/pages/cursors/truncation/errors for every record family.
- [ ] Production tests read only public bounded APIs.
- [ ] Selected retention matrix passes end to end, including tombstone/no-resurrection behavior.
- [ ] Positive human-to-code lineage passes forward and reverse production queries.
- [ ] One immutable FSM and one journal-backed control writer remain.
- [ ] Every M1-M6 file, generated artifact, migration, projection, test, and upstream extension has one owner.
- [ ] All six untracked and all committed prototype paths are rewritten/deleted by their named owner.
- [ ] All Go tests run with `-race`; static/build/Nix/generation/diff gates pass before implementation commits.

## 20. BDD acceptance criteria

- **Given** two byte-identical host CLI invocations, **when** an Enabled
  registration receives both, **then** it mints two operation IDs and returns two
  distinct occurrence JournalIDs in database order, **and should not** expose or
  infer replay, deduplication, a repeat count, a time window, or payload identity.
- **Given** one internal T1 Apply retry, **when** the same operation ID and exact
  canonical input is retried, **then** Provenance returns the original journal
  result, **and should not** convert that storage property into host-delivery
  semantics.
- **Given** only one authentic event fixture is ready, **when** activation is
  generated, **then** that event may be Enabled and queryable while the other 29
  are visibly Withheld with typed reasons, **and should not** claim full-catalogue
  support or register an unproved event.
- **Given** a registered malformed/duplicate/invalid/truncated/over-limit
  delivery, **when** trusted contract/event coordinates exist, **then** T1 records
  one bounded `OccurrenceRecord` and later planes remain empty, **and should not**
  drop the receipt, retain forbidden bytes, or guess semantics.
- **Given** T2 fails after T1, **when** the occurrence is read, **then** the
  receipt remains visible and eligible for later exact interpretation, **and
  should not** roll back with enrichment.
- **Given** one occurrence and two exact codebook/interpreter/build definitions,
  **when** both are interpreted, **then** both immutable batches and all outputs
  resolve their exact definition JournalIDs, **and should not** overwrite history
  or select latest implicitly.
- **Given** unavailable or contradictory capture/enrichment, **when** T2 runs,
  **then** it emits a typed unresolved fact with typed basis, **and should not**
  assert a human, actor, artifact, commit, causality, delivery, or authority fact.
- **Given** a path-only artifact signal, **when** lineage is queried, **then** it
  returns only `ObservedPath` plus the causal gap, **and should not** invent bytes,
  diff, commit, actor, or human motivation.
- **Given** the positive M3 production fixture, **when** forward and reverse
  readers run, **then** the same explicit human-signal/agent/tool/VCS/worktree/
  artifact/commit chain is returned within bounds, **and should not** use direct
  SQL, test exports, or timestamp proximity.
- **Given** one committed state and two context policy versions, **when** each
  plans disclosure, **then** two immutable plan histories resolve their exact
  policy/build definitions and later attempts/results cite the right plan, **and
  should not** mutate FSM state or prior disclosure facts.
- **Given** a delivery attempt whose host acknowledgement is unavailable, **when**
  the result is recorded, **then** history remains delivered/unknown according to
  the selected acknowledgement mode, **and should not** infer acknowledgement.
- **Given** candidate-only, stale, unauthorized, wrong-recipient, or unknown-
  definition context input, **when** planning is attempted, **then** no disclosure
  or FSM state changes, **and should not** let candidate state drive context.
- **Given** a fresh capability operation queued before expiry but admitted after
  expiry, **when** it acquires SQLite write ownership, **then** transaction time
  returns typed expiry and zero partial writes, **and should not** consume the
  capability or advance phase based on a pre-Apply clock check.
- **Given** an already committed capability operation after expiry, **when** its
  exact operation ID/input is retried, **then** exact replay returns the original
  result before current/deadline checks, **and should not** create a second commit.
- **Given** two processes race one capability or one current phase, **when** T3
  commits, **then** one wins and every loser has a typed current/expired/consumed
  result with zero semantic writes, **and should not** mutate context or a direct
  phase projection.
- **Given** Claude 2.1.210 `ElicitationResult`, **when** only host request/server
  strings correlate it, **then** it remains evidence/candidate, **and should not**
  become a registered-human decision or normative transition.
- **Given** each retention option, **when** its parameterized canary/deletion/
  replay matrix runs, **then** only policy-permitted content behavior occurs and
  occurrence/causal metadata remains, **and should not** leak or resurrect raw
  content.
- **Given** a cursor from another query, a future/stale/tampered cursor, zero or
  oversized page, or oversized lineage bounds, **when** a public reader runs,
  **then** it returns the exact typed error before SQL, **and should not** silently
  restart, skip, duplicate, or run an unbounded traversal.
- **Given** lifecycle/phase/lineage/disclosure projection deletion, **when** the
  journal replays, **then** public readers return identical canonical history and
  current state, **and should not** depend on independent projection IDs.
- **Given** a clean generation run, **when** a second host descriptor table,
  replay symbol, semantic generated branch, env/argv operation selector, or
  generic exit-to-deny mapping is introduced, **then** a static/generation test
  fails, **and should not** require a broad custom taint analyzer.

## 21. Tradeoffs, deferrals, and exit state

| Decision | Benefit | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| One Provenance journal and one FSM | No split-brain graph, phase, context, or identity truth | Services use explicit operations and bounded reads |
| Append every delivery | No silent undercount | Host retries remain visible for later analysis |
| Event-granular activation | Useful verified value arrives early without false claims | Registration/support output changes as proof becomes available |
| One canonical occurrence | No conversion drift after T1 | Private ingress capture cannot be reused as a public model |
| Immutable definition JournalIDs | Historical semantic meaning is resolvable | Activation/retirement and old decoders must be retained |
| Separate T1/T2/context/T3 operations | Receipt and honest external-side-effect gaps survive later failures | Users can observe partial processing |
| Minimal transaction-time condition | Correct expiry at lock admission without a predicate language | Requires a reviewed upstream Provenance release before M6 |
| Concrete snapshot readers | Bounded stable black-box validation | Callers paginate and handle typed cursor errors |
| UAT-parameterized retention | No privacy policy is silently chosen | Activation waits for the selected mode's full matrix |

Deferred without loss of M1-M6 integrity: runtime-authored codebook language,
probabilistic causal inference, cross-machine total order, generic fourth
harness, unsupported Claude 2.1.210 human authority, and any deliberate native
deny before its focused UAT.

The next valid action is a fresh independent mirrored review wave coordinated
outside this proposal task. If that wave accepts, the still-open Plan UAT must
resolve Section 18 before ratification. The obsolete IMPL_PLAN remains blocked
by this proposal and must be replaced by the supervisor after those gates. No
implementation, reviewer launch, ratification, commit, or push follows from
creating PROPOSAL-8.

## Appendix A: PROPOSAL-7 mirrored review disposition summary

text:
PROPOSAL-8 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION REVISION 2 - 1/3 (Sections 10-14)

This REVISION 2 set supersedes comments 6617 and 6618 in full. It incorporates the shared-SQLite write-budget input: see description sections 3.2-3.4 for the budget itself, and sections 15-16 and 19-21 in the following comments for its validation case, gates, and tradeoff.

## 10. One immutable FSM and transaction-local capability expiry

### 10.1 Preserved FSM/control direction

`pkg/protocol` owns one private static phase table. Production constructors no
longer accept a spec map. Read-only lookup and iteration return deep copies:

```go
func PhaseSpecFor(protocol.PhaseId) (protocol.PhaseSpec, bool)
func AllPhaseSpecs() []protocol.PhaseSpec
func NewEpochStateMachine(string) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
func NewEpochStateMachineFromState(protocol.EpochState) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
```

The transition law remains the PROPOSAL-7 corrected law, including Review ->
Propose, Plan UAT -> Propose, Code Review -> Worker Slices, and Implementation
UAT -> Worker Slices feedback edges. Generated transition metadata derives from
this source. The live engine/audit writer is cut over once at M6; direct phase
projection writes cannot remain active.

### 10.2 Capability API

```go
type CapabilityState uint8

const (
    CapabilityIssued CapabilityState = iota + 1
    CapabilityBound
    CapabilityRevoked
    CapabilityConsumed
)

type CapabilityOperation uint8

const (
    CapabilityRecordHumanDecision CapabilityOperation = iota + 1
    CapabilityBindSession
    CapabilityBindAssignment
    CapabilityCompleteTask
    CapabilityCommitTransition
)

type CapabilityScope struct { // opaque constructor
    Operation  CapabilityOperation
    Epoch      provenance.TaskID
    Actor      provenance.AgentID
    Role       protocol.RoleId
    Assignment provenance.JournalID
    Sources    []provenance.JournalID
    Bindings   []NativeBinding
    ExpiresAt  time.Time
}

type CommitCandidateInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Candidate   TransitionCandidateID
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Actor       provenance.AgentID
}

type CommittedTransition struct {
    PhaseState      PhaseStateID
    CapabilityState provenance.JournalID
    Decision        provenance.JournalID
}

type EpochControlService interface {
    CommitCandidate(context.Context, CommitCandidateInput) (CommittedTransition, error)
}

type CapabilityExpiredError struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Deadline   time.Time
}
```

`Decision` may be zero only for a transition kind whose constructor declares no
decision effect; there is no pointer ambiguity. `CommittedTransition` has no
replay flag.

### 10.3 Minimal upstream Provenance extension

Inspection of pinned commit `bcce71451b4a` confirms `Apply` already acquires
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, performs exact replay lookup, and then calls the closed
condition evaluator before effects. The minimal feasible extension is one new
condition arm, not a general predicate language:

```go
type ConditionTransactionTimeBefore struct {
    Deadline time.Time
}

const ConditionTransactionTimeBeforeKind provenance.ConditionKind = 3
const ConditionTimeExpired provenance.ConditionFailureReason = 3

type Condition struct { // upstream tagged union after the extension
    Kind                  provenance.ConditionKind
    Selector              provenance.FactSelector
    AssertedJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    TransactionTimeBefore ConditionTransactionTimeBefore
}

type ConditionFailure struct { // upstream typed failure after the extension
    Index             int
    Kind              provenance.ConditionKind
    Reason            provenance.ConditionFailureReason
    AssertedJournalID provenance.JournalID
    ActualJournalID   provenance.JournalID
    Deadline          time.Time
    TransactionTime   time.Time
}
```

In the actual Provenance tagged union, the new condition kind carries exactly
one UTC deadline and requires the fact-selector/JID arm to be zero. Existing
ExactFact/CurrentFact conditions require the deadline arm to be zero. Canonical
encoding stores signed Unix milliseconds; sub-millisecond deadlines are
rejected rather than rounded differently across processes.

The default transaction-time source executes, on the same pinned SQLite
connection after write-lock acquisition:

```text
SELECT CAST(unixepoch('subsec') * 1000 AS INTEGER)
```

Semantics are UTC Unix milliseconds. `transaction_now_ms < deadline_ms` passes;
equality or later returns typed `ConditionTimeExpired`. The source is private,
database-backed production authority; upstream internal tests inject a fake
transaction-time source, so application callers cannot weaken production time.

Evaluation order is fixed:

```text
BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquired
  -> exact OperationID lookup
       -> exact input: return original result
       -> changed input: OperationConflict, zero writes
       -> new operation: continue
  -> CurrentFact(capability == Bound)
  -> TransactionTimeBefore(capability.ExpiresAt)
  -> CurrentFact(phase == expected current state)
  -> write capability Consumed + phase/decision/task effects
  -> COMMIT
```

Pasture maps `ConditionTimeExpired` to a typed capability-expired error. A fresh
operation queued before the deadline but acquiring the lock at/after it loses
with zero journal, capability, phase, decision, task, context, and projection
writes. An exact already-committed retry still returns before deadline/current
state checks. Same operation ID with a changed deadline or any other changed
input conflicts.

Single use, revocation, scope, native binding, actor, role, assignment, and FSM
CAS remain mandatory. No arbitrary SQL, callback, boolean expression, or
application-specific predicate is added to Provenance.

## 11. Complete bounded public reader

### 11.1 Cursor and bounds

```go
type PageSize uint16

func NewPageSize(uint16) (PageSize, error) // accepts 1..256 only

type QueryFingerprint [32]byte

type Cursor struct { // opaque; encoded token has version + checksum
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
    LastJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    QueryFingerprint  QueryFingerprint
}

func ParseCursor(string) (Cursor, error)
func (Cursor) String() string

type PageRequest struct {
    Size   PageSize
    Cursor *Cursor
}

type TruncationReason uint8

const (
    TruncatedPageSize TruncationReason = iota + 1
    TruncatedDepthLimit
    TruncatedNodeLimit
    TruncatedEdgeLimit
)

type PageState struct {
    Next       *Cursor
    Truncated  bool
    Reason     TruncationReason
}

type LineageDirection uint8

const (
    LineageForward LineageDirection = iota + 1
    LineageReverse
)

type LineageBounds struct {
    MaxDepth uint16 // 1..32
    MaxNodes uint16 // 1..256
    MaxEdges uint16 // 1..512
}
```

An initial query with no cursor snapshots the current maximum JournalID. Every
page is ordered by ascending JournalID and resumes strictly after
`LastJournalID`. The query fingerprint is SHA-256 over the canonical typed
filter and direction/bounds. `Cursor.String` includes a versioned canonical
frame and checksum; `ParseCursor` rejects malformed/tampered frames. A cursor
with a different query fingerprint, future snapshot, last ID after snapshot,
missing retained snapshot, or unsupported version returns a distinct typed
error before SQL.

Cursor errors are closed:

```go
type CursorErrorKind uint8

const (
    CursorInvalidPageSize CursorErrorKind = iota + 1
    CursorQueryMismatch
    CursorSnapshotFuture
    CursorStale
    CursorTampered
    CursorUnsupportedVersion
    CursorInvalidLineageBounds
)
```

A cursor is an integrity/stability token, not authorization. Authorization is
checked independently on each read.

### 11.2 Concrete records, queries, pages, and methods

```go
type InterpretationRecord struct {
    ID         InterpretationID
    JournalID  provenance.JournalID
    Occurrence OccurrenceID
    Envelope   SemanticEnvelopeRef
    RecordedAt time.Time
}

type FactRecord struct {
    ID             LifecycleFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    Kind           FactKind
    Schema         LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Payload        EvidencePayloadRef
    Basis          []provenance.JournalID
}

type UnresolvedFactRecord struct {
    ID             UnresolvedFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    FactKind       FactKind
    Reason         UnresolvedReason
    Basis          UnresolvedBasis
    Parents        []provenance.JournalID
}
```

Every filter collection has a 64-value maximum, is constructor-validated, and
is defensively copied. Empty optional filter dimensions mean any; Page and the
required root for lineage are never optional. `Truncated` means more matching
data exists because the named bound was reached; `Next` is non-nil exactly when
continuation is possible.

Production tests and shipped commands may use only `LifecycleReader` or the
underlying public bounded `Journal().Facts()` where explicitly documented.
Direct SQL, private projection DTOs, or test-only exports cannot satisfy an
acceptance gate.

## 12. Malformed ingress, retention boundary, and response

### 12.1 Invalid-delivery matrix

| Input | T1 | T2/T3/context | Process result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled generated registration gives known contract/event; malformed, duplicate, invalid UTF-8, truncated, or over-limit bytes | one bounded occurrence with exact capture disposition | none | neutral exit 0; redacted diagnostic if needed |
| Enabled known registration with unsupported schema | one `CaptureUnsupportedSchema` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Enabled registration and payload event mismatch | one `CaptureEventMismatch` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Withheld or unregistered event | no store open, no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; support report gives typed reason |
| Payload-only unknown event without trusted registration coordinate | no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; stderr explicitly says no receipt |
| Store/definition activation/T1 Apply failure | no false receipt claim | none | neutral exit 0; actionable redacted storage diagnostic |
| T1 succeeds and T2 fails | receipt remains | no partial T2/T3/context | neutral exit 0; internal diagnostic cites occurrence safely |

Host stdout contains only the mechanical native response. It never exposes
JournalID, rowid, ActivityID, database path, raw prompt/tool/transcript data, or
retention keys.

### 12.2 Response boundary

Target-independent interpretation cannot import host response internals.
Generated scripts register and forward only. M1-M4 expose only one mechanical
neutral response. `Stop` and `SubagentStop` are captured before the loop guard;
active loop state produces a suppressed fact and no recursive consultation.

Future allow/deny/ask/defer verdict and process-health encoding remains open UAT.
Generic CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny. A deliberate gate cannot
activate until its exact host fixture and future response UAT pass.

## 13. Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit: exactly 30 events

The source facts below are unchanged from the verified PROPOSAL-7 audit. The
private hostcontract becomes their sole production source; the independent
fixture manifest verifies them. All events require the common `session_id` and
may admit common `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`,
`hook_event_name`, `effort`, `agent_id`, and `agent_type` only where the pinned
descriptor allows. Common presence is not semantic identity.

Behavior abbreviations:

- `OBS`: nonblocking, no mutation, report-and-continue, no reconciliation.
- `GATE`: blocking, no mutation unless stated, exit-2-would-block,
  host-native reconciliation.
- `COND`: conditionally blocking; `config_source=policy_settings` is the pinned
  nonblocking matcher.
- `STOP`: blocking gate consulted only while `stop_hook_active=false`.
- `HUMAN`: blocking explicit-human-response classification, `MutationNone`.

The behavior column describes host capability, not Pasture authority. Only an
Enabled activation is registered; every audit row remains in the independent
catalogue whether Enabled or Withheld.

| # | Event; exact event-specific fields; identity additions; behavior | T2 evidence/candidate and bidirectional use |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `SessionStart`; `source`, `model`, `session_title`; none; OBS | Assert observed session boundary and supplied metadata states. Candidate session bind/resume only with launch capability. M4 may inject committed phase/role/assignment/worktree context. |
| 2 | `Setup`; `trigger`; none; OBS | Assert setup trigger/environment-preparation signal. No transition. M4 may plan bounded environment context. |
| 3 | `SessionEnd`; `reason`; none; OBS | Assert session-end claim/reason. Candidate detachment only; closing a binding requires current capability. M4 revokes session-scoped disclosure. |
| 4 | `UserPromptSubmit`; `prompt`; none; GATE | Record a policy-selected human-signal reference and turn boundary. It is not a registered-human decision. M4 may return committed context; response remains neutral initially. |
| 5 | `UserPromptExpansion`; `prompt`, `command_name`; none; GATE | Record command and expanded-prompt references. Link source only when explicit correlation exists. No direct control. |
| 6 | `Stop`; `stop_hook_active`; none; STOP | Record turn-stop claim, never completion. Candidate checkpoint only with other evidence. Active loop emits suppression; inactive M4 may return feedback. |
| 7 | `StopFailure`; `error`, `error_type`; none; OBS | Record failed-stop/error metadata or protected reference. Recovery candidate only; never success. |
| 8 | `PreToolUse`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; GATE with input mutation capability | Record tool intent and input state/reference. Candidate gate/tool policy; event alone has no control authority. M4 may supply tool context; future M5 may encode a typed gate response. |
| 9 | `PermissionRequest`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `request_id`; required request identity; GATE | Record permission request and tool relation. The pin has no options field. Candidate verdict request only; no transition. |
| 10 | `PermissionDenied`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`; none; OBS | Record observed denied attempt. The pin has no reason/source, so those remain unresolved unless another fact supplies them. Corrective candidate only. |
| 11 | `PostToolUse`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; OBS | Record observed successful result reference. The pin has no duration or artifact identity; artifact confidence requires explicit tool/VCS/worktree enrichment. Candidate progress only. |
| 12 | `PostToolUseFailure`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `error`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; OBS | Record failed tool result/error reference. The pin has no interrupt field. Corrective candidate only. |
| 13 | `PostToolBatch`; `batch_results`; none; GATE | Record bounded batch result reference and explicit members only if captured. Candidate checkpoint from member facts, not batch occurrence alone. M4 may return bounded aggregate context. |
| 14 | `FileChanged`; `file_path`; none; OBS | Assert `ObservedPath` only. Actor, bytes, diff, commit, and prompt remain unresolved until explicit enrichment. M4 may refresh path-scoped rules. |
| 15 | `CwdChanged`; no event-specific fields; none; OBS | Record only the common `cwd` state supplied by the pin. It cannot assert old/new cwd. M4 may refresh scope under selected retention. |
| 16 | `ConfigChange`; `config_source`; none; COND | Record configuration-change source. Candidate invalidation/review only; never changes protocol law. M4 may refresh/revoke affected rules. |
| 17 | `InstructionsLoaded`; `file_path`, `memory_type`, `load_reason`, `globs`, `trigger_file_path`, `parent_file_path`; none; OBS | Record host-reported instruction metadata/inclusion links. Exact content/delivery is unresolved without a snapshot and acknowledgement. No transition. |
| 18 | `WorktreeCreate`; no event-specific fields; none; GATE | Record worktree-create request only. The pin has no returned path. Candidate allocation; normative bind requires assignment capability. Do not replace host creation initially. |
| 19 | `WorktreeRemove`; no event-specific fields; none; OBS | Record removal signal only; the pin has no path. Candidate release; normative unbind requires current lease. M4 may revoke verified worktree context. |
| 20 | `SubagentStart`; common `agent_id`,`agent_type`; required agent identity; OBS | Record child-agent claim and link to parent only when proven. Candidate assignment start; normative bind requires delegation capability. M4 may disclose child scope. |
| 21 | `SubagentStop`; `agent_transcript_path`, `stop_hook_active`; required agent identity; STOP | Record child-stop and transcript reference, never task completion. Active loop suppresses consultation. Completion/handoff remains candidate pending evidence/capability. |
| 22 | `TeammateIdle`; `teammate_name`; none; GATE | Record scoped idle claim. Candidate readiness/missing-work only. M4 may return committed assignment context; no automatic transition. |
| 23 | `TaskCreated`; `task_id`; none; GATE | Record native task claim. Native task ID is not Provenance TaskID. Candidate import/link/create; normative allocation requires governed assignment capability. |
| 24 | `TaskCompleted`; `task_id`; none; GATE | Record native completion claim. Candidate close only after required activity/test/review facts; scoped capability and current task state are mandatory. Future response may ask host to keep working. |
| 25 | `PreCompact`; `trigger`; none; GATE | Record compaction request/trigger. The pin has no instructions field. Candidate continuity checkpoint only. M4 may plan bounded continuity context. |
| 26 | `PostCompact`; `trigger`; none; OBS | Record compaction completion/trigger. The pin has no summary, so summary remains unresolved unless a later contract supplies it. M4 may refresh from retained facts. |
| 27 | `Notification`; `message`, `notification_type`, `title`; none; OBS | Record host attention signal with protected message/title state. Never treat as human response or causation without request identity. |
| 28 | `MessageDisplay`; `message`, `content`; none; OBS | Record display evidence/reference only. It is not transcript truth, a decision, or authority. Later response backends preserve host behavior. |
| 29 | `Elicitation`; `request_id`, `fields`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; GATE | Record external input request/schema/server states. Candidate Pasture decision request only if a proven issued-request challenge binds it; Claude 2.1.210 cannot satisfy normative binding. |
| 30 | `ElicitationResult`; `request_id`, `response`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; HUMAN, MutationNone | Record one observed response and request/server claims. The pin cannot prove original/effective values or an overrider. It remains evidence/candidate only and cannot commit a human decision for this contract. |

Completeness requires rows 1-30 exactly once and in this order. Activation is
orthogonal: a Withheld row remains part of catalogue truth but is absent from
host registration.

## 14. Retention and tombstone matrix, parameterized by UAT

This proposal does not select a retention mode. The selected mode becomes a
blocking UAT output and its entire matrix must pass before any event carrying
that capture class becomes Enabled.

| Mode | Required blocking tests |
|---|---|
| Metadata only | Raw prompt/tool/transcript/path/elicitation bytes never appear in journal, projections, readers, logs, stderr, temporary files, or replay. Missing policy-required content emits typed `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect. |
| Encrypted local payload | Keys are never journaled/logged; missing/wrong key fails closed; ciphertext is bounded and authenticated; deletion appends a tombstone and removes key/object according to policy; readers return tombstoned/missing without plaintext leakage; replay and projection rebuild cannot resurrect deleted content; key rotation preserves permitted refs and history. |
| External content-addressed payload | Store and object refs are typed and bounded; content identity verifies fetched bytes; missing/deleted object returns typed unresolved/tombstoned state; deletion appends a tombstone; journal/projection replay cannot re-upload or resurrect; logs/queries expose no content or credentials. |

All modes preserve occurrence identity, runtime/version envelope, policy-
permitted native binding metadata, causal links, disclosure history, capability
history, and commits. Tombstones never erase the fact that content existed or
rewrite prior JournalIDs. Raw JSON remains behind private retention-policy
accessors and never enters `OccurrenceRecord` or another target-neutral type.

PROPOSAL-8 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION REVISION 2 - 2/3 (Sections 15-18)

## 15. Named production-path proofs and validation

### 15.1 Required black-box tests

1. `TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceReader`: for each Enabled event, generate
   the actual registration, invoke the built command with the authentic raw
   fixture against one file-backed database, and read `OccurrenceRecord` only
   through `LifecycleReader`. Two byte-identical process invocations yield two
   operation IDs and two occurrence JournalIDs with no replay field.
2. `TestWithheldClaudeEventIsNotRegistered`: every Withheld event is absent from
   host registration and present in the support report with the exact typed
   reason. Enabled union Withheld equals the independent 30-event oracle.
3. `TestClaudeLifecycleToInterpretationReader`: the same generated/binary path
   reaches T1, T2, exact definitions, stable slots, and public fact/link/
   candidate/unresolved pages. Direct interpreter/Apply tests cannot substitute.
4. `TestHumanSignalToCommitLineageBlackBox`: a Pasture-issued human signal is
   bound to the host session/request, followed by an agent tool call, selected
   VCS/tool/worktree enrichment, artifact and commit evidence, then queried
   human-to-code and code-to-human through the bounded reader. Missing and
   contradictory enrichment remain `ObservedPath` plus typed unresolved facts;
   no timestamp/session proximity promotes confidence.
5. `TestDisclosurePlanAttemptResultReader`: committed state enters the pure
   projector, then separate plan/attempt/result operations are read publicly;
   candidate/stale/wrong-recipient/unauthorized/unknown-policy cases write
   nothing and projection rebuild is identical.
6. `TestHookCandidateToEpochControl`: a real enabled hook produces a candidate;
   production services issue/bind capability and T3 commits through one FSM,
   then public capability/commit readers return the result. No direct projection
   writer or test-only export counts.
7. `TestTransactionTimeBeforeLockSpanningExpiry`: upstream Provenance holds the
   SQLite writer across the deadline; a fresh queued operation loses after lock
   acquisition with typed expiry and zero writes; an exact committed retry still
   returns its original result.
8. `TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad`: the shared-file write budget in
   3.2 and 3.4. Representative hook-ingress load at the assumed 48-writer
   ceiling runs against one file-backed `pasture.db` while `start_slice`
   delivery is delayed into the contended window. Either the slice starts within
   the 2-second deadline or it fails with the exact honest "enqueued but never
   started" error; every receipt committed during the window remains readable;
   and p99 T1 write-lock hold stays <= 5 ms at exactly one write transaction per
   delivery. This is the only test covering the production characteristic that
   commit `3cc3ca7` stopped provoking.

### 15.2 Definition, reader, privacy, and race matrices

- Activate two codebooks, interpreters, builds, and context policies over the
  same source facts; every dependent record resolves its exact definition
  JournalIDs and never silently selects latest.
- Retire a definition and prove historical resolution still works while new
  active resolution does not choose it.
- Test malformed/tampered/mismatched/future/stale cursors, zero/over-limit page
  and lineage bounds, stable snapshots, no duplicate/skip, continuation,
  explicit cycles, node/edge/depth truncation, and defensive copies.
- Race separate processes or independent handles on fixed actor activation,
  definition activation, distinct receipts, revocation versus consume, two
  consumers of one capability, and two capabilities for one current phase.
- Snapshot journal/capability/phase/decision/context/projection deltas before
  every losing operation and assert zero partial semantic writes.
- Measure write-transaction count and lock-hold distribution for T1 and T2 on
  the shared file, and assert the 3.2 budget: one transaction per delivery, p99
  hold <= 5 ms, 1-second caller deadline honored, and no fixed sub-100 ms retry
  loop anywhere on the hook path.
- Parameterize privacy canaries by the UAT-selected retention mode and run them
  through generated process, journal, readers, logs, stderr, tombstone, and
  replay paths.
- Delete lifecycle/phase/lineage/disclosure projections and rebuild identical
  public results from the journal.

### 15.3 Static and generation guards

- Focused source guard rejects `ReplayKey`, `RecordReplayed`, lifecycle result
  `Replayed`, occurrence dedup/window/count code, and payload digest use as an
  occurrence key.
- Host descriptor ownership/dependency test rejects a second event/field/
  behavior table outside hostcontract and generated derivatives.
- Compile-fail imports prove model/codebook/lowering/context/control cannot
  import private host response/descriptor packages.
- Clean regeneration rejects drift or retired generated assets.
- Subprocess mutation proves argv/env cannot select semantics or authority and
  generic internal errors cannot produce deny.
- Phase parity proves runtime and generated surfaces derive from one immutable
  phase law.

All Go test commands use `-race`; no duplicate non-race wave counts. Commit
gates remain gofmt, go vet, race tests, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build`, Nix checks,
clean generation drift, and `git diff --check`.

## 16. Milestones

| Milestone | First user-visible value | Essential gate | Explicit exclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 progressive receipt | At least one UAT-selected fixture-ready event is registered and publicly queryable; other events are visibly Withheld | fixed actor; no replay symbols; enabled event authentic process proof; invalid matrix; bounded occurrence reader; support report; shared-file write budget (3.2) measured and `TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad` passing | no full-catalogue claim without all 30; no semantics/context/control; no blocking per-tool-call event Enabled before `aura-plugins-cvlu6` resolves |

`internal/lifecycle/projection/**` is owned only by S1. Its v6 schema is generic
over envelope headers, definition refs, parents, typed contexts, and source
JournalIDs, so later slices add semantic readers without modifying projection
truth or adding migrations. S1 is the sole migration/projection owner.

Generated artifact owners are S0 for protocol skills/agents and S2 for Claude
hook registration/support assets. No other slice edits those outputs.

### 17.2 Explicit wiring transfer rule

`cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go` and `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` belong
to S2 through M3. If UAT selects dynamic context injection, the supervisor
transfers those two exact files exclusively to S5 after S2 is merged and closed.
If M5 response wiring requires a change, they transfer exclusively from S5 (or
S2 when S5 did not need them) to S6 after the prior owner closes. There is never
simultaneous ownership. Generated assets remain S2-owned and are changed only
through its generator contract.

### 17.3 L1/L2/L3 leaves per slice

| Existing path | Owner | Disposition |
|---|---|---|

| `internal/lifecycle/key.go`, `key_test.go` | S1 | delete; static guard prevents replacement replay key |
| `internal/lifecycle/frontend.go`, `frontend_test.go`, `fixtures_test.go`, `verifier_internal_test.go` | S2 | replace with private capture and independent activation fixtures |
| `internal/lifecycle/backend.go`, `backend_test.go` | S2 | delete same-package host behavior side door |
