```go
}

type DisclosureRecordKind uint8

const (
    DisclosureRecordPlan DisclosureRecordKind = iota + 1
    DisclosureRecordAttempt
    DisclosureRecordResult
)

type DisclosureRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT or FACT per Kind
    Kind      DisclosureRecordKind
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt   DisclosureAttemptID
    Result    DisclosureResultID
    Status    DisclosureDeliveryStatus
    Recipient ActorRef
}

// Returns the journal identity of the record's own Kind. There is no fourth
// identity and no equality invariant for a caller to maintain.
func (r DisclosureRecord) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type OccurrenceQuery struct {
    Contracts []ir.RuntimeContractID
    Events    []ContractEventKind
    Actors    []provenance.AgentID
    Page      PageRequest
}

type InterpretationQuery struct {
    Occurrences []OccurrenceID
    Definitions []DefinitionJournalID
    Page        PageRequest
}

type FactQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    Kinds           []FactKind
    Definitions     []DefinitionJournalID
    Page            PageRequest
}

type UnresolvedFactQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    Reasons         []UnresolvedReason
    Page            PageRequest
}

type CandidateQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    From            []protocol.PhaseId
    To              []protocol.PhaseId
    Page            PageRequest
}

type LineageQuery struct {
    Root      provenance.JournalID
    Direction LineageDirection

    Bounds    LineageBounds

}

type DisclosureQuery struct {
    Recipients []provenance.AgentID
    Phases     []protocol.PhaseId
    Roles      []protocol.RoleId
    Plans      []DisclosurePlanID

}

// Immutable bodies. No status filter: a body has no status.
type DefinitionReadQuery struct {
    Kinds []DefinitionKind
    Page  PageRequest
}

// Derived state. Status filtering lives here and only here.
type DefinitionStateQuery struct {
    Kinds    []DefinitionKind
    Statuses []DefinitionStatus
    Page     PageRequest
}

type CapabilityQuery struct {
    Capabilities []CapabilityID
    States       []CapabilityState
    Actors       []provenance.AgentID
    Page         PageRequest
}

type CommitQuery struct {
    Epochs []provenance.TaskID
    Phases []protocol.PhaseId
    Page   PageRequest
}

type OccurrencePage struct { Items []OccurrenceRecord; State PageState }
type InterpretationPage struct { Items []InterpretationRecord; State PageState }
type FactPage struct { Items []FactRecord; State PageState }
type UnresolvedFactPage struct { Items []UnresolvedFactRecord; State PageState }
type CandidatePage struct { Items []TransitionCandidateRecord; State PageState }
type LineagePage struct { Nodes []provenance.JournalID; Links []CausalLinkRecord; State PageState }
type DisclosurePage struct { Items []DisclosureRecord; State PageState }
type DefinitionPage struct { Items []DefinitionSnapshot; State PageState }
type DefinitionStatePage struct { Items []DefinitionStateRecord; State PageState }
type CapabilityPage struct { Items []CapabilityStateRecord; State PageState }
type CommitPage struct { Items []CommitRecord; State PageState }

type LifecycleReader interface {
    Occurrences(context.Context, OccurrenceQuery) (OccurrencePage, error)
    Interpretations(context.Context, InterpretationQuery) (InterpretationPage, error)
    Facts(context.Context, FactQuery) (FactPage, error)
    UnresolvedFacts(context.Context, UnresolvedFactQuery) (UnresolvedFactPage, error)
    Candidates(context.Context, CandidateQuery) (CandidatePage, error)
    Lineage(context.Context, LineageQuery) (LineagePage, error)
    Disclosures(context.Context, DisclosureQuery) (DisclosurePage, error)
    Definitions(context.Context, DefinitionReadQuery) (DefinitionPage, error)
    DefinitionStates(context.Context, DefinitionStateQuery) (DefinitionStatePage, error)
    Capabilities(context.Context, CapabilityQuery) (CapabilityPage, error)
    Commits(context.Context, CommitQuery) (CommitPage, error)
}
```

Every filter collection has a 64-value maximum, is constructor-validated, and is defensively copied.
Empty optional filter dimensions mean any; `Page`, and the required root for lineage, are never
optional. `Truncated` means more matching data exists because the named bound was reached; `Next`
is non-nil exactly when continuation is possible.

Production tests and shipped commands may use only `LifecycleReader`, or the underlying public
bounded `Journal().Facts()` where explicitly documented. Direct SQL, private projection DTOs, and
test-only exports cannot satisfy an acceptance gate. **This rule now has a static guard** (§16.4);
PROPOSAL-8 asserted it five times and guarded it zero times while giving the replay rule a guard
(`aura-plugins-237wx` B4).

At M1 the occurrence reader is served **by replay from journal facts**, not from a materialised
index written on the hook path. Enlisting a Pasture index write inside Provenance's Apply
transaction is not possible on the pinned API — `Apply` takes no transaction handle, the
transaction is private to `applyPreparedOperation`, and the only `OpenSQLite` option seeds
`ml_models` — so PROPOSAL-8's "index rows are written inside the owning Apply **or** rebuilt by
replay" offered a branch that cannot be built. The disjunction is deleted and replay is stated
(`aura-plugins-4acdq` item 11(a)).

## 13. Malformed ingress, retention boundary, and response

### 13.1 Invalid-delivery matrix

Every row below is a row of corpus `ingress_invalid.yaml` and is executed by exactly one named
test, `TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus` (§16.1 item 3). PROPOSAL-8 left this matrix as prose with
no named owner (`aura-plugins-237wx` A3).

| Input | T1 | T2/T3/context | Process result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled generated registration gives known contract/event; malformed, duplicate-key, invalid UTF-8, truncated, or over-limit bytes | one bounded occurrence with the exact capture disposition | none | neutral exit 0; redacted diagnostic if needed |
| Enabled known registration with unsupported schema | one `CaptureUnsupportedSchema` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Enabled registration and payload event mismatch | one `CaptureEventMismatch` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Withheld or unregistered event | no store open, no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; support report gives the typed reason |
| Payload-only unknown event without a trusted registration coordinate | no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; stderr explicitly says no receipt |
| Store / definition activation / T1 Apply failure | no false receipt claim | none | neutral exit 0; actionable redacted storage diagnostic |
| T1 succeeds and T2 fails | receipt remains | no partial T2/T3/context | neutral exit 0; internal diagnostic cites the occurrence safely |
| Contended append exceeding the 1-second caller deadline (P0-PIN) | no receipt, zero writes, definite typed failure | none | neutral exit 0; actionable contention diagnostic naming the deadline |

Host stdout contains only the mechanical native response. It never exposes JournalID, rowid,
ActivityID, database path, raw prompt/tool/transcript data, or retention keys.

**Not in this matrix, deliberately:** a semantically-identical-different-byte delivery. The
byte-identical double-invocation case in §16.1 item 1 strictly dominates it for detecting any
reintroduced content-derived dedup key, because identical bytes collapse under every normalization.
Two reviewers disagreed on this; `aura-plugins-237wx`'s argument is the correct one and
`aura-plugins-0lbsy` IMPORTANT 1's request for the case is recorded as rejected rather than
overlooked.

### 13.2 Response boundary

Target-independent interpretation cannot import host response internals. Generated scripts register
and forward only; they never parse the payload, and `MutateGeneratedPayloadParse` (§16.4) proves
that guard bites. M1-M4 expose only one mechanical neutral response. `Stop` and `SubagentStop` are
captured before the loop guard; active loop state produces a suppressed fact and no recursive
consultation.

Future allow/deny/ask/defer verdict and process-health encoding remains open UAT (§19.4). Generic
CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny. A deliberate gate cannot activate until its exact host
fixture and the future response UAT pass.

## 14. Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit: exactly 30 events

Unchanged from PROPOSAL-8, and verified row by row by `aura-plugins-4acdq` against
`internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:69-100`, `internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:322-361`,
and `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go:148-183`, including the five previously-invented rows. The
private hostcontract becomes their sole production source; the independent fixture manifest verifies
them. All events require the common `session_id` and may admit common `transcript_path`, `cwd`,
`permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`, `effort`, `agent_id`, and `agent_type` only where the pinned
descriptor allows. Common presence is not semantic identity.

Behaviour abbreviations: `OBS` nonblocking, no mutation, report-and-continue, no reconciliation;
`GATE` blocking, no mutation unless stated, exit-2-would-block, host-native reconciliation; `COND`
conditionally blocking, `config_source=policy_settings` is the pinned nonblocking matcher; `STOP`
blocking gate consulted only while `stop_hook_active=false`; `HUMAN` blocking explicit-human-response
classification, `MutationNone`.

The behaviour column describes host capability, not Pasture authority. Only an Enabled activation is
registered; every audit row remains in the independent catalogue whether Enabled or Withheld.

| # | Event; exact event-specific fields; identity additions; behaviour | T2 evidence/candidate and bidirectional use |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `SessionStart`; `source`, `model`, `session_title`; none; OBS | Assert observed session boundary and supplied metadata states. Candidate session bind/resume only with launch capability. M4 may inject committed phase/role/assignment/worktree context. |

| 3 | `SessionEnd`; `reason`; none; OBS | Assert session-end claim/reason. Candidate detachment only; closing a binding requires current capability. M4 revokes session-scoped disclosure. |
| 4 | `UserPromptSubmit`; `prompt`; none; GATE | Record a policy-selected human-signal reference and turn boundary. It is not a registered-human decision. M4 may return committed context; response remains neutral initially. **This is the M3 human-signal leg (§16.1 item 4).** |
| 5 | `UserPromptExpansion`; `prompt`, `command_name`; none; GATE | Record command and expanded-prompt references. Link source only when explicit correlation exists. No direct control. |
| 6 | `Stop`; `stop_hook_active`; none; STOP | Record turn-stop claim, never completion. Candidate checkpoint only with other evidence. Active loop emits suppression; inactive M4 may return feedback. |
| 7 | `StopFailure`; `error`, `error_type`; none; OBS | Record failed-stop / error metadata or protected reference. Recovery candidate only; never success. |
| 8 | `PreToolUse`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; GATE with input mutation capability | Record tool intent and input state/reference. Candidate gate/tool policy; event alone has no control authority. M4 may supply tool context; future M5 may encode a typed gate response. |

| 24 | `TaskCompleted`; `task_id`; none; GATE | Record native completion claim. Candidate close only after required activity/test/review facts; scoped capability and current task state are mandatory. Future response may ask the host to keep working. |
| 25 | `PreCompact`; `trigger`; none; GATE | Record compaction request/trigger. The pin has no instructions field. Candidate continuity checkpoint only. M4 may plan bounded continuity context. |
| 26 | `PostCompact`; `trigger`; none; OBS | Record compaction completion/trigger. The pin has no summary, so summary remains unresolved unless a later contract supplies it. M4 may refresh from retained facts. |
| 27 | `Notification`; `message`, `notification_type`, `title`; none; OBS | Record host attention signal with protected message/title state. Never treat as a human response or causation without request identity. |
| 28 | `MessageDisplay`; `message`, `content`; none; OBS | Record display evidence/reference only. It is not transcript truth, a decision, or authority. Later response backends preserve host behaviour. |
| 29 | `Elicitation`; `request_id`, `fields`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; GATE | Record external input request/schema/server states. Candidate Pasture decision request only if a proven issued-request challenge binds it; Claude 2.1.210 cannot satisfy normative binding. |
| 30 | `ElicitationResult`; `request_id`, `response`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; HUMAN, MutationNone | Record one observed response and request/server claims. The pin cannot prove original/effective values or an overrider. It remains evidence/candidate only and cannot commit a human decision for this contract. |

Completeness requires rows 1-30 exactly once and in this order. Activation is orthogonal: a Withheld
row remains part of catalogue truth but is absent from host registration.

## 15. Retention and tombstone matrix, parameterized by UAT, gating M1

This proposal does not select a retention mode. The selected mode is a blocking UAT output and its
entire matrix must pass before any event carrying that capture class becomes Enabled.

**The retention gate is M1, not M4.** PROPOSAL-8 §14 said the matrix must pass before Enabling any
event carrying that capture class, but §16 listed it only under M4 — while M1 Enables payload-bearing
events (`SessionStart` carries `source`, `model`, `session_title`; `UserPromptSubmit` carries
`prompt`) and §6.2's `OccurrenceEnvelopeRef` makes `RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef` mandatory at T1.
The two statements could not both be true (`aura-plugins-237wx` A1). §6.1's
`WithheldRetentionMatrixPending`, §17's M1 gate, and §19.1 all now say M1.

| Mode | Required blocking tests |
|---|---|
| Metadata only | Raw prompt/tool/transcript/path/elicitation bytes never appear in the journal, projections, readers, logs, stderr, temporary files, or replay. Missing policy-required content emits typed `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect. |
| Encrypted local payload | Keys are never journaled or logged; missing or wrong key fails closed; ciphertext is bounded and authenticated; deletion appends a tombstone and removes key/object according to policy; readers return tombstoned/missing without plaintext leakage; replay and projection rebuild cannot resurrect deleted content; key rotation preserves permitted refs and history. |
| External content-addressed payload | Store and object refs are typed and bounded; content identity verifies fetched bytes; a missing or deleted object returns typed unresolved/tombstoned state; deletion appends a tombstone; journal and projection replay cannot re-upload or resurrect; logs and queries expose no content or credentials. |

All modes preserve occurrence identity, the runtime/version envelope, policy-permitted native
binding metadata, causal links, disclosure history, capability history, and commits. Tombstones
never erase the fact that content existed and never rewrite prior JournalIDs. Raw JSON remains behind
private retention-policy accessors and never enters `OccurrenceRecord` or another target-neutral
type.

Each mode is a corpus (`retention_metadata_only.yaml`, `retention_encrypted_local.yaml`,
`retention_external_cas.yaml`) with must-pass and must-fail rows and its own non-vacuity guard
(§16.0).

PROPOSAL-9 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 2/3 (Sections 16-19)

## 16. Validation: corpora, named proofs, matrices, and guards

### 16.0 The corpus harness (new — URD FIX-NOW)

The URD (`aura-plugins-hznvh`) carries a user FIX-NOW, recorded verbatim:

> "Are our test cases taking on the same shape as the ... schema/develop/TESTING.md ? We should
> extract out test cases into YAML fixtures, and utilize a testing harness to perform combinatorial
> and mutation tests over the test corpora."

with the requirement stated as: adopt the Schema corpus idiom for **current and subsequent epoch
acceptance tests** — typed YAML `Case`/`Corpus` rows with must-pass/must-fail classification,
provenance and mutation metadata; non-vacuity and coverage guards; deterministic bounded
combinatorial expansion; and named typed mutation operators. YAML is pure data and contains no
executable Go, SQL, or shell. The same URD records an accepted definition-of-done of "81 corpus
operators + Go concurrency/schema/FSM layer", so this is a shipped, user-accepted idiom.

PROPOSAL-8 adopted none of it, while presenting four large matrices as prose with no named test
(`aura-plugins-237wx` B3). Non-vacuity guards are precisely the mechanism that catches
self-deceiving tests, and this project has now paid for four: the collision table that passed
against a deliberately broken encoder; the mutation that survived because a case varied two things
at once; the grep invariant whose own comment kept it red; and the still-live identity-containment
guard in `internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go` that cannot see a dropped non-identity field
(`aura-plugins-noqor`), alongside
`internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend_test.go:495-529`, which synthesizes each payload from the table
it is meant to check.

```go
// internal/lifecycle/corpus — owned by S1, consumed by every slice.

type Expectation uint8

const (
    MustPass Expectation = iota + 1
    MustFail
)

type CaseID string // opaque validated; unique within a corpus

type CaseProvenance struct {
    Origin    CaseOrigin
    Reference string // file path or public URL. Never a Beads ID (AGENTS.md).
}

type CaseOrigin uint8

const (
    OriginPinnedContract CaseOrigin = iota + 1 // transcribed from the pinned host descriptor
    OriginReviewFinding                        // added because a review found the gap
    OriginAuthored                             // hand-authored oracle
)

type Case struct {
    ID         CaseID
    Expect     Expectation
    Provenance CaseProvenance
    // Raw host bytes are REFERENCED, never inlined, so duplicate keys, invalid
    // UTF-8, byte ordering, and truncation survive into the fixture. Inlining
    // them in YAML normalizes exactly the properties section 13.1 tests for.
    RawBytesPath string
    Dimensions   map[string]string // typed, closed key set per corpus
}

type Corpus struct {
    Name     string
    Cases    []Case
    Expand   ExpansionSpec // deterministic, bounded combinatorial expansion
    Coverage CoverageSpec  // which enum dimensions must be fully covered
}

type NonVacuityReport struct {
    Corpus         string
    CaseCount      int
    ExecutedCount  int
    MustFailCount  int
    UncoveredDims  []string
    GuardsProvenBy []MutationOperatorID
}

type MutationOperatorID uint8

const (
    MutateRemovePayloadField MutationOperatorID = iota + 1
    MutateRemoveIdentityField
    MutateAddSecondDescriptorTable
    MutateAddPhaseAdjacencyTable
    MutateReintroduceReplaySymbol
    MutateEnvSelectedOperation
    MutateGeneratedSemanticBranch
    MutateGeneratedPayloadParse
    MutateGenericErrorToDeny
```

### 16.1 Required black-box production-path proofs

1. `TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceReader` — for each Enabled event, generate the actual
   registration, invoke the built command with the authentic raw fixture against one file-backed
   database, and read `OccurrenceRecord` only through `LifecycleReader`. Two byte-identical process
   invocations yield two operation IDs and two occurrence JournalIDs with no replay field.
2. `TestWithheldClaudeEventIsNotRegistered` — every Withheld event is absent from host registration
   and present in the support report with the exact typed reason. Enabled union Withheld equals the
   independent 30-event oracle exactly once.
3. `TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus` — drives `ingress_invalid.yaml` through generated registration,
   built binary, file-backed journal, and public readers only. Asserts one distinct T1 record with
   the exact `CaptureDisposition` where required; asserts no later-plane effects; asserts that
   untrusted, unregistered, and store-failure inputs produce no false receipt without touching SQL.
   This is §13.1's named owner.
4. `TestHumanSignalToCommitLineageBlackBox` — **the human-signal leg is now named.** A real
   `UserPromptSubmit` occurrence, delivered through the generated registration and the built binary,
   is interpreted by the codebook into `FactHumanSignal` on the evidence plane. That signal is bound
   to the host session/request, followed by an agent tool call, selected VCS/tool/worktree
   enrichment, artifact and commit evidence, then queried human-to-code and code-to-human through
   the bounded reader. Missing and contradictory enrichment remain `RelationObservedPath` plus typed
   unresolved facts; no timestamp or session proximity promotes confidence.
   **`UserPromptSubmit` Enabled is therefore an explicit M3 gate.** It is turn-scoped, not
   per-tool-call, so the `aura-plugins-cvlu6` restriction in §17 does not bar it. A *Pasture-issued*
   human decision is `CapabilityRecordHumanDecision` and is proved at M6 in item 8, not here.
   PROPOSAL-8 required a "Pasture-issued human signal" at M3 with no M3-available issuance path,
   which would have been satisfied by seeding it in the test while the gate reported green
   (`aura-plugins-237wx` A2).
5. `TestDisclosurePlanAttemptResultReader` — committed state enters the pure projector, then
   separate plan/attempt/result operations are read publicly; candidate, stale, wrong-recipient,
   unauthorized, and unknown-policy cases write nothing; a truncated-history case with a
   completeness-required policy produces `DisclosureSuppressed` and no partial packet; projection
   rebuild is identical.
6. `TestClaudeLifecycleToInterpretationReader` — the same generated/binary path reaches T1, T2,
   exact definitions, stable slots, and public fact/link/candidate/unresolved pages. Direct
   interpreter or `Apply` tests cannot substitute.
7. `TestTransactionTimeBeforeLockSpanningExpiry` — upstream Provenance holds the SQLite writer
   across the deadline; a fresh queued operation loses after lock acquisition with typed expiry and
   zero writes; an exact committed retry still returns its original result.
8. `TestHookCandidateToEpochControl` — a real Enabled hook produces a candidate; production services
   `Issue` then `Bind` a capability and T3 commits through one FSM; public capability and commit
   readers return the result. No direct projection writer or test-only export counts. This test also
   carries the *Pasture-issued human decision* leg deferred from item 4.
9. `TestSliceStartAvailabilityUnderHookWriteLoad` — **availability.** Launches the §4.4 writer
   estimate as distinct built-binary child processes on one file-backed `pasture.db` behind a
   barrier, and requires the slice to start within the 2-second deadline for every run of a fixed
   sample. Also asserts the contended/uncontended p99 ratio bound and the absolute
   one-transaction-per-delivery count from §4.6.
10. `TestSliceStartHonestFailureUnderInjectedDelay` — **honest failure.** Deterministically injects
    the delay rather than racing for it, and requires exactly the honest "enqueued but never started"
    error naming the slice id and the deadline, with `Completed=false`, `SliceFailed` fired, no
    fabricated projection success, and every receipt committed during the window still readable
    through the public bounded reader.

Splitting 9 from 10 is `aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 1's fix and it is right: PROPOSAL-8's single test
accepted, as a passing outcome, the regression it existed to prevent. Item 9 can only pass by the
deadline holding; item 10 can only pass by the failure being honest; neither can pass by the other's
outcome.

**Wave placement and flake policy** (`aura-plugins-237wx` B1 fix 4). Item 10 is deterministic and
race-clean and runs in the **default mandatory `-race` wave**. Item 9 makes wall-clock assertions and
is therefore **excluded from the default `-race` wave** and run in an explicitly named measurement
wave without `-race`; §16.4's blanket `-race` rule carries this one named carve-out rather than
silently contradicting a wall-clock threshold. Item 9's parameters: 200 deliveries per writer,
nearest-rank p99 over the sorted per-`Apply` sample, three consecutive runs required green, and a
single flake reopens the §4.4 revisit trigger rather than being retried away.

| S2-CLAUDE-ACTIVATION | host descriptor, generated event/field ordinals, activation states and reasons | independent manifest, partial activation, withheld report, generated-binary T1 path, `ingress_invalid.yaml` corpus, no-second-table guard, generated-payload-parse guard | generator, frontend, registration/codegen, CLI/handler, generated assets, old path removal |
| S3-INTERPRETATION | definition service, derived definition state, build identity, envelope, enrichment, draft/result/slot types | connected T1->T2->reader, two-version history, unknown schema, missing and contradictory enrichment, dirty and missing build, defensive copies | resolver, state fold, codebook, enricher, canonical writer and readers; delete old lowering |
| S4-LINEAGE | typed relation/confidence/query contracts | positive human-to-commit forward and reverse proof from a real `UserPromptSubmit`, missing and contradictory cases, fanout/cycle/depth/node/edge/cursor/replay | VCS/tool/worktree enrichment, link writer, bounded query command |
| S5-CONTEXT | policy/packet/plan/attempt/result/state types, bounded-history selection, UAT-selected channel contract | committed-only, recipient isolation, policy evolution, retry and correlation, attempt crash gap, ack negatives, truncation and suppression, retention corpora | projector, journal service, state rebuild, selected transport and command wiring |
| S6-RESPONSE | typed native response and process-health contract selected by UAT | exact host response fixtures, neutral/fault/deny isolation, timeout budget | mechanical encoder/service and handler wiring |
| S7-PROVENANCE-DEADLINE | closed time condition, canonical fields, typed expiry failure, private transaction-time source | canonical round trip and conflict, DBOS parity, equality boundary, fake-clock unit cases, lock-spanning race | transaction evaluator after replay and lock, public aliases, second Pasture pin |
| S8-CONTROL-CUTOVER | capability scope and thirteen axes, state, issue/bind/revoke/commit inputs, typed mismatch and state errors, phase evidence | thirteen per-axis mismatch cases, three revocation timings, already-consumed, fresh-op across four states, independent-process races, exact retry and conflict, old-writer rejection, projection replay | control service, capability consumption plus phase CAS, engine/handler/audit cutover |

### 18.4 Dependencies and merge timing

| Integration point | Exporter | Consumers | Merge gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IP-P0** context-bearing Apply with caller deadline | upstream Provenance (P0-PIN) | S1 | upstream release and Pasture first re-pin **before S1 L3** |
| IP-0 immutable phase law and adjacency oracle | S0 | S3, S5, S8 | S0 L3 before candidate, context, and control tests |
| IP-1 occurrence/definition/envelope/reader contracts | S1 | S2-S8 | S1 L1 before consumer L1; S1 L3 before Enabled registration |
| IP-2 fixed actor, T1 appender, public occurrence reader | S1 | S2 | S1 L3 before the first Enabled event |
| **IP-2b** first Enabled event with generated registration and built binary | S2 | S1's two load cases in `internal/engine/budget/**` | **S2 L3 before the shared-file black-box gate**. Sequence is `S1 L3 -> S2 L3 -> shared black-box test -> M1 complete`. |
| IP-3 hostcontract generated descriptors and activation manifest | S2 | codegen, S3, S6 | per-event fixture proof before that event becomes Enabled |
| IP-4 T2 result algebra, exact definitions, build identity | S3 | S4, S5, S8 | S3 L3 before lineage, context, and control |
| IP-5 bounded explicit lineage | S4 | S5, S8, user queries | S4 L3 before lineage-dependent context and control rules |
| IP-6 disclosure plan/attempt/result contract | S5 | S6 and readers | UAT channel/ack choice and S5 L3 |
| IP-7 transaction-time condition | S7 | S8 | reviewed upstream release and Pasture second re-pin before S8 L3 |
| IP-8 capability and phase control cutover | S8 | engine, handlers | S0, S3, S4, S7 merged; one cutover, no dual writer |

**IP-2b closes the ordering loop that three reviewers found.** PROPOSAL-8 made the shared-file load
case an S1 **L2** deliverable while it required S2's generated registration and built binary, and
IP-2 ordered S1 before S2 — so an S1 L2 test could only go green after a different slice's L3
(`aura-plugins-u2d51` BLOCKER 1; `aura-plugins-237wx` B1 tail; `aura-plugins-oygyo` R9 residual).

The fix keeps **S1 as owner** and moves the **gate**. S1 owns the T1 write, so S1 owns the proof of
the T1 write budget; and S8, the natural engine owner, arrives at M6, so assigning it there would
leave M1's central claim unproven for five milestones (`aura-plugins-oygyo`). Moving ownership to S2
as `aura-plugins-u2d51` proposed is therefore rejected: it would hand the write budget's proof to a
slice that does not own the write. What changes is timing: the shared-file black-box gate is
declared **post-S2-L3** rather than S1 L2, and S1 additionally keeps a receipt-service
transaction-budget test that drives its own service from N subprocesses without generated
registration and can go green inside S1.

S0 may proceed in parallel with other prerequisite work after ratification. S7 may proceed in
parallel but must not re-pin before P0-PIN has. S2 events activate independently as their fixture
and run refs pass. S3 waits for at least one Enabled T1 vertical, not all 30. Catalogue completion
continues independently and blocks only the complete-catalogue claim.

### 18.5 Prototype quarantine and exact disposition

The six stopped untracked files remain quarantined and cannot be committed as-is:

| Untracked file | Exclusive owner | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go` | S2, then conditional sequential transfer | rewrite as typed process composition; fresh delivery operation; no semantic selection |
| `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go` | S2 | rewrite as a per-Enabled authentic generated/binary/T1/public-reader proof. The current `sql.Open` plus raw `SELECT` at `:132-195` is also the named target of the §16.4 bounded-reader guard. |
| `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` | S2, then conditional sequential transfer | rewrite receipt-first; optional typed stages; mechanical response only |
| `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_test.go` | S2 | invert the parse-before-store and nonzero-refusal assertions |
| `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go` | S1 | delete; replace with the journal-native receipt package; no audit or activity direct writes |
| `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder_test.go` | S1 | delete; replace with result-slot and independent-process append tests |

Committed prototype disposition is also exclusive:

| Existing path | Owner | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/lifecycle/event.go`, `event_test.go` | S1 | replace with the canonical model; remove digest and the one-semantic event |
| `internal/lifecycle/key.go`, `key_test.go` | S1 | delete; the static guard prevents a replacement replay key |
| `internal/lifecycle/frontend.go`, `frontend_test.go`, `fixtures_test.go`, `verifier_internal_test.go` | S2 | replace with private capture and independent activation fixtures |
| `internal/lifecycle/backend.go`, `backend_test.go` | S2 | delete the same-package host behaviour side door |
| `internal/lifecycle/claude/**` | S2 | move and rewrite under ingress from the generated descriptor; no duplicate table |
| `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, `lower_test.go`, `lower_internal_test.go` | S3 | replace with pure T2 canonicalization and effect mapping |
| `internal/runtime/lifecycle.go`, `lifecycle_profiles.go`, `lookup.go` | S2 | replace manual host behaviour tables with generated derivatives and a facade |
| `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go` and generated Claude hook assets | S2 | registration and support only; no parsing, semantics, or authority |
| generated `pasture-lifecycle.py` and the hidden env-selected lifecycle adapter path | S2 | delete when the first replacement event is Enabled; no dual semantic path |
| `internal/tasks/system_identity.go` | S1 | add a read-only persisted `(actor, authority)` resolve for lifecycle ingress; ingress must not invoke the activation aggregate |
| `internal/provadapter/actors.go` | S1 | expose the read-only resolve; leave `ActivatePastureSystem` for bootstrap only |
| `internal/engine/{control,workflow,projection,activities}.go` and direct transition audit writers | S8 | route through journal-backed control; projections and operational evidence only |

## 19. Open Plan UAT decisions

No option below is selected here. The open UAT records the final choice and updates the URD before
ratification and slicing. Each is a real engineering alternative with stated tradeoffs, not an
approval level.

### 19.1 Retention mode — **now an M1 blocker**

- **Metadata only.** Lowest privacy and operations cost. Unavailable content remains explicitly
  unresolved as `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect, so the
  deletion and no-resurrection half of the matrix is trivially satisfied.
- **Encrypted local payload.** Richer local reconstruction. Requires key handling, deletion,
  rotation, tombstone, and no-resurrection guarantees, and a fail-closed path on a missing or wrong
  key.
- **External content-addressed payload.** Durable and shareable evidence. Adds a store, credentials,
  an availability dependency, deletion obligations, and a privacy surface outside the local file.

This choice gates M1, not M4 (§15). Choosing metadata-only is the smallest M1; either payload mode
adds its full matrix to the M1 essential gate before any payload-bearing event can be Enabled.

### 19.2 First activated high-value hooks

UAT receives the current activation readiness report and may select only events whose authentic
exact-version fixture and production path already pass. No grouping overrides per-event proof, and
this proposal does not preselect an event.

This choice is also the shared-file write throttle (§4.5 option E), so the UAT weighs two properties
per candidate event, not only its evidence value:

- **Fanout.** Session- and turn-scoped events (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`,
  `UserPromptSubmit`) produce far fewer deliveries than per-tool-call events (`PreToolUse`,
  `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`), which fire on every tool call and scale with subagent count.
- **Blocking profile.** A gate event appends inside a window the host holds open, so its contention
  competes directly with engine signal delivery, whereas an observational event does not.

Candidate groupings: session spine (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Setup`); human-signal ingress
(`UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`) — note this is the M3 lineage prerequisite;
tool/artifact lineage (`PostToolUse`, `FileChanged`) — note `PostToolUse` is per-tool-call;
multi-agent orchestration (`SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TeammateIdle`).

Enabling any blocking **per-tool-call** event additionally requires `aura-plugins-cvlu6` to have
resolved the start-signal deadline question.

### 19.3 Context delivery and acknowledgement

Delivery alternatives:
- **Generated start/compaction material.** No live host round trip; context is baked into what the
  host loads. Cheapest and most reliable, but refresh is coarse.
- **Dynamic per-contract host response.** Context rides the hook response, so it is phase-exact.
  Requires the response encoder (M5) and couples context to blocking-hook timing.
- **Explicit `pasture epoch context` pull.** Agent asks when it needs context. No host coupling at
  all, but delivery depends on the agent choosing to ask.

Acknowledgement alternatives:
- **Positive host evidence.** Strongest proof; only available where the pinned contract emits it.
- **Explicit agent receipt.** Requires the agent to call back; proves receipt but not comprehension.
- **Unavailable.** Record delivery and unknown. Honest and always available.

UAT selects one compatible pair and its failure and retry semantics. The pair determines which S5
adapter file exists (§18.1) and whether a `DeliveryCorrelationToken` is needed at all (§10.2).

### 19.4 Future verdict and process-health encoding

- **Typed host-native verdict separated from process health.** Cleanest: a deny is a deliberate
  typed value and a crash is not. Requires a per-contract response fixture proving both encodings.
- **Exact native exit/status semantics where the pinned contract proves them.** Least new
  machinery; only defensible for contracts whose exit-code meaning is pinned.
- **Continued neutral-only behaviour.** Zero risk of an internal fault denying a user's work; no
  gating capability ever ships.

No deny, ask, or defer value becomes reachable until this UAT and the exact response fixture pass.
Generic CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny.

### 19.5 Artifact enrichment depth and storage

- **Commit and path metadata only.** Cheapest; lineage answers "which commit" but not "which bytes".
- **Encrypted local diff or snapshot.** Answers "which bytes" locally; inherits the encrypted-local
  key, deletion, and rotation obligations.
- **External content-addressed evidence.** Answers "which bytes" durably and shareably; inherits the
  external store's credential and availability obligations.

Orthogonal to occurrence identity and must be compatible with the retention mode selected in 19.1.
Missing depth never promotes an observation beyond `RelationObservedPath`.

PROPOSAL-9 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 3/3 (Sections 20-22, Appendices A and B)

## 20. Validation checklist

Structural and architectural:

- [ ] Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit remains exactly 30 events in pinned order.
- [ ] Hostcontract is the sole production event/name/field/identity/behaviour source.
- [ ] Phase adjacency exists in exactly one place: `pkg/protocol`. Candidate `(From,To)` is
      validated against `PhaseSpecFor` at emit time.
- [ ] Enabled and Withheld are disjoint, complete, typed, and independently proved.
- [ ] At least one UAT-selected fixture-ready event can deliver M1 without all 30.
- [ ] Every separate delivery has a fresh operation ID and a distinct occurrence JournalID.
- [ ] No lifecycle or public symbol exposes replay, dedup, repeat count, or payload occurrence
      identity, and the guard is scoped to lifecycle results only.
- [ ] `OccurrenceRecord` is the only public post-T1 occurrence type and is deeply immutable.
- [ ] Raw JSON is confined to private ingress and retention code.

INV-1 and identity hygiene:

- [ ] Every record is classified as immutable snapshot, immutable fact, derived projection, or
      build input, and the classification table is the guard's data source.
- [ ] No immutable-snapshot type contains a lifecycle-status enum field. `DefinitionSnapshot` has
      no `Status`.
- [ ] Every derived projection carries `SnapshotJournalID` and is reproduced exactly by replay
      after deleting the projection.
- [ ] Definition state is expressed as append-only `DefinitionStateFact` and read as derived
      `DefinitionStateRecord` folded in JournalID order. `ResolveHistorical` returns no status.
- [ ] No record carries a bare `provenance.JournalID` beside its own typed identity. Every typed
      view exposes `JournalID()`.
- [ ] There is exactly one `Confidence` type; the no-promotion rule is a direct comparison.
- [ ] There is no `DisclosureAttemptID` nonce; the attempt JournalID plus the operation ID are the
      only attempt identities. Any channel nonce lives in the selected adapter.
- [ ] Every disclosure API boundary uses typed IDs, never a bare `provenance.JournalID`.

Semantics, definitions, and build honesty:

- [ ] T2 defines every input, output, exact definition, operation, clock, effect, and slot.
- [ ] Enrichment snapshots are immutable, snapshot-bound, and bounded.
- [ ] Missing or contradictory enrichment is typed unresolved evidence.
- [ ] Definitions resolve by immutable JournalID; retirement never erases history.
- [ ] `BuildIdentityStatus` is typed; only `BuildIdentityExact` backs an Enabled activation or a
      normative commit; dirty and missing builds yield `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild`.
- [ ] Same VCS revision with different build content yields two distinct definitions, neither
      overwriting the other.

Context and control:

- [ ] Context projection is pure and plan/attempt/result facts correlate exactly.
- [ ] Every bounded-history collection has an explicit constructor limit and the newest-first
      at-snapshot selection rule, with typed truncation. Completeness-required truncation suppresses
      the packet rather than delivering it partial.
- [ ] Disclosure current state rebuilds identically from immutable journal history.
- [ ] `EpochControlService` exposes `Issue`, `Bind`, `Revoke`, and `CommitCandidate`, and scope
      mismatch is a typed result naming the mismatched axis.
- [ ] All thirteen `CapabilityScopeAxis` values have an independent test case.
- [ ] Transaction time is checked after SQLite lock acquisition and after exact replay.
- [ ] Capability Bound -> Consumed, expiry, and phase CAS share one Apply.
- [ ] One immutable FSM and one journal-backed control writer remain.

Readers and tests:

- [ ] Readers define concrete typed filters, pages, cursors, truncation, and errors for every record
      family, including `DefinitionStates`.
- [ ] Production tests read only public bounded APIs, **and a static guard enforces it** over a
      named file set, with exactly one whitelisted delta-snapshot helper.
- [ ] §13.1, §14, §15, and the §16.2 matrices are expressed as typed YAML corpora with must-pass and
      must-fail classification and provenance metadata.
- [ ] Every corpus has a non-vacuity guard: non-empty, every declared case executed, every must-fail
      case proven to flip when its guard is removed, and every declared enum dimension covered.
- [ ] Every static guard names the mutation operator that must turn it red, and that operator is
      run.
- [ ] Raw host bytes are separate referenced files, never inlined in YAML.
- [ ] Selected retention matrix passes end to end, including tombstone and no-resurrection
      behaviour, **as an M1 gate**.
- [ ] Positive human-to-code lineage passes forward and reverse production queries from a real
      `UserPromptSubmit` occurrence, with no test-seeded human signal.

Resource model:

- [ ] P0-PIN has landed and Pasture is re-pinned before S1 L3.
- [ ] Hook ingress passes a 1-second caller lock-acquisition deadline and fails with a definite
      typed result and zero writes rather than retrying past it.
- [ ] T1 is exactly one write transaction per delivery on the shared file, with no second
      per-delivery projection, audit, or activation write. Lifecycle ingress never invokes the
      activation aggregate.
- [ ] M1 derives lifecycle projections by replay; the hook path performs no projection write.
- [ ] No fixed sub-100 ms lock-retry loop exists anywhere on the hook path.
- [ ] Contended p99 `Apply` <= K x uncontended p99 measured in the same run, same instrumentation,
      same race mode, with K named once in §4.4.
- [ ] Uncontended hold p99 is measured and reported against the 5 ms design estimate. It is not a
      pass/fail gate, and the proposal says so.
- [ ] `TestSliceStartAvailabilityUnderHookWriteLoad` and
      `TestSliceStartHonestFailureUnderInjectedDelay` both pass; the first is in the named non-race
      measurement wave with a stated sample size and flake policy, the second in the default `-race`
      wave.
- [ ] No blocking per-tool-call event is Enabled before `aura-plugins-cvlu6` resolves the
      start-signal deadline question.
- [ ] The proposal contains no claim that 48 writers is a ceiling, that 240 ms is a worst case, or
      that the budget is enforced.

Ownership and process:

- [ ] Ownership is derived from the set of files that MUST change, then checked for exclusivity.
- [ ] Every M1-M6 file, generated artifact, migration, projection, test, and upstream extension has
      exactly one owner, including `internal/tasks/system_identity.go` and
      `internal/provadapter/actors.go`.
- [ ] `go.mod` / `go.sum` ownership is sequential: P0-PIN then S7, never simultaneous.
- [ ] There is no engine-directory ownership exception; the load cases live in S1-owned
      `internal/engine/budget/**`.
- [ ] All six untracked and all committed prototype paths are rewritten or deleted by their named
      owner.
- [ ] All Go tests run with `-race` except the one named measurement wave; static, build, Nix,
      generation, and diff gates pass before implementation commits.

## 21. BDD acceptance criteria

- **Given** two byte-identical host CLI invocations, **when** an Enabled registration receives both,
  **then** it mints two operation IDs and returns two distinct occurrence JournalIDs in database
  order, **and should not** expose or infer replay, deduplication, a repeat count, a time window, or
  payload identity.
- **Given** one internal T1 Apply retry, **when** the same operation ID and exact canonical input is
  retried, **then** Provenance returns the original journal result, **and should not** convert that
  storage property into host-delivery semantics.
- **Given** only one authentic event fixture is ready, **when** activation is generated, **then**
  that event may be Enabled and queryable while the other 29 are visibly Withheld with typed
  reasons, **and should not** claim full-catalogue support or register an unproved event.
- **Given** an event whose backing build identity is `BuildIdentityDirtySource` or
  `BuildIdentityUnresolved`, **when** activation is generated, **then** the event is Withheld with
  `WithheldUnverifiedBuild`, **and should not** be Enabled or claim a clean provenance envelope.
- **Given** the UAT-selected retention matrix has not passed for an event's capture class, **when**
  activation is generated, **then** the event is Withheld with `WithheldRetentionMatrixPending`,
  **and should not** be Enabled at M1.
- **Given** a registered malformed, duplicate-key, invalid-UTF-8, truncated, or over-limit delivery,
  **when** trusted contract and event coordinates exist, **then** T1 records one bounded
  `OccurrenceRecord` with the exact `CaptureDisposition` and later planes remain empty, **and should
  not** drop the receipt, retain forbidden bytes, or guess semantics.
- **Given** T2 fails after T1, **when** the occurrence is read, **then** the receipt remains visible
  and eligible for later exact interpretation, **and should not** roll back with enrichment.
- **Given** a definition that has been retired, **when** it is resolved historically, **then** the
  immutable body and ref are returned with no status field at all, **and should not** return a
  status inside the snapshot or allow a status to be written into a snapshot.
- **Given** a definition activated then retired, **when** the definition-state projection is deleted
  and the journal is replayed, **then** `DefinitionStateRecord` is reproduced identically in
  JournalID order, **and should not** depend on any mutable status column.
- **Given** one occurrence and two exact codebook, interpreter, and build definitions, **when** both
  are interpreted, **then** both immutable batches and all outputs resolve their exact definition
  JournalIDs, **and should not** overwrite history or select latest implicitly.
- **Given** two builds of the same VCS revision with different build content identities, **when**
  each interprets the same occurrence, **then** two distinct definitions and two distinct
  interpretation histories exist, **and should not** collapse into one build for that revision.
- **Given** unavailable or contradictory capture or enrichment, **when** T2 runs, **then** it emits
  a typed unresolved fact with a typed basis, **and should not** assert a human, actor, artifact,
  commit, causality, delivery, or authority fact.
- **Given** a candidate whose `(From, To)` pair is not adjacent under `PhaseSpecFor`, **when** the
  codebook attempts to emit it, **then** the constructor returns `CandidateAdjacencyError` and no
  candidate is written, **and should not** be deferred to T3's CAS or cause the codebook to carry
  its own adjacency table.
- **Given** a path-only artifact signal, **when** lineage is queried, **then** it returns only
  `RelationObservedPath` plus the causal gap, **and should not** invent bytes, diff, commit, actor,
  or human motivation.
- **Given** a real `UserPromptSubmit` occurrence delivered through the generated registration and
  built binary, **when** the M3 forward and reverse readers run, **then** the same explicit
  human-signal / agent / tool / VCS / worktree / artifact / commit chain is returned within bounds,
  **and should not** use direct SQL, test exports, a test-seeded human signal, or timestamp
  proximity.
- **Given** one committed state and two context policy versions, **when** each plans disclosure,
  **then** two immutable plan histories resolve their exact policy and build definitions and later
  attempts and results cite the right plan, **and should not** mutate FSM state or prior disclosure
  facts.
- **Given** a context projection whose bounded basis, prior-plan, or acknowledgement history is
  truncated under a policy that declares completeness required, **when** planning runs, **then** the
  projector returns `ContextCompletenessError` and a `DisclosureSuppressed` fact is recorded, **and
  should not** deliver a silently partial packet.
- **Given** a delivery attempt whose host acknowledgement is unavailable, **when** the result is
  recorded, **then** history remains delivered or unknown according to the selected acknowledgement
  mode, **and should not** infer acknowledgement.
- **Given** candidate-only, stale, unauthorized, wrong-recipient, or unknown-definition context
  input, **when** planning is attempted, **then** no disclosure or FSM state changes, **and should
  not** let candidate state drive context.
- **Given** a bound capability and a commit request that differs on exactly one of the thirteen
  scope axes, **when** T3 runs, **then** it returns `CapabilityScopeMismatch` naming that exact axis
  with zero writes, **and should not** return a generic refusal or succeed on any axis.
- **Given** a capability revoked before bind, before commit, or racing commit, **when** each timing
  is exercised, **then** each returns a typed state error with zero partial writes across journal,
  capability, phase, decision, context, and projection planes, **and should not** collapse the three
  timings into one outcome.
- **Given** an already-consumed capability, **when** a second commit is attempted, **then** it
  returns `CapabilityStateError{Observed: Consumed, Required: Bound}`, **and should not** produce a
  second commit.
- **Given** a fresh operation ID against stale, revoked, consumed, or expired current state, **when**
  T3 runs, **then** each of the four returns its own typed result with zero writes, **and should
  not** treat them as one case.
- **Given** a fresh capability operation queued before expiry but admitted after expiry, **when** it
  acquires SQLite write ownership, **then** transaction time returns typed expiry and zero partial
  writes, **and should not** consume the capability or advance phase based on a pre-Apply clock
  check.
- **Given** an already committed capability operation after expiry, **when** its exact operation ID
  and input is retried, **then** exact replay returns the original result before current-state and
  deadline checks, **and should not** create a second commit.
- **Given** two separate processes racing one capability or one current phase, **when** T3 commits,
  **then** one wins and every loser has a typed current, expired, consumed, or scope-mismatch result
  with zero semantic writes, **and should not** mutate context or a direct phase projection, and
  **should not** be demonstrated with goroutines in one process.
- **Given** Claude 2.1.210 `ElicitationResult`, **when** only host request and server strings
  correlate it, **then** it remains evidence and candidate, **and should not** become a
  registered-human decision or a normative transition.
- **Given** each retention option, **when** its parameterized canary, deletion, and replay corpus
  runs, **then** only policy-permitted content behaviour occurs and occurrence and causal metadata
  remains, **and should not** leak or resurrect raw content.
- **Given** a cursor from another query, a future, stale, or tampered cursor, a zero or oversized
  page, or oversized lineage bounds, **when** a public reader runs, **then** it returns the exact
  typed error before SQL, **and should not** silently restart, skip, duplicate, or run an unbounded
  traversal.
- **Given** lifecycle, phase, lineage, disclosure, definition-state, and capability-state projection
  deletion, **when** the journal replays, **then** public readers return identical canonical history
  and current state, **and should not** depend on independent projection IDs.
- **Given** hook-ingress write load at the §4.4 writer estimate on one shared `pasture.db`, **when**
  a slice waits for its `start_slice` signal in the named non-race measurement wave, **then** the
  slice starts within the 2-second deadline on every run of the fixed sample, contended p99 `Apply`
  stays at or below K times the uncontended p99 measured in that same run and same race mode, and
  exactly one write transaction occurs per delivery, **and should not** exceed one write transaction
  per delivery, retry the lock on a fixed sub-100 ms interval, or be asserted against an absolute
  wall-clock threshold inside the mandatory `-race` wave.
- **Given** a deterministically injected delay past the start-signal deadline, **when** the slice
  workflow runs in the default `-race` wave, **then** it fails with exactly the honest "enqueued but
  never started" error naming the slice id and the deadline, with `Completed=false` and
  `SliceFailed` fired, and every receipt committed during the window stays readable through the
  public bounded reader, **and should not** fabricate slice success or drop a receipt.
- **Given** a contended append that cannot acquire the write lock within the 1-second caller
  deadline, **when** P0-PIN is in force, **then** it returns a definite typed failure with zero
  writes and a neutral exit 0 with an actionable diagnostic naming the deadline, **and should not**
  stall to the 5-second connection pragma or claim a receipt.
- **Given** a production-path acceptance test file in the named set, **when** it imports
  `database/sql`, imports a projection-internal package, or contains a SQL string literal outside
  the one whitelisted delta-snapshot helper, **then** the static guard fails, **and should not**
  require a broad custom taint analyzer.
- **Given** any type declared an immutable snapshot, **when** a lifecycle-status enum field is added
  to it, **then** the immutability guard fails, **and should not** be caught only by review.
- **Given** a clean generation run, **when** a second host descriptor table, a phase-adjacency table
  outside `pkg/protocol`, a replay symbol, a semantic branch in generated output, generated code
  that parses the payload, an env or argv operation selector, or a generic exit-to-deny mapping is
  introduced, **then** the corresponding static or generation test fails and its named mutation
  operator is the thing that proved it, **and should not** require a broad custom taint analyzer.
- **Given** any corpus in §16.0, **when** it is run, **then** its non-vacuity report shows a
  non-empty corpus, every declared case executed, every must-fail case flipping when its guard is
  removed, and every declared enum dimension covered, **and should not** pass with an unexecuted
  case or an uncovered dimension.

## 22. Tradeoffs, deferrals, and exit state

| Decision | Benefit | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| One Provenance journal and one FSM | No split-brain graph, phase, context, or identity truth | Services use explicit operations and bounded reads |
| Append every delivery | No silent undercount | Host retries remain visible for later analysis |
| Event-granular activation | Useful verified value arrives early without false claims | Registration and support output change as proof becomes available |
| One canonical occurrence | No conversion drift after T1 | Private ingress capture cannot be reused as a public model |
| Immutable definition JournalIDs | Historical semantic meaning is resolvable; the provisional codebook does not fossilize | Activation, retirement, and old decoders must be retained |
| **INV-1: snapshots carry no status; state is facts plus a derived projection** | Removes an entire defect class instead of its third instance; every derived read is replay-checkable | One more static guard, one more classification table, and two reader methods where there was one |
| Separate T1/T2/context/T3 operations | Receipt and honest external-side-effect gaps survive later failures | Users can observe partial processing |
| Minimal transaction-time condition (S7, M6) | Correct expiry at lock admission without a predicate language | Requires a reviewed upstream Provenance release before M6 |
| **Bound the ingress wait upstream (P0-PIN), keep the budget as an SLO** | Turns an unbounded 5-second stall into a bounded, typed, fast failure, for roughly one day of upstream work extending a pattern already proven in the same package. Makes the off-path spool measurable rather than speculative. | Does not *prove* the 240 ms figure and does not bound total concurrent writers. The write budget is an observational SLO with a named revisit trigger, not an enforced contract. |
| **Not building cross-process admission control** | Avoids three bad mechanisms: `flock` leaks permits on crash, a daemon socket makes hooks fail when the daemon is down which is worse than slow, and SQLite-as-semaphore is self-defeating | An adversarial or misconfigured workload can still exceed the writer estimate. Detection is by measurement and by the revisit trigger, not by refusal. |
| **Relative contention bound instead of an absolute p99 gate** | Self-calibrating, so it is invariant to `-race` overhead and CI hardware, and it cannot reproduce the `aura-plugins-ay4yn` flake | Does not detect a uniform slowdown that inflates both numbers equally; the absolute transaction count and the uncontended report cover that gap |
| Concrete snapshot readers | Bounded, stable, black-box validation | Callers paginate and handle typed cursor errors |
| **Corpus idiom with non-vacuity guards** | The mechanism that catches self-deceiving tests, which this project has now paid for four times | A harness to build in S1 and a discipline every slice must follow |
| UAT-parameterized retention, **gating M1** | No privacy policy is silently chosen, and no payload-bearing event ships before its matrix passes | M1 waits for the selected mode's full matrix instead of deferring it to M4 |
| One write transaction per delivery, with activation as the throttle | Keeps hook ingress from starving the engine's 2-second start-signal deadline without adding a batching layer or a new writer daemon | Caps how many high-fanout blocking events can be Enabled at once |

Deferred without loss of M1-M6 integrity: a runtime-authored codebook language, probabilistic causal
inference, cross-machine total order, a generic fourth harness, unsupported Claude 2.1.210 human
authority, and any deliberate native deny before its focused UAT.

Deliberately stated but not solved here: the engine's 2-second start-signal deadline itself. §4
fixes the write model hook ingress must meet, names the measured coupling, bounds the wait, and
requires two load cases that separate availability from honest failure. Whether 2 seconds remains
defensible once hook writes share the file, and whether it should become configurable,
budget-derived, or replaced by a readiness handshake, belongs to `aura-plugins-cvlu6`. Changing that
deadline inside this proposal would be editing another subsystem's contract from the outside.

Also deliberately not solved: an enforced concurrent-writer bound. Option B (off-path spool) is the
recorded escalation and its trigger conditions are in §4.4.

The next valid action is a fresh independent mirrored review wave coordinated outside this proposal
task. If that wave accepts, the still-open Plan UAT must resolve §19 before ratification, and §19.1
now blocks M1 rather than M4. The obsolete IMPL_PLAN `aura-plugins-sgxp6` remains blocked by this
proposal and must be replaced by the supervisor after those gates. No implementation, reviewer
launch, ratification, commit, or push follows from creating PROPOSAL-9.

P0-PIN IS ALREADY SATISFIED — recorded for reviewers.

The proposal treats the upstream context-bearing apply as a pending external dependency whose failure would fail the M1 gate. It landed while this proposal was being written.

  upstream  provenance 0976165224e93175225bad42dcea3807cd578bd9 on feat/governed-allocation-integration, pushed
  pasture   f513772 pins v0.0.4-0.20260730015136-0976165224e9, pushed

Verified in this tree at f513772: go mod verify clean, CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... OK, go vet ./... OK, full CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./... green across 38 packages.

Measured upstream: a writer blocked on the SQLite write lock gives up in ~303ms with a deadline versus ~5.008s without one, and the test was mutation-verified (reverting the plumbing failed at ~5.013s). The capability is an OPTIONAL interface (ContextJournal.ApplyContext), so existing Journal implementers are untouched and nothing in Pasture broke.

Reviewers: do NOT flag P0-PIN as an unmet external dependency. Do still judge whether the proposal cites the capability correctly and whether S1's gating on it is right. The exact upstream signature is ContextJournal.ApplyContext; the proposal was told to reference the capability rather than freeze a signature, so verify it did not freeze a wrong one.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE — Axis B (test quality and validatability), `general` half of the mirrored pair, on PROPOSAL-9 aura-plugins-p4e29.

Binary vote, no severity tree. Design-only; no source, proposal field, commit, or push changed. P0-PIN treated as satisfied and not re-litigated.

All four PROPOSAL-8 Axis-B blockers are substantively closed (evidence in the task description). Four new blockers, three of which share one shape: a gate was correctly moved or newly declared and the ownership/coverage that must satisfy it was not re-derived — the exact failure mode §18.0's own ownership rule exists to prevent, applied to the M1 production file set but not the M1 validation file set.

B1 — Retention gates M1 (§15, §17, §19.1, §20), but §16.0 and §18.1 own retention_encrypted_local.yaml and retention_external_cas.yaml in S5, which §18.1 marks M4, and §18.4 has no integration point ordering any part of S5 before M1. Under two of the three live UAT modes M1 is gated on an M4 slice's corpus AND its production path (key handling, fail-closed, tombstone, rotation). That is the IP-2b loop reintroduced. Second defect in the same gate: §17 makes the whole matrix an unconditional M1 gate while §21 and §15 make it per-capture-class — the A1 defect relocated, not removed.

B2 — Two corpora declare CoverageSpec over enums their owning slice cannot produce, while §16.0 makes non-vacuity failure a hard test failure. reader_cursor.yaml is S1/M1 but TruncatedDepthLimit/NodeLimit/EdgeLimit and CursorInvalidLineageBounds are S4/M3 and TruncatedHistoryBound is S5/M4. guard_mutation.yaml is S1/M1 but at least six of twelve operators mutate S0/S2 artifacts, and §18.3's S1 L2 leaf names only three guards while S2's L2 leaf names two more. Both are red from S1 L2 until M3/M6.

B3 — The non-vacuity condition that justifies the harness ('every MustFail case passes when its guard is removed') is unexecutable for seven of the eight corpora. Case has no field naming the guard or operator that proves it — CaseProvenance covers the URD's provenance half, the mutation half is absent — and NonVacuityReport.GuardsProvenBy is per-corpus, not per-case. All twelve MutationOperatorID values map to §16.4 static guards, so guard_mutation.yaml is the only corpus with a defined 'remove its guard' operation. Concretely: a capability_scope.yaml whose thirteen must-fail rows all refuse on state before reaching the axis comparison satisfies every stated condition — thirteen green rows, one guard, twelve unproven axes. That is 0lbsy BLOCKER 2 surviving its own fix.

B4 — P0-PIN changed the load test's failure mode to receipt loss (§13.1 row 8: no receipt, zero writes) and neither gate can see it. §16.1 item 9 and the §21 BDD assert slice start, the p99 ratio, and one-transaction-per-delivery, and never that a delivery produced a receipt. A hook that gives up at 1s stops competing, so the 2-second start assertion gets EASIER as loss rises; the per-delivery transaction count is satisfied by zero; and §4.6 never says whether a deadline-failed Apply enters the p99 sample — exclude it and the contended tail is censored exactly where it is worst, include it at 1000ms and K=48 against a ~5ms baseline makes a few timeouts fatal. The choice between 'cannot fail' and 'fails on a handful' is left to the implementer, and receipt-loss rate is absent from §4.4's revisit triggers and §22's cost cell while §22 headlines 'Append every delivery | No silent undercount'.

Plus C1-C5 (non-blocking, same revision): §4.6 points at §15.3 and §15.1 items 8/9 which do not exist (real: §16.1 items 9/10, §16.4), and §20 says K is named in §4.4 where it is only referenced; §16.1 items 9/10 have an owner, package, and gate but no L1/L2/L3 leaf in §18.3; the bounded-reader guard is an allowlist and fails open on omission; §16.4's 'a guard with no operator is not a guard' is contradicted by three rows proven by fixtures rather than MutationOperatorID values; 'eight corpora' is ten files.

Explicitly NOT requesting: the semantically-identical-different-byte case (byte-identical dominates; settled), cursor/lineage expansion, all-30 tightening, reversing item 9's -race carve-out, or promoting the uncontended hold to a gate. No over-testing found to remove.

Full review with section and file:line citations and concrete fixes: aura-plugins-3hkoz.

text:
VOTE: REVISE — independent Axis B (test quality and validatability), `general` half of the mirrored pair, on PROPOSAL-9. Review task: aura-plugins-3hkoz.

CLOSED from the PROPOSAL-8 wave, with evidence in the review task: 237wx B1 (relative bound, absolute transaction count, 5ms demoted, p99 in the BDD, sample size / nearest-rank / three-green / no-retry-away flake policy, one-sided -race carve-out, availability and honest-failure split into §16.1 items 9/10); B1 tail (IP-2b, S1 keeps ownership, gate moves post-S2-L3, S1-only receipt-service test, engine-directory exception removed rather than declared); B2 (all seven cases restored and marked, Appendix B re-audited and the three narrowed xwiuk rows marked MODIFY); B3 on adoption (§16.0 harness, eight corpus families, twelve operators); B4 (bounded-reader guard with MutateDirectSQLInProductionTest and exactly one named whitelisted helper); A2 (real UserPromptSubmit, Pasture-issued decision moved to M6); A3 (TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus owns §13.1); item 7 (which races need processes). 0lbsy BLOCKER 1 split, BLOCKER 2 API, BLOCKER 3 build honesty, IMPORTANT 1 and 2 all closed. Superseded replay/digest/pre-parse-no-store/nonzero-refusal assertions all have named delete-or-invert owners in §18.5.

FOUR BLOCKERS, three sharing one shape — a gate moved or was newly declared and its ownership/coverage was not re-derived, which is what §18.0's own rule exists to prevent:

B1 RETENTION GATES M1 BUT IS OWNED AT M4. §15/§17/§19.1/§20 move the gate to M1 (correctly — my prior A1). §16.0 and §18.1 still own retention_encrypted_local.yaml and retention_external_cas.yaml in S5-CONTEXT, milestone M4, and §18.4 has no integration point ordering any part of S5 before M1. Under two of the three live UAT modes M1 is gated on an M4 slice's corpus and on M4-owned production code (key handling, fail-closed on wrong key, tombstone, rotation, no-resurrection) that appears in no M1 ownership column. Same structural defect as 'gates M1 on upstream work scheduled for M6'. Also §17 states the gate unconditionally while §21 and §15 state it per-capture-class — the A1 contradiction relocated. FIX: make §18.1 retention ownership UAT-conditional exactly as it already is for the S5 channel adapter; add an IP-R row to §18.4; resolve §17 to the per-capture-class form and align §20; say in §19.1 what M1's slice set becomes under each option.

B2 CORPUS COVERAGE EXCEEDS ITS OWNER'S MILESTONE, AND NON-VACUITY IS A HARD FAILURE. reader_cursor.yaml (S1, M1) declares all 5 TruncationReason and all 7 CursorErrorKind, but TruncatedDepthLimit/NodeLimit/EdgeLimit and CursorInvalidLineageBounds are reachable only through S4's lineage reader at M3 and TruncatedHistoryBound only through S5 at M4. guard_mutation.yaml (S1, M1) declares all 12 MutationOperatorID, but at least six mutate S0's pkg/protocol or S2's hostcontract and generated assets; §18.3's S1 L2 leaf names three guards, S2's names two more. §16.0 says a failing NonVacuityReport is a test failure, not a warning, so both corpora are red from S1 L2 until M3/M6 — the IP-2b loop at the corpus layer. FIX: add a Milestone field to CoverageSpec and widen per slice via §18.4 rows, or partition both corpora by owner.

B3 THE NON-VACUITY MECHANISM IS UNEXECUTABLE FOR SEVEN OF THE EIGHT CORPORA. §16.0's condition 'every MustFail case actually passes when its guard is removed' is the mechanism the harness exists for. Case has ID/Expect/Provenance/RawBytesPath/Dimensions and no field naming the guard or operator that proves it; the URD requires 'provenance AND mutation metadata' and CaseProvenance covers only the first. NonVacuityReport.GuardsProvenBy is per-corpus, so it cannot express case-to-operator linkage. All twelve operators map to §16.4 static guards, so guard_mutation.yaml is the only corpus with a defined 'remove its guard' operation. Concretely: capability_scope.yaml with thirteen must-fail rows that all refuse on state before reaching the axis comparison passes every stated condition — thirteen rows, one guard, twelve unproven axes, which is 0lbsy BLOCKER 2 surviving its own fix. FIX: add ProvenBy MutationOperatorID to Case (required when MustFail); replace GuardsProvenBy with UnprovenMustFailCases []CaseID; assert each must-fail case flips under its own operator and no must-pass case does; extend the operator set to the behavioural corpora (per-axis scope comparison, cursor fingerprint, CaptureDisposition validator, BuildIdentityExact requirement, retention tombstone, zero-write delta) or scope condition 3 to guard_mutation.yaml explicitly and say so.

B4 THE LOAD TEST CANNOT SEE THE FAILURE MODE P0-PIN CREATED. §13.1 row 8 makes a deadline-exceeded contended append produce no receipt and zero writes, so under the §4.4 writer estimate the designed degradation is dropped receipts. §16.1 item 9 and the §21 BDD assert slice start, the p99 ratio, and one transaction per delivery — never that a delivery produced a receipt. A hook that gives up at 1s stops competing for the lock, so the 2-second start assertion gets easier as loss rises; the per-delivery transaction count is satisfied by a failed delivery contributing zero; item 10 covers only receipts already committed; §13.1 row 8 covers one append, not a rate; and none of §4.4's four revisit triggers is receipt loss. §4.6 also never says how a deadline-failed Apply enters the p99 sample, and the two natural readings give opposite gates: exclude it and the contended tail is censored precisely where it is worst, making the gate weaker as contention worsens; include it at 1000ms and K=48 on a ~5ms baseline makes a few timeouts fatal. §22 headlines 'Append every delivery | No silent undercount' and nothing measures it. FIX: assert delivery outcome in item 9 with a stated failure bound; state the p99 sample rule in §4.6 and §21 (recommend including failures at the full deadline value); add receipt-loss rate as revisit trigger (e) and to §22's P0-PIN cost cell.

NON-BLOCKING, SAME REVISION: C1 §4.6 cites §15.3 and §15.1 items 8/9, which do not exist — the real locations are §16.1 items 9/10 and §16.4 — and §20 says K is 'named once in §4.4' where §4.4 only references it and §4.6 defines K=48. C2 §16.1 items 9/10 have an owner, a package, and a gate, but no leaf in §18.3, so the supervisor will create none. C3 the bounded-reader guard is an allowlist over a set that is not yet enumerable and fails open on omission; invert to a path-pattern denylist with the one named whitelisted helper. C4 §16.4's 'a guard with no operator is not a guard' is contradicted by three rows whose proof is 'compile-fail fixtures' or 'regeneration diff', which GuardsProvenBy []MutationOperatorID cannot record. C5 'eight corpora' is ten files with different owners and milestones.

EXPLICITLY NOT REQUESTED, and no over-testing found to remove: the semantically-identical-different-byte case stays rejected (byte-identical dominates; two rounds settled it); no cursor, lineage, or all-30 expansion; item 9's -race carve-out is correct and should not be reversed; the uncontended hold should stay a report, not a gate.

Every fix above is one sentence, one struct field, or one table row. Full review with section and file:line citations: aura-plugins-3hkoz.

P0-PIN is correctly cited as a capability, not a signature — I confirmed the real upstream shape is the optional 'ContextJournal.ApplyContext' (journal_api.go:298-304) and nothing in the proposal freezes anything conflicting; gating S1 L3 on it is right. Resource section matches UAT 6636 'Do A.' exactly: 48 is an observational SLO (grepped: every 'ceiling'/'worst case'/'enforced budget' hit is a negation or a historical citation), the contention gate is relative, the only absolute gates are a transaction count and a static retry-shape check, items 9/10 are genuinely split, and §22 states plainly that the 240 ms figure is unproven with Option B as the recorded escalation. Ownership re-derived independently rather than trusted: system_identity.go:88 really does call ActivatePastureSystem on the persisted path and S1 now owns it and provadapter/actors.go; the other OpenSQLite site (open.go:45) has no non-test callers so its absence is correct; git status returns exactly the six quarantined untracked files. All seven cases 237wx B2 found dropped are restored and Appendix B corrects the record honestly. PhaseSpec.Transitions verified to exist (state_machine.go:15-18), so the adjacency oracle is real; Confidence comparison direction is correct; identity collapse leaves nothing with two identities and nothing missing one.

Two BLOCKERs, both in material added THIS round, both text-only fixes that reopen no architecture:

A-1 — INV-1's classification is incomplete and one record violates it. §3.0 claims 'every record is classified into exactly one of four kinds' and makes that table the guard's only data source. Four journal-facing records are absent: InterpretationRecord and CommittedTransition (both self-annotated '// IMMUTABLE FACT'), BuildIdentity, and DisclosureRecord. DisclosureRecord is a live violation, not just an omission: it is declared 'IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT or FACT per Kind' and carries Status DisclosureDeliveryStatus while spanning the Plan and Attempt kinds that §3.0 places in the no-status snapshot class. It has no legal class, and because it is unclassified the guard cannot see it. This is the fourth instance of the exact defect class INV-1 was introduced to terminate, present in the same revision that introduces it — the same 'asserted five times, guarded zero times' shape the proposal correctly diagnoses for the bounded-reader rule. Fix: add all four to the table; split DisclosureRecord into three typed records (or declare a tagged-union rule); add a totality guard so an unclassified exported lifecycle type is itself a guard failure.

A-2 — Bind's effect on capability scope is unspecified, and one reading makes six of the thirteen axes vacuous. Both CapabilityIssueInput.Scope and CapabilityBindInput carry Actor and Bindings; CapabilityStateRecord folds to one Scope; nothing says whether Bind must match, may only narrow, or may replace/widen. Under bind-defines, the six native axes compare host-supplied strings to the same host-supplied strings and can never mismatch, which undercuts §14 row 29's 'proven issued-request challenge'. Every case in capability_scope.yaml passes identically under both readings, so no specified test distinguishes them — the same undetectability that made 0lbsy BLOCKER 2 blocking. Secondary: CapabilityScope.Sources is mandatory (1..32) but has no scope axis and no stated role, and which Actor ScopeAxisActor compares is unstated. Fix: state 'scope is fixed at Issue; Bind never widens it' with a typed mismatch on violation, state what each axis compares, state Sources' role, and add three must-fail corpus rows (bind_widens_native_binding, bind_actor_outside_issued_scope, bind_then_commit_with_binding_never_issued) plus one BDD.

Six non-blocking notes in the review task: ResolveActive multiplicity for two simultaneously-Active definitions of one (Kind,ID); the phase-adjacency guard lacks the syntactic precision item 4 has; no CapabilityStateID so two fields fall back to bare JournalID; K=48 is defined in §4.6 while §4.4/§20 claim it is named in §4.4; the '172 mechanically verified ownership paths' carried forward in Appendix B is a fact about PROPOSAL-8's table, not PROPOSAL-9's; and six internal cross-references (§10.2 x2, §15.4, §15.3, §15.1 items 8-9, §15.2) were not updated for the proposal's own one-section shift and now dangle.

I did not reopen settled design: the S7a/S7b split, admission control, permits, the priority lane, the S2 ownership move, and the semantically-identical-different-byte case all stay rejected — I have no new evidence against any of them.
