```go
    Fact       provenance.JournalID
    Source     EnrichmentSource
    Payload    EvidencePayloadRef
    Confidence Confidence
}

type EnrichmentBounds struct {
    MaxFacts uint16 // 1..64
    MaxBytes uint32 // 1..256 KiB
}

type EnrichmentRequest struct {
    Occurrence        OccurrenceRecord
    Envelope          SemanticEnvelopeRef
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
    Bounds            EnrichmentBounds
}

type EnrichmentSnapshot struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT; opaque, deep copied
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
    Facts             []EnrichmentFact
}

type Enricher interface {
    Snapshot(context.Context, EnrichmentRequest) (EnrichmentSnapshot, error)
}
```

The requested snapshot is at or before the reader snapshot and never reads unbounded current
state. Missing or contradictory data remains explicit; an enricher cannot change the occurrence,
semantic envelope, phase, context, or authority.

### 8.2 Typed output algebra

```go
type FactKind uint8

const (
    FactSession FactKind = iota + 1
    FactHumanSignal
    FactAgentAction
    FactToolAction
    FactTaskSignal
    FactWorktreeSignal
    FactArtifactObservation
    FactDecisionSignal
    FactHarnessState
    FactParseIssue
)

type CausalRelation uint8

const (
    RelationPromptedBy CausalRelation = iota + 1
    RelationDesignedBy
    RelationMotivatedBy
    RelationArchitectedBy
    RelationVerifiedBy
    RelationDelegatedTo
    RelationExecutedTool
    RelationProducedArtifact
    RelationObservedPath
    RelationSnapshotOf
    RelationCommittedAs
)

type OutputKind uint8

const (
    OutputFact OutputKind = iota + 1
    OutputUnresolved
    OutputLink
    OutputCandidate
)

type DraftRefKind uint8

const (
    DraftRefCommittedJournal DraftRefKind = iota + 1
    DraftRefBatchOutput
)

type DraftRef struct { // opaque tagged union
    Kind      DraftRefKind
    JournalID provenance.JournalID
    Output    OutputKind
    Ordinal   uint16
}

type FactDraft struct {
    Kind    FactKind
    Schema  LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Payload EvidencePayloadRef
    Basis   []DraftRef
}

type CausalLinkDraft struct {
    From       DraftRef
    To         DraftRef
    Relation   CausalRelation
    Confidence Confidence
    Basis      []DraftRef
}

type TransitionCandidateDraft struct {
    From  protocol.PhaseId
    To    protocol.PhaseId
    Rule  CodebookDefinitionRef
    Basis []DraftRef
}

type CandidateAdjacencyError struct {
    From protocol.PhaseId
    To   protocol.PhaseId
}

type UnresolvedReason uint8

const (
    UnresolvedMissingField UnresolvedReason = iota + 1
    UnresolvedMissingBinding
    UnresolvedMissingDefinition
    UnresolvedMissingEnrichment
    UnresolvedContradictoryEnrichment
    UnresolvedRetentionWithheld
    UnresolvedOverLimit
    UnresolvedUnsupportedSchema
    UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild
)

type UnresolvedBasisKind uint8

const (
    UnresolvedBasisField UnresolvedBasisKind = iota + 1
    UnresolvedBasisBinding
    UnresolvedBasisDefinition
    UnresolvedBasisEnrichment
    UnresolvedBasisRetention
    UnresolvedBasisBudget
    UnresolvedBasisBuild
)

type UnresolvedBasis struct { // opaque tagged union
    Kind       UnresolvedBasisKind
    Field      NativeFieldID
    Binding    NativeBindingKind
    Definition DefinitionJournalID
    Evidence   provenance.JournalID
}

type UnresolvedFactDraft struct {
    FactKind FactKind
    Reason   UnresolvedReason
    Basis    UnresolvedBasis
    Parents  []DraftRef
}

type InterpretationInput struct {
    Occurrence OccurrenceRecord
    Envelope   SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Enrichment EnrichmentSnapshot
}

type InterpretationDraft struct {
    Facts      []FactDraft
    Links      []CausalLinkDraft
    Candidates []TransitionCandidateDraft
    Unresolved []UnresolvedFactDraft
}

type Interpreter interface {
    Interpret(context.Context, InterpretationInput) (InterpretationDraft, error)
}

type InterpretationRegistry interface {
    Resolve(CodebookDefinitionRef, InterpreterDefinitionRef) (Interpreter, error)
}
```

**Adjacency lives in exactly one place.** `TransitionCandidateDraft`'s constructor validates
`(From, To)` against `protocol.PhaseSpecFor(From)` and returns `CandidateAdjacencyError` for a pair
the FSM disallows. T3's `CurrentFact` CAS would reject an illegal commit either way, so authority
was never at risk — but without this rule the ledger fills with permanently-uncommittable
candidates, and the natural "fix" is to teach the codebook the adjacency table, which is how a
second FSM gets born. §6.3 item 5 guards it statically. (`aura-plugins-oygyo` R3.)

`Interpreter` is pure with respect to storage, context, response, and control. It cannot mutate
the occurrence or envelope. All collections are canonicalized, bounded, and copied. There are no
undefined string event names.

### 8.3 Operation service, clock, effects, and result slots

```go
type InterpretationOperationInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Occurrence  OccurrenceID
    Codebook    CodebookDefinitionRef
    Interpreter InterpreterDefinitionRef
}

type InterpretationResult struct {
    Interpretation InterpretationID // the header JournalID; no duplicate bare field
    Facts          []LifecycleFactID
    Unresolved     []UnresolvedFactID
    Links          []LifecycleLinkID
    Candidates     []TransitionCandidateID
}

func (r InterpretationResult) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type InterpretationService interface {
    Interpret(context.Context, InterpretationOperationInput) (InterpretationResult, error)
}
```

The operation service, not the pure interpreter, owns the injected clock. It captures `RecordedAt`
once when it creates the operation input; DBOS or an exact retry reuses the complete input
unchanged. It resolves the occurrence plus all five immutable definitions before calling
`Interpreter`, obtains one bounded enrichment snapshot, canonicalizes output, and calls
`Journal.Apply` once.

Result slots are exact and stable:

| Output | Slot |
|---|---|
| Header | `interpretation` |
| Fact ordinal n | `fact-%03d` |
| Unresolved ordinal n | `unresolved-%03d` |
| Link ordinal n | `link-%03d` |
| Candidate ordinal n | `candidate-%03d` |

Canonical order is output kind, then schema/rule definition JournalID, then canonical body, then
canonical basis. Input slice order cannot change slots. A `DraftRef` to a batch output resolves to
the corresponding same-operation result slot; committed refs require a positive prior JournalID.
The header JournalID is the `InterpretationID`. Same operation ID plus same canonical input returns
the same IDs internally; changed input conflicts. No result exposes a replay flag.

## 9. Journal-native causal lineage

A causal link is an `EffectEvidence` record with the `CausalLinkDraft` shape. Its produced
JournalID is its sole identity. Provenance task `EffectEdgeAdd` continues to mean a task
relationship and is never overloaded. Projection rows index source/target JournalIDs and relation
but allocate no semantic ID.

Cycles are legal when explicitly evidenced. Shared timestamps, sessions, actors, paths, or
worktrees never create a link. A `FileChanged` occurrence can produce only `RelationObservedPath`
with `ConfidenceObserved` until selected tool/VCS/worktree evidence resolves an artifact or commit.

**The no-promotion rule is now a direct comparison.** With one `Confidence` type, a link's
confidence may not exceed the minimum confidence of the enrichment facts in its basis: it is a
`<=` check, not a conversion between two enums that could be written wrongly
(`aura-plugins-oygyo` R1). Missing or contradictory enrichment emits an unresolved fact and cannot
promote confidence.

**The lookup that the comparison runs over is stated, not implied** (`aura-plugins-bxwry` F7).
A link's basis is `[]DraftRef`. Enrichment confidences live on
`EnrichmentFact{Fact provenance.JournalID, Confidence}`. The minimum is taken over exactly those
basis entries whose `DraftRefKind` is `DraftRefCommittedJournal` and whose `JournalID` equals an
`EnrichmentFact.Fact` in the same-operation `EnrichmentSnapshot`. Basis entries that are
`DraftRefBatchOutput`, or that resolve to a committed record that is not an enrichment fact,
contribute nothing to the minimum and cannot raise it. If **no** basis entry resolves to an
enrichment fact, the link's confidence may be at most `ConfidenceObserved`. Collapsing the two
confidence enums removed the type-conversion risk; it did not remove the resolution ambiguity,
and an unstated resolution rule is how a `min` over an empty set silently becomes "unbounded".

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROPOSAL-10 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 2/7 (Sections 10-11)

Authoritative continuation of PROPOSAL-10. Read with the description and continuations 2/3 and
3/3. Section numbering is unchanged from PROPOSAL-9; the map to PROPOSAL-8 is at the end of the
description.

## 10. Complete context disclosure contract

### 10.1 Pure policy projection with bounded history

```go
type ActorRef struct {
    Actor   provenance.AgentID
    Session NativeBinding
}

type AssignmentRef struct {
    Assignment provenance.JournalID
    Task       provenance.TaskID
}

type CommittedPhaseRef struct {
    PhaseState PhaseStateID
    Phase      protocol.PhaseId
}

type ContextBounds struct {
    MaxItems uint16 // 1..64
    MaxBytes uint32 // 1..256 KiB
}

// Explicit constructor limits and a deterministic selection rule for every
// history collection. Without these, a long-lived multi-agent epoch grows the
// projection input without bound and defeats the 1 MiB operation budget.
type ContextHistoryBounds struct {
    MaxBasis            uint16 // 1..64
    MaxPriorPlans       uint16 // 1..32
    MaxAcknowledgements uint16 // 1..32
}

// ContextSelectionRule and ContextSelection.Rule are DELETED (aura-plugins-emmh7
// minor, aura-plugins-bxwry F7). A single-valued enum representing a choice
// nobody makes is not a contract; it is a placeholder that a reader must check
// and a writer must set. The selection rule — newest-first by descending
// JournalID at or before the reader snapshot, then truncate at the bound — is
// an invariant of the projector, stated below and in section 3.2, and the
// versioned context-policy definition already identifies the selection
// semantics that produced a given plan. If a persisted policy is ever proven to
// choose among several validated rules, the enum returns with more than one
// value and DisclosurePlan gains it then.
type ContextSelection struct {
    Bounds    ContextHistoryBounds
    Truncated bool
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type ContextCompletenessError struct {
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Recipient ActorRef
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type ContextPacketRef struct {
    Schema  ContextPacketSchemaRef
    Payload EvidencePayloadRef
}

type ContextProjectionInput struct {
    Recipient        ActorRef
    Role             protocol.RoleId
    Phase            CommittedPhaseRef
    Assignment       AssignmentRef
    Policy           ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope         SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis            []provenance.JournalID // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    PriorPlans       []DisclosurePlanID     // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    Acknowledgements []DisclosureResultID   // bounded, newest-first at snapshot
    History          ContextHistoryBounds
    Bounds           ContextBounds
}

type ContextProjection struct {
    Recipient ActorRef
    Role      protocol.RoleId
    Phase     protocol.PhaseId
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope  SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis     []provenance.JournalID
    Selection ContextSelection
    Packet    ContextPacketRef
}

type ContextProjector interface {
    Project(ContextProjectionInput) (ContextProjection, error)
}
```

`ContextProjector` is pure and receives only exact committed phase/assignment facts and exact
definitions. It has no Journal, FSM, control service, transport, or mutable projection.
Candidate-only, stale, unauthorized, wrong-recipient, and unknown-schema input fails before
planning and cannot mutate any state.

**The selection rule is one invariant, not a field.** Every bounded history collection —
`Basis`, `PriorPlans`, `Acknowledgements` — is selected newest-first by descending JournalID at or
before the reader snapshot, then truncated at its bound. That rule is fixed for M1-M6 and is
asserted in `reader_cursor.yaml`, not stored per plan.

Truncation is never silent. When any bounded history collection is truncated, `ContextSelection`
reports it. Where the context policy declares completeness required for that packet class, the
projector returns `ContextCompletenessError` and the packet is **suppressed**, producing a
`DisclosureSuppressed` fact rather than a partial packet. (`aura-plugins-u2d51` IMPORTANT 2.)

### 10.2 Plan, delivery attempt, and immutable result facts

```go
type DisclosureChannel uint8

const (
    DisclosureGeneratedMaterial DisclosureChannel = iota + 1
    DisclosureDynamicHostResponse
    DisclosureExplicitPull
)

type AcknowledgementMode uint8

const (
    AcknowledgementPositiveHostEvidence AcknowledgementMode = iota + 1
    AcknowledgementExplicitAgentReceipt
    AcknowledgementUnavailable
)

type DisclosureDeliveryStatus uint8

const (
    DisclosureDelivered DisclosureDeliveryStatus = iota + 1
    DisclosureAcknowledged
    DisclosureFailed
    DisclosureRevoked
    DisclosureSuppressed
)

type DisclosurePlanInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Projection  ContextProjection
}

type DisclosurePlan struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Operation provenance.OperationID
    Recipient ActorRef
    Phase     protocol.PhaseId
    Role      protocol.RoleId
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Envelope  SemanticEnvelopeRef
    Basis     []provenance.JournalID
    Selection ContextSelection
    Packet    ContextPacketRef
}

func (p DisclosurePlan) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureAttemptInput struct {
    Plan        DisclosurePlanID
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Channel     DisclosureChannel
    AckMode     AcknowledgementMode
}

type DisclosureAttempt struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Attempt   DisclosureAttemptID
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Operation provenance.OperationID
    Channel   DisclosureChannel
    AckMode   AcknowledgementMode
}

func (a DisclosureAttempt) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureResultInput struct {
    Plan        DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt     DisclosureAttemptID
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    Status      DisclosureDeliveryStatus
    ObservedAt  time.Time
    Evidence    []provenance.JournalID // 0..32
}

type DisclosureResult struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Result  DisclosureResultID
    Plan    DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt DisclosureAttemptID
    Status  DisclosureDeliveryStatus
}

func (r DisclosureResult) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureService interface {
    Plan(context.Context, DisclosurePlanInput) (DisclosurePlan, error)
    BeginAttempt(context.Context, DisclosureAttemptInput) (DisclosureAttempt, error)
    RecordResult(context.Context, DisclosureResultInput) (DisclosureResult, error)
}

type DeliveryRequest struct {
    Plan    DisclosurePlan
    Attempt DisclosureAttempt
}

type DeliveryObservation struct {
    Status     DisclosureDeliveryStatus
    ObservedAt time.Time
    Evidence   []provenance.JournalID
}

type ContextTransport interface {
    Deliver(context.Context, DeliveryRequest) (DeliveryObservation, error)
}
```

**`DisclosureAttemptID` is now the typed attempt JournalID, and the random `[16]byte` identity is
gone.** PROPOSAL-8 carried three identities for one attempt: a journal ID, an operation ID, and a
random nonce. The attempt JournalID plus the operation ID already identify the durable attempt and
the exact retry, so the nonce was an unearned third identity of exactly the kind the UAT rejected
for occurrences (`aura-plugins-u2d51` IMPORTANT 1; `aura-plugins-oygyo` R6 asked for its rationale
and the honest answer is that it does not have one yet).

If the UAT-selected channel genuinely needs a host-visible correlation token that cannot expose a
JournalID — §13.1 forbids JournalIDs crossing the host boundary — the **selected adapter** in S5
introduces a bounded, adapter-local `DeliveryCorrelationToken`, records its relation to the
attempt as a fact, and does not make it a generic lifecycle identity. Deferring it to the adapter
is what lets the need be demonstrated instead of assumed.

Every plan/attempt/result boundary now uses typed IDs with `JournalID()` accessors; no signature
accepts a bare `provenance.JournalID` where a typed disclosure identity is meant.

The operation service captures plan/attempt/result timestamps through an injected clock and
persists the complete operation input. Transport never constructs a plan or mutates disclosure
history. A crash after the attempt fact but before a result remains an honest unknown attempt.

Each write has a mandatory slot: `disclosure-plan`, `disclosure-attempt`, or `disclosure-result`.
Exact same operation ID and input returns the original slot; changed input conflicts. A result
must match its plan and attempt. Delivered, acknowledged, failed, revoked, and suppressed are
separate facts. Acknowledged requires positive evidence under the UAT-selected mode; delivery never
implies acknowledgement.

The channel and acknowledgement constants are typed alternatives, not an active choice. UAT selects
one compatible pair before M4 slicing (§19.3).

### 10.3 Rebuildable current disclosure state

```go
type DisclosureCurrentStatus uint8

const (
    DisclosureStatePlanned DisclosureCurrentStatus = iota + 1
    DisclosureStateAttempted
    DisclosureStateDelivered
    DisclosureStateAcknowledged
    DisclosureStateFailed
    DisclosureStateRevoked
    DisclosureStateSuppressed
)

// DERIVED PROJECTION (INV-1 class 3).
type DisclosureCurrentState struct {
    Recipient         ActorRef
    LatestPlan        DisclosurePlanID
    LatestAttempt     DisclosureAttemptID
    LatestResult      DisclosureResultID
    Status            DisclosureCurrentStatus
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
}

type DisclosureStateProjector interface {
    Rebuild(context.Context, ActorRef, provenance.JournalID) (DisclosureCurrentState, error)
}
```

The projector folds immutable facts in JournalID order. It writes no truth. Deleting disclosure
projection rows and replaying the journal returns the same state. Candidate, stale, unauthorized,
wrong-scope, and unknown-policy facts are never admitted to the fold.

`DisclosureCurrentStatus` (7 values) and `DisclosureDeliveryStatus` (5 values) are deliberately two
enums over different domains: one folds history including "planned, no attempt" and "attempt, no
result" — the crash gap — while the other records what a single result fact says. Two enums over
different domains is simpler than one enum with invalid combinations (`aura-plugins-oygyo`).

## 11. One immutable FSM, the complete control API, and transaction-local expiry

### 11.1 Preserved FSM direction

`pkg/protocol` owns one private static phase table. Production constructors no longer accept a spec
map. Read-only lookup and iteration return deep copies:

```go
func PhaseSpecFor(protocol.PhaseId) (protocol.PhaseSpec, bool)
func AllPhaseSpecs() []protocol.PhaseSpec
func NewEpochStateMachine(string) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
func NewEpochStateMachineFromState(protocol.EpochState) *protocol.EpochStateMachine
```

The transition law remains the PROPOSAL-7 corrected law, including the Review -> Propose, Plan UAT
-> Propose, Code Review -> Worker Slices, and Implementation UAT -> Worker Slices feedback edges.
Generated transition metadata derives from this source. `PhaseSpecFor` is also the single adjacency
oracle consulted by `TransitionCandidateDraft`'s constructor (§8.2). The live engine/audit writer
is cut over once at M6; direct phase projection writes cannot remain active.

### 11.2 Capability API, complete

PROPOSAL-8 exposed only `CommitCandidate` while claiming issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume as
behaviour. A green implementation could have checked only consumed-or-revoked state and omitted a
scope axis entirely, and no test could have caught it (`aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 2;
`aura-plugins-oygyo` R7; `aura-plugins-4acdq` item 8). PROPOSAL-9 completed the API, and both
Axis-A reviewers then found the same argument applying one level down to the transition the
completion added: `Issue` and `Bind` were specified as prose, so the authority they are supposed
to establish was not enforceable by any type or any test.

Three defects, one root cause — *what a Pasture-issued challenge is* had no representation:

1. **No typed Pasture-issued request** (`aura-plugins-wwyvw` BLOCKER A-1). `CapabilityIssueInput`
   carried only `OperationID`, `RecordedAt`, and `Scope`; `CapabilityBindInput` accepted an
   arbitrary binding set; `CommitCandidateInput` carried only candidate, capability, and actor.
   No type represented a Pasture-issued request, the exact response occurrence, or a validated
   request/session binding. §14 row 29 requires "a proven issued-request challenge" and §14 row 30
   confines `ElicitationResult` to evidence — correctly — but nothing in the API made either true.
   A handler could issue and bind a capability from a host-controlled `BindingRequest` value and
   then commit it. The top-level conclusion still held (a host cannot call `Issue` or `Bind`), but
   "the prose forbids it" is the same guarantee level the bounded-reader rule had before §16.4.
2. **`Bind`'s effect on scope was unspecified** (`aura-plugins-i5imy` BLOCKER A-2). Both `Issue`
   and `Bind` carry `Actor` and `Bindings`; `CapabilityStateRecord` folds to exactly one `Scope`;
   nothing said whether `Bind` must match, may only narrow, or may replace. Under *bind-defines*,
   the native axes compare host-supplied strings to the same host-supplied strings and can never
   mismatch — six of thirteen axes become vacuous. **Every case in `capability_scope.yaml` passes
   identically under both readings**, so no specified test distinguished them. That is exactly the
   undetectability that made `aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 2 blocking.
3. **The axis set did not cover its own binding enum** (`aura-plugins-bxwry` F5). Thirteen axes
   covered six of the eight `NativeBindingKind` values; a capability scoped by a turn or a message
   had no axis, so `CapabilityScopeMismatch{Axis}` could not name it and §16.2's one-case-per-axis
   rule could not reach it.

All three are fixed below by adding types and stating rules, not by moving a seam. No interface
is added. `EpochControlService` keeps its four methods.

#### 11.2.1 The Pasture-issued request chain

```go
// IMMUTABLE FACT (INV-1 class 2). Minted by a Pasture request-issuance
// operation under Pasture's own authority. A host cannot create one: its
// JournalID is produced by a Pasture Apply, and the Nonce is Pasture-chosen.
type IssuedRequestRecord struct {
    Request  IssuedRequestID
    Contract ir.RuntimeContractID
    Session  NativeBinding   // Kind == BindingSession, fixed at issuance
    Nonce    ContentIdentity // Pasture-minted challenge placed in the outgoing request
    Operation CapabilityOperation
    IssuedAt time.Time
}

type IssuedRequestRef struct { // opaque constructor; resolves an existing record
    Request  IssuedRequestID
    Contract ir.RuntimeContractID
    Session  NativeBinding
    Nonce    ContentIdentity
}

// The occurrence that carries the host's response to a Pasture-issued request.
// Bind cites it; the binding transaction proves the correlation rather than
// trusting the caller's assertion of it.
type ResponseOccurrenceRef struct {
    Occurrence OccurrenceID
    Request    IssuedRequestID
    Session    NativeBinding
}

type RequestBindingAxis uint8

const (
    RequestAxisRequest RequestBindingAxis = iota + 1
    RequestAxisSession
    RequestAxisContract
    RequestAxisNonce
    RequestAxisResponseOccurrence
)

type IssuedRequestMismatch struct {
    Request IssuedRequestID
    Axis    RequestBindingAxis
}
```

**Where the chain is mandatory.** `CapabilityScope.Operation == CapabilityRecordHumanDecision` is
the only operation for which a host-originated response may contribute to a normative write, so
it is the operation the chain governs:

- `Issue` **requires** a nonzero `IssuedRequestRef` resolving to an existing `IssuedRequestRecord`
  whose contract, session, nonce, and declared operation match exactly. For every other
  `CapabilityOperation` the ref must be zero. A mismatch returns `IssuedRequestMismatch{Axis}`
  with zero writes.
- `Bind` **requires** a `ResponseOccurrenceRef` when the capability was issued against a request.
  Inside the same `Journal.Apply`, before any write, the binding validates: the cited occurrence
  exists and is a committed T1 occurrence; its `BindingRequest` value equals the issued request's
  host-visible request identity; its `BindingSession` value equals `IssuedRequestRecord.Session`;
  and its runtime contract equals `IssuedRequestRecord.Contract`. Any failure returns
  `IssuedRequestMismatch{Axis}` with zero writes.
- `CommitCandidate` consumes only a Bound capability that carries that validated response.

**Claude 2.1.210 is unchanged by this.** The pin cannot prove a Pasture-owned challenge round
trip — there is no field for Pasture to place a nonce into and have it returned — so no Claude
2.1.210 event can satisfy issuance, and `ElicitationResult` remains evidence and candidate only
(§14 rows 29-30, §17 M6 exclusion). The chain exists so that when a contract *can* prove it, the
proof is a type and a transaction rather than a paragraph.

#### 11.2.2 Scope is fixed at Issue; Bind never widens

> **Rule.** `Issue` fixes the complete scope. `Bind` asserts a concrete actor and native identity
> and is refused unless both are already inside the issued scope. `Bind` may narrow. `Bind` may
> never add, replace, or widen.

Concretely, and each with a must-fail corpus row in §16.2:

- `CapabilityBindInput.Actor` must equal `CapabilityScope.Actor` when `Scope.Actor` is nonzero.
  A different actor returns `CapabilityScopeMismatch{ScopeAxisActor}` with zero writes.
- Every `NativeBinding` in `CapabilityBindInput.Bindings` must already be present, kind and value
  exact, in `CapabilityScope.Bindings`. A binding not in the issued set returns
  `CapabilityScopeMismatch{Axis}` naming the axis for that binding kind, with zero writes.
- `Bind` writes no new scope. `CapabilityStateRecord.Scope` is the issued scope, unchanged for the
  capability's whole life. That is why it folds to exactly one `Scope`.

The alternative model — *bind-defines*, where `Issue` mints an actor-less scope that `Bind` fills
in — is **rejected**, and the rejection is recorded rather than left implicit: it makes the native
axes compare host data to host data, which is the vacuity `aura-plugins-i5imy` identified.

#### 11.2.3 What each axis compares

PROPOSAL-9 named thirteen axes and did not say what any of them compared at commit. The table is
now part of the design. `Left` is what the capability carries; `Right` is what the commit supplies
or what the transaction observes.

| Axis | Left (from `CapabilityScope`, fixed at Issue) | Right (at `CommitCandidate`) |
|---|---|---|
| `ScopeAxisOperation` | `Scope.Operation` | the operation the candidate's commit performs |
| `ScopeAxisEpoch` | `Scope.Epoch` | the epoch of the candidate's task |
| `ScopeAxisActor` | `Scope.Actor` | `CommitCandidateInput.Actor` |
| `ScopeAxisRole` | `Scope.Role` | the role of the actor's current assignment |
| `ScopeAxisAssignment` | `Scope.Assignment` | the current assignment JournalID |
| `ScopeAxisCandidate` | `Scope.Candidate` | `CommitCandidateInput.Candidate` |
| `ScopeAxisRuntimeContract` | `Scope.Contract` | the contract of the occurrence the candidate derives from |
| `ScopeAxisNativeSession` | the `BindingSession` value in `Scope.Bindings` | the same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| `ScopeAxisNativeRequest` | `BindingRequest` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| `ScopeAxisNativeToolCall` | `BindingToolCall` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| `ScopeAxisNativeAgent` | `BindingAgent` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| `ScopeAxisNativeTask` | `BindingTask` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| `ScopeAxisNativeWorktree` | `BindingWorktree` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| **`ScopeAxisNativeTurn`** | `BindingTurn` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |
| **`ScopeAxisNativeMessage`** | `BindingMessage` in `Scope.Bindings` | same kind in the bound response occurrence |

**Fifteen axes.** The two additions close `aura-plugins-bxwry` F5: the native axes now cover all
eight `NativeBindingKind` values, so every binding kind is reportable and §16.2's
one-case-per-axis rule reaches all of them. F5's alternative — collapsing the six native axes into
one `ScopeAxisNativeBinding` carrying the mismatched `NativeBindingKind` — is smaller and
drift-proof and was seriously considered. It is **rejected here** for two reasons: it restructures
an axis mapping that `aura-plugins-i5imy` verified one-to-one against PROPOSAL-7 §14.2 and
confirmed closed, and it requires a two-dimensional coverage entry that §16.0's flat coverage
shape does not express. Adding two constants keeps the corpus flat and the settled mapping intact.
If a ninth binding kind is ever added, the drift risk F5 named is real, so §16.4 gains one
enumeration-parity rule: the native `CapabilityScopeAxis` values and the `NativeBindingKind`
values must be in bijection, checked in the same `go/ast` pass, proven by
`MutateAddUnmappedBindingKind`.

**`Sources` is provenance, not a match criterion.** `CapabilityScope.Sources
[]provenance.JournalID // 1..32` is mandatory because a capability must always cite the
Pasture-issued evidence that justified issuing it. It has deliberately **no axis** and is **never
compared at commit**. `aura-plugins-i5imy` was right that a mandatory scope field with no stated
role is exactly the ambiguity this section exists to remove; the role is stated here rather than
inventing a fourteenth comparison that nothing needs.

**There is one actor value, not three.** `CapabilityScope.Actor` is fixed at Issue,
`CapabilityBindInput.Actor` is required to equal it (§11.2.2), and `ScopeAxisActor` compares
`CommitCandidateInput.Actor` against `CapabilityScope.Actor`. The three names denote one value by
construction, and the bind rule is what makes that true rather than hoped.

```go
type CapabilityState uint8

const (
    CapabilityIssued CapabilityState = iota + 1
    CapabilityBound
    CapabilityRevoked
    CapabilityConsumed
)

type CapabilityOperation uint8

const (
    CapabilityRecordHumanDecision CapabilityOperation = iota + 1
    CapabilityBindSession
    CapabilityBindAssignment
    CapabilityCompleteTask
    CapabilityCommitTransition
)

// The fifteen scope axes, each independently checkable, each with its own test
// case, and each with a stated Left/Right comparison in section 11.2.3. The
// first thirteen restore PROPOSAL-7 section 14.2's "wrong actor, role, epoch,
// assignment, candidate, contract, native session, request, tool, agent, task,
// worktree, and operation", which PROPOSAL-8 compressed into the single phrase
// "issue/bind/revoke/expire/consume matrix" (aura-plugins-237wx B2 row 1). The
// last two complete coverage of NativeBindingKind (aura-plugins-bxwry F5); the
// native axes and NativeBindingKind are held in bijection by a section 16.4
// enumeration-parity rule.
type CapabilityScopeAxis uint8

const (
    ScopeAxisOperation CapabilityScopeAxis = iota + 1
    ScopeAxisEpoch
    ScopeAxisActor
    ScopeAxisRole
    ScopeAxisAssignment
    ScopeAxisCandidate
    ScopeAxisRuntimeContract
    ScopeAxisNativeSession
    ScopeAxisNativeRequest
    ScopeAxisNativeToolCall
    ScopeAxisNativeAgent
    ScopeAxisNativeTask
    ScopeAxisNativeWorktree
    ScopeAxisNativeTurn
    ScopeAxisNativeMessage
)

type CapabilityScope struct { // opaque constructor
    Operation  CapabilityOperation
    Epoch      provenance.TaskID
    Actor      provenance.AgentID
    Role       protocol.RoleId
    Assignment provenance.JournalID
    Candidate  TransitionCandidateID
    Contract   ir.RuntimeContractID
    Sources    []provenance.JournalID // 1..32
    Bindings   []NativeBinding        // 0..16
    ExpiresAt  time.Time
}

type CapabilityRevocationReason uint8

const (
    RevokedSupersededScope CapabilityRevocationReason = iota + 1
    RevokedOperatorWithdrawal
    RevokedAssignmentEnded
)

type CapabilityIssueInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Scope       CapabilityScope
    // Required exactly when Scope.Operation == CapabilityRecordHumanDecision;
    // must be zero otherwise. Resolved and validated against the existing
    // IssuedRequestRecord before any write.
    Request IssuedRequestRef
}

type CapabilityBindInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Capability  CapabilityID
    // Must equal the issued Scope.Actor when that is nonzero. Bind never widens.
    Actor    provenance.AgentID
    // Every entry must already be present, kind and value exact, in the issued
    // Scope.Bindings. Bind may narrow, never add or replace.
    Bindings []NativeBinding // 0..16
    // Required when the capability was issued against a Pasture-issued request.
    // Validated for exact request / session / contract / response-occurrence
    // equality inside the same Apply, before any write.
    Response ResponseOccurrenceRef
}

type CapabilityRevokeInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Reason      CapabilityRevocationReason
}

type CommitCandidateInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Candidate   TransitionCandidateID
    Capability  CapabilityID
    Actor       provenance.AgentID
}

// IMMUTABLE FACT (INV-1 class 2). No replay flag.
// ConsumedStateFact was named `Capability` in PROPOSAL-9 while CommitRecord.Capability
// is the ISSUED identity (a CapabilityID). One field name denoting two referents, in
// the revision that had just finished collapsing duplicate identities
// (aura-plugins-bxwry F7). It is now named for what it is and typed like its peer
// CapabilityStateRecord.LatestStateFact.
type CommittedTransition struct {
    PhaseState        PhaseStateID
    ConsumedStateFact CapabilityStateID
    Decision          provenance.JournalID
}

type EpochControlService interface {
    Issue(context.Context, CapabilityIssueInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    Bind(context.Context, CapabilityBindInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    Revoke(context.Context, CapabilityRevokeInput) (CapabilityID, error)
    CommitCandidate(context.Context, CommitCandidateInput) (CommittedTransition, error)
}

// Typed failures. Each is separately observable through a public reader, so a
// test can assert WHICH check refused, not merely that something refused.
type CapabilityScopeMismatch struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Axis       CapabilityScopeAxis
}

type CapabilityStateError struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Observed   CapabilityState
    Required   CapabilityState
}

type CapabilityExpiredError struct {
    Capability CapabilityID
    Deadline   time.Time
}

type BuildIdentityError struct {
    Implementation EpochImplementationRef
    Status         BuildIdentityStatus
}
```

`Decision` may be zero only for a transition kind whose constructor declares no decision effect;
there is no pointer ambiguity. Only `BuildIdentityExact` may back a commit; a dirty or unresolved
build returns `BuildIdentityError` with zero writes (§7.3).

`CapabilityStateID` is new in §3.1 and closes the last identity asymmetry
(`aura-plugins-i5imy` n3): `DefinitionStateRecord.LatestState` was already typed
`DefinitionStateID`, while `CapabilityStateRecord.LatestStateFact` and
`CommittedTransition.Capability` fell back to a bare `provenance.JournalID` for the same concept —
a capability state fact — even though the kind is known there, so §12.2's own exemption
("a different record of unknown kind") did not apply. Both are now `CapabilityStateID`.

### 11.3 Minimal upstream Provenance extension for transaction-local expiry

This section is **unchanged from PROPOSAL-8** and was verified line-by-line against pin `bcce714`
by `aura-plugins-4acdq` and `aura-plugins-oygyo`. It is the S7 / M6 prerequisite. It is **not** the
P0-PIN caller deadline, which is a separate and earlier upstream change (§4.3), and **S7 is not
split**.

```go
type ConditionTransactionTimeBefore struct {
    Deadline time.Time
}

const ConditionTransactionTimeBeforeKind provenance.ConditionKind = 3
const ConditionTimeExpired provenance.ConditionFailureReason = 3

type Condition struct { // upstream tagged union after the extension
    Kind                  provenance.ConditionKind
    Selector              provenance.FactSelector
    AssertedJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    TransactionTimeBefore ConditionTransactionTimeBefore
}

type ConditionFailure struct { // upstream typed failure after the extension
    Index             int
    Kind              provenance.ConditionKind
    Reason            provenance.ConditionFailureReason
    AssertedJournalID provenance.JournalID
    ActualJournalID   provenance.JournalID
    Deadline          time.Time
    TransactionTime   time.Time
}
```

Ordinals 3 and 3 are both free (`facts.go:55-69` and `facts.go:93-98` at the pin). The new
condition kind carries exactly one UTC deadline and requires the fact-selector/JID arm to be zero;
existing ExactFact/CurrentFact conditions require the deadline arm to be zero. Canonical encoding
stores signed Unix milliseconds; sub-millisecond deadlines are rejected rather than rounded
differently across processes.

The default transaction-time source executes, on the same pinned SQLite connection after write-lock
acquisition:

```text
SELECT CAST(unixepoch('subsec') * 1000 AS INTEGER)
```

`transaction_now_ms < deadline_ms` passes; equality or later returns typed `ConditionTimeExpired`.
The source is private, database-backed production authority; upstream internal tests inject a fake
transaction-time source, so application callers cannot weaken production time.

Evaluation order is fixed:

```text
BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquired
  -> exact OperationID lookup
       -> exact input: return original result
       -> changed input: OperationConflict, zero writes
       -> new operation: continue
  -> CurrentFact(capability == Bound)
  -> scope match on all fifteen axes            (section 11.2.3 Left/Right table)
  -> issued-request chain, when the capability carries one:
       exact request / session / contract / nonce
       and the bound response occurrence         (IssuedRequestMismatch, zero writes)
  -> TransactionTimeBefore(capability.ExpiresAt)
  -> CurrentFact(phase == expected current state)
  -> write capability Consumed + phase/decision/task effects
  -> COMMIT
```

The `Bind`-time validations in §11.2.1 and §11.2.2 run in the same shape inside `Bind`'s own
`Apply`: after the exact-operation lookup, before any effect, refusing with zero writes. Neither
`Bind` nor `CommitCandidate` trusts a caller's assertion that a correlation holds; both re-derive
it transactionally from committed facts.

Pasture maps `ConditionTimeExpired` to `CapabilityExpiredError`. A fresh operation queued before the
deadline but acquiring the lock at or after it loses with zero journal, capability, phase, decision,
task, context, and projection writes. An exact already-committed retry still returns before
deadline and current-state checks. Same operation ID with a changed deadline or any other changed
input conflicts.

No arbitrary SQL, callback, boolean expression, or application-specific predicate is added to
Provenance.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROPOSAL-10 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 3/7 (Sections 12-15)

Authoritative continuation of PROPOSAL-10. Read with the description and the other six
continuations. Section numbering is unchanged from PROPOSAL-9.

## 12. Complete bounded public reader

### 12.1 Cursor and bounds

```go
type PageSize uint16

func NewPageSize(uint16) (PageSize, error) // accepts 1..256 only

type QueryFingerprint [32]byte

type Cursor struct { // opaque; encoded token has version + checksum
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
    LastJournalID     provenance.JournalID
    QueryFingerprint  QueryFingerprint
}

func ParseCursor(string) (Cursor, error)
func (Cursor) String() string

type PageRequest struct {
    Size   PageSize
    Cursor *Cursor
}

type TruncationReason uint8

const (
    TruncatedPageSize TruncationReason = iota + 1
    TruncatedDepthLimit
    TruncatedNodeLimit
    TruncatedEdgeLimit
    TruncatedHistoryBound
)

type PageState struct {
    Next      *Cursor
    Truncated bool
    Reason    TruncationReason
}

type LineageDirection uint8

const (
    LineageForward LineageDirection = iota + 1
    LineageReverse
)

type LineageBounds struct {
    MaxDepth uint16 // 1..32
    MaxNodes uint16 // 1..256
    MaxEdges uint16 // 1..512
}

type CursorErrorKind uint8

const (
    CursorInvalidPageSize CursorErrorKind = iota + 1
    CursorQueryMismatch
    CursorSnapshotFuture
    CursorStale
    CursorTampered
    CursorUnsupportedVersion
    CursorInvalidLineageBounds
)
```

An initial query with no cursor snapshots the current maximum JournalID. Every page is ordered by
ascending JournalID and resumes strictly after `LastJournalID`. The query fingerprint is SHA-256
over the canonical typed filter and direction/bounds. `Cursor.String` includes a versioned canonical
frame and checksum; `ParseCursor` rejects malformed or tampered frames. A cursor with a different
query fingerprint, future snapshot, last ID after snapshot, missing retained snapshot, or
unsupported version returns a distinct typed error before SQL. A cursor is an integrity and
stability token, not authorization; authorization is checked independently on each read.

### 12.2 Concrete records, queries, pages, and methods

No record below carries a bare `provenance.JournalID` beside its own typed identity
(`aura-plugins-oygyo` R2, `aura-plugins-u2d51` MINOR 1). Where a field genuinely refers to a
different record of unknown kind — link endpoints, fact basis — `provenance.JournalID` is correct
and is retained.

```go
type InterpretationRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    Occurrence     OccurrenceID
    Envelope       SemanticEnvelopeRef
    RecordedAt     time.Time
}

type FactRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Fact           LifecycleFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    Kind           FactKind
    Schema         LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Payload        EvidencePayloadRef
    Basis          []provenance.JournalID
}

type UnresolvedFactRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Unresolved     UnresolvedFactID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    FactKind       FactKind
    Reason         UnresolvedReason
    Basis          UnresolvedBasis
    Parents        []provenance.JournalID
}

type CausalLinkRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Link           LifecycleLinkID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    From           provenance.JournalID
    To             provenance.JournalID
    Relation       CausalRelation
    Confidence     Confidence
    Basis          []provenance.JournalID
}

type TransitionCandidateRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    Candidate      TransitionCandidateID
    Interpretation InterpretationID
    From           protocol.PhaseId
    To             protocol.PhaseId
    Rule           CodebookDefinitionRef
    Basis          []provenance.JournalID
}

type CapabilityStateRecord struct { // DERIVED PROJECTION
    Capability        CapabilityID
    State             CapabilityState
    Scope             CapabilityScope // the ISSUED scope, unchanged for the capability's life
    LatestStateFact   CapabilityStateID
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
}

type CommitRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT
    PhaseState PhaseStateID
    From       protocol.PhaseId
    To         protocol.PhaseId
    Candidate  TransitionCandidateID
    Capability CapabilityID
    Actor      provenance.AgentID
    RecordedAt time.Time
}

type DisclosureRecordKind uint8

const (
    DisclosureRecordPlan DisclosureRecordKind = iota + 1
    DisclosureRecordAttempt
    DisclosureRecordResult
)

// DisclosureRecord is DELETED. It was declared "IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT or FACT per
// Kind" and carried a DisclosureDeliveryStatus while spanning the Plan and
// Attempt kinds that INV-1 places in the no-status snapshot class. That is not
// a legal value under a rule that says "exactly one of four kinds", the status
// was meaningless for two of three arms, and because the union was absent from
// the classification table the guard could not see it — the fourth instance of
// the defect class INV-1 exists to end, inside the revision that introduced
// INV-1 (aura-plugins-i5imy BLOCKER A-1, aura-plugins-wwyvw BLOCKER A-2).
//
// Three concrete records replace it. Each lands in exactly one INV-1 class,
// only the result arm has a status, and this matches how section 12.2 already
// gives every other record family its own concrete type.

type DisclosurePlanRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Recipient ActorRef
    Phase     protocol.PhaseId
    Role      protocol.RoleId
    Policy    ContextPolicyDefinitionRef
    Selection ContextSelection
}

func (r DisclosurePlanRecord) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureAttemptRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT
    Attempt   DisclosureAttemptID
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Recipient ActorRef
    Channel   DisclosureChannel
    AckMode   AcknowledgementMode
}

func (r DisclosureAttemptRecord) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type DisclosureResultRecord struct { // IMMUTABLE FACT; the status is the assertion
    Result    DisclosureResultID
    Plan      DisclosurePlanID
    Attempt   DisclosureAttemptID
    Recipient ActorRef
    Status    DisclosureDeliveryStatus
}

func (r DisclosureResultRecord) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type OccurrenceQuery struct {
    Contracts []ir.RuntimeContractID
    Events    []ContractEventKind
    Actors    []provenance.AgentID
    Page      PageRequest
}

type InterpretationQuery struct {
    Occurrences []OccurrenceID
    Definitions []DefinitionJournalID
    Page        PageRequest
}

type FactQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    Kinds           []FactKind
    Definitions     []DefinitionJournalID
    Page            PageRequest
}

type UnresolvedFactQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    Reasons         []UnresolvedReason
    Page            PageRequest
}

type CandidateQuery struct {
    Interpretations []InterpretationID
    From            []protocol.PhaseId
    To              []protocol.PhaseId
    Page            PageRequest
}

type LineageQuery struct {
    Root      provenance.JournalID
    Direction LineageDirection
    Relations []CausalRelation
    Bounds    LineageBounds
    Page      PageRequest
}

type DisclosureQuery struct {
    Recipients []provenance.AgentID
    Phases     []protocol.PhaseId
    Roles      []protocol.RoleId
    Plans      []DisclosurePlanID
    Kinds      []DisclosureRecordKind // empty means all three
    Page       PageRequest
}

// Immutable bodies. No status filter: a body has no status.
type DefinitionReadQuery struct {
    Kinds []DefinitionKind
    Page  PageRequest
}

// Derived state. Status filtering lives here and only here.
type DefinitionStateQuery struct {
    Kinds    []DefinitionKind
    Statuses []DefinitionStatus
    Page     PageRequest
}

type CapabilityQuery struct {
    Capabilities []CapabilityID
    States       []CapabilityState
    Actors       []provenance.AgentID
    Page         PageRequest
}

type CommitQuery struct {
    Epochs []provenance.TaskID
    Phases []protocol.PhaseId
    Page   PageRequest
}

type OccurrencePage struct { Items []OccurrenceRecord; State PageState }
type InterpretationPage struct { Items []InterpretationRecord; State PageState }
type FactPage struct { Items []FactRecord; State PageState }
type UnresolvedFactPage struct { Items []UnresolvedFactRecord; State PageState }
type CandidatePage struct { Items []TransitionCandidateRecord; State PageState }
type LineagePage struct { Nodes []provenance.JournalID; Links []CausalLinkRecord; State PageState }
// One page, three typed arms, one ascending-JournalID cursor over their union.
// PageSize bounds the union, not each arm. Adding three reader methods was the
// alternative; one method with typed arms keeps LifecycleReader's shape and keeps
// a single stable ordering across the disclosure family.
type DisclosurePage struct {
    Plans    []DisclosurePlanRecord
    Attempts []DisclosureAttemptRecord
    Results  []DisclosureResultRecord
    State    PageState
}
type DefinitionPage struct { Items []DefinitionSnapshot; State PageState }
type DefinitionStatePage struct { Items []DefinitionStateRecord; State PageState }
type CapabilityPage struct { Items []CapabilityStateRecord; State PageState }
type CommitPage struct { Items []CommitRecord; State PageState }

type LifecycleReader interface {
    Occurrences(context.Context, OccurrenceQuery) (OccurrencePage, error)
    Interpretations(context.Context, InterpretationQuery) (InterpretationPage, error)
    Facts(context.Context, FactQuery) (FactPage, error)
    UnresolvedFacts(context.Context, UnresolvedFactQuery) (UnresolvedFactPage, error)
    Candidates(context.Context, CandidateQuery) (CandidatePage, error)
    Lineage(context.Context, LineageQuery) (LineagePage, error)
    Disclosures(context.Context, DisclosureQuery) (DisclosurePage, error)
    Definitions(context.Context, DefinitionReadQuery) (DefinitionPage, error)
    DefinitionStates(context.Context, DefinitionStateQuery) (DefinitionStatePage, error)
    Capabilities(context.Context, CapabilityQuery) (CapabilityPage, error)
    Commits(context.Context, CommitQuery) (CommitPage, error)
}
```

Every filter collection has a 64-value maximum, is constructor-validated, and is defensively copied.
Empty optional filter dimensions mean any; `Page`, and the required root for lineage, are never
optional. `Truncated` means more matching data exists because the named bound was reached; `Next`
is non-nil exactly when continuation is possible.

Production tests and shipped commands may use only `LifecycleReader`, or the underlying public
bounded `Journal().Facts()` where explicitly documented. Direct SQL, private projection DTOs, and
test-only exports cannot satisfy an acceptance gate. **This rule now has a static guard** (§16.4);
PROPOSAL-8 asserted it five times and guarded it zero times while giving the replay rule a guard
(`aura-plugins-237wx` B4).

At M1 the occurrence reader is served **by replay from journal facts**, not from a materialised
index written on the hook path. Enlisting a Pasture index write inside Provenance's Apply
transaction is not possible on the pinned API — `Apply` takes no transaction handle, the
transaction is private to `applyPreparedOperation`, and the only `OpenSQLite` option seeds
`ml_models` — so PROPOSAL-8's "index rows are written inside the owning Apply **or** rebuilt by
replay" offered a branch that cannot be built. The disjunction is deleted and replay is stated
(`aura-plugins-4acdq` item 11(a)).

## 13. Malformed ingress, retention boundary, and response

### 13.1 Invalid-delivery matrix

Every row below is a row of corpus `ingress_invalid.yaml` and is executed by exactly one named
test, `TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus` (§16.1 item 3). PROPOSAL-8 left this matrix as prose with
no named owner (`aura-plugins-237wx` A3).

| Input | T1 | T2/T3/context | Process result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled generated registration gives known contract/event; malformed, duplicate-key, invalid UTF-8, truncated, or over-limit bytes | one bounded occurrence with the exact capture disposition | none | neutral exit 0; redacted diagnostic if needed |
| Enabled known registration with unsupported schema | one `CaptureUnsupportedSchema` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Enabled registration and payload event mismatch | one `CaptureEventMismatch` occurrence | none | neutral exit 0 |
| Withheld or unregistered event | no store open, no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; support report gives the typed reason |
| Payload-only unknown event without a trusted registration coordinate | no receipt | none | neutral exit 0; stderr explicitly says no receipt |
| Store / definition activation / T1 Apply failure | no false receipt claim | none | neutral exit 0; actionable redacted storage diagnostic |
| T1 succeeds and T2 fails | receipt remains | no partial T2/T3/context | neutral exit 0; internal diagnostic cites the occurrence safely |
| Contended append exceeding the 1-second caller deadline (P0-PIN) | no receipt, zero writes, definite typed failure | none | neutral exit 0; actionable contention diagnostic naming the deadline |

Host stdout contains only the mechanical native response. It never exposes JournalID, rowid,
ActivityID, database path, raw prompt/tool/transcript data, or retention keys.

**Not in this matrix, deliberately:** a semantically-identical-different-byte delivery. The
byte-identical double-invocation case in §16.1 item 1 strictly dominates it for detecting any
reintroduced content-derived dedup key, because identical bytes collapse under every normalization.
Two reviewers disagreed on this; `aura-plugins-237wx`'s argument is the correct one and
`aura-plugins-0lbsy` IMPORTANT 1's request for the case is recorded as rejected rather than
overlooked.

### 13.2 Response boundary

Target-independent interpretation cannot import host response internals. Generated scripts register
and forward only; they never parse the payload, and `MutateGeneratedPayloadParse` (§16.4) proves
that guard bites. M1-M4 expose only one mechanical neutral response. `Stop` and `SubagentStop` are
captured before the loop guard; active loop state produces a suppressed fact and no recursive
consultation.

Future allow/deny/ask/defer verdict and process-health encoding remains open UAT (§19.4). Generic
CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny. A deliberate gate cannot activate until its exact host
fixture and the future response UAT pass.

## 14. Corrected Claude 2.1.210 audit: exactly 30 events

Unchanged from PROPOSAL-8, and verified row by row by `aura-plugins-4acdq` against
`internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:69-100`, `internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:322-361`,
and `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go:148-183`, including the five previously-invented rows. The
private hostcontract becomes their sole production source; the independent fixture manifest verifies
them. All events require the common `session_id` and may admit common `transcript_path`, `cwd`,
`permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`, `effort`, `agent_id`, and `agent_type` only where the pinned
descriptor allows. Common presence is not semantic identity.

Behaviour abbreviations: `OBS` nonblocking, no mutation, report-and-continue, no reconciliation;
`GATE` blocking, no mutation unless stated, exit-2-would-block, host-native reconciliation; `COND`
conditionally blocking, `config_source=policy_settings` is the pinned nonblocking matcher; `STOP`
blocking gate consulted only while `stop_hook_active=false`; `HUMAN` blocking explicit-human-response
classification, `MutationNone`.

The behaviour column describes host capability, not Pasture authority. Only an Enabled activation is
registered; every audit row remains in the independent catalogue whether Enabled or Withheld.

| # | Event; exact event-specific fields; identity additions; behaviour | T2 evidence/candidate and bidirectional use |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `SessionStart`; `source`, `model`, `session_title`; none; OBS | Assert observed session boundary and supplied metadata states. Candidate session bind/resume only with launch capability. M4 may inject committed phase/role/assignment/worktree context. |

| 5 | `UserPromptExpansion`; `prompt`, `command_name`; none; GATE | Record command and expanded-prompt references. Link source only when explicit correlation exists. No direct control. |
| 6 | `Stop`; `stop_hook_active`; none; STOP | Record turn-stop claim, never completion. Candidate checkpoint only with other evidence. Active loop emits suppression; inactive M4 may return feedback. |
| 7 | `StopFailure`; `error`, `error_type`; none; OBS | Record failed-stop / error metadata or protected reference. Recovery candidate only; never success. |
| 8 | `PreToolUse`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; GATE with input mutation capability | Record tool intent and input state/reference. Candidate gate/tool policy; event alone has no control authority. M4 may supply tool context; future M5 may encode a typed gate response. |
| 9 | `PermissionRequest`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `request_id`; required request identity; GATE | Record permission request and tool relation. The pin has no options field. Candidate verdict request only; no transition. |
| 10 | `PermissionDenied`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`; none; OBS | Record observed denied attempt. The pin has no reason/source, so those remain unresolved unless another fact supplies them. Corrective candidate only. |
