| 12 | `PostToolUseFailure`; `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `error`, `tool_use_id`; required tool-call identity; OBS | Record failed tool result / error reference. The pin has no interrupt field. Corrective candidate only. |
| 13 | `PostToolBatch`; `batch_results`; none; GATE | Record bounded batch result reference and explicit members only if captured. Candidate checkpoint from member facts, not batch occurrence alone. M4 may return bounded aggregate context. |
| 14 | `FileChanged`; `file_path`; none; OBS | Assert `ObservedPath` only. Actor, bytes, diff, commit, and prompt remain unresolved until explicit enrichment. M4 may refresh path-scoped rules. |
| 15 | `CwdChanged`; no event-specific fields; none; OBS | Record only the common `cwd` state supplied by the pin. It cannot assert old/new cwd. M4 may refresh scope under selected retention. |
| 16 | `ConfigChange`; `config_source`; none; COND | Record configuration-change source. Candidate invalidation/review only; never changes protocol law. M4 may refresh/revoke affected rules. |
| 17 | `InstructionsLoaded`; `file_path`, `memory_type`, `load_reason`, `globs`, `trigger_file_path`, `parent_file_path`; none; OBS | Record host-reported instruction metadata / inclusion links. Exact content and delivery are unresolved without a snapshot and acknowledgement. No transition. |
| 18 | `WorktreeCreate`; no event-specific fields; none; GATE | Record worktree-create request only. The pin has no returned path. Candidate allocation; normative bind requires assignment capability. Do not replace host creation initially. |
| 19 | `WorktreeRemove`; no event-specific fields; none; OBS | Record removal signal only; the pin has no path. Candidate release; normative unbind requires a current lease. M4 may revoke verified worktree context. |
| 20 | `SubagentStart`; common `agent_id`, `agent_type`; required agent identity; OBS | Record child-agent claim and link to parent only when proven. Candidate assignment start; normative bind requires delegation capability. M4 may disclose child scope. |
| 21 | `SubagentStop`; `agent_transcript_path`, `stop_hook_active`; required agent identity; STOP | Record child-stop and transcript reference, never task completion. Active loop suppresses consultation. Completion/handoff remains candidate pending evidence and capability. |
| 22 | `TeammateIdle`; `teammate_name`; none; GATE | Record scoped idle claim. Candidate readiness / missing-work only. M4 may return committed assignment context; no automatic transition. |
| 23 | `TaskCreated`; `task_id`; none; GATE | Record native task claim. Native task ID is not a Provenance TaskID. Candidate import/link/create; normative allocation requires governed assignment capability. |
| 24 | `TaskCompleted`; `task_id`; none; GATE | Record native completion claim. Candidate close only after required activity/test/review facts; scoped capability and current task state are mandatory. Future response may ask the host to keep working. |
| 25 | `PreCompact`; `trigger`; none; GATE | Record compaction request/trigger. The pin has no instructions field. Candidate continuity checkpoint only. M4 may plan bounded continuity context. |
| 26 | `PostCompact`; `trigger`; none; OBS | Record compaction completion/trigger. The pin has no summary, so summary remains unresolved unless a later contract supplies it. M4 may refresh from retained facts. |
| 27 | `Notification`; `message`, `notification_type`, `title`; none; OBS | Record host attention signal with protected message/title state. Never treat as a human response or causation without request identity. |
| 28 | `MessageDisplay`; `message`, `content`; none; OBS | Record display evidence/reference only. It is not transcript truth, a decision, or authority. Later response backends preserve host behaviour. |
| 29 | `Elicitation`; `request_id`, `fields`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; GATE | Record external input request/schema/server states. Candidate Pasture decision request only if a proven issued-request challenge binds it; Claude 2.1.210 cannot satisfy normative binding. |
| 30 | `ElicitationResult`; `request_id`, `response`, `mcp_server_name`; required request identity; HUMAN, MutationNone | Record one observed response and request/server claims. The pin cannot prove original/effective values or an overrider. It remains evidence/candidate only and cannot commit a human decision for this contract. |

Completeness requires rows 1-30 exactly once and in this order. Activation is orthogonal: a Withheld
row remains part of catalogue truth but is absent from host registration.

## 15. Retention and tombstone matrix, parameterized by UAT, gating M1

This proposal does not select a retention mode. The selected mode is a blocking UAT output and its
entire matrix must pass before any event carrying that capture class becomes Enabled.

**The retention gate is M1, not M4.** PROPOSAL-8 §14 said the matrix must pass before Enabling any
event carrying that capture class, but §16 listed it only under M4 — while M1 Enables payload-bearing
events (`SessionStart` carries `source`, `model`, `session_title`; `UserPromptSubmit` carries
`prompt`) and §6.2's `OccurrenceEnvelopeRef` makes `RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef` mandatory at T1.
The two statements could not both be true (`aura-plugins-237wx` A1). §6.1's
`WithheldRetentionMatrixPending`, §17's M1 gate, and §19.1 all say M1.

**The gate is per capture class, everywhere.** PROPOSAL-9 moved the gate and then stated it two
ways: §17's M1 cell said "UAT-selected retention matrix passing" unconditionally, while this
section and §21 said "before any event carrying that capture class becomes Enabled". A worker
reading §17 and a worker reading §21 build different gates, and §20 sided with §17. That is the
A1 contradiction relocated rather than removed (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` B1, second defect).

> **Retention gate, stated once.** An event may be Enabled only when the UAT-selected retention
> matrix has passed **for the capture class that event carries**. Otherwise it is Withheld with
> `WithheldRetentionMatrixPending`.

§17's M1 cell, §20's checklist item, and §21's BDD are all aligned to this form. The
per-capture-class form is chosen over the whole-matrix form because it is the one that keeps M1
reachable under all three UAT options and makes metadata-only genuinely the smallest M1 — under
the unconditional form, selecting a payload mode would block M1 even for events that carry no
payload.

**Ownership moves with the gate.** A gate at M1 whose corpus and production code are owned by an
M4 slice is the IP-2b loop reintroduced (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` B1, `aura-plugins-bxwry` F1). §18.1
makes retention ownership UAT-conditional exactly as it already makes S5's channel adapter
UAT-conditional, and §18.4 adds **IP-R** so the ordering is stated rather than inferred. The
metadata-only matrix is not merely a corpus over existing behaviour; the two payload matrices
require key handling, fail-closed on a wrong key, bounded authenticated ciphertext, tombstone plus
object removal, no resurrection through replay and projection rebuild, and rotation preserving
permitted refs. None of that can sit in an M4 column while M1 depends on it.

| Mode | Required blocking tests |
|---|---|
| Metadata only | Raw prompt/tool/transcript/path/elicitation bytes never appear in the journal, projections, readers, logs, stderr, temporary files, or replay. Missing policy-required content emits typed `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect. |
| Encrypted local payload | Keys are never journaled or logged; missing or wrong key fails closed; ciphertext is bounded and authenticated; deletion appends a tombstone and removes key/object according to policy; readers return tombstoned/missing without plaintext leakage; replay and projection rebuild cannot resurrect deleted content; key rotation preserves permitted refs and history. |
| External content-addressed payload | Store and object refs are typed and bounded; content identity verifies fetched bytes; a missing or deleted object returns typed unresolved/tombstoned state; deletion appends a tombstone; journal and projection replay cannot re-upload or resurrect; logs and queries expose no content or credentials. |

All modes preserve occurrence identity, the runtime/version envelope, policy-permitted native
binding metadata, causal links, disclosure history, capability history, and commits. Tombstones
never erase the fact that content existed and never rewrite prior JournalIDs. Raw JSON remains behind
private retention-policy accessors and never enters `OccurrenceRecord` or another target-neutral
type.

Each mode is a corpus with must-pass and must-fail rows and its own operator-kill accounting
(§16.0). All three now carry explicit paths, because PROPOSAL-9 assigned
`retention_metadata_only.yaml` an owner and no path (`aura-plugins-bxwry` F7):

| Mode | Corpus path | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata only | `internal/lifecycle/receipt/testdata/corpora/retention_metadata_only.yaml` | S1, unconditionally |
| Encrypted local payload | `internal/lifecycle/retention/testdata/corpora/retention_encrypted_local.yaml` | **S1R**, and only if UAT selects it (§18.1) |
| External content-addressed | `internal/lifecycle/retention/testdata/corpora/retention_external_cas.yaml` | **S1R**, and only if UAT selects it (§18.1) |

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROPOSAL-10 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 4/7 (Section 16)

## 16. Validation: corpora, named proofs, matrices, and guards

### 16.0 The corpus harness: extend `internal/acceptance`, do not build a second one

The URD (`aura-plugins-hznvh`) carries a user FIX-NOW, recorded verbatim:

> "Are our test cases taking on the same shape as the ... schema/develop/TESTING.md ? We should
> extract out test cases into YAML fixtures, and utilize a testing harness to perform combinatorial
> and mutation tests over the test corpora."

with the requirement stated as: adopt the Schema corpus idiom for **current and subsequent epoch
acceptance tests** — typed YAML `Case`/`Corpus` rows with must-pass/must-fail classification,
provenance and mutation metadata; non-vacuity and coverage guards; deterministic bounded
combinatorial expansion; and named typed mutation operators. YAML is pure data and contains no
executable Go, SQL, or shell.

PROPOSAL-8 adopted none of it. **PROPOSAL-9 adopted it by inventing a second framework.**

#### 16.0.1 What is already committed, and why this is the fifth "second X"

`internal/acceptance` exists in the tree today, committed at `269c838` as
`test(acceptance): add deterministic corpus foundation`. It is 3,089 lines including tests, it
is data-only by construction, and it already implements almost everything PROPOSAL-9's §16.0
proposed to build:

| Capability | Where it already is |
|---|---|
| Corpus / case model with must-pass and must-fail classes | `schema.go:11-31,156-173` — `SchemaVersion = "pasture.acceptance-corpus/v1"`, `CaseClass{MustPass, MustFail}`, `Corpus{Schema, ID, MaxGenerated, Cases, Operators}`, `Case{ID, Class, Target, Setup, Expect, Delta, Provenance, Mutations}` |
| **Per-case mutation metadata** | `schema.go:172` — `Case.Mutations []MutationOperatorID` |
| Case provenance | `schema.go:267-271` — `ProvenanceSource{Requirement, Record, Rationale}`, all three required non-empty |
| **Referenced raw-byte fixtures** | `schema.go:193-198` — `DataValue{Inline, Fixture}`, exactly one of the two; `loader.go` rejects an empty fixture path and validates it |
| Typed expectation oracles | `schema.go:89-117` — `OracleKind` with seven values including `OracleNoWrites` |
| Strict data-only YAML loading | `loader.go:140-197` — bounded read, one document only, `KnownFields(true)`, and `rejectExecutableYAML` refusing anchors, aliases, and explicit tags |
| Static input bounds | `schema.go:13-22` — 1024 cases, 4096 generated, 64 operators, 8 MiB document, 1 MiB data value, 256 argv entries |
| Deterministic bounded mutation expansion | `mutation.go:34-133` — sorted deterministic order, canonical-duplicate rejection, no-op rejection, `MaxGenerated` enforcement |
| **Non-vacuity accounting** | `mutation.go:118-131` — an operator that selects zero compatible rows, or generates zero mutants, or an expansion that generates no mutants at all, is an error, not a warning |
| **Kill / survive evaluation** | `report.go:52-191` — `EvaluateMutations` fails when a mutant survives, when a mutant is not executed, when an operator executes zero mutants, or when **an operator kills zero mutants by its declared oracle** |
| Exact per-plane persisted deltas | `schema.go:244-265` — `PersistedDelta` over graph / assignments / decisions / evidence / activities / events / journal / projection |
| **Bounded read-only store snapshot** | `snapshot.go:33-43,84-148` — `SnapshotLimits`, `SnapshotFile` opening `mode=ro` with `query_only(1)` in one read-only transaction, producing `StoreSnapshot{Tables, Semantics, RowCount, ByteDigest, UnrelatedDigest}` with `SemanticSnapshot` per plane |

PROPOSAL-9's §16.0 declared a new package `internal/lifecycle/corpus` with its own `Case`,
`Corpus`, `Expectation`, `CaseProvenance`, `NonVacuityReport`, and `MutationOperatorID`, and §16.2
declared a new `lifecycletest.SnapshotPlaneDeltas` helper. Both duplicate the above. Four of the
six PROPOSAL-9 reviewers converged on it; `aura-plugins-emmh7` cited it line-exactly and made it
its single blocker.

**This is the fifth instance of one defect class this epic has already rejected four times:**
no second graph, no second FSM, no second descriptor table, no second phase-adjacency table — and
now, no second corpus framework. Two YAML schemas, two mutation registries, two non-vacuity
reports, two sets of bounds, and two direct-SQL exceptions would have to evolve together forever,
which is exactly the maintenance burden the URD corpus idiom exists to avoid.

**On how it happened.** This is not an architect error to be charged to the previous round. The
coordinating instruction that produced PROPOSAL-9's §16.0 asked for the URD corpus idiom to be
adopted and did **not** ask whether a corpus framework already existed. Absent that instruction,
the architect designed the types the idiom implies rather than searching the tree for a package
committed two days earlier that no production code yet imports. The corrective is procedural and
is recorded in §18.0: **the must-change derivation now runs over shared test infrastructure as
well as production files**, and a "does this already exist?" search is part of deriving ownership.

> **Rule.** `internal/acceptance` is the **one** shared acceptance-corpus framework for this
> repository. S1 extends it. `internal/lifecycle/corpus/**` is deleted from the plan.
> `lifecycletest.SnapshotPlaneDeltas` is deleted from the plan. Individual corpus files and
> production-path runners stay owned by the vertical slice that owns the behaviour they test.

#### 16.0.2 What S1 adds to `internal/acceptance`

Five additions, each traceable to a PROPOSAL-9 finding. Nothing already listed in §16.0.1 is
re-declared, renamed, or wrapped.

**(a) Authentic capture provenance** — closes `aura-plugins-h8wbo` BLOCKER B1.

`ProvenanceSource` records *why* a case exists. It cannot record that the bytes came from a real
host, so a fixture may be derived from the very descriptor it is supposed to validate, and
`MutateRemovePayloadField` stays green. That failure is live today:
`internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go:100-108` checks only that each declared *identity* field
appears in the payload table, so a dropped non-identity field is invisible; and
`internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend_test.go:501-529` synthesizes each payload from
`mapping.Identities()` — the table it is meant to check — and then asserts against that same
source. `aura-plugins-9umx1` is the standing record of this gap.

```go
// added to internal/acceptance

type CaptureOrigin string

const (
    OriginAuthenticCapture CaptureOrigin = "authentic-capture" // bytes recorded from a real host run
    OriginPinnedContract   CaptureOrigin = "pinned-contract"   // transcribed from the pinned descriptor
    OriginReviewFinding    CaptureOrigin = "review-finding"    // added because a review found the gap
    OriginAuthored         CaptureOrigin = "authored"          // hand-authored oracle
)

// IMMUTABLE. Required in full when Origin == OriginAuthenticCapture.
// A fixture cannot claim authenticity without naming the host that produced it,
// the exact version, how it was captured, and the digest of the bytes on disk.
type CaptureProvenance struct {
    Origin         CaptureOrigin
    Harness        HarnessKind // existing: claude-code | codex-cli | opencode | antigravity
    HarnessVersion string      // exact pinned host version, e.g. "2.1.210"
    CaptureSource  string      // the exact command or mechanism that produced the bytes
    RawFileDigest  string      // "sha256:..." over the referenced DataValue.Fixture file
    CapturedAt     string      // RFC3339 UTC
}
```

`ProvenanceSource` gains one field, `Capture CaptureProvenance`. The loader verifies that
`RawFileDigest` matches the bytes at the case's `DataValue.Fixture` path and refuses the corpus
otherwise, so a stale or swapped fixture fails at load rather than passing silently.

Consequences, each with a gate:

- §6.1's Enabled constructor requires `OriginAuthenticCapture` for the event's fixture. A fixture
  with any other origin yields `WithheldMissingFixture`. A self-derived payload can no longer back
  an Enabled event.
- §16.1 item 1 rejects a non-authentic fixture before executing.
- `MutateRemovePayloadField` deletes a **non-identity** production field and must be killed by the
  independent authentic capture. Against a descriptor-derived fixture it cannot be; against a real
  capture it is. That is the whole point of the operator and it did not previously have an oracle
  that could kill it.

**`aura-plugins-9umx1` becomes an explicit named prerequisite, P0-CAPTURE**, parallel in kind to
P0-PIN: it is not a slice, it gates the first Enabled event rather than a milestone's code, and
its cost is real because it needs a live host at the pinned version. It is recorded in §17 and
§18.4 (**IP-C**) rather than assumed cheap. Its scope at M1 is exactly the events the UAT selects
in §19.2 — not all 30.

**(b) Milestone-scoped coverage** — closes `aura-plugins-3hkoz` B2 and defines one of
`aura-plugins-bxwry` F2's two undefined type names.

```go
// added to internal/acceptance

type Milestone string // "M1".."M6"; ordered, closed, validated

type CoverageDimensionID string // closed per corpus, declared in the corpus document

type CoverageValue string // closed per dimension, declared in the corpus document

type CoverageDimension struct {
    ID        CoverageDimensionID
    Milestone Milestone     // the milestone at which THIS dimension must be fully covered
    Values    []CoverageValue // 1..64, the closed value set
}

type CoverageSpec struct {
    Milestone  Milestone           // the corpus's own owning milestone
    Dimensions []CoverageDimension // 1..32
}

type CoverageResult struct {
    Dimension  CoverageDimensionID
    Milestone  Milestone
    Gated      bool          // false when Dimension.Milestone is later than the run milestone
    Uncovered  []CoverageValue
}
```

A corpus run is evaluated **at a milestone**. A dimension whose `Milestone` is later than the run
milestone is reported with `Gated: false` and does not fail the run; at or before it, an uncovered
value is a hard failure exactly as PROPOSAL-9 stated.

This is not a softening. It is what makes the hard failure mean a real defect rather than a
scheduling artifact. PROPOSAL-9 made non-vacuity a hard failure and then declared coverage its
owner could not produce: `reader_cursor.yaml` is S1 at M1 but `TruncatedDepthLimit`,
`TruncatedNodeLimit`, `TruncatedEdgeLimit`, and `CursorInvalidLineageBounds` are reachable only
through S4's lineage reader at M3, and `TruncatedHistoryBound` only through S5 at M4;
`guard_mutation.yaml` is S1 at M1 but at least six of its twelve operators mutate S0's
`pkg/protocol` or S2's hostcontract and generated assets. Both corpora would have been red from
S1 L2 until M3 and M6, and the predictable resolution under schedule pressure is that the coverage
line gets edited rather than the plan. §18.4 carries a widening row per deferred dimension so the
widening is scheduled rather than remembered.

**(c) A source-mutation family, distinct from data mutation** — closes `aura-plugins-3hkoz` B3.

B3 is right that the condition that justifies the whole harness — *every must-fail case flips when
its guard is removed* — was unexecutable for seven of eight corpora, and right that
`NonVacuityReport.GuardsProvenBy` could not express case-to-operator linkage. Extending
`internal/acceptance` closes most of it **without new types**, because the existing framework
already has what PROPOSAL-9 was missing:

- `Case.Mutations []MutationOperatorID` is already per-case mutation metadata, so B3's proposed
  `ProvenBy` field is not needed — the linkage already exists and the loader already requires it
  to be present and explicit.
- `EvaluateMutations` already reports per-mutant `Killed`/`Survived` with the source case and the
  operator, already fails on a survivor, and already fails when **an operator kills zero mutants
  by its declared oracle** (`report.go:179-181`). B3's proposed `UnprovenMustFailCases` is the
  existing survivor list.
- `mutation.go:97-99` already rejects an operator that produces a canonical no-op, which is the
  "the mutation did not actually change anything" failure in the same family.

What genuinely does not fit is that the twelve §16.4 operators mutate **production source**, not
case data. The existing `applyMutation` transforms argv, stdin JSON, and setup records; it cannot
add a second descriptor table to the repository. So S1 adds a second, explicitly named operator
family rather than bending the first:

```go
// added to internal/acceptance

// Data mutation operators transform a Case (existing family: MutationOperatorID,
// MutationOperator, ExpandMutations, EvaluateMutations). Unchanged.

// Source mutation operators transform PRODUCTION SOURCE in a scratch worktree,
// run one named static guard, and require it to turn red. A guard with no
// operator is not a guard; an operator that leaves its guard green is a
// survivor and fails the run, using the same kill/survive accounting.
type SourceMutationOperatorID string

type SourceMutationOperator struct {
    ID        SourceMutationOperatorID
    Guard     string // the exact test or vet target that must fail
    Rationale string
}

type SourceMutationResult struct {
    OperatorID SourceMutationOperatorID
    Guard      string
    Killed     bool // the guard failed, as required
    Observed   string
}
```

`guard_mutation.yaml` declares source-mutation operators; the other corpora declare data-mutation
operators. Both families report through the same kill/survive accounting, so "an operator killed
zero mutants" remains one rule with one meaning.

The behavioural data operators the other seven corpora need are added by the slice that owns the
corpus, not centrally: drop one capability scope-axis comparison (**one operator per axis**, which
is what makes fifteen rows mean fifteen guards rather than one), drop the cursor query-fingerprint
check, drop one `CaptureDisposition` validator, drop the `BuildIdentityExact` requirement, drop
the retention tombstone check, drop the zero-write delta assertion. The per-axis form is the
specific answer to B3's worked example: thirteen must-fail rows that all refuse on **state** before
the axis comparison is ever reached would satisfy every stated condition while proving one guard.
§16.2 adds the corresponding requirement that each must-fail row fail **for the stated reason**.

**(d) An extensible operator roster** — closes `aura-plugins-bxwry` F3.

PROPOSAL-9 made "all 12 `MutationOperatorID`" a coverage dimension. Freezing the pinned 30 Claude
events is correct because they transcribe an externally fixed contract that Pasture does not
control. Freezing Pasture's own invented operator set is not: if S1 discovers a thirteenth
operator, or that one of the twelve is unbuildable as specified, the corpus spec is wrong rather
than the plan being incomplete.

> **The twelve source-mutation operators in §16.4 are a required minimum, not a closed coverage
> set.** The gate is the property §16.4 already states: **every guard names at least one operator,
> that operator runs, and it kills.** A slice may add operators; it may not remove a guard's
> proof. `guard_mutation.yaml`'s coverage dimension is *guards*, not *operators*.

**(e) Lifecycle target arm, runners, and the zero-write snapshot** — the thin part.

`Target` already has a `TargetNativeEvent` arm with `NativeEvent{Harness, Contract, Event,
InputJSON}` and a `TargetProductionCommand` arm with argv and stdin. Both are exactly what §16.1's
proofs drive: the built `pasture hook lifecycle` binary is a production command, and an authentic
Claude delivery is a native event. S1 adds the lifecycle **runners** — the code that executes a
case against generated registration, the built binary, a file-backed journal, and the public
bounded reader — under the slice that owns each corpus. Runners are not a framework; they are the
per-slice production-path drivers the framework was built to be driven by.

For zero-write proofs, `acceptance.SnapshotFile` already returns `SemanticSnapshot` per plane over
graph, assignments, decisions, evidence, activities, events, journal, and projection — read-only,
bounded, `query_only(1)`, in one read-only transaction. That **is** the plane-delta helper §16.2
needed. `lifecycletest.SnapshotPlaneDeltas` is deleted; §16.4's bounded-reader guard whitelists
`acceptance.SnapshotFile` by name instead, and the exception stays exactly as visible and
countable as PROPOSAL-9 intended, with one fewer thing to maintain.

#### 16.0.3 The non-vacuity contract, restated over the shared framework

Every corpus run, at its evaluation milestone, asserts:

1. the corpus is non-empty, and expansion generates at least one mutant (`mutation.go:129-131`);
2. every declared case and every generated mutant is executed exactly once
   (`report.go:124-135,170-174`);
3. every mutant is **killed** by its declared oracle; a survivor fails with the source case, the
   operator, and a reproduction command (`report.go:159-168`);
4. every declared operator executes and kills at least once (`report.go:175-181`);
5. every `CoverageSpec` dimension gated at this milestone has at least one case per value
   (new, §16.0.2(b));
6. every authentic-capture fixture's `RawFileDigest` matches the bytes on disk
   (new, §16.0.2(a)).

A failing run is a test failure, not a warning. Conditions 1-4 are already implemented and already
tested in `internal/acceptance`; 5 and 6 are what S1 adds.

#### 16.0.4 Corpora, owners, and the matrix each replaces

**Eight corpus families, ten files.** PROPOSAL-9's prose said "eight corpora" while the table's
retention row listed three files with different owners and different milestones
(`aura-plugins-3hkoz` C5).

| Corpus family | Files | Replaces | Owner | Coverage dimensions (milestone gated at) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Invalid ingress | `internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/testdata/corpora/ingress_invalid.yaml` | §13.1 (8 rows) | S2 cases, S1 runner | `CaptureDisposition` all 8 (M1); registration trust (M1); store failure (M1) |
| Claude catalogue | `internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/testdata/corpora/claude_2_1_210_catalogue.yaml` | §14 (30 events) | S2, hand-authored oracle; does not import hostcontract | all 30 `ContractEventKind` (M1); behaviour class (M1); identity additions (M1) |
| Retention | the three files and owners in §15 | §15 (3 modes) | S1 (metadata-only); **S1R** (payload modes, only if UAT selects one) | `EvidencePayloadKind` (M1); deletion, tombstone, resurrection (M1) |
| Definition and build | `internal/lifecycle/interpretation/testdata/corpora/definition_versioning.yaml` | §16.2 definition matrix | S3 | `DefinitionKind`, `DefinitionStatus`, `BuildIdentityStatus` (M2) |
| Capability scope | `internal/lifecycle/control/testdata/corpora/capability_scope.yaml` | §16.2 authority matrix | S8 | all 15 `CapabilityScopeAxis` (M6); all 4 `CapabilityState` (M6); all 3 `CapabilityRevocationReason` (M6); all 5 `RequestBindingAxis` (M6) |
| Reader and cursor | `internal/lifecycle/receipt/testdata/corpora/reader_cursor.yaml` | §16.2 reader matrix | S1 | `CursorErrorKind` — 6 values (M1), `CursorInvalidLineageBounds` (M3); `TruncationReason` — `TruncatedPageSize` (M1), depth/node/edge (M3), `TruncatedHistoryBound` (M4) |
| Races and zero-write | `internal/lifecycle/control/testdata/corpora/race_zero_write.yaml` | §16.2 race matrix | S8 | race shape, loser class, delta plane (M6) |
| Guard mutation | `internal/lifecycle/guard/testdata/corpora/guard_mutation.yaml` | §16.4 guards | S0/S1/S2/S3/S8 each own their own guards' operators; S1 owns the file and the runner | **guards**, not operators: replay, descriptor ownership, phase adjacency, bounded reader, INV-1 shape, INV-1 totality, generated artifact, field completeness, write model, binding-axis parity (each gated at the milestone its guard's subject lands) |

The catalogue corpus has **one** name. PROPOSAL-9 called it `claude_2_1_210_catalogue.yaml` in
§16.0 and `claude_2_1_210_expected.yaml` in §18.1 (`aura-plugins-bxwry` F7); §18.1 now uses the
name above.

The `guard_mutation.yaml` coverage row is what closes B2's second half. Its dimension is the set
of guards, each gated at the milestone its subject lands, so S1 at M1 is responsible for the
guards that exist at M1 — replay, INV-1 shape, INV-1 totality, bounded reader, write model — and
S2's descriptor and generated-artifact guards widen the same corpus at their own milestone through
§18.4. §18.3's S1 L2 leaf and S2 L2 leaf are consistent with this rather than contradicting it.

### 16.1 Required black-box production-path proofs

1. `TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceReader` — for each Enabled event, generate the actual
   registration, invoke the built command with the authentic raw fixture against one file-backed
   database, and read `OccurrenceRecord` only through `LifecycleReader`. Two byte-identical process
   invocations yield two operation IDs and two occurrence JournalIDs with no replay field.
   **The fixture must carry `OriginAuthenticCapture` with a matching `RawFileDigest`** (§16.0.2(a));
   a descriptor-derived fixture is rejected before execution rather than silently accepted, which
   is what makes `MutateRemovePayloadField` killable at all.
2. `TestWithheldClaudeEventIsNotRegistered` — every Withheld event is absent from host registration
   and present in the support report with the exact typed reason. Enabled union Withheld equals the
   independent 30-event oracle exactly once.
3. `TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus` — drives `ingress_invalid.yaml` through generated registration,
   built binary, file-backed journal, and public readers only. Asserts one distinct T1 record with
   the exact `CaptureDisposition` where required; asserts no later-plane effects; asserts that
   untrusted, unregistered, and store-failure inputs produce no false receipt without touching SQL.
   This is §13.1's named owner.
4. `TestHumanSignalToCommitLineageBlackBox` — **the human-signal leg is now named.** A real
   `UserPromptSubmit` occurrence, delivered through the generated registration and the built binary,
   is interpreted by the codebook into `FactHumanSignal` on the evidence plane. That signal is bound
   to the host session/request, followed by an agent tool call, selected VCS/tool/worktree
   enrichment, artifact and commit evidence, then queried human-to-code and code-to-human through
   the bounded reader. Missing and contradictory enrichment remain `RelationObservedPath` plus typed
   unresolved facts; no timestamp or session proximity promotes confidence.
   **`UserPromptSubmit` Enabled is therefore an explicit M3 gate.** It is turn-scoped, not
   per-tool-call, so the `aura-plugins-cvlu6` restriction in §17 does not bar it. A *Pasture-issued*
   human decision is `CapabilityRecordHumanDecision` and is proved at M6 in item 8, not here.
   PROPOSAL-8 required a "Pasture-issued human signal" at M3 with no M3-available issuance path,
   which would have been satisfied by seeding it in the test while the gate reported green
   (`aura-plugins-237wx` A2).
5. `TestDisclosurePlanAttemptResultReader` — committed state enters the pure projector, then
   separate plan/attempt/result operations are read publicly; candidate, stale, wrong-recipient,
   unauthorized, and unknown-policy cases write nothing; a truncated-history case with a
   completeness-required policy produces `DisclosureSuppressed` and no partial packet; projection
   rebuild is identical.
6. `TestClaudeLifecycleToInterpretationReader` — the same generated/binary path reaches T1, T2,
   exact definitions, stable slots, and public fact/link/candidate/unresolved pages. Direct
   interpreter or `Apply` tests cannot substitute.
7. `TestTransactionTimeBeforeLockSpanningExpiry` — upstream Provenance holds the SQLite writer
   across the deadline; a fresh queued operation loses after lock acquisition with typed expiry and
   zero writes; an exact committed retry still returns its original result.
8. `TestHookCandidateToEpochControl` — a real Enabled hook produces a candidate; production services
   `Issue` then `Bind` a capability and T3 commits through one FSM; public capability and commit
   readers return the result. No direct projection writer or test-only export counts. This test also
   carries the *Pasture-issued human decision* leg deferred from item 4.
9. `TestSliceStartAvailabilityUnderHookWriteLoad` — **availability.** Launches the §4.4 writer
   estimate as distinct built-binary child processes on one file-backed `pasture.db` behind a
   barrier, and requires the slice to start within the 2-second deadline for every run of a fixed
   sample. Also asserts the contended/uncontended p99 ratio bound and the absolute
   one-transaction-per-delivery count from §4.6.
   **It additionally asserts delivery outcome**, which PROPOSAL-9 omitted and which is the only
   assertion here that moves in the right direction as the system degrades: per run, count
   deliveries that returned a receipt readable through `LifecycleReader` and deliveries that
   returned typed `IngressDeadlineError`, and **require the deadline-failure count to be zero**.
   Deadline-failed `Apply` calls enter the p99 sample at the full 1000 ms deadline value (§4.6).
   Without this, an implementation dropping 40% of deliveries passes the start assertion *more*
   comfortably than one dropping none, because a hook that gives up at 1 s stops competing for the
   write lock — and the per-delivery transaction count is satisfied by a failed delivery
   contributing zero (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` B4). A nonzero count fails item 9 **and** fires §4.4
   revisit trigger (e); it is not retried away.
10. `TestSliceStartHonestFailureUnderInjectedDelay` — **honest failure.** Deterministically injects
    the delay rather than racing for it, and requires exactly the honest "enqueued but never started"
    error naming the slice id and the deadline, with `Completed=false`, `SliceFailed` fired, no
    fabricated projection success, and every receipt committed during the window still readable
    through the public bounded reader.

11. `TestBuildIdentityHonestyThroughLifecycleReader` — **the public-reader binding for
    `definition_versioning.yaml`.** Executes the corpus's build rows through the generated
    registration and the built binary, then reads definitions, definition state, interpretations,
    and unresolved facts **only** through `LifecycleReader`, and additionally reads the context and
    control planes through their public readers to assert they are empty. It asserts: two
    definitions sharing a VCS revision with different `BuildContent` remain distinct and neither
    claims to be "the" build for that revision; `BuildIdentityDirtySource` and
    `BuildIdentityUnresolved` each surface as a public `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild` fact; and
    neither produces a disclosure plan or a commit. PROPOSAL-9 restored the three build rows to
    §16.2 but bound them to no named black-box test, and §18.3's S3 L2 was a component-test list,
    so a green suite could exercise `DefinitionResolver` directly while the public records
    misreported the build state (`aura-plugins-h8wbo` BLOCKER B2). Owned by S3, gated at M2.

Splitting 9 from 10 is `aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 1's fix and it is right: PROPOSAL-8's single test
accepted, as a passing outcome, the regression it existed to prevent. Item 9 can only pass by the
deadline holding *and* by no delivery being lost; item 10 can only pass by the failure being
honest; neither can pass by the other's outcome.

**Wave placement and flake policy** (`aura-plugins-237wx` B1 fix 4). Item 10 is deterministic and
race-clean and runs in the **default mandatory `-race` wave**. Item 9 makes wall-clock assertions and
is therefore **excluded from the default `-race` wave** and run in an explicitly named measurement
wave without `-race`; §16.4's blanket `-race` rule carries this one named carve-out rather than
silently contradicting a wall-clock threshold. Item 9's parameters: 200 deliveries per writer,
nearest-rank p99 over the sorted per-`Apply` sample **with deadline failures included at the full
1000 ms deadline value**, zero permitted deadline failures, three consecutive runs required green,
and a single flake reopens the §4.4 revisit trigger rather than being retried away.

Item 11 is deterministic and race-clean and runs in the default `-race` wave.

### 16.2 Definition, build, authority, reader, privacy, and race matrices

Each bullet below names its corpus. The seven cases PROPOSAL-8 dropped from PROPOSAL-7 §14 are
restored and marked **[restored]** (`aura-plugins-237wx` B2).

**Definition and build** (`definition_versioning.yaml`):
- Activate two codebooks, two interpreters, two builds, and two context policies over the same
  source facts; every dependent record resolves its exact definition JournalIDs and never silently
  selects latest.
- Retire a definition and prove historical resolution still works while new active resolution does
  not choose it. Prove that `ResolveHistorical` returns no status and that `DefinitionStateRecord`
  is reproduced identically by replaying `DefinitionStateFact` in JournalID order after deleting
  the projection.
- **[restored]** Same VCS revision with two different build content identities: two distinct
  definitions, neither overwriting the other, neither claiming to be "the" build for that revision.
- **[restored]** Dirty source: `BuildIdentityDirtySource` is recorded, produces
  `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild`, cannot back an Enabled activation, and cannot create context or
  control effects.
- **[restored]** Missing or unknown build identity: `BuildIdentityUnresolved` permits T1, yields an
  unresolved T2 fact, and yields no control or context effect.

**Authority** (`capability_scope.yaml`), through the public `EpochControlService` only:
- **[restored]** One case per `CapabilityScopeAxis`, mutating exactly one axis at a time, asserting
  `CapabilityScopeMismatch{Axis}` names the mutated axis. Fifteen cases, not one phrase.
  **Each must-fail row must fail for the stated reason.** Every row declares the per-axis
  source-mutation operator that proves it (§16.0.2(c)), and the row is a survivor — a failure —
  unless dropping *that axis's* comparison flips *that row*. Thirteen rows that all refuse on
  capability **state** before the axis comparison is ever reached would otherwise satisfy every
  stated non-vacuity condition and prove one guard, which is
  `aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 2 surviving its own fix (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` B3).
  Each row's setup therefore establishes a Bound, unexpired, in-scope capability and mutates
  exactly the one axis under test.
- **[new]** `bind_widens_native_binding` — `Bind` supplies a `NativeBinding` absent from the issued
  `Scope.Bindings`. Must fail with `CapabilityScopeMismatch{Axis}` naming that binding kind's axis,
  zero writes, and the issued scope unchanged in `CapabilityStateRecord`.
- **[new]** `bind_actor_outside_issued_scope` — `Bind` supplies an actor other than the nonzero
  issued `Scope.Actor`. Must fail with `CapabilityScopeMismatch{ScopeAxisActor}`, zero writes.
- **[new]** `bind_then_commit_with_binding_never_issued` — a two-step attempt to reach commit with
  a binding that was never in the issued scope. Must fail, zero writes, no capability state change.
  These three rows are what distinguish *scope-fixed-at-Issue* from *bind-defines*; every
  PROPOSAL-9 case passed identically under both readings (`aura-plugins-i5imy` BLOCKER A-2).
- **[new]** Issued-request chain, one row per `RequestBindingAxis`, all zero writes
  (`aura-plugins-wwyvw` BLOCKER A-1):
  `host_only_request_id` — a host-supplied `BindingRequest` value with no `IssuedRequestRecord`
  behind it never reaches `Issue`;
  `wrong_request` — `Bind` cites a response occurrence carrying a different request identity;
  `wrong_session` — the response occurrence's `BindingSession` differs from the issued session;
  `wrong_contract` — the response occurrence's runtime contract differs from the issued contract;
  `wrong_response_occurrence` — the cited occurrence is not the response to this request.
  Plus one must-pass row: issued request → exact response occurrence → single atomic
  consumption and phase CAS.
- **[new]** `sources_is_not_a_match_criterion` — a commit whose `Scope.Sources` no longer resolve
  to the same current facts still succeeds, proving `Sources` is provenance and not a fourteenth
  silent comparison (§11.2.3).
- **[restored]** Three distinct revocation timings: revoke before bind, revoke before commit, and
  revoke racing commit.
- **[restored]** Already-consumed: a second commit against a Consumed capability returns
  `CapabilityStateError{Observed: Consumed, Required: Bound}`.
- **[restored]** Fresh operation ID against stale, revoked, consumed, and expired current state —
  all four, not only expired.
- Issuance, binding, and expiry; two-consumer single-use race; two capabilities racing one current
  phase; exact retry returning before current-state checks; same operation ID with changed input
  conflicting.
- Every loser carries before/after **public-reader** snapshots proving zero partial journal,
  capability, phase, decision, context, and projection writes.

**Reader and cursor** (`reader_cursor.yaml`): malformed, tampered, mismatched, future, and stale
cursors; zero and over-limit page and lineage bounds; stable snapshots; no duplicate or skip;
continuation; explicit cycles; node/edge/depth truncation; defensive copies; and the newest-first
at-snapshot selection rule for every bounded history collection (§10.1). Coverage requires all
seven `CursorErrorKind` and all five `TruncationReason` values, **each gated at the milestone that
makes it reachable** — six cursor errors and `TruncatedPageSize` at M1, `CursorInvalidLineageBounds`
and the depth/node/edge truncations at M3 with S4's lineage reader, `TruncatedHistoryBound` at M4
with S5's bounded history (§16.0.2(b), §18.4).

**Races** (`race_zero_write.yaml`): fixed actor activation, definition activation, distinct
receipts, revocation versus consume, two consumers of one capability, and two capabilities for one
current phase. **Which cases require separate processes is now stated**
(`aura-plugins-237wx` item 7): the T3 capability races and the lock-spanning expiry case
(§16.1 item 7) require **separate processes**, because a single process cannot demonstrate the
property; the remaining races may use independently opened handles, which exercise real WAL and
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` contention through `internal/dbconn.SharedDSN`.

**Zero-write delta snapshots.** Snapshot journal, capability, phase, decision, context, and
projection deltas before every losing operation and assert zero partial semantic writes. These
require table-level reads, which §12.2's rule otherwise forbids. They are therefore the **one named
exception** — and the helper already exists: `acceptance.SnapshotFile` returns
`StoreSnapshot.Semantics`, a bounded read-only `SemanticSnapshot` per plane over graph,
assignments, decisions, evidence, activities, events, journal, and projection
(`snapshot.go:33-43,73-148`), taken with `mode=ro` and `query_only(1)` in one read-only
transaction. PROPOSAL-9 declared a new `lifecycletest.SnapshotPlaneDeltas` for this;
that helper is **deleted** and §16.4's reader guard whitelists `acceptance.SnapshotFile` instead.
The exception stays visible and countable (`aura-plugins-237wx` B4 closing note), with one fewer
thing to keep in step (`aura-plugins-emmh7`).

**Write model** (see §4.6): transaction count per delivery is absolute; contended/uncontended p99
ratio is the relative gate; uncontended hold is measured and reported against the 5 ms design
estimate; no fixed sub-100 ms retry loop anywhere on the hook path; the 1-second caller deadline is
honoured once P0-PIN lands.

**Privacy**: parameterize the canaries by the UAT-selected retention mode and run them through the
generated process, journal, readers, logs, stderr, tombstone, and replay paths.

**Rebuild**: delete lifecycle, phase, lineage, disclosure, definition-state, and capability-state
projections and rebuild identical public results from the journal.

### 16.3 Fixture rules

**[restored]** Raw JSON and binary host bytes remain **separate referenced files** under
`fixtures/**`, named from the corpus by path and never inlined into YAML. Duplicate keys, invalid
UTF-8, byte ordering, and truncation are exactly the properties §13.1 tests for, and YAML
normalization destroys all four (`aura-plugins-237wx` B2 row 7).

The shared framework already enforces this structurally: `acceptance.DataValue` requires exactly
one of `Inline` or `Fixture` (`loader.go` `dataValueWire.convert`), and every raw host delivery
uses `Fixture`. §16.0.2(a) adds the second half — the referenced file's digest must match the
case's `CaptureProvenance.RawFileDigest`, so the bytes cannot be swapped after the capture was
attested.

The independent 30-event oracle is hand-authored and does not import or iterate the production
hostcontract. Self-derived payloads, direct frontend calls, and direct `Apply` never count as
activation proof — and after §16.0.2(a) that is enforced by the fixture's origin rather than
asserted in prose.

### 16.4 Static and generation guards, each proven to bite

> **Rule.** Every guard below names the **operator or mechanical fixture** that must turn it red,
> and that proof runs. A guard with no proof is not a guard.

PROPOSAL-9 stated this as "every guard names the mutation operator", which three of its own eleven
rows then contradicted by naming "compile-fail fixtures" or "regeneration diff" — legitimate proof
mechanisms that are not `MutationOperatorID` values and that the accounting therefore could not
record (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` C4). The rule above is the true one. Source-mutation operators and
mechanical fixtures both report through §16.0.2(c)'s kill/survive accounting.

| Guard | Rejects | Proven by |
|---|---|---|
| Replay source guard | `ReplayKey`, `RecordReplayed`, lifecycle result `Replayed`, occurrence dedup/window/count code, payload digest as occurrence key. Scoped to lifecycle results, leaving `pkg/protocol/task_assignment.go:28` and the other Provenance-operation idempotency flags untouched. | `MutateReintroduceReplaySymbol` |
| Host descriptor ownership + `go list` dependency | a second event/field/behaviour table outside hostcontract and generated derivatives | `MutateAddSecondDescriptorTable` |
| Phase adjacency ownership | a phase-adjacency table outside `pkg/protocol` | `MutateAddPhaseAdjacencyTable` |
| **Bounded-reader guard** | under a **path pattern** — any `_test.go` beneath `cmd/pasture/**`, `internal/lifecycle/**`, or `internal/engine/budget/**` — any `database/sql` import, any projection-internal package import, or any SQL string literal. Exactly one helper is exempt by name: `acceptance.SnapshotFile`. | `MutateDirectSQLInProductionTest` |
| **INV-1 shape guard** | a lifecycle-status enum field inside a declared immutable-snapshot type, or a declared derived-projection type missing `SnapshotJournalID` | `MutateMutableFieldInSnapshot` |
| **INV-1 totality guard (new)** | an exported type in the lifecycle model packages that appears in no §3.0 class, or in more than one | `MutateUnclassifiedLifecycleRecord` |
| **Binding-axis parity guard (new)** | the native `CapabilityScopeAxis` values and the `NativeBindingKind` values not being in bijection | `MutateAddUnmappedBindingKind` |
| Compile-fail imports | model, codebook, lowering, context, and control importing private host response or descriptor packages | compile-fail fixtures |
| Clean regeneration | generation drift or retired generated assets | regeneration diff |
| Generated-artifact behaviour | env/argv operation selection; semantic branching in generated output; generated code parsing the payload; generic internal error mapped to deny | `MutateEnvSelectedOperation`, `MutateGeneratedSemanticBranch`, `MutateGeneratedPayloadParse`, `MutateGenericErrorToDeny` |
| Field/identity completeness | a dropped payload field or identity field that the current containment check cannot see | `MutateRemovePayloadField` (killed only against an `OriginAuthenticCapture` fixture, §16.0.2(a)), `MutateRemoveIdentityField` |
| Write-model guard | a second per-delivery write transaction | `MutateSecondPerDeliveryTransaction` |
| Phase parity | runtime and generated surfaces not derived from one immutable phase law | regeneration diff |

**The bounded-reader guard is a path pattern, not an allowlist.** PROPOSAL-9 scoped it to "a named
set of production-path acceptance test files", which fails open on the exact omission §18.0 was
written about: a test file added later and not added to the set is unguarded, and the set was not
yet enumerable because §18.1's S2 column says only "rewrite untracked command/handler spine tests"
(`aura-plugins-3hkoz` C3). The live violation at `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:132-195`
is precisely a file that would have been on nobody's list before it was written. A denylist over a
path pattern costs nothing and fails closed. The named-set language survives as documentation of
*which* tests the rule is chiefly aimed at — §16.1 items 1-11 plus the S3-S8 black-box tests in
§18.1 — not as the guard's scope.

The guard closes a rule PROPOSAL-8 asserted in §11.2, §15.1 items 1/3/4/5/6, §19 line 22, design
checklist item 18, and the §20 BDD, and enforced nowhere — while giving the replay rule a guard.
The violation is live and reads as ordinary test code: `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go`
opens `sql.Open("sqlite", ...)` at `:133-138` and runs raw `SELECT` over `audit_events`,
`activities`, and `context_edges` at `:139-195`. §18.5 disposes of that file, but a disposition is
not a guard (`aura-plugins-237wx` B4).

**The INV-1 totality guard is the same lesson applied to §3.0.** A classification table that is
the guard's only data source has a blind spot exactly the size of what it omits, and PROPOSAL-9
demonstrated that within one revision by omitting four records including a live violation. The
totality rule turns "every record is classified" from a sentence into a check
(`aura-plugins-i5imy` BLOCKER A-1 fix 3).

All Go test commands use `-race`, with the single named carve-out for §16.1 item 9 stated in §16.1.
No duplicate non-race wave counts. Commit gates remain `gofmt`, `go vet`, race tests,
`CGO_ENABLED=0 go build`, Nix checks, clean generation drift, and `git diff --check`.

Source-mutation operators run in their own named wave, not in the ordinary test wave: each mutates
production source in a scratch worktree, runs exactly one guard target, requires it to fail, and
discards the worktree. No source mutation is ever applied to the working tree a developer or CI
builds from.

PROPOSAL-10 NORMATIVE CONTINUATION 5/7 (Sections 17-19)

Authoritative continuation of PROPOSAL-10. Read with the description and the other six
continuations. Section numbering is unchanged from PROPOSAL-9.

## 17. Milestones

| Milestone | First user-visible value | Essential gate | Explicit exclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0-PIN** (prerequisite, not a milestone) | none | **SATISFIED** — upstream `0976165` landed; Pasture `f513772` pins it; S1 L3 asserts the optional `ContextJournal` and maps its failure to `IngressDeadlineError` | not a slice; does not split S7 |
| **P0-CAPTURE** (prerequisite, not a milestone) | none | an authentic captured raw payload, at the pinned host version, exists under `OriginAuthenticCapture` with a matching digest, for **each event the UAT selects in §19.2** — not for all 30. Tracked as `aura-plugins-9umx1`, recorded as **IP-C** | not a slice; needs a live host at the pinned version, so its cost is stated rather than assumed |
| M1 progressive receipt | At least one UAT-selected fixture-ready event is registered and publicly queryable; other events are visibly Withheld | P0-PIN re-pinned and asserted; P0-CAPTURE satisfied for every Enabled event; fixed actor resolved read-only; no replay symbols; Enabled-event authentic process proof; `ingress_invalid.yaml` corpus green with its operator-kill accounting; bounded occurrence reader served by replay; support report; **UAT-selected retention matrix passing for the capture class of every Enabled event**; write model measured per §4.6 with §16.1 items 9 and 10 passing, including zero deadline-failed deliveries | no full-catalogue claim without all 30; no semantics, context, or control; no blocking per-tool-call event Enabled before `aura-plugins-cvlu6` resolves |
| M2 interpretation | Enabled events produce versioned facts, unresolved facts, links, and candidates | exact definitions; connected T1->T2->reader; stable slots; version evolution; `definition_versioning.yaml` green including dirty and missing build honesty, bound to the public reader by §16.1 item 11 | no context send or normative mutation |
| M3 lineage | Explicit human/agent/tool/worktree/artifact/commit chains query both ways | **`UserPromptSubmit` Enabled**; named positive path (§16.1 item 4); missing and contradictory cases; bounded graph/cursors/replay | no probabilistic or timestamp causation; no Pasture-issued human decision yet |
| M4 context | Committed-state context plan/attempt/result history is queryable | UAT channel/ack choice; exact policy refs; recipient isolation; immutable outcomes; bounded-history truncation and suppression cases | no deliberate deny; no candidate-as-state |
| M5 response | Exact contract response encoding is mechanically verified | future verdict / process-health UAT; per-contract fixture; generic fault and deny isolation | no unsupported host result |
| M6 authority | Scoped current capability can commit selected candidates through one FSM | S7 upstream transaction-time condition and second re-pin; `capability_scope.yaml` green across all fifteen axes, all five `RequestBindingAxis` rows, and the three bind-never-widens rows; process races; old writer disabled; projection replay | Claude 2.1.210 Elicitation authority remains unavailable: the pin cannot prove a Pasture-owned challenge round trip, so no Claude 2.1.210 event satisfies §11.2.1's issuance chain |
| Catalogue completeness | All 30 Claude 2.1.210 events Enabled | independent all-30 authentic process corpus | does not block earlier verified M1 events |

Cross-harness equivalence, a runtime-authored codebook DSL, probabilistic inference, cross-machine
ordering, and a generic fourth harness remain later work and are not prerequisites for M1-M6.

## 18. Exact implementation slices, ownership, leaves, and integration

The supervisor creates Beads slices and L1/L2/L3 leaves only after review, Plan UAT, and
ratification. The paths below are the exact future ownership contract. No two active slices own the
same path. A conditional wiring transfer occurs only after the prior owner is merged, reviewed, and
closed, and is recorded by the supervisor before the next worker starts.

### 18.0 How ownership is derived

`aura-plugins-oygyo` parsed PROPOSAL-8's §17.1 table mechanically: 172 distinct paths, zero
cross-slice conflicts. `aura-plugins-bxwry` re-parsed PROPOSAL-9's §18.1 the same way and measured
188 distinct paths with exactly two multi-owner entries, `go.mod` and `go.sum`, both explicitly
sequential. Both checks are sound. Neither can find the defect `aura-plugins-4acdq` found — a file
that **must** change and is simply absent from the table — because a parse of the list can only
validate the list.

> **Ownership rule.** Ownership is re-derived from the set of files that MUST change to satisfy
> each milestone gate, and only then checked for exclusivity. A file that must change and has no
> owner is a plan defect of the same severity as two owners for one file.

That rule was applied in PROPOSAL-9 to the M1 **production** file set and produced three
additions. It was not applied to the M1 **validation** file set, and three of the four
`aura-plugins-3hkoz` blockers are the consequence: a gate moved or was newly declared and the
ownership or coverage that must satisfy it was not re-derived. Two extensions:

> **Extension 1 — validation is part of the must-change set.** Corpora, harness code, static
> guards, load harnesses, and their integration points are derived and owned the same way
> production files are. A gate at milestone N whose corpus or production path is owned at
> milestone N+k is the same defect as an unowned file.
>
> **Extension 2 — search before declaring.** Before a slice is given a new shared package, the
> derivation asks whether the repository already has one. PROPOSAL-9 declared
> `internal/lifecycle/corpus/**` while `internal/acceptance` sat committed and unowned in the same
> tree, and the table's exclusivity parse could not see it because an existing package that no
> plan row mentions is invisible to a parse of the plan. `internal/acceptance` is now owned
> (S1, §18.1).

Applying the rule and both extensions produced, relative to PROPOSAL-9: `internal/acceptance/**`
gains an owner; `internal/lifecycle/corpus/**` is deleted; retention ownership becomes
UAT-conditional with a new conditional slice **S1R**; the two load cases gain an explicit leaf; and
three corpus paths are corrected or supplied.

**On the "172 mechanically verified paths" carry-forward.** Appendix B previously listed it among
work "carried forward without reopening". That was a fact about PROPOSAL-8's table, not about
PROPOSAL-9's or this one (`aura-plugins-i5imy` n5). What carries forward is the **method**, not the
number. PROPOSAL-9's table measured 188; PROPOSAL-10's table differs again — it adds
`internal/acceptance/**` and the S1R rows and removes `internal/lifecycle/corpus/**` — so it must
be re-parsed, and then checked against the must-change derivation above. Appendix B is corrected
accordingly. Given that Appendix B exists specifically to stop carrying an acceptance forward past
the change that invalidated it, applying that discipline to a row of its own is the point.

### 18.1 Exclusive file ownership

| Slice | Milestone | Exclusive production ownership | Exclusive tests / generated ownership |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0-PIN** | prerequisite to M1, **satisfied** | `go.mod`, `go.sum` — **first** re-pin only, before S1 L3. Upstream work landed in `github.com/dayvidpham/provenance` at `0976165` and is owned there. | upstream tests owned upstream; Pasture side is the pin, plus S1's `ContextJournal` assertion in `internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go` |

## 19. Open Plan UAT decisions

No option below is selected here. The open UAT records the final choice and updates the URD before
ratification and slicing. Each is a real engineering alternative with stated tradeoffs, not an
approval level.

### 19.1 Retention mode — **an M1 blocker**

- **Metadata only.** Lowest privacy and operations cost. Unavailable content remains explicitly
  unresolved as `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld`. No raw object exists to delete or resurrect, so the
  deletion and no-resurrection half of the matrix is trivially satisfied.
- **Encrypted local payload.** Richer local reconstruction. Requires key handling, deletion,
  rotation, tombstone, and no-resurrection guarantees, and a fail-closed path on a missing or wrong
  key.
- **External content-addressed payload.** Durable and shareable evidence. Adds a store, credentials,
  an availability dependency, deletion obligations, and a privacy surface outside the local file.

This choice gates M1, not M4 (§15). **What each option costs is now stated as a slice set, not as
"adds its full matrix"** — PROPOSAL-9 said the latter without saying who owned it, which is exactly
where the omission was visible (`aura-plugins-3hkoz` B1, `aura-plugins-bxwry` F1):

| If UAT selects | M1 slice set | What S5 keeps |
|---|---|---|
| **Metadata only** | S1, S2. `retention_metadata_only.yaml` and the `UnresolvedRetentionWithheld` path are S1's, already in its column. **S1R does not exist.** | nothing retention-specific |
| **Encrypted local payload** | S1, **S1R**, S2. S1R owns `internal/lifecycle/retention/**`, `local_encrypted.go`, and its corpus, and merges before the first payload-bearing Enabled event (IP-R). | disclosure-side consumption only |
| **External content-addressed** | S1, **S1R**, S2. Same as above with `external_cas.go`. | disclosure-side consumption only |

Metadata-only is therefore genuinely the smallest M1: one fewer slice, and the per-capture-class
gate in §15 means a payload mode never blocks an event that carries no payload.

### 19.2 First activated high-value hooks

UAT receives the current activation readiness report and may select only events whose authentic
exact-version fixture and production path already pass. No grouping overrides per-event proof, and
this proposal does not preselect an event.

**This choice also scopes P0-CAPTURE.** Each selected event needs an authentic captured payload at
the pinned host version, under `OriginAuthenticCapture` with a matching digest (§16.0.2(a),
`aura-plugins-9umx1`). Capture cost is real — it needs a live host — so the number of events
selected here is directly the capture work M1 takes on, and IP-C gates the first Enabled event on
it.

This choice is also the shared-file write throttle (§4.5 option E), so the UAT weighs two properties
per candidate event, not only its evidence value:

- **Fanout.** Session- and turn-scoped events (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`,
  `UserPromptSubmit`) produce far fewer deliveries than per-tool-call events (`PreToolUse`,
  `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`), which fire on every tool call and scale with subagent count.
- **Blocking profile.** A gate event appends inside a window the host holds open, so its contention
  competes directly with engine signal delivery, whereas an observational event does not.

Candidate groupings: session spine (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Setup`); human-signal ingress
(`UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`) — note this is the M3 lineage prerequisite;
tool/artifact lineage (`PostToolUse`, `FileChanged`) — note `PostToolUse` is per-tool-call;
multi-agent orchestration (`SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TeammateIdle`).

Enabling any blocking **per-tool-call** event additionally requires `aura-plugins-cvlu6` to have
resolved the start-signal deadline question.

### 19.3 Context delivery and acknowledgement

Delivery alternatives:
- **Generated start/compaction material.** No live host round trip; context is baked into what the
  host loads. Cheapest and most reliable, but refresh is coarse.
- **Dynamic per-contract host response.** Context rides the hook response, so it is phase-exact.
  Requires the response encoder (M5) and couples context to blocking-hook timing.
- **Explicit `pasture epoch context` pull.** Agent asks when it needs context. No host coupling at
  all, but delivery depends on the agent choosing to ask.

Acknowledgement alternatives:
- **Positive host evidence.** Strongest proof; only available where the pinned contract emits it.
- **Explicit agent receipt.** Requires the agent to call back; proves receipt but not comprehension.
- **Unavailable.** Record delivery and unknown. Honest and always available.

UAT selects one compatible pair and its failure and retry semantics. The pair determines which S5
adapter file exists (§18.1) and whether a `DeliveryCorrelationToken` is needed at all (§10.2).

### 19.4 Future verdict and process-health encoding

- **Typed host-native verdict separated from process health.** Cleanest: a deny is a deliberate
  typed value and a crash is not. Requires a per-contract response fixture proving both encodings.
- **Exact native exit/status semantics where the pinned contract proves them.** Least new
  machinery; only defensible for contracts whose exit-code meaning is pinned.
- **Continued neutral-only behaviour.** Zero risk of an internal fault denying a user's work; no
  gating capability ever ships.

No deny, ask, or defer value becomes reachable until this UAT and the exact response fixture pass.
Generic CLI exit code 2 can never become native deny.

### 19.5 Artifact enrichment depth and storage

- **Commit and path metadata only.** Cheapest; lineage answers "which commit" but not "which bytes".
- **Encrypted local diff or snapshot.** Answers "which bytes" locally; inherits the encrypted-local
  key, deletion, and rotation obligations.
- **External content-addressed evidence.** Answers "which bytes" durably and shareably; inherits the
  external store's credential and availability obligations.

Orthogonal to occurrence identity and must be compatible with the retention mode selected in 19.1.
Missing depth never promotes an observation beyond `RelationObservedPath`.
