author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW C (axis: deliverability, testability, traceability) — round 1

VERDICT: REVISE

Scope creep check first: clean. Payload lowering is withdrawn (T14, R6, A10) and no section re-introduces tool arguments, tool output, or prompt text. No mutation arm appears. No native-JSON path appears. R1-R7 and R9 each map to a slice and to at least one acceptance criterion. The findings below are about R8, about arithmetic, about parallel-wave feasibility, and about test strength.

C1 BLOCKER — R8 (feoub 14 groups) is not discharged honestly.
Evidence: the 14 groups are named verbatim on the Plan-UAT record aura-plugins-a6loa (2026-08-04): rejection proofs; deny/input mutation; other lifecycle events; #58 coverage mutations; #63 version matrix; #55 live Claude captures; #54 panic proof; #57 receipt retries; #59 retention/GC; #60 status guard; #61 cause boundary; #62 native lookup; all raw captures beyond the four cleared fixtures; Strike/Grok Build and M4+. Section 4.5 names only the rejection-test groups and the two differential-equivalence cases, then claims "none stays deferred". That claim is false: #63 is explicitly kept deferred by URD R2; #57, #59, #60, #61 and #62 appear nowhere in the proposal; Strike/Grok and M4+ are out of scope; input mutation stays deferred by 1ofi5.
Change requested: replace 4.5 with a 14-row table, one row per named group, each row carrying either (slice, test name) or RE-DEFERRED with the reason. Any group that stays deferred must be raised as a decision in section 8, because URD R8 says all 14 are re-opened.

C2 BLOCKER — Wave-1 event counts contradict S2, so the slices and the sizing are wrong.
Evidence: 4.3 states S2 deletes the 14 existing fixture pairs and leaves the enabled count at 0/0/0. Section 3 then sizes S4 as "capture + enable 20 events", S5 as 8, S6 as 45. Those numbers are the pre-S2 remainders. After S2 the real work is 28 + 10 + 47 = 85 captures, not 73.
Change requested: restate S4/S5/S6 as 28 / 10 / 47 captures, re-size section 9 on 85 events, and state the recapture of the 14 cleared fixtures as explicit rows in the harness that owns them.

C3 BLOCKER — no clearance or privacy procedure for about 85 authentic captures.
Evidence: the current repository standard (feoub R5) cleared exactly four raw fixtures, and only after a field inventory, a credential signature scan, and an explicit user clearance reference. This proposal replaces that with one redaction rule ("home-path-v1") and one optional Clearance string that may be empty. Authentic Claude and OpenCode captures carry prompts, file paths, tool output and environment data; the plan commits them to a public repository.
Change requested: define the per-capture procedure (redaction rule set, automated secret scan as a gate, what the user must inspect and approve, batch or per-event clearance), make Clearance mandatory for every enabled row, and raise the clearance model as a gate decision. Also state which raw payload classes are refused outright.

C4 BLOCKER — Wave 1 cannot run in parallel as written; exclusive ownership is not defined.
Evidence: section 4.2 puts all three harnesses in ONE generated file, activation/proofs.gen.go. Every Wave-1 worker adds rows and regenerates it, so all three collide on every commit. The same applies to internal/inventory/lifecycle_events.gen.go, metamodel.gen.go and the activation report writer. The proposal states a staging discipline only as prose in section 3 and never lists what each worker owns.
Change requested: (a) generate proofs per harness (proofs_claude.gen.go, proofs_codex.gen.go, proofs_opencode.gen.go) and prove single-file ownership; (b) add a file-ownership table for S4/S5/S6 that lists every path each worker may write, with the shared paths named and assigned to the integrator only; (c) state the integration rule: merge in completion order, and the later worker rebases and re-runs generation before the drift gate. Without (a) the staging discipline is not sufficient.

C5 BLOCKER — the capture campaign has no feasibility evidence and no escape route.
Evidence: R1 demands 47/47 on OpenCode. The registered set contains events that a worker cannot trigger on demand (for example installation.updated, server.connected, ide.* class events), and Claude has events that need rare host states. The plan says only "one instrumented session per harness". A worker that cannot produce an event has no defined action, so the slice cannot close and the wave stalls.
Change requested: (a) publish a per-event trigger recipe list per harness, or mark the events that have no known trigger; (b) add a closed-set withheld reason for "no reachable trigger" plus the rule that using it needs a user decision; (c) state what the user must provide: which machine, how many sessions, live Codex authorisation form, and any second host. Section 9 must show the user-hours as well as worker-days.

C6 IMPORTANT — the role and phase matrices are new policy that the user never saw.
Evidence: 4.4 introduces RoleAllows(ActionClass) and PhaseAllows(ActionClass) static matrices. These decide what is BLOCKED on the user machine, and no elicitation round showed their content. Decisions D1-D6 do not include them.
Change requested: add the two matrices in full to the proposal and raise them as a gate decision. A wrong cell denies real work.

C7 IMPORTANT — the gate path is described as read-only but it writes.
Evidence: 4.4 says "no workflow, no writes", then states that the session-to-actor binding is a durable claim written by the lifecycle receipt path at session start. Also the claim is read from PASTURE_ACTOR_ID with no injected seam; AGENTS.md requires that env-driven logic sits behind an injected parameter, with exactly one serial test for the real wiring.
Change requested: correct the wording to "one bounded read on the gate path; one durable claim write at session-start events", and declare the seam type that supplies the actor claim, next to CaptureSink.

C8 IMPORTANT — the unbound-session annotation will reach the user on every gate.
Evidence: D3 and A5 make every gate in a plain session return Proceed with an annotation, and 4.4 maps a Claude annotation to systemMessage. A plain interactive session fires PreToolUse on every tool call, so the user sees the same message all day.
Change requested: either record the unbound annotation durably and stay silent to the host, or state the display cadence (once per session) and prove it with a test.

C9 IMPORTANT — test gating is too weak in three places, and one path can be green while broken.
Evidence: (a) mutation-RED evidence is required only in the S0 list; S1, S2, S3 and the three harness slices have none. (b) The checklist never states -race in the normal flow, never forbids Sleep or fixed-deadline poll loops, and never states one test file per subject. (c) Section 6 asks for a production subtest "through the built binary" for every event. For OpenCode the transport is a generated TypeScript plugin and for Codex it is a generated shell runner. A Go-only proof would pass while the plugin dispatch table is wrong, so 47/47 could ship broken. The repository already has the right shape (codegen/opencode_target_test.go drives Bun, codegen/codex_transport_e2e_test.go drives the generated runner) but the proposal does not extend it.
Change requested: require mutation-RED per slice; state -race, no-Sleep and one-file-per-subject in section 6; and require that the per-event production proof runs through the real transport, that is Bun executing the generated plugin for every enabled OpenCode event and the generated runner for every enabled Codex event.

C10 IMPORTANT — the Clearance field would ship an internal reference.
Evidence: 4.2 defines Clearance as "user clearance reference (Beads id / issue)". Fixture provenance files are committed artefacts, and AGENTS.md forbids bare task identifiers in shipped artefacts; only a GitHub issue or PR URL, or a durable file path, is allowed.
Change requested: restrict Clearance to a GitHub issue URL or a committed clearance-record path, and add a test that refuses a bare task identifier.

C11 MINOR — Codex transport file counts disagree. Section 4.3 says "+10 at S5", section 6 says "Codex +8 runner files", section 6 S7 says 12 transport files. After S2 deletes everything the true numbers are 10 runners and 12 destinations. Please state one number in all three places.

C12 MINOR — the must-fail case "ACP / Gemini / Antigravity changes" from the ELICIT record has no check. Add an assertion that no registration, transport or destination for those targets changes.

C13 MINOR — sizing is not reconciled with the number the user consented to. The ELICIT question priced Universal-authentic at about 0.5 worker-day per event and 54-72 worker-days total. Section 9 gives 35-46 worker-days for a larger event set. Explain the reduction (table-driven leaf work) in section 9 so the user can re-consent.

Path to ACCEPT: C1-C5 must be resolved in the proposal text; C6-C10 need the stated changes; C11-C13 are text corrections.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW A (axis: host-contract truth and end-user behaviour) — round 1

VERDICT: REVISE

Method: every host claim in the proposal was checked against pasture 73f38d0 (read-only). Evidence paths below are pasture-relative.

A1 BLOCKER — the failure-mode table is a mechanical derivation, not a captured host contract; S0 turns it into user-visible blocking.
Evidence: internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:315-318 sets Claude failure = FailureExitTwoBlocks purely from "blocking != NonBlocking"; :391-393 does the same for Codex; :437 and :452 are constants for OpenCode. No per-event exit-code fact from a host is recorded anywhere. metamodel.gen.go therefore declares exit-2-blocks for UserPromptExpansion, PostToolBatch, ConfigChange, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate, PermissionRequest and Elicitation — events for which the repo holds no evidence that a non-zero exit blocks anything.
Change: before S0 ships hostexit.ForFailure, add a per-event, per-host EVIDENCE column (documentation quote or capture) for the exit-code claim. An event with no evidence must map to ExitContinue plus a stderr diagnostic, not to ExitBlock. State this rule in the proposal and add it to the S0 checklist.

A2 BLOCKER — an infrastructure fault is not a policy denial, and A1 (proposal §7) makes the user pay for it.
Evidence: §7 A1 uses Claude UserPromptSubmit as the flagship "evaluation failure -> exit 2" proof. §0 lists the failure sources as validation and storage errors (3m1zix). On Claude, a blocked UserPromptSubmit costs the user the prompt they just typed; the cause would be a pasture SQLite fault, not any user act.
Change: separate FAULT from DENY in hostexit. Keep fail-closed for a real policy Deny. For an internal fault, default to ExitContinue with a loud stderr diagnostic, and make fail-closed-on-fault an explicit opt-in (config key), stated in §4.1 and D-list. If the architect keeps fail-closed on faults, the proposal must state the prompt-loss consequence and make it a Plan-UAT decision.

A3 BLOCKER — T10 annotation breaks OpenCode and spams Claude, on the ordinary user path.
Evidence: .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts acceptProceed() throws unless stdout has EXACTLY one key and decision == "proceed". §4.4 gives OpenCode no annotation shape at all. T10 makes ProceedAnnotated(ReasonUnboundSession) the DEFAULT result for every plain session (PASTURE_ACTOR_ID unset). On OpenCode every gated tool call would then throw; on Claude a systemMessage would print on every PreToolUse.
Change: an unbound session must produce a plain Proceed with byte-identical native output, and the reason must be recorded in the consultation record only. Delete the host-visible annotation for ReasonUnboundSession (revise §7 A5 to assert unchanged native bytes), or specify a per-harness annotation carrier and regenerate acceptProceed to accept it. Also state which harness carries an annotation at all: Claude systemMessage and Codex systemMessage have no in-repo proof, and OpenCode has no carrier.

A4 BLOCKER — Deny on a Stop-family event can trap the user in a loop.
Evidence: lifecycle_profiles.go declares Stop and SubagentStop as blocking gates with StopLoopConsultWhenInactive, and runtime/lifecycle.go documents that policy as the guard against re-blocking a stop that an earlier block caused. §4.4 gatepolicy.Decide ignores StopLoopPolicy: a claimed actor whose assignment episode closes mid-session gets Deny on Stop and the agent cannot end its turn.
Change: gatepolicy.Input must carry StopLoopPolicy, and Decide must never return Deny for a Stop-family event (Proceed and record). Add a table-test row for it in the S3 checklist and a BDD case in §7.

A5 IMPORTANT — the Codex deny channel contradicts the repo's own Codex derivation.
Evidence: internal/lifecycle/nativeresponse/nativeresponse.go:24-47 records the pinned Codex contract from hooks/src/schema.rs and engine/output_parser.rs: HookUniversalOutputWire carries continue (bool), stopReason, suppressOutput and systemMessage; a blocking PreToolUse hook is REJECTED unless continue == true. That is an explicit, user-visible deny shape with a reason field. §4.4 instead maps Codex Deny to exit 2 with stderr, for which the repo holds no evidence.
Change: map Codex Deny to {"continue":false,"stopReason":<reason>} per the recorded contract, or state why exit 2 is preferred and cite the source line. Also preserve today's observation bytes: CodexContinuation returns {} for an observation and {"continue":true} for a gate proceed (nativeresponse.go:70-77); §4.4 flattens both to {"continue":true} and would change committed golden bytes without saying so.

A6 IMPORTANT — an OpenCode Deny is reported to the user as a broken installation.
Evidence: the generated plugin throws on ANY non-zero exit with the text "pasture hook lifecycle for <event> exited <n>: <stderr>; verify PASTURE_BIN and the generated OpenCode 1.18.10 configuration". Under §4.4 a policy Deny takes that same path, so a correct policy decision tells the user to check their binary and configuration. That message is false for a deny.
Change: the plugin generator must distinguish a policy refusal (a dedicated exit code or a typed stdout object) from an invocation fault, and must emit reason-only text for a refusal. Add it to the S6 checklist. Also state, with evidence, what an OpenCode user actually SEES when a named callback throws; the repo has no such evidence today.

A7 IMPORTANT — RequireHuman has no stated recovery path for the user.
Evidence: T11 and §7 A6 downgrade RequireHuman to Deny. The only explicit-human-response event is Claude ElicitationResult, and §3 keeps the Elicitation pair withheld while pasture #80 is open, so the arm appears unreachable in this epic. Where it does fire, the user is blocked with no way to answer, and the host may retry into repeated denials.
Change: state (1) whether the arm is reachable at all before #80 closes, (2) what a user does to unblock, and (3) which events declare Ask capability, with capture evidence. If the arm is unreachable, say so plainly and keep it as a typed stub.

A8 IMPORTANT — in-binary capture (T7) records prompts and tool payloads with no clearance gate and no notice to the user.
Evidence: tools/capture-claude-hook.sh states the standing rule "If a payload cannot be made shareable by value substitution alone, do not commit it", and its redaction is value-only home-path rewriting (home-path-v1). Committed payloads already carry real content: ingress/claude/testdata/fixtures/pre_tool_use_2_1_222.json holds tool_name, tool_input and cwd. Universal-authentic coverage extends the same commit path to UserPromptSubmit (prompt text) and PostToolUse (tool_response) for 75 more events, into a public repository. §4.2 keeps only home-path-v1, and the checklist has no clearance step; the new Clearance field (T4) is optional and ungated.
Change: (1) carry the "do not commit what value substitution cannot clear" rule into AGENTS.md and into the S1 checklist as a mandatory human clearance per fixture; (2) make the generator REFUSE an origin=authentic-capture row whose Clearance is empty; (3) default the capture directory outside the repository; (4) print a one-time stderr notice when capture mode is active, so a user always knows the session is being recorded; (5) state the overwrite and concurrency rule for two invocations of one event.

A9 IMPORTANT — a hook-free main (D6) is a silent loss of function for anyone who tracks the branch.
Evidence: §4.3 sets enabled counts to 0/0/0 at the end of S2 and says the transport wires nothing. Users do not consume pasture only through releases: aura-plugins pins the submodule and a flake input, and nix/hm-module projects hooks/, .codex/ and .opencode/ into the user's home. During the S2-to-Wave-1 window a Home Manager sync would remove every lifecycle hook with no error and no journal data.
Change: recapture the 12 currently enabled events INSIDE S2 (T3 requires the recapture anyway) so the enabled count never falls to zero; or state the window explicitly in CHANGELOG plus a guard that install refuses an activation report with zero enabled events. Add the chosen rule to the S2 checklist.

A10 IMPORTANT — D1 pins to a moving target, and T3 deletes negative controls.
Evidence: D1 says "PATH version at S2 start"; two workers on two days can pin two versions, and nothing records the value at Plan-UAT. Separately, §4.3 deletes all 14 existing pairs, but ingress/claude/testdata/fixtures holds control fixtures that the corpus needs: session_start_2_1_210_digest_mismatch, ..._origin_authored and ..._version_out_of_range. §7 A9 depends on a version-out-of-range control. The Claude contract is a RANGE (profiles.go:241), so the 2.1.222 Claude fixtures are not rejected by the pin bump; only the exact-pinned Codex and OpenCode fixtures are.
Change: freeze the three version literals at the Plan-UAT gate and record them in the proposal. Limit the mandatory recapture to Codex and OpenCode, and state that the three control fixtures are preserved or re-derived; add a checklist line for them.

A11 MINOR — Claude proceed and annotation shapes have no in-repo evidence.
Evidence: {"decision":"proceed"} exists only as the Pasture canonical object (backend MarshalJSON, nativeresponse.go:88-105). No Claude documentation, capture or test in this repo shows that Claude reads "proceed" as a decision value, or that "systemMessage" and "hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision" are accepted at 2.1.25x. The proposal marks the deny and ask shapes as assumptions but presents the proceed and annotation shapes as fact.
Change: mark all four Claude shapes as assumptions in §4.4, and add one S4 capture-backed check per shape.

A12 MINOR — response capability for post-hoc gates, and §7 A3 wording.
Evidence: metamodel.gen.go declares Codex PostToolUse and PostCompact as blocking gate-consultation, and Claude PostToolBatch likewise. A Deny after the tool ran cannot undo anything. §4.4 only says observation events get {false,false,false}.
Change: state that post-hoc gate events declare Deny=false, and list the derivation rule for ResponseCapability. Also fix §7 A3: OpenCode has no PreToolUse event; the OpenCode case is tool.execute.before.

WHAT IS RIGHT (no change asked): the withheld-reason discipline, the closed enums with a refusing zero value, the single FailureMode enum (T8), the table-driven ingress (T12) and IdentityPolicy None (T13), the "no payload in the IR" rule (T14, R6), the sequential pin bump (T1), and the generator check that refuses a target row without a fixture on disk (T5, §7 A7).

Re-review asks for: A1-A4 resolved with host evidence or a changed default; A5-A10 answered with a concrete proposal edit; A11-A12 marked or corrected.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW-B-1 (axis: architecture and data model) — reviewer-b

VERDICT: REVISE

Good, and I do not want these changed: gatepolicy.Decide(Input) as a pure total function over plain data is testable with no store; Decision/DecisionKind/DecisionReason/ExitStatus all refuse their zero value; passing `decision` into middleend.Derive is acyclic (middleend already imports backend, internal/lifecycle/middleend/evaluate.go:8) and cannot touch the gate.WriteIntent lock (internal/lifecycle/gate/gate.go:99-114), because Decision never enters a WriteIntent; T5/T6/T12 correctly move per-event cost from Go code into tables.

BLOCKERS

B1 BLOCKER — the gate types cannot compile as written (import cycle).
Evidence: §4.4 puts SessionClaim and ActorAuthority in internal/tasks (gate_authority.go) while gatepolicy.Input embeds both unqualified, and tasks.ActorAuthority.RoleAllows takes gatepolicy.ActionClass. That is tasks -> gatepolicy AND gatepolicy -> tasks.
Change: move the value types (SessionClaim, ActorAuthority, an assignment-episode view, TaskPhase, ActionClass) into ONE leaf package that neither imports the other — declare the read interface where it is consumed (gatepolicy or a new internal/lifecycle/gateauthority), and let internal/tasks import it and implement it. State the resulting edge explicitly, because today internal/tasks imports lifecycle/{model,projection,receipt} only.

B2 BLOCKER — GateAuthority has no read model; the plan assumes one that does not exist.
Evidence: tasks.ProjectAssignments has ZERO production callers (only internal/tasks/projections_test.go:236,261,271); nothing in the tree constructs an AssignmentTransition outside tests, so there is no producer of the fold input. The one real assignment read is TASK-scoped and paged: internal/tasks/epoch_assignment_service.go:428 uses JournalQueryV1{TaskIDs: ..., Limit: MaxFactPageSize} plus a per-row AuthorityGovernsTaskAt check. The gate needs the opposite shape: all ACTIVE episodes for one ACTOR. No per-task phase projection exists either (task phase lives on the task record, internal/tasks/task_update_atomic.go:110,120). So "one bounded read of already-folded state" (§1, §4.4, checklist S3) is unsubstantiated for a call that runs on every tool use.
Change: name the concrete read — an occupant-scoped journal query or a materialised assignment+phase projection table; state where AssignmentTransition values come from; state the per-gate cost budget with a measurement in the S3 checklist; and make page truncation a TYPED REFUSAL, never a Deny (a truncated read that hides an assignment would deny a legal actor).

B3 BLOCKER — S3 has nothing to prove against; S2 and S3 contradict each other.
Evidence: §4.3 says at the end of S2 "the 14 existing pairs are deleted ... the enabled count is 0/0/0 and the transport wires nothing". §6 (S3) then requires "built-binary deny proof per harness: Claude PreToolUse, Codex PreToolUse, OpenCode tool.execute.before". Those three events are withheld and fixture-less at that point, and the transport wires no hook, so the proof cannot run through the built binary. §3's ordering rationale ("S3 before Wave 1 so every newly enabled gate event is proven against the REAL decision path") depends on the proof existing.
Change: pick one and write it down — (a) S2 recaptures the minimum set (per harness: the session-start event plus one gate event) at the new pins so S3 has a live path, or (b) move the per-harness deny proofs into S4/S5/S6 and make S3's gate a store-level test only, with an explicit note that no harness proof exists until Wave 1.

IMPORTANT

B4 IMPORTANT — TaskPhase is invented and its zero value does not refuse.
Evidence: §5 lists "tasks.TaskPhase (existing phase set exposed read-only)" under "all closed; zero value refuses". There is no TaskPhase in internal/tasks. The underlying provenance.Phase (provenance pkg/ptypes/enums.go:420-437) starts at iota 0 = PhaseRequest, so a missing map entry in ActorAuthority.Phases silently reads as "request phase" and PhaseAllows answers on garbage.
Change: declare TaskPhase with an explicit Unset zero arm, expose lookup as (TaskPhase, bool), and add a closed DecisionReason for "phase unknown" that refuses rather than guessing. Correct the §5 claim.

B5 IMPORTANT — the role/phase matrices have no source of truth, and they are the combinatorial risk in this design.
Evidence: §4.4 says RoleAllows/PhaseAllows "reuse the role constraint ids already in internal/codegen/context.go roleConstraints by ID". That map is UNEXPORTED, lives in internal/codegen (context.go:119-120), and is keyed by protocol.RoleId (architect/supervisor/worker/reviewer). The gate's roles are tasks.AssignmentRole with three different arms — RoleOwnerResponsibility, RoleGoverningSupervisor, RoleAxisReviewer (internal/tasks/material_events.go:141-151). The reuse is not mechanically possible, and the real surface is ActionClass(10) x AssignmentRole(3) plus ActionClass(10) x Phase(13) = ~160 hand-authored cells that no test forces anyone to justify.
Change: state the AssignmentRole -> protocol.RoleId relationship (or drop the reuse claim); publish the two matrices as ONE exported table each with a default of DENY-or-refuse for an unlisted cell; and add an exhaustiveness test that fails when a new ActionClass, AssignmentRole, or Phase arm is added without a row.

B6 IMPORTANT — the session->actor claim is underspecified on its failure arms and conflicts with today's read-only lifecycle identity.
Evidence: §4.4 writes the claim "by the existing lifecycle receipt path at session-start events" when PASTURE_ACTOR_ID is set. That path is documented as read-only with respect to actor activation and HARD-REFUSES any actor that is not the pinned system actor (internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:19-45, especially the `actor != expected` refusal at :38-40). The DecisionReason set has no arm for an unknown or unregistered claimed actor, and no arm for "gate fired in a session whose start event was never observed" — which is normal for Codex/OpenCode where the claim depends on an enabled session-start observation.
Change: say whether the claim is a separate durable table or rebinds receipt attribution (and if the latter, what happens to the system-actor invariant); add ReasonUnknownActor and a defined behaviour for a gate in a session with no observed start (silently unbound = a silent gate hole; make it an annotated Proceed with its own reason, or a Deny — but name it).

B7 IMPORTANT — T13 misreads the waist's unresolved model.
Evidence: T13 says identity-free OpenCode observations land "with `unresolved` identities, exactly as the waist already models". waist.UnresolvedReason has exactly ONE arm, UnresolvedToolCall, and IsValid accepts only it (internal/lifecycle/waist/event.go:106-123); unresolvedFacts REFUSES every other identity kind with a typed error (event.go:264-283). Today those 45 events simply declare no identities (hostcontract/opencode_1_18_10.go:39-48) — that is not the same thing.
Change: state which it is. If "declare nothing", say IdentityPolicyNone is a table label with no waist effect. If a correlation gap must be recorded, add the reviewed UnresolvedReason arm as an explicit S1 item. Either way, state what an identity-free occurrence does to the receipt/projection correlation key when 45 of them land per session (R6 stays intact; my concern is the ordering/correlation model, not payload).

B8 IMPORTANT — T8 counts two FailureMode enums; there are THREE.
Evidence: registration/types.go:12,24-27 (2 arms); ingress/internal/hostcontract/types.go:7,19-22 (2 arms, a separate type); runtime/lifecycle.go:186-196 (6 arms). The lossy collapse lives in hostcontract too: openCodeFailure maps every non-observe-only runtime mode to FailureExitTwoBlocks (opencode_1_18_10.go:62-66), and hostcontractgen has its own failure() writer (ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen/main.go:214).
Change: name all three in T8 and in §6 S0, delete openCodeFailure, and state the resulting import edge (registration and hostcontract both gaining internal/runtime; hostcontract already imports it, registration does not). Also list the behaviour change for the OpenCode events whose declared mode stops being exit-2-blocks.

MINOR

B9 MINOR — two exit-code authorities. internal/errors maps CategoryConnection to exit 2 (errors.go:244) and hostexit.ExitBlock is also 2. For a gate event the collision happens to fail closed, but for a report-and-continue event a storage/connection error would block the host. State that `pasture hook lifecycle` bypasses the category->exit table completely and that Outcome is the single exit authority for that command; add it to the S0 checklist.

B10 MINOR — ResponseCapability{Deny, Ask, Annotate} is 3 bools = 8 states, several of which are meaningless (Ask without Deny). Give it a validity rule or make it a closed capability enum, so a table row cannot declare an impossible host.

B11 MINOR — cite the IP-1 comment when you retire it. hostcontract/codex_0_146_0.go:21-47 says the divergence is "inert" ONLY because the frontend binds 2 events and rejects the other 8. S5 enables 10/10, which ends that condition. That sentence makes T8's re-derivation MANDATORY before S5, not a tidy-up; the decoupling reason it names (the then-parallel M3 runtime-profile slice) has landed. Quote it in T8 so a later reader does not re-open the decision.

B12 MINOR — receipt.ConsultationRecord gains typed kind + reason. Say that its stored shape is versioned and name the golden/fixture files that change, so the durable schema change is reviewed, not implied.

Re-review: I will re-check B1, B2, B3 (design change), B4-B8 (text change) on the next round.

author: David Huu Pham
text: SUPERSEDED by PROPOSAL-2 aura-plugins-dhxn8s (2026-08-29). Round-1 verdicts: reviewer-a REVISE (A1-A12), reviewer-b REVISE (B1-B12), reviewer-c REVISE (C1-C13). Every finding is dispositioned in PROPOSAL-2 (delta tables T2'-T22, section 0b, 4.5 14-row table, 4.6 clearance, section 8 D1-D9).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW C (axis: deliverability, testability, traceability) — round 2 on PROPOSAL-2

VERDICT: REVISE — two open items only (C5 residual, C6), both text-sized. Eleven of the thirteen round-1 findings are resolved, and the new sections are a large improvement.

C1 RESOLVED. Section 4.5 is a 14-row table using the a6loa verbatim names, each row carrying a slice or a RE-DEFERRED reason, and D8 puts the re-deferred set in front of the user. The upstream state line in 0b (#55 closed, the rest open) makes the rows checkable.
C2 RESOLVED. Section 1 states 20 + 8 + 45 = 73 Wave-1 captures plus 12 recaptures and 3 controls in S2, total 85, and the per-harness end counts 8+20=28, 2+8=10, 2+45=47 now add up. T3' also removes the hook-free window.
C3 RESOLVED. Section 4.6 gives a six-step procedure, T20 makes Clearance mandatory and durable, the secret scan runs in the normal test flow, refused payload classes are named, and D7 asks the user. See C14 for the one timing gap.
C4 RESOLVED. Section 3.2 is a real ownership table, proofs are generated per harness with per-harness ordinal ranges, and the integration rule states rebase, regenerate, drift-green, and stage-only-owned-paths. See C15 for one residual cell.
C5 STILL OPEN (narrowed). The closed-set escape exists (WithheldNoReachableTrigger, user decision recorded), but two parts of the finding remain:
  (a) A17 asserts 28/30, 10/10, 47/47 flatly, while section 4.2 permits an event to be withheld for no reachable trigger. The two cannot both hold. Change requested: make A17 read "the R1 counts, less any event withheld under a user-approved no-reachable-trigger decision named in the harness report", so the acceptance criterion cannot be both met and missed.
  (b) The plan still does not state what the USER must supply. Change requested: add one line to section 9 giving, per harness, the number of instrumented live sessions and the user hours, plus the rule that each harness slice produces its trigger recipe list first and reports any unknown-trigger event to the user before its capture window closes. Worker-days alone cannot be scheduled when the work needs the user at a live host.
C6 STILL OPEN. T22 and D5 promise the two legality tables "shown in full at the gate", and section 4.4 declares only the map types plus an exhaustiveness test. The 3x10 and 13x10 cells ARE the gate behaviour: they decide what is blocked on the user's machine. As written no reviewer can judge the policy, no acceptance criterion pins any cell except A5, and the implementer would author 160 cells of new policy alone. Change requested: put the default rule plus the named exceptions in section 4.4 (for example "Verdict = Allow for every cell, Deny only for these listed role x action and phase x action pairs"), or the full tables. D5 stays as the user decision on that content.
C7 RESOLVED. The write path is now described honestly: two materialised tables updated in the same transaction as the assignment events, one claim write at session start, two reads on the gate path, receipt attribution unchanged. HookEnvironment is the injected seam with one serial real-wiring test, as AGENTS.md requires.
C8 RESOLVED. T10' plus A6: plain Proceed, native bytes byte-identical, reason durable only. No host-visible annotation exists in the epic.
C9 RESOLVED. Section 6 states mutation-RED per assertion, race in the normal flow, no Sleep or fixed-deadline polls, one test file per subject, and A18 refuses a Go-only proof for Codex and OpenCode. Extending codex_transport_e2e_test.go and opencode_target_test.go per event is the right reuse of what already exists.
C10 RESOLVED. Clearance is a committed CLEARANCE.md path, the validator refuses empty, wrong suffix and bare task-id shapes, and A12 covers it.
C11 RESOLVED. 4 destinations after S2, 12 after S5, 10 runners, stated the same way in 3, 4.3 and 6.
C12 RESOLVED. Section 6 plus A19 add the no-change assertion for ACP, Gemini and Antigravity, introduced in S1 and kept.
C13 RESOLVED. Section 9 reconciles the ELICIT figure and explains the per-event cost drop and the added substrate. The arithmetic checks out (Wave 0 28-35, total 43-54 critical path, 58-73 summed).

NEW FINDINGS

C14 IMPORTANT — clearance is granted after the captures can already be published.
Evidence: 4.6 step 5 makes the user's Impl-UAT ACCEPT the clearance, and records the GitHub PR URL in CLEARANCE.md. A PR URL means the raw fixtures were already pushed to a public remote before the user approved them.
Change requested: state the order explicitly — field inventory and secret scan must be green BEFORE any push, and the fixtures must not reach a public remote before the user approves the batch (private branch, draft, or approval-then-push). Name who performs the push. Add it to D7 so the user rules on it.

C15 MINOR — one Wave-1 cell is not exclusively owned. Section 3.2 assigns internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go to all three workers as "W(rows)". Row-level sharing of one Go file is not exclusive ownership. Change requested: split the profile rows per harness file, or state that this file is integrator-owned and that workers submit their evidence and capability cells as a patch applied at merge.

C16 MINOR — clarify that FailureEvidence gates faults only. T16 and 4.1 make an unevidenced blocking row fall back to ExitContinue. A reader can take that to mean a policy Deny on such an event also stops blocking, which would break R4. Add one sentence: FailureEvidence governs the FAULT exit only; a policy Deny always uses the harness deny channel from T18.

C17 MINOR — D8 says "the six RE-DEFERRED groups" and then lists seven (input mutation, #63, #57, #59, #60, #61-general, Strike/M4+). Correct the count so the user's decision covers a known set.

Path to ACCEPT: C5(a), C5(b) and C6 in the proposal text; C14 added to 4.6 and D7. C15-C17 are corrections.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW A (axis: host-contract truth and end-user behaviour) — round 2 on PROPOSAL-2

VERDICT: REVISE

Round-1 findings A1-A12 are almost all closed, and the deltas are good: T15 (fault != deny), T16 (evidence per row), T17 (stop-loop guard), T18 (recorded deny channels), T19 (capability enum), T20/§4.6 (clearance), T2'/T3' (frozen pins, main never hook-free). Three items stay open and two new host-contract defects appeared. Each has a small, stated fix.

STATUS OF ROUND-1 FINDINGS

A1 (failure modes derived, not captured) — RESOLVED. T16 + §4.1 FailureEvidence, generator refusal, unevidenced row runs as ExitContinue, D9 states the consequence. See A13 for one wrong item in the S0 evidence list.
A2 (fault is not a deny) — RESOLVED. T15, §4.1 ForFault, FailOpen default, PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED seam, §7 A2, D4 states the prompt-loss consequence plainly. See A14 for the durable fault record.
A3 (annotation breaks OpenCode, spams Claude) — RESOLVED. T10' makes an unbound session a byte-identical plain Proceed with a durable-only reason; §7 A6 asserts it.
A4 (Deny can trap a Stop) — RESOLVED. T17, Decide rule 2, §7 A7.
A5 (Codex deny channel) — RESOLVED. T18 uses the recorded contract; §7 A11 pins {} / {"continue":true} / {"continue":false,"stopReason":..}.
A6 (OpenCode deny reported as a broken install) — RESOLVED. T18 splits a typed deny object (exit 0, reason-only throw) from an invocation fault (non-zero exit, existing text); §7 A10; §10 lists the opencode_hooks.go change.
A7 (RequireHuman recovery) — RESOLVED. T11' states the arm is unreachable in this epic, keeps it a typed stub, and names the recovery path for when #80 closes.
A8 (capture privacy) — RESOLVED in substance. T7' + T20 + §4.6 (outside-repo dir, one notice, numbered files, field inventory, free-text-v1, secret scan, refused classes, mandatory Clearance path). See A16 for the provenance bookkeeping after substitution.
A9 (hook-free main) — RESOLVED. T3' keeps 8/2/2 through S2; D6 withdrawn.
A10 (moving pin, deleted controls) — RESOLVED. T2' freezes the three versions in the frontmatter and stops S2 if PATH moves; T3' re-derives the 3 Claude controls.
A11 (Claude native shapes unevidenced) — STILL OPEN: T18 marks the Claude DENY object as an assumption to capture in S4, but says nothing about the PROCEED shape. {"decision":"proceed"} is a Pasture-canonical object (nativeresponse.go:88-105) with no in-repo proof that Claude reads it; §7 A6 now locks those bytes in as "byte-identical to today". Missing: one S4 evidence row for the Claude proceed shape, or a stated finding in the S4 report that Claude ignores the object and proceed rests on exit 0 alone. Either is acceptable; silence is not.
A12 (post-hoc gates must not deny) — RESOLVED. T19 derivation rule, with ActionPostHoc in the action set.

NEW FINDINGS

A13 MINOR — the S0 evidence list names events that are not documented upstream. T16 says S0 ships evidence "for the Claude events whose exit-2 semantics are documented upstream (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PermissionRequest)". PostToolUse is declared non-blocking in the repo (metamodel.gen.go: report-and-continue), so it needs no evidence; PermissionRequest is not a documented Claude hook event and is not registered in hooks/hooks.json. Change: state that the S0 report prints the cited URL per row and that any row whose URL cannot be produced ships unevidenced (ExitContinue). Drop PostToolUse and PermissionRequest from the "documented" list, or cite them.

A14 IMPORTANT — the durable fault record can itself be the thing that failed. §4.1 and §7 A2 require "a durable fault record" on every fault, but the commonest fault is a storage fault, so the record write will fail too. Nothing states the second-order behaviour. Change: state that the fault record is best-effort; when it cannot be written the outcome degrades to the stderr diagnostic only, never to a block, a retry loop, or a wait. Add the case to the S0 ForFault table test (fault + record-write fails => same Outcome).

A15 IMPORTANT — no invocation deadline, and OpenCode waits forever. Evidence: hooks/hooks.json sets timeout 10 for every Claude hook; .codex/hooks.json sets 600; the generated OpenCode plugin awaits child.exited inside Promise.all with NO timeout (.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts:16-21). T21 adds up to one point read plus one bounded page plus up to 64 task-record reads per gate on SQLite; under lock contention this can exceed the Claude 10-second budget, and on OpenCode a stuck binary freezes the session with no error and no way out for the user. Change: (1) `hook lifecycle` carries its own deadline, set below the smallest host budget, and deadline expiry takes the FAULT path (fail-open by default); (2) the generated OpenCode plugin kills the child at that same deadline and reports a fault, not a deny; (3) add a BDD case and an S3 checklist line ("gate under a held write lock returns within the deadline on all three transports"). Measure it in the same S3 SQLiteBusy run the cost budget already uses.

A16 MINOR — clearance substitution must update the provenance it invalidates. §4.6 step 3 rewrites free-text values AFTER the binary wrote the provenance with rawFileDigest and redaction "home-path-v1". Unless the clearance step recomputes the digest and rewrites Redaction to the full applied rule list, ValidateFixture fails, or worse the provenance states a redaction rule that is not the one applied — a false claim about what was removed. Change: state that clearance recomputes the digest and sets Redaction to the applied rule list (for example "home-path-v1+free-text-v1"), and add the round trip to the S1 checklist.

A17 BLOCKER — a Deny may be emitted through a channel with no evidence that it blocks, so the record and reality can disagree. T16 governs FAULT mapping only ("hostexit.ForFailure maps an unevidenced row to ExitContinue"). T19 derives CapabilityDeny for every pre-action gate with no reference to evidence. For Claude the deny channel IS exit 2 (T18), the same mechanism T16 refuses to trust without evidence. So after S4, a claimed actor with no assignment can produce Deny + exit 2 on an event where exit 2 is not known to block: the consultation record durably says "denied", the host proceeds anyway, and §7 A4's guarantee is false for those events. Change: bind capability to evidence — an event whose deny channel has no FailureEvidence declares CapabilityNone; `Encode` already refuses a Deny on a CapabilityNone event (S3 checklist), so gatepolicy must map that refusal to a FAULT and record the decision as unenforced, never as an enforced Deny. State the rule in T19, add it to the S3 checklist, and add a BDD case: "Given a deny on an event whose deny channel has no evidence, Then the record marks the decision unenforced and the host is not told it was blocked."

WHAT IS RIGHT: §0b is an honest fact table with the round-1 corrections named; §3.2 gives real exclusive ownership; §4.6 is a usable clearance procedure with refused payload classes; §6 forces transport-level proofs (Bun and the generated runner), which is what makes A4 and A10 mean anything; D4, D5, D8 and D9 put the real user choices at the gate in plain terms.

RE-REVIEW ASKS: A17 (rule + checklist + BDD case), A15 (deadline on both sides + checklist line), A14 and A16 (one sentence each), A11 and A13 (one report line each). No other change requested; everything else on this axis is accepted.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW-B-2 (axis: architecture and data model) — reviewer-b

VERDICT: REVISE

Round-1 findings

B1 (import cycle) — RESOLVED. T9' + §4.4: gateauthority is a leaf holding the value types and the Reader; tasks imports it and implements it; gatepolicy imports gateauthority/backend/runtime. No cycle remains. (One accuracy nit in B16 below.)
B2 (no read model) — PARTLY RESOLVED, see B13. T21 + §4.4 now name two materialised tables, a cost budget, a truncation refusal and a backfill. The shape is right. The `active` column has no write trigger — B13.
B3 (S3 had nothing to prove against) — RESOLVED. T3' recaptures the 12 enabled events inside S2, enabled never drops below 8/2/2, main is never hook-free, and S3's deny proofs run on those events through the real transport.
B4 (TaskPhase) — RESOLVED. gateauthority.TaskPhase has an explicit Unset zero, PhaseFromProvenance converts, and `any Episode.Phase == Unset -> Refusal(RefusalPhaseUnknown)` refuses instead of guessing. See B15 for the conversion's own total-ness.
B5 (role/phase matrices) — RESOLVED. T22: two exported tables, exhaustiveness tests, unlisted cell refuses, the roleConstraints reuse claim is dropped, content goes to the user as D5. The per-episode role AND phase check with an OR across episodes is stated in §4.4, which is what I asked for.
B6 (session claim) — RESOLVED. SessionClaim.Known + ReasonUnknownActor; receipt attribution stays the system actor so the lifecycle_identity.go:19-45 invariant is untouched; the no-observed-start window is stated per harness and lands as unbound Proceed.
B7 (waist unresolved) — RESOLVED. T13' makes IdentityPolicyNone a table label with no waist effect and adds no UnresolvedReason arm.
B8 (three FailureMode enums) — RESOLVED. T8' names all three, deletes openCodeFailure and hostcontractgen's failure() writer, and lists the behaviour delta. Import direction is safe: internal/runtime imports only artifact, codegen/ir and effects, so registration -> runtime adds no cycle.
B9 (two exit authorities) — RESOLVED. §4.1: Outcome is the sole exit authority for `hook lifecycle`; the category table is bypassed; the S0 checklist proves both directions.
B10 (ResponseCapability 3 bools) — RESOLVED. T19 makes it a closed 4-arm enum with a stated derivation rule. See B14 for the consequence Decide does not yet handle.
B11 (IP-1 comment) — RESOLVED. T8' quotes the "inert only because the frontend binds 2 of 10" sentence and retires it in the S0 report.
B12 (ConsultationRecord shape) — RESOLVED. Consultation v2 is versioned and the changed goldens are listed in the S3 report.

New findings

B13 BLOCKER — the materialised gate read model has no write trigger for its most important column, and the backfill cannot produce it.
Evidence: §4.4 says `pasture_actor_assignment(actor, assignment, task, role, active)` is "upserted in the SAME transaction as AssignmentStarted / AssignmentEnded". There is no AssignmentEnded fact in this repo. Episode start facts are written as raw journal events at internal/tasks/epoch_candidate_commands.go:308 and :442 (`epochTaskEvent(..., FamilyAssignmentStarted.EventKind(), ...)`) plus the transfer paths — NOT through the `MapMaterialEvent` choke point (material_events.go:728), and `AssignmentStartedEvent` has no production caller. Episode ACTIVENESS is not an event at all: it is a journal predicate, `Journal().AuthorityGovernsTaskAt(authority, task, now)` (epoch_assignment_service.go:463,470; assignment_transfer.go:152,171; governed_create_slice.go:150). So governance can end with no pasture-side write to hook, and a cached `active` goes stale in BOTH directions — stale false gives Deny(ReasonNoActiveAssignment) to a legal actor, stale true gives Proceed to an actor whose authority ended. The backfill has the same hole: folding existing events through ProjectAssignments finds only Started transitions (there are no Ended ones), so every historical episode backfills as active=true.
Change: pick one and write it into §4.4 —
 (a) make the table an ACTOR->ASSIGNMENT INDEX with no `active` column (actor, assignment, task, role), and evaluate activeness at read time with AuthorityGovernsTaskAt per candidate, bounded by MaxEpisodes; or
 (b) keep `active` only if you name the exact governance-change write points that maintain it, route every one through a single choke point, and add a replay-consistency test that rebuilds the table from journal truth and fails on any difference, plus a rebuild/repair command.
Either way: name the real write sites (epoch_candidate_commands.go:308,442; assignment_transfer.go; governed_create_slice.go), state how ProjectAssignments' AssignmentEnded transitions are produced (or stop citing that fold as the backfill), and re-state the T21 cost budget for whichever shape you choose.

B14 IMPORTANT — Decide can return Deny for an event that has no deny channel, and the operator sees a fault instead of a policy answer.
Evidence: T19 gives post-hoc gates CapabilityNone; §4.4's Decide rule list has no capability rule and `gatepolicy.Input` carries no capability field; nativeresponse.Encode is "capability-checked" and returns an error, which T15 routes to the fault path — under the FailOpen default that is exit 0 plus a diagnostic that reads like a bug, for what was in fact a legal policy decision.
Change: add `Capability runtime.ResponseCapability` to Input and a rule ahead of the table rules: capability == CapabilityNone -> Proceed with a durable reason (for example ReasonNoDenyChannel). Keep Encode's refusal as a programming-error guard only, and add the pair to the S3 Decide table.

B15 IMPORTANT — the three reads are not one snapshot, and the mirror enums have no sync guard.
Evidence: §4.4's handler flow does a claim point read, a bounded episode page, and N task-record phase reads (N up to MaxEpisodes = 64) with nothing tying them to one instant, so an assignment that ends between read 2 and read 3, or a phase that moves during the N reads, yields a torn view that can Deny a legal actor. Separately, gateauthority.AssignmentRole "mirrors tasks.AssignmentRole" (material_events.go:141-151) and TaskPhase mirrors provenance.Phase (ptypes/enums.go:420-437) with no stated behaviour for PhaseFromProvenance on an out-of-range value and no test that fails when an upstream arm is added.
Change: state that the whole authority read runs in ONE read transaction or at ONE journal watermark, and that a watermark move mid-read is a Refusal, not a Deny; make PhaseFromProvenance total with unknown -> TaskPhaseUnset (which already refuses); add a mirror-exhaustiveness test for both enums that goes RED when tasks.AssignmentRole or provenance.Phase gains an arm. Consider materialising phase alongside the episode row if the S3 measurement shows the 64 point reads dominate the per-gate budget.

B16 MINOR — two small accuracy fixes in §4.4. (1) gateauthority is described as importing "provenance ids + runtime only", but Reader.ResolveSession takes ir.HarnessID, so internal/codegen/ir is in the leaf set too; say so, or the leaf claim will be read as a rule and broken later. (2) `Result{Decision, Refusal}` states "exactly one set" as prose; give it constructors and IsValid so the invariant is typed like every other value in this plan.

B17 MINOR — §4.4 names the episode-ending family as "AssignmentEnded"; the closed family set is FamilyAssignmentCompleted (material_events.go:52-57), and its own comment says it does NOT mutate task status. Whatever B13 resolves to, use the real family names and state which families, if any, end an episode for gate purposes.

Re-review: B13 is the only blocker. I will re-check B13, B14 and B15 next round; B16/B17 are text.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW A (axis: host-contract truth and end-user behaviour) — round 3 on PROPOSAL-3

VERDICT: ACCEPT

No BLOCKER remains on this axis. All six round-2 items are closed with the correct host facts, and §0c records the two facts I could not find in round 2 (Claude's documented no-op continuation; the 1 s Ingress tier bounds only the receipt append). Two IMPORTANT items below are carry-forward asks for the IMPL_PLAN, not blockers.

ROUND-2 FINDINGS

A11 (Claude proceed shape unevidenced) — RESOLVED. §0c states the fact plainly: Claude's documented no-op continuation is exit 0 with empty stdout, and {"decision":"proceed"} is Pasture's own object with no Claude evidence. T27 + D10 + §7c A24 change the Claude encoder to emit no bytes, keep the object as the OpenCode contract (which the generated plugin's acceptProceed requires) and as the durable canonical form, and list the changing goldens in the S3 report. This is the right direction: it stops asserting a shape the host was never shown to read.
  One wording clean-up for the IMPL_PLAN, not a finding: PROPOSAL-2 §7 A6 says an unbound session gives bytes "byte-identical to today". After T27 that is no longer true for Claude. Restate A6 as "identical to that harness's proceed bytes as defined by T27".

A13 (S0 evidence list overstated) — RESOLVED. §6c drops PostToolUse (non-blocking) and makes PermissionRequest conditional on the 2.1.251 catalogue registering it, leaving PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SubagentStop as the documented set.

A14 (durable fault record can be the failing component) — RESOLVED. T28 makes it best-effort and leaves the Outcome unchanged when it cannot be written.

A15 (no invocation deadline; OpenCode waits forever) — RESOLVED in substance. T24 adds the HookInvocation tier at 5 s, ordered correctly against the four existing tiers and below the Claude 10 s budget with process-start headroom; expiry takes the fault path; the docs guard pins the row; §7c A21 and the S0 checklist prove it with a held write lock and a condition wait (no Sleep). The OpenCode kill timer is the right backstop — see A18 for its scheduling.

A16 (substitution invalidates provenance) — RESOLVED. T29 recomputes the digest over the committed bytes and lists every rule applied in order, and the existing digest check turns a stale provenance into a hard error.

A17 (deny through an unevidenced channel) — RESOLVED, and resolved better than I asked. T23 derives capability from evidence in the generator, refuses a hand-set capability, and rule 9 turns an unenforceable Deny into Proceed(ReasonUnenforcedDeny) recorded durably, with no Encode error and no fault. §7c A20 proves it. The record and the host now agree.

NEW FINDINGS (IMPORTANT; neither blocks ratification)

A18 IMPORTANT — the OpenCode kill timer lands three slices after the OpenCode gate goes live. §6c schedules the 8 s kill timer test in S6, but S3 already enables a real deny decision on tool.execute.before through the generated plugin and already edits internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go for the typed deny object and the reason-only throw (PROPOSAL-2 §10). Between S3 and S6 an OpenCode user whose binary stalls (held write lock, a hung read) has no timeout at all: the plugin awaits child.exited inside Promise.all with no timer (.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts:16-21), so the session freezes with no error and no way out. Change: move the kill timer and its Bun test into S3, in the same edit that adds the deny object; keep S6 for the per-callback generator work. State it in §6c.

A19 IMPORTANT — publish per-event enforcement, so "47/47" cannot be read as "47 gates enforce". T23 is honest, and its direct consequence is that many enabled events will carry CapabilityNone: on Claude only the four documented rows (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop) can deny, so after S4 a user could read "28/30 enabled" while about four events actually enforce a decision. Nothing in the plan shows the difference to the reader. Change: (1) the per-harness activation report carries the derived ResponseCapability and the FailureEvidence source per event; (2) each harness Impl-UAT states two counts, "enabled" and "enforcing", with the unenforced list; (3) add one BDD line: given a harness activation report, when read, then every enabled event shows its capability and its evidence source. This is small table work on artefacts the plan already generates, and it is what makes R4 legible to the person who has to trust the gate.

WHAT IS RIGHT: T25/T26 replace the cached active flag with a read-time governance predicate under one snapshot and a torn-snapshot refusal on the fault path — that removes a whole class of "the record says denied but the journal says otherwise" errors. T30 makes the clearance private-first, so no raw capture reaches a public remote before the user's ACCEPT, with the ACCEPT quoted verbatim. §4.4c publishes the two legality tables as default-ALLOW plus named exceptions, which a user can actually read and approve at D5. D11 states the user's own time cost (2-4 hours per harness) instead of hiding it.

For the Plan-UAT gate, the decisions that carry real user consequence on this axis are D4 (fault fails open by default, with the prompt-loss consequence of the alternative stated), D10 (Claude proceed becomes empty stdout) and D5 (the two tables). All three are stated in terms a user can decide on.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW-B-3 (axis: architecture and data model) — reviewer-b

VERDICT: REVISE — no BLOCKER remains. Three IMPORTANT gaps, all inside the S3 gate read model, all fixable by a text delta; the architecture itself is now sound.

Round-2 findings

B13 (materialised `active` had no write trigger) — RESOLVED. T25 removes the cached flag: the table indexes started episodes only, `recordAssignmentStart` is the single choke point for the two raw writers (epoch_candidate_commands.go:308,442) and the transfer paths, governance is evaluated at read time with AuthorityGovernsTaskAt(authority_jid, task, snapshotJID), the backfill infers no activeness, and a journal-replay consistency test plus `gate rebuild-index` back it. A22 pins the exact failure I raised. See B18 for the one residue.
B14 (Deny with no deny channel became a fault) — RESOLVED. T23 binds capability to evidence, Input carries Capability, and rule 9 turns a Deny on a CapabilityNone event into Proceed with ReasonUnenforcedDeny instead of an Encode error. A20 proves it. Rules 4, 6 and 8 all produce a "verdict Deny" that passes through 9, so the downgrade is uniform.
B15 (torn read, mirror enums) — RESOLVED in principle. T26 gives one snapshotJID, one read transaction, RefusalSnapshotTorn on the fault path, mirror-enum sync tests, and `PhaseFromProvenance` returning (TaskPhase, bool) with out-of-range refusing. See B19 for the mechanism.
B16 (leaf import set, untyped Result) — RESOLVED. §4.4c names provenance ids + codegen/ir + runtime, and Result is constructor-owned with Decided/Refused plus accessors.
B17 (non-existent family name) — RESOLVED. 0c records the real families (FamilyAssignmentStarted, FamilyAssignmentCompleted) and T25 indexes only started facts.

New findings

B18 IMPORTANT — the index is still a cache, and its ONLY failure direction is a wrong Deny.
Evidence: the assignment authority is not knowable before the operation commits — today it is recovered by a backwards scan over journal ids (epoch_assignment_service.go:514-540, `scan(high, low)` calling AuthorityGovernsTaskAt per candidate) precisely because the authority row sits between the operation anchor and the material event. So `recordAssignmentStart` can only write `authority_jid` AFTER the journal Apply returns, not in the same transaction. A crash, a cancelled context, or any future writer that misses the choke point leaves an assignment started in the journal with no index row; rule 6 then reads len(Episodes)==0 and DENIES a legal actor. The consistency test and the rebuild command catch the systematic case, not the window.
Change: give the index a watermark (highest journal id it has consumed) and make the read self-checking — at gate time, if the journal head carries FamilyAssignmentStarted facts beyond the watermark, either catch up (the query is already EventKind-filtered and bounded, epoch_assignment_service.go:428) or return a typed RefusalIndexStale on the FAULT path. State the rule in one line: an incomplete index must never produce a Deny. Add the case to the S3 Decide table and to A22's neighbourhood.

B19 IMPORTANT — the snapshot-torn check names a field that does not exist.
Evidence: T26 says "if any task record's last JournalID > snapshotJID". `provenance.Task` (pkg/ptypes/types.go:160-174) has no JournalID; it carries only UpdatedAt. A worker implementing T26 literally would have to invent a field on a third-party type, and A23 cannot be written as specified.
Change: name the real mechanism. The journal query already supports it — JournalQueryV1 carries TaskIDs, AfterJournalID and SnapshotMaxJournalID (used at epoch_assignment_service.go:485), so the torn test is "any task event for the episode's tasks with JournalID > snapshotJID", or read the phases through a query bounded at snapshotJID in the first place. If you prefer a column, say that the pasture projection gains a per-task last-journal-id and who maintains it. Also fix the 0c citation: AuthorityGovernsTaskAt is journal_api.go:292 (dbos_store.go:424 is the borrowed wrapper), so a reader looking at :403 finds unrelated code.

B20 IMPORTANT — T23 silently disarms the S3 deny proofs for Codex and OpenCode.
Evidence: T23 makes CapabilityDeny conditional on the row carrying FailureEvidence for its blocking channel, and rule 9 downgrades any Deny on a CapabilityNone row to Proceed(ReasonUnenforcedDeny). T16 has S0 ship evidence for the CLAUDE rows only, and 6c schedules the per-harness evidence rows in S4/S5/S6. S3, however, must prove a real deny through the real transport on Claude PreToolUse, Codex PreToolUse AND OpenCode tool.execute.before (§3 of PROPOSAL-2, A4). With no evidence row at S3, the two non-Claude proofs become proceed-with-ReasonUnenforcedDeny and A4 cannot pass.
Change: state that S3 fills the FailureEvidence and capability rows for exactly those three events, and cite what satisfies T16 for each — the in-repo recorded contracts you already found (0b: nativeresponse.go:24-47 for the Codex continue/stopReason channel; the OpenCode acceptProceed/throw contract) — or move the two proofs to S5/S6 and say so. Note also for the user that until a harness slice supplies evidence, D9 plus T23 means gates on that harness neither block on fault nor enforce a policy Deny; D9's wording currently covers only the fault half.

Re-review: B18, B19 and B20 are text deltas; no interface in §4.4c has to change. I will re-check exactly those three next round.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW C (axis: deliverability, testability, traceability) — round 3 on PROPOSAL-3 (delta over PROPOSAL-2)

VERDICT: REVISE — one substantive finding (C18) and one artefact-hygiene finding (C19). All six of my round-2 items are resolved.

C5 RESOLVED. A17' now reads "the counts OR every shortfall carries WithheldNoReachableTrigger / WithheldUnclearablePayload with the user's decision in CLEARANCE.md", so the criterion and the escape no longer contradict. Section 6c makes every Wave-1 worker publish the per-event trigger recipe list BEFORE capturing and raise unknown-trigger events to the user before the UAT. D11 states the user-side cost (about 2-4 hours of live sessions per harness, worker-driven, Codex live per the lifted rider). That is enough to schedule the campaign.
C6 RESOLVED. Section 4.4c publishes both tables as "default ALLOW plus named exceptions" with a rationale per row, the exhaustiveness test regenerates the grid from the rule and fails on a missing cell, and D5 puts exactly that content to the user. The rule order is numbered 1-10 and each arm names its path (durable only, FAULT, or host-visible).
C14 RESOLVED. T30 plus 4.6c invert the sequence: capture, substitute, scan green, CLEARANCE.md written locally, Impl-UAT against the LOCAL worktree, and only then push and PR. A25 asserts that no fixture exists on any remote before ACCEPT. That closes the publication-before-approval hole.

C18 IMPORTANT (blocks ACCEPT) — as planned, role and phase legality can never reach a host, and the user asked for it by name.

The user's Round-1 answer named "Phase and role legality" as gate state beside assignment authority, so half of R4's chosen state would ship inert without the user knowing.
