author: David Huu Pham
text:
IMPL_PLAN REVIEW — reviewer-b (axis: architecture and data model)

VERDICT: REVISE — one BLOCKER, four IMPORTANT, three MINOR. The decomposition is good: S3's leaf graph (L1 -> {L2, L4}; L2 -> L3 -> {L6, L7}; L7 -> L8; L4 -> L5; {L5, L6, L8} -> L10; L9 -> L11) matches the data dependencies, the leaf packages and import edges are stated with a test that enforces them (S3-L2), and the four corrections in section 9 are all real: I confirm four assignment-start writers, the dbos_store.go:424 implementation line, and that internal/lifecycle/receipt has no testdata (only the inline pair at golden_v1_test.go:17 and :22).

Rulings requested in section 9 — both splits are CORRECT.
- Mirror-enum helper in S1-L9 (qg4fp7) and application in S3-L2 (78cal7): right. The helper is enum-agnostic; only the mirrors it guards are S3 types.
- FailureEvidence in S0-L2 (0s656x) and ResponseCapability in S3-L7 (llt3k5): right, and for a stronger reason than stated — T23 makes capability a FUNCTION of evidence, so evidence must exist first, and the pre-action versus post-hoc classification only becomes meaningful when Decide exists.

PB1 BLOCKER — `authority_jid` has no stated source, in either the choke point or the backfill (leaves 1sg9v6 S3-L4, wivrye S3-L1, lwmdw3 S3-L5).
Evidence: S3-L4 defines `pasture_actor_assignment(actor, assignment, task, role, authority_jid)` and S3-L5 step 5 consumes it in `AuthorityGovernsTaskAt(authority_jid, task, snapshotJID)`. No leaf says where the value comes from. In the tree today the authority journal id for an assignment-start event is NOT carried in the event: it is RECOVERED by a backwards linear scan over journal ids, `scan(high, low)` calling the predicate per candidate, at internal/tasks/epoch_assignment_service.go:514-540, precisely because the authority row sits between the operation anchor and the material event. Two consequences the plan does not face: (1) at the choke point the value can only come from the Apply result (`CommittedResult` emitted events or result slots) AFTER the journal commit, which is also why S3-L4's "same transaction as the journal Apply where the code allows it" is probably never; (2) the backfill in S3-L4 indexes ALL historical FamilyAssignmentStarted facts, and with no recorded authority it degenerates into that backwards scan PER FACT — an O(journal) per row migration run from `ensurePastureTablesOnce` (tracker.go:159), i.e. on an ordinary user command.
Change: add the source to S3-L4 explicitly — name the field of `provenance.CommittedResult` that yields the authority journal id at the choke point, and name the backfill mechanism (reuse of `assignmentAuthorityForEvent`, with a stated bound, or a different recorded fact). Add it to the S3-L1 spike as probe 6: "the assignment authority JournalID is obtainable from the Apply result at write time, and obtainable for a historical started fact within a stated bound". If neither is reachable at v0.0.7, that is exactly the STOP condition the spike exists for.

PB2 IMPORTANT — the spike (wivrye S3-L1) proves five READS but the gate path also WRITES.
Evidence: Amendment B18 puts the watermark catch-up inside `Snapshot` (S3-L5 step 2), which writes `pasture_actor_assignment` rows and advances `last_indexed_jid` on the hook path. Probe 5 asks only whether one READ transaction can hold the reads. Pasture tables share the store handle with the provenance journal, whose writer ownership is what the SQLiteBusy tier exists for.
Change: add a probe that a pasture-owned table can be written from the gate path without disturbing provenance write ownership, and that failure to acquire it inside the SQLiteBusy tier surfaces as the timeout that becomes `RefusalIndexStale`. Also record in S3-L5 that the decision may be taken on the merged in-memory view with persistence best-effort, that two concurrent catch-ups are a covered case (the upsert is idempotent), and that a failed persist degrades to `RefusalIndexStale` or the in-memory answer, NEVER to a Deny.

PB3 IMPORTANT — nothing owns the session-claim WRITE.
Evidence: S3-L5 (lwmdw3) says `pasture_session_claim` "is written ONCE per session by the session-start receipt path when `HookEnvironment.ActorClaim` is non-empty", and tests "a second claim for the same session refuses" — but S3-L5's owned files are gate_reader.go, its test and the DDL row (the READ side). S3-L10 (4vsuum) owns internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go for the gate wiring and never mentions the claim. S0-L4 (x9waaw) only reads the environment variable. Acceptance criterion A4 cannot be proven without the write.
Change: name the owning leaf and file for the claim write (the session-start receipt path in internal/handlers or internal/tasks), state that it must not disturb the read-only system-actor invariant at internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:19-45, and add the once-per-session refusal test to that leaf rather than to the reader.

PB4 IMPORTANT — the per-gate cost budget omits the governance predicate calls (jojxa5 S3-L11, lwmdw3 S3-L5).
Evidence: S3-L11 states the budget as "one claim point read, one bounded index page capped at 64 episodes, and N task-record reads with N capped at 64". S3-L5 step 5 additionally calls `AuthorityGovernsTaskAt` once PER INDEXED ROW — up to 64 journal predicate evaluations per gate, on every tool call — plus step 7's torn probe. The committed cost test would pass a budget that does not describe the work.
Change: restate the budget as claim read + index page + N governance predicates + N phase reads + one torn probe, all with N capped at MaxEpisodes, and have the S3-L11 cost test count all five classes. If the measurement is poor, the fallback (materialise phase, or narrow the index read by task) belongs in the report, not in a later slice.

PB5 IMPORTANT — rule 6's watermark condition cannot live in `Decide` (xmwel2 S3-L6 versus lwmdw3 S3-L5).
Evidence: S3-L6 says "Rule 6 applies ONLY when the watermark equals the journal maximum after catch-up", but its `Input` is {Event, Action, Semantic, StopLoop, Capability, Claim, Authority} — it carries no index-completeness fact, so a pure function cannot honour that condition. The guarantee actually lives in the Reader, which refuses with `RefusalIndexStale` before returning.
Change: pick one home and say so in both leaves. Either delete the condition from S3-L6 and state that `Snapshot` guarantees a complete index or refuses, or add an explicit typed field (for example `Authority.IndexComplete`) and a rule that refuses when it is false. Add the chosen case to the S3-L6 decision table.

PB6 IMPORTANT — the whole epic is serialised behind a spike that can stop it.
Evidence: integration point I11 says Wave 1 starts only after S3 merges, and section 10 says S3-L1 can STOP S3. S6 is the long pole (14-18 days) and the capture campaigns cost the USER 2-4 hours of live sessions per harness (D11). Nothing in S4/S5/S6 capture, clearance or target-row work depends on I11; only the per-event byte assertions do.
Change: state in section 1 that the Wave-1 CAPTURE campaigns may start once S2 merges, in their own worktrees, and that only the proof leaves wait for S3. Also state the fallback if the spike fails: a provenance release and re-pin is a user decision with precedent (v0.0.7 in the DBOS epic), and name what pauses meanwhile.

PB7 MINOR — missing dependency edge: S3-L5 (lwmdw3) implements `gateauthority.Reader` and `Snapshot` but is blocked only by S3-L4. It needs the S3-L2 (78cal7) types. Add `bd dep add aura-plugins-lwmdw3 --blocked-by aura-plugins-78cal7`.

PB8 MINOR — two leaves own the same file region: S3-L4 owns "internal/tasks/open_unified.go (the DDL list only)" and S3-L5 owns "the pasture_session_claim DDL row in open_unified.go". One worker runs the slice, so this is not a race, but the ownership table should name one owner for the DDL list (S3-L4) and have S3-L5 add its row through it. Same class: S3-L7 edits internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_{claude,codex,opencode}.go, which S1-L7 (vywkkd) creates — correct across sequential slices, worth one sentence so a worker does not create them twice.

Nothing else on my axis. The S3 leaf set covers every finding I raised in rounds 1-4 (B1 by S3-L2, B4/B5 by S3-L2 and S3-L3, B13/B18 by S3-L4 and S3-L5, B14/B20 by S3-L7, B15/B19 by S3-L5, B12 by S3-L8), and the corrections in section 9 show the exploration checked the code rather than the prose.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PLAN REVIEW C (axis: deliverability, testability, traceability) — IMPL_PLAN, leaf level

VERDICT: REVISE — two BLOCKERs (PC1, PC2), four IMPORTANT, five MINOR. The plan is strong: every leaf I read carries file ownership, a named test subject, mutation-RED expectation and archive-copy gates, and the measured-baseline sections are honest (four raw writers not two; dbos_store.go:424 not :403; no receipt golden files; OpenCode 43 rows not 47). The findings below are gaps, not a rewrite.

PC1 BLOCKER — acceptance criterion A16 is discharged by NO slice and tested by NO leaf.
Evidence: section 2 maps A1-A15, A17'-A27 and A-B18, but A16 appears nowhere in the IMPL_PLAN, in any of the eight slices, or in any of the 54 leaves. A16 is "Given any enabled event, When its L2 is inspected, Then only kind, semantic, identities, ordering and declared signals. Should Not carry tool arguments, tool output or prompt text." That is requirement R6 and the user's central ruling: payload lowering was WITHDRAWN after four rounds of questions. It is also a MUST-FAIL case on the elicitation record.
Why it matters here: 73 new events land in Wave 1, each with a new fixture and new declared fields. Without a structural test, one target row that declares a free-text field would lower prompt or tool content into the IR and every gate stays green. This is the ship-broken-but-green case for the requirement the user cared most about.
Change requested: give A16 a permanent home in S1 next to the no-change guard — a test that walks EVERY enabled event's L2 and fails if any value outside {kind, semantic, identities, ordering, declared structured signals} appears — and list A16 in the section 2 row for S1, S4, S5 and S6 so each harness re-asserts it over its own new events.

PC2 BLOCKER — S1 cannot pass its own gates as written (leaf S1-L1).
Evidence: S1-L1 makes `Clearance` REQUIRED for `Origin == OriginAuthenticCapture` and adds the refusals, while 18 fixture pairs on main (Claude 14, Codex 2, OpenCode 2) have no Clearance field. The leaf says it "states in its report exactly which existing fixtures now fail, so S2 knows its full workload". The S1 gate is `go test -race -count=1 ./...` green on an archive copy, and S1 merges before S2. A tree with 18 hard corpus errors cannot merge, and the standing constraint forbids disabling a test to get through.
Change requested: pick one and write it into S1-L1 — (a) S1-L1 backfills the 18 provenance files with a `Clearance` path to the CLEARANCE.md template it already creates, recording the existing clearance history for those fixtures; or (b) the requirement is scoped to fixtures whose harnessVersion equals a frozen pin, and S2-L3 flips it to unconditional once the old fixtures are deleted; or (c) S1 and S2 merge as one slice. Option (a) or (b) keeps the slice boundary.

PC3 IMPORTANT — S2 recaptures 12 live events with none of the Wave-1 capture safeguards (leaf S2-L3).
Evidence: S2-L3 requires LIVE recaptures of Claude 8 (including PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, PreCompact, PostCompact), Codex 2 and OpenCode 2, plus 3 re-derived controls. The trigger-recipe-first rule, the `WithheldNoReachableTrigger` escape and the D11 user-time expectation are attached only to S4/S5/S6 (section 6c "Wave 1, every harness"). S2 has no trigger-recipe leaf, no escape and no stated user time, yet its exit criteria are absolute: 8/2/2 enabled and "main is never hook-free".
Change requested: add an S2 trigger-recipe leaf ahead of S2-L3 that covers the 12 recaptures and the 3 controls; state the user time S2 needs; and give S2-L3 the same escape, with the consequence for the 8/2/2 exit criterion written down (an event that cannot be re-triggered is raised to the user BEFORE the old fixture is deleted, so coverage never silently drops).

PC4 IMPORTANT — the user-time figure does not scale with the work (leaves S4-L1, S5-L1, S6-L1).
Evidence: all three trigger-recipe leaves repeat the same sentence, "about 2-4 hours of live sessions for this harness". S4 captures 20 events, S5 captures 8 and S6 captures 45. At 2-4 hours for 45 events, S6 allows under five minutes per event including session setup, trigger and verification, while the same slice is sized at 14-18 worker-days.
Change requested: state a per-harness user-time figure, and have each trigger-recipe leaf publish its own estimate from the recipe list BEFORE capture starts, so the user can accept or reschedule. D11 gave one number for a campaign that was not yet decomposed; the leaf is the right place to correct it.

PC5 IMPORTANT — the Wave-1 integrator duty has no owner, no leaf and no gate.
Evidence: section 4 assigns the shared generated files (registration/*.gen.go, event_kinds.gen.go, metamodel.gen.go, inventory/lifecycle_events.gen.go, ingress/*/payload_*.gen.go) and internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go to "the integrator", and the integration rule says the integrator performs one authoritative regeneration per merge. No slice, no leaf and no acceptance criterion covers that work; S7 starts only after all three merges and does not include it.
Change requested: name the integrator and give the duty a leaf or an explicit supervisor checklist item with its own gate — after EACH Wave-1 merge, on an archive copy: one authoritative `make generate`, drift clean, the three-harness parity test green, and the ownership table re-checked against the diff. Without it, the second and third merges have no defined party and no proof.

PC6 IMPORTANT — six leaves instruct the worker to do what the standing constraints forbid.
Evidence: section 6 says "Workers implement, validate, commit locally and report. Workers NEVER push, never open a pull request, and never close a Beads task." Leaves S4-L3 step 8, S4-L7, S5-L3, S5-L6, S6-L3 and S6-L7 all say "After ACCEPT: push, open the pull request, and append its URL to CLEARANCE.md in the landing commit."
Change requested: name the actor in all six leaves (the supervisor or the architect pushes and opens the pull request after the ACCEPT; the worker only writes the verbatim ACCEPT into CLEARANCE.md and reports). This also strengthens A25: if the worker has no push path, the private-first rule does not rest on worker discipline alone.

PC7 MINOR — wrong paths and a wrong command name. S4-L3 owns "internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude-code/testdata/**", but the tree path is internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/testdata/** (section 4 uses the correct one). S4-L2 verifies `claude-code --version`; the binary on PATH is `claude`, as S2-L1 correctly writes.

PC8 MINOR — S2-L1 says "Files owned: None" and then requires a committed assertion in internal/runtime/version_test.go. Name that file as owned so the ownership table stays complete.

PC9 MINOR — two intra-slice file shares are declared only in prose: S0-L5 and S0-L6 both edit cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go, and S4-L5 and S4-L6 both edit cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_claude_test.go. Both are ordered by a real dependency edge, so they are safe, but the ownership statement should say "shared inside the slice, ordered by dependency" so a later reviewer does not read it as a violation of the exclusive-ownership rule.

PC10 MINOR — leaf S6-L4 has no dependency edge at all; its precondition ("rebase onto main and confirm the S3 kill timer is intact") is prose only. Add the edge to whatever must land first, or state that its only precondition is the merged S3 baseline that the whole slice already carries.

PC11 MINOR — authenticity evidence does not reach the user. S4-L2, S5-L2 and S6-L2 record "the event, the trigger used, the capture time and the raw digest" per capture, but the report leaves (S4-L7, S5-L6, S6-L7) do not list that log in their contents. The user's ACCEPT is the clearance AND the authenticity judgement, so the per-capture record should be in front of them.
Change requested: add the per-capture log (event, trigger, time, digest) to the report contents of the three report leaves.

Path to ACCEPT: PC1 and PC2 must be fixed in the plan and in the named leaves; PC3-PC6 need the stated leaf edits; PC7-PC11 are corrections.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEW A (axis: host-contract truth and end-user behaviour) — IMPL_PLAN

VERDICT: REVISE

I read the plan, all 8 slices and all 54 leaves, and I re-measured the disputed facts at main 73f38d0. The leaf-level discipline is good: every host-visible behaviour I traced carries an owner, a real-transport proof and a mutation-RED expectation. One measured fact in section 9 is wrong and would send a worker after work that is already done, so this is a REVISE with a small, cheap correction list.

FINDINGS

PA1 BLOCKER — the "OpenCode 43 rows" correction is false; the file already holds 47.
Leaves: S2-L2 (aura-plugins-2fyuvb), S2-L5 report item 5 (aura-plugins-e5oh4w), IMPL_PLAN section 9 item 4, slice S2 (aura-plugins-kthzht) baseline line.
Measured now at 73f38d0: .opencode/pasture-opencode.json "activation" holds 47 rows (2 enabled: session.created and tool.execute.before; 45 withheld). internal/inventory/lifecycle_events.gen.go holds 47 OpenCode rows. metamodel.gen.go holds 47 OpenCode events (Claude 30, Codex 10). There is nothing to reconcile from 43 to 47.
What IS true in that correction, and must stay: OpenCode has no separate activation REPORT file; its activation array is folded into the target manifest, which is why S1-L8 (aura-plugins-rlwt8r) creates .opencode/pasture-opencode-activation.json.
Change: delete the "43 rows" claim from section 9 item 4, from S2-L2 and from the S2 report list, and restate the S2 OpenCode work as "confirm the 47 registered rows survive the pin bump to 1.18.19 and report the upstream event diff". Keep the S1-L8 report-file work unchanged. A worker acting on "43 rows" would either hunt four rows that exist or add duplicates.

PA2 IMPORTANT — an unproven Claude response object ships in S3 and no leaf ever proves it.
Leaves: S3-L8 (aura-plugins-ib8pu4) states that a Claude deny on PreToolUse and PermissionRequest also emits the hookSpecificOutput deny object and calls it "an ASSUMPTION captured in S4". No S4 leaf captures it: S4-L1/L2 capture event PAYLOADS, and S4-L4 seeks exit-code evidence for the event rows. Capturing what the host SENDS proves nothing about what the host ACCEPTS on stdout. So the object would be emitted to a real host from S3 onward and never verified.
Change: in S3, emit only the evidenced channel (exit 2 with the reason on stderr) for a Claude deny; add the hookSpecificOutput object in S4 as a named work item with its own capture or documentation evidence, recorded in the same FailureEvidence row style. If the architect prefers to keep it in S3, then S4-L4 must carry an explicit item "verify the deny response object against a live 2.1.251 host" with a stated fallback.

PA3 IMPORTANT — one published deny cell cannot be reached on any harness, and the user approves that table at D5.
Leaves: S3-L3 (aura-plugins-fj2d0l) publishes AxisReviewer DENY Subagent, and PlanUAT / Ratify / ImplUAT / Landing DENY Subagent. S3-L6 (aura-plugins-xmwel2) puts rule 1 (observation) and rule 2 (stop-loop guard) BEFORE the tables at rule 8.
Measured: on Claude and on Codex, SubagentStart is an observation and SubagentStop is a gate with stop-loop consult-when-inactive (metamodel.gen.go); OpenCode registers no subagent event at all. So every subagent event exits at rule 1 or rule 2, and the Subagent deny cells can never produce a Deny, and cannot even record ReasonUnenforcedDeny. By contrast Worktree, TaskLifecycle and ConfigChange ARE reachable on Claude (WorktreeCreate, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, ConfigChange are gates), which is exactly what C18 sends to S4.
Change: add a REACHABILITY column to the two published tables and to the D5 text: per denied cell, the events that can reach it, per harness, or "unreachable". S3-L3's exhaustiveness test gains one case that fails when a cell is denied but no registered event maps to its action class on any harness. S4-L6 (aura-plugins-w39t7r) should pick its two demonstration cells from the REACHABLE set. A user must not approve a rule that nothing can apply.

PA4 IMPORTANT — the stated unbound-session window for Codex and OpenCode is wrong.
Leaves: S3-L5 (aura-plugins-lwmdw3) says "Codex and OpenCode before S5 and S6 enable their start events", and S3-L11 (aura-plugins-jojxa5) repeats it as report item 5.
Measured: the enabled set after S2 is 8/2/2, and those sets already contain the start events. .codex/hooks.json registers SessionStart (and PreToolUse); the generated OpenCode plugin registers the catch-all event handler guarded to session.created (and tool.execute.before). Codex fixtures on disk are session_start_0_146_0 and pre_tool_use_0_146_0; OpenCode fixtures are session_created and tool_execute_before.
Change: correct both leaves. If a real window remains it is a different one (for example a session that STARTED before the claim table existed, or a session started while the hook was not installed) — state that window instead, because it is the one a user will actually meet after upgrading mid-session.

PA5 IMPORTANT — do not let the consultation v2 work touch the read-only v1 compatibility pin.
Leaf: S3-L8 (aura-plugins-ib8pu4) says consultation v2 "goldens" means the evidence-kind string plus the inline constant pair at receipt/golden_v1_test.go:17 and :22, and asks the worker to list them as changing.
Measured: that pair is the pin for interpreted.v1, a different record kind, and its own comment states "interpreted.v1 is a read-only legacy kind, so this byte sequence must decode unchanged forever, with no in-place migration". Consultation v1 to v2 must not move it. A worker following the leaf text could rewrite the pin and silently destroy the proof that pre-existing durable evidence still decodes.
Change: state in S3-L8 and in the S3 report that goldenV1InterpretedPayload and goldenV1InterpretedSHA256 MUST be unchanged, and that only the consultation evidence-kind string and any cmd/pasture readback golden move. Add an assertion that the v1 pair is byte-identical after the slice.

PA6 MINOR — an empty capability column can be read as "no capability".
Leaf: S1-L8 (aura-plugins-rlwt8r) adds responseCapability and failureEvidence to every activation report row and leaves them "at their unset or empty value" until S3 and S4/S5/S6 fill them. Between S1 and S4 a reader cannot tell "derived as None" from "not yet derived".
Change: render the unset value as an explicit token (for example "unset") and keep the empty string only for a genuinely absent evidence source; S4-L7 and A27 then compare filled values, not blanks.

RULINGS REQUESTED

R1. Mirror-enum test placement (S1 versus S3): the plan's split is CORRECT. S1-L9 (aura-plugins-qg4fp7) builds one reusable helper and applies it to the enums that exist (CaptureProof, ProductionProof, WithheldReason); S3-L2 (aura-plugins-78cal7) applies the same helper to gateauthority.AssignmentRole and gateauthority.TaskPhase, which cannot exist before S3. Section 6c's literal placement is not achievable and the handover is stated in the S1 report. Keep as planned.

R2. FailureEvidence in S0 versus ResponseCapability in S3: the plan's split is CORRECT and is the right order on this axis. FailureEvidence is a fact about the HOST and S0's hostexit.ForFault cannot map a blocking mode without it, so it must land with S0. ResponseCapability is DERIVED from that evidence plus the pre-action versus post-hoc classification, and ActionClass only exists in S3, so deriving it earlier would need a second, unvalidated classification. S0-L2 (aura-plugins-0s656x) already states the boundary in a "Scope boundary" section, and S3-L7 (aura-plugins-llt3k5) owns the derivation and the A27 equality test. Keep as planned, with PA6 applied to the intermediate report rendering.

R3. Section 9 corrections: items 1 and 3 are VERIFIED. Item 1: four raw start-fact writers, at epoch_candidate_commands.go:304, :438, :530 and :866, all building assignmentStartPayload (epoch_assignment_service.go:262), plus assignment_transfer.go — S3-L4 (aura-plugins-1sg9v6) carries the corrected list and a structural choke-point test that turns RED on a fifth writer. Item 3: internal/lifecycle/receipt has no testdata directory and the only golden is the inline pair — verified, and see PA5 for the limit on touching it. Item 2 (dbos_store.go:424) is inside the external pinned provenance module and I did not verify it; S3-L1 (aura-plugins-wivrye) probes it as a blocking spike, which is the right treatment. Item 4 is WRONG — see PA1.

WHAT IS RIGHT ON THIS AXIS (no change asked)
- Every host-visible behaviour I traced has a real-transport proof owned by a named leaf: Claude through the built binary as hooks.json invokes it (S4-L5), Codex through the generated .sh runner (S3-L10, S5), OpenCode through Bun executing the generated plugin (S3-L10, S3-L9, S6), with "a Go-only proof does not count" repeated at slice level.
- S0-L5 (aura-plugins-soaqv4) fixes the silent proceed with a built-binary test per failure mode and keeps the best-effort fault record; S0-L6 (aura-plugins-lit0vi) proves the deadline with a HELD WRITE LOCK and a condition wait, and pins the tier in the docs guard.
- S3-L9 (aura-plugins-h7cbzo) treats operator text as a truth claim: pinned help phrases proven load-bearing by mutation, no stray database on a malformed path, and the kill timer proven by a stalled fake binary through Bun.
- S1-L4 (aura-plugins-8yrtxu) and S1-L6 (aura-plugins-hqnytd) keep capture from ever failing the host, keep the recording notice, and make the clearance private-first with a secret scan that must go RED on a planted token of each shape.
- S4-L6 (aura-plugins-w39t7r) refuses to claim enforcement without evidence and makes "record-only" a reportable outcome rather than a silent one.

RE-REVIEW ASKS: PA1 (restate the OpenCode S2 work), PA2 (order the Claude deny object behind its evidence), PA3 (reachability column plus one test case), PA4 (correct both leaves), PA5 (protect the v1 pin), PA6 (one token). No structural change to the slices, the waves or the ownership table is requested.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
S0-L3 IMPLEMENTED at pasture ac0f04a (see git log; the commit adds only the two hostexit files).

PACKAGE internal/lifecycle/hostexit (pure: no environment, no clock, no store)
- ExitStatus {Unset, ExitContinue, ExitNonBlockingError, ExitBlock} with Code() returning
  0 / 1 / 2 and NO code for the unset zero value, IsValid() and String().
- Outcome {Exit ExitStatus; Stdout []byte; Stderr string}.
- FaultPolicy {Unset, FaultFailOpen, FaultFailClosed} with IsValid() and String().
- ForFault(mode, evidence, policy, err) (Outcome, bool).
- ForDecision(native []byte, exit ExitStatus, stderr string) Outcome.

RULES AS BUILT
- ForFault maps an INTERNAL fault only. It never encodes a policy Deny.
- Fail-open, any mode: ExitContinue plus the diagnostic.
- Fail-closed + an arm that blocks by exit code + evidence present: ExitBlock.
- Fail-closed, anything else: ExitContinue plus the diagnostic.
- A fault NEVER writes stdout, so no native continuation is invented for an event that was
  not evaluated.
- ok=false for a nil error, an unset or out-of-range mode, and an unset or out-of-range
  policy. The Outcome is the zero value in that case, so a caller cannot read a refused
  mapping as exit 0.
- ForDecision does not consult the policy or the evidence, so an evaluated Deny cannot be
  weakened.

DIAGNOSTIC. Composed as an ir.Diagnostic, so it renders the six parts the repository already

S0-L4 IMPLEMENTED at pasture 1c5f1f0.

FILES: cmd/pasture/hook_environment.go, cmd/pasture/hook_environment_test.go (new; both owned
by this leaf).

API
- type HookEnvironment struct { FaultPolicy hostexit.FaultPolicy; CaptureDir string;
  ActorClaim string }
- func HookEnvironmentFromOS(lookup func(string) (string, bool)) (HookEnvironment, error)
  is the PURE parser; the environment is injected.
- func hookEnvironment() (HookEnvironment, error) is the one production caller that names
  os.LookupEnv. The hook command calls it, so there is no second code path.

SEMANTICS
- Default fault policy is FaultFailOpen.
- PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED accepts exactly "1" (fail closed) and "0" (fail open). Any other
  non-empty value is REFUSED with an actionable error; the hook does not guess.
- SET-BUT-EMPTY reads as UNSET for all three variables. An empty PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED is
  not an opt-in; an empty PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR is not a capture directory; an empty
  PASTURE_ACTOR_ID is no claim.
- A capture directory that is only space is refused. This parser reads the value only; the
  capture sink owns the rules about acceptable directories (that is the next slice).
- An actor id that is blank or padded is refused, because an inexact identifier would
  attribute the session to the wrong actor.
- A nil lookup is refused.
- The zero HookEnvironment carries an unset fault policy, which hostexit.ForFault refuses, so
  skipping the parser fails loudly.

TESTS (cmd/pasture/hook_environment_test.go, one file for this subject)
- TestHookEnvironmentTreatsSetButEmptyAsUnset: 12 cases over unset / empty / "0" / "1" /
  malformed / padded for each variable, driven by an injected lookup, all parallel.
- TestHookEnvironmentRefusesAMissingLookup and TestHookEnvironmentZeroValueIsUnusable.
- TestHookEnvironmentReadsTheRealProcessEnvironment: the ONE serial test (t.Setenv, no
  t.Parallel) that drives the production entry point against the real process environment,
  including the exported-but-empty case.
- Every refusal is asserted actionable: it names the function, the file, when in the hook it
  failed, and carries no internal process reference.

S0-L5 IMPLEMENTED at pasture 275b3c6. This closes the silent-proceed defect (aura-plugins-3m1zix).

WHAT CHANGED (cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go)
- lifecycleOutcome produces ONE hostexit.Outcome for every path out of the command: the
  normal path, an environment refusal, a flag error, unexpected positional arguments, a
  handler error, and a recovered panic.
- emitLifecycleOutcome is the ONLY writer of host-facing bytes and the only place the process
  leaves. An UNSET exit status is itself reported and exits 1, so no path can become a silent
  exit 0.
- The internal/errors category table is BYPASSED. That table answers to an operator at a
  terminal; this command answers to a host.
- An event this build does not declare resolves to observe-only, so a stale generated hook
  cannot block a session on a name the build cannot even name.
- The flag-error path runs through the same fault path (cobra handles a flag error before
  RunE), using whatever coordinates parsed.
- Durable fault record: one JSON line appended to lifecycle-faults.jsonl BESIDE the database.
  It is outside the store on purpose, because the commonest fault is that the store could not
  be opened; a record that needed the failing store would be lost when it is needed. The write
  is BEST EFFORT: on failure the fault is still reported on stderr and the Outcome does not
  change.
- internal/runtime.LookupLifecycleFailure(harness, nativeName) is the one narrow lookup of a
  row by native NAME. The typed contracts still have no string lookup; this answers only
  "which failure mode and which citation", returns false for an unknown name, and cannot
  reach identities, fields or ordering. It was added to internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go,
  which S0-L2 owns; S0 is sequential with one worker, so this is the ordered intra-slice
  sharing the plan allows.

MEASURED BEHAVIOUR THROUGH THE BUILT BINARY (all in the new subject file
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go, using buildLifecycleBinary)
- PreToolUse (evidenced, exit-2-blocks) + PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 + storage fault
  -> exit 2, EMPTY stdout, diagnostic on stderr saying "the host refuses the operation".
- The same, under the default fail-open -> exit 0, diagnostic, ONE durable fault record,
  NO native continuation.
- SessionStart (report-and-continue) + the same storage fault + FAIL_CLOSED=1 -> exit 0.
- CATEGORY-TABLE BYPASS PROOF: the SAME "connection error" fault, which the category table
  classes as exit 2, exits 2 on PreToolUse and 0 on SessionStart in the same run.
- An undeclared event name under FAIL_CLOSED=1 -> exit 0, record says observe-only.
- A flag error and an unexpected positional argument on an evidenced gate under FAIL_CLOSED=1
  -> exit 2, empty stdout.
- A healthy invocation is unchanged: PreToolUse still exits 0 with {"decision":"proceed"};
  SessionStart still exits 0 with empty stdout; no fault record is written.

PANIC ARM (pasture issue #54) - PLEASE READ, REVIEWERS. The panic arm is proven in-process
against the EXACT production functions (lifecyclePanicCause + lifecycleFault), which the
deferred recover in lifecycleOutcome calls. It is NOT driven through the built binary,
because no host input can make the binary panic on purpose: every panic reachable in the tree
is a contract-construction panic that no CLI input can reach. Adding an input that could
would mean shipping a second code path whose only user is a test, which the no-dual-path rule
forbids. If the reviewers want a transport-level panic proof, they must first rule on how to
get a real panic without a test-only trigger.

- Two existing assertions pinned exact operator phrases ("the event was recorded but the host
  received no continuation; inspect the database and retry the hook input" in

S0-L6 IMPLEMENTED at pasture b3cf7c4 (plus a gofmt commit 7de8e09).

THE TIER
- internal/timeouts.Profile gains hookInvocation and the HookInvocation() accessor.
- New takes it as a SIXTH argument, between startSlice and workflowResult.
- Ordering enforced by New: SQLiteBusy 500 ms < Ingress 1 s < StartSlice 2 s <
  HookInvocation 5 s < WorkflowResult 30 s.
- Production 500ms/1s/2s/5s/30s; Test 500ms/2s/3s/6s/30s; DeadlineTest
  25ms/250ms/500ms/1s/2s. All three keep the ordering.
- Every timeouts.New caller updated in the same commit: internal/engine/
  concurrency_spike_test.go, internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go,
  internal/lifecycle/receipt/definition_test.go. There is no non-test caller.
- AGENTS.md tier table and the package doc table both carry the new row; the docs guard
  productionTiers list carries HookInvocation, so both rows are now pinned to the live value.

MEASURED HOST BUDGETS THAT JUSTIFY 5 s
- Claude Code: 10 s per hook by default (the generated hooks/hooks.json timeout). SMALLEST.
- Codex: 600 s. Far larger.
- OpenCode: the generated plugin awaits the child process exit with NO timeout of its own.
5 s leaves 5 s of headroom under the smallest budget for process start, which is asserted by
TestProductionHookInvocationSitsBelowTheSmallestHostBudget.

A REAL DEFECT FOUND WHILE PROVING A21. Handing the deadline down as a context is NOT enough.
With the database held under a real SQLite write lock, the built binary took 31.4 SECONDS to
return, because layers below retry on their own ceilings (internal/audit/migrate.go
busyRetryCeiling is 30 s) and do not all read the context. That is more than three times the
Claude budget, so the session was already frozen. The hook now runs the work in a goroutine
and SELECTS on the deadline, which bounds the invocation whatever the layers below do. On
expiry the work is abandoned and reported as a fault; that is safe because the process exits
at once and SQLite rolls an abandoned transaction back. Reviewers should look here first.

TESTS
- internal/timeouts/profile_test.go (existing subject, extended):
  the ordering rule now covers HookInvocation on every known profile;
  TestNewRejectsAHookInvocationDeadlineOutsideItsOrder, a 6-case table (below/equal ingress,
  below/equal start_slice, above/equal workflow-result);
  TestProductionHookInvocationSitsBelowTheSmallestHostBudget.
- internal/timeouts/docs_guard_test.go: the new row is pinned in AGENTS.md and in the package
  doc through the existing productionTiers list.
- cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go (the S0-L5 subject):
  TestLifecycleHookReturnsInsideItsDeadlineWhileTheDatabaseIsLocked. A second connection takes
  the real write lock with BEGIN IMMEDIATE; the test waits on a CONDITION (a channel the
  writer closes once the lock is really held) with a bounded timeout, runs the built binary,
  measures the elapsed time, and releases the lock only after the process returned. NO
  time.Sleep and NO fixed-deadline poll.

    RED: "timeout profile is inverted: the workflow-result wait 30s must be strictly above the
    hook-invocation deadline 40s".
20. Removed the AGENTS.md row.
    RED: "the AGENTS.md timeout table has no row giving HookInvocation as 5s".
21. Removed the package-doc row.
    RED: "the package doc tier table has no row giving HookInvocation as 5s".
22. Removed the select on the deadline, leaving only the handed-down context.
    RED: elapsed 31.4 s, "is not less than 9s" and "is not less than 10s" ("the hook must
    always return inside the smallest host budget"). This is the defect described above.

cmd/pasture, internal/timeouts, internal/engine and internal/lifecycle/... ok; make fmt clean.

warned about no longer needs a name, and the Codex coverage work ends the condition it
describes. It also carried four internal process references (M3-SLICE-1, SLICE-1, SLICE-2,

Claude budget, so the session was already frozen. The hook now runs the work in a goroutine
and SELECTS on the deadline, which bounds the invocation whatever the layers below do. On
expiry the work is abandoned and reported as a fault; that is safe because the process exits
at once and SQLite rolls an abandoned transaction back. REVIEWERS SHOULD LOOK HERE FIRST.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. pasture ISSUE #54 (PANIC PROOF)

CLOSED BY THIS SLICE, with one honest limit stated below.

A recovered panic is now a FAULT and never a silent proceed. lifecycleOutcome installs the
recover, lifecyclePanicCause describes it, and lifecycleFault maps it through hostexit.ForFault
under the event's declared mode and the user's policy. A panic writes no stdout, reports on
stderr, is appended to the durable fault record, and blocks only when the row cites evidence
and the user opted into fail-closed. The old behaviour printed the recovered value and
returned nil, so a panic exited 0 with empty stdout.

THE LIMIT. The panic arm is proven IN-PROCESS against the exact production functions the
deferred recover calls, and NOT through the built binary. No host input can make the binary
panic on purpose: every panic reachable in the tree is a contract-construction panic that no
CLI input reaches. Adding an input that could would mean shipping a second code path whose
only user is a test, which the no-dual-path rule forbids. If a transport-level panic proof is
wanted, the reviewers must first rule on how to obtain a real panic without a test-only
trigger.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. VALIDATION CHECKLIST

PROPOSAL-2 section 6, S0 rows
 [x] three FailureMode enums -> one; openCodeFailure + hostcontractgen failure() deleted
 [x] FailureEvidence rows + generator refusal (refusal in row validation AND as a strict
     generation gate that runs before any write)
 [x] ForFault table over 6 modes x {FailOpen, FailClosed} x {evidence, none} = 24 cells.
     Exactly 2 cells block; the leaf said "flip one FailClosed-with-evidence cell", which
     matches, and the blocking-cell count is 2 because only 2 of the 6 arms block by exit code
 [x] built-binary: strict gate + FailClosed + evidence -> exit 2; strict gate + FailOpen ->
     exit 0 + diagnostic + durable fault record; report-and-continue -> exit 0;
     panic -> fault (in-process, see section 6)
 [x] Outcome bypasses the category table: the SAME connection-error fault exits 2 on
     PreToolUse under fail-closed and 0 on SessionStart in the same run
 [x] TestRefusalNeverMapsToConnectionExitCode unchanged and PASSING

PROPOSAL-3 section 6c, S0 rows
 [x] HookInvocation tier + docs-guard row; expiry -> fault path, proven by a built-binary test
     that holds the real SQLite write lock, waits on a CONDITION with a bounded timeout, and
     releases the lock only after the process returned. No time.Sleep, no fixed-deadline poll
 [x] FailureEvidence gates FAULT exits only. ForDecision does not read the evidence or the
     policy, so an evaluated Deny cannot be weakened

Every-slice rules
 [x] mutation-RED evidence for every new assertion (27 mutations, section 1)
 [x] go test -race in the normal flow; green on the archive copy
 [x] no time.Sleep, no fixed-deadline poll in any new test
 [x] one test file per subject; the only new test files are for genuinely new subjects
     (internal/lifecycle/hostexit, cmd/pasture/hook_environment, the hook exit contract, the
     epic-wide safety guard)
 [x] no internal reference in any added line of shipped code, help text or generated artefact
 [x] ACP / Gemini / Antigravity unchanged, and asserted permanently (S0-L7)
 [x] no Git hook installed, core.hooksPath untouched, and asserted permanently

Acceptance criteria discharged: A1, A2, A3, A19, A21.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST

 1. The 31-second measurement and the goroutine-plus-select deadline in
    cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go. Abandoning in-flight work on expiry is the sharpest
    decision in this slice.
 2. The BlocksByExitCode ruling in section 4: does the epic agree that throw-fail-fast is
    outside the evidence rule?
 3. The panic proof limit in section 6.
 4. The Codex re-derivation scope ruling in section 3.
 5. The known divergence handed to S4 and S5 at the end of section 4.
 6. The durable fault record lives in a file beside the database, not in the database, because
    the commonest fault is that the database could not be opened. Is a JSON-lines file the
    right durable surface for this epic?

text:
UPDATED against the ARCHITECT RULING (which supersedes the earlier accept-in-principle). The finding stands and its shape is now fixed by the ruling rather than by my preference.

The ruling names the ROOT DEFECT: retry ceilings do not honour the context, so handing the 5 s deadline down as a context bounds nothing. The goroutine-select at 3de1beb treats the symptom. Judged as INCOMPLETE, not wrong.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE TEST, which is my axis. The required shape has three parts; part 2 is a test shape that is easy to fake:

  "the goroutine-select deadline STAYS as a BACKSTOP ONLY, with a test
   proving it is NOT what normally fires"

A test that only proves the backstop WORKS satisfies the words and leaves the primary fix absent, green. The proof needs BOTH halves and they assert opposite things:

  NEGATIVE (the load-bearing half): with the store held under a write lock, the
  invocation returns through the CONTEXT-CANCELLED path within one SQLiteBusy
  tier, and the abandonment branch is NOT reached. Assert on the path taken --
  the cause text and the recorded fault name a cancelled retry, not an expired
  hook deadline -- and on the tier, not on the 5 s budget. If this half asserts
  only "returned in under 5 s", it passes with the ceilings unchanged and the
  primary fix missing.

  POSITIVE: with the primary fix in place, force the backstop (work that ignores
  cancellation) and prove it still bounds the invocation and reports honestly.

Today's test is the reason this matters: its stderr assertion matches the GENERIC fault prefix, which every fault produces, so it cannot distinguish the two paths at all. It would pass unchanged whichever path ran. Whatever S0-L8 lands, that assertion has to become path-specific or the negative half is not real.

text:
VOTE: REVISE — 1 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT, 3 MINOR. Axis A: host-contract truth and end-user behaviour. SHA 3de1beb.

METHOD. Reviewed on my own archive copy of the SHA (git archive, git init, own commit), never in the worker's worktree, and no make generate anywhere near it. I built the binary from that copy and RAN it for every host-visible claim rather than reading the tests: the OpenCode and Claude fault exits, both fault policies, the flag-error path, the fault record, and a payload with a planted token. I also re-measured the generated artefacts and the failure-mode counts.

BLOCKER
aura-plugins-9azlzv — the fail-open guarantee is false on OpenCode. Measured on the built binary: an opencode tool.execute.before fault exits 0 with EMPTY stdout under both policies. The generated plugin then runs acceptProceed(""), JSON.parse("") throws, and the named callback aborts, so a pasture fault reaches the user as a failed tool call. PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED is also silently a no-op on every OpenCode named callback. The behaviour predates this slice, but the universal guarantee is this slice's, and it is proven for Claude shapes only. Fix by scoping the claim and handing a named acceptance case to the leaf that owns the plugin generator, or by teaching the plugin that exit 0 with empty stdout means "not evaluated, continue". Not by writing a proceed object on the fault path.

IMPORTANT
aura-plugins-tj8skz — the deadline diagnostic asserts durable state it cannot know. The receipt is committed before the encode, so an abandoned invocation may already have written the occurrence, while the text says "before any decision was written" and "this lifecycle event is not evaluated". Needs a typed stage argument so the expiry path says the durable state is unknown. Verified in your favour on the rest: no DBOS on the hook path, so nothing is left pending for a later process, and the process ends promptly, so SQLite discards the uncommitted transaction. The abandonment is safe; only the claim is too strong. The 5 s tier stays right — it is derived from the host budget, not from how long the work can take.
aura-plugins-hsfyws — neither recover() is exercised. The panic test builds a cause and maps it; it never runs a recover. The goroutine recover is the only guard for a panic inside the work, and without it the runtime exits 2, which Claude reads as a BLOCK with a stack trace as the reason. It IS provable with no dual path: inject a panicking io.Reader through the cobra SetIn seam and call the production lifecycleOutcome.
aura-plugins-7pprls — the Codex profile comment says no Codex reference is committed. One is: nativeresponse.go:24-47 records the pinned 0.146.0 output contract with its source revision, and the ratified amendment names that file as the Codex evidence. Left as is, it can send a later slice into a live capture campaign that costs the user hours for a fact already in the tree.
aura-plugins-yjb0jq — after the one-vocabulary change, two committed artefacts disagree: registration/claude_2_1_210.gen.go carries 15 exit-2-blocks while the metamodel carries 4. Inert today, since nothing reads registration.Event.Failure, but they are 15 uncited blocking claims per harness in a shipped file. The OpenCode catalogue already derives Failure from the runtime mapping; do the same for Claude and Codex, or drop the field.

MINOR
aura-plugins-70w7n1 — the reason given for excluding throw-fail-fast is wrong even though the exclusion is right; the plugin does read the exit code and convert it. Includes a warning that S3 must not key the capability derivation on BlocksByExitCode alone, or every OpenCode gate derives CapabilityNone and the OpenCode deny proof becomes unsatisfiable.
aura-plugins-dxernu — the deadline bounds the work, not the whole invocation; the fault record write and the stderr write happen after expiry.
aura-plugins-eicet7 — lifecycle-faults.jsonl has no cap, no rotation and no reader, in the user's home, fed by a condition that repeats on every invocation. Your surface question answered: the file is the right place, because the database is the thing that fails.

THE THREE RULINGS YOU ASKED FOR
1. Abandonment: safe, and the tier is right. The diagnostic is NOT honest about what was abandoned — see aura-plugins-tj8skz. That is the one thing to change here.
2. BlocksByExitCode: the exclusion is correct for S0 on reasons (b) and (c). Reason (a) is factually wrong about the plugin and must be restated — see aura-plugins-70w7n1.
3. Panic proof: not sufficient as it stands, and it can be made sufficient cheaply without a test-only production path — see aura-plugins-hsfyws.

HANDOVER LIST, CHECKED. The 19 demoted rows are right: Claude 11, Codex 8, OpenCode 0, and the four kept Claude rows are exactly the four the cited reference documents as blocking on exit 2. The counts reconcile against metamodel.gen.go (Claude 4 blocking of 30, Codex 8 demoted of 10, OpenCode 32 observe-only plus 15 throw-fail-fast). Nothing in that list propagates an error to S4, S5 or S6.

WHAT IS RIGHT, AND WORTH SAYING. The silent proceed is really gone: every path, including a flag error before RunE, produces one Outcome, and an unset status cannot become a quiet exit 0. The fault-versus-decision split is carried in the types, not in prose, so a Deny cannot be weakened by a missing citation. The evidence rule demotes a guess instead of trusting it, which is the right default for somebody else's program. The 31 s measurement and the select are a genuine find: handing a context down was not enough, and the slice proved it with a real write lock and a condition wait rather than a sleep. The diagnostics name what, why, where, when, impact and fix, and the fault record is best-effort so bookkeeping never blocks a host.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-10 CODE REVIEW — reviewer-b (axis: architecture and data model), SLICE S0, ROUND 1
SHA reviewed: 3de1beb4da8260b8775cbf5517e06f29ef3f86aa, on an ARCHIVE COPY. The worker's live worktree was not touched.

COUNT: 1 BLOCKER / 5 IMPORTANT / 3 MINOR
Severity groups: BLOCKER aura-plugins-at7b0q, IMPORTANT aura-plugins-j5aqex, MINOR aura-plugins-j2r822.
Findings: B1 mihekg (BLOCKER, also a child of this slice) · B2 n9o42i · B3 xqau8l · B4 4b248h · B5 zgqcaw · B6 mjzw08 · B7 2u3a2j · B8 44tvz0 · B9 ktufsb.

GATES I RAN (I am the gate runner this wave; the other two reviewers stayed read-only)
- go test -race -count=1 ./... on a fresh archive copy of the SHA: 72 packages ok, exit 0, no failure, no data race.
- make generate on a SECOND fresh archive copy, committed at the SHA before generating: exit 0, git status clean, ZERO drift.
- The worker's note about the gate scaffold is CORRECT and I reproduced both sides: on a copy with no commit, internal/handlers TestHookRecord_RealGit_RepoAndRemotes fails with the git rev-parse error and the suite reports 71 ok plus that one failure; after one commit the same copy is fully green. It is the scaffold, not the slice.

THE THREE ITEMS THE WORKER RAISED

1. THE GOROUTINE AND THE ABANDONED WORK — the shape is RIGHT. Keep it.
   - The 31.4 s measurement is the real finding, and the plan was wrong: a context deadline cannot bound work whose lower layers retry on their own ceilings. A select at the boundary is the only construction that bounds the invocation whatever those layers do, and the host budget is a hard external constraint, so the bound has to be unconditional.
   - Can it leak or corrupt? I checked the ownership question rather than taking the report's word. The receipt path opens provenance through provenance.OpenBorrowedSQLite (internal/tasks/open_unified.go:211), which is the DIRECT SQLite journal. The DBOS workflow path in the provenance module (its dbos_adapter RunWorkflow surface) is NOT constructed anywhere in pasture: I searched the whole tree for NewDBOSAdapter and found no non-test use. That matters, because a DBOS-backed Apply killed mid-flight is exactly the thing that could leave a PENDING workflow row for a LATER process to recover, which would be an abandoned invocation racing a later one. With the borrowed SQLite journal there is no such row: an abandoned transaction dies with the process and the next connection rolls the journal back. So no leak that outlives the process, and no cross-invocation race.
   - Can it race a LATER invocation? Not through pasture state, for the reason above. Within one process it cannot happen either: nothing calls lifecycleOutcome in-process (the tests exercise lifecycleFault directly), so no abandoned goroutine survives inside a test binary holding a temp database.
   - Versus making the retry ceilings context-aware: do BOTH, in this order. The select stays, because it is the only bound that does not depend on every layer behaving. The ceilings that ignore their context (internal/audit/migrate.go busyRetryCeiling and its peers) are a separate defect that still bites pastured and every other command, and it should be filed as a follow-up outside this slice rather than pulled in.
   - The one thing the shape costs is stated wrongly, which is finding B3: the deadline can fire AFTER the receipt commits, so "the work was abandoned" and "this lifecycle event is not evaluated" are claims the hook cannot make.
   - One more constraint to write down: this construction is only safe because the process exits immediately after. If a future caller ever reuses lifecycleOutcome in-process, the abandoned goroutine keeps a store handle. One sentence in the function comment fixes that for good.

2. BlocksByExitCode EXCLUDING throw-fail-fast — the ruling is CORRECT and the enum vocabulary is right. FailureMode names the native failure behaviour; BlocksByExitCode is a predicate about ONE channel. OpenCode refuses by throwing inside the plugin chain, and that contract is committed in this repository, so the evidence rule has nothing to add to it. The three reasons in section 4 agree with each other and with the code, and there is no modelling error in the single enum. What IS wrong is that the same predicate then answers a different question inside ForFault, which makes PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED a silent no-op on OpenCode. That is finding B4, and it is a separation-of-questions fix, not an enum fix.

3. THE IN-PROCESS PANIC PROOF — I agree, and I would refuse the alternative. Shipping an input that makes the binary panic means shipping a second code path whose only user is a test, and the no-dual-path rule exists for exactly this. The proof runs against the production functions the deferred recover calls, and the recover itself is exercised through the built binary by the other fault cases. That is the honest limit and it is stated in the report. No change requested. If a later reviewer wants a transport-level panic, the only clean way is a fault injected at a seam that production already has, and no such seam exists here.

ALSO RULED, since the report asks
- The Codex re-derivation scope ruling (section 3) is CORRECT: the leaf limits the owned region of codex_0_146_0.go to the comment, the checklist does not list a re-derivation, and the stated behaviour-change list requires no Codex value to move. Retiring the comment while keeping the load-bearing fact is the right trade, and dropping the four internal process references from shipped source is required by the references standard.
- THE 19 DEMOTIONS ARE CORRECT AND COMPLETE. I checked them against the table rather than the list. Claude: every row built by the unevidenced gate helper plus ConfigChange (conditionally blocking) and ElicitationResult (explicit human response) is exactly the eleven named — UserPromptExpansion, PermissionRequest, PostToolBatch, ConfigChange, WorktreeCreate, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, PreCompact, Elicitation, ElicitationResult — and the four kept rows (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreToolUse, SubagentStop) are the four that cite the host reference. Codex: codexLifecycleMapping passes FailureStrictExitTwoBlocks as the blocking arm, so all eight gates demote, which is the whole gate set. OpenCode: none, because its rows are throw-fail-fast and observe-only and neither is gated by the rule. One detail the report's prose gets slightly wrong and the code gets right: evidenceBoundFailure returns report-and-continue for an unevidenced BLOCKING row on every harness, so the demoted Codex gates land on report-and-continue and not on their harness's non-blocking arm. Worth one word in the report, since S5 will read that sentence.
- The durable fault record as a JSON-lines file BESIDE the database: right call, and the reason given is the strongest one — the commonest fault is that the store could not be opened, and evidence that needs the failing store is lost exactly when it is needed. It needs the retention sentence in finding B7, nothing more.

WHAT IS GOOD, and I do not want it changed
- hostexit is genuinely pure and the whole table is testable without a store, which is what makes the 24-cell proof meaningful.
- Every closed enum introduced here refuses its zero value, and ExitStatus.Code returning (int, bool) is the right shape: an undecided path cannot become a silent exit 0.
- ForFault and ForDecision as two named doors, with the package doc stating that a Deny never passes through the fault door, is exactly the FAULT-versus-DENY separation the proposal asked for, and it is enforced by the signature rather than by prose: ForDecision cannot see the policy or the evidence.
- 27 mutations, each restored, and several of them mutate the RIGHT thing: mutation 16 restores the original defect and shows the new assertions catch it.

author: David Huu Pham
text: SUPERVISOR: carried into the fix leaf aura-plugins-p2f8wh (S0-L8) in the worker's own text, per reviewer-c's forward note. text:
PHASE-10 ROUND 1 CONSOLIDATED TALLY, all three axes reported.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TWO REVIEWER CONFLICTS, escalated to the team lead rather than resolved by the supervisor.

CONFLICT 1 - the scope of the retry-ceiling fix.
- The ARCHITECT ruled: make the ceilings context-aware as the PRIMARY fix, in S0, with S0's ownership extended (leaf aura-plugins-p2f8wh).
- reviewer-b, after checking ownership rather than trusting the report, says: KEEP the select, and file the context-blind ceilings as a follow-up OUTSIDE this slice, because they still bite pastured. Its evidence: the receipt path opens provenance.OpenBorrowedSQLite (open_unified.go:211), the DIRECT SQLite journal, and NewDBOSAdapter is constructed nowhere in pasture; so a killed process CANNOT leave a pending workflow row for a later process to recover, which is the danger a DBOS-backed Apply would carry. Nothing calls lifecycleOutcome in-process either, so no abandoned goroutine survives inside a test binary.
- reviewer-a independently agrees the abandonment is SAFE and that 5 s is still right, having verified no DBOS runs on the hook path and that the process ends promptly so SQLite discards the uncommitted transaction.
So both reviewers who examined it conclude the current shape is safe, and one argues the ceiling work belongs outside S0. The architect ruled it belongs inside. The supervisor does not choose.

CONFLICT 2 - the panic proof.
- reviewer-b: the in-process proof is right and it would REFUSE the alternative, because a panic-on-demand input is a second code path whose only user is a test.
- reviewer-a (aura-plugins-hsfyws): the proof is NOT sufficient, because neither recover() is exercised, and an unrecovered goroutine panic exits 2, which Claude reads as a BLOCK with a stack trace as the reason. It offers a route with NO dual path: inject a panicking io.Reader through the EXISTING cobra SetIn seam.
The two positions may be reconcilable: reviewer-a's route uses an existing seam and adds no production branch, which is what reviewer-b objects to. The supervisor does not choose.

Both conflicts are with the team lead now. The fix round does not start until they are resolved, because both change what the fix worker must build.

author: David Huu Pham
text: REVIEWER-C RANKED POSITION, given in advance and carried into the fix leaf aura-plugins-p2f8wh: (1) BEST a production seam justified on its own merits - the point between 'receipt committed' and 'host told' is a real design boundary where the commit-before-stdout invariant lives, so judge a proposed seam as a design change, not a testing convenience; (2) ACCEPTABLE a weaker structural argument stated plainly, on the precedent of the in-process panic proof, with the LIMIT stated where a later reader meets it - the code comment at the deadline, the S0 report, and the text closing the ruling - not only in a report nobody re-reads; (3) LAST back to the architect, because a ruling whose condition the code cannot meet is the architect's to re-shape. Accepted if reported as such with the residual gap stated; a finding if reported as the invariant proven. Raising the blocker is NOT a failure of the fix round.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SHARPENED after the team-lead ruling that BlocksByExitCode correctly excludes throw-fail-fast, with the reason "on OpenCode a policy refusal is the typed deny object (T18), not an exit code, and a non-zero exit there is a FAULT".

I verified that claim rather than taking it. It is TRUE, and it makes this finding a gap in the DESIGN, not only in the generated plugin.

Verified against the ratified proposal text (T18): OpenCode proceed is {"decision":"proceed"} at exit 0; OpenCode deny is {"decision":"deny","reason":...} at exit 0 with the plugin throwing reason-only text; a non-zero exit stays an invocation FAULT with the existing "verify PASTURE_BIN" text. Verified against the tree at this SHA: the plugin throws on any non-zero exit (pasture-lifecycle.ts:21) and accepts exactly one object at exit 0 (acceptProceed, :25-32).

So OpenCode has exactly TWO declared channels: an exit-0 typed object, and a non-zero fault. A fail-open fault is NEITHER. It is exit 0 with empty stdout, which is not a typed object, so acceptProceed throws and the user's tool call fails. The FAULT-that-continues has no shape on OpenCode, in the current tree and in T18 as ratified.

That is the whole finding, stated in the ruling's own vocabulary: the design gives OpenCode a refusal shape and a fault-that-blocks shape, and no fault-that-continues shape, while fail-open is the default and produces exactly that outcome on every harness.

The fix therefore belongs with the deny-object work in the leaf that owns the plugin generator (aura-plugins-h7cbzo), and it is one more accepted stdout shape or one accepted empty case, not a new channel. What S0 must do is stop stating the guarantee universally.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULING VERIFIED, and it supplies a better sentence than the one I proposed.

The team lead ruled that BlocksByExitCode correctly excludes throw-fail-fast because on OpenCode a policy refusal is the typed deny object and a non-zero exit is a fault. I checked that against the ratified T18 text and against the tree at this SHA (pasture-lifecycle.ts:21 throws on any non-zero exit; acceptProceed at :25-32 accepts exactly one exit-0 object). The ruling holds.

So the comment at internal/runtime/lifecycle.go:208-211 should not say the plugin does "not read an exit code" - it does, at line 21 - and should instead say what the ruling says: on OpenCode the REFUSAL channel is the typed object returned at exit 0, and a non-zero exit is a fault, so the exit code is not the refusal channel and the citation rule does not apply to it. Same conclusion, true premise.

The exclusion itself is settled and needs no change. This stays a MINOR about the sentence.

The warning for S3 stands and is now more concrete: if the capability derivation keys on BlocksByExitCode alone, every OpenCode named callback derives CapabilityNone, rule 9 turns every OpenCode deny into ReasonUnenforcedDeny, and the OpenCode deny proof owed by aura-plugins-4vsuum cannot be satisfied. The evidence for the OpenCode refusal channel is a committed artefact of this repository plus its Bun test, not a host documentation URL.

I accept the routing: the catalogue RE-DERIVATION belongs to S5 leaf aura-plugins-1w7rkf, and the Claude side to S4-L4. I am not asking S0 to re-derive anything. Two things stay with S0:

author: David Huu Pham
text:
COMPATIBLE WITH THE RULING, and narrowed so that it cannot be read as re-opening it.

The team lead ruled that the in-process panic proof for pasture issue #54 is ACCEPTED and that no test-only panic path goes into the binary. I agree with both, and this finding asks for neither. It asks for ZERO change to shipped code.

What is accepted: #54 is closed for the mapping of a panic to a fault, and for the main-path recover.
What is still unproven, and is the whole of this finding: the recover INSIDE the work goroutine (cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:137-141). The outer deferred recover cannot catch a panic raised there, because it is a different stack. If that guard is ever removed, the Go runtime terminates the process with status 2 and prints a stack trace on stderr, and Claude reads exit 2 as a BLOCK with stderr as the reason shown to the model. A pasture crash would arrive at the user as a policy refusal. Nothing turns RED today if the guard disappears.

The proof needs no production trigger. cobra already owns the seam: the command reads its payload through cmd.InOrStdin(), which cmd.SetIn replaces in a test. An io.Reader whose Read panics is a test INPUT. It panics inside HookLifecycleNative, which is inside the goroutine, so calling the production lifecycleOutcome with that reader exercises the real guard. Nothing test-only is compiled into the binary, which is exactly the condition the ruling sets.

If the supervisor still reads this as inside the settled ruling, downgrade it to MINOR rather than dropping it: the regression it guards against converts a fault into a host-visible refusal, which is the one confusion this slice exists to remove.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEWER-A (host-contract truth and end-user behaviour) on the new required shape, before the work starts. Three inputs.

1. THE 500 ms QUESTION IS FRAMED WRONG, and the real answer is friendlier than the framing.
The requirement says "a cancelled context stops the retry loop within ONE SQLiteBusy tier (500 ms)". That is CANCELLATION LATENCY, not a give-up budget. It does not mean a user's hook gives up on a locked database after 500 ms. The give-up budget stays the 5 s HookInvocation deadline: the hook keeps retrying for up to 5 s, and when the deadline cancels, the retry loop must notice within 500 ms instead of grinding on to its own 30 s ceiling.
Judged as a user experience, that reads correctly: a busy database costs a short wait and then a fail-open with a diagnostic, and never a frozen session. If the intent really were "give up after 500 ms", I would push back - 500 ms is well inside normal contention for a database several hook processes are writing to at once, and abandoning that early would drop journal evidence a one-second wait would have captured, with a 10 s host budget going unused. Please state the tier as the budget and the 500 ms as the latency, in the leaf and in the report, so nobody implements the stricter reading by accident.

2. DO NOT LOWER THE CEILINGS GLOBALLY. busyRetryCeiling (internal/audit/migrate.go) bounds retrying a schema migration that lost the file lock to another process; AGENTS.md documents both 30 s ceilings as deliberately outside the timeout profile. `pasture migrate` and the daemon have no host waiting on them and a legitimate reason to wait 30 s. Make the loops honour the CALLER'S context, so the hook path is bounded by its 5 s deadline and every other caller keeps the ceiling it has today. A global reduction would turn a legitimate concurrent migration into a failure for a user who never ran a hook.

3. PART 3 OF THE INVARIANT IS NOT EXHAUSTIVE. Details and evidence are in finding aura-plugins-9ogja9. In short: the receipt is two separate durable writes (receipt/service.go:85 blob, :122 journal), so a third outcome exists - a committed payload blob with no occurrence - and the code names it deliberately at service.go:83-84 as a reclaimable orphan, preferred over the corruption case of a journal row naming an absent blob. It is also the outcome the deadline will produce most often, because the journal append is where a locked database makes the invocation wait. Prove the triple, prove the real invariant (never an occurrence naming an absent blob), and count the orphans one abandoned invocation leaves.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RESTATED by reviewer-b after the team-lead ruling (BlocksByExitCode excludes throw-fail-fast: RULED CORRECT; on OpenCode a policy refusal is the typed deny object of tradeoff T18, and a non-zero exit there is a FAULT).

I agree with the ruling and I withdraw the fix I proposed. Making an ExitBlock non-zero on OpenCode would collide with T18: the plugin reads a non-zero exit as an invocation fault and prints the "verify PASTURE_BIN" text, so a policy refusal would reach the user as a broken installation.

The finding itself stands, narrowed. Under T18 the OpenCode refusal channel is the typed deny object, and that object does not exist until S3. So PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED has NO channel at all on OpenCode in this slice, and nothing says so. The option's own help text and the hostexit package doc describe a behaviour one of the three harnesses cannot perform.

Concrete change requested, replacing my earlier one:
1. State it where the user reads it: PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED blocks on hosts that refuse by process exit code; on OpenCode the refusal channel is the typed deny object, which arrives with the gate work.
2. State it in the hostexit package doc beside the ForFault table.
3. Pin it with one test, so the day the deny object exists somebody has to come back and decide whether a FAULT may use it.
4. Note for S3: when the deny object exists, the open question is whether an unevaluated event may use the refusal channel at all. My reading is that it may — fail-closed means refuse because we could not evaluate — but that is a decision for the architect, not for the S3 worker.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-10 REVIEW — reviewer-b, ROUND 1 ADDENDUM after the corrected archive recipe and the two rulings relays. Same SHA 3de1beb.

REVISED COUNT: 1 BLOCKER / 7 IMPORTANT / 5 MINOR.
New: B10 aura-plugins-6p28ql · B11 aura-plugins-jycdyy · B12 aura-plugins-uvdys7 · B13 aura-plugins-i97efx. B4 (4b248h) is restated in place. B10 and B11 also BLOCK the fix leaf aura-plugins-p2f8wh, because they change what it must build.

ON THE ARCHIVE RECIPE. Your corrected recipe matches what I actually ran, and I had already reported both sides of it: without a commit the suite reads 71 ok plus TestHookRecord_RealGit_RepoAndRemotes failing on the missing HEAD; with one commit it is 72 ok, exit 0, no data race. I also ran the drift gate on a SECOND copy, committed at the SHA before generating, because a copy that is generated before it is committed cannot show drift: result was exit 0 and a clean tree. Both copies are deleted.

MY FIRST REVIEW FOCUS, AS RULED: can the abandonment break the commit-before-stdout invariant?
NO, and I can say why rather than assert it. internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go Receive writes the BLOB first and the journal operation second, and its own comment states the reason: an orphan blob is reclaimable, a journal row naming an absent blob is corruption. The append is one operation. Above it, deliveryCommit runs EnsureActiveMetamodel before Receive, and that activation is idempotent under a content-derived operation id. So an abandoned invocation lands in one of four states — nothing, an activation with no receipt, an orphan blob with no journal row, or a committed receipt with no stdout — and the corrupting state is unreachable. The invariant holds.

Two consequences, both filed:
- The required part-3 wording ("either a committed receipt or NO receipt, never a partial write") is not exact, because of the orphan blob. B11 gives the four states and, more usefully, shows how to PROVE the property instead of arguing it: receipt.Service is a struct of injected fields, so a test can supply an Appender that blocks until the deadline fires and assert the interleaving through the real commit sequence. No new production path.
- The host is still told the wrong thing when the deadline fires after a commit. That is B3, unchanged, and it is the only real cost of the shape.

MY SECOND FOCUS: is making the ceilings context-aware safe in the packages that own them?
Safe at the migrator, and the ordering assumption you suspected is not there: each step is ONE transaction, it re-reads MAX(version) after taking the lock and no-ops when a concurrent migrator moved past it, and database/sql rolls a transaction back when the BeginTx context is cancelled. Keep "one step, one transaction" as an assertion in the fix.

But the premise needs correcting before the fix leaf starts, which is B10 and is the sharpest thing I found this pass. beginImmediateWithRetry ALREADY honours the context: it passes ctx to BeginTx and selects on ctx.Done() between attempts, with a fully actionable cancellation error. internal/engine/dbosinit.go newDurableContext does the same. The context simply never arrives: runStep opens with a hard-coded context.Background(), Migrate takes no context at all, and neither does the store opener the hook uses (OpenTaskTracker(dbPath string), and the handler's own opener type is func(string)). So the 31.4 s was not a loop ignoring a deadline; it was a deadline that never reached a loop which would have obeyed it. The primary fix is therefore a SIGNATURE change threaded from the hook through the opener into Migrate and runStep, which is a wider blast radius than "make the ceilings context-aware" and should be sized before the worker starts. The peer survey should also be re-run with the right question: does the site RECEIVE a context and select on it, not does it have a wall-clock ceiling.

ON THE OTHER RULINGS
- BlocksByExitCode excluding throw-fail-fast: I agree, and I have withdrawn the fix I proposed in B4, which would have collided with T18 by turning a policy refusal into the plugin's "verify PASTURE_BIN" fault text. B4 now asks only that the slice SAY that PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED has no channel on OpenCode until the typed deny object exists in S3. My BLOCKER B1 is unaffected and is now better supported by T18: a fault must not reach the user as a refusal, and today a fail-open fault does exactly that on OpenCode because an empty stdout makes acceptProceed throw.
- The in-process panic proof: accepted, and I said so independently.
- The Codex re-derivation moving to S5: right, and it corrects me. I read the committed comment at this SHA and the CODE is exactly what the ruling wants — it keeps the divergence note, states the inertness and its condition, drops the four internal references, and names the re-derivation condition. Nothing to change there. What claims the retirement is the REPORT (section 3, "QUOTED AND RETIRED", "the coupling it warned about no longer needs a name"), and by your own rule that is the case I should raise: B12. I also withdraw my round-1 endorsement of that framing; I judged it before the ruling.

author: David Huu Pham
text:

BLOCKER: fail-open must hold on EVERY harness. Two layers, both in S0 with ownership extended, owned by NEW leaf aura-plugins-lx5905 (S0-L9): (1) Go PRIMARY - a fail-open FAULT emits that harness's CONTINUE bytes (Claude empty stdout; Codex {"continue":true} for gates and {} for observations; OpenCode {"decision":"proceed"}), exit 0, diagnostic, best-effort record. The rule 'fault = no continuation' is REPLACED by 'fault = continue bytes + diagnostic'. (2) Generator BELT - the OpenCode plugin treats empty stdout with exit 0 on a named callback as 'not evaluated, continue', so an OLD binary cannot abort a tool call either. Proof through the built binary AND Bun; with PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 the typed deny object with a fault reason, so the opt-in stops being a no-op on OpenCode. The fail-open claim in docs and help is restated to match.
CONFLICT 1 RESOLVED in the reviewers' favour: the ownership evidence is accepted. The goroutine-select at 5 s IS the S0 fix and stays. The context-blind retry ceilings LEAVE S0 and are folded into aura-plugins-wmi6ep as their own task with the measured sites; they still bite pastured but do not block this epic. Leaf aura-plugins-p2f8wh is rewritten: parts 1 and 2 dropped, the abandonment-safety proof and the path-specific deadline assertion kept.
CONFLICT 2 RESOLVED with reviewer-a's route, which also satisfies reviewer-b's objection: inject a panicking io.Reader through the EXISTING cobra SetIn seam, no production branch, and assert the recover maps to the FAIL-OPEN Outcome and NOT exit 2. author: David Huu Pham
text:
CONFLICT RAISED BY THE WORKER, escalated to the team lead rather than resolved by the supervisor.

THE CONFLICT is between this leaf's test list and finding aura-plugins-4b248h as RESTATED by reviewer-b AFTER the team-lead ruling.
- This leaf (written by the supervisor from the ruling) requires: with PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1, emit the TYPED DENY OBJECT with a fault reason, so the opt-in stops being a no-op on OpenCode.
- Finding 4b248h says the opposite is the correct S0 outcome: under T18 the OpenCode refusal channel IS the typed deny object, and that object DOES NOT EXIST until S3. So PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED has NO CHANNEL AT ALL on OpenCode in this slice, and the defect is that nothing SAYS so. Its asks are three statements and one pin, not an implementation.
- reviewer-b also WITHDREW its earlier proposed fix for the same reason: making an OpenCode ExitBlock non-zero collides with T18, because the generated plugin reads a non-zero exit as a BROKEN INSTALLATION ('verify PASTURE_BIN'), so a policy refusal would reach the user as a broken install.

THE WORKER'S THREE REASONS FOR NOT GUESSING, all sound:
1. The typed deny object's SHAPE is S3's to define; inventing it in S0 pre-empts a design S3 owns, and acceptProceed would have to learn a second accepted shape at the same time.
2. reviewer-b names the underlying question as the ARCHITECT'S: may a FAULT - an event that was NEVER EVALUATED - use the REFUSAL channel at all? Building it answers that question by implementation.
3. It is not needed for the BLOCKER. Both blockers are about FAIL-OPEN stopping the user's tool call, and that is fixed and proven.

PROVISIONAL STATE: the worker has built the 4b248h shape (limitation stated in the hostexit package doc beside the fault table and in the PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED help and diagnostic text, pinned by TestFailClosedHasNoChannelOnTheThrowingHost, which FAILS the day the deny object exists so somebody must decide deliberately). It continues on option A so the round is not stalled, and will change it if the ruling differs.

SUPERVISOR NOTE: the leaf text is MINE, written from the ruling; the worker did not misread it. If the ruling stands as written, I will correct the leaf.

author: David Huu Pham
text: FIXED at e8a53f3aab2f07f0fed15098fd18a35de13854bf. The generator belt lands too: the plugin reads an empty body at exit 0 on a named callback as not-evaluated-continue, so an OLD binary cannot abort a tool call either.
