text:
ROUND-4 REVIEW, AXIS A (host-contract truth and end-user behaviour), at
707ba8f4267c78bf487a349077c2f504477db639. Review task aura-plugins-h1zj9w.
VERDICT: REVISE - 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 3 MINOR.

I am the replacement axis-A reviewer. I read the recorded findings rather than
re-deriving them. Every number below I measured myself, on an archive copy of
707ba8f with the required initial commit, and with a binary BUILT from that copy.

=====================================================================
1. THE FAIL-OPEN GUARANTEE HOLDS ON EVERY HARNESS. VERIFIED.
=====================================================================
Store made unopenable, one faulting invocation per row, exit code and stdout
read from the built binary:

  claude-code SessionStart          exit 0  stdout <empty>
  claude-code PreToolUse            exit 0  stdout <empty>
  codex       SessionStart          exit 0  stdout {}
  codex       PreToolUse            exit 0  stdout {"continue":true}
  opencode    session.created       exit 0  stdout <empty>   (observation)
  opencode    session.updated       exit 0  stdout <empty>   (observation)
  opencode    tool.execute.before   exit 0  stdout {"decision":"proceed"}
  opencode    chat.message          exit 0  stdout {"decision":"proceed"}

Undeclared events take the harness-universal continuation:
  claude-code NoSuchEvent <empty> / codex NoSuchEvent {"continue":true} /
  opencode no.such.event {"decision":"proceed"}.
Every one carries the stderr diagnostic. So the rule is "fault = continue bytes
+ diagnostic", not "fault = no continuation", exactly as the supersession says.

MY OWN MUTATION, because the guarantee is worth one: I made the OpenCode gate arm
of nativeresponse.FaultContinuation return the empty continuation - the round-1
BLOCKER, restored. THREE tests turned RED together, including the built-binary
one: TestFaultContinuationIsTheHostProceedForEveryHarness,
TestTheFaultContinuationMatchesTheEvaluatedProceed and
TestAPanicInTheWorkGoroutineIsAFaultAndNeverABlock. Restored; tree verified clean.

BOTH SKEW DIRECTIONS.
- New binary against an OLD installed plugin: I read the plugin at the base
  commit 73f38d0. Its observation path never inspects stdout and swallows the
  error, so an empty body on an OpenCode observation cannot abort anything; its
  gate path needs the canonical object, which the new binary emits.
- OLD binary against the CURRENT generated plugin: covered by the generator belt
  TestOpenCodeGeneratedPluginContinuesOnAnEmptyBody, which runs the REAL
  generated module under Bun with a fake pasture that writes nothing at exit 0,
  and asserts the callback continues AND leaves output.args untouched.
- The two generated artefacts (.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts and
  internal/target/opencode/assets/hooks/pasture-hooks.ts) are byte-identical.

=====================================================================
2. THE OPENCODE OBSERVATION ARM AND ITS REPAIR. THE CLAIM IS TRUE, AND IT IS
   STRONGER THAN THE WORKER STATED, BECAUSE IT IS AN ENFORCED INVARIANT.
=====================================================================
I verified the claim against the HOST CONTRACT, not against the test.

The worker justified the empty body by ONE event ("session.updated carries
surface opencode-catch-all-sse"). That would be a coincidence about one row.
It is not: internal/runtime/lifecycle.go:541-565 REFUSES a contract in which an
OpenCode named-output row is anything other than a blocking gate consultation,
and refuses a catch-all/SSE row that is anything other than a non-blocking
observation. So on OpenCode, observation and catch-all SSE are the same set BY
VALIDATION. FaultContinuation keys on the SEMANTIC while the safety argument is
about the SURFACE, and that gap is closed by this contract rule rather than by
the current row list. No OpenCode observation can reach a named callback.

So the question my axis had to answer - does a failed observation now say
something different from a successful one on a surface that DOES read stdout -
is answered NO, and structurally. The gate arm stays pinned at the canonical
object, which I measured above.

MY OWN MUTATION: I disabled the observation arm. RED in three places, including
the repaired built-binary proof TestWithheldOpenCodeEventIsNotAdmittedByBuiltCLI.
Restored; tree clean. The repaired assertion is load-bearing, not weakened.

=====================================================================
3. THE PANIC PROOF. VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE.
=====================================================================
Both recover sites are exercised through cobra's own seams and no shipped branch
exists for either:
- TestAPanicInTheWorkGoroutineIsAFaultAndNeverABlock injects a panicking reader
  through cmd.SetIn. It asserts ExitContinue, code 0, an explicit NotEqual(2)
  with the reason spelled out ("exit 2 is a BLOCK on Claude Code"), the OpenCode
  continue bytes, "panicked" on stderr, and one durable record with
  outcomeClass "fault" and hostExit "continue".
- TestAPanicBeforeTheWorkStartsIsAFaultAndNeverACrash reaches the main-path
  recover through cmd.SetContext(nil) and asserts the fail-open outcome with
  Claude's empty continue bytes.
The deferred recover is installed FIRST in lifecycleOutcome, above the coordinate
and environment reads, and its position is pinned structurally.

=====================================================================
4. THE A2 SUPERSESSION AND ITS TRUTH SURFACES. SHIPPED TEXT NOW MATCHES SHIPPED
   BEHAVIOUR ON THE USER-FACING SURFACE. ONE MAINTAINER SURFACE STILL DOES NOT.
=====================================================================
The CHANGELOG entry is now correct AND it separates the two OpenCode surfaces in
a user's terms: the events a plugin callback waits on get the carry-on bytes; the
event stream is only watched, nothing there reads stdout, "and a failure on it
writes nothing, which is what a success on it writes". That is exactly what I
measured. It also warns a person debugging an integration that these bytes say
only "do not stop on our account" and that the invocation is recorded as a fault.
The past-tense description of the old plugin behaviour is honest.
The supersession in the code (hostexit package doc, "THE RULE THIS REPLACES") is
clear and names the reopening risk.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG: aura-plugins-hu5yhh below. See it.

=====================================================================
5. THE ORPHAN COUNT. THE OPERATOR TEXT IS CORRECT AND I ACCEPT THE DEVIATION.
=====================================================================
Run against a clean store, the command prints the number AND, on the same code
path at zero, the note. All three required claims are present in the operator's
own terms - what an orphan is, that it is expected and reclaimable rather than
damage WITH THE REASON (blob before journal row, because a spare blob is
reclaimable while a row naming an absent blob could not be repaired), and what a
large number means (not corruption; repeated abandonment; investigate the store
contention). The note travels in the JSON too, which is the right call: a
dashboard that renders the number alone is precisely how the misreading happens.
The `--help` Long text says the same three things and is pinned byte-for-byte.
So the number does not teach the false lesson, and an operator is not sent to
hunt for the one state this slice proves cannot exist.

THE DEVIATION (a sibling subcommand instead of a footer on `list`): ACCEPTED, and
I would have refused the alternative. The leaf required "reports zero on a clean
store", so the line cannot be conditional, and an unconditional footer would have
forced a regeneration of the byte-identical `list` golden - weakening the
invariant to add a decoration. The sibling appears in `hook lifecycle --help`,
which is itself pinned. Do NOT ask for it on `list`.
The correctness trap the worker recorded (a count taken without a projection
rebuild reports EVERY blob as an orphan - the most alarming wrong number this
store can produce) is real and is handled by rebuilding first, exactly as `list`
does.

=====================================================================
6. THE PRODUCTION DEADLINE TIER DID NOT MOVE. VERIFIED AT THE SOURCE.
=====================================================================
internal/timeouts/profile.go: ProductionProfile() = New(Production, 500ms, 1s,
2s, 5s, 30s). HookInvocation is 5 s, below the 10 s Claude budget with the stated
headroom, and the pin still asserts the PRODUCTION value. The tier is an
in-process parameter with no environment variable and no flag; the user-safety
reason for that refusal is now AT the declaration, in both directions
(shortening stops proving the host's budget; lengthening can freeze the user's
own session, measured at about 31 s against a 10 s budget).

=====================================================================
FINDINGS (all MINOR; all are truth surfaces, none changes behaviour)
=====================================================================
aura-plugins-hu5yhh  three shipped comments (hostexit.go:28-31, hostexit.go:44-47,
  hook_lifecycle.go:270-273) say IN THE PRESENT TENSE that an empty body makes the
  generated OpenCode plugin throw. The plugin generated by THIS commit does not:
  it logs "did not evaluate" and continues, and a belt test proves it under Bun.
  The permanent reason is written at none of the three sites: pasture cannot know
  WHICH plugin is installed, and an ALREADY-INSTALLED older one still throws. As
  written, a reader who checks the claim finds it false and may conclude the belt
  removed the hazard, which would reintroduce the round-1 BLOCKER for every user
  who has not regenerated their plugin. The observation arm in nativeresponse.go
  already words this correctly and is the model to copy.

aura-plugins-4u265z  an operator who sets PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 and faults on
  an UNEVIDENCED row gets exit 0 and a diagnostic whose fix clause tells them to
  set PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 - the action they already took - with no
  sentence saying why it did not take effect here. Measured on claude-code
  PreCompact / Notification / PostToolUse and codex PreToolUse. The behaviour is
  correct (D9), only the telling is not. The OpenCode arm of the same diagnostic
  already does this correctly and is the precedent inside this slice.

aura-plugins-k8mmor  `pasture hook lifecycle orphans` is a NEW operator command
  and the CHANGELOG never mentions it (no "Added" heading in Unreleased). The
  release notes are the surface where an operator learns a command exists - this
  repository uses them that way for `pasture queue concurrency` in 0.0.8 - so the
  number this round spent itself making safe to read is reachable only by someone
  who already knows the word.

=====================================================================
NOTES FOR THE RECORD
=====================================================================
- The handover-count distinction is preserved: 11 Claude + 8 Codex + 0 OpenCode =
  19 DEMOTED rows, and the manifest-versus-runtime DIVERGENCE is 20 rows. Two
  different questions. I did not conflate them and neither does the tree.
- The exit condition is not met by this round: 3 MINOR outstanding, so a
  fix-free 0/0/0 round is still required after they are fixed.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ROUND-8 VERDICT, host-contract truth and end-user behaviour axis (review aura-plugins-x5njhq).
SHA 020d20395b2e6bf57798555e3ab4e5bfd5ea86be. Everything below was measured on a BUILT BINARY of
that SHA, in an archive copy outside the worktree. The copy and both binaries are deleted.

TALLY: 0 BLOCKER, 0 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR.
  MINOR aura-plugins-8qm2d8 - the declared-mode guard walks 11 of 87 rows while its doc says it
  walks every row of every shipped profile.
VOTE: REVISE.

1. THE alm8al FIX LANDED. Measured with PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 and a directory as --db:
   claude-code PreCompact  -> exit 0, empty stdout, "declared failure mode exit-2-blocks,
     effective failure mode report-and-continue", and the EVIDENCE sentence WITH its action
     ("add the host documentation or a committed capture showing the host refuses on that exit code").
   codex PreToolUse        -> exit 0, stdout {"continue":true}, "declared failure mode
     strict-output-exit-2-blocks, effective failure mode report-and-continue", same evidence
     sentence with its action.
   claude-code PostToolUse -> exit 0, the MODE sentence, which is true of an observation.
   claude-code Notification-> exit 0, the MODE sentence. I built the payload by hand because no
     Notification fixture exists; the row is declared observe (lifecycle_profiles.go), and the
     diagnostic matched.
   claude-code PreToolUse  -> exit 2, cited by the Claude hooks reference, unchanged.
   MUTATION I RAN MYSELF: key the branch on fault.Mode again. The built-binary test turned RED on
   both declared-blocking rows, with the failure text naming the missing evidence sentence. The
   pin is on the delivery, not on a hand-built Fault. The three new tests plus
   ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/runtime/... ./internal/handlers/... are green.

   THE PHASE LINE, JUDGED AS A TRUTH CLAIM PER READER: "declared failure mode exit-2-blocks,
   effective failure mode report-and-continue" is ACCEPTED. Naming two modes does not confuse the
   operator, because the phase line is not where the operator acts: Impact says the host continues
   and Fix says what to do, and both name ONE outcome. The second mode is what makes the first one
   safe to print: without it a reader who saw only "exit-2-blocks" would expect a refusal that did
   not happen. The pair is the smallest text that is true. The register is already
   maintainer-facing (Where names an internal function), so "add the host documentation or a
   committed capture" does not imply an operator knob that does not exist; the word "committed"
   names the channel.

2. THE FAIL-OPEN GUARANTEE STILL HOLDS, re-measured on every harness and BOTH policy skews
   (default, and PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1), all exit 0 with the stderr diagnostic:
     claude-code gate + observation  -> EMPTY stdout
     codex gate                      -> {"continue":true}
     codex observation               -> {}
     opencode named gate             -> {"decision":"proceed"}
     opencode observation            -> NOTHING
   --format json does not move the fault text onto stdout, which is right: stdout is the host
   channel and a JSON diagnostic there would corrupt the continue bytes.

3. THE SIXTH PRESENT-TENSE CLAIM. Correcting it was right and deleting it would have been worse.
   The reason given is TRUE: the generated plugin invokes the binary with harness, event and HOST
   version only (internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go), so nothing in an invocation identifies the
   installed plugin, and an older installed plugin runs JSON.parse("") on a named callback. The
   claim is now past tense with a permanent reason at all four surviving sites
   (hostexit.go package doc, hostexit_test.go x2, nativeresponse_test.go) plus
   cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go. Deleting it would leave the continue-bytes rule with no stated
   cause, which is the exact door TestTheDocumentedFaultRuleCannotBeSilentlyReverted exists to
   shut.

4. THE PRODUCTION TIER DID NOT MOVE. internal/timeouts/profile.go ProductionProfile is
   500ms/1s/2s/5s/30s. HookInvocation is 5s against the 10s Claude budget. No timeouts file is in
   the round-7 or round-8 diff.

5. THE JUDGEMENT I WAS ASKED TO RULE ON - the unpinned CHANGELOG entry: CONFIRMED, the worker was
   right. A release note is dated history, not a contract surface. The standing constraint is about
   a pin that LOOSENS; no pin was added, so it does not apply, and adding a prose pin to a note
   that will never be edited again would create the loosening pin the constraint warns about. Both
   truth claims of the entry are proven where the operator meets them: the per-row reason and its
   action by the built-binary test, and "no exit code changed" by the exit column of the same test
   (exit 2 still on the cited Claude gate). The residual risk is a stale note, not a wrong operator
   action, because the text the operator reads is stderr, and that IS pinned.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-10 ROUND 8, host-contract axis: REVISE 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR. Review task aura-plugins-x5njhq; finding aura-plugins-8qm2d8.
THE alm8al FIX LANDED, proven on a binary the reviewer BUILT ITSELF. All five rows measured with PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1: claude-code PreCompact and codex PreToolUse now read the EVIDENCE sentence with its action at exit 0; PostToolUse and Notification read the mode sentence and are correct; claude-code PreToolUse still exits 2. It RE-RAN THE ORIGINAL MUTATION ITSELF - keying the branch on fault.Mode again - and the built-binary test turns RED on both declared-blocking rows.
FAIL-OPEN HOLDS on all three harnesses and BOTH policy skews, and --format json does not move the diagnostic onto stdout. PRODUCTION TIER UNCHANGED at 500ms/1s/2s/5s/30s.
THE SIXTH CLAIM: correcting rather than deleting was right, and the reason is TRUE - the generated plugin passes only harness, event and HOST version, so NOTHING IDENTIFIES THE INSTALLED PLUGIN, and an older installed one still runs JSON.parse("").
RULING ON THE UNPINNED CHANGELOG ENTRY: CONFIRMED ACCEPTABLE, and the reasoning is better than the question. A RELEASE NOTE IS DATED HISTORY, NOT A CONTRACT SURFACE. The standing constraint governs a pin that LOOSENS, and NO PIN WAS ADDED - so adding one would CREATE the loosening pin the rule warns about. Both truth claims of the entry are proven where the operator MEETS them: the per-row reason and its action by the new built-binary test, and "no exit code changed" by that test's exit column. The residual risk is a STALE NOTE, not a wrong operator action, because the text the operator reads is stderr and STDERR IS PINNED.

THE ONE FINDING, 8qm2d8 MINOR, is the THIRD INSTANCE IN THIS SLICE OF ONE PATTERN, and I have promoted it to a standing constraint in IMPL_PLAN section 6.
TestEveryDeclaredRowDiffersFromItsEffectiveModeOnlyByTheEvidenceRule DOCUMENTS that it "walks every row of every shipped profile". It walks A HAND-WRITTEN LIST OF 11 EVENT NAMES against 87 DECLARED ROWS (30 Claude, 10 Codex, 47 OpenCode), and its size assertion is checked > 8, so it pins the SMALL number.
MEASURED: the reviewer gave an UNLISTED declared blocking gate (ClaudeEventPermissionRequest) declaredFailure = FailureObserveOnly. EVERY TEST STAYED GREEN, including that one - and the built binary then told the operator "its declared failure mode observe-only does not refuse through a process exit code", WHICH IS THE EXACT UNTRUTH alm8al REMOVED. The same mutation on a LISTED row turns it RED.
No shipped row is wrong today, so there is no user harm now; the finding is the FALSE COVERAGE CLAIM.
THE PATTERN, now a constraint: A GUARD THAT CLAIMS EXHAUSTIVE COVERAGE MUST DERIVE ITS POPULATION, NEVER HAND-LIST IT. Three instances in S0 alone - the A16 guard blind to all 73 Wave-1 events; the placement guard globbing two packages while claiming the repository and leaving this slice's own seam green; and now this one. THE MUTATION THAT DETECTS IT: apply the defect to a row the list does NOT name.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-10 ROUND 8, architecture axis: REVISE 0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 3 MINOR. Review task aura-plugins-pii5s8; BLOCKER group we90l2 closed empty.
GATES, ALL FOUR RUN FROM INSIDE AN ARCHIVE COPY AND EACH CHECKED TO HAVE DONE WORK: build RAN and passed; go test -race RAN with 71 packages ok and 9 no-test-files, no FAIL, no data race; make generate RAN, listed generated files and go generate lines with no missing target, and git status was EMPTY so no drift; nix flake check RAN and passed. Copies deleted, worktree untouched. It also noted the shared scratchpad holds OTHER AGENTS' files and it removed only its own - correct behaviour.

THE IMPORTANT yg6kwq IS THE SAME FINDING THE HOST-CONTRACT AXIS RAISED AS 8qm2d8, REACHED INDEPENDENTLY FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION. That is the strongest signal available and it is the second time this round two axes converged. Its measurement differs and is worth keeping: it gave an uncovered CLAUDE row (FileChanged) the OpenCode observe-only arm and go test over the WHOLE REPOSITORY stayed GREEN.
IT ALSO STATED AN HONEST MITIGATION THAT THE OTHER AXIS DID NOT: the 11 hand-listed rows DO cover all six construction paths, so a shared-constructor mutation is still caught. What escapes is EXACTLY the per-row divergence the test claims to catch. That distinction matters for judging severity and it was volunteered rather than omitted.

1egpul MINOR IS A FORWARD HAZARD FOR S3 AND I HAVE ALREADY CARRIED IT THERE. The exit-contract test is still named TestLifecycleHookExitFollowsTheDeclaredFailureMode and two comments say the DECLARED mode decides the exit - the exact rule this round forbids. MEASURED: keying the exit table on DeclaredMode leaves the suite GREEN, because Evidence.IsPresent() makes the two expressions EQUIVALENT for every row that exists today. SO THE INVARIANT 'only the effective mode reaches an exit status' IS ACCIDENTAL AT THIS SHA, NOT STRUCTURAL. S3 adds the evidence-bound capability derivation, a second consumer of the same distinction, so leaf S3-L7 aura-plugins-llt3k5 now carries the hazard and must make the invariant structural or say why it cannot be.
biq01u MINOR: the durable fault record writes ONE mode, so on the built binary a DEMOTED GATE and a DECLARED OBSERVATION are BYTE-IDENTICAL in every failure field of lifecycle-faults.jsonl. The stderr text tells them apart, so no operator action is lost - but the MAINTAINER ARTEFACT THAT OUTLIVES THE PROCESS does not.
g8nbip MINOR: a refusal names one field while six conditions can cause it, and 'declared' is now a specific field name.

WHAT IT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: the alm8al acceptance criterion IS DISCHARGED on a binary it built itself; the declared/effective split is correct at ALL EIGHT construction sites and a zero declaration CANNOT slip through - its mutation removing declaredFailure made newLifecycleContract REFUSE NAMING THE ROW, and removing DeclaredMode from the undeclared-event fallback turned two built-binary tests RED with a loud exit 1, NEVER a silent exit 0; the fault/decision split is intact; the placement guard is sound, walking over 300 of 470 non-test Go files with two justified exemptions each proven reached, skipping .git, testdata, node_modules and a separate Go module.
IT RECORDED ONE NON-FINDING WORTH KEEPING: the placement guard is a SUBSTRING match, so a doc comment elsewhere merely NAMING ReclaimableCount would turn it RED with a message asserting that file counts orphans. None exists today.

author: David Huu Pham
text: VOTE: REVISE - 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR (aura-plugins-383qcu). SHA 020d203. The central proof was re-run on BOTH sides by this axis and holds. The one MINOR is on the guard round 7 added, not on the fix it protects.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
S0 REVIEW ROUND 8, AXIS C (deliverability, testability, traceability) - VOTE: REVISE
SHA 020d20395b2e6bf57798555e3ab4e5bfd5ea86be, three commits over fa4522a.
TALLY: 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR. NOT the fix-free round.
Review task aura-plugins-84u2b2. Severity groups: BLOCKER aura-plugins-ryvurz (CLOSED, empty),
IMPORTANT aura-plugins-xyfvhx (CLOSED, empty), MINOR aura-plugins-8s3km5 (one finding,
aura-plugins-383qcu). Read-only round: no gate was run by this axis; two archive copies, both deleted.

=====================================================================
1. THE CENTRAL MUTATION, RE-RUN BY ME ON BOTH SIDES. THE FIX IS AT THE DELIVERY.
=====================================================================
panic("MUTATION: branch 1 reached") inside the evidence arm of failClosedAdvice, the same arm on
both sides (fault.DeclaredMode.BlocksByExitCode() at 020d203, fault.Mode.BlocksByExitCode() at
fa4522a), then the WHOLE ./cmd/pasture package, which is where the built-binary suite lives:
  020d203 + panic   FAIL after 193 s. Two named rows, claude-code PreCompact and codex PreToolUse,
                    and the stack is the DELIVERY: main.lifecycleOutcome -> main.lifecycleFault ->
                    hostexit.ForFault -> hostexit.faultDiagnostic, through the real process.
                    TestTheDiagnosticSeparatesTheDeclaredModeFromTheEffectiveOne fails too.
  fa4522a + panic   ok after 192 s. GREEN. The arm was dead at the SHA this round inherited.
  020d203 clean     ok after 202 s.
This is the third time the slice had to prove a fix reaches the delivery. It does. The dead branch
is alive, and the proof is a suite that changes colour, not a sentence in a report.

=====================================================================
2. THE MUTATIONS: REAL AND PERFORMABLE. NINE RE-PERFORMED, NOT READ.
=====================================================================
Each was applied to an archive copy, run, and reverted. RED unless stated.
 1 panic in branch 1                                RED at 020d203, GREEN at fa4522a (above).
 2 key the arm on the effective mode again          RED through the BUILT BINARY on both declared
                                                    blocking rows, and RED in the hostexit unit.
 3 declaredFailureArm consults the evidence         RED at the phase-line pin AND at the profile walk.
 4 remove the ", effective failure mode" clause     RED.
 5 drop !DeclaredMode.IsValid() from ForFault       RED on both new refusal cases.
 6 a declared mode that is not the harness arm      RED at the profile walk and the phase line.
 7 name ReclaimableCount in nativeresponse          RED naming the file.
 8 narrow the walk root to one package              RED.
 9 move one exemption path                          RED.
Not re-performed, and why: the two "GREEN under the two-package version" halves need the OLD guard
restored, and round 6 measured both GREEN independently; naming the count in lifecycle_identity.go
and in the dispatch handler is the same mechanism as 7, already shown.
A METHOD WARNING FOR LATER ROUNDS, because it nearly cost me two false GREENs: a -run pattern
passed through a shell variable can keep its literal quotes, and Go then silently runs NO test and
reports ok. Two of my runs said ok with "[no tests to run]". A mutation whose run names no test has
not been performed. I re-ran all four with the pattern quoted correctly.

=====================================================================
3. PIN DIRECTION: NOTHING LOOSENED
=====================================================================
Five assertion lines were removed and every one has a stronger replacement, all in the orphans
guard: Glob NoError -> WalkDir NoError with a message; NotEmpty(sources) -> Greater(walked, 300);
per-file ReadFile NoError -> the walk error; Greater(walked, 10) -> Greater(walked, 300);
Equal(1, exempted) -> a reached check on EACH of two exemption paths. Scope went from two packages
to the repository. ForFault gained a refusal (an unset or invalid DeclaredMode) and the refusal
table gained the two matching cases. The hostexit cell table gained DeclaredMode = the cell mode,
which is neutral for a table that exercises the exit path. The uncited subtest now builds the shape
production really builds instead of one production cannot construct, which is a strengthening.
No narrowing this round. No pin was loosened.

=====================================================================
4. THE ONE DELIBERATE NON-PIN: THE CHANGELOG. THE JUDGEMENT STANDS. I OVERTURN NOTHING.
=====================================================================
I did not reason from the earlier precedent. I tested each truth claim of the entry with my own
mutation and required the BUILT BINARY to change colour.
  "No exit code changed."      MUTATION: blocks := FailClosed && DeclaredMode.BlocksByExitCode(),
                               which makes an uncited declared gate exit 2 under the opt-in. RED on
                               both declared blocking rows of the built-binary test, and RED on two
                               cells of the hostexit table. The claim is pinned by behaviour.
  "A non-blocking event reads the same sentence as before."
                               MUTATION: reword the mode sentence. RED at the built-binary
                               PostToolUse case and at the hostexit unit subtest. Pinned.
  "Such an event now reads that it carries no host evidence ... would make it able to block."
                               Pinned by the panic mutation above, which is RED only because the
                               real binary prints that sentence.
  "The diagnostic also names the declared mode and the effective mode separately."
                               Pinned by mutation 4.
So the entry states nothing that a green suite would let a person write falsely. The worker's
reasoning is sound on its own terms too: a golden on release-note prose has no reader who can act
on its failure except by editing the golden, and this slice has already produced one pin that
protected the copies and not the delivery. RULING: no prose pin. Not a finding.
ONE NOTE, and it is the gap ALREADY FILED as aura-plugins-u1n47j, not a new one: nothing pins the
EXISTENCE of the entry. That is the class gap, and it belongs before S1 and S3 add commands.
A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH RECORDING SO NOBODY RE-MEASURES IT: swapping the exit table to the declared
mode while KEEPING the evidence conjunct leaves every suite green. That is correct and is not a
finding: the conjunct already excludes every uncited row, so the two readings are the same value on
every row production can build. The mutation that MOVES an exit code is the one above, and it is RED.

=====================================================================
5. TRACEABILITY: FOUR FINDINGS, THREE COMMITS, EACH DISCHARGED BY IDENTIFIABLE WORK
=====================================================================
alm8al  -> 32650a5. 3cel64 and orikqk (one site) -> 262063e. x4bcdp -> 020d203.
k2xmgx  -> all three commit bodies, which is the finding itself.
Each commit body names its own mutations and its own ownership. Nothing is discharged by a commit
that does not name it.

=====================================================================
6. THE TWO STANDING CHECKS THAT SILENTLY REGRESS
=====================================================================
COMMENTS, NOT DESCRIPTIONS ALONE. Two of the five findings carry an instruction that exists ONLY in
a comment, and both were honoured to the letter.
  alm8al comment: "A BUILT-BINARY ASSERTION ON claude-code PreCompact OR codex PreToolUse THAT
  READS THE EVIDENCE SENTENCE." Delivered on BOTH rows, and I proved the assertion able to fail
  rather than reading it. The same comment made the PROSE correction part of the finding: the
  claim "all four are declared report-and-continue" is corrected in the round-7 commit body and in
  the test comment at hostexit_test.go, both checked.
  x4bcdp comment: "go repo-wide, take the two exemptions." Delivered exactly, exemptions named by
  PATH, each with its own reached check.
OWNERSHIP. Eight files were touched and ALL EIGHT are named in a commit Ownership paragraph.
Commit 1 declares internal/runtime/lifecycle.go and lifecycle_profiles.go as outside the ROUND-7
LEAF list, with the reason. I checked the claim rather than the ruling: the declared mode is the
value of a profile ROW, the row is built by the four mapping constructors in lifecycle_profiles.go
and validated in lifecycle.go, and there is no other place the correct value exists. So the
widening is necessary, not incidental. Both files are inside the SLICE-level owned set (the
plan-time "modify" list), so the slice statement did not widen and the same-commit rule was met by
declaration. There is one production caller of ForFault and three production
LifecycleFailurePolicy literals; all four set the new field, so the new refusal cannot fire in
production.

=====================================================================
7. THE SIXTH-SITE FIX: VERIFIED BY MY OWN SEARCH, AND IT IS A CORRECTION
=====================================================================
I did not accept the exhaustive-search claim. Repository-wide, case-insensitive, all file types:
29 files mention a throw. Every prose site about the generated plugin and an EMPTY BODY is now past
tense about this build and present tense only about an ALREADY-INSTALLED OLDER PLUGIN, which is
true: hostexit.go:32 and :56, hostexit_test.go:48 and :611, nativeresponse_test.go:120,
hook_lifecycle.go:279. The other hits are the OpenCode plugin source, the enum name, or
runtime/lifecycle.go:213, which is about a NON-ZERO EXIT and is a different subject and true.
The repair is a CORRECTION, not a deletion: every site keeps the permanent reason, that pasture
cannot know which plugin is installed. Deleting the sentence would have removed the justification
of the guard, which is the worse repair, and the guard would then read as stale to the next person.

=====================================================================
8. THE FINDING
=====================================================================
MINOR aura-plugins-383qcu. The guard round 7 ADDED,
TestEveryDeclaredRowDiffersFromItsEffectiveModeOnlyByTheEvidenceRule, says it "walks every row of
every shipped profile" and walks a hand list of 11 of the 87 shipped rows (30 Claude, 10 Codex, 47
OpenCode). It is the only guard on the new declared mode, and a wrong declared mode is invisible to
every behaviour and visible only to an operator.
MEASURED ON THE BUILT BINARY, both sides, on claude-code Elicitation, a declared blocking uncited
gate that the list does NOT hold: unmutated it reads the TRUE evidence sentence with its action;
with that ONE row given a declared mode of observe-only it reads "its declared failure mode
observe-only does not refuse through a process exit code" - alm8al reopened, word for word - and
the guard stays GREEN. On claude-code PermissionRequest the same wrong value left the WHOLE
REPOSITORY green: 72 packages, 0 FAIL. Control: the same wrong value on the Claude ARM turns the
guard RED, so it works inside its list only.
It is cheap: ClaudeLifecycleEvents(), CodexLifecycleEvents() and OpenCodeLifecycleEvents() are
already exported and return the whole catalogue, so the exhaustive walk needs no new API and stays
at the same public boundary. Wave 1 is where it bites - S4, S5 and S6 add harness rows, and those
rows are the ones outside the eleven.
SHAPE: this is x4bcdp (a guard scoped too narrowly) and 3cel64 (a completeness claim untrue at the
SHA that makes it) reproduced inside the guard that repaired them.

=====================================================================
9. THE DECISION
=====================================================================
REVISE, on one MINOR that is on the GUARD and not on the fix. The alm8al repair itself is delivered,
measured on both sides, and I could not shake it with five mutations. If the MINOR is fixed with the
mutation named on it, this axis expects a fix-free round.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
S0 ROUND 9 - WORKER REPORT (worker-s0-fix6). Final SHA 57311425c9d7863b82a1271fd2e14e5bb3f46c48.
Three commits: 44476e2, 865d61d, 5731142. Branch slice/rp2tju-s0-failure-modes.

=====================================================================
0. THE INHERITED SHA WAS GATED FIRST, AND IT WAS GREEN
=====================================================================
020d20395b2e6bf57798555e3ab4e5bfd5ea86be, on an archive copy (git archive + git init +
remote origin + initial commit), every gate run FROM INSIDE the copy.
- go build ./...            : exit 0, dev shell named (Go go1.26.3).
- go test -race -count=1 ./...: 72 packages, all "ok", 0 FAIL. THE GATE NAMED ITS PACKAGES,
  so it ran; cmd/pasture took 263.7 s.
- make generate             : NAMED ITS TARGETS (opencode, claudecode "wrote 36 generated
  asset(s), removed 0 stale", codex, metamodel), then git status --porcelain was EMPTY.
- nix flake check --no-build: cgo-disabled-build, race and installer all green.
So the branch I resumed was not red, and nothing I report below is inherited damage.

=====================================================================
1. THE GUARD NOW DERIVES ITS POPULATION (8qm2d8 / yg6kwq / 383qcu - ONE DEFECT, THREE AXES)
=====================================================================
FIX. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go.
everyShippedLifecycleRow() derives the rows from the ALREADY EXPORTED catalogs -
ClaudeLifecycleEvents(), CodexLifecycleEvents(), OpenCodeLifecycleEvents() - and takes the
native name from each event. No new API, same public boundary. The walk asks the public
lookup for EVERY derived row and grants NO EXEMPTION: a derived row the lookup does not
declare is a failure, not a skip.
SIZE ASSERTION. checked > 8 is gone. Two assertions replace it: checked == len(rows), and a
FLOOR of 87, the number only the full set reaches (30 Claude, 10 Codex, 47 OpenCode). The
floor is what a shrunken catalog fails; the equality is what a skipped row fails.
PROSE. The doc comment now says the population comes from the catalogs, so the coverage it
claims is the coverage it has. The test name is kept because it is now TRUE. The commit body
states the 11-of-87 defect and the measurement, so no commit-message claim overstates.

MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, EACH RUN NAMED ITS TEST:
- BEFORE, on an archive copy of the INHERITED SHA, with the old hand list in place:
  claude-code Elicitation (an unlisted declared blocking uncited gate) given
  declaredFailure = FailureObserveOnly ->
  "--- PASS: TestEveryDeclaredRowDiffersFromItsEffectiveModeOnlyByTheEvidenceRule (0.00s)
   ok github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/cmd/pasture 0.643s". GREEN. The reviewers' measurement
  reproduces exactly.
- AFTER, on my tree, the SAME mutation ->
  "--- FAIL ... claude-code Elicitation runs as something other than it declares, and the
   ONLY rule allowed to do that is the failure-evidence rule, which acts on an exit-code arm".
  RED, and it NAMES THE ROW.
- SECOND UNLISTED ROW: claude-code PermissionRequest, same mutation -> RED, names
  "claude-code PermissionRequest".
- CONTROL, LISTED ROW: claude-code PreCompact, same mutation -> RED, names
  "claude-code PreCompact". The rows the old list held are still covered.
- SIZE MUTATION: ClaudeLifecycleEvents() cut to one row (loop bound ClaudeEventSetup) -> RED,
  although every row it still returns is correct. The floor is load-bearing.
All five runs printed "=== RUN Test..." and a "--- FAIL"/"--- PASS" line for that test. None
printed "no tests to run".
WHY IT MATTERS IN WAVE 1: the derived walk covers S4/S5/S6 rows the day they are added, with
no test edit.

=====================================================================
2. THE EXIT CONTRACT NOW TEACHES THE RULE THAT HOLDS (1egpul)
=====================================================================
TestLifecycleHookExitFollowsTheDeclaredFailureMode is renamed
TestLifecycleHookExitFollowsTheEffectiveFailureMode. Its header comment now says the
EFFECTIVE mode decides, and adds WHY: the failure-evidence rule demotes an uncited blocking
row before any exit decision, so a row can declare the blocking exit code and still exit 0.
The two comments (the error-category subtest and its assertion message) now say EFFECTIVE.
SCOPE HELD. I did NOT attempt the structural half. The invariant is accidental at this SHA
because Evidence.IsPresent() makes the two expressions equivalent for every row that exists,
and the second consumer arrives on the S3 leaf. Nothing here widens toward it.

=====================================================================
3. THE DURABLE RECORD SEPARATES THE TWO MODES (biq01u)
=====================================================================
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go writes declaredFailureMode beside failureMode, with a comment
saying which is which and why both are kept.
NEW PIN: TestTheFaultRecordTellsADemotedGateFromADeclaredObservation runs the BUILT BINARY on
claude-code PreCompact (a demoted gate) and PostToolUse (a declared observation) against the
same real storage fault, and asserts (a) the two records carry the SAME failureMode, which is
the reason the field alone cannot separate them, and (b) declaredFailureMode is
"exit-2-blocks" for the first and "report-and-continue" for the second.
MUTATION-RED: writing failure.Mode into declaredFailureMode ->
"--- FAIL: TestTheFaultRecordTellsADemotedGateFromADeclaredObservation ... expected
"exit-2-blocks", actual "report-and-continue"". The run named the test.
The member is always populated: both undeclared-event literals in hook_lifecycle.go already
set DeclaredMode, so no record can carry an empty declaration.

=====================================================================
4. THE REFUSAL NAMES WHAT WAS NOT USABLE (g8nbip)
=====================================================================

text:

MEASURED: go doc ForFault prints only the signature; go doc Fault.UnusableInputs prints the fault table, the six refusal reasons and the Deny rule, running into the UnusableInputs text mid-sentence. hostexit is the sole exit authority and that block is the only normative statement of the fault table in the tree. No gate sees it. Fix is one blank comment line, plus a doc-attachment assertion so it cannot come back.
- MINOR aura-plugins-ygdd3u — the derived guard require.Equal(len(rows), checked) cannot fail: checked++ is unconditional and the only abort above it is require.True, which ends the test first. PROVED by making one row unreachable through the public lookup: the walk turned RED at the require.True and the equality never spoke, in the exact case its message describes. The floor of 87 is the only size guard.
- MINOR aura-plugins-epe7df — Fault.UnusableInputs returns operator English as untyped strings from the core exit type; suggest a typed FaultInput with Explain().
- MINOR aura-plugins-gqd1ay — the unclassifiable-fault message joins the list with the same "; " that separates the clauses after it, so a two-input list has no visible end; the only test covers the one-item case.

THE ROUND-9 FIX IS REAL AND I CONFIRMED IT INDEPENDENTLY. The derivation is sound at the data-model level: newLifecycleContract refuses a profile whose event count and mapping count differ, a repeated event value, or a repeated native name, so the catalog IS the profile population and no shipped row can sit outside it. Mutations of my own: a wrong declared mode on claude-code WorktreeCreate and on opencode tool.definition — neither in the old hand list — both turn the walk RED naming the row; deleting the Codex arm from the derived population turns it RED at the floor; a CONSISTENT wrong pair (both modes wrong) is invisible to this guard by design but is caught by the contract validator on OpenCode and by TestPinnedLifecycleContractsMatchStrictFixture on Claude, so that door is shut; the hostexit arm mutation and the declaredFailureMode record mutation both turn RED as their comments claim.

NO BEHAVIOUR MOVED beyond leaf items 2 to 4. Four files only. The 5 s HookInvocation tier and its ordering invariants are untouched, ForFault keeps its signature and the same six refusal conditions, and its one production call site is unchanged.

Inherited SHA 5731142. FINAL SHA e0c12c7acfa8701aed27219543e6fbcb70b94353.
Four commits: 476fae1, 808e0ec, 06369ae, e0c12c7. Each carries an Ownership paragraph.
Files touched, all owned exclusively by this slice and no others:
internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit.go, internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit_test.go,
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go, cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go.

=====================================================================
GATE OF THE INHERITED SHA 5731142 - run from INSIDE an archive copy
=====================================================================
The copy was made with git archive + git init + git remote add origin + an initial
commit, as required. Every command below was run after cd into the copy, and each
one is confirmed to have REALLY RUN, not to have passed by naming nothing.

build   ACTUALLY RAN, PASS. The dev shell printed "Pasture dev shell (Go go1.26.3)".
        No "directory prefix . does not contain main module".
test    ACTUALLY RAN, PASS. go test -race -count=1 ./... exit 0.
        72 packages reported ok, 0 FAIL lines. Packages were NAMED, including
        cmd/pasture and internal/lifecycle/hostexit. A run that named no package
        would not have produced 72 ok lines.
generate ACTUALLY RAN. make generate NAMED ITS TARGETS and wrote assets
        ("claudecode-assets: wrote 36 generated asset(s), removed 0 stale",

        "No rule to make target". git status afterwards was CLEAN: no drift.
flake   ACTUALLY RAN, PASS. cgo-disabled-build, installer and race all green.

VERDICT ON THE INHERITED SHA: green on all four gates. The round-10 findings are
truth and assertion defects, not gate failures, which matches three consecutive
rounds with no BLOCKER.

=====================================================================
ITEM 1 - THE DOC-ATTACHMENT DEFECT (yiudjj on axis A, okb19k on axis B)
=====================================================================
CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading the diff.

go doc BEFORE, on the inherited SHA:
  $ go doc ./internal/lifecycle/hostexit ForFault
  func ForFault(fault Fault) (Outcome, bool)
  [THE SIGNATURE AND NOTHING ELSE - no doc line at all]

  $ go doc ./internal/lifecycle/hostexit Fault.UnusableInputs
  func (f Fault) UnusableInputs() []string
      ForFault maps an internal fault to the Outcome the host receives.
      The table is small and total:
        - fail-open, any mode: continue, with the host's CONTINUE BYTES ...
        - fail-closed, a mode that blocks by exit code, WITH evidence: block ...
        - fail-closed, anything else: continue, exactly as fail-open.
      The second result is false when there is nothing to map: ... A false result
      is a programming error at the call site, never a host outcome, so the caller
      must treat it as one and must not fall through to a silent exit 0.
      ForFault never encodes a policy Deny. A Deny is an evaluated answer and goes
      through ForDecision, where neither the fault policy nor missing evidence can
      weaken it. UnusableInputs names EVERY member of the fault that ForFault
      cannot use, ...
  [the fault table, the six refusal reasons and the Deny rule, running into the
   UnusableInputs text MID-SENTENCE, exactly as both reviewers measured]

go doc AFTER, on the final SHA: each symbol prints its own text and nothing else.
ForFault carries the whole table, the six refusal conditions, the silent-exit-0
warning and the Deny rule. Fault.UnusableInputs carries only its own two
paragraphs plus the design note of item 6. Full text is in the two commits.

FIX: the method and its own doc comment were MOVED above the ForFault block.
No signature, no behaviour, no call site changed.

THE ASSERTION, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE ROUND.
New test TestTheFaultTableIsDocumentedOnTheExitAuthorityItself in
internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit_test.go. It does NOT read comments as text.
It parses hostexit.go with parser.ParseComments and reads the comment group THE
PARSER BINDS to each declaration - the same rule the go tool uses, so what it
reads is what go doc prints. Helper declaredDoc(t, name) resolves a plain
function name or a receiver-qualified method name ("Fault.UnusableInputs") and
returns the ATTACHED doc, or "" when the declaration has none. It then asserts
the fault table, the silent-exit-0 warning and the Deny rule are attached to
ForFault, and are NOT attached to the helper, and that the helper still keeps its
own doc so the repair does not simply move the hole.

MUTATION-RED EVIDENCE, PERFORMED, NOT DESCRIBED. The blank line was removed again
and Fault.UnusableInputs was moved back inside the ForFault doc block, in a
scratch copy outside the repository. Result, with the -run pattern passed as a
literal and the run NAMING the test:
  --- FAIL: TestTheFaultTableIsDocumentedOnTheExitAuthorityItself (0.00s)
  FAIL github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/lifecycle/hostexit
Five assertions turned RED:
  "" does not contain "must not fall through to a silent exit 0"
  "" does not contain "fail-closed, a mode that blocks by exit code, WITH evidence: block"
  "" does not contain "A Deny is an evaluated answer"
  helper doc should not contain "must not fall through to a silent exit 0"
  helper doc should not contain "fail-closed, a mode that blocks by exit code, WITH evidence: block"
The three empty-string failures are ForFault's ATTACHED doc being empty, which is
the defect itself, seen directly.

THREE CONTROLS RUN UNDER THE SAME MUTATION, which is what proves the new guard is
not a rebuild of the old one:
  gofmt -l on the mutated file: SILENT. It does not flag it.
  TestTheDocumentedFaultRuleCannotBeSilentlyReverted: --- PASS. The existing
    text guard STAYED GREEN under the exact defect, because it reads the package
    doc and then concatenates every comment group in the file, so neither of its
    checks knows which declaration a comment belongs to.
  go doc ForFault under the mutation: printed the signature and nothing else.
So the new assertion sees what the old guard cannot see by construction.

=====================================================================
ITEM 2 - THE ASSERTIONS THAT PROVED SOMETHING ELSE (v0zwcg on C, ygdd3u on B)
=====================================================================
ALL THREE CLAIMS RE-MEASURED ON THIS TREE. The finding is correct on every point.

(a) THE CITED MUTATION DOES NOT REACH EITHER ASSERTION. ClaudeLifecycleEvents was
cut to a single row. Result:
  panic: what: lifecycle contract "claude-code/claude-code@2.1.210" has 1 typed
  events and 30 mappings; why: every event in the closed pinned catalog must map
  exactly once; where: newLifecycleContract; ...
  github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/runtime.mustLifecycleContract[...]
The walk never runs. That run proves a PRE-EXISTING refusal and would stay RED if
the floor line were deleted, exactly as the finding says.

(b) THE FLOOR DOES WORK, under the mutation nobody had named. ONE Claude row was
removed CONSISTENTLY - the enum member ClaudeEventElicitationResult, its entry in
claudeLifecycleEventNames, its mapping entry, and its one frontend registration -
so the catalog stayed self-consistent and the contract still built. Result:
  Error: "86" is not greater than or equal to "87"
  --- FAIL: TestEveryDeclaredRowDiffersFromItsEffectiveModeOnlyByTheEvidenceRule
Consistent with the reviewer's measurement to the digit. THE FLOOR IS NOT WEAKENED.

(c) THE REACHED-EQUALITY CANNOT FAIL. claude-code WorktreeCreate was made
unreachable through the public lookup. Result:
  Error: Should be true
  Messages: claude-code WorktreeCreate is in the shipped native catalog, so the
            public lookup must declare it; this walk grants NO exemption
  --- FAIL: TestEveryDeclaredRowDiffersFromItsEffectiveModeOnlyByTheEvidenceRule
RED at require.True, and THE EQUALITY NEVER SPOKE - in the exact case its old
message described ("a row skipped here is a row no assertion above saw"). In the
(b) run it read 86 == 86 and PASSED. checked++ is unconditional and the only
abort above it ends the test first, so no production change can reach it.

FIX APPLIED, comment and failure-message text only, no production change and no
assertion change. A per-assertion account now names what turns EACH line RED,
including that (a) is a pre-existing refusal rather than a floor failure, that
(b) is the only measured mutation reaching the floor, and that the equality
guards A FUTURE EDIT TO THE WALK. The equality message was corrected to say that:
it now reads "the walk itself was edited: it no longer counts one row per derived
row. No production change can reach this line ... so it guards a later exemption,
filter or early continue added inside this loop".

ON KEEPING IT RATHER THAN REMOVING IT, stated rather than decided silently.
KEPT. It is the only line that would notice an exemption, a filter or a continue
added before the counter inside that loop, and such an edit would silently shrink
the population every assertion above sees while every one of them stayed green.
Once the message says it guards a future test edit and not a production change,
it is honest and it costs one line. Deleting it would leave the walk with no
statement at all that its population is the derived one. I did NOT restructure
it, because any restructuring that made it reachable would have to make the
counter conditional, which is the very shape the line exists to detect.

=====================================================================
ITEM 3 - THE SEPARATOR (tsq6wm on axis A, gqd1ay on axis B)
=====================================================================
THE LIST IS KEPT, as both axes judged correct: it replaced a sentence that named
one field of six and was wrong. Only the shape changed.
The defect, seen in the mutated output: a six-input refusal ended
  "...; the cause is nil, so there is no fault to report; this happened in
   lifecycleFault (cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go) after the event coordinates..."
and "this happened in lifecycleFault" reads as a seventh item.
New shape: each item carries its ordinal, the lead-in states the count and agrees
with it, and a full stop closes the list before the next clause. One item now
reads "one input of the fault was not usable: (1) the declared failure mode is
unset or not a known mode." Six items read "6 inputs of the fault were not
usable: (1) ...; (2) ...; ... (6) the cause is nil, so there is no fault to
report. This happened in lifecycleFault ...". The "these inputs" lead-in in front
of a one-item list is gone.
NEW TEST TestTheUnusableInputListHasAVisibleEnd covers the WIDEST list, all six
inputs, which no test reached while only the one-item case was covered.
MUTATION PERFORMED: join with "; ", restore the "these inputs" lead-in, drop the
ordinals and the closing full stop. RED, and the run NAMED both tests:
  --- FAIL: TestTheUnusableInputListHasAVisibleEnd
  --- FAIL: TestAFaultThatCannotBeClassifiedNamesEveryInputThatWasNotUsable
with failures on "6 inputs of the fault were not usable:", on each of "(1) "
through "(6) ", on "one input of the fault was not usable: (1) ", and on the
closing "...no fault to report. This happened in lifecycleFault".

=====================================================================
ITEM 4 - 2q0317: exit 1 that still claimed the host is not blocked
=====================================================================
TRUTH-SURFACE AND LATENT-HAZARD FIX. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: same arm, same exit
status, same one call site.
The ExitNonBlockingError comment said "No fault path produces this status today",
which is FALSE, because the classify-refusal arm in the command IS a fault path.
It now names that one arm, says the arm is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather
than by luck - ForFault refuses only on inputs the command always supplies, which
is why an unknown event, an unknown host version, an unknown harness and a
malformed payload all fail open at exit 0 - and says what would make it
reachable: a caller that builds a Fault from a value it did not set, such as a
new fault stage, a new policy, or a continuation taken from a host table with no
entry for the event. It also states that on the generated OpenCode plugin any
non-zero exit is read as a broken installation and throws, so this status is not
the non-blocking report its name promises.
The diagnostic itself said only "the host is not blocked", true of pasture's
intent and false of what an OpenCode user would see. It now says both: pasture
did not ask the host to block, AND the hook still leaves with exit 1 and a host
that reads any non-zero exit as a broken pasture installation stops the tool call
on it. Pinned by an assertion on "stops the tool call".

=====================================================================
ITEM 5 - q9fsh1: the empty failureMode in the durable record
=====================================================================
EMPTY WAS NOT THE HONEST VALUE. String() of an invalid FailureMode returns "",
so on the unmappable arm the record wrote "" and gave no reason, while stderr
named every unusable input. An empty string there cannot be told apart from a
member the writer forgot, and the record is the artefact that outlives the
process while stderr is kept nowhere.
FIX: recordedFailureMode renders an invalid mode as "unset-or-unknown", so the
record says WHICH of the two happened; a valid mode is still recorded verbatim.
The record also carries a new unusableFaultInputs member, empty on every fault
the exit authority could map, holding the refusal reasons on the one arm it could
not - and they come from the SAME function stderr asks, so the two artefacts
cannot describe different conditions. That last property is asserted.
NEW TEST TestTheUnmappableFaultRecordSaysWhatStderrSays drives the arm through
the REAL production lifecycleFault path with a real temporary store path and
reads the file it leaves. It is not a unit test of the helper.
TWO MUTATIONS PERFORMED, each run NAMING the test:
  return mode.String() unconditionally from recordedFailureMode ->
    --- FAIL: TestTheUnmappableFaultRecordSaysWhatStderrSays
    expected: "unset-or-unknown"  actual: ""
  drop the unusableFaultInputs member from the record map ->
    --- FAIL: TestTheUnmappableFaultRecordSaysWhatStderrSays
    Should be true / "the record must carry the refusal reasons, because it is
    the artefact that outlives the process and stderr is not kept anywhere"

=====================================================================
ITEM 6 - epe7df: the typed FaultInput suggestion. DECLINED, WITH REASONING.
=====================================================================
DECLINED. The reasoning is written into the UnusableInputs doc comment, where the
next reader meets the decision, rather than left in a review thread.
WHAT I WEIGHED.
Against taking it now: everything this result reports is a PROGRAMMING ERROR at
the call site - the exit authority already says so - not a host condition, and
the action is identical for all six conditions, which is to report it with the
cause. There is exactly ONE caller and it prints. No caller wants to branch on
which member was wrong, and none is planned, so the type-ness would ship with no
consumer. Cost: it is a type change on hostexit.Fault, the core exit type, which
this slice has already changed THREE times - the type gained DeclaredMode, gained
UnusableInputs, and has just had its documentation reattached - and each of those
re-opened every guard pinned to the type. A fourth change on the round whose
purpose is to make the remaining surfaces true buys no measured behaviour and
risks the surfaces just repaired.
WHAT I WEIGHED ON THE OTHER SIDE, and it is real: my own item-5 change writes
these English sentences into the durable record, which makes them a de facto
schema for anything that later reads that file. That RAISES the value of the
suggestion rather than lowering it. A reader that groups faults by cause needs a
stable key and cannot get one from English that may be reworded. I have written
that consumer into the code as the explicit trigger to revisit, so the decline
can expire on evidence rather than on taste.
WHAT MUST SURVIVE EITHER ANSWER, also written down: the sentence must not move
away from the condition that produces it. That adjacency is what stops the
refusal and the explanation from describing different things, and it is asserted
by test today.
NO CONTRADICTION BETWEEN FINDINGS WAS FOUND in this round. The one interaction
worth naming is the item-5 / item-6 one above, and it is an interaction rather
than a conflict, so I resolved it in the open instead of escalating it.

text:
# SLICE-S0-REVIEW-B-12 — architecture and data model, round 12

SHA e0c12c7acfa8701aed27219543e6fbcb70b94353 (4 commits over 5731142; 4 files, +360/-41).
Review task aura-plugins-rugj45.

VOTE: REVISE.
TALLY: 0 BLOCKER, 0 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR.
  BLOCKER group aura-plugins-catbid   CLOSED EMPTY
  IMPORTANT group aura-plugins-b6x1sc CLOSED EMPTY
  MINOR group aura-plugins-7gr9t7     aura-plugins-dz5du2

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## GATES — ALL FOUR RAN, ON AN ARCHIVE COPY OF e0c12c7, FROM INSIDE THE COPY

  go build ./...                  RAN, PASS. Entered the dev shell (Go 1.26.3), exit 0.
  go test -race -count=1 ./...    RAN, PASS. NAMED 80+ REAL PACKAGES, so it is not the
                                  "no main module" false green: cmd/pasture ok 313.7s,
                                  internal/tasks 62.7s, internal/engine 48.0s,
                                  internal/lifecycle/hostexit ok 1.05s. NO data race.
  make generate                   RAN, NO DRIFT. NAMED REAL TARGETS (go generate for
                                  opencode/claudecode/codex/metamodel; "claudecode-assets:
                                  wrote 36 generated asset(s), removed 0 stale"), so it is
                                  not the "No rule to make target" false green.
                                  git status after it: EMPTY.
  nix flake check --no-build      RAN, PASS. cgo-disabled-build, race, installer all green.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. THE DOC-ATTACHMENT GUARD — CORRECT, AND LOAD-BEARING. MEASURED.

RIGHT SYMBOLS: yes. It pins ForFault (three phrases: the silent-exit-0 warning, the
fail-closed-with-evidence row of the table, and the Deny rule) AND asserts the same three
are NOT on Fault.UnusableInputs. Both halves are needed; only the pair states "the table is
on the authority AND nowhere else".

CAN IT PASS VACUOUSLY? NO, on both paths I could find.
  - Declaration moved out of the file. MUTATION RUN: I moved the ForFault doc and func into
    a new file forfault.go in the SAME package. The guard turned RED with an actionable
    message: "hostexit.go declares no ForFault, so this guard is pinned to a name that no
    longer exists; rename the pin or restore the declaration". Loud, not vacuous. So the
    fixed filename "hostexit.go" is a false RED on a future file split, never a false GREEN,
    and it tells the maintainer what to do. I accept that trade.
  - File renamed away: parser.ParseFile errors and require.NoError ends the test.
  - Doc absent: declaredDoc returns "", and Contains("" , phrase) fails. The NotContains half
    could pass vacuously on an empty helper doc, and the worker CLOSED THAT HOLE with the
    positive Contains on the helper's own sentence. That is the right shape.

IS IT LOAD-BEARING? MEASURED. I reproduced the round-11 defect exactly — moved
func (f Fault) UnusableInputs() back between the ForFault doc block and "func ForFault" with
no blank line — and ran both guards together:
  TestTheFaultTableIsDocumentedOnTheExitAuthorityItself   RED on all FIVE assertions
    (3 Contains on the authority, now ""; the helper Contains; 2 NotContains on the helper,
     which had inherited the whole exit contract)
  TestTheDocumentedFaultRuleCannotBeSilentlyReverted      STAYED GREEN
The old text guard cannot see the defect; the new one sees it five ways. It reads the comment
group the PARSER BINDS to the declaration, which is what go doc prints, and its own doc says
why file.Comments cannot do this. Nothing to fix.

## 2. THE KEPT EQUALITY — I ACCEPT THE WORKER'S REASONING, AND THE REASON IS NOW IN THE CODE.

I raised in an earlier round that require.Equal(len(rows), checked) cannot be turned RED by
any production change. That is still true and the worker does not dispute it: checked++ is
unconditional and sits immediately after a require that ends the test first.

The stated reason to keep it holds. Any restructuring that made the line reachable — an
exemption, a filter, an early continue placed before the counter — is exactly the edit that
would silently shrink the population every assertion above walks, and this is the only line
that would notice. Deleting it would remove the detector for the one failure it exists to
detect. THE REASON IS NOW RECORDED IN THE CODE, in two places: the doc block enumerates what
turns EACH assertion red one by one, and the require message itself now says "No production
change can reach this line ... it guards a later exemption, filter or early continue added
inside this loop". The message no longer claims a detection the test does not make. Closed
on my axis.

The floor is also now honest: the doc names the ONLY measured mutation that reaches it
(remove one Claude row consistently -> "86 is not greater than or equal to 87") and states
that the cut-to-one-row mutation cited before does NOT reach it, because newLifecycleContract
panics first. Correct, and correctly attributed.

## 3. THE DECLINED epe7df — THE DECLINE IS SOUND AND ITS EXPIRY TRIGGER IS FALSIFIABLE.

The decline reasoning is right for today: every one of the six conditions is a programming
error at the call site, the action is identical for all six, there is ONE caller, and it
prints. A typed value would add a second list to keep in step with the six conditions and buy
no behaviour. In a slice that has changed this core type three times, declining a fourth
change for no behaviour is the conservative call and I agree with it.

The expiry trigger is the good part: it names a CONSUMER, not a preference — "a reader that
must group faults by cause needs a stable key, and cannot get one from English that may be
reworded" — and it says what to do then (add a typed member and KEEP the sentence beside the
condition, so the refusal and the explanation still cannot diverge). That is a trigger a
later reviewer can test for, which is what makes a decline reviewable rather than final.
ACCEPTED.

One caveat, which is my finding below rather than an objection to the decline: the trigger
rests on "the durable fault record now carries these sentences, which makes them a de facto
schema", and on real data that member is currently null on every line.

## 4. THE DURABLE RECORD — ONE FINDING.

recordedFailureMode is right and is proved right. MUTATION RUN: I made it return
mode.String() unconditionally, and TestTheUnmappableFaultRecordSaysWhatStderrSays turned RED
("expected: unset-or-unknown, actual: <empty>"). The rule it embodies is the correct one:
an empty string in a durable record cannot be told apart from a member the writer forgot.

THE SAME RULE IS BROKEN BY THE MEMBER ADDED BESIDE IT. unusableFaultInputs is a nil []string
on every mappable fault, so it marshals to JSON null, not to []. MEASURED on the production
path with a probe: {"...","unusableFaultInputs":null}. That is the shape of essentially every
line the file will ever hold, because the refusal arm is unreachable by construction. The
comment at hook_lifecycle.go:472 calls it "empty", which is not what the bytes say, and no
test pins the member on the mappable arm at all — the only assertion on it is inside the
unreachable-arm test. See aura-plugins-dz5du2 for the fix and the mutation that must go RED.

## 5. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED — VERIFIED AGAINST THE PINS, NOT AGAINST THE TESTS.

  - HookInvocation tier: Production 5s (profile.go:99), Test 6s, DeadlineTest 1s. UNMOVED.
    The strict ordering below the 30 s workflow-result wait still holds.
  - The fault/decision split: hostexit.go changes are COMMENTS AND DECLARATION ORDER ONLY.
    ForFault's body, ForDecision, the evidence rule and the policy arms are byte-identical.
  - The exit-1 arm: same Outcome, same Exit, same trigger condition. Only the sentence
    changed, and it changed toward the truth — it now says the generated OpenCode plugin

literal. The message half was fixed this round and the exit half was not.
That is finding aura-plugins-s8hd20, and my evidence is a mutation nobody asked
for: exitWithCode(1) -> exitWithCode(0) on that arm leaves the WHOLE cmd/pasture
package GREEN (ok, 203.571s). The comment two lines above says the arm "must
never become a silent exit 0"; that sentence has no guard, and the condition it
guards is the exact defect aura-plugins-3m1zix filed this slice for.
Full detail, the ExitNonBlockingError "EXACTLY ONE fault path" consequence, and
a small suggested fix are on aura-plugins-s8hd20.

## 4. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED BEYOND THE TWO FIXES — CONFIRMED

Diff e0c12c7..5c03402 is FIVE files: AGENTS.md (+9), hook_lifecycle.go,
hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go, hostexit.go, hostexit_test.go.
The only non-comment production changes in the whole range are the two fixes
(unusable := []string{}; recordedCause) plus the move of the arm-two message
into a function. Everything else is prose.

THE TIER DID NOT MOVE. internal/timeouts/profile.go is NOT in the diff, and
HookInvocation still reads 5s in the package doc table and still has its
accessor. The fault/decision split, the derived-mode guard, the doc-attachment
guard, the barrier and the call-site pins are all untouched by this range.

## 5. MY OWN MUTATIONS

M1 (asked)  var unusable []string           -> RED, named test. Correct.
M2 (asked)  cause.Error()                   -> RED with the panic. Correct.
M3 (MINE)   exitWithCode(1) -> exitWithCode(0) on the unset-exit arm
            -> GREEN over the whole package. THIS IS THE FINDING.

The two fixes this round was asked for are correct, are proven on the production
path rather than in a unit test, and the class of each was swept beyond the site
the finding pointed at. I would have voted ACCEPT on those alone. The unasked
mutation found a real, latent, unpinned guard on the sibling arm of the same
function the round edited, so the round is not clean.
