author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-10 ROUND 14, host-contract truth and end-user behaviour axis: REVISE 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR.
Review task aura-plugins-evdles; BLOCKER 86kpqm and IMPORTANT ig8o0q CLOSED EMPTY; MINOR 50itxy holds aura-plugins-b8o8n7.
Everything below was measured on a binary I built myself from an archive copy of 5c03402 in the dev shell (Go go1.26.3). Control: go test on the UNMUTATED copy, cmd/pasture ok 202.0s, nativeresponse ok, hostexit ok. So every RED below is a real RED.

=== 1. THE FAIL-OPEN GUARANTEE SURVIVED THE FOURTH CHANGE TO hostexit.go AND hook_lifecycle.go ===
14 runs, 7 rows x both policy skews, real storage fault (the database path made unopenable), production path, no test seam.
  claude-code PreToolUse / PreCompact / PostToolUse   stdout 0 BYTES on all six
  codex PreToolUse gate                               {"continue":true}   (17 bytes, both skews)
  codex SessionStart observation                      {}                  (2 bytes, both skews)
  opencode tool.execute.before gate                   {"decision":"proceed"} (22 bytes, both skews)
  opencode session.created observation                NOTHING             (0 bytes, both skews)
ALL 14 EXIT 0 WITH THE STDERR DIAGNOSTIC AND A DURABLE RECORD, except the ONE cited row: claude-code PreToolUse under PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 exits 2 with empty stdout. That is the only blocking cell and it is the evidenced one.
THE FIVE DEGENERATE PROBES ALSO FAIL OPEN, each exit 0 with a record:
  unknown event on claude-code (empty stdout) and on opencode ({"decision":"proceed"});
  unknown host version 9.9.9; malformed payload "not-json{"; unknown harness "bogus-harness" (empty continuation, not a guessed shape); EMPTY STDIN on all three harnesses, each with its own correct continue bytes.
I ADDED TWO PROBES OF MY OWN THAT NO ROUND HAD RUN: a BAD FLAG (--bogus) and an UNEXPECTED POSITIONAL ARGUMENT. Both take the fault path and fail open at exit 0 with the harness's continue bytes, including {"decision":"proceed"} on the OpenCode gate. The SetFlagErrorFunc arm has NO recover of its own, so it was worth measuring rather than reading.

=== 2. THE TWO PREDECESSOR FINDINGS, BOTH CONFIRMED FIXED, BOTH SIDES MEASURED ===
04trrl, the nil cause that panicked the record writer. I built TWO binaries from the same reachability mutation (cause = nil at the head of lifecycleFault) and ran claude-code PreToolUse against an unopenable database:
  BEFORE the fix (recordedCause reverted to cause.Error()): EXIT 2, stdout 0 bytes, stderr = "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [RECOVERED, REPANICKED]" with the frame main.recordLifecycleFault at hook_lifecycle.go:513, NO RECORD FILE. The defect exactly as reported.
  AFTER the fix: EXIT 1, stdout 0 bytes, stderr = the full numbered list ending "(1) the cause is nil, so there is no fault to report.", and the durable line IS present with cause "unset-or-missing" and unusableFaultInputs ["the cause is nil, ..."]. Both sides confirmed.
I ALSO CONFIRMED ITEM 1 ON THE PRODUCTION PATH, unmutated: every one of the 14 records above carries "unusableFaultInputs":[] and not null.
isb8qu, the over-wide "stops the tool call" clause. CHECKED AGAINST THE GENERATED PLUGIN, not against the report. .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL to internal/target/opencode/assets/hooks/pasture-hooks.ts (diff empty), and in it:
  line 21  invokeLifecycle: "if (exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(...)" — UNCONDITIONAL on any non-zero exit;
  line 52  toolExecuteBefore: awaits invokeLifecycle with NO try/catch, so a GATE throw propagates and STOPS the tool call;
  line 43  sessionCreated: wraps the await in try/catch and only console.errors, so an OBSERVATION is NOT stopped.
THE NARROWED CLAIM IS TRUE ON ALL THREE PROSE SITES. The worker found a third site the finding had not named and narrowed it too.

=== 3. THE EXIT-CODE DIFFERENCE, SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT ===
BOTH NUMBERS ARE RIGHT AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. The whole lifecycle path has exactly TWO recovers — hook_lifecycle.go:151 (lifecycleOutcome, top level) and :233 (the work goroutine) — and main() has NONE, so an escaped panic is the Go runtime's exit 2.
  A panic in the record writer reached from a NORMAL-PATH lifecycleFault call is caught by the :151 recover, which re-enters lifecycleFault with the panic as the cause; that second call maps, and the process exits 0 fail-open WITH a record. I BUILT THIS CASE (pre-fix writer, nil cause at ONE call site only) and measured EXIT 0, stdout 0 bytes, RECORD PRESENT, stderr = the ordinary fail-open diagnostic and NOT a panic trace.
  A panic in the record writer reached from INSIDE that recover has nothing left to catch it. The worker's mutation (nil at the head of lifecycleFault) hits BOTH calls, so the second panic escapes; the runtime prints "[recovered, repanicked]" and the process exits 2 with NO record.
SO THE ROUND-13 WORKER'S EXIT 2 IS THE ONE THAT MATCHES THE REPORTED SUBSTANCE. "Empty stdout, a nil-pointer panic ON STDERR, no list and no record" is only producible by the escaping variant, and that variant exits 2; the exit-0 variant leaves a record and prints no panic. The round-12 exit 0 is a correct number for a narrower mutation, not for the state it was reported beside.
THE PRACTICAL ANSWER: the :151 recover catches a record-writer panic ONCE. It cannot catch the second one, so nil-safety in the writer is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces, which is why 04trrl deserved its fix.

=== 4. THE EVIDENCE SENTENCE STILL REACHES ITS ROWS, WITH THE ACTION ===
claude-code PreCompact and codex PreToolUse, both under fail-closed, both read "PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED is already set and it had no channel on this event: the event declares the blocking exit code but carries no host evidence for it ... to make this event able to block, ADD THE HOST DOCUMENTATION OR A COMMITTED CAPTURE showing the host refuses on that exit code", with declared mode exit-2-blocks / strict-output-exit-2-blocks against effective report-and-continue.
claude-code PostToolUse reads the OTHER sentence, keyed on its declared mode report-and-continue. claude-code PreToolUse under the opt-in still exits 2. The record and the stderr agree on every row I read.

=== 5. THE PRODUCTION TIER HAS NOT MOVED ===
timeouts.ProductionProfile is 500ms / 1s / 2s / 5s / 30s. HookInvocation is 5s against the 10s Claude budget, and the package doc still states that budget. MY OWN MUTATION, swapping ProductionProfile for TestProfile in the command's RunE, turns TestTheProductionPathWiresThePassThroughBarrierAndTheProductionTier RED plus TestLifecycleHookReturnsInsideItsDeadlineWhileTheDatabaseIsLocked. The tier is pinned at the wiring, not only in the table.

=== 6. MY OTHER MUTATION, AND WHY THIS AXIS CHOSE IT ===
The Claude arm of the fail-open promise is the one that looks like nothing: its continue bytes ARE the empty body, so a regression there is invisible to a reader. MUTATION: make nativeresponse.FaultContinuation return the canonical {"decision":"proceed"} object for claude-code. RESULT: RED in TWO packages and at THREE levels — TestFaultContinuationIsTheHostProceedForEveryHarness (both the gate and the observation subtests), TestTheFaultContinuationMatchesTheEvaluatedProceed, and five BUILT-BINARY tests in cmd/pasture including TestLifecycleHookExitFollowsTheEffectiveFailureMode and TestAPanicBeforeTheWorkStartsIsAFaultAndNeverACrash. The quietest arm of the guarantee is the best guarded one.

=== 7. THE ONE FINDING: aura-plugins-b8o8n7, MINOR ===
The durable fault record is lost SILENTLY when the resolved database path has no directory component. lifecycleFaultRecordPath returns "" and recordLifecycleFault returns without a word — while the SAME writer's two other failures, the open failure and the append failure, both print "the fault above is reported on this stream only".
MEASURED TWO WAYS, both exit 0 with the correct continue bytes and no record file: --db pasture.db, and the DOCUMENTED environment variable PASTURE_DB_PATH=pasture.db with no flag at all. grep "fault record" on the stderr of the second: ZERO hits.
IT MAKES TWO SHIPPED SENTENCES FALSE: AGENTS.md says the line is appended "in the same directory as the database the invocation would have used", and the record-unknown diagnostic tells the reader to "read the fault record file beside the database for this invocation".
The DEFAULT is not affected — DefaultDBPath falls back to ".pasture/pasture.db", whose directory is ".pasture" — and the generated hooks pass no --db, so the shipped wiring is safe. It needs an operator who sets a bare relative name.
NO TEST REACHES IT: lifecycleFaultRecordPath has three references in the tree and all three are in hook_lifecycle.go.
MINOR because THE HOST OUTCOME IS UNHARMED: fail-open holds, the bytes are right, the diagnostic is on stderr. What is lost is the evidence and the truth of the two sentences that point at it.

=== 8. AN ANSWER FOR THE DELIVERABILITY AXIS, WHICH OWNS THE COUNT ===
I ran the supervisor's grep myself. "the host is not blocked" over the whole tree is SIX textual occurrences: TWO in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go (:384 and :566, both doc comments recounting the retired sentence as history) and FOUR in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go (:1110 an assertion message, :1121 and :1126 the test's own doc and MUTATION note, :1139 the assert.NotContains that IS the guard). SIX is the textual count; ONE was the live operator-facing count and it is swept. Note that the worker's list of four named internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit.go:126, which does NOT contain that string — its wording is "the host is NEVER blocked" — so the worker's four is neither the textual count nor a subset of it. THE CODE IS RIGHT; the report's enumeration is not. No live site carries the retired sentence.

=== 9. SCRATCH ===
I deleted ONLY my own paths under the session scratchpad (r14a, mA, mB, mC, mD, m1, m3, r14probe.*, r14ids, r14dirs). No other agent's directory was touched, and I ran nothing in the live worktree: no build, no make generate, no git checkout.

  BEFORE the fix (recordedCause reverted to cause.Error()): EXIT 2, stdout 0 bytes, stderr = "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [RECOVERED, REPANICKED]" with the frame main.recordLifecycleFault at hook_lifecycle.go:513, NO RECORD FILE. The defect exactly as reported.
  AFTER the fix: EXIT 1, stdout 0 bytes, stderr = the full numbered list ending "(1) the cause is nil, so there is no fault to report.", and the durable line IS present with cause "unset-or-missing" and unusableFaultInputs ["the cause is nil, ..."]. Both sides confirmed.
I ALSO CONFIRMED ITEM 1 ON THE PRODUCTION PATH, unmutated: every one of the 14 records above carries "unusableFaultInputs":[] and not null.
isb8qu, the over-wide "stops the tool call" clause. CHECKED AGAINST THE GENERATED PLUGIN, not against the report. .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL to internal/target/opencode/assets/hooks/pasture-hooks.ts (diff empty), and in it:
  line 21  invokeLifecycle: "if (exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(...)" — UNCONDITIONAL on any non-zero exit;
  line 52  toolExecuteBefore: awaits invokeLifecycle with NO try/catch, so a GATE throw propagates and STOPS the tool call;
  line 43  sessionCreated: wraps the await in try/catch and only console.errors, so an OBSERVATION is NOT stopped.
THE NARROWED CLAIM IS TRUE ON ALL THREE PROSE SITES. The worker found a third site the finding had not named and narrowed it too.

=== 3. THE EXIT-CODE DIFFERENCE, SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT ===
BOTH NUMBERS ARE RIGHT AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. The whole lifecycle path has exactly TWO recovers — hook_lifecycle.go:151 (lifecycleOutcome, top level) and :233 (the work goroutine) — and main() has NONE, so an escaped panic is the Go runtime's exit 2.
  A panic in the record writer reached from a NORMAL-PATH lifecycleFault call is caught by the :151 recover, which re-enters lifecycleFault with the panic as the cause; that second call maps, and the process exits 0 fail-open WITH a record. I BUILT THIS CASE (pre-fix writer, nil cause at ONE call site only) and measured EXIT 0, stdout 0 bytes, RECORD PRESENT, stderr = the ordinary fail-open diagnostic and NOT a panic trace.
  A panic in the record writer reached from INSIDE that recover has nothing left to catch it. The worker's mutation (nil at the head of lifecycleFault) hits BOTH calls, so the second panic escapes; the runtime prints "[recovered, repanicked]" and the process exits 2 with NO record.
SO THE ROUND-13 WORKER'S EXIT 2 IS THE ONE THAT MATCHES THE REPORTED SUBSTANCE. "Empty stdout, a nil-pointer panic ON STDERR, no list and no record" is only producible by the escaping variant, and that variant exits 2; the exit-0 variant leaves a record and prints no panic. The round-12 exit 0 is a correct number for a narrower mutation, not for the state it was reported beside.
THE PRACTICAL ANSWER: the :151 recover catches a record-writer panic ONCE. It cannot catch the second one, so nil-safety in the writer is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces, which is why 04trrl deserved its fix.

=== 4. THE EVIDENCE SENTENCE STILL REACHES ITS ROWS, WITH THE ACTION ===
claude-code PreCompact and codex PreToolUse, both under fail-closed, both read "PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED is already set and it had no channel on this event: the event declares the blocking exit code but carries no host evidence for it ... to make this event able to block, ADD THE HOST DOCUMENTATION OR A COMMITTED CAPTURE showing the host refuses on that exit code", with declared mode exit-2-blocks / strict-output-exit-2-blocks against effective report-and-continue.
claude-code PostToolUse reads the OTHER sentence, keyed on its declared mode report-and-continue. claude-code PreToolUse under the opt-in still exits 2. The record and the stderr agree on every row I read.

=== 5. THE PRODUCTION TIER HAS NOT MOVED ===
timeouts.ProductionProfile is 500ms / 1s / 2s / 5s / 30s. HookInvocation is 5s against the 10s Claude budget, and the package doc still states that budget. MY OWN MUTATION, swapping ProductionProfile for TestProfile in the command's RunE, turns TestTheProductionPathWiresThePassThroughBarrierAndTheProductionTier RED plus TestLifecycleHookReturnsInsideItsDeadlineWhileTheDatabaseIsLocked. The tier is pinned at the wiring, not only in the table.

=== 6. MY OTHER MUTATION, AND WHY THIS AXIS CHOSE IT ===
The Claude arm of the fail-open promise is the one that looks like nothing: its continue bytes ARE the empty body, so a regression there is invisible to a reader. MUTATION: make nativeresponse.FaultContinuation return the canonical {"decision":"proceed"} object for claude-code. RESULT: RED in TWO packages and at THREE levels — TestFaultContinuationIsTheHostProceedForEveryHarness (both the gate and the observation subtests), TestTheFaultContinuationMatchesTheEvaluatedProceed, and five BUILT-BINARY tests in cmd/pasture including TestLifecycleHookExitFollowsTheEffectiveFailureMode and TestAPanicBeforeTheWorkStartsIsAFaultAndNeverACrash. The quietest arm of the guarantee is the best guarded one.

=== 7. THE ONE FINDING: aura-plugins-b8o8n7, MINOR ===
The durable fault record is lost SILENTLY when the resolved database path has no directory component. lifecycleFaultRecordPath returns "" and recordLifecycleFault returns without a word — while the SAME writer's two other failures, the open failure and the append failure, both print "the fault above is reported on this stream only".
MEASURED TWO WAYS, both exit 0 with the correct continue bytes and no record file: --db pasture.db, and the DOCUMENTED environment variable PASTURE_DB_PATH=pasture.db with no flag at all. grep "fault record" on the stderr of the second: ZERO hits.
IT MAKES TWO SHIPPED SENTENCES FALSE: AGENTS.md says the line is appended "in the same directory as the database the invocation would have used", and the record-unknown diagnostic tells the reader to "read the fault record file beside the database for this invocation".
The DEFAULT is not affected — DefaultDBPath falls back to ".pasture/pasture.db", whose directory is ".pasture" — and the generated hooks pass no --db, so the shipped wiring is safe. It needs an operator who sets a bare relative name.
NO TEST REACHES IT: lifecycleFaultRecordPath has three references in the tree and all three are in hook_lifecycle.go.
MINOR because THE HOST OUTCOME IS UNHARMED: fail-open holds, the bytes are right, the diagnostic is on stderr. What is lost is the evidence and the truth of the two sentences that point at it.

=== 8. AN ANSWER FOR THE DELIVERABILITY AXIS, WHICH OWNS THE COUNT ===
I ran the supervisor's grep myself. "the host is not blocked" over the whole tree is SIX textual occurrences: TWO in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go (:384 and :566, both doc comments recounting the retired sentence as history) and FOUR in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go (:1110 an assertion message, :1121 and :1126 the test's own doc and MUTATION note, :1139 the assert.NotContains that IS the guard). SIX is the textual count; ONE was the live operator-facing count and it is swept. Note that the worker's list of four named internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit.go:126, which does NOT contain that string — its wording is "the host is NEVER blocked" — so the worker's four is neither the textual count nor a subset of it. THE CODE IS RIGHT; the report's enumeration is not. No live site carries the retired sentence.

=== 9. SCRATCH ===
I deleted ONLY my own paths under the session scratchpad (r14a, mA, mB, mC, mD, m1, m3, r14probe.*, r14ids, r14dirs). No other agent's directory was touched, and I ran nothing in the live worktree: no build, no make generate, no git checkout.

Each carried the full stderr diagnostic. The record lines name the effective AND declared mode:
codex PreToolUse records declared strict-output-exit-2-blocks, effective report-and-continue,
failureCitedBy empty - the unevidenced demotion, visible in the artefact.
Observation rows: opencode file.edited 0 bytes; codex SessionStart {}; claude SessionStart
0 bytes. The gate/observation byte split is exactly what nativeresponse documents.
PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1: claude-code PreToolUse rc=2, hostExit block, empty stdout. Every
other row rc=0 with its continue bytes.

2. THE DEGENERATE PROBES. Ten of them, all rc=0, all with the harness's continue bytes and a
durable record: unknown event on claude-code AND on opencode; unknown host version; malformed
payload (not-json); unknown harness; EMPTY STDIN on codex and on opencode; a bad flag
(--nope=1, through the SetFlagErrorFunc arm); an unexpected positional argument on claude-code
and on opencode. An undeclared OpenCode event emits the GATE bytes, not silence - that is
deliberate and is written where FaultContinuation decides it ("Gates, explicit human responses
and undeclared events take the canonical object"), so it is not a finding.

3. b8o8n7 IS FIXED, BOTH WAYS IT IS REACHED, AND THE NO-REGRESSION HALF HOLDS.
  --db pasture.db            rc=0, stdout 0 bytes,  no record, ONE new line naming the loss
  PASTURE_DB_PATH=pasture.db rc=0, stdout {"decision":"proceed"}, no record, the SAME line
  --db sub/pasture.db        rc=0, ONE record line in sub/, ZERO "could not place" lines
The message quotes the resolved store path, names the function and the file, says the fault is
on this stream only, and gives BOTH ways out (--db, PASTURE_DB_PATH). The host outcome does not
move on any of the three.

4. THE NARROWED EXIT-1 CLAIM IS STILL TRUE. In the generated OpenCode plugin - and both
artefacts are byte-identical, .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts and
internal/target/opencode/assets/hooks/pasture-hooks.ts - invokeLifecycle throws on ANY non-zero
exit; toolExecuteBefore (a GATE) does not catch it, so the throw reaches the callback and stops
the tool call; sessionCreated (an OBSERVATION) catches and only logs. Both exit-1 diagnostics now
name the gate rows and the observation rows separately, and both name
hostexit.ExitNonBlockingError rather than a literal. The ExitNonBlockingError doc no longer says
"EXACTLY ONE fault path".

5. THE EVIDENCE SENTENCE REACHES ITS ROWS. Under PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1, claude-code
PreCompact and codex PreToolUse both carry "the event declares the blocking exit code but carries
no host evidence for it ... to make this event able to block, add the host documentation or a
committed capture showing the host refuses on that exit code" - the claim AND the action.
claude-code PostToolUse carries the MODE sentence instead ("its declared failure mode
report-and-continue does not refuse through a process exit code"). The OpenCode gate carries the
third, surface sentence. claude-code PreToolUse exits 2. Four different readers, four different
true sentences.

6. THE PRODUCTION TIER DID NOT MOVE. internal/timeouts/profile.go:99 ProductionProfile is
New(Production, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s, 30s); HookInvocation is 5 s, and AGENTS.md line 155 still
carries **5 s** against the documented 10 s Claude budget.

7. BASELINE. go test -count=1 on ./cmd/pasture/... ./internal/lifecycle/hostexit/...
./internal/lifecycle/nativeresponse/... - all ok, cmd/pasture 200.273s.

=== THE THREE MINOR ===

zfzao0 - ALL THREE fault-record failures tell the operator the fault is "above". It is BELOW.
recordLifecycleFault runs inside lifecycleFault and returns; emitLifecycleOutcome writes the
fault diagnostic afterwards. Measured on two of the three arms: the record message is line 1 of
standard error and the fault is line 2. The round ADDED the third instance and its new test PINS
the phrase, with the stated reason that the two siblings use it. Fix all three at once.

wzencw - ONLY THE DIAGNOSTIC WAS FIXED. The AGENTS.md sentence still says, unconditionally, that
a hook that cannot evaluate "appends one JSON line ... in the same directory as the database the
invocation would have used". On the two routes above it appends nothing. The same section also
says most hosts never show the standard error of an exit-0 hook, so the reader that sentence is
written for is the one reader the new diagnostic cannot reach. The comment beside the fix says
the SILENCE made the sentence false; the missing RECORD did, and reporting the loss does not
change whether the file exists. There is also a THIRD promise, and it is USER-FACING: the
generated OpenCode plugin's console message says "read ... the lifecycle fault record beside the
pasture database".

v383ra - MY OWN MUTATION, AND THE HALF THE ORIGINAL FINDING ASKED FOR. Replace the quoted
lifecycleStorePath() with flagDBPath in the new refusal. FULL, UNFILTERED
go test ./cmd/pasture/... -> ok, 196.478s. GREEN. On the built mutant, the documented
PASTURE_DB_PATH route prints: the store path "" names no directory - which is exactly the
"cannot tell which of the two rules produced the path" failure that function's own doc comment
says it exists to prevent. No test in cmd/pasture drives PASTURE_DB_PATH into this arm, although
both the production comment and the test comment claim both routes were measured, and b8o8n7
asked for a BUILT-BINARY pin.

=== WHAT IS GOOD AND MUST NOT BE UNDONE ===
- The two exit-1 arms now BOTH name a declared hostexit status and exit through Code(). The
  round's own test states the mutations that turn it red, and they are the right mutations.
- The recordedCause comment now separates the two panic arms instead of merging them, and states
  which one keeps the record and which one escapes to exit 2. That merged sentence was the
  measured cause of two reviewers reporting different exit codes.
- The unusable-input trigger now lives in ONE place with both ends of the pointer pinned. That is
  the right resolution: a parser author of lifecycle-faults.jsonl opens AGENTS.md, not a Go file.
- The fix did NOT repair the record placement, and that restraint is correct. The record belongs
  beside the store, and inventing a directory for a bare relative name would put evidence
  somewhere nobody looks.

SIXTEEN ROUNDS, SIXTH CONSECUTIVE WITH NO BLOCKER, FOURTH WITH NO IMPORTANT. I did not lower the
standard to close the slice, and I would not have voted ACCEPT on the three fixes alone: two of
the three MINOR are truth defects in text this round wrote or pinned, and the third is a mutation
that shows a claim the round states twice is held once.

TestTheUnusableInputTrigger turns it RED AT BOTH CITATIONS - AGENTS.md and the Fault.UnusableInputs

the flag route and the environment route; route 2 the MkdirAll arm; route 3 the open arm through

text:
# SLICE-S0-REVIEW-B-20 (round 20, axis B: architecture and data model) - VOTE: REVISE

Review task aura-plugins-lla4j0. SHA 223f86a795c6df88acf93cb594f193634050ffe3, three commits
over 1ce711e.

TALLY 0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR.
- BLOCKER group aura-plugins-pq0iep: EMPTY, closed.
- IMPORTANT group aura-plugins-otospy: aura-plugins-647hcl.
- MINOR group aura-plugins-n78nu9: aura-plugins-4g28el.

## Gates, run from INSIDE a git-archive copy of the SHA. EACH ONE ACTUALLY RAN.
- go build ./... - RAN, PASS. Dev-shell banner printed, no "no main module".
- go test -race -count=1 ./... - RAN, PASS. 72 packages ok, cmd/pasture 269.802s, exit 0,
  no FAIL and no race report.
- make generate - RAN, PASS. Real generation output (36 claudecode assets, codex agents,
  opencode and metamodel targets), and git status is EMPTY afterwards: no codegen drift.
- nix flake check --no-build - RAN, PASS. cgo-disabled-build, installer and race all green.

## What I verified on my axis

1. THE STREAM PIN HOLDS FOR THE MUTATION IT WAS BUILT FOR. I re-ran two of the five arm
   mutations myself, cmd.ErrOrStderr() to cmd.OutOrStdout():
   - arm 1, the no-directory refusal (line 528): RED, and the message names the arm and the
     line - "an if arm at hook_lifecycle.go:509 reports on cmd.OutOrStdout()".
   - arm 5, the APPEND arm (line 623): RED, "an if arm at hook_lifecycle.go:622".
   Both were green across the whole package before this round. The founding-defect mutation
   is now caught arm by arm and again over the whole function.

2. THE BRANCH ENUMERATION IS COMPLETE FOR BRANCHES. Verified by mutation: a SWITCH-SHAPED
   silent return is RED on the count assertion, where it passed last round. I also checked
   the escapes the arm loop alone would miss - a report inside a nested branch, or inside a
   func literal, or outside every branch - and the whole-function count assertion
   Len(whole, len(arms)) closes each of them, in the conservative direction. No SIXTH
   BRANCH SHAPE escapes.
   BUT THE POPULATION IS THE WRONG DOMAIN. See aura-plugins-647hcl: the guard reads
   BRANCHES, the document promises ROUTES THAT LOSE THE RECORD, and the unchecked
   defer file.Close() at hook_lifecycle.go:621 is a loss route with no branch and no word.
   Measured: routing the line through an unchecked buffered flush leaves the guard ok in
   0.613s, the FULL UNFILTERED cmd/pasture package ok in 198.652s, and every
   internal/lifecycle package ok.

3. THE COUNT AND THE SPLIT ARE TRUE. Five guarded branches: no directory, encode, MkdirAll,
   open, append. Four are user-reachable. The fifth, the json.Marshal arm, IS unreachable by
   construction and I checked it rather than took it: every member of the record map is a
   string, a []string, or a value converted to string - lifecycleCoordinates carries
   HarnessID (string-converted), Event string and HostVersion string;
   FailureEvidence.Source is a string; the three enum members go through String();
   hostContinuation is string(outcome.Stdout); failureMode and cause go through helpers that
   return strings. encoding/json cannot refuse any of those, and invalid UTF-8 in a string is
   replaced rather than refused. 5 = 4 + 1 CONFIRMED.

4. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. The diff over 1ce711e is exactly four files - AGENTS.md,
   hook_lifecycle.go, hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go, hostexit_test.go - and the whole of
   the hook_lifecycle.go change is COMMENT TEXT (the renamed test cited in two places). No
   codegen file and no plugin artefact moved, which make generate confirms independently by
   leaving the tree clean. The tier, the fault/decision split, the derived guard, the
   doc-attachment guard, the barrier and the call-site pins are untouched by this diff and
   the full race suite holds them.

5. THE CITATION PIN. The change from assert.Contains to a word-boundary regexp is correct for
   the shape it was aimed at: a PREFIX rename now has a word character after the match, so
   the boundary fails and both citations go RED. It also holds for an underscore suffix,
   because the boundary treats underscore as a word character. The AGENTS.md sentence is now
   true, and refusing option (b) was right.

## RULING ON THE APPEND ARM: THE STRUCTURAL PIN IS SUFFICIENT. S0 DOES NOT NEED THE BYTES.

The worker flagged this rather than hiding it, and refused to add a production seam whose only
user is a test. Both are correct and both match this slice's own precedent - the json.Marshal
arm was accepted structurally, and a test-only production branch was refused for the panic
proof.

The claim the append arm carries is that it SPEAKS and that it speaks ON STANDARD ERROR. Both
are properties of the source, and the structural guard now reads exactly those two - I
measured the arm RED under the stdout mutation at line 623. Bytes would add only one further
fact: that the arm is REACHED on a real write failure. That fact costs a filesystem-level
input.

I WOULD NOT ACCEPT that cost. A loopback filesystem needs mount privilege, which the Nix
check sandbox does not have, so the test would either be skipped there - a guard that is
absent exactly where the gate runs - or it would force the gate out of the sandbox. A disk
quota needs a filesystem mounted with quotas on, which is a property of the developer machine
and not of the repository, so the suite would pass or fail on where it was run. Either one is
a new dependency of EVERY future test run in exchange for one reachability fact about a
best-effort evidence file that never decides the host outcome.

THE ONLY DEPENDENCY I WOULD ACCEPT is an error-injecting io.Writer supplied through a seam
that ALREADY EXISTS for another reason. No such seam exists at this call site, and inventing
one is the production-branch-for-a-test the worker rightly refused. So: keep the structural
pin, and do not open this again in a later round.

ONE CONSEQUENCE, and it is why aura-plugins-647hcl is IMPORTANT rather than MINOR: accepting
structure as the sole witness on this side of the writer makes the DOMAIN that structure is
read over load-bearing. That domain is branches, and a loss route without a branch is outside
it by construction. Fix the domain and the structural pin becomes sound; leave it and the
document keeps promising a route the guard cannot hold.

## Not the 0/0/0 round
Nineteen rounds have each been decided by a mutation nobody asked for, and round 20 is no
different: the buffered-flush mutation is green across the full package. VOTE: REVISE.

text:
PHASE-10 ROUND 20, HOST-CONTRACT TRUTH AND END-USER BEHAVIOUR AXIS: REVISE.
0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 2 MINOR at 223f86a795c6df88acf93cb594f193634050ffe3.
Review task aura-plugins-si57wn. BLOCKER group aura-plugins-wgz5dw CLOSED EMPTY.
IMPORTANT aura-plugins-v3he6q holds aura-plugins-4ajb9z. MINOR aura-plugins-8r500c holds
aura-plugins-tf2x2c and aura-plugins-jmw5j7.

METHOD. Archive copy of 223f86a, git-initialised with the origin remote, one binary built in
it. THREE further copies each carried ONE mutation and its own binary. Every number below was
read off a process or off a test run, never off a test name. I ran no gate; that axis is not
mine. My scratch copies are deleted.

=== 1. THE FOUNDING MUTATION IS NOW CAUGHT, AND THE NEW BYTES PIN IS REAL ===
cmd.ErrOrStderr() -> cmd.OutOrStdout() in the DRIVABLE OPEN ARM of recordLifecycleFault:
  TestTheFaultRecordOpenFailureIsReportedOnStandardErrorOnly  FAIL
  TestEveryFailingArmOfTheFaultWriterTellsTheOperatorOnStandardError  FAIL, at both the
  arm-by-arm assertion (:1832, "an if arm at hook_lifecycle.go:615 reports on
  cmd.OutOrStdout()") and the whole-function one (:1850).
Before round 19 the same edit left the whole package green. THE REINSTATEMENT IS PINNED.
THE MUTANT BYTES ARE EXACTLY WHAT MY PREDECESSOR MEASURED. OpenCode gate row, store path a
directory and the record path a directory: mutant stdout 481 bytes -
"pasture hook lifecycle could not open its fault record ... is a directory; the fault below is
reported on this stream only" AHEAD OF {"decision":"proceed"}. Control at this SHA: 22 bytes,
{"decision":"proceed"} alone. Replayed through the shipped plugin acceptProceed under Bun
1.3.13 - mutant THROWN "response is not JSON: SyntaxError ... Unexpected identifier pasture",
control PROCEED ACCEPTED. Both plugin artefacts are byte-identical (cmp).
THE EISDIR CLAIM HOLDS FOR THE USER I AM. uid 1000: the open arm reports "is a directory",
which is EISDIR and not a permission refusal. I also ran it as uid 0 with full capabilities in
a user namespace (unshare -r): SAME ARM, same message, exit 0, {"decision":"proceed"}. A
permission bit would not have bound that user; EISDIR does. The test input is root-proof as it
claims.

=== 2. THE FAIL-OPEN GUARANTEE, RE-MEASURED. 31 RUNS, NOT ONE VIOLATION ===
Store made unopenable (the --db path is a directory). DEFAULT (fail-open), 17 probes, EVERY
one exit 0 with that harness continue bytes and one durable record line:
  claude-code PreToolUse 0 bytes | codex PreToolUse {"continue":true} | opencode
  tool.execute.before {"decision":"proceed"} | opencode file.edited 0 bytes | codex
  SessionStart {} | claude-code SessionStart 0 bytes.
DEGENERATE PROBES, all exit 0 with continue bytes and a record: unknown event on claude-code
AND on opencode; unknown host version; malformed payload (not-json); unknown harness; EMPTY
STDIN on codex, opencode AND claude-code; a bad flag (--nope=1, through the SetFlagErrorFunc
arm); an unexpected positional argument on claude-code AND on opencode.
FAIL-CLOSED (PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1), 14 probes: exit 2 EXACTLY on the evidenced Claude
gate rows - PreToolUse, and the same row reached by empty stdin, malformed payload, bad flag,
unexpected positional and unknown host version. Exit 0 on the Claude observation row, on
PreCompact, on PostToolUse, on the unknown event, on every OpenCode row with its proceed bytes,
on Codex, and on the unknown harness. The blocking diagnostic names declared and effective
mode, the policy, the host evidence URL and the way back out (unset PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED).
NOT ONE PROBE produced an empty OpenCode body, a silent proceed, or a byte on stdout that was
not the harness continuation.

=== 3. THE LOSS-ROUTE PROSE IS NOW TRUE, ROUTE BY ROUTE, ON THE BINARY ===
AGENTS.md "### The lifecycle fault record" claims FIVE guarded failures, FOUR user-reachable,
ONE unreachable by construction, and says a directory that merely exists is not enough.
MEASURED, each on the built binary, OpenCode gate row:
  ROUTE 1a --db pasture.db (bare name)      exit 0, 22 bytes stdout, NO record, "could not
                                            place its fault record: the store path
                                            "pasture.db" names no directory"
  ROUTE 1b PASTURE_DB_PATH=pasture.db       identical, and the quoted path is the resolved one
  ROUTE 2a parent is a FILE                 exit 0, 22 bytes, NO record, "could not create the
                                            directory for its fault record"
  ROUTE 2b parent 0555, child must be made  exit 0, 22 bytes, NO record, same arm
  ROUTE 3a store directory exists, 0555     exit 0, 22 bytes, NO record, "could not open its
                                            fault record"
  ROUTE 3b a directory stands at the name    exit 0, 22 bytes, same arm
  CONTROL writable directory                 exit 0, 22 bytes, ONE record line
So route 3 - the route the paragraph was wrong about twice - is now named and is measured
true, and the closing fix line requires a directory that exists AND is writable AND has space.
Route 4 (append) is the only reachable route I could not drive; see my ruling on A below. The
paragraph and the code enumeration now agree on the count.

=== 4. THE PRODUCTION TIER HAS NOT MOVED ===
internal/timeouts/profile.go:98 ProductionProfile is New(Production, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s, 30s).
HookInvocation is 5 s. AGENTS.md:155 still carries **5 s** and :164-166 still names the 10 s
Claude Code budget. internal/timeouts is untouched by the three round-19 commits.

=== 5. THE ROUND SCOPE IS WHAT IT SAYS ===
git diff --stat 1ce711e..223f86a: four files - AGENTS.md, cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go,
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go, internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit_test.go.
NO codegen file, NO plugin artefact. Verified independently. No internal reference (Beads id,
SLICE-N, PROPOSAL-N, round number) enters any shipped diagnostic or AGENTS.md line in the diff.

=== THE ONE IMPORTANT: aura-plugins-4ajb9z ===
MY OWN MUTATION, production only, no test edited. ONE LINE ADDED beside the existing correct
stderr report in the drivable MkdirAll arm:
  cmd.OutOrStdout().Write([]byte("pasture: the fault record directory could not be made\n"))
FULL, UNFILTERED go test ./cmd/pasture/ ./internal/lifecycle/... -count=1 -> GREEN, cmd/pasture
ok 200.472s, exit 0. On the built mutant, OpenCode gate row, loss route 2: stdout 76 bytes with
the note AHEAD of {"decision":"proceed"}; replayed through acceptProceed under Bun 1.3.13 it
THROWS "response is not JSON". Control 22 bytes, PROCEED ACCEPTED. On a GATE callback nothing
catches that throw, so the user's tool call stops. THE FOUNDING BLOCKER, REINSTATED BY ONE
ADDED LINE, WITH THE WHOLE TREE GREEN.
WHY THE GUARD MISSES IT: faultWriterReports (:1732-1759) collects a stream only for a call on
the identifier fmt named Fprint/Fprintf/Fprintln. Any other write shape is invisible - and the
shape I used is the idiom THIS SAME FILE uses for stdout at hook_lifecycle.go:718.
TWO SENTENCES THIS ROUND SHIPPED ARE MEASURABLY WIDER THAN THE GUARD:
 - hook_lifecycle.go:496-497, PRODUCTION SOURCE: "no arm's word can move onto standard output".
 - the test doc at :1788-1791: the stream claim is "measured on the bytes a host actually
   receives and not only in the syntax tree". That holds for ONE of the THREE DRIVABLE arms.
   The open arm has assert.Empty(run.Stdout) at :1981 and CATCHES my injection when I put it
   there instead (RED). The no-directory arm's built-binary test CAPTURES stdout into a buffer
   at :1891-1893 and never asserts on it. The MkdirAll arm's pin is in-process and reads
   stderr only.
GRADED IMPORTANT for the same reason my axis graded aura-plugins-xrbt06 IMPORTANT in round 18:
behaviour at this SHA is correct and no user is harmed today, but the guard presented as
closing this family does not hold the property that decides harmless from blocking, and the
claim that it does is now in the production source where the next author reads it.
FIX, either is sufficient and both are small: (a) make the guard read the WRITER of every write
in the function, not only fmt.Fprint*, with the same exact-expression match the file already
uses - this is also what makes the STRUCTURAL cover of the two undrivable arms sound; or (b)
assert.Empty on the stdout buffer the no-directory built-binary test already captures, and
drive route 2 through the binary the same way.

=== THE TWO MINOR ===
aura-plugins-tf2x2c - THE OPEN-ARM TEST NAMES THE WRONG ASSERTION FOR ITS OWN MUTATION. Its doc
(:1951-1953) says the ErrOrStderr->OutOrStdout mutation "turns RED on the stdout assertion".
MEASURED: it turns RED at :1974, require.Contains(run.Stderr, "could not open its fault
record"), which is a REQUIRE and stops the run; assert.Empty at :1981 is never evaluated. The
test is red for a correct reason; the sentence names the wrong carrier. The stdout assertion is
not dead - it is what catches the injection in 4ajb9z - so the fix is to the sentence.
aura-plugins-jmw5j7 - THE CARRIER EDGE MAKES S0 UNCLOSABLE. See my ruling on B.

=== RULING A: IS A STRUCTURAL PIN SUFFICIENT FOR THE APPEND ARM? YES. ===
I would REFUSE a loopback filesystem or a quota for it, and I would refuse a production seam
whose only user is a test. Reasons, in order:
1. THE ARM CARRIES NO SEPARATE TRUTH TO MEASURE. Its report is one fmt.Fprintf on the same
   single constant faultRecordLossSuffix that the other four carry, so drift between arms is
   impossible by construction. What a bytes test would add over the structural pin is the
   STREAM at run time, and the stream is fully determined by the one expression the guard pins
   exactly.
2. THE COST IS A NEW TEST DEPENDENCY on filesystem-level input, in a package whose suite
   already runs 200 s. The slice has twice paid a real price for a cheap pin and both times
   the pin was the right shape, not a heavier harness.
3. THE PRECEDENT IS CONSISTENT. This slice accepted the structural argument for the encode arm
   (unreachable by construction) and refused a test-only production branch for the panic proof.
   The append arm is the same class: undrivable without changing what production code is.
4. THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO STOP AND ASK rather than simulate a failure it could not produce.
   A simulated write failure would have pinned the simulation.
ONE CONDITION, AND IT IS EXACTLY MY IMPORTANT: a structural pin is sufficient ONLY WHILE THE
STRUCTURE IS SEEN WHOLE. The two arms covered structurally are covered by a guard that reads
one call shape. Fix (a) of 4ajb9z is therefore not only a stdout fix - it is what makes my
answer to this question true.

=== RULING B: THE CARRIER IS REAL AND SUFFICIENT. I DO NOT HOLD S0 OPEN ON THAT ITEM. ===
MY PREDECESSOR'S TWO GROUNDS ARE BOTH DISCHARGED, and I verified each rather than reading the
report.
GROUND 1, the ownership premise: it was measured false and it has been CORRECTED where it was
written - in aura-plugins-u5ju80 itself, which now records that S0 wrote the sentence, that
the section-4 table is a WAVE-1 parallel-write table answering a different question, and that
the error was the supervisor's own. The routing now stands on the reason that was always the
honest one: correcting a GENERATED artefact needs a regeneration in the shared checkout, which
the standing staging rule forbids in a live worktree.
GROUND 2, "there is no carrier": there is one now, and it is first-class. u5ju80 holds BOTH the
correction AND the non-regression duty; it names all three sites (internal/codegen/
opencode_hooks.go:145, .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts:32, internal/codegen/
opencode_target_test.go); it names the reference wording (the two ends S0 corrected) and warns
the writer to read the CORRECTED AGENTS.md paragraph; and it asks for the phrase to be proved
load-bearing by mutation in the existing subject file. EDGES VERIFIED IN THE GRAPH: S6
(aura-plugins-ok39i3) is blocked-by u5ju80, and the finding aura-plugins-wzencw is blocked-by
u5ju80, so the finding CANNOT close when the S0 leaf closes. The round-17 leaf aura-plugins-
l4a7oj no longer claims wzencw in its closes-list; it carries an explicit
"partially_addresses_do_not_close" instead. That is precisely the test my predecessor set - a
task that OUTLIVES the closure of the finding that raised it, naming file, line and reference
wording - and it is met.
MY REMAINING OBJECTION IS NOT TO THE CARRIER BUT TO WHAT ITS EDGE DOES TO THE SCHEDULE, filed
as MINOR jmw5j7: u5ju80 -> wzencw -> r2emjl -> dqilos -> hc2jq3 -> gt001f. As recorded, S0
cannot reach a closed state until a WAVE-1 S6 leaf closes, and S1 cannot start until S0 closes.
Decide that deliberately and write it down - either close wzencw in S0 as PARTIALLY DISCHARGED
with the carrier named, or state plainly that S0 stays open in Beads until S6-L9 lands. What
must not happen is a closure achieved by quietly stepping over an edge somebody put there on
purpose.

=== THE STANDARD ===
NINETEEN ROUNDS, AND THIS ROUND COULD HAVE CLOSED THE SLICE. I did not lower the bar to reach
the exit and I did not manufacture a finding to avoid it. The IMPORTANT is my own mutation, run
on production source only, with the full unfiltered command and its timing recorded, the mutant
bytes measured, and the harm replayed through the shipped plugin; it has a one-line fix with a
precedent in the same file. Everything the round claims to have fixed, I re-measured and found
true.

=== GATES, EACH RUN FROM INSIDE AN ARCHIVE COPY OF d71e578, AND EACH ACTUALLY RAN ===
The copy is a fresh git repository built from `git archive d71e578`, with the pasture remote set.

4. nix flake check --no-build — RAN, exit 0: cgo-disabled-build, installer and race all green.

=== THE PINS DID NOT LOOSEN. FOUR ESCAPE MUTATIONS RE-RUN ON PRODUCTION SOURCE ===
  - a bare cmd.OutOrStdout().Write beside the open arm's correct stderr report: RED on BOTH
    TestEveryFailingArmOfTheFaultWriterTellsTheOperatorOnStandardError and
    TestTheFaultWriterDiscardsNoResultThatCouldCarryALoss.
  - a bare `defer file.Close()` back in place of the checked closure: RED on both.
  - a switch-shaped silent return added before the MkdirAll arm: RED on the arm enumeration.
  - the guard renamed in the test file alone: held by TestEveryTestNameCitedByTheLifecycleSourceExists.
Everything round 21 and round 22 claim to have fixed, I re-measured and found true.

=== RULING ON MY AXIS: THE FOUR POPULATIONS ARE NOT JOINTLY EXHAUSTIVE. THE THIRD ESCAPE EXISTS ===

I FOUND IT, and it is the same shape as the first two: the sentence written above the guard is
wider than the domain the guard is read over.

aura-plugins-yk3cpc — A WRITE WITH NO WRITER EXPRESSION. faultWriterWrites can only see a call
whose Fun is a SelectorExpr. fmt.Print, fmt.Printf and fmt.Println write to os.Stdout through an
IMPLICIT writer that appears in no expression, so guard 2 does not collect it and guard 3, which
refuses the STREAM ITSELF, has no expression to refuse. Bind the two results to real names and
guard 4 is silent too. MEASURED: `written, printErr := fmt.Println(...)` with `_ = written` and
`_ = printErr`, added to the close arm of recordLifecycleFault — full unfiltered cmd/pasture ok
208.076s and every internal/lifecycle package ok. The close arm is the ONE arm this round states
cannot be driven by the suite (test:2534-2538), so on that arm the structure is the sole witness,
and the witness is blind. In production that arm fires on a deferred-write filesystem, the bytes
land ahead of the host continuation, and on an OpenCode gate row the plugin's JSON.parse throws
and stops the user's tool call. That is aura-plugins-mihekg, reachable again with a green tree.

aura-plugins-iy9t5p — A DEFERRED CLOSURE BODY IS NEVER AN ARM. Three places (hook_lifecycle.go:
502-505, test:2022-2026, and the require message at test:2103-2106) say the reader collects "the
bodies of deferred closures". faultWriterArms has no *ast.FuncLit case. The count is 6 today only
because the one closure that exists happens to contain an if. MEASURED: a second deferred closure
holding `syncErr := file.Sync(); _ = syncErr` — arm count stays 6, nothing requires it to speak,
and the blank-identifier rule of guard 4 does not reach a result bound to a real name. That is a
record lost in silence, the identical defect round 21 fixed for `defer file.Close()`.

ARE THE GUARDS DEAD? NO. Guard 2's stdout-specific message can only fire for a resolved writer
that also names a forbidden stream, so guard 3 always fires with it — but BOTH are asserts, not
requires, so neither suppresses the other, and guard 2 stays alive on its own for every
sinkUnknown writer that names no stream at all (a parameter, a struct field, a buffer). The
redundancy buys a second, more specific message. That is a fair price and not a false witness.

IS COUNT EQUALITY THE RIGHT RELATION? YES, AS IT STANDS. The swap you name — one arm silent,
another reporting twice — cannot hide behind it, because the per-arm require.NotZero runs FIRST
and calls FailNow on the silent arm. The equality is doing a different job: it catches a report
standing OUTSIDE every collected arm, which the arm loop cannot see. Its one soft spot is
nesting, since an outer arm's ast.Inspect counts a report that stands inside an inner arm; but
today there is no nesting, and if nesting arrives the equality FAILS LOUDLY rather than passing.
That is the safe direction. NOTE FOR THE FIX: adding the FuncLit case for aura-plugins-iy9t5p
CREATES that nesting (closure body and the if inside it), so the counting relation has to be
re-derived in the same change and not merely re-run.

=== RULING ON THE QUESTION PUT TO THE WAVE: THE "os.OpenFile(" SOURCE-TEXT SINK RULE ===
I UPHOLD THE SUPERVISOR'S PROVISIONAL READING. Keep it. Reasons, in order:
1. IT REFUSES, IT DOES NOT ADMIT. An unresolvable writer is sinkUnknown and fails. The failure
   direction is the one that cannot ship a defect.
2. THE REFUSAL IS TRUE AND ACTIONABLE. The message at test:1992-2003 says plainly that this is
   NOT a claim that the maintainer wrote to standard output, names BOTH legitimate sinks, and
   tells them what to do for each. That is the property round 21 was told to fix, and it is fixed.
3. THE ALTERNATIVE COSTS PRODUCTION SHAPE FOR A TEST. Encoding the sink in the type system means
   a named seam — a sink type, or an io.Writer handed in — whose only consumer is the guard. This
   slice has repeatedly and rightly refused a production seam whose only user is a test (the panic
   proof, the append arm), and I would refuse one here on the same ground.
4. THE FAILURE IS AT TEST TIME, NOT IN FRONT OF AN OPERATOR.
WHAT I WOULD CHANGE, AND ITS PRICE, WHEN THE OPEN DOES MOVE INTO A HELPER: do not weaken the rule
to a name match. Resolve ONE level into a helper declared in the same package and take the sink
from that helper's returned os.OpenFile call, keeping the refusal for anything deeper. Cost is
about thirty lines of AST work plus a second population sentence naming the one level of
indirection. Until that day arrives, the syntactic rule with a safe failure is the right data
model and I would not spend the round on it.
ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A FINDING: the prefix admits ANY os.OpenFile call, not the record's path. It
is closed today only by assert.Len(records, 1) at test:2144. If a second file is ever opened here,
that assertion is what stands between you and a second unexplained sink; keep it.

=== RULING ON ROUND 22: THE CONTENT PIN OVER SHIPPED TEXT IS THE RIGHT RELATION ===
It does NOT duplicate the drift guard. The drift guard states an EQUALITY between the artefacts
and the generator; it is true of the false sentence and of the true one alike, which is exactly
the worker's reason and it is correct. The new pin states a PROPERTY of the content — that the
line offers the record rather than promising it, and names why it may be absent. Those are
different relations over different domains, and a repository that holds only the equality can
ship a wrong promise with everything green.
BYTE EQUALITY ACROSS THREE FILES IS NOT A MAINTENANCE TRAP HERE, because `make generate` is what
keeps the two artefacts equal to the generator and gate 3 above proves it holds at this SHA. A
hand edit of one artefact is precisely what the pin exists to refuse. The require on the read and
the require on `found` mean it cannot pass vacuously if a file moves.
PACKAGE. cmd/pasture reading the repository root is defensible and I do not raise it: the claim is
"the plugin promises only what the fault writer delivers", and the fault writer lives in
cmd/pasture. Putting it in internal/codegen would put the promise beside the recipe and away from
its referent, which is the mistake the pin was written to avoid. The truth it depends on —
retiredFaultRecordPromise and the loss routes — is stated beside the code that produces it.

=== THE STANDARD ===
Two axes would close this slice at 0/0/0 and I did not reach for it. Both findings are my own
mutations, run on production source only, on an archive copy, with the full unfiltered package
timing recorded, and each has a small fix stated at the population and not at the example. I did
not manufacture a MINOR to look thorough: the round-22 pin and the os.OpenFile rule are both
sound, and I said so.

text:
ROUND 23, AXIS A (host-contract truth and end-user behaviour). SHA d71e578, two commits over 223f86a.
VOTE: REVISE. Tally 0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR.
Review task aura-plugins-cf405u. Groups: BLOCKER aura-plugins-zq97z2 (CLOSED, empty), IMPORTANT aura-plugins-3gn6m0, MINOR aura-plugins-31stxn.
FINDINGS: IMPORTANT aura-plugins-vqdkyu; MINOR aura-plugins-u0qn7t.

READ-ONLY. Binary built from an archive copy of d71e578; the shipped plugin replayed under Bun; two mutations applied to the archive copy only and reverted (git status clean after each).

## The round-22 measurement, repeated and CONFIRMED
RECORD WRITTEN (opencode tool.execute.before, empty stdin, --db in a real directory): exit 0, stdout {"decision":"proceed"}, one record line, stderr one line, and the record path is NOT named on stderr (grep count 0).
RECORD LOST, four drivable routes, each exit 0 with correct host bytes and each quoting a path and ending in the shared loss clause: (1) --db pasture.db, quotes the store path; (2) parent is a file, quotes the directory it tried to create; (3) a directory at the record path, quotes the record path; (4) a symlink to /dev/full, quotes the record path, ENOSPC.
So the worker's premise holds: stderr distinguishes the two cases, the record path is spoken only when the record is lost.

## JUDGEMENT OF THE NEW SENTENCE
The record clause is now honest: it offers rather than promises, gives the reason, and covers both cases. That half is fixed.
The sentence FAILS on its own imperative. Its first and third clauses send the operator to standard error, and the plugin that prints it spawns pasture with stderr:"pipe", reads fd 2 into a local, and uses that local ONLY inside the exitCode !== 0 throw. On the belt route, which is exit 0 with an empty body, the diagnostic is captured and dropped, and because fd 2 is piped and not inherited it never reaches the host's own stream either. Replayed under Bun against the shipped artefact with a stand-in older binary: the belt line printed, the host continued, and the child's diagnostic text was ABSENT from every stream. The operator who obeys the instruction finds nothing, and cannot tell which of the two cases they are in — the exact distinction this rewrite was made to give them. It is the round-22 defect in new words: evidence named to a reader who cannot reach it. The plugin already surfaces stderr on the non-zero-exit route, so the idiom exists; one line inside invokeLifecycle makes the imperative true, and I measured that it does. Detail and the suggested pin are in aura-plugins-vqdkyu.
The name and the place ARE real: lifecycleFaultRecordFile is "lifecycle-faults.jsonl" and lifecycleFaultRecordPath puts it beside the resolved store path, matching AGENTS.md. Verified against the product, not against the sentence.
No internal references in either shipped artefact.

## THE OTHER MANDATED CHECKS, ALL RE-MEASURED, ALL CLEAN
1. FAIL-OPEN. Three harnesses x both policy skews x unknown event, unknown host version, malformed payload, unknown harness, empty stdin, a bad flag, an unexpected positional: every combination exit 0 with a non-empty stderr, no silent proceed, and no empty OpenCode gate body (opencode gate rows always {"decision":"proceed"}, codex {"continue":true}, claude-code empty by contract). The D4/D9 matrix is honoured on the real harness ids: claude-code PreToolUse (evidenced blocking gate) + PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 -> exit 2; UserPromptExpansion (unevidenced gate) + fail-closed -> exit 0; SessionStart -> exit 0; every row fail-open -> exit 0. An unknown harness id resolves to observe-only and never blocks, and the fail-closed diagnostic says in words that the opt-in had no channel on that event.
2. FOUNDING MUTATION, still dead. cmd.ErrOrStderr() -> cmd.OutOrStdout() on the open arm (drivable): TestEveryFailingArmOfTheFaultWriterTellsTheOperatorOnStandardError RED at three assertions and TestTheFaultRecordOpenFailureIsReportedOnStandardErrorOnly RED. Built the mutant: stdout carries the 268-byte diagnostic AHEAD of {"decision":"proceed"}, and the shipped plugin replayed against it threw "response is not JSON" — the user's tool call stopped. Reverted.
3. THE SIXTH ARM cannot fire on a healthy run. The checked Close reports only when Close returns an error. 30 faulting invocations with a healthy record write: 30 record lines, 0 close reports, and no other stray byte on stderr. The record-written case carries exactly one stderr line.
4. THE TIER HAS NOT MOVED. ProductionProfile HookInvocation = 5s, half the 10s Claude budget, and timeouts.New still refuses an inverted tier. TestProfile 6s, DeadlineTest 1s.
5. MY OWN MUTATION. I renamed the product's record file (lifecycleFaultRecordFile -> "lifecycle-fault-records.jsonl") to ask whether anything ties the shipped operator sentence to the file the product really writes. RED, but only in internal/codegen (TestOpenCodeGeneratedGateSurvivesARealPastureFault); the whole cmd/pasture package stayed green for 203s, although that package owns BOTH the constant and the pin on the sentence that names the file. The name therefore cannot drift silently, so I file no finding, but the tie is incidental: the belt pin asserts a substring and never compares it with lifecycleFaultRecordFile. Recording it so a later round can decide whether to anchor it deliberately.

The slice is close. The fail-open guarantee, the exit authority, the fault-writer sweep and the tier all hold under re-measurement. What remains is one clause of freshly shipped operator text that its own reader cannot act on.

text:
VOTE: REVISE - 0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR (plus one duplicate withdrawn to axis A).
Axis C, round 23, SHA d71e578 (1cd72d5 + d71e578 over 223f86a). Read-only. Gates run by another axis.

FINDINGS
- BLOCKER group aura-plugins-p8kpkj: CLOSED EMPTY.
- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-j8lqii: hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go:2052-2057 claims the close
  arm is driven on host bytes by TestEveryDrivableFaultRecordLossIsMeasuredOnTheHostBytes.
  That test says, at :2534-2538, that the close arm is NOT driven there, and it has two
  subtests, neither of them the close arm. Both sentences are new in 1cd72d5.
- MINOR aura-plugins-4ek5ia: AGENTS.md's SIX/FIVE fault-route counts are hand-kept and no test
  reads them; the code-side count IS pinned at :2102, so a seventh arm bumps the test and
  leaves the document behind. This is the same argument round 22 used to build the OpenCode
  belt pin.
- WITHDRAWN as a duplicate: aura-plugins-mwkvf5, the AGENTS.md "route route" duplicated word.
  Axis A filed the identical finding as aura-plugins-u0qn7t this same round. It is still open.

THE REACH CLAIM IS TRUE. Every cited mutation re-run on an archive copy of d71e578, each alone,
with the failing line read from the run and not from the report.
ROUND 21
1. bare cmd.OutOrStdout().Write beside a correct stderr report, in the MkdirAll arm:
   RED at :2570 (host bytes, REACHED - the run reported "Should be empty, but was pasture:
   leaked", so no require above it called FailNow), and at :2112, :2133, :2140, :2152, :2271.
2. bare `defer file.Close()` restored: RED at :2271 and :2102. Both REACHED, both claimed.
3. `_, _ = file.Write([]byte("partial"))`: RED at :2271 as claimed, and at :2144.
4. unchecked buffered flush (bufio.NewWriter + `defer buffered.Flush()`): RED at :2271 as
   claimed, and at :2133, :2140, :2144. The report cites ":2126/:2138"; those two lines are a
   closing brace and an append statement, not assertions. The true assertion is :2140. The
   mutation IS red and DOES reach real assertions; only the two line numbers in the report are
   off. Noted, not filed.
5. guard renamed IN THE TEST FILE ONLY: RED at :2166 and :2330, exactly as claimed. The rename
   was a PREFIX extension and the \b anchor still refused it.
ROUND 22, all four on the corrected operator sentence
6. restore the retired clause in the shipped plugin only: RED at :2685, :2706, :2710, :2714,
   :2720.
7. restore it in the generator only: RED at the same five.
8. stale-regeneration reword ("A line may also have been appended" -> "A line was appended") in
   one artefact: RED at :2710 and :2720, the agreement assertion, as claimed.
9. drop the standard-error clause in all three files: RED at :2706, as claimed.

MY OWN MUTATIONS, THREE
A. THE SWAP (the count-relation question). Open arm silenced, MkdirAll arm made to report
   TWICE, so the report count still equals the branch count. NOT hidden: RED at :2122
   (require.NotZero, per arm) and at the byte pins :2492/:2495. Count equality does not hide a
   swap, because the claim is stated per arm before it is stated over the count.
B. VACUITY OF THE ROUND-22 PIN. Renamed .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts away: RED at
   :2679 with the message "if it has moved, this pin must move with it rather than pass
   vacuously". It cannot pass on a missing or renamed file.
C. THE NEW RESOLUTION SEAM. Hoisted `operator := cmd.OutOrStdout()` and reported through it:
   RED at :2112, :2133 and :2152, and the message names the binding ("is handed operator, which
   this function binds to cmd.OutOrStdout()"). The seam that stopped the false refusal did not
   open an escape.

THE OTHER CHECKS
1. VACUOUS PASSES: every new guard is non-empty at both ends. require.Len(arms, 6);
   assert.Len(reports, 6) and assert.Len(records, 1); require.NotEmpty(declared) AND
   require.NotEmpty(cited) in the citation guard; require.NoError on each ReadFile and
   require.NotEmpty(found) in the belt pin. Verified by mutation B for the belt pin.
2. COUNT RELATION 5 -> 6: verified by mutation A. No swap passes.
3. PIN DIRECTION: nothing loosened. The removed assertions are require.Len(arms,5) ->
   require.Len(arms,6); require.NotEmpty(streams) -> require.NotZero(reports), which excludes
   the record write and is stricter; two assert.Equal("cmd.ErrOrStderr()", stream) ->
   assertFaultWriterStream, which admits a second sink only because the write population now
   SEES the record write, which the old fmt-only population did not; and the deliberate
   require -> assert at :2492, whose only effect is that the run continues, confirmed by
   mutation A reporting both :2492 and :2495 from one run.
4. THE ROUND-22 PIN: not vacuous (B), and not a duplicate of the codegen drift guard. The drift
   guard compares an artefact WITH its generator and would agree on a wrong sentence; this pin
   states what the sentence must and must not say, then requires byte equality across all
   three. Mutations 6-9 separate the two: 8 is caught only by the agreement half, 9 only by the
   content half.
5. TRACEABILITY: branch total over 223f86a is EXACTLY SIX files. Each commit carries an
   Ownership paragraph naming exactly the files that commit touched - 1cd72d5 three, d71e578
   four (opencode_hooks.go plus both artefacts plus the test file). The round-22 growth is
   stated in the commit that made it, as the standing rule requires. The SLICE description's
   ownership fold, which is the supervisor's half, still stops at round 3.
6. HONEST LIMITS: the limit IS stated, at :2534-2538, in the words "that limit is stated rather
   than dressed up as coverage". It is also contradicted forty lines earlier - that is finding
   aura-plugins-j8lqii, and it is the only reason this vote is not ACCEPT.
7. THE FOURTH FILE: none. `git grep` at d71e578 finds the retired clause in NO shipped file
   (only in the test, as the constant it refuses), and finds "Pasture did not evaluate",

author: David Huu Pham
text:

IMPORTANT aura-plugins-8rbxdh; MINOR aura-plugins-utar7q.
FINDINGS: IMPORTANT aura-plugins-qx9up0; MINOR aura-plugins-8p19wa.

READ-ONLY. Nothing was written, created or deleted inside the worktree. Every gate and every
mutation ran in my own archive copy under my scratch directory. Two copies: one pristine
gate copy, never edited; one mutation copy, reverted with `git checkout -- .` after each
mutation and left clean. The shared scratch area was touched only for my own directories.

## ALL SIX GATES RAN, FROM INSIDE THE ARCHIVE COPY OF 312e469

1. go build ./...                     RAN. exit 0.
2. go test -race -count=1 ./...       RAN. exit 0, 72 packages ok, no FAIL, no DATA RACE.
3. make generate                      RAN. exit 0, and `git status --porcelain` printed
                                      NOTHING afterwards. Clean.
4. nix flake check --no-build         RAN. exit 0. cgo-disabled-build, installer and race
                                      all green.
5. gofmt -l .                         RAN. gofmt's OWN exit code was captured inside the dev
                                      shell, not a pipeline's: exit 0, ZERO files listed.
6. go vet ./...                       RAN. exit 0.

NEGATIVE CONTROL FOR GATE 5, because a checker that lists nothing is indistinguishable from
one that is not looking. I copied hostexit.go into a separate scratch directory, appended a
function with wrong indentation and a doubled space, and ran the same command: gofmt LISTED
probe.go, AND ITS EXIT CODE WAS STILL 0. That confirms both halves -- the checker looks, and
the trap is real: gofmt -l never exits non-zero, so the gate is "prints nothing", never an
exit code. `make fmt` was not used.

## THE DECOMPOSITION. I JUDGE IT CORRECT.

IS "WAS THE DELIVERY WRITTEN?" THE RIGHT SINGLE AXIS? Yes, and the code proves it by
counterexample rather than by assertion. The type is a total, exclusive partition of ONE
epistemic axis with three answers -- yes, no, and pasture did not learn -- and "unknown" is a
peer of the other two rather than a defect, because the type reports pasture's KNOWLEDGE of a
fact and not the fact. The rejected alternative, a stage that also answered "was it
evaluated?", is not a function of the first axis: ErrLifecycleDeliveryRefused is (written,
NOT evaluated) and ErrLifecycleCommittedWithoutContinuation is (written, evaluated). Two
distinct points share one value of the chosen axis, so a combined stage would have needed a
fourth arm and each arm would then carry two meanings. The stage is not carrying two
questions in disguise. Whether pasture could evaluate is stated once, in the What, and that
sentence is true of both users.

IS THE PAIR TABLE THE RIGHT RELATION, OR A CROSS-PRODUCT THAT SHOULD BE A DERIVATION? It is
already a derivation IN THE PRODUCT CODE: recordClause is computed once from the stage, above
the switch, and every arm that speaks of the journal concatenates it. The twelve pairs are
not a model cross-product; they are a GUARD OVER THAT DERIVATION, and the defect they guard
-- an arm hard-coding a sentence instead of taking the derived clause -- is visible only by
driving each arm, because from outside the package there is no way to assert "this arm used
the derived local". So the relation is right. I proved it fires: I wrote
"and no occurrence was recorded for it" into the blocking arm's impact, and
TestTheBlockingArmMakesNoDurableStateClaim went red naming the reason.

THE BLOCKING-ARM EXCLUSION. SOUND. The arm never reads fault.Stage, so a durable-state
sentence there would be a claim made on behalf of every stage that can reach it. The
exclusion is not an absence: it is a POSITIVE pin that forbids all three sentences, driven
with the stage most likely to leak into it. One drive is enough precisely because the
forbid-list is all three sentences and not one.

IS ANY STAGE UNREACHABLE, OR ANY PAIR VACUOUS? No. All three stages have a production
producer -- not-recorded on four routes, record-unknown on the deadline, recorded on the
refused delivery, which is measured end to end on a real store for all three harnesses. All
twelve inputs map and each is asserted. Note that ErrLifecycleCommittedWithoutContinuation is
unreachable on the production path today (PassThroughCommitBarrier cannot fail and both
encoders cannot), so the recorded stage rests on the refused-delivery producer; that is
stated in the source and is not a defect. The one imprecision I found in the twelve is the
MINOR: four pairs are NAMED for an arm they do not reach, because the stage is half the
selector and the row names state only the other half.

## THE ROUTES. I ENUMERATED THEM MYSELF, FROM THE SOURCE, AND THE LIST I WAS GIVEN IS WRONG.

Six lifecycleFault calls, all in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go: :152 outer panic recovery,
:170 environment refusal, :175 argument refusal, :250 deadline abandonment, :283 handler
error, and :848 THE FLAG-PARSE ERROR inside the SetFlagErrorFunc registered in init().
THE SIXTH ROUTE IS NOT THE ORPHANS SUBCOMMAND. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans.go holds
no lifecycleFault call and no FaultStage reference; it is a read-side operator command. The
sweep's judged reason, written in this round's own commit, names that non-existent route and
omits the flag-parse one -- which is the only route outside lifecycleOutcome and therefore
the one whose truth conditions differ most. That is aura-plugins-qx9up0.

EVERY ROUTE'S DECLARED STAGE IS TRUE OF IT ON THIS SHA. I checked each against what has
happened at that point in the program, not against the report:
 - :152, :170, :175, :848 fault before the store is opened. not-recorded is true.
 - :250 abandons work that runs in a goroutine and commits the receipt before the bytes are
   produced. record-unknown is true.
 - :283 selects recorded for exactly the two sentinels, and I verified both at their source:
   ErrLifecycleDeliveryRefused is returned only AFTER service.Receive succeeded
   (internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:245-273), and ErrLifecycleCommittedWithoutContinuation
   only after HookLifecycleResponse returned nil (:460-474). The default not-recorded covers
   deliveryWarrant, EnsureActiveMetamodel, deliveryDerive and a failing Receive, none of which
   commits a delivery.
THE SECOND DEFECT IS VERIFIED. Both routes now declare recorded, and the fix is load-bearing:
restoring the pre-round stages turned four tests red.
I LOOKED FOR A THIRD AND FOUND ONE. It is aura-plugins-qx9up0.

## RULING ON LIMIT 1 -- THE SWEEP DOES NOT PROVE A STAGE IS TRUE OF ITS ROUTE

ACCEPTED AS A STRUCTURAL LIMIT, REFUSED AS A COVERAGE EXCUSE, AND THE GAP IS NARROWER THAN
THE LIMIT AND ALSO REAL. The limit itself is correctly stated and cannot be closed by an AST
reader: whether a durable write precedes a call site is not decidable from the syntax there,
so no cheap structural relation replaces it. The right complement is a behavioural drive per
route, and FOUR OF SIX ROUTES ALREADY HAVE ONE -- I confirmed by mutation that the deadline
route and the handler-error route each turn multiple tests red when their stage is swapped
for another judged one. TWO DO NOT. Swapping the flag-parse route to recorded left the whole
cmd/pasture package green for 208.416s; swapping the argument-refusal route left it green for
210.552s. So the limit is not uniform: it bites on exactly the two routes the enumeration
gets wrong.
PRICE OF THE CHANGE I DEMAND: two behavioural cases on the built binary, one positional
argument and one unparsable flag, asserting "durable state not-recorded" on stderr. No lock,
no goroutine, no fixture, and buildLifecycleBinary already exists -- call it a few dozen
lines. I am NOT demanding a stronger structural relation, only that the two undriven routes
join the four driven ones. After that the limit shrinks to the panic-recovery route alone,
which is limit 2.

## RULING ON LIMIT 2 -- THE PANIC RECOVERY DECLARES NOT-RECORDED OVER A POST-COMMIT REGION

LEGITIMATE FOLLOW-UP. S0 MUST NOT FIX IT. No finding raised.
REASON, measured on the source rather than assumed. The window is real but empty on this SHA.
The outer defer covers three things after a successful commit: `native := work.native`, the
`return hostexit.ForDecision(...)` struct literal, and `defer cancel()`. None can panic. It
also covers the lifecycleFault calls themselves, so a panic inside recordLifecycleFault on
the deadline or the recorded route WOULD re-enter with not-recorded and overwrite a true
record-unknown or recorded with a false not-recorded -- and that is the honest statement of
the hazard, sharper than "a panic after the commit". But recordLifecycleFault's one known
panic source is recordedCause on a nil cause, and the sentinel there closes it; the source
already says that sentinel is load-bearing. So the false claim is unreachable by construction
today, exactly like the two exit-1 arms this package already documents as unreachable and
handles anyway.
THE COST OF FIXING IT BADLY IS HIGHER THAN THE HAZARD. The obvious fix -- a mutable
"stage so far" the recovery reads -- reintroduces the shared mutable claim that this package
removed when it made Stage a required call-site argument whose zero value is refused.
IF IT IS FIXED LATER, HERE IS WHAT THE RECOVERY IS ALLOWED TO KNOW: only the WEAKEST TRUE
claim for the region it is standing in, never a stronger one. Concretely that is
not-recorded from the head of lifecycleOutcome until the work goroutine is STARTED, and
record-unknown from that instant onward -- because from the moment the goroutine exists,
pasture cannot know which side of the commit a panic landed on. It must never be allowed to
say "recorded". One local, set on the line that starts the goroutine, read only by the
deferred recovery. That is a deliberate choice about knowledge, which is why it belongs to a
round that can make it and not to a fix bolted onto this one.

## EARLIER ESCAPES RE-RUN. ALL STILL CAUGHT. NONE HAS ROTTED.

Each mutation applied alone to the mutation copy and reverted:
 - bare cmd.OutOrStdout().Write in the append arm -> RED, both the write-population guard and
   the discard guard, naming the stream and the OpenCode consequence.
 - bare `defer file.Close()` -> RED, discard guard, and the arm count guard.
 - writer-less fmt.Println in the close arm -> RED, named as os.Stdout implicit, named by no
   expression.
 - `if closeErr == nil` -> RED, "a branch of this writer is entered when a call SUCCEEDED".
 - live-variable discard (`syncErr := file.Sync()` appended to a slice) -> RED, both guards.
 - callee write (a neighbour function naming stdout on the writer's behalf) -> RED, "may not
   CALL a function in this file that names a stream it may not use itself".

## MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION

 A. Wrote a durable-state sentence into the BLOCKING arm's impact -> RED,
    TestTheBlockingArmMakesNoDurableStateClaim. The exclusion holds.
 B. Swapped the DEADLINE route to not-recorded, a judged stage, so the AST sweep passes ->
    the sweep did pass, and TWO behavioural tests went red. Limit 1 does not bite here.
 C. Swapped the FLAG-PARSE route to recorded -> GREEN, 208.416s. Limit 1 bites here.
 D. Swapped the ARGUMENT-REFUSAL route to recorded -> GREEN, 210.552s. Limit 1 bites here.

## THE DERIVED STAGE TABLE. VERIFIED, AND IT CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY.

I appended a fourth stage, added it to IsValid and gave it a String():
TestEveryFaultStageRendersItsOwnDurableStateOnEveryArm went RED with
"stage \"probe\" is declared and this sweep does not ask about it". The derivation holds.
It cannot pass vacuously either: the inner loop requires each of the three written stages to
be IsValid, so an IsValid that answered false for everything fails there instead of skipping
silently.
THE TWO REFUSAL PROBES ARE CONFIRMED COMPUTED. stageAboveTheLastArm() derives the sentinel
from IsValid, and under the same four-stage mutation BOTH probes stayed correct --
TestFaultStageZeroValueRefuses and the "stage above the last arm" case moved to the new
sentinel instead of asserting that a declared stage was invalid.
OBSERVATIONS, NOT FINDINGS, on that derivation: the scan bound `candidate < 64` is itself
written down on a uint8 type, so a hand-assigned stage at or above 64 would escape; with iota
this cannot happen, and I do not ask for a change. The mode, policy and exit-status probes
still use written-down `+1` expressions of the shape the stage probe was corrected away from;
they fail LOUDLY rather than silently if an arm is appended, so they are a maintainer cost
and not an untruth, but the same correction would be cheap.

## OTHER THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND

 - The OpenCode diagnostic forwarding is MEASURED, not asserted: the belt proof now reads
   stdout and stderr apart, spawns a real fake binary that writes on stderr at exit 0, and
   requires the plugin to forward it. Real transport, real Bun.
 - Both plugin artefacts carry the identical change, and make generate leaves the tree clean.
 - The AGENTS.md route list moved to SIX guarded failures / FIVE user-reachable with the
   close route written out, and it is held against the code count by the arm guard.
 - No orphan probe residue: my copies are outside the worktree and the worktree was never
   written to.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ACCEPT. Both findings are the same class this slice has graded as findings
for twenty-seven rounds: a statement about a POPULATION that is wider or narrower than the
population it is read over. The IMPORTANT one is not a wording slip -- the enumeration is
wrong at BOTH ends, and the end it is wrong about is provably the end nothing drives. I did
not manufacture it: I found it by doing what this round asked, enumerating the routes myself
instead of taking the list, and then I measured the consequence twice.
