and mutation ran in my own archive copy of 1eeb7f2 under my own scratch directory. Four
mutant binaries were built there and every mutation was reverted with `git checkout --`
immediately after its build; the tracked tree ended clean. Nothing of another team's was
touched in the shared scratch area.

## MY THREE ROUND-28 FINDINGS. ALL THREE ARE FIXED. VERIFIED ON RENDERED BYTES.

1. aura-plugins-s6e9eo - FIXED. Each of the three decode-stop dispositions now carries its
own fix and NEITHER names an identity field NOR the host version. Driven, claude-code:
  malformed  -> "Send well-formed JSON. Nothing about the fields or the host version was
                 inspected on this route, because ingress stopped at the decode ..."
  invalid UTF-8 -> "Send UTF-8. Nothing about the fields ... stopped at the encoding check"
  duplicate field -> "Send each field once. ... no field or version check was reached"
The identity clause is gone from all three; it is present only where the identities were
reached. Two mutations prove the fix is HELD, not merely present: setting
ReachedIdentities:true on the malformed row turned
TestEachRefusalDispositionCarriesTheFixThatFollowsIt RED naming the route that never ran;
widening the UnsupportedSchema fix arm to `default:` turned the same test RED on all three
decode-stop subtests.
CaptureTruncated and CaptureOverLimit HAVE NO PRODUCER AT THIS SHA - I grepped the whole
tree, they appear only in the enum and in the comment that says why they are absent, not
even in a test. Removing them silenced NOTHING: I drove the over-limit route and it has its
own message ("The native payload exceeds the 1048576-byte bound"), and `hook lifecycle list`
was EMPTY afterwards, so its "no occurrence was recorded for it" is true. An unlisted
disposition would fall to the `!named` default, which refuses to invent a reason and says so.

THE HOST-VERSION REVERSAL, JUDGED AS THE OPERATOR READS IT. THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO RESTORE
IT. "Was it inspected?" and "could it be the cause?" are different questions, and the
sentence only ever asks the second: it says "CHECK TOO that the host version on the command
line is the version the host actually runs, BECAUSE THE EVENT A HOST REPORTS CAN CHANGE
BETWEEN VERSIONS". That is an instruction plus a hypothesis, not a claim of inspection, and
the hypothesis is TRUE of this route by construction - the --event value comes from an
artefact pasture generated for a PINNED host version, so a host on a different version that
renamed the event produces exactly this refusal. It is also USEFUL: it is the only clause
that reaches the cause an operator cannot see from the payload alone. It is correctly ABSENT
on the three decode-stop routes, which say plainly that the version was not inspected there,
and correctly PRESENT on unsupported-schema, where a renamed correlation field is the same
class of cause. I verified the ordering claim at the source rather than taking it: claude's
validateMembers checks hook_event_name BEFORE the identity loop, so "did not reach them" is
true of the mismatch route.

2. aura-plugins-54tbuy - THE PANIC IS FIXED, ON BOTH PATHS, AND I DROVE BOTH.
  PATH ONE, the reachable one: panic injected in PassThroughCommitBarrier.AfterCommit, which
  runs after the durable commit INSIDE the work goroutine. rc 0, {"decision":"proceed"},
  "durable state record-unknown", "an occurrence for it MAY OR MAY NOT exist - look for it in
  the lifecycle occurrence journal", one fault record line. `hook lifecycle list` on that
  store held the row WITH A FULL INTERPRETED SET. The retired sentence is gone and the hedge
  is honest.
  PATH TWO, the weaker claim: panic injected BEFORE the work goroutine starts. rc 0,
  continue bytes, "durable state not-recorded", "no occurrence was recorded for it", and
  `hook lifecycle list` was EMPTY. TRUE.

  reads, widened ONCE on the line that starts the work, never "recorded". Deleting that
  widening line turns TestTheOuterPanicRecoveryNeverClaimsMoreThanItsRegionCanSupport RED,
  so the worker's replacement for its own dead pin is live.

3. aura-plugins-innp1u - FIXED. The dead filter is gone. The message now says "none of the
identities this event requires was bound (session, tool-call)", which is a claim about
PASTURE'S OUTCOME and is true - every parser returns nil bindings on a refusing disposition,
which I re-confirmed at all three parsers. It no longer implies a discrimination it cannot
make, and a single-identity event renders the singular form ("the session identity this
event requires was not bound"), which I drove.

## RE-MEASURED. NOTHING ASSUMED.

4. THE BLOCKER aura-plugins-j30cwo DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Fifteen drives, three harnesses x
five probes (identity-A missing, identity-B missing, both missing, RENAMED, EMPTY STRING).
EVERY ONE: rc 0; the harness's own continue bytes (opencode {"decision":"proceed"} 22 B,
codex {"continue":true} 17 B, claude-code empty by contract); a 2008-2035 byte diagnostic
saying WAS NOT EVALUATED; exactly ONE lifecycle-faults.jsonl line; and one journal row with
interpreted=- on `hook lifecycle list`. The founding fail-open defect is closed.

5. THE USER-HARM WITNESS. The plugin SHIPPED AT 7e8be34, taken VERBATIM out of git, imported
into a Bun replay against a binary built from 1eeb7f2 on a healthy store:
  good payload            -> "HOST-CONTINUED: the user's tool call proceeds", bun rc 0
  RENAMED IDENTITY FIELDS -> "HOST-CONTINUED: the user's tool call proceeds", bun rc 0
A MIXED INSTALL IS NOW SAFE. That is the case lifecycleContinuation's own comment names as
the reason the bytes exist, and it is delivered.

6. REGRESSION. ELEVEN valid invocations - three claude-code events, two codex, two opencode,
and four more under version skew - ZERO stderr bytes and ZERO fault records on every one.

7. FAIL-OPEN. 42 measurements: three harnesses x two host-version skews x seven degenerate
probes (empty stdin, whitespace, null, [], {}, truncated JSON, over-limit). ALL 42 rc 0. NO
SILENT PROCEED - every one carried a diagnostic of 1058 B or more. NO EMPTY OPENCODE GATE
BODY - all 14 OpenCode rows emitted {"decision":"proceed"}, all 14 Codex rows
{"continue":true}.

8. THE FAIL-CLOSED OPT-IN ON THE UNBINDABLE ROUTE IS LIVE AND CORRECT PER HARNESS.
claude-code PreToolUse with a renamed session field: unset -> rc 0 "exit continue"; set ->
RC 2 "exit block" with the right fix ("to let the host continue ... unset
PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED"). Codex continues under the opt-in and says WHY in ITS words -
the evidence rule, with the action that would change it. OpenCode continues and says a
DIFFERENT and equally correct why - the exit code is not a channel this host reads. Two
reasons, two rows, neither borrowed.

9. THE FOUNDING MUTATION IS STILL RED AND STILL LETHAL. ErrOrStderr -> OutOrStdout in
emitLifecycleOutcome: RED on six subtests of TestLifecycleLeafFaultsExitZeroAndReport and on
TestWithheldOpenCodeEventIsNotAdmittedByBuiltCLI. LETHAL: I built the mutant and replayed the
7e8be34 plugin under Bun against it - renamed fields gave "pasture hook lifecycle response is
not JSON" and HOST-CONTINUED was never printed. The founding harm returns the moment the
guard is removed.

10. THE 5 s TIER, MEASURED END TO END. A real BEGIN EXCLUSIVE held by a separate process:
rc 0, {"decision":"proceed"}, a 1553-byte diagnostic naming its "5s hook-invocation
deadline", durable state record-unknown, one fault record line, and an EMPTY journal
afterwards. Against the 10 s Claude budget that leaves 5 s, and the 10 s figure is not
folklore - it is the `"timeout": 10` written in this repository's own hooks/hooks.json and
in the generated claude-code asset. The pin refuses under 2 s headroom.

11. THE TWO NEWLY DRIVEN ROUTES. Argument refusal and flag-parse refusal both give rc 0, the
harness's continue bytes and one fault record line, and on BOTH the ONLY file beside the
record is the record: NO pasture.db, NO -wal, NO -shm. "not-recorded" is true of them, on the
filesystem and not only in the code. Their MINOR is aura-plugins-tuonu5, on a different
clause.

12. MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION - FOUR, all built and driven.
  M1 ReachedIdentities:true on the malformed row -> RED, naming the step that did not run.
  M2 the UnsupportedSchema fix arm widened to `default:` -> RED on all three decode-stop
     dispositions. Round 28's per-disposition fix is genuinely held.
  M3 delete the `panicStage = FaultStageRecordUnknown` widening -> RED. The replacement for
     the worker's dead pin is live.
  M4 the founding stream swap, re-run as a LETHALITY probe under real Bun (item 9).

## WHY THIS IS NOT AN ACCEPT

Both IMPORTANTs are the class this slice has graded for twenty-nine rounds: a sentence that
is true of the population its author had in mind and false of the one the operator is in.
  aura-plugins-jljuzn - a Claude payload that CARRIES every identity field under the exact
  declared name is told it does not carry them or renamed them, because the unknown-member
  refusal shares a disposition with the missing-identity refusal. I proved it with a CONTROL:
  delete the extra member and the same session_id binds and stderr is zero bytes. A host that
  ADDS a field is the commonest host evolution there is, and Claude is the only harness that
  refuses on it.
  aura-plugins-kregfh - a REGRESSION OF THIS ROUND. Fixing 54tbuy gave record-unknown a
  second producer, and the fix clause keyed on that stage still speaks only for the first:
  a panicking invocation is told a long-running store writer is the usual reason and to retry
  once it releases the store, on the same line whose cause says the work panicked. I drove
  the deadline route too and the clause is CORRECT there, which is what makes it wrong here.
Neither breaks the host contract. Both give the reader a first step that cannot succeed.

I did not manufacture either. I found the first by driving an input nothing in the tree
drives, and the second by reading the fix line of a route this round newly created.

text:
ROUND 30 COMPLETE. FINAL SHA 098f1b3, worktree clean, nothing pushed, nothing closed. Ten items; item 3 landed PARTIALLY with an explicit ask attached.
ITEM 1: the route sweep said "the command's source" and parsed ONE file. Now parses every non-test source of the package. MEASURED BOTH WAYS: a seventh route in hook_lifecycle_orphans.go is RED with the fix and GREEN with the reader reverted to one file.
ITEM 2: the default durable-state claim was not-recorded, which ASSERTS nothing was written - a promise about every unenumerated error, falsified by a journal appender that can fail after a successful commit with no sentinel. Default is now record-unknown (the weakest claim), and the ordinary refusals keep the precise one on EVIDENCE via ErrLifecycleBeforeDurableWrite, set once at the line the durable region begins. internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go was NOT needed.
ITEM 3 PARTIAL + ASK: reproduced with a control (one added member -> 2000B of false diagnostic; remove it -> 0B). The shared sentence is now TRUE for all three causes of the disposition and the route is DRIVEN. It still cannot DISCRIMINATE; the split needs internal/lifecycle/model/occurrence.go and internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/capture.go, both outside my set. ASKED, not assumed.
ITEM 4: the writer remedy was keyed on a stage with three producers; moved to the deadline cause and pinned by a PAIR that shows it appears for the deadline and not for a panic. A hostexit assertion that REQUIRED the misplaced remedy is corrected with its reason.
ITEMS 5-10: paraphrase recognition restored while keeping the derived set; the static phase clause dropped (this package holds no event, and the flag-parse route names it ""); a derived failure mode must name itself; lifecyclePanicCause's swallowed doc restored; the "Round 27" ordinal removed; and 1eeb7f2's over-naming corrected in this commit's message, with named==touched verified mechanically before reporting.

copies and one previous-SHA copy in my own scratch directory, and every mutation was reverted and
verified reverted with git status.

GATES — ALL SIX RAN, FROM INSIDE AN ARCHIVE COPY OF 098f1b3 (git archive + git init + origin + one
commit). EACH IS REPORTED AS RUN OR NOT RUN.
1. go build ./...                 RAN. exit 0.
2. go test -race -count=1 ./...   RAN. exit 0. 72 packages ok, no FAIL, no DATA RACE.
3. make generate                  RAN. exit 0, then `git status --porcelain` produced ZERO lines.
4. nix flake check --no-build     RAN. exit 0; cgo-disabled-build, race and installer all green.
5. gofmt -l .                     RAN. ZERO lines ending in .go. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: I added a
   deliberately misformatted probe_bad_format.go, gofmt listed exactly that one .go file, I removed
   it and the count returned to zero, so the checker is looking. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: gofmt -l exits
   0 EVEN WHEN IT LISTS FILES — the exit code carries no verdict, so the count of .go lines is the
   only signal, and I never used `make fmt`, which is a fixer that cannot fail.
6. go vet ./...                   RAN. exit 0.

MY THREE ROUND-30 FINDINGS: TWO DISCHARGED, ONE DISCHARGED IN ITS FIRST HALF AND REGRESSED IN ITS
SECOND.

1. aura-plugins-pr4i4a — DISCHARGED. RE-RAN MY OWN MUTATION BOTH WAYS. A seventh lifecycleFault
   route in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans.go is now RED on the count assertion ("expected 6,
   actual 7"). With the reader reverted to the single named file and the SAME seventh route in
   place, the test is GREEN in 0.558s. The reader is what does the work.
   THE QUESTION THE ROUND PUT TO ME — package, command or file? — AND MY ANSWER.
   The reader's population is now the PACKAGE: every non-test .go file in cmd/pasture, which is 27
   files today spanning task, queue, install, bundle, epoch, migrate and status as well as the hook.
   The doc prose still says "READS THE COMMAND'S SOURCE" and the count message still says "this
   command has SIX fault routes", so the SENTENCE says command while the READER holds package.
   I judge that acceptable, and I say why rather than waving it through: the mismatch is in the SAFE
   direction. The reader is a SUPERSET of the command, so no route of the command can escape it, and
   the block immediately above the loop names the true population in capitals. THE PACKAGE IS ALSO
   THE ONLY CORRECT BOUNDARY AVAILABLE: lifecycleFault is unexported, so the package is exactly the
   set of code that can call it; a file boundary is provably too narrow (measured today); and a
   "command" is not a unit any Go reader can see, because cobra commands are values, not compilation
   units. The residue is that a lifecycleFault call planted in a SIBLING command of the same package
   would stop the build loudly with a message that names the wrong scope — loud and safe, which is
   the right failure direction, so I do not raise it.
   AND NON-TEST IS THE RIGHT BOUNDARY. A _test.go caller cannot ship a route to an operator, and
   including test files would make the count fail on every helper that drives the writer — cost with
   no safety. The exclusion drops only code that cannot reach a host. The reader takes a directory
   listing, so it also parses files a build constraint would exclude; that is over-reading again, and
   over-reading is the safe side of this question.

2. aura-plugins-367em3 — FIRST HALF DISCHARGED, SECOND HALF REGRESSED. THE IMPORTANT.
   THE DEFAULT IS RIGHT. record-unknown is the only claim true of every unenumerated error, and the
   journal appender that commits and then fails without a sentinel no longer produces "no occurrence
   was recorded for it".
   THE EVIDENCE LOCAL DOES NOT RECREATE THE RUNNING MUTABLE CLAIM, and I say so plainly because that
   was the question. It is ONE boolean, declared false, assigned true ONCE, read only by one deferred
   wrap. It carries a REGION, not a CLAIM, so it cannot be consulted with a stale stage the way the
   deleted "stage so far" could. "Weakest claim as default, evidence where we have it" IS the right
   decomposition.
   THE BOUNDARY IS WRONG. The marker is set immediately after dispatch.parse and BEFORE
   open(in.DBPath), while its own comment says it sits "on the line the durable region begins". An
   open that FAILED opened nothing. MEASURED ON BUILT BINARIES OF BOTH SHAS with the same authentic
   fixture: a --db under a read-only directory said "not-recorded ... no occurrence was recorded for
   it" at 1eeb7f2 and says "record-unknown ... an occurrence for it MAY OR MAY NOT exist — look for
   it in the lifecycle occurrence journal" at 098f1b3, on a run whose own cause line reads "unable to
   open database file". A FRESH DATABASE ON FIRST RUN behaves the same way. An UNSUPPORTED HARNESS is
   worse: its refusal is raised in HookLifecycleNative before hookLifecycle is entered, so no evidence
   covers it, and the repository's own TestInvalidInvocationCreatesNoDatabaseFile asserts ON THE
   FILESYSTEM that this route creates no pasture.db while the shipped sentence tells the operator a
   row may exist. CONTROL: the refusals above the marker keep the precise claim — unknown event and
   empty --host-version both still say not-recorded. The evidence reaches; it starts too early.
   NOTHING HOLDS IT: with `durablePossible := true` the whole of ./cmd/pasture is ok in 227.854s and
   ./internal/handlers is green. Details, both-SHA measurements and a three-part fix in
   aura-plugins-8fzhd0.

3. aura-plugins-m5pe7g — DISCHARGED. RE-RAN MY MUTATION: a seventh FailureMode admitted by IsValid
   with no String arm turns TestEveryDeclaredFailureModeNamesItself RED, and the message NAMES THE
   NUMBER — "failure mode 7 is declared VALID and has no name". Matching the neighbouring stage
   sweep, as asked.

THE STANDING ESCAPES — ALL EIGHT RE-RUN, EACH APPLIED ALONE AND REVERTED. NONE LOOSENED.
  bare cmd.OutOrStdout().Write in an arm -> RED twice (discarded result AND "a fault-writer report
  was put on standard output"); bare `defer file.Close()` -> RED naming the deferred close; a
  writer-less fmt.Println in the close arm -> RED; the report moved into a callee that writes to
  stdout -> RED, and the message names the callee AND the line inside it that names the stream;
  `_ = closeErr` live-variable discard -> RED; `if closeErr == nil` -> RED naming the success guard;
  a durable-state sentence hard-coded into the blocking arm -> TestTheBlockingArmMakesNoDurableStateClaim
  RED. THE PARAPHRASE LEAK, WHICH LOOSENED ONCE AND WAS RESTORED, IS RESTORED: I used a PARAPHRASE
  and not the exact string — "no occurrence has been recorded for it" — in the OpenCode fail-closed
  arm, and TestEveryFaultStageRendersItsOwnDurableStateOnEveryArm is RED on two subtests. Paraphrase
  recognition is genuinely back.

MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION — TWO.
  A. `durablePossible := true`, which destroys the evidence for every route. GREEN across
     cmd/pasture (227.854s) and internal/handlers. That is the reach half of the IMPORTANT.
  B. The route-sweep reader reverted to one file WITH the seventh route still planted, to prove the
     new reader and not something else is what turns the escape RED. GREEN, as predicted.

THE SUPERVISOR'S RULING ON aura-plugins-kqm151 — I UPHOLD IT ON BOTH GROUNDS, AND I CHECKED BOTH
RATHER THAN DEFERRING TO IT.
GROUND (a), TRUE AND IMPRECISE RATHER THAN FALSE. VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT. I drove all three causes
on the built binary against an initialised store — one added member, a dropped required identity,
and an identity present but empty — and the three diagnostics are BYTE-IDENTICAL. The reason is a
disjunction that is true whichever fired; the trailing clause "so none of the identities this event
requires was bound (session, tool-call)" is a fact about the capture result, which carries no
bindings in all three cases; and the fix instructs a comparison IN BOTH DIRECTIONS that will find
the cause in every one of the three. The operator's first step SUCCEEDS. That is precisely the
discriminator this slice has used to separate a defect from a limit, and it separates this one.
The condition the ruling rests on is also met, and I checked it rather than assuming it: the limit
is written where a reader meets it, in the doc comment of
TestAHostThatAddsAFieldIsRefusedWithATrueSentence ("AN HONEST LIMIT, STATED ... it does not
DISCRIMINATE").
GROUND (b), THE MODEL SHOULD BE CHANGED WHERE IT IS OWNED. THIS IS MY AXIS AND THE RULING IS RIGHT,
for a reason stronger than the one given. model.CaptureDisposition is not merely shared: it is a
PERSISTED member of the occurrence model (Occurrence.Capture), read by all three ingress parsers
and by two handlers, and its value domain is what a later reader of an old row will interpret.
Splitting the disposition therefore changes the value domain of a stored column — a compatibility
decision, not a wording one. The alternative that avoids the enum, carrying a typed cause out of
validateMembers beside the disposition, still changes the Claude ingress parser's result shape, and
that parser is the S4 surface in a WAVE 1 that is parallel under an exclusive ownership table. S0
taking it would be exactly the collision the slice's own ownership statements exist to prevent. So
the deferral is right on model locality AND on ownership, and I would have ruled the same.
ONE CONDITION, AND IT IS PROCESS, NOT CODE, SO IT IS NOT A FINDING. aura-plugins-kqm151 has NO
dependency edge to any slice or epic, so today it is a deferral with no address; and the protocol
says every review severity reaches zero before a wave closes, with the FOLLOWUP epic fed only by
user-DEFER'd UAT items. Wire it to the slice that owns the model, or put it in front of the user at
the Impl-UAT gate as a deferral for them to accept. Do not let a reviewer-originated remainder leave
through a label.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ACCEPT, AND WHY I DID NOT MANUFACTURE IT. Seven of my eight escape mutations,
both re-run findings and every gate came back exactly as the round intended, and I say so. The one
IMPORTANT is a REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THE COMMIT UNDER REVIEW, measured on two built binaries with
the same input, on the fault that the sibling code in this very file calls the commonest one there
is. It is small — one line moves — and it is the same shape as the defect it was fixing, pointing
the other way: a claim that is no longer as wide as its evidence, and now narrower.

## MY THREE ROUND-30 FINDINGS

2. aura-plugins-kregfh - DISCHARGED, AND THE PAIR IS REAL. I drove BOTH routes on the built

## MY RULING ON aura-plugins-jljuzn - I DO NOT OVERTURN YOURS

THE RULING IS RIGHT. A sentence that lists three causes where one fired IS good enough to ship
HERE, and it does not waste the reader's day. My reasons, measured rather than argued:

- IT IS TRUE FOR ITS INPUT IN ALL THREE CASES. I drove the added-member payload with a CONTROL:
  an authentic PreToolUse payload binds with ZERO stderr bytes; add ONE member and the same
  payload renders 2226 bytes of refusal, byte-for-byte the same message the missing-identity and
  renamed probes get. The message is a disjunction and the disjunction holds every time.
- THE REMEDY DISCRIMINATES THE THREE CAUSES FOR THE READER MECHANICALLY. "Compare the payload
  with this build's Claude registration for "PreToolUse" in BOTH directions ... a host that ADDS
  a field is refused here just as one that renames or drops a correlation field is." That is one
  set difference over one event's field list. It is a minute of work, not a day, and it names the
  non-obvious direction explicitly, which is the direction an operator would never guess.
- IT CARRIES A SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY REACHABLE REMEDY: the host-version check. On Claude that one
  is fully actionable, because the generated hooks.json passes
  --host-version "${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:-unknown}", so the operator can see and test it.
- A TRUE-BUT-IMPRECISE SENTENCE IS A DIFFERENT ANIMAL FROM THE ONES THIS SLICE REFUSED TO SHIP.
  Every one of those sent the reader somewhere the answer COULD NOT BE. This one sends them
  somewhere the answer IS, and makes them read three lines instead of one.

ONE OBSERVATION TO ATTACH TO aura-plugins-kqm151, NOT A FINDING OF MINE. The first remedy asks
the reader to compare against "this build's Claude registration", and NO PRODUCT SURFACE
DISCLOSES IT for Claude. `hook lifecycle manifest` prints only the metamodel name, version,
content digest and journaled flag - I ran it. hooks/hooks.json carries no allowedFields. The
OpenCode plugin DOES embed the whole registration (allowedFields and identities per event) on
the operator's disk, so the same sentence is fully actionable there and only partly actionable on
Claude - which is the harness the finding was raised on. Naming the cause would make the
disclosure unnecessary; disclosing the registration would make naming the cause unnecessary.
Either closes it, and kqm151 is the right place for that choice. I did not file it separately
because the message does not lie and the operator retains a reachable first step.

## WHY THIS IS NOT AN ACCEPT

Both findings are mine, both were found by doing what the round asked, and neither was
manufactured.
  aura-plugins-ddaysb came out of item 3's instruction to TEST the sweep claim rather than accept
  it. The sweep re-asked the sentences keyed on the stage; nobody re-derived the producer set of
  the stage table's DEFAULT. An unsupported harness is a pre-store refusal that never passes the
  marker this round added, so it is told its occurrence "MAY OR MAY NOT exist" and to read the
  fault record "beside the database" when no database was ever opened - proved on the filesystem,

unmarked write and a second durable-state claim present.

- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-oglyx4 — the structural durable-region guard: a write in an else
  branch, and a write through receipt.EnsureActiveMetamodel, both stay green.
- IMPORTANT aura-plugins-f21nfo — the durable-state class rule is a four-word vocabulary; a
  claim reworded around it leaks into every arm and into the blocking arm, tree-green.

text:

Review task aura-plugins-onhzmp. VERDICT: REVISE — 0 BLOCKER / 2 IMPORTANT / 2 MINOR.

THE SIX GATES, EVERY ONE ACTUALLY RUN, from inside an archive copy of 1e3bb18 (git archive ->
git init -> origin remote -> one commit), never in the worktree:
1. go build ./... (CGO_ENABLED=1)                 RAN, rc=0.
2. go test -race -count=1 ./...                   RAN, rc=0. 72 packages ok, 0 FAIL, no data
                                                  race. cmd/pasture 310.99s.
3. make generate                                  RAN, rc=0; git status --porcelain EMPTY, so
                                                  no drift.
4. nix flake check --no-build                     RAN, rc=0; cgo-disabled-build, installer and
                                                  race all green.
5. gofmt -l .                                     RAN; printed NOTHING. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: a
                                                  deliberately misformatted badpkg/bad.go in a
                                                  throwaway tree made gofmt -l print
                                                  "badpkg/bad.go" and STILL EXIT 0, so the
                                                  empty output above is a real result and not
                                                  an exit code mistaken for one.
6. go vet ./...                                   RAN, rc=0.

JUDGEMENT OF THE RE-DERIVATION, WHICH IS THE THING I WAS ASKED TO JUDGE.
The data model is RIGHT and I could not falsify it.
- "The region is the set of points from which a row can exist" is the correct definition. It is
  a property of WRITES, and it makes the region derivable rather than remembered.
- "Exactly two write attempts" is TRUE at this SHA. I enumerated hookLifecycle myself rather
  than trusting the sentence: service.Receive on the invalid-capture arm, and deliveryCommit.
  Nothing else there can leave a row — open(in.DBPath) creates a file but no occurrence,
  tasks.NewLifecycleReceiptService constructs, gate.NewDeliveryIntent and gate.Legalize are
  pure, dispatch.parse is pure, io.ReadAll reads, tracker.Close flushes. This is the twelfth
  population this slice has stated and the first one I could not break.
- "The wrapper is a property of the region, not of one function" is right, and the producer pin
  holds it: deleting the ErrLifecycleBeforeDurableWrite wrap from HookLifecycleNative turns
  TestEveryRefusalBeforeAWriteSaysNoRowExists/the_harness_is_not_one_this_build_supports RED.
  The three routes each also stat the store path, so the claim is checked against the thing it
  claims.

MY OWN ESCAPE, RE-RUN: moving the marker back above open(in.DBPath) turns
TestTheDurableRegionBeginsAtItsWrites RED, naming hook_lifecycle.go:282 and :315 and failing
the marker-count assertion. My round-32 finding aura-plugins-8fzhd0 is CLOSED by construction.

TWO MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION AGAINST THE NEW GUARD, BOTH GREEN (finding aura-plugins-oglyx4):
- an unmarked service.Receive in an ELSE branch. The walk descends into IfStmt.Body only; Else,
  For, Range, Switch, Select, bare blocks and FuncLit bodies are unvisited.
- an unmarked receipt.EnsureActiveMetamodel(ctx, service) at the top level. attemptsWrite names
  two syntactic shapes ("service".Receive and the identifier deliveryCommit), so any other
  writer is invisible — and receipt.Service has four further committing methods while
  EnsureActiveMetamodel is a real write called one function away in the same file.
The bidirectional relation (no write without a marker, no marker without a write) is the RIGHT
relation and it cannot pass vacuously in the total case, because require.NotZero(writes) fires
if the reader stops recognising writes. It passes vacuously in the PARTIAL case, which is what
both mutations exercise.

THE PARAPHRASE RULE (finding aura-plugins-f21nfo). "Names one of three nouns" is a new
written-down list in disguise — a list of four words instead of three phrases. Adding a second,
foreign durable-state claim phrased around them ("a row for it may or may not exist in the
lifecycle store, so look for it there") left BOTH internal/lifecycle/hostexit AND cmd/pasture
green, in every arm of the sweep; the same trick works on the blocking arm. The literal control
is caught, so the arm is pinned against the vocabulary and nothing else. Deleting the superseded
machinery outright was right; the successor's stated reach is wider than its actual reach.

THE EVIDENCE-WORD COUPLING: SOUND, AND PINNED. Holding the word to the evidence AND to the
advice beside it is the correct relation, because they are two renderings of one field by
different code, and a guard that requires either to say a particular thing would pin a wording
instead. Both stated mutations turn TestTheEvidenceWordAgreesWithTheEvidenceAndWithTheAdviceBesideIt
RED: rendering "none" always, and inventing a citation. No finding.

STANDING ESCAPES, ALL RE-RUN AT THIS SHA. NONE LOOSENED:
- bare cmd.OutOrStdout().Write                     RED (both writer guards).
- bare defer file.Close()                          RED (both).
- writer-less fmt.Println in the close arm         RED (both).
- the callee write (a neighbour names stdout)      RED (both).
- the live-variable discard (syncErr -> append)    RED (discard guard).
- if closeErr == nil                               RED (arm guard).
- the blocking-arm durable-state sentence, literal RED.

1. THE BLOCKER aura-plugins-j30cwo, RE-DRIVEN. Five identity probes (good, renamed, empty,

9. THE 5 s TIER, END TO END. A real BEGIN EXCLUSIVE held by a separate process: elapsed 5.01 s,

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ROUND 38, AXIS A (host-contract truth and end-user behaviour). SHA 64d00ff, ELEVEN commits over
223f86a. Review task aura-plugins-1cju1n.
VOTE: REVISE - 0 BLOCKER, 3 IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-2v44ss, aura-plugins-k9fhq5,
aura-plugins-ipl2ue), 0 MINOR. Severity groups created eagerly; BLOCKER aura-plugins-uraa66 and
MINOR aura-plugins-ng6t5m closed empty.

I READ EVERY DIAGNOSTIC I DROVE. I did not count them. All three findings come from reading, and a
presence count would have reported this round CLEAN.

1. MY ROUND-36 FINDING hdm0sp IS FIXED, ON RENDERED BYTES, ON ALL THREE HARNESSES. A zero-byte
   stdin now renders "validation error: The host sent no payload: standard input carried zero
   bytes", followed by the guidance IN THE SAME SENTENCE - the worker's report that the guidance
   had to move out of Fix and into What is correct, and the guidance DOES reach the console. The
   CATEGORY is now validation, not storage. Every clause is TRUE for a zero-byte payload: nothing
   was parsed, and the arm stands BEFORE open(in.DBPath), so "no database was opened" is true on
   the filesystem - no pasture.db, no -wal, no -shm is created. It says what the operator did
   (an empty stream, not a malformed one) and what to do (a hook wired without its input
   redirected, a wrapper consuming stdin, a manual invocation with nothing piped). NO SQLite
   constraint text, NO table name. THE HOST IS STILL SAFE: rc 0 on all three, empty Claude
   continue bytes, {"continue":true} on Codex, {"decision":"proceed"} on OpenCode, exactly ONE
   fault-record line each, and `hook lifecycle list` EMPTY. Fail-open holds.
   THE PIN IS LETHAL. MUTATION: delete the len(raw)==0 arm from hookLifecycle, rebuild.
   TestAnEmptyStandardInputNamesTheRealCondition turns RED on ALL THREE subtests, and the
   NOT NULL constraint on lifecycle_payload_blobs.body comes straight back to the operator.

2. MY ROUND-36 FINDING 8wrvbv HAS A PIN AND THE PIN IS NOT DEAD.
   TestTheWarrantRefusalCarriesItsOwnEvidence reads deliveryCommit's warrant arm and requires the
   ErrLifecycleBeforeDurableWrite wrap. MUTATION: revert the wrap to `return
   backend.HostResponse{}, err`. The guard turns RED with the found text quoted. It also states
   its own limit - it is structural because no host payload can drive a warrant refusal.

3. THE BLOCKER j30cwo ROUTES, FIVE IDENTITY PROBES x THREE HARNESSES, EACH DIAGNOSTIC READ.
   Valid, renamed identity, dropped identity, empty identity value, added member. Every refusal:
   rc 0, the harness's own continue bytes, ONE fault-record line, ONE journal row. Every valid:
   rc 0, ZERO stderr, ONE journal row, ZERO fault lines.
   READING THEM PRODUCED TWO OF THE THREE FINDINGS. The Claude "renamed/dropped/empty" sentence is
   true. The Claude "added member" sentence is true. The CODEX and OPENCODE added-member probes
   were ACCEPTED with zero stderr - and the refusal text those harnesses DO print claims they
   refuse added members and require exact identity names. Both claims measured false
   (aura-plugins-ipl2ue). A Claude payload with no hook_event_name binds every identity correctly
   and is still told "the payload describes a different event" (aura-plugins-2v44ss).

4. THE BUN WITNESS. The plugin SHIPPED at 7e8be34, taken verbatim with `git show`, against a
   binary built from 64d00ff. toolExecuteBefore: HOST-CONTINUED, bun rc 0, output.args byte-equal
   to the host-owned value, occurrence recorded, ZERO faults. sessionCreated: no throw. A MIXED
   INSTALL IS SAFE.

5. THE SIX DURABLE-STATE ROUTES, each with `hook lifecycle list` AND a filesystem read AFTER it.
   unsupported harness / read-only directory / withheld event / flag parse / argument refusal /
   ZERO-LENGTH PAYLOAD. All six: rc 0, "durable state not-recorded", "no occurrence was recorded
   for it", NO "MAY OR MAY NOT". List EMPTY where a store existed. NO pasture.db, -wal or -shm
   created on the flag-parse, argument-refusal or zero-length routes. NOTHING written under the
   read-only directory, and its record-loss line is FIRST and names the exact path it tried. NO
   ROUTE DISAGREES WITH ITSELF.

6. ZERO STDERR ON VALID WORK. TWELVE valid invocations - six claude-code events, three codex, three
   opencode, including both host-version skews. TWELVE of twelve rc 0 with EXACTLY ZERO stderr
   bytes.

7. FAIL-OPEN. 42 measurements: three harnesses x two host-version skews x seven degenerate probes
   (empty stdin, whitespace, null, [], {}, truncated JSON, over-limit at 1.15 MB). ALL 42 rc 0,
   ALL 42 with the harness's continue bytes, ALL 42 with a diagnostic. AND I READ ALL SEVEN
   DIAGNOSTICS. Four of the seven are correct. Two are not: `{}` renders "the payload describes a
   different event" (aura-plugins-2v44ss), and `[]` renders "not well-formed JSON" for
   well-formed JSON (aura-plugins-k9fhq5). The zero-length column, which was wrong last round, is
   now right. NO STORAGE ERROR LEAKED ANYWHERE IN THE 42.

8. FAIL-CLOSED OPT-IN, three CORRECT and DIFFERENT answers. claude-code rc 2, "exit block",
   "unset PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED". codex rc 0, {"continue":true}, the EVIDENCE reason: the event
   "carries no host evidence for it, and pasture will not refuse a user's operation on an
   unevidenced claim". opencode rc 0, {"decision":"proceed"}, the CHANNEL reason: the exit code
   "this host does not read as a refusal, so it cannot stop this event today". No reason borrowed
   from another harness.

9. THE FOUNDING MUTATION IS STILL RED AND STILL LETHAL UNDER REAL BUN. ErrOrStderr ->
   OutOrStdout in emitLifecycleOutcome, built and replayed against the 7e8be34 plugin under Bun
   1.3.13: the dropped-identity and empty-identity probes each give "pasture hook lifecycle
   response is not JSON", the plugin THROWS, and the user's tool call would stop. Three runs,
   identical. The pristine binary continues on all three.

10. THE 5 s TIER, END TO END. A real BEGIN EXCLUSIVE held by a separate process: elapsed 5.01 s,
    rc 0, {"decision":"proceed"}, a diagnostic naming its "5s hook-invocation deadline", durable
    state record-unknown, ONE fault line, EMPTY list afterwards - inside what record-unknown
    allows. THE 10 s FIGURE WITH ITS RANGE: hooks/hooks.json holds ELEVEN hook rows; NINE carry
    "timeout": 10; EIGHT of those nine are the pasture lifecycle rows and ALL EIGHT carry it.
    5 s of 10 s, headroom holds.

11. MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION - FOUR, ALL BUILT AND DRIVEN.
    M1 delete the zero-length arm: RED on all three harnesses. Item 1.
    M2 revert the round-35 warrant wrap: RED. Item 2.
    M3 the founding ErrOrStderr -> OutOrStdout, replayed under real Bun: LETHAL. Item 9.
    M4, MY OWN: force activation.Codex0_146_0 to fail, so LifecycleHarnessCoordinates drops Codex
       through its silent `continue`. TestAnEmptyStandardInputNamesTheRealCondition then runs TWO
       subtests instead of three and PASSES - its `require.NotEmpty` does not notice a derived
       population that shrank. REPORTED, NOT FILED: the same mutation turns internal/handlers RED,
       so the narrowing is held elsewhere and no live defect follows from it. I say it here rather
       than file it, because a population that can shrink without its own reader noticing is the
       shape this slice has paid for repeatedly.

12. THE ROOT THE THREE FINDINGS SHARE, stated once. captureDispositionAdviceByDisposition gives
    each disposition ONE reason and ONE fix, as constants. But the parsers funnel SEVERAL causes
    into each disposition, and the THREE parsers do not agree on what they enforce. So a constant
    per disposition cannot be true of every input that reaches it, nor of every harness it is
    printed for. hdm0sp, kqm151 and these three are all that one shape. Widening each sentence is
    the correct repair for this round; the durable repair is that the advice be DERIVED - from the
    cause the parser carries, and from what the dispatched parser actually enforces - which is the
    lesson this slice has already applied to its guards and has not yet applied to its prose.

NOT RE-FILED. The Claude "proceed" non-enum answer is aura-plugins-uieu0p (S4) - I saw it again on
six Claude invocations. The ClearanceAuthority data value is aura-plugins-xw71qw (S1). The
three-cause schema refusal limit is aura-plugins-kqm151 (S4); aura-plugins-ipl2ue is NOT that item
and says why in its own text.

SANITY. The worktree was never written to. Archive copy of 64d00ff at a scratch path, four mutant
copies each separate and kept, binary built inside the nix dev shell (go1.26.3). Another axis owns
the full gate set.

IT IS NOT CLEAN. I did not lower the standard to say so and I did not manufacture anything to
avoid saying it. THE PRODUCT IS CORRECT ON EVERY ROUTE A HOST CAN REACH: fail-open holds on 42 of
42 degenerate probes and 15 of 15 identity probes, valid work is silent 12 of 12, the founding harm
returns only under mutation, a mixed install is safe under real Bun, all six durable-state routes
agree with the filesystem, and the 5 s tier fits inside the 10 s host budget. WHAT IS WRONG IS
WHAT THREE DIAGNOSTICS SAY. Two of them sit in the same seven-probe set that hid hdm0sp for
thirty-five rounds, on the probes next to the one that was caught.

THE ACCOUNTING I WAS ASKED TO VERIFY, LINE BY LINE, AND NOT ACCEPT.
DERIVED, GENUINELY -- I drove each derivation rather than reading it:
  THE INTERNAL-REFERENCE FORMS. Derived, and the best work of the round. The forms are read out of
  the two numbered items of the AGENTS.md rule that DEFINES them, and an exemplar with no pattern
  is REFUSED by name. MEASURED: adding ", and wave codes (`W7`)" to that rule block turns the guard
  RED -- "AGENTS.md spells these forbidden forms and this guard cannot recognise them: [W7]". It
  also states its own boundary (the two numbered items, not the whole section) and says why, which
  is the correct treatment of the paragraphs that backtick the CLI fields the rule targets.
  THE STAGE SWEEP'S ARMS. Derived from allFailureModes() and FaultPolicy.IsValid(). Not a list
  moved: the coverage half over stages is still checked against IsValid, the arms half is now
  enumerated from the types, and require.NotEmpty stops a vacuous derivation. What it does NOT vary
  (DeclaredMode, held equal to Mode) is stated with a reason, and I checked the reason against the
  production switch: no impact arm reads DeclaredMode; only the FIX line does, and the fix line is
  the part the equality rule already declares out of scope.
  THE WRITER RECOGNISER. Derived by identity, not spelling -- serviceNames starts at the
  constructor's first result and grows transitively. It refuses to be vacuous (require.NotEmpty on
  the name set, require.NotZero on the writes). One residual, filed as aura-plugins-4nutw3.
  THE ZERO-LENGTH TEST'S HARNESS SET. Genuinely derived: handlers.LifecycleHarnessCoordinates
  ranges the frontendRegistry the command dispatches on and picks the first ENABLED event by
  resolving the same generated activation proofs, so a coordinate cannot silently drive the
  withheld arm. I checked the one thing that looked like a hole -- harnesses dropped on an
  activation error or with no enabled event -- and it is not one: such a harness cannot reach the
  read at all, so its absence is correct rather than a missing row.
  THE DISPOSITION SWEEP'S POPULATION. Derived from the production advice table, and compared as a
  SET, not a cardinality.
STATED, EACH CHECKED FOR TRUTH AND FOR COMPLETENESS:
  THE IMPACT EQUALITY covers the impact clause and not the fix clause. TRUE and COMPLETE -- the
  limit sits on expectedImpactClause, names the fix clause and the rest of the diagnostic, and
  impactClauseOf reads exactly the clause the rule composes.
  THE WARRANT-REFUSAL PIN is structural because no host payload can drive it. TRUE, and the reason
  given (the contract is derived from the delivery the parser produced) matches the code. The guard
  refuses to pass vacuously if the warrant call or its refusal arm disappears.
  THE DISPOSITION SWEEP derives DISPOSITIONS while the population that matters is CAUSES. TRUE,
  COMPLETE, and the most honest sentence in the round: it says the derivation would NOT have caught
  the omission that exposed the defect, and names what it does close.
  THE OUTER PANIC REGION has no reachable producer. The CONCLUSION is true. The ENUMERATION
  supporting it is not complete -- aura-plugins-v6c44k.

THE CLOSING SWEEP, ATTACKED HARDEST, AS ASKED. FOUR QUESTIONS, FOUR ANSWERS.
  IS "ZERO FLAGGED" DISTINGUISHABLE FROM "LOOKS AT NOTHING"? YES, and I proved it end to end rather
  than trusting the two vacuity checks. A guard planted in the subject file with a class claim, an
  inline []string{"alpha","beta"} and no disclaimer is RED, named by file and function. The sweep
  fires. Both vacuity checks are the right two and neither is decorative.
  IS THE SIGNATURE THE RIGHT SIGNATURE? The IDEA is right -- ask what the code RANGES OVER, not
  what the doc means. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS NARROWER THAN THE IDEA. It recognises a range over a
  composite literal only when EVERY element is a string literal. A list of struct rows is
  invisible, and so is a list of typed constants.
  CAN I WRITE A GUARD WITH THIS DEFECT THAT THE SWEEP DOES NOT FLAG? YES, AND IT IS THE ARCHETYPE.
  A planted guard claiming "every declared arm" over an inline []struct{Name string; Code int}
  passes. That is the exact shape of aura-plugins-1zkbym -- four hand-listed Mode/Policy struct
  rows under a doc that said "every arm" -- which is the finding this systemic round was built
  around. The sweep does not recognise the population shape of the defect it exists to close, and
  none of its five stated limits names that shape. IMPORTANT aura-plugins-o6zf1o.
  IS THE CLAIM-VOCABULARY ADMISSION HONEST, OR THE SAME DEFECT WEARING AN EXEMPTION? The admission
  is honest about its MECHANISM -- it says plainly that the vocabulary narrows which guards are
  asked. Its JUSTIFICATION is where it slips: "admissible only because it is not the whole rule ...
  the structural half is what makes the asking worth anything" reads as though the structural half
  covers for the vocabulary, when the two are a CONJUNCTION and either half missing means no flag.
  I do not file that as a separate finding, because the sentence before it states the mechanism
  correctly and a reader who reads both is not misled. What I do file is the DISCHARGE side, which
  is a word match: a guard with the class claim and the recognised list shape is cleared by the
  word "derived" or "population" appearing anywhere in its doc, about any other subject. Measured
  green. MINOR aura-plugins-z8bj8k.

THE MECHANISM RE-ENUMERATED AT THIS SHA, MYSELF, NOT FROM THE SENTENCE. "EXACTLY TWO WRITE
ATTEMPTS" IS STILL TRUE. The new zero-length arm returns BEFORE open(in.DBPath), so it opens no
store and writes nothing; it cannot be a third producer. The writers remain service.Receive on the
invalid-capture arm and deliveryCommit. Nothing else in hookLifecycle can leave a row: the
dispatch, the activation lookup, the version check, the bounded read, dispatch.parse and
gate.Legalize are pure or read-only, the open creates a file and no occurrence, the service
construction constructs, tracker.Close flushes. The guard agrees: two writes against two markers on
the unmutated source.

ALL STANDING ESCAPES RE-RUN AT THIS SHA. NONE LOOSENED.
  the founding ErrOrStderr -> OutOrStdout in emitLifecycleOutcome   RED, and LETHAL: 20+ tests in
    cmd/pasture fail, including every built-binary route. The founding harm returns the instant the
    guard is removed, and nothing has weakened that.
  the append arm's writer swapped to stdout                         RED (writer guard).
  a bare `defer file.Close()`                                       RED (discard guard).
  a writer-less report in the close arm (fmt.Printf)                RED on BOTH writer guards, and
    the message names os.Stdout as implicit and named by no expression.
  the discarded close result (`_ = file.Close()`)                   RED (discard guard).
  the inverted close guard (`closeErr == nil`)                      RED (arm guard).
  the marker moved back above open(in.DBPath)                       RED on the marker-count rule.
  a durable-state sentence added to the BLOCKING arm                RED.
  the third paraphrase into the OpenCode fail-closed arm            RED by equality. The paraphrase
    leak that was green two rounds ago is closed by exhaustion, not by vocabulary.

MUTATIONS OF MY OWN INVENTION -- FOUR, ALL MEASURED, THREE GREEN.
  A. The struct-row population planted in the subject file. GREEN. The IMPORTANT.
  B. The class claim discharged by the word "population" in a sentence about another axis. GREEN.
     A MINOR.
  C. `var svc = service` in place of `svc := service`. GREEN with an unmarked write present, on
     the same writer, defeated by one keyword. A MINOR.
  D. A new backticked exemplar added to the AGENTS.md rule block. RED by name. Not a finding -- it
     is the proof that the internal-reference population is derived and not a list moved.

WHAT IS NOT A FINDING, SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE A CLEAN ANSWER IS WORTH AS MUCH AS A DIRTY ONE.
The SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR is correct on every route I could reach at this SHA, and the systemic round
did what it set out to do: five populations that were lists are now derived from the product's own
sources, and each one refuses to pass vacuously. Four of the five derivations I could not break.
All four of my own round-36 findings are properly closed, two of them in the strongest form
available. No operator sees a different byte because of anything I filed.

IT IS NOT CLEAN, AND I DID NOT LOWER THE STANDARD TO SAY SO, NOR MANUFACTURE ANYTHING TO AVOID
SAYING IT. The one IMPORTANT is the closing sweep itself: it was written to end the class "a rule
described one level more general than it is written", it proves itself with a negative control
rather than an instance, and its structural half does not recognise the population shape of the
archetype it was built for. That is the thirteenth instance, and it is in the guard against the
class. The three MINORs are a discharge that fires on a word, a recogniser that follows one
statement kind while claiming every name, and a stated limit that enumerates four constructs and
omits the four calls beside them.

  invisible, and so is a list of typed constants.

  passes. That is the exact shape of aura-plugins-1zkbym -- four hand-listed Mode/Policy struct
  rows under a doc that said "every arm" -- which is the finding this systemic round was built
  around. The sweep does not recognise the population shape of the defect it exists to close, and
  none of its five stated limits names that shape. IMPORTANT aura-plugins-o6zf1o.
  IS THE CLAIM-VOCABULARY ADMISSION HONEST, OR THE SAME DEFECT WEARING AN EXEMPTION? The admission
  is honest about its MECHANISM -- it says plainly that the vocabulary narrows which guards are
  asked. Its JUSTIFICATION is where it slips: "admissible only because it is not the whole rule ...
  the structural half is what makes the asking worth anything" reads as though the structural half
  covers for the vocabulary, when the two are a CONJUNCTION and either half missing means no flag.
  I do not file that as a separate finding, because the sentence before it states the mechanism
  correctly and a reader who reads both is not misled. What I do file is the DISCHARGE side, which

  word "derived" or "population" appearing anywhere in its doc, about any other subject. Measured
  green. MINOR aura-plugins-z8bj8k.

ATTEMPTS" IS STILL TRUE. The new zero-length arm returns BEFORE open(in.DBPath), so it opens no
store and writes nothing; it cannot be a third producer. The writers remain service.Receive on the
invalid-capture arm and deliveryCommit. Nothing else in hookLifecycle can leave a row: the
dispatch, the activation lookup, the version check, the bounded read, dispatch.parse and
gate.Legalize are pure or read-only, the open creates a file and no occurrence, the service
construction constructs, tracker.Close flushes. The guard agrees: two writes against two markers on
the unmutated source.

ALL STANDING ESCAPES RE-RUN AT THIS SHA. NONE LOOSENED.

It WORKS MECHANICALLY and it DOES NOT HOLD THE RULE.

now answered from measurement rather than from the narrow range.

not an investigation.

derives its MODE axis from the type and hand-lists its POLICY axis, while the
neighbouring stage sweep now enumerates both axes from their own types. FaultPolicy
is a two-valued user opt-in, so the hole is real but not reachable today. Recorded
so a later slice that adds a policy knows where to look.

The one IMPORTANT is not bookkeeping. The guard that this round wrote to stop a
derivation narrowing has, itself, a derivation that is still narrower than the
list it replaced — for a third of the population — and the check that was meant
to prove otherwise is a hand-picked sample of the cases that pass. Both halves
are mutation-proved. I did not lower the standard to reach 0/0/0 and I did not
invent anything to avoid it.

Built binary (fix) versus a binary built from main 0992877 (base), driven on fresh stores, 12 cases, outputs normalised for path and timestamp only, `diff -r`: IDENTICAL.

Held-lock route, real process: python3 holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE on the store (WAL) until the hook returns. fix: rc 0, elapsed 5.01 s, stdout 0 bytes, stderr contains "the hook stopped waiting at its 5s hook-invocation deadline and abandoned the work for event "SessionStart" ... : context deadline exceeded", "durable state record-unknown", "MAY OR MAY NOT exist"; fault record faultStage record-unknown, hostExit continue, outcomeClass fault. base: rc 0, elapsed 5.01 s, byte-identical stderr and record (timestamp aside).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULING NEEDED: is the loser's exit 5 in the two-daemon race a product defect?

Worker worker-scenario-names, branch fix/scenario-test-names (pasture main 99635ef). Item 3 is STOPPED at this point per the assignment. Items 1, 2 and 4 continue.

WHAT HAPPENS (read from code; every location is in the tree or the pinned module cache)
1. pastured start order (cmd/pastured/main.go buildDaemonRuntime): initAuditTrail -> tasks.OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions (audit migrator; a second opener waits on BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a 30 s busy-retry ceiling, internal/audit/migrate.go) -> RegisterWellKnownAgents -> engine.New.
2. engine.New (internal/engine/engine.go ~232-252) opens the shared handle, then runs the durable schema gate RequireSupportedDurableSchema BEFORE the durable bootstrap. The gate is provenance.RequireSupportedDBOSSystemSchema (provenance v0.0.7 internal/dbossys/dbossys.go): it reads dbos_migrations; a version below FirstSupportedMigrationVersion = 42 is SchemaStateSuperseded and the gate refuses. The refusal is permanent by design: the pasture wrapper (internal/engine/dbosinit.go supersededDurableSchemaError) is a CategoryStorage error, exit 5, and it runs outside the bounded bootstrap retry.
3. The winner's durable bootstrap (dbos-transact-golang v1.2.0, 47 SQLite migration files) applies one migration per transaction with the version row updated in the same transaction. So between the winner's 1st and 41st commit the file records a version in 1..41.
4. A loser that reaches the gate in that window reads e.g. version 1, is classified superseded, and exits 5 with: "storage: This pasture build can't open the database <path>: an older build, or an interrupted first start, left it in a layout this build doesn't read. Cause: dbossys.RequireSupportedSchema: <path> records DBOS system schema version 1, below the supported floor 42 -- ... caution: a first launch that is still creating this database records a below-floor version until its migrations finish, so confirm that no other process is opening the same file before you delete anything ...". That text is not in acceptedLoserOutcomes, so waitReady calls t.Fatalf("pastured-2 exited before readiness"). The data invariants hold (the gate only reads).
5. Both layers already know the transient case exists: provenance's message carries the "caution" clause, and pasture's Fix step 2 says "A first start is still running right now, in another process ... Let it finish and run the command again; delete nothing." The product chooses to refuse and to hand the retry to the operator.

REPRODUCTION
- go test -race -count=20 -run TestScenario12_ConcurrentMigratorRace ./internal/audit: 20/20 PASS, 24.8 s total (about 1.2 s per run). Both processes reach "daemon runtime ready".
- Same, with one busy loop per CPU for the whole run: 20/20 PASS, 51.9 s. No loser exit observed.
- The user ruled the load reproduction is not needed; I stopped there. The window is the winner's bootstrap (47 transactions on a fresh file, tens of milliseconds locally); on a CI runner the loser's own start-up lands in it often enough to fail the job (task description: "reads DBOS system schema version 1, exits 5").

WHY THIS NEEDS A RULING
The loser fails SAFELY by the test's definition (no write; a diagnostic that names the condition in its cause clause). But the headline sentence blames "an older build, or an interrupted first start", and the process refuses a file that another process is creating at that moment, instead of waiting for it. Two concurrent first starts of pastured on one file therefore fail one of them nondeterministically, and the operator must retry by hand. Whether that is acceptable behaviour or a defect is a product decision, not a test decision.

OPTIONS
A. Not a defect (test-only). The race test accepts the superseded refusal as a safe-loser outcome ONLY when the output carries the in-progress clause, and additionally asserts the durable version the daemons left equals the runtime's final version (no partial durable write). Cost: the nondeterministic start-up failure is codified; operators keep the manual retry.
B. Defect (product + test). In engine.New, treat a below-floor read as transient while dbos_migrations is advancing: re-inspect on a bounded backoff (the same policy shape as dbosRaceRetryPolicy) and refuse only when the version is stable across the window. An old-build file has a stable version, so it is still refused after one re-read (about 25-50 ms extra); a concurrent first start converges to "supported" and start-up proceeds. The race test then keeps the superseded refusal LOUD (a regression), and waits on: winner ready AND loser terminal (ready, or one of the bounded outcomes), then the invariants. Cost: a product change in internal/engine (dbosinit.go/engine.go) plus deterministic unit tests with an injected inspector; touches files outside my three.

My reading: B is what the daemon's own Fix text already tells the operator to do by hand. I do not decide this. I will not hide the refusal in the test's accepted set without a ruling.

WHILE WAITING: item 1 (renames) and item 2 (sweep) are done in the worktree and will be committed on green gates; item 4 (guard) decision follows in the final report.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
USER RULING 2026-09-04 (verbatim): "Sure do B."
Applied: OPTION B, product change. engine.New re-inspects the durable schema version for a bounded time while the migrations table is advancing and refuses only on a STABLE below-floor version; the diagnostic names the concurrent-start case only when progress was observed and the bound expired; the race test keeps the refusal loud for a genuinely old database and proves the loser now becomes ready against the migrated store. Scope widens to internal/engine and its tests. Worker continues; one Fable review follows.

RACE-TEST FIX (ruling: option B)
Reproduction: 0/20 idle (24.8 s) and 0/20 under one busy loop per CPU (51.9 s); the user ruled further load reproduction unnecessary. Mechanism read from code: engine.New ran the durable schema gate (provenance floor 42) before the bootstrap; the winner commits 47 migrations one per transaction; a loser that read between commits 1 and 41 was refused for good as an older build, exit 5.
A second, hidden loser path surfaced as soon as the accepted set was narrowed: in 1 of 6 runs the loser died at its FIRST statement with "cannot relax foreign-key enforcement ... database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)", exit 2. The fixture is a rollback-journal file; both daemons switch it to WAL at open; the switch's read-to-write upgrade is not covered by SQLite's busy handler. The old generic entry "audit trail initialisation failed" had hidden it.
Product changes:
(1) internal/engine/schema_gate.go — the gate now waits, progress-based. Mechanism chosen: the library gate runs first on the pooled handle (the floor decision stays the library's); only on refusal does the look take ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same handle — it blocks on the driver's busy_timeout while a migration transaction holds the write lock and reports that as a writer in flight — then reads the recorded version under it for progress only, and rolls back. Chosen over a bare re-read because a re-read cannot see an open uncommitted transaction. Windows from the injected profile: SQLiteBusy = poll interval and stability window (500 ms production); WorkflowResult = bound (30 s). No tier is defined for waiting out a peer's bootstrap; WorkflowResult is the closest (outermost whole-operation wait) and its production value equals the two existing 30 s ceilings; both tier documents say so. Sentences: stable and never moved -> unchanged older-build sentence (Fix bullet about a running first start now says "stalled"); progress observed then bound expired -> "Couldn't open the database <path>: another process was migrating it and did not finish within 30s." (never "older build"; cause is the last observation, not the library sentinel); cancelled -> its own sentence. A lock met by the library's own first read counts as a writer in flight. Known limit written in the file: a live migrator that neither commits nor holds the lock for a whole window still reads as stable.
(2) internal/audit/open_retry.go + sqlite.go — the foreign-key pragma and the base-table creation now run through the migrator's own busy retry (busyRetryCeiling 30 s reused; no new constant). A spent ceiling reports "Another pasture process held the audit database while this one was opening it." exit 5.
(3) internal/handlers/controller.go passes the production profile its handle was opened with; internal/lifecycle/guard/timeouts_test.go lists schema_gate.go; AGENTS.md and profile.go: "seven today" -> "eight today" and one paragraph on the gate's two tiers.
Test now waits on: each daemon's terminal start-up state (ready or exit), then the verdict — at least one ready; every early exit = exit 5 + one of four true sentences — then the four invariants as the daemons left the file, plus engine.RequireSupportedDurableSchema on that file, then the reopen no-op invariants. Every wait is bounded (readinessTimeout 90 s, arithmetic in its doc); cleanup kills a leaked daemon.

GUARD DECISION (item 4)
The two existing guards visit STRINGS handed to them (rendered stderr), not files; their file walk only derives the task-id corpus. Widening them to every _test.go in internal/audit and internal/tasks would go RED today on 10 other files, 140 hit lines (migrate_v2_v3_test.go 42, migrate_test.go 29, well_known_test.go 17, c4_provenance_unmodified_test.go 14, tracker_race_test.go 12, six more) — far above the ten-line fix budget — and a sweep scoped to my three files would be a list called a population, which the guard's own doctrine forbids. text:
FOLLOW-UP — third loser path fixed. NEW FINAL SHA fdb9aac on fix/scenario-test-names (5 commits over 99635ef; not pushed; tree clean). Supersedes the SHA in the previous report; everything else in that report stands.

NEW COMMIT
5. fdb9aac fix(tasks): let two daemons register the built-in agents at once — internal/tasks/well_known.go, internal/tasks/well_known_concurrent_test.go (ownership named == touched, verified with git show --name-only).

THE PATH
Two daemons on one file both miss the fast-path lookup for a built-in agent's name, both mint an agent through provenance, and both try to bind their own id to that name. pasture_well_known_agents.name is UNIQUE, so the daemon that took the write lock second died with "UNIQUE constraint failed: pasture_well_known_agents.name" (exit 5). The race test refused it correctly.

THE FIX (product, per ruling B)
bindWellKnownAgent (extracted from ensureWellKnownAgent) inserts with ON CONFLICT(name) DO NOTHING and reads the bound id back inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. A daemon whose insert was skipped adopts the id the other daemon bound and writes no role row of its own: the other daemon's transaction, which this one waited behind on the write lock, already committed both rows together. The minted agent that lost stays unused, which the file's ordering note already allowed for a crash between minting and binding. No schema change.

TESTS (internal/tasks/well_known_concurrent_test.go)
- TestBindingASecondMintedIdToABoundNameKeepsTheFirstAndWritesNoSecondRoleRow: two minted ids bound to one name in the order the lock imposes; the second call returns the first id; one mapping row; one role row (the first id's); none for the second.
- TestTwoProcessesRegisteringTheBuiltInAgentsAtOnceAgreeOnEveryId: two real trackers on one fresh file, a start barrier, RegisterWellKnownAgents concurrently; both succeed; 15 mapping rows, 15 distinct names, 15 role rows bound to a name; both caches hold the same id for every name and it is the id the file binds.
- MUTATION (bare INSERT restored, ON CONFLICT dropped): both RED — "the second binding of \"pasture/automaton/check-constraints\", as the process that lost the write lock makes it, failed: storage error: Pasture couldn't save the name-to-id mapping for the built-in agent \"pasture/automaton/check-constraints\". Cause: constraint failed: UNIQUE constraint failed: pasture_well_known_agents.name" and "registration B failed while A registered the same names: ... UNIQUE constraint failed: pasture_well_known_agents.name". File restored byte-identical.

FIRST-START WRITE INVENTORY (pastured main -> initAuditTrail -> engine.New), each under a concurrent second process
- audit open (internal/audit/sqlite.go): PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF and ensureSchema — retried on a held file (17be7e2); DDL is IF NOT EXISTS.
- audit migrator (internal/audit/migrate.go): every step under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with the version re-checked under the lock; a step another process completed is skipped.
- tasks.OpenTaskTracker: ensurePastureTables — CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS only; system identity — INSERT OR IGNORE on a singleton row, then re-read (first writer wins by design); provenance store open — retried on busy by the library for up to 30 s (provenance internal/sqlite/db.go).
- RegisterWellKnownAgents: fixed above. Its provenance RegisterSoftwareAgent mints a fresh row per call by design; the binding reconciles.
- initHooksManager: OpenAuditDBForFreeFloating opens a handle on a file this process has already switched to WAL; RegisterDefaultRecorders is in-memory.
- engine.New: durable schema gate — waits out a layout in flight (d2f86b8); ensureProjectionTable — IF NOT EXISTS; durable bootstrap — bounded retry on the lost-race signature (existing); queue rows — QueueConflictAlwaysUpdate; governed allocator bind — no CREATE or INSERT found in provenance.NewHostBoundGovernedAllocator.
- What cannot be made idempotent by this change: a write lock the peer holds for longer than one SQLite busy window (500 ms) while this process registers or creates tables. The driver's busy_timeout bounds each such wait; a loss beyond it now fails the race test loudly with its text quoted, by design, instead of being accepted.

REVIEW of 56a8c25 (fix/scenario-test-names, four commits over pasture main 99635ef) — reviewer-scenario-names, axes A+B+C.

VOTE: REVISE. Tally: 1 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 3 MINOR.

1. THE GATE'S CONTROL FLOW AS I READ IT (internal/engine/schema_gate.go)
Entry points: RequireSupportedDurableSchema <- engine.New (pastured, pasture-recovery-probe, enginetest) and handlers.gateDurableSchema <- openClient <- OpenEpochController / queue command. Not reached by `pasture hook lifecycle` (it opens tasks.OpenTaskTracker only).
awaitSupportedDurableSchema: Validate(profile) -> CategoryConfig error; interval = SQLiteBusy (500 ms prod), bound = WorkflowResult (30 s prod), deadline = now+bound. First look: usable -> nil; error -> unreadable sentence. Loop: deadline reached -> progressed ? unfinished sentence : older-build sentence; pause(interval) with ctx -> cancelled sentence; look: usable -> nil; writerHeld -> progressed, quiet reset; superseded -> moved = state changed or version changed -> progressed, quiet reset; else if !progressed and quiet >= interval -> older-build sentence. So: a genuinely old file is refused after exactly one window (500 ms; one window more than main). Once progress was seen the wait runs to the bound whatever happens after (a stalled migrator is reported as "did not finish within 30s", which is true, and the re-run gives the older-build sentence; safe design, docs imprecise -> MINOR hps019). Two losers: each holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE for microseconds; measured four concurrent losers on one old file: all refused with the sentinel in ~30 ms, no deadlock, no false "migrating". Progress read: dbos_migrations is a single-row table (UPDATE per migration in dbos-transact-golang v1.2.0; provenance v0.0.7 reads the same SELECT ... LIMIT 1), so LIMIT 1 without ORDER BY is correct. Worst case wall clock = bound + one interval + one busy window (~31 s). Cancellation: real-clock probes — cancel during a pause returns at the cancel (150 ms) with the cancelled sentence; cancel while BEGIN IMMEDIATE is blocked returns after that busy window (504 ms) with the cancelled sentence (modernc does not abort a busy wait on ctx). Serial budget: pastured has no budget (signal ctx); the CLI controller passes context.Background(); the hook path never reaches the gate.

2. HOOK PATH BUDGET (axis A) — byte-identical.
`pasture hook lifecycle` -> handlers.HookLifecycleNative -> tasks.OpenTaskTracker -> audit.NewSqliteAuditTrail, which NOW runs the foreign-key pragma and ensureSchema through retryOnBusy with context.Background() and a 30 s ceiling. That is the pre-existing shape (the migrator already ran to its own 30 s ceiling; cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go documents that the store opener takes no context) and the invocation is bounded by the select on the 5 s deadline that abandons the work goroutine and exits. Driven on the built binaries from 56a8c25 and 99635ef, same store path, 12 routes: claude-code SessionStart 2.1.222, codex SessionStart 0.146.0, opencode session.created 1.18.10, each valid / session identity dropped / zero-length stdin / held lock (a second process holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE + a CREATE TABLE for the whole run, lock confirmed held by a refused probe). Every route: rc 0, stdout byte-identical (empty for claude and opencode, `{}` for codex), stderr byte-identical (0 / 2176 / 1605 / 1463 bytes claude; 0 / 1984 / 1599 / 1457 codex; 0 / 1988 / 1591 / 1449 opencode), held-lock elapsed 5.01 s on both binaries with "stopped waiting at its 5s hook-invocation deadline and abandoned the work" on all three harnesses. Fault records 9 lines each (timestamps, not byte-compared). No new wait is reachable from a hook invocation.

3. THE GATE — MY MUTATIONS (archive copy, -race)
- GM1 progress signal ignored (writerHeld no-op, moved=false): RED — loser test ("the gate refused a layout another process was still writing"), outlives-bound test, cancelled test; stable-old-layout test stays GREEN (refuses an old file promptly).

- Real-clock probes (no mutation): cancel during pause / during probe / four concurrent losers — all as designed (see 1).

4. THE AUDIT RETRY (internal/audit/open_retry.go, sqlite.go)
Bounded by busyRetryCeiling 30 s (start of last attempt), backoff 50 ms -> 2 s, ctx honoured between attempts; wraps only the two statements outside the migrator's transaction (PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, which is the first statement and carries the WAL switch; ensureSchema, all IF NOT EXISTS). isBusyError matches SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED text only; a corruption ("malformed") is returned unchanged on attempt 1. Mutation AM1 (retry on any error): RED "attempts = 11, want 1". Mutation MC (retry disabled under the two-daemon test, x12): 4/12 RED, every one exit 2 "cannot relax foreign-key enforcement ... database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)" — the loser path the worker reported at 1/6 is real and the retry covers it; with the retry, 0 losers in 80 runs (the loser proceeds to readiness). Right layer: yes, the first statement on a fresh connection is where the un-handled read-to-write upgrade lives.

5. THE RACE TEST (internal/audit/migrate_v3_backfill_test.go)
No time.Sleep in any changed file. Each daemon is awaited to a terminal state (ready log or exit) on a 90 s timer; verdicts: at least one ready; every early exit must be exit 5 AND one of four sentences; invariants as the daemons left the file, the daemon-left file must pass engine.RequireSupportedDurableSchema, then reopen and invariants again; cleanup kills a leaked daemon. Guard list has 8 entries; dbosRaceRetryCeiling and busyRetryCeiling are both 30 s as AGENTS.md says. Q1. DOES EVERY ADDED PIN NAME ITS MUTATION?
- L1 PS4 (two boundary cases): the leaf body names none. reviewer-b's comment on the leaf names it: drop the frozen-pin condition so the exemption covers every fixture; the frozen-pin case turns RED. Performable. OK.
- L1 reviewer-a (enumerate the exemption): NO mutation named. I name it: widen the exemption from the enumerated list back to the version predicate, or to every fixture; the case "an unlisted fixture at an OLD pin with no Clearance" turns RED.
- L2 PS2 (pin operator text): the mutation is named in general form (remove or alter the phrase). The text is not enumerated. I enumerate four sites: (1) the duplicate-ordinal refusal names both arms and the ordinal; (2) the out-of-range refusal names the arm, its ordinal and the harness range; (3) the String() values of the two new reasons; (4) the corpus refusal for arm 6 or 7 without a CLEARANCE.md path names the event and the reason. Each is pinned by phrase and shown RED by editing the phrase.
- L8 PS1 ("unset" token): named. See Q2.
- L9 reviewer-b (Git-hook guard, source mutation): named. Performable inside an archive copy with one non-comment line that carries the needle. No hook is installed.
- xw71qw: a decision, no pin.

Q2. IS EVERY NAMED MUTATION ONE I CAN PERFORM?
- L8 PS1, second clause: "show that the A27 equality check can then no longer tell the two cases apart" is NOT performable in S1. The A27 check belongs to S4-L7 and does not exist. I perform the first clause: render the empty string and the report-shape test turns RED, saying "unset" and absent are different states. The second clause is for S4-L7 when the check exists. Same class: "a row derived as None renders None" needs ResponseCapability, an S3 type. In S1 I pin the token table (three distinct tokens: "unset", "none", "") and that every S1 row renders "unset" for capability. The None derivation is S3's to prove.
- CONTRADICTION in L1, surfaced, not chosen. reviewer-b's PS4 case says "a fixture at an OLDER pin does NOT require Clearance". reviewer-a's fix says the exemption is an ENUMERATED list, so an UNLISTED fixture requires Clearance whatever its version. Under the enumeration, reviewer-b's older-pin case is false for an unlisted fixture. Proposed reconciliation for a ruling: key the exemption on the enumerated declared rawFileDigest of the legacy sidecars. Cases: (a) a listed legacy fixture without Clearance is accepted; (b) an unlisted fixture at a frozen pin without Clearance is refused; (c) an unlisted fixture at an OLD pin without Clearance is refused (this replaces reviewer-b's older-pin case). Mutations: drop the list check, cases (b) and (c) turn RED; replace the list with the version predicate, case (c) turns RED. I do not commit L1 until this is ruled.

Q3. DID A FIX ADD OPERATOR TEXT WITHOUT A PIN?
- L1 reviewer-a: the refusal for an unlisted fixture without Clearance is new operator text with no pin asked. I pin its load-bearing phrases: the fixture digest, the phrase that names the exemption list, and the fix (add a Clearance path to a CLEARANCE.md).

F3 xw71qw. Nothing in the binary writes a clearance authority: zero non-test Go hits. author: David Huu Pham
text:
SUPERVISOR-S1 RULINGS on worker-s1a's section-4 self-check, 2026-09-05. The self-check is NOT nil and it was worth doing: it found one real contradiction and two routing questions before any code was written. That is the outcome the check exists for.

RULING 1 — the L1 (5onrkf) contradiction. THE ENUMERATION WINS; reviewer-b's REQUIREMENT survives, only its EXAMPLE changes.
The two findings do not disagree about the goal. reviewer-b asked that the boundary be asserted DIRECTLY, by explicit cases that do not depend on what other fixtures happen to hold. reviewer-a asked that the exemption cover a CLOSED set, because a version predicate leaves it open to every future fixture. reviewer-b's "older pin is exempt" was written as an ILLUSTRATION of a direct assertion, at a time when the exemption WAS a version predicate. Under an enumeration that illustration is false, and reviewer-b's actual requirement — direct, non-incidental cases — is fully met by the worker's three cases.
ADOPTED, with one strengthening. Key the exemption on BOTH the committed fixture PATH AND its declared rawFileDigest. Both must match an enumerated entry.
- The PATH half closes reviewer-a's hole: an unlisted fixture is never exempt, whatever its version.
- The DIGEST half closes a hole neither reviewer named: keyed on the path alone, the CONTENT at a listed path could be replaced later and stay exempt from the one enforceable half of the privacy promise. The exemption must cover the fixtures that exist today, not the names they happen to sit under.
CASES: (a) a listed legacy fixture without Clearance is ACCEPTED; (b) an unlisted fixture at a FROZEN pin is REFUSED; (c) an unlisted fixture at an OLD pin is REFUSED — this replaces reviewer-b's older-pin case and is the case that proves the exemption is not a version predicate.
NON-VACUITY CONTROL, required: the enumerated list is non-empty AND every entry resolves to a fixture that exists in the tree. A stale entry is an error. Without this the list can rot to empty and every case above still passes while guarding nothing.
MUTATIONS, all performable: drop the path check -> (b) and (c) RED. Replace the pair with the version predicate -> (c) RED. Change one enumerated entry's digest so it no longer matches that fixture's declared digest -> that fixture stops being exempt and its refusal turns RED. Empty the list -> the non-vacuity control turns RED.
S2 INHERITS A LIST, NOT A PREDICATE, which is what leaf S2-L3 needs to delete and to prove "an exempt fixture can no longer exist".
Both reviewer findings are DISCHARGED by this shape. State the reconciliation in your report so the review wave reads the ruling and not the two original texts.
