RESULT: NOT NIL. 2 pins without a mutation, 5 mutations I cannot perform as written, 2 operator texts without a pin, 4 contradictions, 5 files outside my set. No code is written yet.

Q1. DOES EVERY ADDED PIN NAME ITS MUTATION?
- L4 PS2: yes ("remove or alter the phrase").
- L5 reviewer-a: yes (narrow the Claude range; a wrong exact version).
- L6 reviewer-a: the free-text assertion, yes. The 4 KiB tool-response assertion ("enforce step 7 the same way"): NO mutation named. I add one: plant a tool-response field over 4 KiB in a fixture; RED naming the fixture and the field.
- L10 reviewer-b: yes (register a new event with a free-text field; no test edit).
- L11 PS1: yes, both. reviewer-a age bound: covered by the original "remove the age threshold". reviewer-b "no OTHER command reaches the reclaim": NO mutation named. I add one: call the reclaim from `hook lifecycle orphans`; the reach guard turns RED.
- L7: no amendment. Clean.

Q2. CAN THIS WORKER PERFORM EVERY NAMED MUTATION? Five cannot be performed as written.
- P1 (L10). "REGISTER A NEW EVENT" means a row in hostcontract/*.go plus regeneration of registration/*.gen.go. Side B may not regenerate and may not touch a generated file. I CAN perform the same-class mutation on the runtime profile rows I own (lifecycle_profiles_*.go): add an event arm and a mapping that declares a "prompt" identity; the guard must go RED with no test edit. The guard will derive its population from BOTH tables (the runtime contracts and registration.*().Events). RULING NEEDED: is the registration-side mutation run by the reviewer on its own copy, or may I hand-edit the generated file in a throwaway archive copy that is deleted after the run?
- P2 (L11). THE AGE BOUND HAS NOTHING TO READ. lifecycle_payload_blobs is (digest, body, byte_count) WITHOUT ROWID (internal/audit/migrate_v5_v6.go). No written-at column exists, and an orphan has no occurrence row to borrow received_at from. Every age case (older reclaimed, younger kept, in-flight kept) is unperformable without a schema change: a new audit migration (v7 to v8) that adds a written-at column, and receipt.SQLiteBlobStore.Put that stamps it. internal/audit/* and receipt/journal.go are outside my set. RULING NEEDED.
- P3 (L11). THE SINGLE CALL SITE. The reclaim must run only after a SUCCESSFUL lifecycle commit, inside the hook deadline, on the tracker that is already open. That point is handlers.hookLifecycle after deliveryCommit (internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go): outside my set, and in nobody's set. I can own internal/tasks/lifecycle_reclaim.go and its test (the bounded reclaim, the cap, the narrow delete interface the S0 forward note asks for, the reach guard). The one call needs a ruling.
- P4 (L4). THE SINK CANNOT REACH THE PRODUCTION PATH FROM MY FILES. HookEnvironment.CaptureDir is parsed in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go. The handler reads stdin only AFTER the activation check: a WITHHELD event refuses before any byte is read ("The input was not read"), and withheld events are exactly what a capture campaign records. So the capture must read stdin BEFORE the handler, in the work goroutine of cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go: bounded read, sink.Record, then a bytes.Reader to the handler. That file is outside my set. Change text in R1.
- P5 (L5). A VERSION FAULT HAS NO CHANNEL FROM MY FILES. The per-harness Parse returns a Capture with no error, and model.CaptureDisposition has no version arm. The fault that names the observed and the admitted versions must be raised by the handler before parse (internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go), outside my set. See C1.

Q3. DID A FIX INTRODUCE OPERATOR TEXT WITHOUT A PIN?
- L5 reviewer-a: the inadmissible-version diagnostic ("naming the observed and the admitted versions") is new operator text with no pin named. I will pin two load-bearing phrases (the observed version; the admitted version or range) and mutate each.
- L4 PS2: the reason folded into "never creates directories" becomes the missing-directory warning. I will pin its load-bearing phrase and mutate it.
- L6, L7, L10, L11: no new operator text. The reclaim (L11) emits nothing on success. A reclaim FAILURE must not be silent (S0 rule: swallowed is not silent), but the handler has no stderr writer. DECISION NEEDED: silent best-effort, or one stderr line through the cmd layer.

CONTRADICTIONS, surfaced and not chosen:
- C1 (L5 vs the shipped design and S0 pins). L5 puts version ADMISSION on the live hook path. The tree says the opposite in three places: model/envelope.go ("provenance, not an admission check"); handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:258 and hook_lifecycle_raw.go:179 (Why text); cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go:3996 and :4095, which PIN "this build retains the version without using it as an admission check" on the unbindable-payload diagnostic. ALSO: the generated Claude hooks pass `--host-version "${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:-unknown}"` (internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go:177; hooks/hooks.json). tools/capture-claude-hook.sh falls back to `claude --version` because that variable can be absent. If Claude Code does not export it, EVERY Claude invocation carries "unknown"; no range admits "unknown"; admission faults on every event and the user loses all journaling under fail-open. That is the failure reviewer-a's finding exists to prevent, from a different cause. Options: (a) admission judges only a parseable version; an unparseable one is recorded as provenance and admitted with a diagnostic; (b) admission as written; (c) another rule. Also: who edits the three texts and the pin.

Section 6 says the worker writes the ACCEPT and reports; the team lead pushes. L6 was not among the six corrected leaves. I will write AGENTS.md per section 6 unless told otherwise.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CARRY-FORWARD FROM S1, recorded by supervisor-s1 on 2026-09-05 so it is not lost. This is a note, not a scope change.

S1 leaf rlwt8r (S1-L8) renders a capability column on all three activation reports. reviewer-b required the explicit "unset" token to be PINNED with a named mutation, because acceptance criterion A27 depends on it: if "unset" degrades to the empty string, a downstream check can compare blanks and pass VACUOUSLY.

S1 performs the half it can: the renderer is mutated to emit "" where it emits "unset" and the pin turns RED. S1 CANNOT perform the other half, because it needs the derived-capability type that arrives in S3. The value cannot be "derived as None" in S1; the type does not exist yet.

WHAT S3 MUST DO when it derives ResponseCapability: perform the second mutation. Show that a capability DERIVED as None renders a value DISTINCT from the not-yet-derived token "unset" and distinct from the empty string, and that a downstream comparison cannot pass by comparing two blanks.

THE DISTINCTION IS THREE-WAY, not two-way, and S1 pins all three shapes it can reach: a CITATION where evidence exists; "unset" where the value is NOT YET DERIVED; the EMPTY STRING reserved for a genuinely ABSENT evidence source. A reader cannot act on a column that collapses "not yet known" into "none". S3 must keep the three apart when it fills the column.

text:
TEAM-LEAD RULINGS RELAYED BY supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05, AND ONE CORRECTION OF MY OWN EARLIER RULING. The lead's text is authoritative where it differs from mine. I name the difference rather than quietly replace it, because a superseded claim is corrected by a later statement that names it.

L1 EXEMPTION (lead ruling Q2). ADOPTED as the lead states it. The exemption is keyed on the ENUMERATED rawFileDigest list of the 14 legacy Claude sidecars. Cases: (a) a listed legacy fixture without Clearance is ACCEPTED; (b) an unlisted fixture at a frozen pin without Clearance is REFUSED; (c) an unlisted fixture at an OLD pin without Clearance is REFUSED. Mutations: drop the list check -> (b) and (c) RED; replace the list with the version predicate -> (c) RED.
SUPERSESSION, to be read before the review wave: reviewer-b's case "a fixture at an OLDER pin does NOT require Clearance" is SUPERSEDED by reviewer-a's later enumeration fix, for any UNLISTED fixture. reviewer-b's REQUIREMENT — that the boundary is asserted DIRECTLY, by cases that do not depend on what other fixtures happen to hold — is unchanged and is met by cases (a), (b) and (c).
TWO ADDITIONS I KEEP FROM MY EARLIER RULING, because they are strictly additive and neither reviewer named them. If the lead refuses either, the lead's word stands.
- ALSO KEY ON THE COMMITTED PATH, not the digest alone. Keyed on a declared digest alone, a NEW fixture that copies a listed digest inherits the exemption. Both the path and the declared digest must match an enumerated entry.
- NON-VACUITY CONTROL, mandatory: the list is NON-EMPTY and every entry resolves to a fixture that exists in the tree; a stale entry is an error. Without it the list can rot to empty while every case above still passes and nothing is guarded. Mutation: empty the list, the control turns RED.

xw71qw (lead ruling F3). THE LEAD'S RULING REPLACES MINE. I ruled DELETE THE FIELD, on the ground that I could not confirm that issue 56 covers the CODEX sidecars, which are the two that carry the tracker id, since the issue is titled for OpenCode and is CLOSED. THE LEAD SUPPLIED THE FACT I LACKED: issue 56 is the EXTERNAL LINK of the Beads task the id names. That was the whole basis of my objection, so my objection falls.
DO THIS: set https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/issues/56 as the value in the four legacy sidecars (codex session_start_0_146_0 and pre_tool_use_0_146_0; opencode session_created_1_18_10 and tool_execute_before_1_18_10) and in the two test literals. The OpenCode sidecars carry an UNCOMMITTED .agents.local path today, which is the same defect class — a reference a reader cannot follow — so they change too.
THE TYPE DECISION STANDS AND THE LEAD ACCEPTED IT: a Clearance IS the committed CLEARANCE.md path that holds the verbatim acceptance; clearanceAuthority RETIRES with the legacy sidecars in leaf S2-L3. So the URL is a BRIDGE for four fixtures that S2 deletes, not a second durable-reference shape for new work. No new fixture may use it.
WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE from my ruling, because the lead did not touch it and it is the reason the finding exists: this defect survived every prose sweep because it is DATA THE PRODUCT CARRIES, not prose. The bare-tracker-id refusal must NOT stop at the Clearance field. Add a guard that DERIVES its population by walking EVERY committed provenance sidecar and refuses any field value matching the bare-tracker-id pattern, with a non-vacuity control: plant one and show RED naming the file and the field. A hand list of four files would pass its own mutations and be blind to every sidecar S2 and Wave 1 add.

MAKEFILE (lead ruling F4). Side A's, generate target only. Unchanged from my ruling. Side B does not touch the Makefile.

F8 (lead ruling). KEEP the array in .opencode/pasture-opencode.json and keep the agreement assertion. Do NOT widen to opencode_target_test.go.

F1 IS A RECORDED DEVIATION, NOT A RULING, and it must appear in the slice report AND as a comment on leaf 7fcvjf: only the 14 Claude sidecars are CaptureProvenance-shaped; the Codex and OpenCode evaluations use canonical-shape sidecars synthesized in temporary directories from the real bytes.

OWNERSHIP. Every widening of a side's set appears in the slice ownership statement IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT USES IT. Side A's set now also holds: the four legacy provenance sidecars; internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/fixture_digest_test.go; cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go; the Makefile generate target. Side B must not touch those six files or the Makefile, and has been told.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SUPERVISOR-S1 RULINGS on worker-s1b's section-4 self-check, 2026-09-05. The check found more than side A's did, and two of its findings are the kind that ship green and unfixed. I re-measured the three load-bearing facts in the tree before ruling. All three HOLD.

MEASURED, so the rulings rest on the tree and not on the report:
- lifecycle_payload_blobs is created at internal/audit/migrate_v5_v6.go with columns digest, body, byte_count ONLY. There is NO timestamp. An age bound has nothing to read. CONFIRMED.
- internal/lifecycle/model/envelope.go carries the comment "not an admission check; payloads are retained even when this value falls...". CONFIRMED.
- Every generated Claude hook row invokes the binary with --host-version "${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:-unknown}" (internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go and the shipped internal/target/claudecode/.../hooks.json). CONFIRMED, in the SHIPPED artefact, for every event.

RULING 1 and 2 (L11 s6k7mg, the age bound and the call site): SURFACED, NOT DECIDED HERE. DO NOT IMPLEMENT L11 YET. Move it to the END of your queue and proceed with everything else.
The leaf asks for a bound the schema cannot express. The two honest options both cost more than a leaf: (i) add an audit migration plus a stamp in the blob writer, which is a SCHEMA CHANGE on the durable store inside a substrate slice that S3 also touches; or (ii) take the reclaim OFF the hook path and give it an explicit command, which reviewer-a already pre-authorised in the leaf text as the fallback when the bound is not provable.
I am not choosing a schema change on my own authority, and L11 is P2 and last in your order, so nothing waits on it. It goes to the team lead with both costs. If option (ii) is chosen, ruling 2 disappears with it, because there is then no hook-path call site. If option (i) is chosen, the single statement in internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go IS YOURS and your set widens.
NOTE FOR WHOEVER DECIDES: an explicit command still cannot tell an ORPHAN from a blob whose append is IN FLIGHT without a timestamp. Option (ii) must therefore say what makes it safe, not merely move the code.

RULING 3 (L4 8yrtxu, reaching the production path): YES. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go IS YOURS, for the capture wiring only. Your set widens; state it in the same commit.
The reasoning is the same one that gave side A the Makefile: the wiring is the ENTRY POINT of the thing you own. Side A has no leaf that touches this file, so the sets stay disjoint.
THIS FINDING IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE IN YOUR CHECK. A capture sink that cannot capture a WITHHELD event captures nothing the campaign needs, because every event Wave 1 must capture is withheld today. The leaf would have shipped green and useless.
THREE CONDITIONS, and they are not optional, because the review wave must prove the hook path is BYTE-IDENTICAL against a binary built from d3edb79 on the existing 8 Claude, 2 Codex and 2 OpenCode enabled events:
- THE EARLIER STDIN READ IS GATED ON PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR BEING SET. When it is unset, the ordering and the bytes are exactly as they are today. Pin that: with the variable unset, the path is unchanged.
- A CAPTURE FAILURE NEVER CHANGES THE HOST OUTCOME. It is fail-open with one notice. A full disk must not turn a proceed into a fault.
- THE READ STAYS INSIDE THE 5 s INVOCATION DEADLINE. Bound it; do not let a slow or never-closing stdin hold the host.
Mutations: unset the variable and show the ordering pin RED if the read moves anyway; make the sink fail and show the host outcome unchanged.

RULING 4 (L5 gf4wdu, version admission): DO NOT BUILD A LIVE ADMISSION GATE IN S1. The leaf's admission clause is SUPERSEDED BY MEASUREMENT, and I surface it to the team lead and to reviewer-a rather than let you choose.
reviewer-a's finding feared that an EXACT check would refuse every event the day Claude Code auto-updates. Your measurement shows something worse and present TODAY: the shipped hook passes the literal string "unknown" whenever CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION is absent from the host environment. NO RANGE ADMITS "unknown". So an admission gate would fault on EVERY Claude event on any machine where that variable is not set, and under fail-open the user would lose all journaling silently. That is the exact end-user harm reviewer-a raised, reached by a shorter road.
Against that stand three shipped texts and a PIN. Turning provenance into admission is a behaviour change on the live path that the byte-identity proof would have to refuse.
SO, FOR S1: the shared dispatch validates the PAYLOAD BINDING and RECORDS the host version as PROVENANCE, exactly as the shipped comment says. It admits nothing on the version. The version-range statement belongs where it already lives and is safe — the CORPUS evaluator, side A's leaf 7fcvjf, which reads fixtures and not live events. State the per-harness shape THERE: range for Claude, exact for Codex and OpenCode. Your leaf keeps the IdentityPolicy label with NO waist effect, which is what its title promises.
THE "unknown" FINDING IS A REAL DEFECT AND IT IS NOT S1'S TO FIX. The journal may record the literal "unknown" as a Claude host version, which makes every downstream version claim unreliable. It lives in the generated Claude transport. I am filing it upward; do not fix it and do not work round it.

RULING 5 (L10 1vk1v7, the registration mutation): PERFORM IT IN A THROWAWAY ARCHIVE COPY. That is not the live worktree and not the shared checkout, so the staging rule is respected: the rule exists to stop generation side effects reaching a shared tree, not to stop you proving a guard can fail.
CONDITIONS: the copy is discarded; NOTHING is staged from it; and the report names the file you hand-edited, the event you registered and the MESSAGE TEXT that turned RED.
DO NOT let this narrow the guard. The guard must DERIVE its population from BOTH tables so it covers rows you do not own. RULING RECORD, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Two exchanges CROSSED, so this comment states what is IN FORCE and what was PROPOSED AND WITHDRAWN. A reviewer reading the earlier comments will meet both; nothing is deleted, and each superseded line is named.

WITHDRAWN 1 — the sidecar URL. The team lead proposed replacing the persisted clearance authority in the four legacy sidecars with https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/issues/56, and I relayed it. THE LEAD HAS WITHDRAWN IT. IN FORCE: DELETE the `clearanceAuthority` key from the four legacy sidecars and remove the two assertions that read it (internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/fixture_digest_test.go and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go).
THE REASON IS A DISTINCTION WORTH CARRYING: the id-to-issue link the lead verified is a TRACKER FACT, not a CLEARANCE FACT. Issue 56 records an OpenCode capture experiment; the two sidecars carrying the tracker id are the CODEX ones. Writing that URL there would assert that those captures were cleared under that record, which nobody on this team can confirm. A value that LOOKS right and asserts an unconfirmable fact is worse than one that is honestly wrong.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TEAM-LEAD RULING on S1-L11 (s6k7mg), 2026-09-05. Decides supervisor-s1 rulings 1 and 2 (surfaced, not decided). OPTION (i), MADE SAFE BY MECHANISM. The reclaim stays on the hook path, after a successful commit, as the leaf says. The age bound gets something to read, and every writer window gets a real ceiling.

MEASURED FIRST, on the user's live store (read-only; a copy for the probes): lifecycle_payload_blobs holds 14,490 blobs, 54.8 MB (min 388 B, max 359 KB). lifecycle_occurrences holds 0 rows and journal holds 0 rows. EVERY blob is an orphan. Cause: the installed binary writes the blob, then fails at tasks.ResolveLifecycleIdentity ("the required bootstrap identity has not been established yet") and exits 0 under fail-open. The orphan growth this leaf was activated for is not a projection; it is the present state of the user's machine. That defect is filed separately; it is not S1's. Record the numbers on this leaf as the activation measurement.

THE RULING, six parts. Each is a mechanism, and each names its mutation.
1. SCHEMA. New audit migration v7 -> v8, internal/audit/migrate_v7_v8.go, on the shape of migrate_v6_v7.go; MaxKnownSchemaVersion becomes 8. `ALTER TABLE lifecycle_payload_blobs ADD COLUMN written_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (unix nanoseconds). Legacy rows keep 0 and are OLDER THAN ANY BOUND; that is correct, because the 14,490 orphans on the user's store are exactly the legacy rows. Mutation: run the migration test against a v7 store with a referenced legacy blob and show it is never reclaimed (named-by-nothing holds at any age).
2. STAMP. receipt.Service.Receive passes s.Clock.Now() to the blob write; the blob seam becomes a NARROW WRITE INTERFACE (Put with the written-at value) and a SEPARATE NARROW DELETE INTERFACE that only the reclaim constructs, per the S0 forward note on this leaf. Mutation: remove the stamp and show the age test RED (every fresh blob reads as legacy and is reclaimed at once).
3. THE BOUND IS THE WorkflowResult TIER of the injected timeouts Profile (30 s in production; DeadlineTestProfile in tests). It is the longest deadline any writer may hold. That claim is made TRUE by two mechanisms, not by inspection: (a) `pasture hook lifecycle raw` runs under a WorkflowResult-tier context deadline and reports a fault on expiry, as the native path does at the HookInvocation tier; (b) receipt.Service.Receive REFUSES a context that carries no deadline, or a deadline later than now plus the WorkflowResult tier, with a validation error that names the tier. No writer can then hold an unbounded window between the blob write and the append. Mutations: call Receive with context.Background() and show the refusal message; remove the refusal and show the in-flight test RED; remove raw's deadline and show the refusal fires on raw. Enumerate every Receive caller (production and tests) in the report; each test caller passes a deadline.
4. ELIGIBILITY AND CAP. A blob is reclaimed when no lifecycle_occurrences row names its digest AND written_at < now minus the tier; oldest first; at most 64 per invocation; one statement inside the invocation's own context (so it shares the 5 s budget). Mutations as the leaf already names: drop the named-by-nothing condition (a referenced blob is deleted, RED); drop the age bound (an in-flight blob is deleted, RED); drop the cap (the budget test is RED).
5. THE SINGLE CALL SITE is internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go, after deliveryCommit returns nil, NATIVE path only; raw does not reclaim; the fault path does not reclaim. A reclaim error writes ONE stderr line through the handler's diagnostic writer and never changes the host outcome. Mutation: call the reclaim from the fault path and show RED; make the reclaim fail and show the host bytes unchanged. The reach guard states what it reads and what it does not.
6. BUDGET PROOF. With more orphans than the cap, exactly the cap is reclaimed and the invocation stays inside its budget; the proof waits on a condition, never a clock.

- the earlier stdin read is GATED on PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR being set, and with it UNSET the ordering and the bytes are exactly today's, which is PINNED;
- a capture failure NEVER changes the host outcome; it is fail-open with one notice;
- the read stays inside the 5 s invocation deadline.

- cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go (capture wiring only)

- internal/lifecycle/ingress/inventory.go
SIDE A'S SET IS UNCHANGED BY ALL OF THIS. The two sets remain DISJOINT, which is the condition the A/B split rests on. Every widening is stated in the SAME COMMIT that uses it.

The rule given to side B: if anything it builds appears to require editing one, that is a SIGNAL THAT LIVE BEHAVIOUR CHANGED WITHOUT INTENT, and the worker STOPS AND REPORTS instead of updating the pin. A pin edited to match new work has stopped testing anything.

- xw71qw: DELETE the field, NO URL. worker-s1a was stopped before it touched the four sidecars, so nothing was written and nothing needs undoing.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L10 1vk1v7 DONE (worker-s1b). Commit 360ae53 on slice/rp2tju-s1-b (on top of L7 30ee142). Porcelain empty after commit.

OWNERSHIP, named == touched (git show --stat 360ae53: 1 file): internal/lifecycle/waist/l2_content_guard_test.go (new, package waist_test).

WHAT THE GUARD IS. Three data-driven checks over EVERY row of the three pinned lifecycle profiles (population = the contracts' own Events(), 87 rows) tied to EVERY row of the three registration manifests (87):
1. Declaration guard: a profile row may declare as an identity only a field of a declared correlation kind whose name is an identifier name (a bare identifier ending in "id": all 13 declared fields are; prompt, tool_input, tool_response, message, output are not). RED names the row and the field.
2. Registration tie: every profile row has one registration row by native name and the reverse; every registration identity must exist in the profile row with the same kind and requirement; the registration may never declare MORE identities than the profile row. The tie on identities is DIRECTIONAL because the registration is silent on identities for the 19 unproven Codex (8) and OpenCode (11) rows; that number is pinned and can only shrink deliberately. A free-text identity added to the registration alone breaks the tie; added to the profile alone hits check 1; added to both hits check 1.
3. Wire guard: an L2 built from each row's declared identities with synthetic identifier values is derived through middleend.Derive; the interpreted record must carry exactly {semantic, identities, unresolved_facts, contract, manifest} with nested {kind,value}/{reason}/{id,version,content}; every identity value must be one of the supplied identifiers; a gate row's consultation record must carry exactly {legalized, response, interpreted} with {authority}/{decision}/{result_slot, content_digest}.

GATES on an archive copy of 360ae53, from inside the copy: build rc=0; vet rc=0; go test -race -count=1 ./... rc=0 with ok=72 packages, fail=0, DATA RACE=0, no-test-files=9; nix flake check --no-build rc=0; gofmt -l 0 files, negative control 1. Generate drift: NOT RUN (side A owns generation); no generated file is in the diff.

MUTATION-RED evidence (applied, run, restored by copy; NO edit to the test file in any of them):
- Free-text field on a target row: prompt declared as an identity on UserPromptSubmit -> `row claude-code/UserPromptSubmit declares "prompt" as a correlation identity, but that name is not an identifier name (a bare identifier ending in id); a field with this name carries content, and content never enters an L2`.
- Tool arguments and tool output: tool_input on PreToolUse and tool_response on PostToolUse -> the same sentence naming `claude-code/PreToolUse ... "tool_input"` and `claude-code/PostToolUse ... "tool_response"`.
- THE DATA-DRIVEN MUTATION (reviewer-b): a NEW profile event "Probe" (enum arm, name, mapping) declaring a prompt identity -> the subtest `TestEveryProfileIdentityFieldIsAnIdentifierName/claude-code/Probe` appeared and turned RED with `row claude-code/Probe declares "prompt" as a correlation identity ...`; the tie test also RED (`profile row claude-code/Probe has no registration row`).
- POSITIVE CONTROL: the same new event with a legal probe_id identity -> `--- PASS: TestEveryProfileIdentityFieldIsAnIdentifierName/claude-code/Probe` and `--- PASS: TestEveryProfileRowDerivesOnlyTheClosedWireShape/claude-code/Probe`, with no test edit; only the tie failed, for the missing registration row, which is the correct answer for a half-registered event.
- Inlined body: a `body` member added to the interpreted record (receipt/interpreted.go, temporary) -> on every row: `the interpreted record of claude-code/SessionStart carries members [body contract identities manifest semantic unresolved_facts]; the closed set is [semantic identities unresolved_facts contract manifest], and a member outside it is content the L2 must not carry`.

PERFORMABILITY NOTE (P1 from the self-check): the registration-side mutation ("register a new event" in hostcontract plus regeneration) was NOT performed by me; side B may not regenerate. The runtime-profile-side mutation above is the same class and was performed. The reviewer can run the registration-side one on its own copy; the tie check refuses a registration row that lifts an identity the profile lacks.

RE-ASSERTION NOTE for the harness slices (reviewer-b's note): the guard is data-driven, so a harness worker proves nothing more than that the guard RAN over its new rows (the subtest names appear in -v output); a second hand-listed copy is not needed and must not be written.

DEVIATIONS from the leaf text: (a) "walk EVERY enabled event's L2" is widened to every REGISTERED row of every profile (87), since a withheld row today becomes enabled tomorrow without a test edit; (b) the population is derived from the runtime profiles AND the registration manifests rather than the registration tables alone, because the registration exposes identity kinds but not field names, and the L2's identity names come from the profile.

FILE OUTSIDE MY SET, as a REPORT: waist.NewIdentity (internal/lifecycle/waist/event.go) accepts an identity VALUE with internal whitespace ("hello world" passes; only surrounding whitespace, control characters and size are refused). A value-level production refusal of prose-shaped identity values would close the last door at the value rather than the declaration. Not required by A16 as written; recorded for a ruling.

L4 8yrtxu: SINK AND TESTS DONE; PRODUCTION WIRING BLOCKED ON RULING R1 (worker-s1b). Commit eadacec on slice/rp2tju-s1-b (after 30ee142, 360ae53). Porcelain empty.

OWNERSHIP, named == touched (git show --stat eadacec: 2 files): internal/handlers/capture_sink.go (new), internal/handlers/capture_sink_test.go (new).

WHAT IT IS. CaptureSink (interface), DirectoryCaptureSink, NewDirectoryCaptureSink(dir, repoRoot, warnings), EnclosingRepositoryRoot(start), CaptureStem(harness, event, version). File name: <harness>_<snake_event>_<version_underscored>.<n>.json, created O_EXCL at one above the highest number present. Refusals (absolute; outside the repository, lexical AND after symlink resolution; must exist and be a directory; never created) each write ONE warning to the injected stream and return an error the caller uses to continue with capture off. ONE notice per sink, printed on the FIRST successful record (not at construction), so "capture mode is recording this session to <dir>" is true when read. The sink has no handle on stdout or the exit status, so the host outcome cannot change through it.

GATES on an archive copy of eadacec, from inside the copy: build rc=0; vet rc=0; go test -race -count=1 ./... rc=0 with ok=72 packages, fail=0, DATA RACE=0, no-test-files=9; nix flake check --no-build rc=0; gofmt -l 0 files, negative control 1. Generate drift: NOT RUN (side A owns generation); no generated file in the diff.

MUTATION-RED evidence (applied, run, restored by copy; the run named the test each time):
1. Allow an in-repository directory (both refusal branches disabled): TestCaptureSinkRefusesADirectoryInsideTheRepository and ...RefusesASymlinkThatResolvesInsideTheRepository RED, `An error is expected but got nil.`
2. Notice phrase "recording" -> "writing": RED, `expected: "pasture: capture mode is recording this session to <dir>" actual: "pasture: capture mode is writing this session to <dir>"`.
3. Missing-directory reason removed: RED, `... does not contain "a directory pasture creates is one you did not choose"`.
4. Relative-path reason removed: RED, `... does not contain "would land somewhere you did not choose"`.
5. Inside-repository reason removed: RED, `... does not contain "can reach a commit before it is cleared"`.
6. "the host is not affected" clause removed at both sites: three tests RED, each `does not contain "the host is not affected"`.
7. "so this payload was not captured" clause removed: two tests RED, `does not contain "so this payload was not captured"`.
8. Notice on every record instead of once: RED, `should have 1 item(s), but has 25`.
9. Overwrite instead of numbering (O_TRUNC, fixed n=1): RED, the second record came back as `.1.json` and the first record's bytes were replaced.

DEVIATIONS from the leaf text, with reasons:
(a) Record takes ir.HarnessID, not acceptance.HarnessKind. The hook command holds an ir.HarnessID; the sink writes no provenance, so the corpus vocabulary has no reader in it; the acceptance kind for Codex ("codex-cli") also differs from the hook id ("codex"), and a conversion at a call site I do not own would serve nothing.
(b) NewDirectoryCaptureSink takes a third argument, the warnings stream. The leaf says "a stderr warning"; a package-level stderr would make every refusal unreadable by a test, so the stream is injected and the hook passes its standard error.
(c) "unchanged Outcome" and A13 ("When the hook runs") are NOT yet proven at the binary. They need the call site in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go (ruling R1 in my self-check). Until it lands the sink is not reachable from the binary, and the commit message says so. When ruled, the R1 change is about 15 lines: build the sink from env.CaptureDir with repoRoot = EnclosingRepositoryRoot(cwd) and cmd.ErrOrStderr(); on refusal continue with capture off; on success read stdin bounded to model.MaxNativePayloadBytes+1 in the work goroutine BEFORE handlers.HookLifecycleNative (a withheld event refuses before any byte is read, and withheld events are what a capture campaign records), Record, then hand bytes.NewReader(raw) to the handler. I will add the built-binary proof (relative and in-repo PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR -> warning on stderr, unchanged exit and stdout, no file) in that change.

OBSERVED WHILE TESTING: on this machine /tmp itself is a git repository (/tmp/.git exists), so a temporary directory is never repository-free here. The no-repository test case skips with the repository named when the machine cannot arrange it; the positive cases (a .git directory and a .git file) run and pass. Recorded so a reviewer seeing SKIP knows why.

THE RULING, restated: cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go IS SIDE B's, FOR THE CAPTURE WIRING ONLY. The supervisor assigned it, the team lead briefly held it with the other ownerless files, and the lead has CONFIRMED the assignment. Side A has no leaf that touches it, so the sets stay disjoint. The widening is stated in the same commit that uses it.

THE WORKER'S PROPOSED SHAPE IS APPROVED as consistent with the ruling: build the sink from env.CaptureDir with the enclosing repository root and stderr; on refusal continue with capture off; a bounded stdin read in the work goroutine before HookLifecycleNative; Record; hand a bytes reader to the handler.

Continuing with capture off is correct, but a SILENT refusal is not — the operator must learn once that capture was requested and did not happen. author: David Huu Pham
text:
L5 gf4wdu: SHARED DISPATCH AND IDENTITY POLICY DONE; VERSION ADMISSION BLOCKED ON RULING C1 (worker-s1b). Commit 90dbfff on slice/rp2tju-s1-b (after 30ee142, 360ae53, eadacec). Porcelain empty.

OWNERSHIP, named == touched (git show --stat 90dbfff: 6 files): internal/lifecycle/ingress/validate.go (new), internal/lifecycle/ingress/validate_test.go (new), internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/capture.go, internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/capture.go, internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/capture.go (each only where it calls the shared dispatch; the Claude strict pass moved into the shared file), internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go (IdentityPolicy label, shared file).

WHAT IT IS. ingress.Validate applies the shared refusals in the Claude order (UTF-8, one JSON object with no trailing value, no repeated member) and returns the exact bytes, digest, members and disposition; the three parsers call it first and keep only the per-host binding. Before: the struct-decoding Codex and OpenCode parsers ACCEPTED invalid UTF-8 and repeated members as valid. After: the same malformed input is refused with the same disposition on every harness; valid input binds exactly as before (case-insensitive member match of the struct decoders kept). ingress.EventByNativeName is the validating reverse lookup with the harness and the name in the refusal; the handler's own lookup loop is unchanged (the S2 handover). runtime.IdentityPolicy is DERIVED from the identities column (None when a row declares no identity), so it cannot disagree with the table; no waist arm added; the single UnresolvedReason arm is pinned.

GATES on an archive copy of 90dbfff, from inside the copy: build rc=0; vet rc=0; test-race: ok=73 fail=0 race=0 no-test-files=9 === OVERALL RESULT=0 (0 = all five green) ; nix flake check --no-build rc=0; gofmt -l 0 files, negative control 1. Generate drift: NOT RUN (side A owns generation); no generated file in the diff.

MUTATION-RED evidence (applied, run, restored by copy; each run named its test):
1. opencode/file.edited (IdentityPolicyNone) given an unresolved tool-call kind: `row opencode/file.edited declares no identity and must declare no unresolved kind` (Should be empty, but was [tool-call]) and `row opencode/file.edited landed with an unresolved reason although it declares no identity; an identity-policy-none row never touches waist.UnresolvedReason` (was [{tool-call-unresolved}]). This is the leaf's named mutation.
2. The unknown-name refusal without the harness: `does not contain "the claude-code registration"` (every harness subtest RED).
3. The shared UTF-8 refusal disabled: `codex refused "a lone invalid byte" with 2; every harness must refuse the same malformed input with the same disposition` (2 = malformed; 3 = invalid-UTF-8 expected), same for opencode and claude-code.

C-GUARD-REACH: the IdentityPolicyNone population is derived from the three contracts' Events() with a non-vacuity control on both labels (at least one None row and at least one Declared row); EventByNativeName is checked against every manifest event plus four undeclared spellings per manifest; the harness parser set is the three ingress packages with a pinned count of 3.

DEVIATIONS from the leaf text, with reasons:
(a) NO HOST-VERSION ADMISSION on the live path in this commit (ruling C1 pending): the tree states three times that the observed version is provenance and not an admission check, a pin in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go holds that sentence, and the generated Claude hooks pass --host-version "${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:-unknown}". Whichever ruling comes, the admission function lives in validate.go and the FAULT is raised in the handler (R3, outside my set).
(b) EventByNativeName is defined and tested but the handler still runs its own loop (the leaf's stated S2 handover); replacing the loop is an edit to internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go (R3).
(c) "no correlation key" is proven through lineage.DeriveLinks over two zero-identity occurrences (no link derived), because a correlation key is what a lineage chain threads over; "ingress-order ordering" is stated on the label's doc and not asserted separately, since the row's Order() column is already pinned per row by the profile table test.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULINGS ON SIDE A's FOUR ADDITIONAL FILES, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Recorded on the durable channel, because a second mailbox drop has now occurred: worker-s1a reported that its commits still wait on three rulings that were decided and sent hours earlier. Beads is the channel that does not drop. Both workers are told to prefer it.

1. internal/codegen/opencode_manifest_test.go: SIDE A's. It is the SUBJECT TEST of an emitter side A owns, and the OpenCode manifest emitter now emits four files rather than three because of the new activation report. Updating that emitter's own pin from 3 to 4 is inside the leaf.

2. internal/codegen/skill_registry_test.go: SIDE A's, ADD THE LINE — AND IT IS ALSO A RECORDED FINDING, because side A has found a defect it is NOT being asked to fix. That guard HAND-LISTS each harness's generated outputs. That is exactly the shape the standing coverage rule forbids: a hand list with a loose check PASSES ITS OWN MUTATIONS while making a coverage claim it cannot keep, and the claim then stops the next reader looking. Adding one addExpectedOutput line keeps the guard working and keeps its claim false.
RULED: add the line so the new report is not flagged as orphaned; DO NOT widen S1's scope to re-derive the guard; RECORD IT AS A FINDING and the supervisor routes it upward. Scope discipline and honesty are both served: the defect is written down where the next reader meets it, and this slice does not grow to swallow it.

3. internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/catalogue_test.go: SIDE A's. IT IS IN NOBODY'S SET AND IT IS NOT SIDE B'S — side B owns validate.go, validate_test.go, secretscan_test.go, inventory.go and the three per-harness capture.go call sites only.
MAKE THE ONE-LINE CHANGE TO THE EXPLICIT CLAUDE EVALUATOR AND DELETE THE COMPATIBILITY BRIDGE. This is a ruling and not a preference. A package-level `Evaluate` bound to the Claude evaluator IS THE EXACT SHAPE OF THE DEFECT LEAF 7fcvjf EXISTS TO REMOVE: its acceptance criterion says the evaluator must NOT silently evaluate a non-Claude fixture against the Claude contract. A Claude-bound default kept in the package for one test's convenience is a loaded gun for the NEXT caller, however carefully it is documented and however correctly it refuses a foreign sidecar today. The documentation and the refusal protect the callers that exist; the shape endangers the callers that do not exist yet, which is the population the leaf is written for.

4. The Makefile generate target: SIDE A's, as already ruled, one line, with the load-bearing proof in both directions and the mandatory zero-arm hard error in the generator.

SIDE A's DEVIATIONS, ACCEPTED AS REPORTED, each to be named in the slice report with its reason:
- the evaluator checks the sidecar's HARNESS BEFORE its VERSION, because a foreign sidecar is a CATEGORY ERROR and not a version verdict. Every committed Claude corpus row decides as before; only a synthetic precedence case in the activation tests changed.
- the evidence column renders THREE distinct values, which is exactly the distinction ruled earlier: the EMPTY STRING for a row the contract declares non-blocking (a genuinely ABSENT source, the reserved meaning), the CITATION for a cited blocking row, and "unset" for an UNCITED blocking row. A reader cannot act on a column that collapses "not yet known" into "none".
- the capability column is "unset" on every row until S3 derives it.

STATUS AT THIS POINT: all five side-A leaves are implemented in the worktree and green per package, with mutation-RED evidence named by test — L1 23/23, L2 22/22, L3 16/16, L8 19/19 including one regeneration-based, L9 9/9 — and NOT YET COMMITTED. Nothing blocks the commits. Side B has four commits and a clean tree.

text:
TWO RULINGS ON SIDE B's ITEM 4, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Side B proceeded without the three side-A names rather than idle, which was right. Two REAL RISKS came out of it, and both must be closed BEFORE the fold. Neither is a criticism of proceeding.

4a. A SECOND EXEMPTION LIST NOW EXISTS, AND TWO LISTS THAT LOOK ALIKE WHILE MEANING DIFFERENT THINGS IS A DEFECT THIS PLAN ALREADY NAMES.
Side B exempts SEVEN fixtures, by payload digest, from the free-text assertion. Side A exempts FOURTEEN legacy Claude sidecars, by committed path and declared digest, from the CLEARANCE requirement. Side B proposed to "converge with A's list at the fold".
RULED: DO NOT CONVERGE THEM. They answer DIFFERENT QUESTIONS over DIFFERENT POPULATIONS, and they should almost certainly stay TWO lists. Merging them would produce one list that is wrong for both purposes, and the merge would be invisible afterwards.
WHAT IS REQUIRED INSTEAD: each list STATES WHAT IT COUNTS AND WHY, in the source, beside the list — side B's is "fixtures that carry free text and predate the redaction rule"; side A's is "fixtures that predate the clearance procedure". Each carries the NON-VACUITY CONTROL: non-empty, every entry resolves to a fixture that exists, a stale entry is an error. AT THE FOLD THE SUPERVISOR CHECKS THAT NEITHER LIST HAS SILENTLY BECOME THE OTHER.
WHY THIS IS RULED AND NOT LEFT TO THE FOLD: the plan already records this exact failure once. Three DIFFERENT populations were all called "the existing fixtures" — 18, 14, and 12 enabled plus 3 controls — and NONE of them was wrong on its own. A number that can be enumerated must be enumerated, and a list that can be named must say what it counts.

4b. THE TOLERANT READER IS A HEDGE AND IT EXPIRES.
Side B's corpus assertion reads "redaction" as A STRING OR A LIST, so that it passes whatever side A ships. That asserts almost nothing about the shape. It is the same degradation the standing rules name for a loosened pin: the test still passes and NO LONGER READS THE THING IT WAS WRITTEN TO READ.
RULED: it is a TOLERANT READER ONLY UNTIL SIDE A PUBLISHES THE SHAPE. The moment the shape lands on 5onrkf, side B TIGHTENS IT TO THE SINGLE SHAPE and PROVES THE TIGHTENING BY MUTATION — offer the other shape and show RED. Both states are reported, so the reviewer sees the hedge existed and sees it closed.

STATE, verified by read-only peek at this point. SIDE B: FIVE commits, tree CLEAN — 30ee142 the profile split with an 87-row committed table test and a placement guard; 360ae53 the L2 content guard, data-driven over 87 profile rows tied to 87 registration rows, with the new-event mutation run and NO test edit; eadacec the capture sink; 90dbfff the shared ingress refusals, EventByNativeName and the derived IdentityPolicy; 41ed546 the clearance procedure with its enforced steps, the secret scan over every testdata file, three CLEARANCE.md templates and the AGENTS.md section with pinned phrases. Each SHA gated green on an ARCHIVE COPY: build, vet, race naming 72 packages with 0 fail and 0 race, flake, gofmt with its negative control, and generation correctly reported as NOT SIDE B's to run. That is the evidence shape this slice asked for.
SIDE A: still ZERO commits and THIRTY-FIVE uncommitted paths, with all five leaves implemented and green per package. It remains the one open risk on the slice.

PROCEDURE, applied for the second time and now routine: side B reported items 1, 2 and 3 as blocked when all three had been ruled hours earlier. Under the standing rule those lines are treated as STALE, not as new questions, and the worker is told to READ THE TASK COMMENTS FROM 00:43 ONWARD and to acknowledge by LISTING THE RULINGS BACK. Both workers demonstrably use bd, since their leaf reports are posted there, so the durable channel works even when an inbox does not.

text:
R1 PROOF for the capture-sink wiring (worker-s1b). NOT applied to my worktree: cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go is outside my set. Measured on a throwaway archive copy of 41ed546 with the proposed change applied.

THE CHANGE (patch at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1b/r1.patch; 2 files):
- cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go: after the environment and the positional-argument check, before the work goroutine: `input := cmd.InOrStdin(); if env.CaptureDir != "" { input = captureHostPayload(cmd, coords, env.CaptureDir, input) }`, and the handler receives `Input: input`. captureHostPayload (new, same file): resolves the enclosing repository of the working directory with handlers.EnclosingRepositoryRoot, builds handlers.NewDirectoryCaptureSink(dir, repoRoot, cmd.ErrOrStderr()); on refusal returns stdin unchanged (the sink has warned); otherwise reads stdin bounded to model.MaxNativePayloadBytes+1 exactly as the handler does, records, and returns bytes.NewReader(raw) (a read error is handed on after the bytes read). About 40 lines with comments. No change to the handler package.
- cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_capture_test.go (new): built-binary proof on the WITHHELD Claude event Notification through runLifecycleHookOn. Baseline: exit 0, empty stdout, "is withheld" on stderr. Relative PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR: same exit, same stdout, stderr carries `PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR is "captures", which is not an absolute path, so nothing is captured` and still "is withheld", no notice. In-repo dir (<root>/internal): same exit, same stdout, "which is inside the repository at", no file written there. Accepted dir outside: same exit, same stdout, `pasture: capture mode is recording this session to <dir>`, still "is withheld", and <dir>/claude-code_notification_2_1_210.1.json holds the exact payload bytes.

RESULT on the copy: `--- PASS: TestCaptureDirectoryRefusalsLeaveTheHostOutcomeUnchanged (0.66s)`; the S0 wiring pin `TestTheProductionPathWiresThePassThroughBarrierAndTheProductionTier` PASS; `TestEveryWorkErrorMapsToTheDurableStateItCanSupport` PASS; go build and go vet clean. This is A13 measured on the binary: a withheld event, the whole point of a capture campaign, is captured before the handler refuses it, and the refusal is unchanged.

RULING NEEDED: who applies it. If ruled to me, I commit it as its own commit with an ownership paragraph that widens my set by these two files and the reason, and I run the five gates on it.

- STATE IN THE REPORT that the read stays inside the 5 s invocation deadline.

text:
DELIVERY PATH RECORDED, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. The TEAM LEAD relayed every side-B ruling DIRECTLY to worker-s1b at about 01:2x, after the worker sent the lead a backstop note saying two of its messages to the supervisor had no acknowledgement and that it was STANDING BY on R1, C1 and L11 as unruled.
The rulings the lead relayed are the ones already decided and already on these tasks: R1 with its four conditions; C1 build NEITHER shape; L11 option (i) per the six-part ruling on s6k7mg, with the widened file set and the Receive-caller enumeration done FIRST; the TWO-LIST ruling (side B's seven free-text exemptions and side A's fourteen clearance exemptions stay SEPARATE, each stating what it counts and why); and the TOLERANT READER ruling (the string-or-list reader is a hedge that expires the moment side A publishes the shape, and the tightening is proved by mutation).
NOTHING WAS RE-DECIDED. Only the delivery path changed, and it is recorded so a reader can tell an order that was re-sent from an order that was re-made.
THE DELIVERY FAILURE RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the worker's notes reached the supervisor while the supervisor's rulings did not reach the worker, and the worker's own reports reached the lead. Beads is therefore the CHANNEL OF RECORD for the rest of this slice: an order goes on the TASK FIRST and the inbox second, a worker RE-READS THE TASK COMMENTS BEFORE reporting a block, and a "blocked" line is treated as STALE until the worker acknowledges by listing the rulings back.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RELAY RULE ADOPTED FOR THE REST OF S1, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Recorded so a reader knows why orders now arrive by a different path, and so the same rule can be reused in S2 and S3.

THE MEASURED FAULT IS ASYMMETRIC, which is why the fix is a route change and not a retry policy. Worker notes reach the supervisor. Worker reports reach the team lead. Lead orders reach the workers. THE SUPERVISOR'S OUTBOUND LEG TO THE WORKERS IS THE ONE THAT DROPS. Retrying on a broken leg costs time and delivers nothing; the evidence is three dropped-order events and side A idle with five implemented and green leaves while holding a durable copy of every ruling it waited for.

THE RULE:
1. The supervisor records EVERY order on the LEAF and on gt001f FIRST. Beads is the channel of record and it does not drop.
2. For any order a worker must act on, the supervisor sends the team lead ONE LINE: "RELAY <worker>: <leaf id>, comment at <time>: <one-sentence gist>". The lead forwards a SHORT POINTER. The gist stays under three sentences; THE DURABLE TEXT LIVES ON BEADS.
3. Workers keep reporting to the supervisor by Beads comments and by message; that leg works.
4. The supervisor keeps verifying by READ-ONLY PEEK. A COMMIT IS THE PROOF AN ORDER WAS READ; an acknowledgement is a message, and messages are what is failing.
5. Long orders are NOT re-sent through the supervisor's own outbound leg.

ONE CONDITION ON THE COMPRESSION, and it is the risk the rule introduces. A POINTER CARRIES AN INSTRUCTION; THE DURABLE TEXT MUST KEEP THE REASON. A worker that receives only an instruction cannot check it, cannot notice when it is wrong, and cannot surface a contradiction — which is the behaviour this slice has depended on twice. So the Beads comment behind every pointer states the MECHANISM and the EVIDENCE, not merely what to do.
THE CASE THAT PROVES IT, from this slice: the path-versus-digest condition on the L1 exemption was ARGUED when it was ruled, and side A's own corpus then DEMONSTRATED it — three session-start sidecars share one payload, so one digest already maps to three files and a fourth file carrying that payload would inherit the exemption for free. A pointer saying "key on path as well as digest" is obeyable. Only the reason makes it checkable, and only a checkable rule gets challenged when it is wrong.

TWO POINTERS ARE LIVE UNDER THE NEW RULE: worker-s1a to 5onrkf (key the exemption on path AND digest; state which population was counted, since 11, 12 and 14 are all in play; then COMMIT), and worker-s1b to hqnytd (the Redaction shape is published, so the tolerant reader tightens to the list shape and the tightening is proved by mutation).

text:
THE THREE NAMES FOR SIDE B (worker-s1a, 2026-09-05), as implemented in internal/acceptance/capture.go and internal/lifecycle/activation/types.go on branch slice/rp2tju-s1-a:

1. REDACTION. Go: field `Redaction string` on `acceptance.CaptureProvenance`, JSON key "redaction". It is ONE STRING that encodes an ORDERED LIST: either "none" alone, or every applied rule in the order applied, joined by ",", for example "home-path-v1,free-text-v1". The closed rule set is the Go type `acceptance.RedactionRule` with constants `acceptance.RedactionNone` ("none"), `acceptance.RedactionHomePath` ("home-path-v1"), `acceptance.RedactionFreeText` ("free-text-v1"). Parse it with `acceptance.ParseRedaction(value string) ([]acceptance.RedactionRule, error)`: it refuses an empty value, a rule outside the set, a rule listed twice, and "none" combined with a rule, and it returns the rules in the recorded order. WHY A STRING AND NOT A JSON ARRAY: the fourteen committed Claude sidecars already carry a scalar ("none", "home-path-v1"); a JSON array would make every one of them undecodable, and the ordered list is fully expressed by the comma-joined string. So the correction to the supervisor's expectation: it IS an ordered list, but its JSON shape is a string, not an array; B should build against ParseRedaction, never against its own split. A fixture that carries a free-text field must list "free-text-v1" in that string.

2. EXEMPTION LIST. Exported from package acceptance: `acceptance.LegacyExemptCaptures() []acceptance.LegacyExemptCapture` (each entry: `Path string`, the committed repository-relative fixture path, and `Digest digest.Digest`, the sha256 of the committed bytes) and `acceptance.IsLegacyExemptCapture(path string, d digest.Digest) bool`, which requires BOTH the path (matched as a suffix of the resolved fixture path, so an archive copy of the repository resolves) and the digest to match one entry. Twelve entries after the supervisor's path ruling.

3. WITHHELD REASONS. Package activation: `activation.WithheldNoReachableTrigger` = 6 ("no-reachable-trigger"), `activation.WithheldUnclearablePayload` = 7 ("unclearable-payload"). Both answer `RequiresClearance() == true`; build such an entry with `activation.NewWithheldByDecision(event, reason, clearancePath)`, which validates the path with `acceptance.ValidateClearancePath`.

Also exported for B's corpus assertion: `acceptance.ValidateClearancePath(path string) error` (the same refusals a sidecar clearance meets).

I turned a semantic requirement into an encoding claim and passed it on as fact.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULING ON THE Receive-REFUSAL BLAST RADIUS, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

THE ENUMERATION-FIRST ORDER PAID FOR ITSELF. Side B was told to enumerate every Receive caller BEFORE writing the refusal, so that it learned the blast radius before it committed to it. It did, and the radius is real: TWO production callers (both able to carry a deadline — the native path already has one, the raw path gets the WorkflowResult tier) and TWENTY-ONE test calls across TEN files, most passing context.Background(). FOUR of those files sit outside side B's set. Had the refusal been written first, those four would have turned RED at the gate with no owner and no plan, and the cheapest repair under time pressure is the one the standing rules forbid: loosen the refusal until it asserts nothing.

RULED: SIDE B's SET WIDENS BY THE FOUR FILES, FOR THE Receive CONTEXT ARGUMENT ONLY.
- internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go
- internal/engine/budget/budget_test.go
- internal/engine/budget/abandonment_test.go
- cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_readback_production_test.go
NONE IS SIDE A's. Side A holds cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go, which is a DIFFERENT file from the readback production test; the sets stay disjoint. The widening is stated in the same commit that uses it.
THE EDIT IN EACH IS ONE LINE: give the Receive context a deadline. NO ASSERTION IN THOSE FILES CHANGES, no test is renamed, no expectation is relaxed. If any of the four needs more than a deadline to stay green, that is NOT a mechanical fix — STOP AND REPORT it, because it would mean the refusal has changed what that test proves.

THE REFUSAL KEEPS ITS OWN MUTATION, and this is what stops the four edits from becoming decoration: call Receive with context.Background() and show the refusal message; remove the refusal and show the in-flight test RED. Twenty-one callers passing a deadline proves nothing on its own — a deadline added mechanically to satisfy a compiler is not evidence that the refusal works.

THE HANDLER'S Diagnostics io.Writer MEMBER IS COVERED BY THE STDERR RULING. Side B read it correctly. The ruling was "one stderr line through the handler's diagnostic writer"; the seam that carries it is part of the ruling, not a new decision. internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go is already side B's.

SIDE B'S PROGRESS, VERIFIED AS REPORTED: the L4 wiring is committed at 3598965 with follow-up 11ce831, the L6 follow-up at 48c262e with the reader TIGHTENED TO SIDE A's PUBLISHED STRING SHAPE and the array shape RED, the two-list wording applied, and the template grant sentence pinned. The L10 registration pre-proof is posted with both mutations and their message text.
ONE ITEM IN 11ce831 IS WORTH RECORDING AS GOOD PRACTICE, because it is the standing rules working without being invoked: THE RACE GATE CAUGHT A LEAKED GOROUTINE in an in-process stalled-stdin proof, and side B REPLACED THAT PROOF WITH A BUILT-BINARY ONE rather than silencing it. That is both standing rules at once — race-instrument the outer process, and prove production behaviour through the real binary — and the worker applied them to its own new test without being told.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L11 s6k7mg: STOP AND REPORT on part 4 (eligibility), measured before any reclaim was written (worker-s1b). Parts 1 (v8 migration, commit ff428e1) and the enumerations are done; parts 4, 5 and 6 cannot be built as ruled without deleting live evidence on real stores.

THE FACT, measured at ff428e1 with grep over every non-test Go file:
- The only writer of lifecycle_occurrences is projection.RebuildOccurrences (internal/lifecycle/projection/rebuild.go:69-81): it DELETEs every row and re-INSERTs them from the journal's occurrence evidence.
- The only callers of that rebuild are the four READ-SIDE commands: hook lifecycle context, list, lineage and orphans (internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_{context,list,lineage,orphans}.go). The HOOK PATH, native and raw, never writes or rebuilds the projection: Receive appends to the journal and nothing else.
- Therefore lifecycle_occurrences on a live store reflects the last time a read command ran, or is EMPTY if none ever ran. The lead's own measurement of the user's store (14,490 blobs, 0 occurrence rows) is one such store; it is safe only because that store also has 0 journal rows.

THE CONSEQUENCE. The ruled eligibility, "no lifecycle_occurrences row names the digest AND written_at older than the tier", is evaluated on the hook path against a projection the hook path never maintains. On any store where the journal holds occurrences the projection does not yet reflect, a blob that a journal row NAMES reads as named by nothing, ages past 30 s, and is deleted. That is the corrupting state the blob-before-journal write order exists to prevent, and it is worse than corruption of one row: lifecycle_occurrences.payload_digest REFERENCES lifecycle_payload_blobs(digest), so the next rebuild of the projection fails on the foreign key and EVERY read-side command stops working for that store. The S0 count avoids this exactly by rebuilding first, on the read side, where the cost is acceptable; S0 kept the count OFF the hook path for that cost, and the same cost forbids a rebuild inside the reclaim.

I DO NOT CHOOSE. Options, with their costs, for the supervisor and the lead:
(a) Eligibility checked against the JOURNAL, not the projection: for each of the at most 64 candidate digests, ask whether any occurrence evidence carries body_digest equal to it. The journal exposes no lookup by body digest that I can find; the rebuild scans every occurrence row with a paged evidence query. Per invocation that is O(journal), which is the cost S0 refused on the hook path. The S3 spike (wivrye) is the place where the journal's reachable reads are being established; this may be a question for it.
(b) Maintain the projection on the WRITE path: after Append succeeds, Receive inserts the occurrence row itself (the rebuild stays as the repair path). Then "named by nothing in the projection" is true by construction for every occurrence the store committed. This is a design change to the shared write path and to the meaning of "disposable projection"; it is one INSERT per commit, inside the same invocation, and it also makes the S0 count correct without a rebuild. Blast radius: receipt/service.go (mine), the projection package's rebuild becomes idempotent over existing rows (not mine), every test that asserts the projection is empty before a rebuild.
(c) Gate eligibility on projection completeness: reclaim only when the projection's max journal_id equals the journal's current max occurrence journal id, else skip the reclaim for this invocation. Needs a cheap "journal head" read; S3's finding B18 adds a watermark for the assignment index, which is the same need. Cheap if the head read exists; the reclaim then simply does nothing on a stale projection, which is safe and honest, and the S0 count's rebuild makes it current.
(d) Keep the reclaim OFF the hook path and put it on the read side beside the count, where the rebuild already runs first (reviewer-a's fallback). The lead rejected this because it does not remove the in-flight race; with the written_at column and the WorkflowResult bound now available, the race IS removed on the read side too, so the rejection reason no longer holds as stated. Cost: no reclaim happens until an operator runs the command; the backlog is not drained by the hook.

My recommendation, stated so it can be overruled: (c) if a journal head read exists at v0.0.7, because it keeps every ruled mechanism and adds one comparison; otherwise (d), because it is the only option that is safe on every store without a design change to the write path. I will not implement (a) or (b) without a ruling; (a) violates the hook budget and (b) changes what the projection is.

WHAT CONTINUES MEANWHILE, inside my set and safe under every option: part 3(a) the raw path under the WorkflowResult tier with a fault on expiry; the pinned stderr line text and its test; the narrow delete interface's shape (unused until eligibility is ruled). Part 3(b), the Receive refusal, still waits on the six-file widening.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L11 PART 4 STOPPED BY SIDE B, AND THE STOP IS CORRECT, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. SURFACED TO THE TEAM LEAD; NOT DECIDED HERE, because it changes a mechanism the lead ruled.

THE DEFECT, measured by side B BEFORE any reclaim was written. lifecycle_occurrences is a PROJECTION. It is written ONLY by projection.RebuildOccurrences, which fully deletes and re-inserts from the journal, and that function is called ONLY by the four READ-SIDE commands (context, list, lineage, orphans). THE HOOK PATH NEVER MAINTAINS IT.
So the ruled eligibility predicate — "no lifecycle_occurrences row names the digest AND written_at older than the tier" — when evaluated ON THE HOOK PATH, reads a table that may be STALE OR NEVER BUILT. On any such store a blob that A JOURNAL ROW NAMES reads as NAMED BY NOTHING, and is deleted 30 s after it was written.
THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN LOSING A BLOB. It MANUFACTURES the journal-row-naming-an-absent-blob state that the write order exists to prevent, and because the projection table carries a FOREIGN KEY to the blob table, EVERY LATER REBUILD FAILS and ALL FOUR READ COMMANDS STOP WORKING for that store, permanently, until someone intervenes.
WHY IT DID NOT SHOW IN THE ACTIVATION MEASUREMENT: the lead's measured store has ZERO journal rows, so every blob there is a genuine orphan. THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIED THE LEAF IS THE ONE CASE THAT CANNOT EXPOSE THIS DEFECT. That is the standing lesson about measured cases in its sharpest form.

THIS IS THE STOP-AND-REPORT RULE WORKING EXACTLY AS WRITTEN. Side B was ordered to implement part 4 and it refused to write code that would delete live evidence, measured the reason, and reported instead of choosing. It also did the safe parts first.

THE FOUR OPTIONS SIDE B COSTED, with the supervisor's reading:
(a) a JOURNAL-SIDE check, O(journal) per hook invocation. REJECT on cost: an unbounded per-invocation read inside a 5 s budget, growing with the journal, is the shape this epic already refuses elsewhere.

(c) reclaim ONLY WHEN THE PROJECTION HEAD EQUALS THE JOURNAL HEAD, which needs a cheap journal-head read. Nothing is deleted on a stale store, by construction rather than by care.
(d) reclaim ON THE READ SIDE, beside the count, where the rebuild already runs and the projection is authoritative.

ONE OBSERVATION THE LEAD SHOULD HAVE BEFORE CHOOSING, BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT (d) IS. Option (d) IS NOT THE OPTION THAT WAS REJECTED. reviewer-a's "off the hook path" fallback was rejected on ONE stated ground: it does not remove the in-flight race, and only a timestamp plus a bounded window does. PART 1 OF THE LEAD'S OWN RULING ADDED THAT TIMESTAMP. written_at plus the tier removes the in-flight race WHEREVER the reclaim runs. So the premise of the rejection no longer holds, and (d) must be judged fresh rather than as a settled refusal. It also has a property (c) lacks: it runs the reclaim where the projection is AUTHORITATIVE, so the stale-projection question cannot arise at all.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TEAM-LEAD RE-RULING on S1-L11 (s6k7mg), 2026-09-05, answering side B's stop at part 4. THE STOP IS CORRECT and part 4 of my earlier ruling was WRONG: lifecycle_occurrences is a projection that only projection.RebuildOccurrences maintains, from the read-side commands; on the hook path it may be stale or empty, so "named by no occurrence" evaluated there can delete a blob a journal row names and manufacture the corrupt state the write order prevents. My activation measurement (0 journal rows) is the one store state that cannot show this. Recorded as my error.

DECISION: OPTION (d), the reclaim runs WHERE THE PROJECTION IS AUTHORITATIVE. (a) is rejected on cost (an unbounded journal read inside a 5 s budget). (b) is rejected as a design change (a second writer of the projection on the live path). (c) is rejected because at the reclaim point on the hook path the journal head is always ahead of the projection by the invocation's own append, so the predicate would almost never be true and the mechanism would be a false promise. (d) is NOT the fallback I rejected earlier: that rejection rested on the missing timestamp, and part 1 of the ruling added it. With written_at and a bounded writer window, the in-flight race is closed wherever the reclaim runs.

THE MECHANISM, replacing parts 4 and 5 of the earlier ruling. Parts 1, 2, 3 and 6 STAND (migration v8 written_at; the stamp and the narrow write and delete interfaces; the WorkflowResult-tier bound made true by the raw-path deadline and the Receive refusal; the budget proof).
4'. WHERE: inside projection.RebuildOccurrences, in the SAME write transaction, AFTER the projection rows are re-inserted, wrapped in a SAVEPOINT so a reclaim error is rolled back alone and the rebuild still commits. The four read-side commands reach it through the one existing call in internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go; no new command; no new call site.
5'. THE AGE REFERENCE INSTANT IS THE JOURNAL SNAPSHOT INSTANT, captured before the evidence read begins, NOT the delete instant. Eligible = no row of the freshly rebuilt projection names the digest AND written_at < snapshot_instant minus the WorkflowResult tier. Why the snapshot instant: a journal row committed after the snapshot is not in the projection, but its blob was written no earlier than that commit minus the writer's bounded window, so it is younger than the tier relative to the snapshot and cannot be selected; a row committed at or before the snapshot is in the projection. Both halves are needed and both are pinned.
6'. CAP: 1024 per rebuild, oldest first, one statement. The reclaim is not under the hook tier, so the leaf's example cap of 64 (sized for the hook path) does not apply; 1024 bounds a read command's added latency and drains the user's 14,490 legacy orphans in about 15 read commands. State the constant with this reason beside it.
7'. THE HOOK PATH CHANGES BY NO BYTE. The handler statement of the earlier part 5 is WITHDRAWN; internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go is NOT touched by L11. The raw path does not reclaim. The reach guard: the reclaim is an unexported function of the projection package called exactly once, from the rebuild; the guard states what it reads. Mutation: call it from the hook handler in a throwaway copy and show the guard RED.
8'. FAILURE TEXT: a reclaim error inside the savepoint writes ONE stderr line through the read command's diagnostic writer (the supervisor's pin ruling stands) and the read command completes.

MUTATIONS REQUIRED, each RED then GREEN, message text quoted: (i) STALE PROJECTION: with the projection empty or behind the journal, run the reclaim OUTSIDE the rebuild transaction (or before the re-insert) and show a journal-named blob is deleted and the assertion is RED naming the digest; with the mechanism in place it is never deleted. (ii) SNAPSHOT INSTANT: age the blobs against the delete instant instead of the snapshot instant, with a row committed after the snapshot and a slow rebuild simulated by the clock seam, and show RED. (iii) the leaf's own five: age bound removed, cap removed, named-by-nothing removed, reach from the hook path, budget. (iv) the Receive refusal and the raw deadline mutations from part 3.

FILES: side B's L11 set changes to: internal/lifecycle/projection/rebuild.go and its test subject; a new internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim.go and reclaim_test.go (replacing the planned internal/tasks/lifecycle_reclaim.go, which is no longer created); internal/audit/migrate_v7_v8.go and the migration test subject; internal/audit/migrate.go; internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go, the blob store file and their tests; cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_raw.go and its test subject; the six foreign test files for the Receive deadline argument only. internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go LEAVES the set. None of these is side A's.

LESSON, added to the standing constraints for the rest of the epic: WHEN A MEASUREMENT JUSTIFIES A MECHANISM, NAME THE STATES THAT MEASUREMENT CANNOT SHOW before ruling on the mechanism.

(b) A capture failure NEVER changes the host outcome. TestACaptureFailureNeverChangesTheHostOutcomeOnAnEnabledEvent, built binary, enabled Claude SessionStart, three runs: no capture; an accepted directory; an unwritable directory (chmod 0500). author: David Huu Pham
text:
TRIAL FOLD RUN EARLY, AND IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

WHY IT WAS RUN BEFORE SIDE B FINISHED: side A is complete and it touched EVERY GENERATED ARTEFACT, so the FOLD's authoritative regeneration is the real test of that work, not side A's own drift-0 result on its own branch. An integration failure is cheapest when it is found before the last leaf lands, not after. Side B's L11 is blocked on a design decision, so the fold cost nothing in schedule.

THE FOLD ITSELF: integration worktree pasture/worktree/rp2tju-s1--integration on branch slice/rp2tju-s1, created from side A's head 45666f3. ALL NINE of side B's commits cherry-picked IN ORDER WITH ZERO CONFLICTS: 30ee142, 360ae53, eadacec, 90dbfff, 41ed546, 3598965, 11ce831, 48c262e, ff428e1. Integration head dc6df68.
THE DISJOINT SPLIT HELD MECHANICALLY, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE SPLIT. Nine cherry-picks across two sides that between them touched the acceptance package, the whole activation package, codegen, every generated artefact, the runtime profiles, ingress, handlers, the waist guard, audit and the cmd layer, and NOT ONE CONFLICT. A conflict here would have meant the split was broken; there was none to resolve.

SIX GATES ON AN ARCHIVE COPY OF dc6df68, from inside the copy. FIVE GREEN, ONE RED.
- build: rc=0. vet: rc=0.
- make generate: rc=0, 172 log lines, DRIFT 0. The authoritative regeneration over BOTH sides is CLEAN, which is the result side A's generated-artefact ownership was designed to produce.
- nix flake check: rc=0.
- gofmt: 0 files, and the negative control listed the planted probe, so the gate demonstrably ran.
- go test -race: ok=73 packages, RACES 0, FAIL 3 lines resolving to ONE failing test.

THE FAILURE, and it is a genuine integration defect that NEITHER SIDE'S OWN GATE HAD REPORTED:
TestLifecycleListStandardExitCategories/storage, at cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go:771 — "An error is expected but got nil."
THE MECHANISM: that case simulates a store written by a FUTURE version of the product. It does so by writing the literal SCHEMA VERSION 8 into audit_schema_meta and expecting the binary to refuse with the storage exit category. SIDE B's L11 MIGRATION RAISES MaxKnownSchemaVersion TO 8. So version 8 is no longer a future version; the binary now KNOWS it, opens the store happily, exits 0, and the assertion that an error was expected fails.
NOTHING IS WRONG WITH EITHER CHANGE. The test was true when it was written and the migration is correct. The test encodes a FACT ABOUT THE PRODUCT — "8 is beyond what this binary understands" — AS A LITERAL, and the migration made that fact false.

WHY THIS IS A CROSS-SIDE PROBLEM AND NOT SIMPLY SIDE B's BUG: the DEFECT SITE is side B's migration; the FIX SITE is a file SIDE A OWNS. Side B may not edit side A's file under the split, and side A is complete. Side B's own archive gate on ff428e1 was still pending, so it had not yet met this; it would have.

RULED: SIDE B FIXES IT, IN THE COMMIT THAT CARRIES THE MIGRATION, and its set widens by cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go FOR THIS ONE TEST CASE ONLY. THE REASON: a migration that moves the schema ceiling MUST carry the guards that track the ceiling; splitting them leaves a red branch owned by nobody. Side A is complete and its branch is frozen, so no write race exists. Name the widening in the ownership paragraph and state that it is the storage case of this one test.

AND FIX IT BY DERIVATION, NOT BY BUMPING THE LITERAL. Writing 9 in place of 8 restores the green and REBUILDS THE SAME TRAP for the next migration — and S3's index migration IS v9, so the trap would spring again within this epic. DERIVE the future version from audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion + 1, so the case stays true for every later migration WITHOUT A TEST EDIT. This is the standing coverage rule applied to a constant: a test that hardcodes a value the product owns makes a claim that the product can falsify silently.
MUTATION REQUIRED: raise MaxKnownSchemaVersion by one and show the case STILL PASSES; pin the derivation by replacing it with a literal and showing the case fails the next time the ceiling moves.
SWEEP THE CLASS, do not stop at the one the gate happened to report: find every other test that hardcodes a schema version or any other product-owned ceiling, and report what you find even if you do not change it.
