author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULINGS, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05: the Put seam widening, the parser fold item, and the schema-literal routing.

1. THE Put SEAM: THE WIDENING EXTENDS, ON THE SAME TERMS. Side B's set covers the Put ARGUMENT as well as the Receive CONTEXT argument, in internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go, internal/engine/budget/budget_test.go (two fakes), internal/lifecycle/projection/persisted_v1_test.go and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans_test.go. ONE MECHANICAL LINE EACH, NO ASSERTION CHANGED, NO TEST RENAMED, and a STOP-AND-REPORT if any needs more than the argument — because that would mean the seam change altered what that test proves.
NONE IS SIDE A's. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans_test.go is a DIFFERENT FILE from cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go, which is side A's. The sets stay disjoint. Name all of them in the ownership paragraph.
THE REASONING IS THE SAME ONE AS THE CONTEXT ARGUMENT and it transfers exactly: the alternative is a red branch owned by nobody, and the cheapest repair under time pressure is the one the standing rules forbid.

BUT ONE DESIGN CHECK COMES WITH IT, BECAUSE THE RIPPLE IS EVIDENCE. THREE FOREIGN FAKES IMPLEMENT THE BLOB STORE. If a signature change forces edits in three fakes and two callers, ASK WHETHER THE INTERFACE THE PRODUCTION CODE DEPENDS ON IS ACTUALLY NARROW. The ruling's own words are a NARROW WRITE interface and a SEPARATE NARROW DELETE interface that ONLY THE RECLAIM CONSTRUCTS. If the reclaim and the writer each depend on the SMALLEST interface they need, a fake for one of them does not have to satisfy the other, and the ripple shrinks by construction rather than by permission. STATE IN THE REPORT what each new interface declares and which callers depend on which. If the ripple is unavoidable after that, it is unavoidable and the widening covers it; if the split removes some of it, that is the split doing its job.

2. THE PARSER IS A NAMED FOLD OBLIGATION, NOT A LOOSE END. Side B correctly reports that acceptance.ParseRedaction exists ONLY on side A's branch, so side B cannot call it without failing to compile, and its reader parses the string itself until the fold. THAT IS CORRECT AND IT IS NOT A SECOND PARSER BY CHOICE — it is a second parser by BRANCH TOPOLOGY, which is a different thing and must not be allowed to become the first by default.
RECORDED AS FOLD OBLIGATION F-1: AT THE FOLD, SIDE B's LOCAL PARSING IS REPLACED BY A CALL TO acceptance.ParseRedaction, IN ONE COMMIT ON THE INTEGRATION BRANCH, and the three ruled mutations (unknown rule, duplicate rule, "none" beside an applied rule) are re-run against the SHARED parser. The supervisor checks this at the fold; it does not depend on anyone remembering it. Two parsers for one wire format is a divergence no test on either branch can see, and this value is integration point I5, consumed by S2, S4, S5 and S6.

3. THE SCHEMA LITERAL IS ROUTED TO SIDE A by the team lead: worker-s1a makes a ONE-LINE SIXTH COMMIT deriving the future version from audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion + 1 in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go, with the mutation (use the constant ITSELF and show RED) and an ownership paragraph. It stays 8 on side A's branch and BECOMES 9 AT THE FOLD, which is exactly the property that makes the derivation right rather than a bump. SIDE B TAKES NO ACTION on it; the one RED test in side B's ff428e1 gate is fully explained by this and is not a side-B defect.
S3's index migration is v9, so a literal bump would have sprung the same trap inside this epic. The derivation removes the trap for every later migration WITHOUT A TEST EDIT.

4. L11 RE-RULED BY THE LEAD AS OPTION (d), and side B's stop was correct: part 4 of the original ruling was wrong. The reclaim moves INSIDE projection.RebuildOccurrences, in the SAME write transaction after the re-insert, under a SAVEPOINT so a reclaim error rolls back alone while the rebuild commits. THE HOOK PATH CHANGES BY NO BYTE and internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go LEAVES side B's set. internal/tasks/lifecycle_reclaim.go is NO LONGER CREATED. Parts 1, 2, 3 and 6 stand.
THE STANDING CONSTRAINT THE LEAD ADDED FROM THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING TO COME OUT OF IT: WHEN A MEASUREMENT JUSTIFIES A MECHANISM, NAME THE STATES THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT SHOW BEFORE RULING. The store that justified this leaf had ZERO journal rows, which is the one state in which the defect is invisible.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TWO SUPERSESSIONS, supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Both correct rulings I recorded earlier on this task. I name them rather than let a reviewer meet two contradictory texts.

SUPERSESSION 1 — THE SCHEMA LITERAL. My 01:44 ruling said "SIDE B FIXES IT, IN THE COMMIT THAT CARRIES THE MIGRATION, and its set widens by cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go for this one test case". THAT IS OVERRULED. SIDE A FIXES IT, in a one-line SIXTH commit in its own file.
THE LEAD'S REASON IS BETTER THAN MINE AND IT IS THE RULE THIS WHOLE SLICE RESTS ON: TWO WRITERS ON ONE FILE ACROSS THE SPLIT IS THE COLLISION THE SPLIT EXISTS TO PREVENT. I reasoned that the guard should travel with the ceiling that broke it, which is sound in isolation; but side A's branch is not frozen until its last commit lands, so my routing would have put both workers on one file at the same time — and I had ALREADY relayed the order to side A at 01:45 on the lead's earlier routing, so my own recorded ruling contradicted what I had sent. THE DERIVATION SATISFIES MY REASON ANYWAY, WITHOUT THE COLLISION: the guard reads audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion, so it TRAVELS WITH THE CEILING BECAUSE IT READS THE CEILING. It evaluates to 8 on side A's branch and becomes 9 at the fold with no edit.
WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the refusal of the 8-to-9 bump, and the mutation (use the constant ITSELF, not plus one, and show RED). The ceiling sweep is added to side A's order, reporting hits outside its own file WITHOUT editing them.
SIDE B TAKES NO ACTION and MUST NOT TOUCH cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go. The single RED test in side B's ff428e1 gate is EXPLAINED by this and is recorded as explained, not as an open failure.

SUPERSESSION 2 — THE Put SEAM. My 01:45 ruling extended side B's widening to the Put ARGUMENT across five foreign lines. THAT IS SUPERSEDED BY A BETTER SHAPE: RESHAPE, NOT WIDEN. The Put SIGNATURE STAYS. The blob store STAMPS written_at FROM A CLOCK IT HOLDS — the wall clock by default, with the scripted clock injected through a constructor option in side B's own file. NO FOREIGN LINES ARE TOUCHED FOR PART 2 AT ALL.
THIS IS THE OUTCOME THE DESIGN CHECK WAS ASKING FOR, AND IT IS WHY THE CHECK WAS ATTACHED. I granted the widening but required side B to state what each new interface declares and which caller depends on which, on the ground that A RIPPLE THROUGH THREE FOREIGN FAKES IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE INTERFACE, NOT MERELY A COST TO BE AUTHORISED. The answer turned out to be that the ripple was avoidable entirely. A permission slip would have bought a green branch and left a wide seam; the question bought a narrow one and five untouched files.
THE MUTATION STANDS: remove the stamp and show the age test RED.

STATE AFTER BOTH: side A owes ONE more commit (the derived literal, plus the sweep report), then it stands down; any later side-A fix goes to a FRESH worker. Side B owes L11 parts 2 (reshaped), 3b and 6, and the option-(d) projection reclaim. Side B's set does NOT grow for part 2.

FOLD PROCEDURE AGREED WITH THE LEAD: when side A's sixth SHA is reported and gated, the integration branch is RE-CREATED FROM SIDE A's NEW HEAD, side B's commits are cherry-picked in order again, and the six gates re-run on a fresh archive copy. dc6df68 STAYS RECORDED AS THE TRIAL FOLD WITH ITS RESULT — it is the evidence that the split held mechanically and that the authoritative regeneration came back drift 0, and a later fold does not erase what an earlier one proved.
FOLD OBLIGATION F-1 STILL STANDS: at the fold, side B's local redaction parsing is replaced by a call to acceptance.ParseRedaction in one commit, and the three ruled mutations are re-run against the shared parser.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L11 s6k7mg: ACK of the option-(d) re-ruling, and TWO SEAMS THAT EXCEED THE RULED WIDENING, reported before I build on them (worker-s1b). Gate on 0a4b7ff (part 3a): 72 packages green, 0 races, RED only on side A's schema literal as already reported.

SEAM 1, part 3(b), the Receive refusal. "A deadline later than now plus the WorkflowResult tier" needs the tier on receipt.Service; the service has no profile today (only the appender's Ingress deadline). I add `Window time.Duration` set by tasks.NewLifecycleReceiptServiceWithProfile from profile.WorkflowResult(), refused when zero (the same rule the appender applies to a zero Deadline; a silent zero would disable the bound). CONSEQUENCE: every test that builds a Service LITERAL must set it. In my set: the receipt tests (5 files). Foreign: internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go:111 builds a literal, so it needs TWO one-line edits (the context deadline AND `Window: time.Second`), which is "more than a deadline". Per your instruction I stop on that file and ask: extend the widening to that one field, or rule a shape without it. budget_test.go, abandonment_test.go and the readback test build their service through the constructor, so the context line alone suffices there.

SEAM 2, part 8', the stderr line. The four read-side handlers (list, context, lineage, orphans) take `(ctx, out io.Writer, in, format)` and the four cmd files pass cmd.OutOrStdout(); NONE carries a diagnostic writer, and tasks.RebuildLifecycleOccurrences(ctx, tracker) carries none either. "One stderr line through the read command's diagnostic writer" therefore needs: a `Diagnostics io.Writer` member on the four handler input structs, four one-line edits in cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_{list,context,lineage,orphans}.go passing cmd.ErrOrStderr(), and tasks.RebuildLifecycleOccurrences gaining the writer (and the clock and the tier) to hand to the projection. Nine files outside my L11 set. I DO NOT EDIT THEM. Ask: widen for exactly that field and line each, or rule an interim.

WHAT I BUILD NOW, all inside my L11 set and correct under either answer: internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim.go (the unexported reclaim: eligible = unnamed in the fresh projection AND written_at < snapshot instant minus the window; oldest first; cap 1024 with its reason; SAVEPOINT; one diagnostic line on failure through the writer it is given); rebuild.go gains RebuildOptions{Clock, Window, Diagnostics}, all REQUIRED, and a reclaiming rebuild entry that captures the snapshot instant BEFORE the evidence read; the plain RebuildOccurrences(ctx, journal, db) keeps its shape and behaviour so the four callers stay byte-identical until the writer is threaded; receipt/journal.go gains the narrow delete type that only the reclaim constructs, executing inside the rebuild's transaction. Tests in projection/reclaim_test.go with the ruled mutations. The Put stamp (part 2) and the Receive refusal (3b) wait on seam 1 and the Put-argument extension.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SCHEMA-CEILING SWEEP (worker-s1a, team-lead addendum). COMMIT 73ea25b on slice/rp2tju-s1-a, an EMPTY commit that names f7556a7 (history is not rewritten; a later commit names the earlier one). Porcelain EMPTY. Six-gate archive run on 73ea25b in progress; result follows here.
SWEPT: every *_test.go in the repository (legacy/ excluded) for a literal that encodes the audit schema ceiling: audit_schema_meta writes with a numeric version, comparisons against 7/8/9, "newer than known" written as a number.
FIXED (files this side owns): cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go:766, the only hit, already derived in f7556a7 as audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion+1 (8 on this branch, 9 at the fold without an edit). A bump to 9 was refused: S3's index migration is v9 and would spring the same trap. Mutation: the known version instead of the newer one -> TestLifecycleListStandardExitCategories/storage RED "An error is expected but got nil".
REPORTED, NOT EDITED (files this side does not own):
- internal/audit/migrate_v6_v7_test.go:187 TestCurrentV7DatabaseIsIdempotentAndCascades seeds VALUES(7,1) as "the current database" and runs Migrate. The literal encodes the ceiling by intent: once side B's v8 step exists, the case migrates a v7 store instead of proving the current store is idempotent. Whether it still passes at the fold depends on the v8 step; either way its claim changes silently. Owner: side B's schema work (s6k7mg) or the audit package owner.
- internal/audit/migrate_test.go:255 TestMigrate_NewerSchema_RejectedWithStructuredError seeds version 99 as a future version; its assertions read the constant, so it stays true until a ninety-ninth migration. Low risk; same class.
NOT HITS, listed so the sweep can be checked: the seeds of versions 4, 5 and 6 (internal/audit/migrate_v4_v5_test.go:58; migrate_v5_v6_test.go:16,40; migrate_v6_v7_test.go:19,155) are the INPUT versions of the migration steps under test; the floor assertions MaxKnownSchemaVersion >= 4 (migrate_v2_v3_test.go:764; migrate_v3_backfill_test.go:252) are floors; "--schema-version claude-code/9.9.9" (cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_raw_test.go:332) is a host-contract version, not the audit schema; every other reference reads audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion. Two comments in internal/audit/migrate_test.go (lines 236, 239) describe the ceiling as 2 or 4: prose, stale, not literals.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FINDING RAISED BY THE SUPERVISOR AT VERIFICATION, plus one withdrawal. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

FINDING S-1, MINOR BUT IN THE ONE CLASS THIS EPIC HAS A STANDING RULE FOR: AN INTERNAL PROCESS REFERENCE REACHED A SHIPPED FILE AND A COMMIT MESSAGE.
Side A's commit f7556a7 adds this comment to cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go, which is a SHIPPED FILE:
  "a later schema version lands on another branch of this slice, and a hard-coded literal would become a known version at the fold and stop proving the refusal"
and its commit message repeats "on another branch of this slice, so at the fold 8 becomes a known version".
"THIS SLICE", "ANOTHER BRANCH OF THIS SLICE" AND "THE FOLD" ARE PROCESS ARTEFACTS OF THIS TEAM. They are exactly what the standing rule excludes from shipped code, generated artefacts, help text and commit messages, alongside tracker ids and proposal names. A reader of this repository in six months has NO WAY to resolve them: there is no slice, no fold and no other branch in the tree they can see. The comment's ENGINEERING CONTENT is correct and worth keeping; only the process words must go.
WHY IT IS WORTH RAISING AND NOT WAIVING: the rule exists because these references are invisible to the person who writes them — they are the author's true, present context. This is the SECOND instance in this slice, after the persisted tracker id in the capture sidecars, and the two have the same shape in different media: DATA in the first case, PROSE in this one. A sweep for tracker ids would not have found either.
THE FIX: restate the comment in terms a repository reader can check, naming the MECHANISM and not the process. The fact is simply that the audit schema ceiling MOVES, so a literal that encodes "newer than known" stops being newer the moment the ceiling passes it; the derivation from audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion+1 is what keeps the case true. No process word is needed to say that.
THE COMMIT MESSAGE IS NOT AMENDED. Shared history is not rewritten in this epic, and reviewers cite SHAs. THE SUPERSEDED CLAIM IS CORRECTED BY A LATER COMMIT THAT NAMES f7556a7, which is the standing rule for exactly this case.

OBSERVATION ON 73ea25b, NOT A FINDING: side A recorded the ceiling sweep as a commit that CHANGES NO FILE. The CONTENT IS EXCELLENT — it separates true hits from look-alikes (the input versions of migration steps, the floor assertions, and a host-contract version that is not an audit schema version at all), and it names the two hits in files side A does not own WITHOUT EDITING THEM, which is the reporting rule working. An ownership paragraph is vacuous on an empty commit, so nothing is verified there; the sweep is accepted on its content and is recorded here so it also lives on the durable channel.

WITHDRAWAL, as directed by the team lead and recorded naming both texts: MY 01:45 GRANT OF THE Put WIDENING IS WITHDRAWN. Part 2 is RESHAPED, NOT WIDENED: the Put SIGNATURE STAYS, and the blob store stamps written_at from a CLOCK IT HOLDS — the wall clock by default, with the scripted clock injected through a CONSTRUCTOR OPTION in side B's own file. internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go, internal/engine/budget/budget_test.go, internal/lifecycle/projection/persisted_v1_test.go and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans_test.go ARE NOT TOUCHED FOR PART 2.
THE SIX-FILE WIDENING FOR THE Receive DEADLINE ARGUMENT (part 3b) STANDS; only the Put half is withdrawn.
THE DESIGN CHECK STAYS AND IS NOW THE POINT: side B states what the NARROW WRITE interface and the NARROW DELETE interface each declare and which caller depends on which. With the signature unchanged the fakes need NO EDIT AT ALL, which is THE RIPPLE SHRINKING BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by permission — the outcome the check was asking for.

SIDE A's SIXTH COMMIT IS VERIFIED IN THE TREE: f7556a7, ONE file, the literal replaced by audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion+1, ownership paragraph present, porcelain empty, six gates green on an archive copy (73 packages, 0 races, drift 0), and the mutation RED by name — writing the constant ITSELF gives "An error is expected but got nil". The derivation is correct and it is the property that matters: 8 on side A's branch, 9 at the fold, with no edit.

text:
RECOMMENDATION AGAINST AN EDIT, AND A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE INTERNAL-REFERENCE CLASS. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Measured on the integration head before any work was ordered.

1. THE ROUTED EDIT TO internal/audit/migrate_v6_v7_test.go IS NOT NEEDED, AND I RECOMMEND NOT DOING IT. The team lead routed side A's sweep hit to side B: seed from audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion, re-describe the test, mutate by seeding the constant minus one. I measured the tree first and the ground has already moved twice.
- SIDE B ALREADY DISCHARGED THE HONESTY HALF, unprompted, inside ff428e1: TestCurrentV7DatabaseIsIdempotentAndCascades became TestV7DatabaseIsPromotedAndStillCascades. THE RENAMED TEST IS STABLE AT EVERY FUTURE CEILING. "A v7 database is promoted and still cascades" is true at v8, at v9 and at v99. The literal 7 is no longer a ceiling encoded as a number; it is the INPUT VERSION of a migration path, which side A's own sweep correctly classified as NOT a hit elsewhere in the same package.
- THE PROPERTY THE OLD NAME CLAIMED IS ALREADY COVERED, AND ALREADY DERIVED. TestMigrateV2toV3_Idempotent_ReRunNoop in internal/audit/migrate_v2_v3_test.go asserts that a second Migrate on an ALREADY-CURRENT database changes nothing, and it reads audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion FROM THE CONSTANT rather than a literal. That is exactly the test the routing would create.
SO THE ROUTED EDIT WOULD ADD A THIRD TEST DUPLICATING AN EXISTING DERIVED ONE, AND WOULD DESTROY A USEFUL v7-SPECIFIC PROMOTION TEST TO DO IT. Two properties are currently covered by two tests: "an old v7 store is promoted and its cascades survive" and "the current store is idempotent under a re-run". Merging them loses the first. RECOMMENDATION: NO EDIT; record the hit as DISCHARGED by ff428e1 plus the existing derived idempotency test. The team lead decides.

2. FINDING S-2, AND IT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS IN THIS SLICE: internal/audit CARRIES PROCESS REFERENCES IN SHIPPED TEST FILES, INCLUDING IN FAILURE TEXT A PERSON READS.
- migrate_v2_v3_test.go:690 "currently v4 after S4" — this is BOTH a process reference AND A FALSE COUNT: MaxKnownSchemaVersion is 8.
- migrate_v2_v3_test.go:765 error text "want >= 4 (S4 must bump to 4 or higher)" — a process reference INSIDE A FAILURE MESSAGE, which is operator-facing text by the standing rule.
- migrate_test.go:76 "once S4 lands"; :185 "S4 must migrate epoch_id"; :189 "S3 backfill"; :199 "the contract S5 (OpenTaskTracker)".
- c4_provenance_unmodified_test.go:19 "the first S1 commit on this implementation epoch".
THESE ARE PRE-EXISTING AND NOT CAUSED BY S1. They come from an earlier epoch whose slice numbers are unrelated to this one's, which makes them WORSE THAN MEANINGLESS TO A READER TODAY: "S4" here does not mean this epic's S4, so a reader who resolves it resolves it WRONGLY.
THEY ARE ALREADY FILED: pasture #140 is the process-reference sweep (409 lines across 81 files, to be retired behind a shrinking baseline). THESE HITS BELONG TO #140 AND NOT TO S1. S1 DOES NOT GROW TO SWALLOW THEM — that is the same routing call made for the hand-listed inventory guard, which went to S2-L7.
WHAT S1 DOES OWE: the two instances S1 ITSELF CREATED are fixed inside S1 — the persisted tracker id in the capture sidecars (done, side A) and the process words in the f7556a7 comment (finding S-1, routed to a fresh side-A worker). A slice cleans up what it wrote; it does not adopt the whole backlog.

WHY THIS KEEPS APPEARING, and it is worth stating once: THREE INSTANCES IN ONE SLICE, IN THREE DIFFERENT MEDIA — persisted DATA in a sidecar, a source COMMENT, and a test FAILURE MESSAGE. No single sweep finds all three, and each was invisible to its author because a process reference is the author's true, present context. Only a reader without that context can see it resolves to nothing.

No tasks/lifecycle_reclaim.go. internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go untouched.

MECHANISM. projection.RebuildOccurrencesReclaiming(ctx, journal, db, RebuildOptions{Clock, Window, Diagnostics}) = the existing rebuild plus the reclaim, inside the same write transaction, after the re-insert, under SAVEPOINT reclaim_orphans. The plain RebuildOccurrences the four read commands call is UNCHANGED and reclaims nothing (pinned). Snapshot instant = Clock.Now() taken BEFORE the evidence read. Eligible = no row of the fresh projection names the digest AND written_at < snapshot minus Window. Oldest first, at most ReclaimCap = 1024 (constant, reason beside it). Options all required; a zero window and a missing stream are refused with their reasons. A reclaim failure rolls back the reclaim alone, the rebuild commits, and ONE line goes to the Diagnostics stream: `pasture: the orphan payload reclaim inside the projection rebuild failed: <cause>; this happened in the projection rebuild (internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim.go) after the projection rows were rebuilt; the rebuild still completed and nothing was deleted; the orphan payload blobs stay where they were, and the next read command retries the reclaim` (pinned). receipt.PayloadReclaimer is the only delete door, runs only inside a transaction it is handed, and is constructed only by the reclaim.

TESTS (projection/reclaim_test.go, real store, real journal): unnamed-older reclaimed / unnamed-inside-window kept / named kept at any age / legacy-0 named kept / legacy-0 unnamed reclaimed, oldest first; the plain rebuild reclaims nothing; snapshot-instant proof with a journal wrapper that ADVANCES the clock on the evidence read (a slow read), the in-flight blob kept; cap pinned at 1024 and exactly the cap reclaimed of 1030, the six youngest wait for the next rebuild; a never-rebuilt projection with a journal-named blob written 1000 s ago keeps it; a reclaim made to fail (written_at column renamed away) leaves the rebuild complete with one pinned line and nothing deleted; option refusals; the reach guard over every non-test source of the module (exactly one reclaim call from rebuildOccurrences; exactly one PayloadReclaimer construction in reclaim.go; ZERO production callers of the reclaiming entry today, stated, because the read commands keep the plain rebuild until their diagnostic stream is threaded).

MUTATIONS, each RED then restored green:
(i) stale projection, reclaim moved before the delete/re-insert: TestStaleProjectionNeverLosesAJournalNamedBlob RED, `the reclaiming rebuild must complete` (the journal-named blob was deleted and the re-insert failed on the foreign key).
(ii) snapshot at the delete instead of before the read, with the slow-read clock: RED, `a blob younger than the window relative to the SNAPSHOT instant must be kept (sha256:43af9787...); ageing it against the delete instant reclaims an in-flight blob`. (A first shape of this test could not see the mutation because both versions read the clock once; the seam now advances on the journal READ, which is the fact that distinguishes them.)
(iii) age bound removed (before = far future): the same in-flight blob reclaimed, RED on two tests.
(iv-a) cap constant raised to 1<<20: RED on the pin `the cap sizes a read command's added latency and drains the measured legacy backlog in about fifteen commands`. (iv-b) the SQL LIMIT dropped: RED `exactly the cap is reclaimed in one rebuild` (all 1030 gone). (My first cap test derived its counts from the constant and stayed green under iv-a; it now pins the value.)
(v) named-by-nothing removed from the delete: RED on two tests, `Received unexpected error` — the FOREIGN KEY refused the delete of a named blob, so the reclaim reported a failure; the FK is the second enforcer reviewer-b predicted.
(vi) receipt.PayloadReclaimer constructed in handlers.hookLifecycle on a throwaway copy: the reach guard RED, `the narrow delete type is constructed only by the reclaim; a construction anywhere else is a second delete door`.
(vii) budget: the cap test waits on nothing but the two rebuilds.

STILL WAITING on the seams posted at 01:5x: part 2 (Put with the written-at value: five foreign Put lines), part 3(b) (Window on Service: backend_test.go needs two lines), and part 8' emission (Diagnostics threaded through tasks.RebuildLifecycleOccurrences, four handler inputs and four cmd files). The reclaiming entry is complete and tested but unreachable from a command until the third is ruled; the reach guard states that count and refuses a hook-path caller.

text:
L11 s6k7mg PARTS 2 (RESHAPED) AND 6 DONE (worker-s1b). Commit 13efa73. Porcelain empty. Five gates running on an archive copy of 13efa73; result posted when it lands.

ACK, listed back: (1) the schema literal is side A's (f7556a7, then a84e6c1); I take no action and do not touch cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go. (2) The Put widening is WITHDRAWN; part 2 is reshaped; no foreign line changes for part 2. (3) The six-file widening for the Receive deadline ARGUMENT stands. (4) The migrate_v6_v7_test.go seed edit is CANCELLED; the discharge is stated below and I do not edit that file again. (5) Finding S-1 is side A's and is fixed at a84e6c1; finding S-2 is routed to pasture #133; nothing for side B. (6) Fold obligation F-1 stands (acceptance.ParseRedaction at the fold, three mutations re-run).

GATE ON 1e61991 (option-(d) reclaim): build, vet, flake and gofmt green; test-race RED on exactly ONE test, side A's TestLifecycleListStandardExitCategories/storage at cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go:771 ("An error is expected but got nil"), the VALUES(8,1) literal that f7556a7 derives from the ceiling. Recorded as explained, not as an open failure.

DISCHARGE OF SWEEP HIT 1, stated per the ruling: ff428e1 renamed TestCurrentV7DatabaseIsIdempotentAndCascades to TestV7DatabaseIsPromotedAndStillCascades, a claim true at every future ceiling; the idempotency property is held by TestMigrateV2toV3_Idempotent_ReRunNoop, which reads audit.MaxKnownSchemaVersion. No further edit.

PART 2, WHAT (internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go): SQLiteBlobStore holds an unexported clock. Put writes written_at = clock instant in unix ns. With no clock (the production literal SQLiteBlobStore{DB: db} in tasks, unchanged) it stamps the WALL clock; a scripted clock enters only through NewSQLiteBlobStore(db, WithPayloadClock(clock)), both in my file. The Put signature is unchanged, so the three fakes and the two literal callers outside my set are untouched.

FINDING, MINE, THE STATE THE AGE BOUND DID NOT COVER (named per the standing lesson): the old INSERT was ON CONFLICT(digest) DO NOTHING. A writer re-delivering a body whose digest an OLD ORPHAN already carries would leave written_at at the orphan's instant, so a read command between that writer's Put and its append would see an unnamed blob older than the window and DELETE it; the append would then name an absent blob, the corruption the write order exists to prevent. FIX in the same commit: ON CONFLICT(digest) DO UPDATE SET written_at = max(stored, new): the stamp follows the latest Put and never moves back. Pinned by two tests (below), mutation M2.

THE TWO NARROW DOORS, as the design check asked: the WRITE door is the BlobStore interface, declaring exactly Put(ctx, digest, body); its only caller is receipt.Service.Receive, which depends on nothing else of the store, so a fake that records the call satisfies it. The concrete SQLiteBlobStore carries Put plus read-only inspection (Exists, Reclaimable, ReclaimableCount) and NO delete. The DELETE door is receipt.PayloadReclaimer{Tx}, declaring exactly ReclaimOrphansWrittenBefore(ctx, before, limit); its only constructor is projection.reclaimOrphanPayloads inside the rebuild transaction (the reach guard from 1e61991 pins that). TestTheWriteDoorAndTheDeleteDoorStayNarrow pins all three method sets by reflection and that the delete door does not implement the write door.

PART 6, THE BUDGET PROOF under option (d): the "invocation" is a read command and its budget is the CAP, not a tier. Behavioural half (already in 1e61991): with 1030 orphans one rebuild reclaims exactly 1024 oldest-first and the next reclaims the remaining 6, waiting on nothing but the rebuilds. Structural half (new, TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement): the reclaim issues exactly ONE statement on the transaction, and that statement carries LIMIT ?, the age bound, the named-by-nothing condition and oldest-first order, so the added latency scales with the cap and not with the backlog. WHAT IT VISITS: the body of ReclaimOrphansWrittenBefore in journal.go, every call on the transaction and the literal it is given. WHAT IT DOES NOT READ: any other function, the projection package, or SQLite's plan.

TESTS: internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal_test.go (NEW; the store had no test file in its package, so this is the subject's file): stamp from the scripted clock; refresh on repeated Put and never backwards, one row per digest; the literal store's wall-clock stamp bracketed by two readings (a condition, no wait); the narrow doors. internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim_test.go: through the PRODUCTION Put, a blob written at the snapshot instant survives and one written before the window is reclaimed; a re-delivered legacy-orphan body is protected by its new writer while the untouched legacy orphan is reclaimed (control); the one-statement pin.

MUTATIONS, each on the live file with a backup restored and porcelain checked, run by name:
M1 stamp removed (old three-column insert): RED TestPutStampsTheWriteInstantFromTheStoreClock "written_at must be the store clock's instant at the Put, never the migration default"; TestAStoreBuiltAsALiteralStampsTheWallClock; TestARepeatedPutRefreshesTheStampAndNeverMovesItBack; TestAFreshlyPutBlobIsNeverReclaimedWhileItsWriterMayStillAppend "a blob the production store wrote inside the window is never reclaimed: its writer may still be between the blob write and the journal append"; TestARedeliveredOrphanBodyIsProtectedByItsNewWriter. This is the ruled mutation: every fresh blob reads as legacy and is reclaimed at once.
M2 stamp kept, refresh removed (DO NOTHING): RED TestARepeatedPutRefreshesTheStampAndNeverMovesItBack "a repeated Put of the same body must refresh written_at to the later instant; a stamp left at the first instant lets the reclaim delete the blob under the second writer's append"; TestARedeliveredOrphanBodyIsProtectedByItsNewWriter "a legacy orphan whose body a new writer re-delivered inside the window is protected by that writer's refreshed stamp".
M3 no clock stamps zero: RED TestAStoreBuiltAsALiteralStampsTheWallClock "a store with no scripted clock must stamp the wall clock, never zero".
M4 a second statement in the reclaim: RED TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement "the reclaim issues exactly one statement on the transaction: [ExecContext: `SELECT 1` QueryContext: `DELETE ...`]".
M5 a Delete method on the store: RED TestTheWriteDoorAndTheDeleteDoorStayNarrow "the concrete store writes and inspects; a delete on it would make its doc false and the value unsafe to hand around".
M6 cap dropped from the statement: RED TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement "the one statement carries the cap as its LIMIT" AND TestReclaimCapIsOldestFirstAndExactlyTheCap "exactly the cap is reclaimed in one rebuild" (both halves of the budget proof).

STILL OPEN, the two seams from 01:47, restated with a recommendation because no ruling named them:
SEAM 1, part 3(b). The refusal "deadline later than now plus the WorkflowResult tier" needs the tier on receipt.Service (Window). The tier is known ONLY in tasks.NewLifecycleReceiptServiceWithProfile, so beyond the six granted deadline lines it needs TWO foreign one-line edits: internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:116 gains `Window: profile.WorkflowResult()` in the production Service literal, and internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go:111 gains `Window: time.Second` in its literal. A zero Window REFUSES (the same rule the appender applies to a zero Deadline); a default would be the silent zero. No shape I can find avoids both lines. One more fact for the ruling: the check must compare ctx.Deadline() against the WALL clock (time.Until), because a context deadline is a wall-clock instant; comparing it against s.Clock would refuse every test that scripts a 1970 clock. RECOMMENDATION: extend the widening by exactly those two lines. I do not edit either file until ruled.
SEAM 2, part 8'. One stderr line through the read command's diagnostic writer needs a Diagnostics io.Writer (plus the clock and the tier) threaded through tasks.RebuildLifecycleOccurrences, the four handler input structs and the four cmd files: nine files outside my set. Until ruled, the four read commands run the PLAIN rebuild and the reach guard pins ZERO production callers of RebuildOccurrencesReclaiming: the reclaim is built, proven and NOT REACHED in production. RECOMMENDATION: widen for exactly one field or line in each of the nine; in that commit I also switch the AGENTS.md fault-record sentence "nothing deletes them yet", which becomes false the moment the reclaim is reached.

NEXT, without waiting: nothing on L11 remains that is inside my set. I hold until seams 1 and 2 are ruled; the gate result on 13efa73 follows as a separate comment.

THE TWO NARROW DOORS, as the design check asked: the WRITE door is the BlobStore interface, declaring exactly Put(ctx, digest, body); its only caller is receipt.Service.Receive, which depends on nothing else of the store, so a fake that records the call satisfies it. The concrete SQLiteBlobStore carries Put plus read-only inspection (Exists, Reclaimable, ReclaimableCount) and NO delete. The DELETE door is receipt.PayloadReclaimer{Tx}, declaring exactly ReclaimOrphansWrittenBefore(ctx, before, limit); its only constructor is projection.reclaimOrphanPayloads inside the rebuild transaction (the reach guard from 1e61991 pins that). TestTheWriteDoorAndTheDeleteDoorStayNarrow pins all three method sets by reflection and that the delete door does not implement the write door.

PART 6, THE BUDGET PROOF under option (d): the "invocation" is a read command and its budget is the CAP, not a tier. Behavioural half (already in 1e61991): with 1030 orphans one rebuild reclaims exactly 1024 oldest-first and the next reclaims the remaining 6, waiting on nothing but the rebuilds. Structural half (new, TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement): the reclaim issues exactly ONE statement on the transaction, and that statement carries LIMIT ?, the age bound, the named-by-nothing condition and oldest-first order, so the added latency scales with the cap and not with the backlog. WHAT IT VISITS: the body of ReclaimOrphansWrittenBefore in journal.go, every call on the transaction and the literal it is given. WHAT IT DOES NOT READ: any other function, the projection package, or SQLite's plan.

TESTS: internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal_test.go (NEW; the store had no test file in its package, so this is the subject's file): stamp from the scripted clock; refresh on repeated Put and never backwards, one row per digest; the literal store's wall-clock stamp bracketed by two readings (a condition, no wait); the narrow doors. internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim_test.go: through the PRODUCTION Put, a blob written at the snapshot instant survives and one written before the window is reclaimed; a re-delivered legacy-orphan body is protected by its new writer while the untouched legacy orphan is reclaimed (control); the one-statement pin.

M1 stamp removed (old three-column insert): RED TestPutStampsTheWriteInstantFromTheStoreClock "written_at must be the store clock's instant at the Put, never the migration default"; TestAStoreBuiltAsALiteralStampsTheWallClock; TestARepeatedPutRefreshesTheStampAndNeverMovesItBack; TestAFreshlyPutBlobIsNeverReclaimedWhileItsWriterMayStillAppend "a blob the production store wrote inside the window is never reclaimed: its writer may still be between the blob write and the journal append"; TestARedeliveredOrphanBodyIsProtectedByItsNewWriter. M2 stamp kept, refresh removed (DO NOTHING): RED TestARepeatedPutRefreshesTheStampAndNeverMovesItBack "a repeated Put of the same body must refresh written_at to the later instant; a stamp left at the first instant lets the reclaim delete the blob under the second writer's append"; TestARedeliveredOrphanBodyIsProtectedByItsNewWriter "a legacy orphan whose body a new writer re-delivered inside the window is protected by that writer's refreshed stamp".

M5 a Delete method on the store: RED TestTheWriteDoorAndTheDeleteDoorStayNarrow "the concrete store writes and inspects; a delete on it would make its doc false and the value unsafe to hand around".

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SIDE B's Put FINDING, AND TWO SEAMS. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

SIDE B's FINDING IS REAL, IT IS ITS OWN, AND THE RULING DID NOT ANTICIPATE IT. The old Put was ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. So a writer RE-DELIVERING a body that an OLD ORPHAN ALREADY CARRIES kept THE ORPHAN'S STAMP, and a read command running between that Put and its journal append would see an OLD written_at, judge the blob eligible, and DELETE IT UNDER THE APPEND. That is the exact corruption the age bound exists to prevent, reached by a path the bound does not cover: the blob is old, but THE WRITE IN FLIGHT IS NEW.
The fix is in the same commit — DO UPDATE SET written_at = max(stored, new) — and it is the right direction, because taking the MAXIMUM makes the row look YOUNGER and therefore SAFER, never older. Pinned, mutation RED.
WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: the whole L11 design rests on "written_at is the moment this body's current write began". DO NOTHING silently broke that invariant for every duplicate body, and duplicates are the normal case for a content-addressed store. A stamp that is not refreshed is not a stamp; it is a fossil. Side B found it while implementing the mechanism, which is where this class of defect is findable at all.

SEAM 1, PART 3b: RULED, GRANTED, BOUNDED. Side B's set widens by TWO more one-line edits beyond the six deadline lines: internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:116 (Window: profile.WorkflowResult()) and internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go:111 (Window: time.Second). A zero Window refuses, so these two callers cannot survive the refusal without them. NEITHER IS SIDE A's; side A is final at a84e6c1 and its branch is frozen, so no write race exists. ONE LINE EACH, NO ASSERTION CHANGED, STOP AND REPORT if either needs more.
ONE CONDITION, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: STATE THE TWO-CLOCK BOUNDARY IN SOURCE, BESIDE THE CHECK. The refusal compares ctx.Deadline() against THE WALL CLOCK, because a context deadline is a wall-clock fact. The reclaim's age compares written_at against THE INJECTED CLOCK the store now holds. TWO DIFFERENT CLOCKS DECIDE TWO PARTS OF ONE MECHANISM. That is defensible and probably unavoidable, but it is EXACTLY the kind of fact that rots silently: a test that scripts the injected clock far from wall time makes the two decisions disagree, and the failure would read as a flake. Say in the source WHICH DECISION USES WHICH CLOCK AND WHY, and name it in the report.

SEAM 2, PART 8': SURFACED TO THE TEAM LEAD, NOT RULED HERE, because nine files is a scope decision and it arrives late in the slice.
THE FACT THAT DECIDES IT, IN SIDE B's OWN WORDS: UNTIL THE SEAM EXISTS, THE READ COMMANDS RUN THE PLAIN REBUILD AND THE RECLAIM IS BUILT BUT NOT REACHED IN PRODUCTION.
A RECLAIM THAT IS BUILT, TESTED AND NEVER REACHED IS THE WORST OF THE THREE POSSIBLE OUTCOMES. It satisfies the leaf on paper, it passes every gate, and the user's 14,490 orphans keep growing exactly as before — while the slice report says the reclaim landed. Unreachable code that looks delivered is worse than absent code, because absent code is visible. SO THE MERGED STATE MUST NEVER BE "BUILT BUT NOT REACHED" WITHOUT THAT BEING NAMED IN THE SLICE REPORT AND ACCEPTED DELIBERATELY.
BEFORE WIDENING BY NINE FILES, CONSIDER INVERTING THE DEPENDENCY. The seam as described THREADS A Diagnostics io.Writer, a clock and a tier DOWN through tasks.RebuildLifecycleOccurrences, four handler inputs and four command files. The alternative is to PUSH NOTHING DOWN AND RETURN WHAT HAPPENED UP: the rebuild returns its reclaim outcome (a count and an error), and THE COMMAND LAYER, WHICH ALREADY HOLDS A DIAGNOSTIC WRITER, decides what to print. The rebuild then needs NO writer, and the handler inputs may need nothing at all.
THREE REASONS TO PREFER IT: the rebuild stays a DATA OPERATION rather than gaining an output device; the stderr rule is satisfied AT THE LAYER THAT ALREADY OWNS STDERR; and the file count falls out of the design instead of being authorised. It is the same move that turned the Put widening into the Put reshape — ASK WHETHER THE RIPPLE IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SHAPE BEFORE AUTHORISING THE RIPPLE.
SIDE B HOLDS ON SEAM 2 UNTIL RULED. Nothing else on L11 is inside its set.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TEAM-LEAD RULING ON SEAM 2 (2026-09-05, answers supervisor-s1's 02:14Z comment). INVERT THE DEPENDENCY. Nothing is threaded down; the outcome is returned up.
1. projection.RebuildOccurrences takes its reclaim inputs (snapshot clock, the WorkflowResult tier, the cap) from ONE small options value that the tasks store supplies from what it already holds: its injected timeouts Profile for the tier; a clock the store holds (wall clock by default, scripted clock through a test-only constructor option, the same shape as the blob store's clock in part 2); the cap constant from the projection package. It takes NO writer.
2. The rebuild returns a ReclaimOutcome (reclaimed count; the reclaim error, if the SAVEPOINT rolled back) beside its own error. A reclaim error never fails the rebuild.
3. The tasks wrapper returns the outcome up. The layer that ALREADY holds the diagnostic writer (the read-side handler if it holds one, else the command) prints the ONE pinned stderr line when the outcome carries an error, and prints nothing on success. No handler input and no command gains a writer, a clock or a tier.
4. BOUND: side B states the file list BEFORE writing; if it exceeds SEVEN files, stop and report the list. Expected: rebuild.go, reclaim.go, their tests, tasks/lifecycle_identity.go, and the four print sites (or fewer if they share a helper).
5. "BUILT BUT NOT REACHED" IS REFUSED as an end state. The merged state must reach the reclaim from every read-side command that rebuilds the projection. Proof through the REAL binary: a store seeded with legacy orphans (written_at 0) and one referenced blob; run a read command with --db; up to the cap are reclaimed, the referenced blob survives, stdout is the command's normal output, stderr is empty; mutation = remove the reclaim call from the rebuild and show RED naming the surviving orphan count.
6. The two-clock boundary is stated in source as the supervisor conditioned: the Receive refusal compares ctx.Deadline() to the wall clock; the reclaim age compares written_at to the store's clock; both are wall clock in production and the test that scripts one must script both.
7. The DO UPDATE SET written_at = max(stored, new) fix on Put is ACCEPTED as part of part 2 and is recorded as a deviation on the IMPL_PLAN (a duplicate body re-delivered onto an old orphan must refresh the stamp, or a read command can reclaim under an in-flight append); its pin and mutation stand.
Seam 1 (two one-line edits: tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:116 and backend/backend_test.go:111 for a non-zero window) is confirmed as granted.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SEAM 2 RULED: INVERT. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05, recording the team lead's ruling and what it changes.

THE SHAPE: the rebuild takes its reclaim inputs from ONE OPTIONS VALUE that the tasks store supplies FROM WHAT IT ALREADY HOLDS — the Profile for the tier, a store-held clock with a test-only option, the cap constant — and it RETURNS a ReclaimOutcome beside its error. THE LAYER THAT ALREADY OWNS STDERR PRINTS THE ONE LINE. No writer, no clock and no tier threads down.
BOUND: side B STATES THE FILE LIST FIRST, and MORE THAN SEVEN FILES IS A STOP-AND-REPORT. The nine-file estimate was for the threading shape; the inversion should cost less, and the bound makes that claim CHECKABLE rather than hoped for. A widening that is authorised open-ended cannot be shown to have been the cheaper design.

"BUILT BUT NOT REACHED" IS REFUSED AS AN END STATE, and this is the part that matters most. The proof is a REAL-BINARY one: legacy orphans PLUS ONE REFERENCED BLOB; a read command reclaims up to the cap; THE REFERENCED BLOB SURVIVES; stderr is EMPTY on the success path; and the MUTATION REMOVES THE CALL.
WHY THAT PROOF SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE: it tests the three claims that can each fail silently and independently — that the reclaim RUNS AT ALL in production (the mutation that removes the call must turn it RED), that it DELETES THE RIGHT ROWS (the cap), and that it DELETES NOTHING ELSE (the referenced blob survives). A Go-level test of the reclaim function proves only the middle one. The whole reason this seam existed was that the function could be perfect and never called.

WHAT THIS RULING SETTLES ABOUT METHOD, worth recording once because it has now happened three times in this slice: A RIPPLE THROUGH FOREIGN FILES IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SHAPE, NOT MERELY A COST TO AUTHORISE. The Put widening became the Put reshape and touched no foreign file; the nine-file threading became a returned value; and in both cases the question that produced the better design was the same one — ASK WHETHER THE RIPPLE IS TELLING YOU SOMETHING BEFORE YOU SIGN FOR IT. The one time the ripple was real and unavoidable, the Receive deadline argument, the widening was granted and bounded instead.

ALSO CONFIRMED: the seam-1 grant stands WITH the two-clock condition — the source states which decision reads the WALL clock (the ctx.Deadline() refusal) and which reads the INJECTED clock (the written_at age), and why. Side B's DO UPDATE SET written_at = max(stored, new) fix is ACCEPTED and recorded as a deviation on the IMPL_PLAN.

REMAINING ON SIDE B: part 3b (granted, in progress), then seam 2 under the inversion with its file list stated first. Then the fold from side A's frozen head a84e6c1, fold obligation F-1, the six gates, and the review wave.

text:
L11 s6k7mg PART 3(b) PROVEN ON A THROWAWAY COPY, NOT COMMITTED; the widening it needs is now EXACT (worker-s1b). Copy: /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1b/tw-3b (archive of 13efa73 plus the patch); patch: /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1b/l11-3b.patch (494 lines). My worktree is untouched (porcelain empty at 13efa73).

THE MECHANISM (internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go, +32): Service gains `Window time.Duration`, documented as the WorkflowResult tier. Receive calls boundedWriter(ctx) after the gate, delivery and wiring checks and BEFORE the blob write, so an ungated or malformed delivery still meets its own refusal first and nothing reaches the store. Three refusals, all CategoryValidation, all naming the tier in the headline (StructuredError.Error() prints the headline only, so the tier had to be there): `The lifecycle receipt service has no writer window (the WorkflowResult tier).`; `The lifecycle delivery carries no deadline; every writer must expire within the 30s writer window (the WorkflowResult tier).`; `The lifecycle delivery deadline is 2s away, beyond the 1s writer window (the WorkflowResult tier).` Zero Window REFUSES (the appender's zero-Deadline rule). The deadline is compared against the WALL clock (time.Until), see mutation B.

PROOF ON THE COPY: receipt, backend, budget, tasks green; cmd/pasture Readback/Raw/Orphans green (the raw path's 30 s deadline and the native hook's 5 s deadline both lie inside the 30 s window; the DeadlineTestProfile's 2 s window accepts its own tiers). Mutations, each restored and re-run green:
A refusal removed: RED TestReceiveRefusesADeliveryWhoseContextCarriesNoDeadline, TestReceiveRefusesADeadlineBeyondTheWriterWindow, TestReceiveRefusesAServiceWithoutAWriterWindow, all "Receive must refuse"; the control TestReceiveAcceptsADeadlineInsideTheWindow stays green.
B deadline compared against the injected clock (deadline.Sub(s.Clock.Now())): RED on EVERY accepted-delivery test in the package, e.g. TestReceiveWritesBlobBeforeOccurrence "The lifecycle delivery deadline is 496826h19m36.108s away, beyond the 1s writer window" (the scripted clock reads 1970). This is the fact I stated: a context deadline is a wall-clock instant, and only a wall-clock comparison bounds anything.
C zero window silently defaults to 30 s: RED TestReceiveRefusesAServiceWithoutAWriterWindow "Receive must refuse".

THE WIDENING, EXACT, per file, measured on the patch (lines added/removed):
INSIDE MY SET: service.go +32/-0; service_test.go +88/-12 (helper boundedContext, four tests, `Window: time.Second` on six literals, six call contexts); gate_test.go +4/-5, origin_test.go +4/-5, consultation_test.go +2/-3 (literals and contexts; the `context` import leaves those three); gate_integration_test.go and origin_integration_test.go +2/-1 (the context line).
FOREIGN, NEEDING THE RULING:
1. internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go +1/-1: the production Service literal gains `Window: profile.WorkflowResult()`. PRODUCTION, the one place the profile is known; without it every production delivery is refused.
2. internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go +8/-1: `Window: time.Second,` in its literal (one line) and the one Receive call's context, via a five-line boundedContext helper. The six-file grant covers the context; the ONE literal line is the extension I ask for.
3. internal/engine/budget/budget_test.go +19/-3: three Receive call contexts, plus a boundedContext(t, profile) helper (it takes the deadline from the profile each test built its service with, so the measurement tests under the production profile keep their 30 s) and the clocklessDeadline type below. Context only, as granted; the helper is the shape of that edit.
4. internal/engine/budget/abandonment_test.go +4/-2: one Receive context via the helper, AND the abandonment proof's own context. That proof holds the Receive between blob commit and journal append and cancels it ITSELF; a WithTimeout there would put a clock back into a proof that was made clock-free on purpose. So it wraps its cancellable context in `clocklessDeadline{Context: cancellable, at: time.Now().Add(profile.WorkflowResult())}`: Deadline() reports an instant, Done and Err stay the parent's. Two lines in the proof, one six-line type in budget_test.go (same package). That is more than "the deadline argument" in shape though not in meaning; I name it so the ruling can refuse it.

MUTATION B IS THE EVIDENCE FOR THE TWO-CLOCK CONDITION, and it is better evidence than my argument for it. Comparing the deadline against the INJECTED clock turns every scripted-clock test RED with "496826h away". That is the two clocks disagreeing, measured, in the exact way I said would read as a flake if nobody wrote it down. NOW IT IS WRITTEN DOWN WITH A NUMBER. State it in source beside the check.

(b) THE clocklessDeadline WRAPPER IS GRANTED, and it is the right instinct rather than a workaround.
THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: the abandonment proof was made CLOCK-FREE ON PURPOSE. Satisfying the refusal with a real context.WithTimeout would PUT A CLOCK BACK INTO A PROOF THAT WAS DELIBERATELY BUILT WITHOUT ONE — a silent regression of a property this project paid for, where the failure would appear later as a flake under load and nobody would connect it to this line.

FOUR CONDITIONS, and they exist because a context that reports a deadline it does not enforce IS A TRUE STATEMENT ONLY INSIDE A TEST:
1. IT LIVES IN A TEST FILE AND NEVER IN PRODUCTION. If it can be imported by production code, the refusal it satisfies becomes a formality.
2. IT CARRIES A COMMENT NAMING WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it reports a deadline for the refusal and DOES NOT ENFORCE ONE; enforcement stays with cancellation; the production guarantee is unaffected.
3. IT IS USED ONLY WHERE THE CLOCK-FREE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATE. Everywhere else the file passes a REAL deadline. If the wrapper spreads to every foreign test file, THE REFUSAL LOSES ITS TEST COVERAGE while every test stays green — the pin-that-loosens shape in a new dress.
4. NAME IN THE REPORT which files got a REAL deadline and which got the wrapper, and why each.
THE boundedContext HELPER IS ACCEPTABLE as the form of "the deadline argument" in the foreign test files, under condition 3: one helper instead of a repeated literal is better, provided the choice between a real deadline and the wrapper stays per-file and stated.

THE COMMIT: side B applies (a) and (b) as ONE commit naming ALL TWELVE FILES. It must MARK WHICH FILES ARE ITS OWN SET AND WHICH ARE GRANTED WIDENINGS, so a reviewer can check the grant covers every foreign file without reconstructing the history. Anything beyond the granted list is a STOP-AND-REPORT.

SEAM 2 IS NO LONGER OPEN — side B's report predates the ruling. THE TEAM LEAD RULED THE INVERSION: the rebuild takes its reclaim inputs from ONE OPTIONS VALUE the tasks store supplies from what it already holds (Profile for the tier, a store-held clock with a test-only option, the cap constant), and RETURNS a ReclaimOutcome beside its error; THE LAYER THAT ALREADY OWNS STDERR PRINTS THE LINE. text:
SEAM 2 EXCEEDS ITS BOUND: SIDE B STOPPED CORRECTLY. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Surfaced to the team lead with two shapes it did not consider. I verified the structural facts myself before passing it up.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE: RebuildLifecycleOccurrences is called from FOUR handlers — hook_lifecycle_orphans.go:83, hook_lifecycle_context.go:61, hook_lifecycle_list.go:67, hook_lifecycle_lineage.go:55 — and is declared at internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:88 returning ERROR ONLY. Side B's reason is correct and structural: THE HANDLERS OPEN THE TRACKER THEMSELVES from in.DBPath and return (int, error), so THE LAYER THAT OWNS STDERR NEVER HOLDS THE STORE. An outcome returned upward must cross four handler returns and four command sites. THIRTEEN FILES IS AN HONEST COUNT, not a lazy one; side B checked a pointer sink, a typed warning in the error channel and printing from the handlers, and each costs the same eight files or is refused by the ruling.

TWO SHAPES NEITHER OF US NAMED, offered in order of preference.

SHAPE 1 — DEFAULT THE SINK, INJECT FOR TESTS. THIS INVERTS THE QUESTION FROM "WHO MUST PASS THE WRITER" TO "WHO MUST SILENCE IT".
The tracker gains a diagnostics sink whose PRODUCTION DEFAULT IS STDERR, set where the tracker is opened (open_unified.go, which this leaf already touches for the store clock). Tests inject io.Discard through the same test-only option that already carries the clock. NO HANDLER SIGNATURE CHANGES AND NO COMMAND SITE CHANGES, because nobody has to CARRY the writer down — the store already has one by default.
It satisfies the ruling's intent exactly: the rebuild still owns no output DEVICE it was given by a caller; it has a sink the store was constructed with, which is the same shape as the store-held CLOCK the ruling already accepted. Estimated files: lifecycle_identity.go, open_unified.go, the projection reclaim, and their tests — INSIDE THE BOUND OF SEVEN.
THE ONE OBJECTION TO WEIGH: a library that writes to stderr BY DEFAULT is normally poor practice. Here the store is CLI-and-daemon-only, the ruled output is exactly ONE LINE ON FAILURE, and the success path is silent, so the blast radius is a single diagnostic on a path that is already a command.

SHAPE 2 — ONE CALL SITE NOW, THE OTHER THREE LATER. Wire the reclaim into ONE read command, prove it with the real binary there, and record the remaining three as a follow-up. That satisfies the refusal of "built but not reached", because the reclaim IS reached in production by a real command with a real proof, and it costs roughly four files.
IF THIS IS CHOSEN, NAME THE HAZARD IN THE SAME BREATH: the natural single site is the ORPHANS command, and RECLAIMING INSIDE IT CHANGES WHAT IT REPORTS — the command that measures orphans would mutate the thing it measures, so its output must state "reclaimed N, remaining M" rather than silently returning a smaller number. A command whose count changes because the command ran is a defect unless the output says so.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS SHAPE 1. It keeps ALL FOUR read commands reaching the reclaim, needs no follow-up, stays inside the bound, and reuses a pattern the ruling has ALREADY ACCEPTED for the clock. Shape 2 is the safe fallback if a default stderr sink is refused on principle.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, whatever is chosen: the merged state must not be "BUILT BUT NOT REACHED". The ruling already refuses it, and side B has been told to write nothing for seam 2 until this is decided.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE: RebuildLifecycleOccurrences is called from FOUR handlers — hook_lifecycle_orphans.go:83, hook_lifecycle_context.go:61, hook_lifecycle_list.go:67, hook_lifecycle_lineage.go:55 — and is declared at internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go:88 returning ERROR ONLY. Side B's reason is correct and structural: THE HANDLERS OPEN THE TRACKER THEMSELVES from in.DBPath and return (int, error), so THE LAYER THAT OWNS STDERR NEVER HOLDS THE STORE. An outcome returned upward must cross four handler returns and four command sites. THIRTEEN FILES IS AN HONEST COUNT, not a lazy one; side B checked a pointer sink, a typed warning in the error channel and printing from the handlers, and each costs the same eight files or is refused by the ruling.

TWO SHAPES NEITHER OF US NAMED, offered in order of preference.

SHAPE 1 — DEFAULT THE SINK, INJECT FOR TESTS. THIS INVERTS THE QUESTION FROM "WHO MUST PASS THE WRITER" TO "WHO MUST SILENCE IT".
The tracker gains a diagnostics sink whose PRODUCTION DEFAULT IS STDERR, set where the tracker is opened (open_unified.go, which this leaf already touches for the store clock). Tests inject io.Discard through the same test-only option that already carries the clock. NO HANDLER SIGNATURE CHANGES AND NO COMMAND SITE CHANGES, because nobody has to CARRY the writer down — the store already has one by default.
It satisfies the ruling's intent exactly: the rebuild still owns no output DEVICE it was given by a caller; it has a sink the store was constructed with, which is the same shape as the store-held CLOCK the ruling already accepted. Estimated files: lifecycle_identity.go, open_unified.go, the projection reclaim, and their tests — INSIDE THE BOUND OF SEVEN.
THE ONE OBJECTION TO WEIGH: a library that writes to stderr BY DEFAULT is normally poor practice. Here the store is CLI-and-daemon-only, the ruled output is exactly ONE LINE ON FAILURE, and the success path is silent, so the blast radius is a single diagnostic on a path that is already a command.

SHAPE 2 — ONE CALL SITE NOW, THE OTHER THREE LATER. Wire the reclaim into ONE read command, prove it with the real binary there, and record the remaining three as a follow-up. That satisfies the refusal of "built but not reached", because the reclaim IS reached in production by a real command with a real proof, and it costs roughly four files.
IF THIS IS CHOSEN, NAME THE HAZARD IN THE SAME BREATH: the natural single site is the ORPHANS command, and RECLAIMING INSIDE IT CHANGES WHAT IT REPORTS — the command that measures orphans would mutate the thing it measures, so its output must state "reclaimed N, remaining M" rather than silently returning a smaller number. A command whose count changes because the command ran is a defect unless the output says so.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS SHAPE 1. It keeps ALL FOUR read commands reaching the reclaim, needs no follow-up, stays inside the bound, and reuses a pattern the ruling has ALREADY ACCEPTED for the clock. Shape 2 is the safe fallback if a default stderr sink is refused on principle.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, whatever is chosen: the merged state must not be "BUILT BUT NOT REACHED". The ruling already refuses it, and side B has been told to write nothing for seam 2 until this is decided.

PART 3(b) IS DONE at 648c469: thirteen files all named in the ownership paragraph, the two one-line grants applied, the two-clock boundary STATED IN SOURCE in Service.boundedWriter and SQLiteBlobStore.writeInstant, and mutations A, B and C re-run RED from the worktree. Five gates running on an archive copy.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TEAM-LEAD RULING ON SEAM 2, SECOND ROUND (2026-09-05, answers supervisor-s1's 02:26Z comment). SHAPE 1, with two tightenings. Shape 2 is REJECTED: partial reach is "built but reached by one command", and the follow-up it creates has no owner.
1. THE SINK IS A REQUIRED CONSTRUCTION INPUT OF THE STORE, NOT A LIBRARY DEFAULT. The tracker is constructed with a diagnostics writer; a nil writer is REFUSED at construction with a validation error naming the field, the same shape as receipt.Service refusing a missing dependency. The unified production opener (open_unified.go, already in side B's set for the store clock) passes the process stderr. Tests pass io.Discard or a buffer through the same test-only option that carries the clock. Nobody threads a writer down; the store was built with one. This keeps the objection to a default-stderr library from arising: there is no default, only an explicit opener.
2. ENUMERATE EVERY PRODUCTION CONSTRUCTION SITE of the tracker (the CLI opener; the daemon if it constructs one) and show each passes a non-nil sink; the nil refusal is the mechanism that makes the enumeration complete. Mutation: construct with nil and quote the refusal.
3. THE ORPHANS COMMAND HAZARD APPLIES UNDER SHAPE 1 TOO, because all four read commands now reclaim inside their rebuild, and the orphans command measures what it just mutated. Its output MUST state both numbers, reclaimed this run and remaining, as pinned operator text; mutation = drop the reclaimed phrase and show RED. The other three read commands print nothing on success and the one pinned line on a reclaim error.
4. The rebuild still returns the ReclaimOutcome (count, error) so the orphans command can print its numbers from data rather than from a side effect; the store's sink receives only the failure line.
5. FILE BOUND stays at seven: lifecycle_identity.go, open_unified.go, the projection reclaim and rebuild with their tests, and the orphans handler's output. State the list first; more is a stop-and-report.
6. The real-binary reachability proof of the previous ruling stands for ALL FOUR read commands (one proof per command, or one table-driven proof that derives the four from the command tree with a non-vacuity control).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SEAM 2 RULED: SHAPE 1, WITH TWO TIGHTENINGS THAT IMPROVE ON WHAT I PROPOSED. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

TIGHTENING 1, AND IT IS A REAL CORRECTION OF MY PROPOSAL, NOT A REFINEMENT. I proposed a sink with a PRODUCTION DEFAULT of stderr. The lead ruled a REQUIRED CONSTRUCTION INPUT instead: NIL IS REFUSED with a validation error, the unified opener supplies stderr, and tests supply io.Discard or a buffer through the same test-only option that carries the clock. Every production construction site is ENUMERATED, and THE REFUSAL IS THE COMPLETENESS MECHANISM.
WHY THAT IS STRICTLY BETTER THAN MY VERSION, and it is the same lesson this slice keeps teaching: MY DEFAULT WOULD HAVE MADE AN UNENUMERATED CONSTRUCTION SITE SILENTLY CORRECT. A site nobody thought about would have got stderr and worked, so nobody would ever learn the site existed — and the day a site needed a different sink, the default would hide it. A REQUIRED INPUT FAILS LOUDLY AT EXACTLY THE PLACE THE ENUMERATION WAS INCOMPLETE. It is a derived population rather than a hand list, applied to construction sites instead of to test rows.

TIGHTENING 2: THE ORPHANS HAZARD APPLIES UNDER SHAPE 1 TOO, AND I ATTACHED IT ONLY TO SHAPE 2. That was my error. All four read commands now reclaim inside their rebuild, so the command that REPORTS orphans CHANGES the number it reports BY RUNNING. The orphans command must print RECLAIMED-THIS-RUN AND REMAINING as PINNED OPERATOR TEXT. A count that changes because the command ran is a defect unless the output says so, and that is true whichever shape delivers the reclaim.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: the rebuild still RETURNS the ReclaimOutcome; the bound stays at SEVEN FILES with the list stated FIRST; and the REAL-BINARY REACHABILITY PROOF covers ALL FOUR READ COMMANDS.
SHAPE 2 IS REJECTED, for the right reason: partial reach plus an OWNERLESS FOLLOW-UP. A follow-up with no owner is how "built but not reached" comes back later wearing a different name.

BOTH HAZARDS ARE NOW IN THE REVIEWER PROMPT'S ATTACK LIST at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s1/launch-reviewer-s1-r1.md, written as ATTACKS rather than as things to read:
- construct the tracker with a NIL sink and require a VALIDATION REFUSAL, not a silent fallback; then check every production construction site supplies a real sink, so a site nobody enumerated FAILS LOUDLY. A refusal that can be bypassed is the finding.
- check the orphans command prints BOTH numbers as pinned text, that each is true of the run that produced it, that a reader can tell them apart, and mutate each phrase to RED.
- run the real-binary reachability proof for EACH of the four read commands, with the decisive mutation being REMOVING THE CALL: if the suite stays green with the reclaim never invoked, the leaf shipped unreachable and every unit test of it proved nothing.

text:
STOP-AND-REPORT, L11 s6k7mg PART 3(b): THE GATE ON 648c469 IS RED BEYOND SIDE A'S LITERAL, AND THE RULED REFUSAL REFUSES THE S0 ABANDONMENT PROOF BY CONSTRUCTION (worker-s1b). No further commit until ruled. 83c7803 (comment-only correction, stacked on 648c469) is RED for the same reason and was not gated.

THE GATE (archive copy of 648c469): build, vet, flake, gofmt green; test-race 70 packages ok, 0 races; RED on NINE tests. One is side A's literal (explained). EIGHT are the new refusal reaching callers outside the six-file grant, every one with the same text: "The lifecycle delivery carries no deadline; every writer must expire within the 30s writer window (the WorkflowResult tier)."
 cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go: TestAnInvocationAbandonedAfterItsCommitTellsTheHostTheTruth, TestAdviceFollowsTheCauseAndNotTheClassifier ("the invocation finished without reaching the commit boundary"). THE S0 PINS, EDITED BY NOBODY.
 cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go:1309, :1365: TestEnabledCodexHandlersToDurableReadBack, TestCodexAndOpenCodeGateDifferentialPreservesProviderFacts. SIDE A'S FILE, FROZEN.
 cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_lineage_production_test.go:183: TestLineageOverCapRefusesAndCommitsNothing.
 cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_context_production_test.go:173: TestContextDisclosurePostCommitStdoutFailureReportsStderrWithTrailIntact.
 internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_test.go:105: TestHookLifecycleResponseOpenCodeCommitsBeforeReturning.
 internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_manifest_test.go:72: TestHookLifecycleMetamodelReadSurface.
 internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_codex_test.go:139 (a subtest of the readback above).
And ONE in my own set: internal/lifecycle/receipt/gate_integration_test.go:95 "rebuild occurrences: ... context deadline exceeded": the 1 s deadline I gave that test is reused across its projection rebuild, which under -race took longer than 1 s. My file, my fix (a per-call deadline at the production window).

WHY, MEASURED: (1) Every hook path reaches Receive through handlers.HookLifecycle, and the tests above call that handler, or Receive, with context.Background(). They are outside the six files the grant named because the grant was drawn from Receive's DIRECT callers; the handler's callers were not in the enumeration. (2) The S0 abandonment proof passes lifecycleOutcome a deadline WITH NO CLOCK IN IT: trippedDeadline.derive (hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go:1155) returns context.WithCancel(parent), which reports NO Deadline(). That is the property the proof was built for (AGENTS.md: "a deadline with NO clock in it"). The ruled refusal "a context that carries no deadline" therefore refuses that proof BY CONSTRUCTION, not by accident, and the file it lives in may be edited by nobody.

MY ERROR, STATED PLAINLY: before committing I ran cmd/pasture only with -run 'Readback|Raw|Orphan' and did not run internal/handlers at all; the archive-copy gate is what caught it. The throwaway proof was correct for the packages it ran and silent about the rest.

OPTIONS, FOR THE RULING; I CHOOSE NONE:
 (C) SPLIT THE REFUSAL. Receive refuses only a deadline BEYOND the window and a zero window; it ACCEPTS a context with no deadline. The "no unbounded writer" claim then rests on the two production wirings, both already pinned by name in source: the native path derives context.WithTimeout at the HookInvocation tier (TestTheProductionPathWiresThePassThroughBarrierAndTheProductionTier pins the factory verbatim) and the raw path derives WithTimeout at the WorkflowResult tier (TestTheRawPathRunsUnderTheWorkflowResultTier). The S0 proof and every foreign Background test pass unchanged; NO untouchable file is touched; the six-file widening and the clockless wrapper become unnecessary and can be reverted by a later commit. COST: it changes the ruled mechanism, and a future third writer that forgets a deadline is caught by no refusal, only by a missing pin.
 (D) KEEP THE REFUSAL AS RULED and widen: five foreign test files for the deadline argument (lineage_production, context_production, handlers/hook_lifecycle_test, handlers/manifest_test, handlers/codex_test), PLUS a fresh side-A worker for hook_lifecycle_production_test.go (two contexts), PLUS a ruling that lets ONE line of the S0 file change: trippedDeadline.derive returns a context that REPORTS a deadline (the clockless wrapper shape granted at 02:21) while still tripping only on the signal. Faithful to the ruling; three grants, one of them on a file nobody edits.
 (E) REVERT 648c469 and 83c7803 by a later commit that names them, and re-land 3(b) under whichever of (C) or (D) is ruled.
RECOMMENDATION, offered not chosen: (C) is the only shape that touches no untouchable file and keeps the bound provable by pins that already exist; (D) is the only shape that keeps the refusal the ruling described.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PART 3(b) IS RED BEYOND SIDE A's LITERAL. SIDE B STOPPED CORRECTLY. SURFACED TO THE TEAM LEAD. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

THE ANALYTICAL POINT THE THREE OPTIONS DO NOT NAME, AND IT SHOULD DECIDE THE RULING: THE REFUSAL TESTS THE WRONG PROPERTY. It refuses a context that CARRIES NO DEADLINE. The property the age bound actually needs is that NO WRITER HOLDS AN UNBOUNDED WINDOW between the blob write and the journal append. THOSE ARE NOT THE SAME PROPERTY. A context bounded by CANCELLATION is bounded; it simply reports no Deadline().
THE TREE PROVES IT RATHER THAN ARGUING IT: the S0 abandonment proof passes a deadline WITH NO CLOCK — trippedDeadline.derive is context.WithCancel(parent), which reports no Deadline() — and it is a CORRECT, DELIBERATELY CLOCK-FREE proof that this project paid to build. THE RULED REFUSAL REFUSES A CORRECT CALLER BY CONSTRUCTION. When a guard refuses something correct, the guard's predicate is wrong, not the caller.
SO THE REFUSAL IS BOTH OVER-BROAD AND UNDER-AIMED: it rejects correct cancellation-bounded callers, while the risk it was written for is a caller whose window can EXCEED the tier.

SECOND FACT, AND IT IS A LESSON ABOUT THE ENUMERATION ITSELF: the six-file grant was drawn from Receive's DIRECT callers. Every hook path reaches Receive THROUGH handlers.HookLifecycle, and tests in five further files call THAT with context.Background(). THE ENUMERATION WAS A HAND-DRAWN BOUNDARY (direct callers) WHERE THE POPULATION IS TRANSITIVE (every path that reaches Receive). That is the same defect class this epic keeps finding in guards, occurring this time in an ENUMERATION rather than in a test. An enumeration that decides a blast radius must be derived the same way a guard's population must be derived.
Two of the newly RED files are UNTOUCHABLE: side A's hook_lifecycle_production_test.go is FROZEN, and the S0 proof file is edited by nobody.

SIDE B'S OWN ERROR, REPORTED BY IT WITHOUT PROMPTING AND RECORDED AS GOOD PRACTICE: its pre-commit run covered cmd/pasture only, under -run 'Readback|Raw|Orphan', and NEVER RAN internal/handlers. THE ARCHIVE-COPY GATE CAUGHT WHAT THE FILTERED RUN COULD NOT. This is the standing trap in a new dress — a filtered run is not a run of the suite, and it produces a green that means nothing about the packages it skipped. 83c7803 is stacked on top, RED the same way, and was NOT gated.

MY RECOMMENDATION: OPTION C, WITH ONE ADDITION.
C narrows the refusal to what the bound actually needs: refuse a deadline BEYOND the window (a real violation) and a ZERO window (a misconfiguration), and ACCEPT no-deadline. It touches no untouchable file, it makes the six-file widening REVERTIBLE, and it stops refusing correct callers.
THE ADDITION, because C's residual risk is real: C rests the bound on "the two production WithTimeout wirings already pinned by name", AND A PAIR PINNED BY NAME IS A HAND LIST. A production caller added later without a bounded window would pass unnoticed, which is exactly the hole the refusal was meant to close. SO DERIVE IT: assert over the PRODUCTION call paths that reach Receive that each carries a bounded window, so a new path is covered WITHOUT A TEST EDIT, with a non-vacuity control that an empty derived set is RED.
HOW TO LAND IT: as a FORWARD CORRECTION. A later commit narrows the refusal and NAMES 648c469 and 83c7803. Shared history is not rewritten in this epic, so option E's revert is done by a later commit, never by an amend or a rebase. 83c7803 must be gated, not assumed.
OPTION D IS THE WEAKEST: it keeps a predicate that refuses a correct caller, and it pays for that by editing a FROZEN file, spawning a fresh side-A worker, and putting one line into the S0 proof to make a deliberately clock-free test report a deadline it does not have. That is three concessions bought to defend a wrong predicate.

SIDE B WRITES NOTHING UNTIL RULED.

A context bounded by CANCELLATION is bounded, and the S0 abandonment proof is exactly such a caller: correct, deliberately clock-free, and refused by the old predicate BY CONSTRUCTION.

THE FOREIGN FOOTPRINT GOES BACK TO ZERO. The six foreign deadline edits AND the test-only deadline wrapper are REVERTED by the same forward-correcting commit. The mutation is REMOVING RAW'S WithTimeout.
THAT REPLACES A PAIR PINNED BY NAME. A hand list of two would have let a production writer added later pass unnoticed — the exact hole the refusal existed to close, reopened by the fix for it.

LANDING: ONE LATER COMMIT NAMES 648c469 AND 83c7803. History is not rewritten. 83c7803 IS GATED, NEVER ASSUMED — it was stacked and RED and had never been gated, which is how it reached this point unnoticed.

Side B's pre-commit run covered cmd/pasture under a -run filter and never ran internal/handlers; the full-suite archive gate caught eight RED tests it could not see.
