L11 s6k7mg PART 3(b) FORWARD-CORRECTED PER OPTION C, commit 8e444aa naming 648c469 and 83c7803 (worker-s1b). Porcelain empty. Five gates running on an archive copy. 83c7803 WAS GATED, as ruled: build, vet, flake, gofmt green; test-race 70 ok, 0 races, RED on the same class as 648c469 (eleven --- FAIL lines including subtests: the eight refusal hits plus side A's literal), recorded here as the RED it was.

ACK, listed back: (1) the refusal is narrowed: Receive ACCEPTS a context with no deadline; REFUSES a deadline beyond the window and a zero window; both pinned and mutated. (2) The six foreign deadline edits and the test-only wrapper are reverted by the same commit; the two seam-1 window lines survive only because a zero window would otherwise be constructed there. (3) The bound is a DERIVED guard over production writers, population from the cobra command tree, non-vacuity of at least two, go/ast form as the ruled fallback with the reason stated. (4) One later commit names both corrected SHAs; nothing rewritten. (5) Lessons noted: an enumeration that decides a blast radius is derived like a guard's population; a filtered run says nothing about the packages it skipped. (6) Seam 2 bound is TEN; I state the partition in that commit's ownership paragraph.

WHAT 8e444aa DOES:
- internal/lifecycle/receipt/service.go: the no-deadline arm returns nil with the reason in source (a cancellation-bounded context is bounded; the property the age bound needs is that no PRODUCTION writer holds an unbounded window, enforced where production contexts are made, and named by the guard's test name). The beyond-window and zero-window refusals and the MEASURED two-clock comment stay.
- Reverted to 13efa73 text: internal/engine/budget/budget_test.go and abandonment_test.go (contexts, boundedContext helper, the clocklessDeadline type), cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_readback_production_test.go, and the context edits in my six receipt test files. Kept: `Window: profile.WorkflowResult()` in internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go (untouched by this commit) and `Window: time.Second` in backend_test.go. NET FOREIGN FOOTPRINT AGAINST 13efa73: those two lines, measured with git diff --stat.
- THE DERIVED GUARD, cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_writers_test.go, TestEveryLifecycleWriterCommandBoundsItsWindow. POPULATION: the live tree, hookLifecycleCmd and hookLifecycleCmd.Commands(), every entry with a RunE; each RunE's source body is located from its runtime position (runtime.FuncForPC -> file:line -> the FuncLit or FuncDecl starting there). WRITER-NESS, derived twice: internal/handlers non-test sources are parsed and every top-level function whose same-package call closure contains a call whose selector is Receive is a "reacher"; a command is a writer when its RunE's same-package closure over cmd/pasture calls handlers.<reacher>. NON-VACUITY: at least two writers or RED (today: pasture hook lifecycle, pasture hook lifecycle raw). ASSERTION: the writer's closure contains context.WithTimeout(_, timeouts.ProductionProfile().<Tier>()) or a call passing context.WithTimeout as a value beside timeouts.ProductionProfile() (the native outcome seam). WHAT IT VISITS / DOES NOT READ stated in its doc. FORM: go/ast, because the raw import's tier is 30 s under the profile the built binary runs under, so a held-lock behavioural run would cost that per run; the native path keeps its held-lock behavioural proof in the S0 file. It is SERIAL: it reads the shared command tree and the package's serial sweep classifies it (the sweep turned RED under t.Parallel and named it, which is that guard working). Classified in guardSweepOwned (list entry only; no S0 pin touched).

PACKAGE RUNS BEFORE COMMIT, IN FULL THIS TIME: receipt, backend, budget, tasks, handlers, cmd/pasture: all green except side A's literal.
MUTATIONS, live file with backup, restored, porcelain checked:
- raw's context.WithTimeout replaced by context.WithCancel: RED TestEveryLifecycleWriterCommandBoundsItsWindow "pasture hook lifecycle raw reaches the receipt store but builds no bounded context: every lifecycle writer must derive its context through context.WithTimeout from a tier of timeouts.ProductionProfile(), or the window between its payload write and its journal append is unbounded and the orphan reclaim's age bound is a false claim"; and RED TestTheRawPathRunsUnderTheWorkflowResultTier (the existing source pin).
- the handlers predicate renamed (Receive -> ReceiveNothing): RED "no handler reaches a Receive call; the derivation is broken, not the tree".
- service refusals (from the worktree): beyond-window "The lifecycle delivery deadline is 2s away, beyond the 1s writer window (the WorkflowResult tier)."; zero window "has no writer window (the WorkflowResult tier)"; TestReceiveAcceptsAContextWithNoDeadline and TestReceiveAcceptsADeadlineInsideTheWindow are the controls.
- the reviewer's attack "add a new writer command without a bounded window in a throwaway": not run by me; the guard's population is the live tree, so a registered leaf whose RunE reaches a reacher without the spelling is RED by construction.

NEXT: seam 2 as one commit over the ten files, on the ruling already given, starting now; its report states the partition and the mutations.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PART 3(b) FORWARD CORRECTION VERIFIED IN THE TREE, WITH ONE REPORT-ACCURACY FINDING. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

VERIFIED AND CORRECT:
- 8e444aa NAMES BOTH 648c469 AND 83c7803, so the superseded claims are corrected by a later commit and no history is rewritten. Checked mechanically.
- 83c7803 was GATED as ruled and recorded RED, rather than assumed. It was stacked and ungated, which is how it reached that point unseen.
- The derived guard exists and is derived: TestEveryLifecycleWriterCommandBoundsItsWindow, population from the LIVE COBRA TREE with writer-ness derived through the Receive reachers in internal/handlers, non-vacuity of two, RED by name when raw's WithTimeout becomes WithCancel. That is a derived population with a control, not a pair pinned by name.
- The full package runs were UNFILTERED this time, in handlers and cmd/pasture, which is the direct answer to the filtered-run lesson.

FINDING S-3, MINOR, AND IT IS ABOUT A CLAIM RATHER THAN ABOUT CODE. The report states: "Net foreign footprint against 13efa73 is the two window lines." THE TREE SAYS OTHERWISE. `git diff --stat 13efa73 8e444aa` shows FOUR files outside side B's core set, not two:
1. internal/lifecycle/backend/backend_test.go, one line — a granted window line. Claimed.
2. internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go, one line — the other granted window line. Claimed.
3. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_failuremode_test.go, ONE ADDED LINE — NOT CLAIMED.
4. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_writers_test.go, A NEW FILE OF 281 LINES — NOT CLAIMED.
BOTH UNCLAIMED FILES ARE ACCEPTED ON THEIR SUBSTANCE, and I checked each rather than taking the summary:
- the failuremode change is a LIST ENTRY in guardSweepOwned adding "hook_lifecycle_writers_test.go" to the sweep partition. NO PIN IS TOUCHED, which honours the rule that nobody edits the failuremode pins. It is also MECHANICALLY FORCED: a new test file in that package that is classified in neither partition would fail the partition guard. Correct, and it should have been named.
- the new writers_test.go IS THE DERIVED GUARD THE RULING REQUIRED, so it is implied by the ruling in the same way tracker.go is implied by the sink ruling. A new subject gets a new file under the one-file-per-subject rule.
WHY A MINOR IS WORTH RAISING HERE AT ALL: A FOOTPRINT CLAIM IS EXACTLY WHAT A REVIEWER RE-MEASURES. The ownership discipline of this slice rests on NAMED EQUALS TOUCHED, and a summary that says "two" where the diff says "four" fails that check on its face, even though every one of the four is defensible. The standing rule is that a count states its range and that no claim goes without evidence in the tree; a report is operator-facing text for the next reader.
REQUIRED BEFORE REVIEW: correct the footprint sentence to name all four and say why each is there. Nothing in the code changes.

- the reclaim call removed from the rebuild: RED TestEveryReadCommandReachesTheReclaim for ALL FOUR, each "<command>: exactly the cap (1024) of 1027 legacy orphans is reclaimed by one run; 1028 rows survive"; RED TestTheOrphansReportSaysWhatThisRunReclaimedAndWhatRemains; RED TestTheReclaimIsReachedOnlyFromTheRebuild.
- the reclaimed line dropped from the text renderer: RED TestTheOrphansReportSaysWhatThisRunReclaimedAndWhatRemains "five legacy orphans are older than any bound, so this run reclaims all five and says so" and RED TestOrphanCountIsZeroOnACleanStoreAndTrueAfterAbandonedInvocations at both readings.
- nil sink / nil clock: refused with the quoted headlines (tests pass; the refusal is the mechanism).
FULL RUNS (unfiltered): internal/lifecycle/..., internal/handlers, internal/engine/..., cmd/pasture: green except side A's literal. internal/tasks: green except the four tests below.

STOP 1 (posted 02:42, still open): cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans.go, Long and Short text only ("Count" -> "Reclaim and count"; "The command deletes nothing" replaced by the two-number statement). The patch is prepared at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1b/orphans-long.py and NOT applied.

STOP 2, NEW, AND IT IS THE REFUSAL DOING ITS JOB: internal/tasks/system_identity_internal_test.go (white-box, package tasks) calls the INTERNAL constructor openTaskTrackerWithOptions at SIX sites (lines 62, 88, 189, 193, 312, 365) with bare openTaskTrackerOptions literals. Each is a construction site nobody enumerated, and the ruled refusal now stops it: four tests RED with "open fixture tracker: validation error: The unified store has no diagnostics sink." (TestSystemIdentityPersistedNoncanonicalGenesisFailsClosed, TestSystemIdentityPersistedMissingGenesisFailsClosed, TestSystemIdentityConcurrentFirstOpenConverges, TestSystemIdentityCrashAfterGenesisCommitConvergesOnReopen). The public openers are untouched by this: every production site goes through them and they pass the defaults. THE FIX IS SIX SMALL EDITS IN THAT ONE FILE: each literal gains `clock: wallClock{}, diagnostics: io.Discard` (or the two fields through one local helper). The alternative, moving the refusal up into the public openers so bare internal literals pass, would make the internal constructor a construction site the refusal does not see, which is the exact hole the ruling closed; I do not recommend it.

ASK: add the two files, cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans.go (help text only) and internal/tasks/system_identity_internal_test.go (six literals, two fields each), making twelve. On the ruling I apply both, re-run the full packages, commit the twelve as ONE commit with the partition in the ownership paragraph, and gate it on an archive copy. Nothing is committed until then.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SEAM 2 BOUND: RAISED TO TWELVE. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05, under the principle the team lead accepted at 02:33Z. The lead may overrule; it is notified.

THE TEST IS WHETHER THE OVERAGE COMES FROM THE REQUIREMENTS OR FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION. Both files come from the requirements.
1. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans.go — its HELP TEXT says "The command deletes nothing". THE RULING MAKES THAT SENTENCE FALSE, because the command now reclaims inside its rebuild. Operator text is a truth claim, so shipping it unchanged means SHIPPING A FALSE STATEMENT TO THE USER ABOUT WHETHER A COMMAND DELETES THEIR DATA. That is the most consequential sentence in this leaf's operator surface. NOT DROPPABLE, and it must be PINNED like the two orphan numbers.
2. internal/tasks/system_identity_internal_test.go — the ruled NIL-SINK REFUSAL FIRES at its six bare internal-constructor literals, turning four tests RED with "The unified store has no diagnostics sink." NOT DROPPABLE without weakening the refusal, which is refused.

ITEM 2 IS THE COMPLETENESS MECHANISM WORKING, MEASURED, AND IT IS THE VINDICATION OF THE TEAM LEAD'S CORRECTION TO MY PROPOSAL. I proposed a sink with a PRODUCTION DEFAULT of stderr. The lead ruled a REQUIRED INPUT with NIL REFUSED, on the ground that a default would make an UNENUMERATED CONSTRUCTION SITE SILENTLY CORRECT.
THAT UNENUMERATED SITE EXISTS. It is a white-box internal test constructing the store directly, and no enumeration of the OPENERS would have found it, because it does not go through an opener. UNDER MY DEFAULT IT WOULD HAVE COMPILED, RUN, PASSED AND TOLD NOBODY. Under the refusal it turned four tests RED and named itself. The mechanism found the hole the mechanism was written for, on its first run, in a place neither of us predicted.

RULED: THE BOUND IS TWELVE. Side B applies both, names all twelve in the ownership paragraph marking which are its own set and which are widenings, and anything beyond twelve is a fresh stop-and-report.
ONE ADDITION, because item 1 is operator text: PIN THE CORRECTED HELP SENTENCE AND PROVE THE PIN BY MUTATION. A help line that says a command deletes nothing, on a command that deletes, is the exact defect class this epic treats as a review axis — and the correction must not be able to drift back silently.

THE PROOFS REPORTED, to be re-driven independently at review: the four-command real-binary reachability proof DERIVED FROM THE LIVE TREE, with exit 0, stderr EMPTY on success, EXACTLY 1024 OF 1027 legacy orphans reclaimed, THE REFERENCED BLOB SURVIVING, and RED FOR ALL FOUR COMMANDS WHEN THE CALL IS REMOVED; both orphans numbers pinned in TEXT AND JSON; the nil-sink and nil-clock refusals quoted; the opener enumeration derived by go/ast; and one failure line on the store's sink with silence on success.
NOTE FOR THE ORPHANS TEXT: 1024 of 1027 means THREE REMAIN. The command must report reclaimed-this-run AND remaining as two distinct, true numbers, and a reader must be able to tell them apart.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SEAM 2 BOUND: RAISED TO FOURTEEN, WITH ONE MANDATORY CONTROL. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. Same test as before, applied a third time; the team lead may overrule and is notified.

THE TWO FILES ARE cmd/pasture/testdata/help-golden/hook-lifecycle-orphans.txt (in full) and hook-lifecycle.txt (line 12, the orphans Short). THEY ARE THE ENCODED FORM OF THE VERY HELP TEXT THE RULING CHANGED. Their content is not a second decision; it is the SAME decision, stored as bytes. A golden that pins a sentence the ruling made false cannot stay as it is without the suite asserting the false sentence. REQUIREMENT-DRIVEN, so the bound moves. Side B did the right thing by stopping rather than recapturing quietly.

THE MANDATORY CONTROL, AND IT IS THE WHOLE RISK OF THIS STEP: A GOLDEN RECAPTURE IS WHERE A PIN GOES BLIND. The update path is ONE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, and it rewrites the file to whatever the binary currently prints. IF ANY UNINTENDED CHANGE HAS CREPT INTO THE HELP OUTPUT, THE RECAPTURE ABSORBS IT SILENTLY AND THE TEST GOES GREEN ASSERTING THE NEW BYTES. The pin survives; its power does not. That is the pin-that-loosens shape in its native habitat, and a recapture is the one operation that can perform it without anyone editing an assertion.
SO: AFTER THE RECAPTURE, READ THE GOLDEN DIFF AND REPORT IT. State the exact lines that changed and CONFIRM THAT EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE DELETION-CLAIM CHANGE. If any other byte moved, that is a FINDING, not a recapture — stop and report it. Re-run WITHOUT the variable afterwards, as side B already plans, so the committed goldens are proved to match the binary.

RULED: THE BOUND IS FOURTEEN. One commit, all fourteen named in the ownership paragraph with own-set and widenings marked, the golden diff reported, the partition updated, then the archive gate. ANYTHING BEYOND FOURTEEN IS A FRESH STOP-AND-REPORT.

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING, AND WHY IT IS NOT SCOPE CREEP: every overage in this leaf has come from ONE DECISION — that the reclaim runs inside the read commands — PROPAGATING THROUGH EVERY SURFACE THAT DESCRIBES OR CONSTRUCTS THAT BEHAVIOUR: the tracker that must hold a sink, the white-box test that constructs it directly, the help text that claims the command deletes nothing, and now the goldens that store that claim as bytes. THE FILE COUNT IS MEASURING THE REACH OF THE DECISION, NOT THE APPETITE OF THE IMPLEMENTATION. Each stop has stated the count before writing, which is exactly what the bound was for.

THE REVIEWER'S ATTACK LIST GAINS: read the golden DIFF and require it contains ONLY the deletion-claim change, because an unintended byte absorbed by a recapture is invisible afterwards; then REVERT the goldens and require RED, proving they still read the help output at all.

The parser call would still be correct; the vocabularies would have parted. The worker's mutation proves it — renaming ingress.FreeTextRule turns the guard RED.
THREE LINES, IN THE FILE IT ALREADY OWNS, WITH A NAMED AND PERFORMABLE MUTATION. It is granted.
AND THE WAY IT WAS RAISED IS THE POINT: the worker went BEYOND THE LETTER of its order, in the DIRECTION OF THE ORDER'S PURPOSE, and FLAGGED IT FOR A RULING INSTEAD OF SLIDING IT IN. author: David Huu Pham
text:
TEAM-LEAD RULING ON REVIEW FINDING iv6zqh (2026-09-05, S1 round 1 IMPORTANT). The finding is correct and it SUPERSEDES part 1 of my L11 ruling where that part said "DEFAULT 0; legacy rows are OLDER THAN ANY BOUND". A blob written by a pre-v8 binary has no stamp, and "0 is older than any bound" gives an in-flight old-binary writer no grace at the upgrade instant. Two rules replace it:
1. THE MIGRATION STAMPS EVERY PRE-EXISTING ROW WITH THE MIGRATION INSTANT. The ALTER keeps a constant DEFAULT 0 (SQLite requires a constant), then one UPDATE in the same migration transaction sets written_at = the migration instant for every existing row. The first reclaim of legacy orphans therefore waits one writer window after the upgrade, the same grace a new writer gets. The user's 14,490 legacy orphans become eligible 30 s after the upgrade, not at once.
2. written_at = 0 MEANS UNKNOWN AND IS NEVER ELIGIBLE. A row an old binary inserts AFTER the migration (during the mixed-binary window) receives the column default 0 and is never reclaimed by this rule; a later re-delivery of the same body by the new binary refreshes the stamp through the existing max() update and makes it eligible in due course. A small, bounded, rare leak is accepted over a manufactured corruption; state that trade in the source beside the predicate.
CONSEQUENCES, all in one fix commit: the eligibility predicate gains "AND written_at > 0"; TestMigrateV7ToV8AddsWrittenAtAndLeavesLegacyRowsAtZero is renamed and re-pointed to assert the migration-instant stamp; the AGENTS.md sentence "Legacy blobs stamped 0 by the migration are older than any bound and drain at the cap per read command" is corrected to the two rules above; the reclaim doc comment states the two-clock note and the unknown-age rule.
MUTATIONS REQUIRED: (a) the reviewer's: on a v7 store with one unstamped blob, the first v8 read command reclaims nothing (RED when the migration stamps 0 again); (b) a row with written_at 0 inserted after the migration is never reclaimed at any age (RED when the "> 0" clause is dropped); (c) a legacy row stamped with the migration instant IS reclaimed once the window has elapsed, proven with the scripted clock (RED if the UPDATE is dropped, because then every legacy row is 0 and never drains, which is the opposite failure).
Recorded as a deviation on the IMPL_PLAN. The stale "DEFAULT 0 = older than any bound" text in my earlier comments is superseded by this comment.

author: David Huu Pham
text: SECTION 14 DEVIATION ADDENDUM (team lead, 2026-09-05, S1-L11, from review finding iv6zqh): the v8 migration stamps pre-existing blobs with the MIGRATION INSTANT (not 0), and written_at = 0 means unknown age and is never eligible for reclaim. Reason: an in-flight old-binary writer at the upgrade instant must get the same grace as a new writer; a rare bounded leak of mixed-window rows is accepted over manufactured corruption. Full ruling on s6k7mg.

REVIEW ROUND 1: REVISE, 0 BLOCKER / 1 IMPORTANT / 4 MINOR. supervisor-s1 analysis, 2026-09-05. NO FIX WAS APPLIED THIS ROUND, so nothing closes on it.

WHAT HELD, recorded because a clean result is evidence only when it is stated: byte-identity on ALL TWELVE enabled events, also on a v7 store and also with a capture directory set; six gates green on the reviewer's OWN archive copy (74 packages, 0 fail, 0 races, drift 0); SEVENTY-TWO MUTATIONS RE-DRIVEN AT THE DEFECT SITE, including the registration-side re-drive, the reclaim-call removal RED on all four commands, a new writer command without a bounded window RED with no test edit, the help revert, the golden revert, and the raised schema ceiling still passing; a cancellation-bounded context ACCEPTED and the S0 proofs untouched; ownership named equals touched on ALL TWENTY-FIVE commits; the golden diff holding only the deletion-claim change; the foreign footprint back to one Window line plus partition entries.

THE IMPORTANT (aura-plugins-iv6zqh) IS A REAL DEFECT AND THE REVIEWER WAS RIGHT TO SURFACE IT RATHER THAN CHOOSE. It contradicts a ruled mechanism, so it goes to the team lead.
THE DEFECT: `written_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` makes every pre-existing blob read as INFINITELY OLD. So THE FIRST v8 READ COMMAND RECLAIMS A BLOB WRITTEN MOMENTS EARLIER BY A PRE-v8 BINARY, with NO GRACE PERIOD, and the old writer's late journal append then hits the foreign-key failure that side B's own mutation (i) already pins. Measured with both built binaries: a v7 store, an unstamped blob, then `hook lifecycle orphans` printed "reclaimed by this run: 1 / remaining: 0".
THE ROOT OF IT, stated plainly: DEFAULT 0 CONFLATES TWO DIFFERENT FACTS — "written before v8" and "written long ago". They diverge in exactly one case, and it is the case an upgrade creates: an OLD BINARY WRITING NEAR THE MIGRATION INSTANT. The ruling's justification was that the user's 14,490 orphans are legacy rows, which is TRUE and remains true; the ruling simply did not consider a writer still running across the upgrade.
THE REVIEWER'S FIX IS RIGHT BUT INCOMPLETE, AND THE GAP MATTERS: stamping existing rows with THE MIGRATION INSTANT protects every blob written BEFORE the migration, and the legacy orphans still drain, thirty seconds later than before. IT DOES NOT PROTECT A BLOB WRITTEN AFTER THE MIGRATION BY A BINARY THAT DOES NOT STAMP — a long-running daemon or an older installed binary on the same store. Such a row lands with written_at = 0 again and is reclaimable at once.
SUPERVISOR RECOMMENDATION, BOTH HALVES TOGETHER:
1. THE MIGRATION STAMPS EXISTING ROWS WITH THE MIGRATION INSTANT, so legacy orphans drain one window after the upgrade rather than instantly.
2. THE RECLAIM REFUSES ANY ROW WHOSE written_at IS 0. After part 1, a zero can only mean A POST-MIGRATION WRITER THAT DID NOT STAMP, whose age is therefore UNKNOWN — and an unknown age must never satisfy an age bound. This is the same principle the slice already applied to the diagnostics sink: A MISSING VALUE IS REFUSED, NOT DEFAULTED.
TOGETHER THEY CLOSE BOTH CASES AND COST NOTHING THE LEAF NEEDS: the 14,490 legacy orphans still drain at the cap, one window later.
MUTATIONS TO REQUIRE: run the migration and show a pre-existing row is NOT reclaimed within the window and IS reclaimed after it; insert a row with written_at = 0 AFTER the migration and show it is NEVER reclaimed; and re-drive the reviewer's own measured case with both binaries and require the reclaim to refuse.
IF THE RULING STANDS UNCHANGED, THE AGENTS.md SENTENCE MUST CHANGE, because it currently promises that legacy blobs stamped 0 drain at the cap while the measured behaviour is that a moments-old blob is destroyed. One of the two must give.

THE FOUR MINORS ARE MINE TO ROUTE AND ALL FOUR MUST REACH ZERO; no severity is deferrable in this slice.
- n2ufvp, operator text: OrphanPayloadNote prints "the pasture store.Every read command" with a MISSING SPACE, in text AND JSON, WHILE THE WORDING PIN STAYS GREEN. The defect is not the space; it is that THE PIN DOES NOT READ THE JOIN. Fix the text and TIGHTEN THE PIN so the mutation that produced this reads RED.
- jw6w0z, internal references: process words in SIX shipped test comments and FIVE side-B commit messages. Same class as finding S-1, which side A corrected on its own side; side B's half was never swept. The comments are fixed in place. THE COMMIT MESSAGES ARE NOT AMENDED — a later commit NAMES them, as the standing rule requires and as side A already did.
- udrqwz, count accuracy: the free-text exemption is REPORTED as seven digests and the committed list holds SIX. Same class as finding S-3. A number that can be enumerated must be enumerated and must match the tree.
- vz7aah, coverage claim: the opener guard says it "passes" while it checks CLOSURE REACH, and a contrived exported opener STAYS GREEN. The runtime nil-sink refusal catches it, so the product is safe; THE GUARD'S CLAIM IS FALSE. Either derive the population properly or CORRECT THE CLAIM to what it actually checks. A guard that overstates its reach stops the next reader looking.

ROUTING: ONE FIX ROUND covering all five, on the integration branch, by a FRESH worker, once the team lead rules the IMPORTANT. Bundling avoids two review rounds for one set of findings.

WHAT CHANGED (8 files, ownership named == touched via git show --stat, porcelain empty):
1. internal/audit/migrate_v7_v8.go: the ALTER keeps the constant DEFAULT 0; ONE UPDATE in the same transaction sets written_at = the migration instant (the same unix-ns value recorded as applied_at of version 8) on every pre-existing row; the step reads the table back and REFUSES to record version 8 while any row still carries 0 (requireNoUnstampedBlob). Doc states the two-facts conflation and the unknown-age rule.
2. internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go: the one reclaim statement gains "AND b.written_at > 0"; the doc beside the predicate states 0 = UNKNOWN, never eligible, and the accepted trade (small, bounded, rare leak over a manufactured corruption; the Put max() refresh lifts it in due course).
3. internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim.go: doc states the unknown-age rule and the two-clock note (which decision reads which clock).
4. AGENTS.md: the sentence "Legacy blobs stamped 0 by the migration are older than any bound and drain at the cap per read command" is REPLACED by the two rules.
5. internal/audit/migrate_v7_v8_test.go: TestMigrateV7ToV8AddsWrittenAtAndLeavesLegacyRowsAtZero RENAMED to TestMigrateV7ToV8StampsEveryPreExistingBlobWithTheMigrationInstant and re-pointed (stamp == applied_at of version 8, inside the run's [before, after]); new TestMigrateV7ToV8RefusesToRecordTheVersionWhileAPreExistingBlobIsUnstamped drives the guard directly.
6. internal/lifecycle/projection/reclaim_test.go: the legacy-0 assertions re-pointed (unstamped orphan NEVER reclaimed; unstamped named never reclaimed); the redelivered-body control uses an old KNOWN stamp and a second half shows the max() refresh lifting an unstamped orphan; NEW TestAnUnstampedBlobIsNeverReclaimedAtAnyAge (kept ten years past the window; control at written_at 1 reclaimed); NEW TestAPreExistingBlobIsReclaimedOnlyOneWindowAfterTheUpgrade (a v7-shaped store upgraded through tasks.OpenTaskTracker, scripted clock inside the window keeps it, one past the window reclaims it); the one-statement pin requires "b.written_at > 0".
7. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_orphans_test.go: seedLegacyOrphans stamps ONE HOUR in the past (a KNOWN instant; the state a legacy orphan is in one window after the upgrade) instead of 0; NEW TestTheFirstReadCommandAfterTheUpgradeReclaimsNothingWrittenBeforeIt through the BUILT BINARY: a store at version 7 (the column and the version-8 row removed from a store this build made; the older build itself is not run, the doc says so) with an unstamped blob; `hook lifecycle orphans` upgrades and prints "orphan payload blobs reclaimed by this run: 0" and "orphan payload blobs remaining: 1"; the stamp read back == applied_at of version 8; then a row inserted unstamped AFTER the upgrade: JSON reclaimed 0, remaining 2.
8. internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal_test.go: comment corrected (an unstamped row would leak, not drain).

MUTATIONS on an archive copy of d077eca (/home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1-fix1/mutations-fix1-d077eca.log), each quoting the message:
M1 the migration stamps 0 again (UPDATE + stamp guard removed): RED TestMigrateV7ToV8StampsEveryPreExistingBlobWithTheMigrationInstant "the referenced pre-existing blob carries 0 after the upgrade; every pre-existing row must carry the migration instant, or the first read command would treat a moments-old blob as older than any bound"; RED TestAPreExistingBlobIsReclaimedOnlyOneWindowAfterTheUpgrade "a pre-existing blob carries 0 after the upgrade; the migration must stamp it with the migration instant"; RED (built binary) TestTheFirstReadCommandAfterTheUpgradeReclaimsNothingWrittenBeforeIt "the pre-existing blob must not carry 0 after the upgrade" and "the pre-existing blob carries exactly the migration instant the upgrade recorded".
M2 the "AND b.written_at > 0" clause dropped: RED TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement "the one statement refuses an unknown age: a blob at written_at 0 is never eligible"; RED TestAnUnstampedBlobIsNeverReclaimedAtAnyAge "a blob at written_at 0 is never reclaimed, even ten years past the window: 0 means the age is unknown, and an unknown age never satisfies an age bound"; RED TestReclaimingRebuildReclaimsOnlyUnnamedBlobsOlderThanTheWindow "an unnamed blob at written_at 0 has an UNKNOWN age and is NEVER reclaimed: an unknown age must not satisfy an age bound"; RED (built binary) "a row inserted after the upgrade with no stamp has an unknown age and is never reclaimed; the migration-instant row is still inside the window" and "both rows remain and both are counted as orphans".
M3 the UPDATE dropped, the guard kept: the migration REFUSES, RED "verify lifecycle v8 payload blob stamps: 2 pre-existing payload blobs still carry written_at 0 after the upgrade statements ran; every pre-existing row must carry the migration instant" (two audit tests) and RED TestAPreExistingBlobIsReclaimedOnlyOneWindowAfterTheUpgrade "the production opener must upgrade the version 7 store".

author: David Huu Pham
text:
TWO-BINARY RE-DRIVE DONE (worker-s1-fix1), the finding's own case, with binaries built from archive copies of d3edb79 (old) and 4e34e36 (new; the fix head), sqlite3 3.51.2 from the dev shell, log at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1-fix1/twobin:
1. OLD binary bootstrapped the store (`task create`): schema version 7; lifecycle_payload_blobs columns digest, body, byte_count (no stamp).
2. OLD binary ran one enabled SessionStart hook (claude-code 2.1.222, the committed fixture): rc 0, 1 blob.
3. A second blob inserted through the v7 shape (digest, body, byte_count), standing for the old writer between its two writes: 2 blobs.
4. Moments later the NEW binary ran `hook lifecycle orphans`: it upgraded the store to version 8 and printed "orphan payload blobs reclaimed by this run: 0" / "orphan payload blobs remaining: 1"; stderr EMPTY; both blobs now carry written_at 1788580491009624161 == applied_at of version 8; 2 blobs remain. THE RECLAIM REFUSED. (At 3078523 the same steps printed "reclaimed by this run: 1 / remaining: 0", the measured defect; M4 in the mutation log reproduces that through the test with both halves removed.)
5. One observation for the record, not a change to the fix: the OLD binary, run again on the upgraded store, REFUSES at open with the existing newer-schema rejection ("This audit database was written by a newer pasture (version 8) than this build supports (version 7)"), exit continue, no write. So an UNSTAMPED row after the upgrade cannot come from an old binary that opens the store after the upgrade; it can only come from an old process that opened the store BEFORE the upgrade and reached its blob write AFTER it (open -> version check -> ... -> Put), a narrower window than "a long-running daemon or an older installed binary". Rule 2 (0 = unknown, never eligible) still covers exactly that window and costs nothing; both halves stand as ruled.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FIX APPLIED by worker-s1-fix1, commit 4e34e36 on slice/rp2tju-s1 (1 file, internal/tasks/tracker_test.go; ownership named == touched; porcelain empty). I chose DERIVE, so the claim becomes true, and the doc also names the covering mechanism for what the guard does not read.
THE GUARD NOW CHECKS: for every exported function returning protocol.TaskTracker, walk the same-package closure; require at least one call to openTaskTrackerWithOptions in it; for EVERY such call require the options argument to be ROOTED in productionOpenDefaults(): the call itself, or a local whose declaration in the enclosing function is assigned from that call (:= or var). A composite literal is not rooted, whatever it reaches. Separately, productionOpenDefaults itself must name os.Stderr and wallClock{} in its body. The doc states what it visits, what it does not read (what an OpenTaskTrackerOption does to the value AFTER rooting, e.g. a nil sink; that is caught at runtime by the refusal in openTaskTrackerWithOptions, pinned by TestTheStoreRefusesANilDiagnosticSinkAndANilClock), non-vacuity (>= 2 openers derived), and the mutations.
MUTATIONS on an archive copy of 4e34e36, NO test edit, each RED naming the opener (log /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s1-fix1/mutations-fix245-4e34e36.log):
M1 OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions starts from openTaskTrackerOptions{} -> RED "production opener OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions passes openTaskTrackerWithOptions an options value that is not rooted in productionOpenDefaults() (in OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions): it must pass the call itself or a local assigned from it, or the opener carries neither the process stderr nor the wall clock".
M2 THE REVIEWER'S CASE, a new exported OpenTaskTrackerBare passing openTaskTrackerOptions{timeouts: productionOpenDefaults().timeouts} -> RED "production opener OpenTaskTrackerBare passes openTaskTrackerWithOptions an options value that is not rooted in productionOpenDefaults() (in OpenTaskTrackerBare): ..." author: David Huu Pham
text: STANDING CONSTRAINT ADDITION (team lead, 2026-09-05, from S1): A MOVED CEILING FALSIFIES CLAIMS AT A DISTANCE. When a change moves a ceiling or a closed set (a schema version, an enum arm count, a cap, a pinned version), every claim about it elsewhere becomes suspect: literals in tests, sentences in docs and help text, package comments, AGENTS.md. Measured three times in S1 with three different detectors (fold gate: a schema literal; reviewer: an AGENTS.md sentence; worker side report: a package doc). Rule: the commit that moves the ceiling sweeps for claims about it and states each surviving claim as a mechanism that reads the ceiling, never as a hand-maintained number. Second addition: an ENUMERATION that decides a blast radius is derived like a guard's population (transitive callers, not direct ones). Third: a filtered test run says nothing about the packages it skipped; only the full-suite archive-copy gate counts.

SUPERVISOR GATE ON 0aead71: FIVE GREEN, ONE RED, AND THE RED IS A LOAD-INDUCED FLAKE IN A PRE-EXISTING TEST. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

THE RUN, on an archive copy from inside the copy: build rc=0; vet rc=0; make generate rc=0 with 172 log lines and DRIFT 0; nix flake check rc=0; gofmt 0 files with the negative control listing the probe. TEST-RACE rc=1: ok=73, fail=3 lines, races 0.
THE FAILURE: TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets, in internal/engine, at subworkflows_test.go:2582 — "mark ... pending updated 0 rows, want 1; the row is no longer marked as running, so it finished instead of being interrupted and recovery would have nothing to do". internal/audit itself was ok.

I RE-RAN internal/engine ALONE ON THE SAME ARCHIVE COPY: ok, 38.961s. GREEN. The full-suite run took 71.627s for that package, nearly twice as long, which is the signature of contention rather than of a defect.
THE CAUSE IS CONCURRENCY BETWEEN GATES, NOT THE COMMIT. Three full race suites were running on this machine at once — the supervisor's, the team lead's and the reviewer's, all on the same head. The test tries to INTERRUPT A RUNNING WORKFLOW and then assert that recovery has something to do. Under load THE WORKFLOW FINISHED BEFORE THE TEST COULD MARK IT, so the test had nothing left to interrupt.

I MUST CORRECT SOMETHING I WROTE. I told the reviewer and the team lead that, since 4e34e36 was green and this commit changes only a comment, "ANY DIFFERENCE COULD ONLY COME FROM THAT COMMENT". THAT WAS WRONG AS STATED. It omitted the whole class of load- and timing-dependent failures, and the very next run produced one. A prediction that names only one possible cause invites the reader to accept the first explanation that fits, which is exactly the reasoning error this slice keeps guarding against elsewhere. THE CORRECT STATEMENT WOULD HAVE BEEN: a difference comes from the commit, from the environment, or from a test that is not deterministic — and the way to tell them apart is to RE-RUN THE FAILING PACKAGE ALONE, which is what settled it.

FINDING S-5, ROUTED OUT OF S1, NOT BLOCKING IT. TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets DEPENDS ON WINNING A RACE against a workflow completing. That is a FIXED-TIMING DEPENDENCE, which the standing constraints forbid: a proof waits on a CONDITION, and a clock may only be a failure ceiling. Under enough load the test loses the race and reports a failure that says nothing about the product.
IT IS PRE-EXISTING AND NOT S1's: internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go is untouched by this slice, on both sides. A slice cleans up what it wrote, so this goes to a follow-up like the other pre-existing items, and it should be filed where the DBOS test-performance work lives.
IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN PACKAGE: it makes ANY green on this repository weaker under parallel gating, and this team now runs three concurrent gates as a matter of course. A flake that only appears under load is a flake that appears exactly when several people are checking the same claim at once.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROUND: 0aead71 IS GATE-GREEN ON EVERY DETERMINISTIC AXIS — build, vet, generate with drift 0, flake, gofmt with its control — and its one RED is reproduced as an environmental flake and cleared by an isolated re-run. THE HEAD STANDS. The reviewer runs its own gate as ordered; if it meets the same failure, THIS IS THE EXPLANATION AND THE REMEDY: re-run internal/engine alone before reporting it as a finding.
PRACTICAL NOTE FOR THE TEAM: three simultaneous full race suites on one machine is enough to tip this test. Stagger them, or accept that an isolated re-run is part of reading the result.

text: LEAD GATE on 0aead71 RESOLVED (2026-09-05 ~04:25Z): the one red was TestEngineShutdown_ReturnsNilWhenTheRuntimeStopsInsideItsBudget (internal/engine, 'GetResult after 30s ... database is locked (SQLITE_BUSY)'), run while three full race suites shared the machine (load average 23; engine package 79 s against 49-53 s in the two earlier green lead gates; 47 lock-wait lines). Isolated re-run of internal/engine on the SAME archive copy: ok 35.9 s, budget ok 3.4 s. The other five gates were green (drift 0, gofmt 0, control listed). author: David Huu Pham
text:
S-4 VERIFIED, AND THE FLAKE DIAGNOSIS IS NOW CONFIRMED BY TWO RUNS ON ONE SHA. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05.

TWO INDEPENDENT SIX-GATE RUNS ON THE SAME COMMIT 0aead71 DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE:
- the fix worker's run: test-race ok=74, fail=0, race=0. GREEN.
- the supervisor's run: test-race ok=73, fail=3 lines, race=0, failing on TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets.
SAME SHA, SAME GATE, SAME MACHINE, DIFFERENT RESULT. A defect cannot be present in one run of a commit and absent in another; NON-DETERMINISM CAN. Together with the isolated re-run of internal/engine (GREEN at 38.9s against 71.6s under load), the cause is settled: THREE CONCURRENT FULL RACE SUITES, and a test that must WIN A RACE against a workflow completing. The product is not implicated.
THIS IS WHY A GREEN IS A CLAIM AND NOT A FACT UNTIL SOMEONE SAYS HOW IT WAS OBTAINED. Had only the worker's run existed, we would have had a green nobody could reproduce; had only mine existed, we would have chased a defect that is not there.

FINDING S-5 STANDS AND IS ROUTED OUT OF S1: internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go depends on winning a race against a workflow completing, which is the FIXED-TIMING DEPENDENCE the standing constraints forbid. It is untouched by this slice on both sides, so it is PRE-EXISTING and belongs with the DBOS test-performance work.

S-4 IS VERIFIED AND IT IS BETTER THAN WHAT WAS ASKED FOR. The migration list gains the v7 -> v8 line, and "This binary tops out at v7" is replaced by A MECHANISM: the ceiling IS MaxKnownSchemaVersion and the steps ARE migrationSteps(). SO THE SENTENCE CANNOT GO STALE AGAIN — S3's v9 will not falsify it.
THE CLAIM THAT THE TWO CANNOT DISAGREE SILENTLY IS ITSELF DEFENDED, which is what I asked the reviewer to check: TestMigrate_FreshDB_LandsAtMaxKnownVersion requires a fresh Migrate to land at the constant, so a table ending BELOW it fails, and Migrate refuses a table with a gap. The worker also checked whether any test reads the prose list or the removed sentence — a grep for "tops out" over the tests returns NO HIT — so nothing depended on the text that was removed. That is the right pair of questions for a doc change: what did the old text promise, and what enforces the new promise.
THE 173-VERSUS-172 GENERATE LOG LINE IS EXPLAINED, NOT IGNORED: the extra line is a nix eval-cache "database is busy (ignored)" warning from a CONCURRENT NIX PROCESS, not generate output. Drift is 0. A one-line difference in a log count is exactly the kind of small anomaly that is usually waved through, and it was chased instead.

ONE MORE CEILING CLAIM IN THE SAME FILE, REPORTED AND NOT EDITED, AND THE ROUTING IS CORRECT. migrate.go:78-79 documents MaxKnownSchemaVersion as "Bumped by S2 (->3, landed) and S4 (->4, landed)". It is STALE SINCE v5 and it carries PROCESS WORDS. IT WAS ALREADY FALSE BEFORE THIS BRANCH EXISTED, so this branch did not falsify it and it goes to the sweep, exactly as the fourteen other pre-existing sites did. A SLICE CLEANS UP WHAT IT WROTE.
IT IS RECORDED HERE WITH ITS FILE AND LINES SO THE SWEEP CANNOT LOSE IT, because it now sits TWO LINES FROM A SENTENCE THIS SLICE JUST CORRECTED, and the next reader of that file will meet both. It is also a FIFTH instance of the ceiling class and a further instance of the process-word class in a shipped file.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
INTERIM EVIDENCE 1 of 2 (reviewer-s1-r2, round 2 on integration head 0aead71). Posted so an interruption loses nothing. Verdict follows in the final comment.

HEAD VERIFIED: worktree rp2tju-s1--integration at 0aead71 on slice/rp2tju-s1, porcelain empty, 31 commits over d3edb79; 3078523 is an ancestor and the six commits after it chain d077eca -> aca3398 -> 8a2b4cd -> 86f767c -> 4e34e36 -> 0aead71 with no rewrite (every round-1 SHA cited on cv79sf still resolves).

SIX GATES on MY OWN archive copy of 0aead71 (git archive + git init + remote, run from inside the copy, CGO_ENABLED=1 passed inside with env): build rc=0; vet rc=0; go test -race -count=1 ./... rc=0 with 74 packages ok, 0 FAIL, 0 DATA RACE, 9 no-test-files; make generate rc=0, 172 log lines, drift 0; nix flake check --no-build rc=0; gofmt -l 0 .go files with the planted probe listed by the negative control (1). Matches the lead's gate on 4e34e36.

BYTE-IDENTITY PROOF, binaries built from my archive copies of d3edb79 and 0aead71, run on the 12 enabled events (Claude 8 at 2.1.222, Codex 2 at 0.146.0, OpenCode 2 at 1.18.10; OpenCode stdin built as the generated plugin builds it, JSON.stringify of the callback value and of {input, output:{args}}), each on a fresh store bootstrapped by the same binary (task create), fixture bytes on stdin, PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR unset: exit code, stdout bytes and stderr bytes IDENTICAL on all 12 (exit 0, stderr empty; stdout empty on the non-blocking rows, {"decision":"proceed"} on the blocking Claude rows and tool.execute.before, {} on Codex SessionStart, {"continue":true} on Codex PreToolUse). UPGRADE CASE, store bootstrapped by the d3edb79 binary (schema v7) and the hook run by the 0aead71 binary: identical on all 12. CAPTURE DIR SET (absolute, outside any repository): exit and stdout identical to base on all 12, stderr exactly ONE line "pasture: capture mode is recording this session to <dir>", one file <harness>_<snake_event>_<version>.1.json per event and its bytes equal the fixture bytes (cmp). RELATIVE capture dir: exit and stdout identical, one warning line, nothing captured. PASS.

THE FIVE FIX RE-DRIVES, each on my own copy, each run naming its test, message text quoted:
1. iv6zqh. (a) Migration stamps 0 again (UPDATE made a no-op, guard removed) -> RED TestMigrateV7ToV8StampsEveryPreExistingBlobWithTheMigrationInstant "the referenced pre-existing blob carries 0 after the upgrade; every pre-existing row must carry the migration instant, or the first read command would treat a moments-old blob as older than any bound"; RED TestAPreExistingBlobIsReclaimedOnlyOneWindowAfterTheUpgrade; RED (built binary) TestTheFirstReadCommandAfterTheUpgradeReclaimsNothingWrittenBeforeIt "the pre-existing blob must not carry 0 after the upgrade". (b) "AND b.written_at > 0" dropped -> RED TestTheReclaimIsOneBoundedStatement "the one statement refuses an unknown age", RED TestAnUnstampedBlobIsNeverReclaimedAtAnyAge "a blob at written_at 0 is never reclaimed, even ten years past the window", RED TestReclaimingRebuildReclaimsOnlyUnnamedBlobsOlderThanTheWindow, RED the built-binary case. (c) BOTH halves removed (the round-1 measured defect as it was) -> RED through the built binary. (d) THE OVER-PROTECTION ATTACK, nothing ever eligible (predicate written_at > MaxInt64-1) -> RED TestAPreExistingBlobIsReclaimedOnlyOneWindowAfterTheUpgrade at the second reclaim, RED the control "a blob at written_at 1, the smallest KNOWN stamp, is reclaimed by the same run", RED TestEveryReadCommandReachesTheReclaim on all four commands and the orphans report test: a fix that protects everything is caught. Two-binary case re-driven inside the byte-identity run: the d3edb79 store, then the 0aead71 binary's first hook on it, identical bytes; the built-binary test reconstructs the v7 shape and prints "reclaimed by this run: 0 / remaining: 1" then, with an unstamped row inserted AFTER the upgrade, "reclaimed 0 / remaining 2". AGENTS.md now states the two rules; the sentence about blobs stamped 0 draining at the cap is gone; I read the new paragraph against the mechanism and it is true of it (0 after the upgrade can only come from an older build writing to the upgraded store; legacy orphans drain one window later at the cap).
2. n2ufvp. The space removed again -> RED TestOrphanCountWordingSaysWhatItIsThatItIsExpectedAndWhatALargeNumberMeans at the join pin AND at the boundary sweep, which names the glued bytes ".E". The pin reads the join now.
3. jw6w0z. Tree-wide sweep, mine: added lines of git diff d3edb79..0aead71 over every shipped file type and the whole head tree for tracker ids, SLICE-/PROPOSAL- names, "review wave", "slice report", "the fold", "this slice", "this side", "the side's file set", "orphan-reclaim leaf": NO hit in any shipped file added by this branch ("registered leaf" is the cobra tree, "slice" is a Go slice, "epoch" is the product's own command; the only hits in the tree are the protocol product's own skill docs under skills/, the ruled domain vocabulary). COMMIT MESSAGES, all 31 swept and mapped to SHAs: process words remain ONLY in d1feeb0, 06df190, 3710f49, d9a2382, 53fb6ee (named and restated by 8a2b4cd) and f7556a7, 73ea25b (named and restated by a84e6c1); no other message carries the class; no history was rewritten.
4. udrqwz. Counted against the tree: the map freeTextExemptDigests holds SIX rows (four Claude, one Codex, one OpenCode); the comment beside it states SIX, how it is counted (len of the map; the corpus walk keeps it from being smaller, the resolve loop from being larger) and how the number moves. Matches.
5. vz7aah. The fix DERIVES. My contrived exported opener OpenTaskTrackerBare passing openTaskTrackerOptions{timeouts: productionOpenDefaults().timeouts} (the round-1 case that stayed green) -> RED "production opener OpenTaskTrackerBare passes openTaskTrackerWithOptions an options value that is not rooted in productionOpenDefaults()". The options opener started from a fresh literal -> RED naming OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions. os.Stderr removed from the defaults -> RED "productionOpenDefaults never names os.Stderr". EXTRA: the unexported registered opener openTaskTrackerImpl (the implementation behind protocol.OpenTaskTracker) given an unrooted literal -> RED too, because it sits in the exported opener's closure; so the one production site the derivation does not name directly is still covered.
S-4 (0aead71). The doc's claim attacked: MaxKnownSchemaVersion raised to 9 with the table unchanged -> RED TestMigrate_FreshDB_LandsAtMaxKnownVersion "schema version after Migrate = 8, want 9" and RED TestMigrate_RoundTrip_OpenMigrateReopen "audit_schema_meta row count after reopen = 7, want 8"; the list in the doc ends at v7 -> v8 and matches migrationSteps(); the gap refusal is in Migrate. The claim is true of the pins it names.

Batch 2 (side A) and batch 3 (L11 and guards) follow in interim evidence 2.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
INTERIM EVIDENCE 2 of 2 (reviewer-s1-r2, round 2 on 0aead71). Side-A attacks, the L11 and guard attacks, and the round-1 confirmations, each on my own archive copies with NO edit to the guard under test unless marked control; every run named its test; message text quoted.

SIDE A. L1: a NEW fixture copying a LISTED digest at an UNLISTED path with no clearance (zz_copy_2_1_222.json + the copied sidecar) -> RED TestLegacyExemptionListEqualsCommittedSidecarsWithoutClearance "committed sidecar for internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/testdata/fixtures/zz_copy_2_1_222.json has no clearance and is not on the legacy exemption list; either add a clearance path to the sidecar or, if it predates the clearance field, add its path and digest", and RED the closed 2.1.222 inventory in ingress/claude; the activation corpus tests stay green because their population is the declared corpus, which is not the guard that answers this question. Exemption list emptied -> RED "the legacy exemption list is empty while committed sidecars without a clearance still exist". TWO LISTS: the clearance exemption (12 entries keyed on committed path AND declared digest; its comment states 14 shaped sidecars, 12 reaching the exemption, 11 distinct payloads and why) and the free-text exemption (6 digest keys; its comment states the population, the counting rule and SIX): different populations, different questions, each says so beside itself, neither became the other. SCHEMA CEILING: MaxKnownSchemaVersion raised 8 -> 9 with the table unchanged -> TestLifecycleListStandardExitCategories/storage STILL PASSES; the constant itself in place of +1 -> RED "An error is expected but got nil". L10 REGISTRATION RE-DRIVE, independent, on the GENERATED file, NO test edit: a NEW event "Probe" registered with a free-text identity -> RED TestEveryProfileRowIsTiedToOneRegistrationRow "the registration manifests declare 88 events and the lifecycle profiles declare 87 rows; every event is described by exactly one row on each side"; FieldPrompt lifted into the UserPromptSubmit registration row -> RED "registration row claude-code/UserPromptSubmit declares 2 identities but its profile row declares 1; a registration may not lift a field into an L2 that the profile does not declare as correlation". GENERATOR: the Codex capture table emptied -> go generate EXITS 1 "codex_targets.go declares no capture proof arm at all; a harness file must declare at least one arm of each kind, so either the table is empty or the source walk no longer matches its rows, and an empty generation would pass every range check over nothing" and the package RED (TestGeneratedProofConstantsMirrorTheDeclarationTablesBothWays "2 source arm(s) have no mapping on the mirror side: [CodexPreToolUse CodexSessionStart]" plus three Codex activation tests); the walk made to match nothing (element type aliased so the go/ast walk finds no table) -> go generate EXITS 1 "declares no capture proof table (a var of element type captureProofDeclaration)", a hard error, never a silent empty generation. L6: an Anthropic-shaped key planted in session_start_2_1_222.json -> RED TestNoCommittedTestdataCarriesASecretShape "carries a Anthropic API key at byte 12 (53 bytes); a committed fixture must never carry a credential, so remove or substitute it". ONE PARSER: inventory_test.go calls acceptance.ParseRedaction; no local split of the redaction string remains in ingress (grep); the only other ParseRedaction callers are the owner and its own test.

L11 AND GUARDS, all on 0aead71. THE DECISIVE ONE, the reclaim call removed from the rebuild (call replaced by a no-op of the same signature) -> RED TestEveryReadCommandReachesTheReclaim for ALL FOUR commands, each "<context|lineage|list|orphans>: exactly the cap (1024) of 1027 legacy orphans is reclaimed by one run; 1028 rows survive", RED TestTheOrphansReportSaysWhatThisRunReclaimedAndWhatRemains, RED TestTheReclaimIsReachedOnlyFromTheRebuild "the reclaim is called exactly once, from the rebuild, inside its transaction after the re-insert". DERIVED WRITER GUARD: a NEW command "probe" registered under hook lifecycle whose RunE reaches handlers.HookLifecycleRaw under context.WithCancel, NO test edit -> RED TestEveryLifecycleWriterCommandBoundsItsWindow "pasture hook lifecycle probe reaches the receipt store but builds no bounded context: every lifecycle writer must derive its context through context.WithTimeout from a tier of timeouts.ProductionProfile()..."; raw's WithTimeout -> WithCancel -> RED the same guard naming raw and RED TestTheRawPathRunsUnderTheWorkflowResultTier. CANCELLATION-BOUNDED CONTEXT: TestReceiveAcceptsAContextWithNoDeadline, TestReceiveAcceptsADeadlineInsideTheWindow and the two refusals GREEN (control); the S0 proofs TestAnInvocationAbandonedAfterItsCommitTellsTheHostTheTruth and TestAdviceFollowsTheCauseAndNotTheClassifier GREEN and untouched (git diff d3edb79..0aead71 on that file is three partition entries added and one moved; no pin changed). NIL SINK: the refusal replaced by a default of os.Stderr -> RED TestTheStoreRefusesANilDiagnosticSinkAndANilClock "a nil diagnostics sink must be refused at open"; EVERY production construction site enumerated by grep over non-test Go (33 sites in internal/handlers, cmd/pastured, cmd/pasture-recovery-probe, internal/testutil) goes through OpenTaskTracker or OpenTaskTrackerWithOptions, both rooted in productionOpenDefaults(), and the registered openTaskTrackerImpl too. HELP TEXT reverted to "The command deletes nothing" -> RED TestTheOrphansHelpSaysTheCommandReclaims and RED both goldens. GOLDENS reverted to the d3edb79 bytes -> RED TestNativeHelpGoldenBytesUnchanged on both files (they still read the help). GOLDEN DIFF d3edb79..0aead71 on help-golden/: exactly three hunks, all the deletion-claim change; no other byte. STALE PROJECTION, the reclaim moved before the delete/re-insert -> RED TestStaleProjectionNeverLosesAJournalNamedBlob "the rebuild must complete". SNAPSHOT at the delete instant instead of before the read -> RED TestReclaimAgesAgainstTheSnapshotInstantNotTheDeleteInstant "...ageing it against the delete instant reclaims an in-flight blob". CAPTURE read made unconditional -> RED TestTheCaptureReadIsGatedOnTheVariableAndSitsInsideTheWork "the capture call must be guarded by an if". THE TWO NUMBERS: the reclaimed line dropped from the text -> RED two tests; JSON remaining falsified (+1) -> RED "the JSON reader gets the remaining number" and "both renderers must report the same remaining number"; the two numbers SWAPPED in text -> RED "five orphans ... this run reclaims all five and says so" and "after the reclaim nothing remains"; SWAPPED in JSON -> RED "the JSON reader gets the reclaimed number" and "the JSON reader gets the remaining number". A reader can tell them apart and each is pinned as its own value. text: RECORDED AS ITS OWN ITEM, NOT A FINDING AGAINST 0aead71 (reviewer-s1-r2): TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets, internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go. OPEN FINDINGS: NONE. All five round-1 findings are fixed and were RE-DRIVEN AT THEIR DEFECT SITES by an independent round-2 reviewer, each turning RED. The round-1 group tasks uxp9x1 and 93s2j9 remain OPEN AS BOOKKEEPING for the team lead's top-down closure; the supervisor closes nothing.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE LEAF TEXT, each with its reason
1. L1: the clearance exemption is an ENUMERATED list keyed on committed PATH AND declared digest, not a version predicate. Reason: a predicate exempts every future fixture; a digest alone lets a copied payload inherit the exemption, which the corpus proves is real because three session-start sidecars share one payload. reviewer-b's older-pin case is superseded for unlisted fixtures.
2. xw71qw: the persisted clearanceAuthority key is DELETED, with no replacement URL. Reason: a clearance authority IS the committed CLEARANCE.md path; the proposed issue URL would have asserted a clearance fact nobody could confirm.
3. L3 gains the per-harness version-admission shape and the patch-bump test, moved from L5. Reason: every shipped Claude hook passes --host-version "${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:-unknown}", so a LIVE admission gate would fault on every Claude event and silently lose all journaling. The transport defect is filed as aura-plugins-bm1ci8 under S4.
4. L3 also deletes the package-level Evaluate bridge. Reason: a Claude-bound default is the shape the leaf exists to remove.
5. L11 grew a SCHEMA MIGRATION (v7 -> v8, written_at) and a WorkflowResult deadline on the raw path. Reason: the ruled age bound had nothing to read and no ceiling on the raw writer.
6. L11's reclaim moved from the hook path to INSIDE projection.RebuildOccurrences under a SAVEPOINT. Reason: lifecycle_occurrences is a projection the hook path never maintains, so the ruled predicate would have DELETED BLOBS A JOURNAL ROW NAMES on any stale store.
7. The Receive refusal was narrowed to a beyond-window deadline and a zero window, ACCEPTING no-deadline, and the bound moved to a DERIVED guard over production writers. Reason: the first predicate refused a CORRECT cancellation-bounded caller, including an S0 proof built clock-free on purpose. All six foreign deadline edits and the test-only wrapper were reverted; the foreign footprint is one Window line plus partition entries.
8. The diagnostics sink is a REQUIRED construction input with nil refused, not a default, and the rebuild RETURNS its outcome rather than receiving a writer. Reason: a default would make an unenumerated construction site silently correct — and one exists, a white-box internal test no opener enumeration could reach.
9. written_at is stamped with the MIGRATION INSTANT and a zero means UNKNOWN and is never eligible. Reason: DEFAULT 0 conflated "written before v8" with "written long ago", so the first read command after an upgrade destroyed a moments-old blob.
10. The orphans command now reports TWO numbers and its help says it reclaims. Reason: it mutates what it measures, and the old help told a user it deletes nothing.
11. One redaction parser: the ingress reader calls acceptance.ParseRedaction. Reason: the duplicate existed only by branch topology, and a rule added to the owner would never have reached the copy.
12. The Makefile generate target, the four legacy sidecars, catalogue_test.go, fixture_digest_test.go and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go joined side A's set; twelve paths joined side B's. Each was demanded by a ruled requirement, and each is named in the commit that used it.
13. L8's second mutation clause is DEFERRED TO S3, recorded on llt3k5: the derived-None case needs a type S3 introduces. The performable half was performed.
14. Only 14 Claude sidecars are CaptureProvenance-shaped; the Codex and OpenCode evaluations use canonical sidecars synthesised in temporary directories from the real bytes.
15. The mirror-enum work is the reusable helper only, applied to enums that exist; S3 applies it to the gateauthority mirrors.

ROUTED OUT OF S1, EACH WITH A HOME: aura-plugins-bm1ci8 (the "unknown" Claude host version, S4); aura-plugins-1uja39 (the hand-listed generated-output inventory guard, S2-L7); pasture #133 and #140 (pre-existing process references, including 14 sites at d3edb79 and the stale MaxKnownSchemaVersion doc at internal/audit/migrate.go:78-79, with the note that a sweep guard must EXCLUDE agent-role words, which are this product's own domain vocabulary, and must cover DATA, COMMENTS and FAILURE MESSAGES).
ONE ITEM STILL NEEDS A HOME, AND IT IS THE ONLY ACTION I AM LEAVING OPEN: FINDING S-5, TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets in internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go depends on WINNING A RACE against a workflow completing, which is the fixed-timing dependence the standing constraints forbid. It is pre-existing and untouched by this slice. It weakens every green under parallel gating, and this team now runs concurrent gates as routine. It belongs with the DBOS test-performance work and the team lead should file it.

DECISIONS THE USER MUST MAKE: NONE for S1. The clearance approvals are per-harness Impl-UAT items in S4, S5 and S6; S1 built the procedure and captured nothing.

THE TEAM LEAD IS THE INTEGRATOR: it pushes, opens the pull request, waits for both CI runs, merges, confirms the push-to-main run, and closes the chain top-down.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FINDING S-5 REFINED, AND IT NOW CARRIES ITS OWN FIX. supervisor-s1, 2026-09-05. This does not change the round-2 verdict, which stands at ACCEPT 0/0/0 on 0aead71.

THE MECHANISM, from reviewer-s1-r2 and worth more than the observation was: TestRecovery_RecoveredSlicesObeyTheLimitTheRestartedEngineSets WAITS ON A CONDITION until the running count reaches the limit, and THEN marks those rows as still running before the crash. A SLICE THAT COMPLETES IN THE WINDOW BETWEEN THE OBSERVATION AND THE MARK MAKES THE MARK STALE, and the test then reports "updated 0 rows, want 1".
SO THE TEST IS NOT NAIVELY TIME-DEPENDENT — IT DOES WAIT ON A CONDITION, WHICH IS THE RULE. The defect is subtler and worth stating precisely, because the rule as usually written would pass this code: THE OBSERVATION AND THE ACTION IT JUSTIFIES ARE NOT ATOMIC. Waiting on a condition is not enough if the world may change between the wait and the use of what the wait established. Under load that window widens until it is routinely lost.
THE FIX THE REVIEWER NAMES: A BARRIER THE TEST HOLDS, so the observed slices cannot complete between the observation and the mark. That removes the race rather than making it rarer, which is the distinction between a fix and a longer timeout.

EVIDENCE THAT IT IS PRE-EXISTING AND NOT THIS BRANCH'S: internal/engine/subworkflows_test.go has an EMPTY DIFF from d3edb79 to 0aead71. Untouched by both sides.
FIVE INDEPENDENT FULL-SUITE RUNS EXIST ON THIS BRANCH AND ONLY ONE HIT IT: the supervisor's (73/3, under three concurrent race suites), against green runs from the fix worker, the team lead, the reviewer (internal/engine ok in 67.6 s) and the supervisor's own isolated re-run (38.9 s). A defect present in one run of a commit and absent in four others is non-determinism, and the load figures say which kind.

WHY IT IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN FORGETTING: IT WEAKENS EVERY GREEN ON THIS REPOSITORY EXACTLY WHEN SEVERAL PEOPLE CHECK THE SAME CLAIM AT ONCE. This team now runs concurrent gates as a matter of course — four ran on this slice today — so the failure mode appears precisely at the moment a result is being independently confirmed, which is the moment it does the most damage to trust in the gate.
IT IS NOT S1's TO FIX. A slice cleans up what it wrote. It belongs with the DBOS test-performance work, and the team lead files it.

THE ROUND-2 RE-POINT RULINGS ARE ALL DISCHARGED, confirmed by the reviewer: it reviewed 0aead71 as the head; it ATTACKED THE S-4 DOC CLAIM RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT — raising the ceiling without a step turns TestMigrate_FreshDB_LandsAtMaxKnownVersion and TestMigrate_RoundTrip_OpenMigrateReopen RED, the prose list ends at v7 -> v8 and matches migrationSteps(), the gap refusal lives in Migrate, and NO RESIDUAL LITERAL CEILING REMAINS in the doc. So the doc did not merely move its claim to a place nothing enforces, which was the risk I asked to be tested.

text:
RECORD FOR THE OPENCODE HARNESS OWNER (worker-s2, 2026-09-05), from a measured defect fixed on slice/rp2tju-s2 at 755bcacb26396f1d770d522bae5ff2d66c276503; GitHub issue https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/issues/142.
THE GENERATED PLUGIN NEVER LOADED IN A REAL OPENCODE. OpenCode's loader (packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts applyPlugin -> readV1Plugin "detect", then getLegacyPlugins) reads the module's default export first; an object with server() is used and nothing else is read; a bare function default falls back to Object.values(mod) and THROWS "Plugin export is not a function" on the first non-function export. The generated module default-exported the bare function and also exported an array and a string. Identical loader code at v1.18.10 and v1.18.29. The Bun production proofs imported the named functions directly and never crossed the loader, so every proof stayed green while the host logged "failed to load plugin".
FIX: default export { id: "pasture-lifecycle", server: PastureLifecycle }; named exports kept; a Bun proof now applies the host's acceptance rule (TestOpenCodeHooksModule_SatisfiesHostPluginLoaderRule); the enabled-handlers proof calls .server(...). Verified on OpenCode 1.18.29: plugin loaded, session.created captured.
TWO THINGS THE 47-EVENT WORK MUST KEEP: (a) any new export from the generated module must be a function or the v1 default must stay an object, or the host refuses the whole plugin; (b) a real-host load check belongs beside the Bun proofs, because the Bun proofs alone cannot see the loader. Also measured: the plugin's --host-version argument comes from a hand-maintained literal (internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go openCodeHostVersion = "1.18.10"), not from the runtime contract; the pin-bump work makes it read the root.

## Rules applied, in order

`home-path-v1` rewrites every spelling of the capturing user's home directory
to the `user` placeholder: the absolute path `/home/<user>`, the relative
spelling `home/<user>/`, and the directory slug a host derives from a path
(`-home-<user>-`), which is how the earlier committed corpus carries it. It
applies wherever any spelling occurs, including inside free text.
`free-text-v1` replaces each free-text string the inventory flagged by `x`
placeholder text of the same raw length. Keys, nesting, types and nulls are
unchanged; after both rules the committed bytes contain no occurrence of the
user name (asserted by the clearing run). Rules applied per fixture, in order:

- session_start_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1
- pre_tool_use_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.tool_input.command, .tool_input.description)
- post_tool_use_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.tool_input.command, .tool_input.description, .tool_response.stdout)
- post_tool_batch_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.tool_calls[0].tool_input.command, .tool_calls[0].tool_input.description, .tool_calls[0].tool_response)
- post_tool_use_failure_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.tool_input.command, .tool_input.description, .error)
- pre_compact_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1
- post_compact_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.compact_summary)
- session_end_2_1_261.json: home-path-v1
- the three controls below carry the session_start bytes and its rules.

## Secret scan

`TestNoCommittedTestdataCarriesASecretShape` (internal/lifecycle/ingress/secretscan_test.go)
run over the whole module with these fixtures and their sidecars in place:
PASS, zero hits, 2026-09-05. Reach control on the same run: an Anthropic
API-key shape planted into a copy of one new fixture in this directory turned
the scan RED naming that file and the byte offset; the copy was discarded.
`TestSecretScanIsRedOnEachPlantedShape` (all nine shapes): PASS.

## Refused classes

No fixture carries a tool response above 4096 bytes: the largest tool
response is 52 bytes (post_tool_batch) and 50 bytes (post_tool_use stdout).
The 7734-byte post_compact payload carries `compact_summary`, the host's own
summary of the session (7085 bytes of free text, not a tool response); it was
substituted by free-text-v1 and is committed as placeholder text of the same
length. No payload is an environment dump. Every free-text field on every
event was substituted. No payload was unclearable; no event is left withheld

# Clearance record

This file records how the fixtures in this directory were captured, cleared
and accepted. Fill every section before the acceptance test; leave the last
two sections for the acceptance and the landing. The procedure is documented
in AGENTS.md under "Capturing host payloads and clearing them into fixtures".

## Harness and pinned version

Claude Code 2.1.261, verified with `claude --version` immediately before the
session on 2026-09-05: `2.1.261 (Claude Code)`. Admission is a floor: this
version and every later release; the contract records 2.1.261.

## Capture

Captured in one live session on 2026-09-05, into
`~/.local/share/pasture-captures/claude`, with `PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR`
set. Paths in this record are spelled with `~` for the capturing user's home
directory; the fixture bytes themselves carry the `/home/user` placeholder that
`home-path-v1` writes. The sessions were interactive terminal sessions of the real host binary on the
user's machine, run at the user's direction by the team's operators; the user
did not type the prompts. Nothing captured reached any remote before the
user's acceptance recorded below.

Build kit: one `pasture` binary, sha256
`0b9a6fbde02493ba7325e772e78703adf2dc11533c882854ac0f7defa9ce5441`, built with
`CGO_ENABLED=0` from an archive copy of head 47d1c94 with the two version
roots moved to the versions above (artifact/aggregate_types.go, the three
`Contract.Version` literals under internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract)
and `make generate` run, so every transport carried the new version.
Environment in the host's shell: `PASTURE_BIN` = that binary,
`PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR` = the directory below (absolute, outside the repository,
pre-existing), `PASTURE_DB_PATH` = `~/.local/share/pasture-captures/scratch/pasture.db`
(a scratch database; the live store was not touched). On this scratch
database every hook printed one fail-open fault line ("cannot resolve

## Rules applied, in order

Per fixture, the value-only rules applied in the order applied, as listed in
the provenance sidecar: `home-path-v1`, then `free-text-v1` where the
inventory flagged free text. Structure, keys, types and nulls are unchanged.

`home-path-v1` rewrites every spelling of the capturing user's home directory
to the `user` placeholder: the absolute path `/home/<user>`, the relative
spelling `home/<user>/`, and the directory slug a host derives from a path
(`-home-<user>-`), which is how the earlier committed corpus carries it. It
applies wherever any spelling occurs, including inside free text.
`free-text-v1` replaces each free-text string the inventory flagged by `x`
placeholder text of the same raw length. Keys, nesting, types and nulls are
unchanged; after both rules the committed bytes contain no occurrence of the
user name (asserted by the clearing run). Rules applied per fixture, in order:

My first six-gate run reported 1 failing package for this reason alone; adding an origin remote and re-running the package alone gave ok. A reviewer who does not chase it records a false red, and a reviewer who assumes it is environmental could dismiss a real one.
CHANGE: skip on a missing or unparsable origin remote with the same wording as the existing skip, so the test states the environment it needs.
MUTATION THAT PROVES THE FIX: run it in a repository with no origin remote: it must skip, not fail.

DEFECT: the release note says "Admission is a floor at each recorded version: a host at or above it is admitted, a host below it is refused with the version it needs." It never says WHERE the floor is judged, and on the surface an operator meets first, the live hook path, nothing is judged at all.

MEASURED with two binaries I built myself and a bootstrapped database per case, with an EMPTY stderr on every run below (my first attempt without bootstrapping measured only the fail-open path and I discarded it): `pasture --db <fresh> hook lifecycle --harness claude-code --event SessionStart --host-version 2.1.260`, one patch BELOW the floor, exits 0 and writes the same bytes as 2.1.261 with no fault line. A prerelease at the floor, 2.1.261-rc.1, is also admitted on that path, although the contract refuses a prerelease. A version far above the floor (9.9.9 / 3.0.0 / 2.0.0) is admitted, as intended.

The operator learns the truth only when `pasture install` refuses. The missing phrase is the one that reader needs.

THE UPSTREAM EVENT DIFF, re-derived from the sources and not read from the report.

OPENCODE, from ~/codebases/sst/opencode: packages/schema/src/installation-event.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL at v1.18.10 and v1.18.29 (sha256 f9b2331c...) and spells installation.update-available, so the spelling fix and the "identical at both tags" comment are both true. PRODUCTION PROOFS at the new fixtures, all real paths. Claude 8 through the built binary, by my own runs. THE THREE KNOWN ITEMS HANDED TO MY JUDGEMENT.
1. The word "reviewer" twice in the 7cd5434 commit message: NOT A FINDING. History is never rewritten on this branch, no shipped file carries the word, the worker reported it and the supervisor recorded it, and the ruling on the slice task already says the remedy for a superseded wording is a later commit that names it. 2. The stronger I1 citation: VERIFIED. The installed 2.1.261 binary carries its own per-event hook table with an exit-code paragraph; all three rows quote it verbatim and each quote is attributed to the right event. The fix touching the runtime profile as well as the catalogue is CORRECT and necessary: FailureEvidence is a runtime-profile field and the activation report renders the citation from there, so the catalogue alone would claim a gate that nothing cites and the evidence rule would demote it in silence. TestClaudeBlockingRowsCiteTheirEvidence holds that.
3. The two further counts I2 swept: VERIFIED as reads. The Codex catalogue declares 7 gate rows, which I re-derived by reading the rows, and the divergent set is 22 rows, which the test derives and asserts against the recorded set in both directions.

CONTRADICTIONS, surfaced and NOT chosen.
C-1: the round-1 report states that BOTH frozen legacy goldens are byte-identical to d56bc90. MEASURED: internal/lifecycle/receipt/golden_v1_test.go IS byte-identical; internal/lifecycle/projection/persisted_v1_test.go IS NOT. d105103 changed one line, the occurrence envelope's contract, from the literal "claude-code/2.1.210" to a read of registration.ClaudeCode2_1_261().Contract.String(). The FROZEN parts are untouched and I confirmed them: goldenV1InterpretedPayload still carries "claude-code/claude-code@2.1.210", goldenV1InterpretedSHA256 is unchanged, and the read-back assertion still requires that 2.1.210 contract. The legacy-record property therefore still holds where it is asserted, and I raise no finding. What I surface is that the pre-M5 v1 record this test writes now carries TODAY's contract in its occurrence envelope while its interpreted payload carries 2.1.210, and that it will follow every future bump. Somebody should decide whether that is wanted.
C-2: the generated .codex/agents/*.toml header says "Codex 0.153.0 exposes no skill or self-service spawn function". Codex 0.153.0 ships the collab tools spawn_agent, send_input, resume_agent, wait and close_agent (codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs, CollabAgentTool::SpawnAgent maps to "spawn_agent"; codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1834 lists all five), skill item and dependency types (app-server-protocol schemas, SkillToolDependency) and a skills configuration key (core/src/config/edit.rs). spawn_agent is present at rust-v0.146.0 TOO, so S2 did not falsify a sentence that was true: it moved the version and re-asserted the claim at the new version without re-checking it. Codex has no native agent-profile schema with a functions key at all, so the sentence is a claim about pasture's own modelling of the host surface, and re-deriving the Codex profile is a later slice by my brief. I therefore do NOT raise it as an S2 finding. If the supervisor rules that moving the version re-asserts the claim in scope, it is an IMPORTANT for round 3, and the change is one sentence naming what the host does expose.
C-3: the retired OpenCode record wrapper is refused, which is right, but the REASON is false of that input. Feeding {harness,event,payload} to the head binary gives "the payload is not a JSON object, so no field could be read from it" with the fix line "Send a JSON OBJECT ... check both that they parse AND that the top level is an object". The payload IS a JSON object; only its event member has the wrong kind, so json.Unmarshal into callbackValue fails and internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/capture.go:37 lands on CaptureMalformed. internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:686 argues at length that the SHAPE sentence is "the one that is true of every input" of that arm; it is not, because a valid object with one mistyped member reaches the same arm. The code and the message are IDENTICAL at d56bc90 (I diffed both), so by the precedent that ruled C1 out of S2 this belongs to the slice that owns ingress diagnostics, with the measurement attached. It matters because the retired wrapper is exactly the shape an operator with an old fixture or an old transport will send after this slice.

WHAT IS SOLID AND SHOULD NOT BE REOPENED: the floor and its three installer sites; the twelve recaptures and their clearance evidence, digest by digest; the derived enabled floor and its equality with the policy list; the L7 inventory guard, which caught a new emitter output with no test edit and refuses to pass vacuously; the deletion of the legacy and free-text exemptions, with the inverted guards proven on a planted committed fixture and on an empty population; the three production paths; ownership and the internal-reference record.
OUT OF SCOPE, not re-litigated: C1 (the AGENTS.md empty-stdout sentence versus the gate bytes, recorded on aura-plugins-ectjb1), the capturing user's name in the 18 files outside testdata, the absence of a live version-admission gate on the hook path, the gate decision model, and pasture #140 process-reference debt in files S2 did not touch.
