THE INPUT I SENT. The retired shape, an object with three members, built from the committed raw fixture:
{"harness": "opencode", "event": "session.created", "payload": {"event": {"id": "evt_0718dc1ec002GDEcwTfJUw7Eu6", "type": "session.created", ...}}}
Checked independently before sending: the top level is an OBJECT with the keys event, harness and payload, and the member `event` is a STRING.

THE COMMAND, through the head binary I built, with a bootstrapped store:
pasture --db <fresh> hook lifecycle --harness opencode --event session.created --host-version 1.18.29 < the wrapper above
Exit 0 (fail open, as ruled), one fault line on standard error.

THE REFUSAL TEXT, verbatim, the part that is wrong (the cause and the fix):
"validation error: The OpenCode payload for event \"session.created\" at host version \"1.18.29\" could not be bound, so the event WAS NOT EVALUATED: the payload is not a JSON object, so no field could be read from it. Nothing was derived from this delivery and no gate was consulted, so the event had no part in the host's answer; the row carries the disposition that refused it and an empty interpreted set. Send a JSON OBJECT: a well-formed array, string or number is refused here too, because the event's fields are read from an object's members. Nothing about the fields or the host version was inspected on this route, because ingress stopped at the decode; capture the exact bytes the host sent and check both that they parse AND that the top level is an object."

WHY IT IS FALSE. The payload IS a JSON object and it DID decode. The operator is told to send an object and to check that the top level is an object, and they already did both, so the message sends them to look at the one thing that is correct.

THE TRUE REASON, and the two files that produce it.
internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/capture.go:33-38: after ingress.Validate returns CaptureValid, Parse unmarshals the body into the package's `callbackValue` struct, whose `Event` field is a nested OBJECT ({type, properties.sessionID}). The wrapper's `event` member is a STRING, so encoding/json returns a type error, and the code maps ANY unmarshal error to model.CaptureMalformed.
internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:679-692: the CaptureMalformed arm of captureDispositionAdviceByDisposition renders the sentence above. Its own comment argues that "not well-formed JSON" would be false for `[]`, `"hello"` and `123`, and concludes that the SHAPE sentence "is the one that is true of every input" of that arm. That conclusion is wrong at head: the arm also receives a well-formed OBJECT whose member has the wrong KIND, which is exactly the retired wrapper.
So the true reason for this input is: the payload decoded as an object, but a member the event's schema needs has the wrong JSON kind (here `event` is a string where an object is required), so no field could be read from it.

FILE AND LINE SUMMARY: the false sentence lives at internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:686 (Reason) and :687-690 (Fix); the branch that routes this input there is internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/capture.go:37.

WHOSE IT IS. NOT S2's, by the precedent that ruled C1 out of this slice. I diffed both files against d56bc90: internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go carries the SAME sentence at base, and internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/capture.go differs from base by ONE line only, the manifest read (registration.OpenCode1_18_10 -> registration.OpenCode1_18_29). The behaviour and the wording are identical at base, so S2 introduced neither. I record it here because S2 RETIRED the wrapper shape, so this slice is what makes an operator meet this message: anyone holding an old fixture, an old capture file or an old transport now sends exactly this input.

THE CHANGE I WOULD MAKE, when the owning slice takes it. Split the arm by cause instead of by disposition, so the sentence matches the input: keep the present shape sentence for a body that is not an object at all (array, string, number, or a fragment that does not parse), and add a second cause for a body that IS an object but whose member kinds do not match the event's schema, naming the member and the kind it needed. That means opencode/capture.go must stop collapsing every unmarshal error into CaptureMalformed and distinguish "not an object" from "a member has the wrong kind"; the disposition set already has room for it, and the handler's own map refuses to invent a reason for an unlisted disposition, which is the right default.

MUTATION THAT PROVES THE FIX. Two inputs, one assertion each, both through the built binary or the handler: (1) send `[]` and require the present shape sentence, so the existing wording stays load-bearing for the input it is true of; (2) send {"event": "session.created", ...}, an object whose `event` member is a string, and require a message that names the MEMBER and its wrong kind and does NOT contain "the payload is not a JSON object". Today (2) fails, because both inputs get sentence (1). A control keeps it honest: send the committed raw fixture and require exit 0 with no fault line.

WHY IT IS NOT A BLOCKER OR AN IMPORTANT FOR THIS SLICE: nothing unsafe happens. The wrapper is refused, the delivery is recorded with the disposition that refused it, the interpreted set is empty, no gate is consulted, and the host proceeds on its own default under the ruled fail-open policy. The cost is one operator's time, spent looking in the wrong place.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L1 VERDICT: YES a393c8c550d12f68cf7988974c51af1ebc7fe175 (branch slice/rp2tju-s3), with ONE probe FAILED (probe 5) that does NOT stop S3 but DOES require an amendment to the leaf text of S3-L5, and with probe 6b measuring a number the plan text did not predict.

Why YES: every fact the gate read model needs is reachable through the public API of the pinned provenance v0.0.7. Nothing must be copied, vendored, or reached through a provenance internal package. No provenance release and no go.mod re-pin is needed for the read model. The one capability that is NOT obtainable (a single read transaction spanning the pasture-side reads and the journal reads) is already covered by a mechanism the plan carries: the torn check of finding B19, which probe 4 proves works.

FILE: internal/tasks/gate_reader_feasibility_test.go (new, 978 lines, the only file touched). Nine test cases. Every case names in its doc comment what turns it RED, and every named mutation was DRIVEN to RED in throwaway archive copies (quoted below). No case says "feasibility only": every one carries a performable mutation.

=========================
1. PER PROBE
=========================

PROBE 1 — PASS. AuthorityGovernsTaskAt is callable through the EXPORTED interface.
- Reached by: var journal provenance.Journal = tracker.Journal(). trackerImpl.Journal (internal/tasks/tracker.go:222) forwards to provenance.Tracker.Journal, which is how internal/tasks already reaches it (assignment_transfer.go, epoch_assignment_service.go). The interface method is journal_api.go:292; the borrowed wrapper is dbos_store.go:424; the body is internal/sqlite/operations_helpers.go:1060. Cited by name, not by line, from here on.
- Also proven: the beforeJID bound excludes the authority's own row.
- MUTATION: the same authority against a task it does not govern. RED: "AuthorityGovernsTaskAt(8, governed) = false; want true, because the episode was just committed and never ended".

PROBE 2 — PASS. The current maximum JournalID is one query.
- The query: QueryTaskEvents(JournalQueryV1{OrderBy: OrderByJournalID, Limit: 1}); the answer is the returned JournalTaskEventPageV1.SnapshotMaxJournalID.
- IMPORTANT SEMANTIC, measured, not assumed: that value is the maximum over the WHOLE journal, every kind, not over task events only. The implementation is SELECT COALESCE(MAX(journal_id), 0) FROM journal, taken whenever the caller leaves SnapshotMaxJournalID zero. An authority row or an operation anchor therefore moves it.
- ON AN EMPTY JOURNAL it yields 0. This was measured, not inferred: a store opened by the production opener has committed no journal row until the first command, so the probe reads 0 on a freshly opened store.
- MUTATION: skip the one appended event. RED: "journal maximum after one appended event = 4; want strictly above 4, because the append committed at least one journal row".

PROBE 3 — PASS. A bounded catch-up page is one query with a caller-set page size.
- The query: JournalQueryV1{OrderBy: OrderByJournalID, EventKinds: [FamilyAssignmentStarted.EventKind()], AfterJournalID: watermark, Limit: N}. It returns only the facts above the watermark, in canonical order, and sets Next when more remain.
- On S-11 (which page size S3 uses): provenance.MaxFactPageSize is 256 and it bounds the FACT page API (decisions and evidence, internal/journal/facts.go), NOT QueryTaskEvents. QueryTaskEvents.Limit has no upper cap; it validates only that the limit is not negative. So S3 does NOT reuse MaxFactPageSize by necessity; it must state its own page size and its reason. Recommendation for lwmdw3: define an S3-owned constant, because the gate budget is what bounds this page, not a provenance fact-page rule.
- MUTATION: page from the wrong watermark. RED: "catch-up page above watermark 14 = []; want exactly the one assignment-start fact 17 on task \"human-service--01a07348-...\"".

PROBE 4 — PASS. The torn probe works exactly as the plan states.
- The query: JournalQueryV1{OrderBy: OrderByJournalID, TaskIDs: <episode tasks>, AfterJournalID: snapshotJID, Limit: 1}. Zero rows on a quiet journal; exactly one row after one write on an episode task.
- MUTATION (the one the leaf asks for): point it at the wrong task set. RED: "torn probe above snapshot 9 after one write on task \"human-service--01a07348-...\" = 0 rows; want exactly one, because any row means the snapshot is torn".

PROBE 5 — FAIL. ONE READ TRANSACTION CANNOT HOLD THE PASTURE READS AND THE JOURNAL READS TOGETHER.
- How a pasture package obtains a transaction on the shared handle TODAY: the ONLY site is bindWellKnownAgent in internal/tasks/well_known.go, which calls auditDB.BeginTx. The shared DSN sets _txlock=immediate (internal/dbconn), so every such transaction is an IMMEDIATE WRITE transaction, and the write lock is taken at BEGIN.
- The gap: pasture opens the journal with provenance.OpenBorrowedSQLite(auditDB) (internal/tasks/open_unified.go), so the journal shares the pasture *sql.DB POOL, not the pasture TRANSACTION. The Journal interface exposes no transaction-scoped variant; every journal read leases its OWN connection. Two measured consequences:
  (a) AT THE PRODUCTION POOL SIZE OF ONE (DefaultDBPoolSize = 1, internal/tasks/pool.go:46) a journal read issued while a pasture transaction is open CANNOT OBTAIN A CONNECTION AT ALL. Measured: the predicate call did not return inside a two-second ceiling and returned only after the transaction rolled back. THIS IS A LIVE-PATH HAZARD FOR S3, not only a design nicety: a gate that holds an auditDB transaction across a journal read will hang for the whole hook budget on a production store.
  (b) ABOVE POOL SIZE ONE the journal read succeeds, on a DIFFERENT connection, therefore under a DIFFERENT read snapshot. Measured with the mutation the leaf asks for: the same reads on two transactions with a write between them; the first transaction saw the same row count before and after the write, the second saw strictly more.
- MUTATION: release the connection before the predicate runs. RED: "the governance predicate returned (err=<nil>) while a pasture transaction held the only pooled connection; want it to wait, because provenance leases its own connection from the same pool and the pool size is one".
- CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN, for the supervisor to rule on: the lwmdw3 sentence "All of steps 3 to 7 run inside ONE read transaction on the store handle" must be WITHDRAWN, in the same way finding PB1 withdrew "in the same transaction where the code allows it" from 1sg9v6. The correct statement is: the pasture-side reads (claim, index) may share one read transaction; every journal-side read (the governance predicate, the catch-up page, the torn probe) runs OUTSIDE it and must not be issued while it is open. The snapshot is then pinned by SnapshotMaxJournalID and the torn probe of B19 is what makes the composite read safe. That mechanism already exists in the plan, which is why this FAIL does not stop S3.
- SMALLEST PROVENANCE CHANGE THAT WOULD CLOSE IT, if the user ever wants the true single transaction: add a transaction-scoped read surface to the Journal contract, for example a ReadIn(tx *sql.Tx) Journal or a Snapshot(ctx) (JournalSnapshot, release) that binds the reads to a caller-supplied connection. COST ESTIMATE: it touches the journal read entry points and their connection binding (the bindScope path in internal/sqlite plus the borrowed wrapper), the exported contract in journal_api.go, and its tests; roughly 8 to 16 hours, plus a provenance release and a pasture go.mod re-pin. I DID NOT START IT, and I do not recommend it: the torn check already buys the same guarantee at read time, and the design would gain a way for a gate to hold a connection on a live user database.

PROBE 6a — PASS, on BOTH write paths.
- PATH ONE, a direct journal Apply that carries the assignment-start effect (the shape the assignment service's own tests seed): THE EXACT FIELD IS provenance.CommittedResult.ResultSlots, the binding whose Slot equals the ResultSlotID the caller set on its EffectAssignmentStart effect; THE VALUE IS THAT BINDING'S ProducedJournalID, and its Kind is provenance.JournalKindAuthority. EmittedEvents is NOT a source: it is the task_event closure only, and the authority row is not a task event (asserted by the probe).
- PATH TWO, the composed governed allocation, WHICH IS THE SHAPE ALL FOUR PRODUCTION ASSIGNMENT WRITERS USE (they emit no EffectAssignmentStart at all; provenance creates the child authority): THE EXACT FIELD IS GovernedAllocationComposedResult.Closure().Children()[i].AssignmentRow.JournalID (provenance.GovernedChildBinding, provenance.GovernedProducedRow, both exported through reexports.go). The sibling TaskRow.JournalID carries the child's task row and is NOT the authority. Proven live, through a bound test allocator running one RunAllocateComposed.
- BOTH IDS EQUAL WHAT THE EXISTING BACKWARDS RECOVERY FINDS. The probe calls the production method assignmentAuthorityForEvent as the oracle and compares.
- AVAILABLE ONLY AFTER THE JOURNAL COMMIT, stated plainly: neither field exists before Apply (or before the allocation) returns. THE INDEX WRITE THEREFORE CANNOT SHARE THE JOURNAL APPLY TRANSACTION. S3-L4 must say "after Apply". This confirms the PB1 wording already in 1sg9v6.
- MUTATION one: compare the recovered id against the material event id. RED: "the backwards scan recovered authority 6; the Apply result slot yielded 6; want the same id" (the mutant prints the unmutated field, which is why the two numbers read alike; the comparison it makes is against the event id).
- MUTATION two: read TaskRow where AssignmentRow belongs. RED: "the backwards recovery found authority 10; the composed closure yielded 9; want the same id".
- CONSEQUENCE: at the choke point S3-L4 needs NO scan at all. It reads the id from the result it already has. The scan only matters for the backfill.

PROBE 6b — PASS, and THE PLAN'S COST ASSUMPTION IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. MEASURED, in operations, never in wall-clock time; no sleep anywhere.
- JOURNAL SIZE USED: 3028 journal rows, of which 3000 are filler task events, plus 2 assignment-start facts. A second measurement runs on the composed-allocation shape.
- THE COST IS NOT O(journal) PER FACT IN GENERAL. It is the DISTANCE the backwards walk covers: from the material event down to the event's producing operation, and, only if that finds nothing, from below that operation down to the TASK'S BIRTH.
- MEASURED, three shapes:
  1. ADJACENT (one operation writes the authority and its material event): 2 predicate calls over 1 candidate.
  2. COMPOSED GOVERNED ALLOCATION on a NEWLY CREATED child task, which is what the four production writers do: authority row 10, material event 12, distance 2; 3 predicate calls over 2 candidates. THE PRODUCTION SHAPE IS CHEAP, because the child task's birth is inside the same allocation.
  3. SEPARATED (the authority committed by an EARLIER operation than its material event, with a 3000-event stretch between them): 3018 predicate calls over 3017 candidates. THE FALLBACK WALK IS ONE PREDICATE CALL PER JOURNAL ID OF THE STRETCH.
- THE TOTAL, for a backfill: the sum of those per-fact distances. For a store whose assignment starts are all shape 2 the total is about 3 calls per fact and an on-command migration could pay it. For a store that holds ANY shape-3 fact the per-fact cost is the whole stretch between that task's birth and its assignment start, so ONE long-lived task with a late assignment costs a full journal walk on an ordinary user command. Shape 3 is what an assignment start on an OLD task produces: TransferTaskAssignment (internal/tasks/assignment_transfer.go) and a replacement assignment on a long-lived task are exactly that.
- WHY A HARD PER-FACT NUMBER CANNOT BE STATED: the cost is a property of the STORE'S HISTORY, not of the code. A migration cannot know the distance before it walks it.
- RECOMMENDATION, among the three shapes the leaf names: THE ONE-SHOT OFFLINE REBUILD through "pasture gate rebuild-index" (S3-L9), with only a BOUNDED CATCH-UP on the command path. This is also the reviewer preference recorded on 1sg9v6, and the measurement supports it for a stronger reason than "close to the limit": THE BOUND IS UNKNOWABLE IN ADVANCE, so no on-command migration can promise it. A bounded scan window is the second choice; it silently leaves facts unindexed, which the Reader must then report as an incomplete index. Reusing a different recorded fact is not available: nothing records the authority today, which is the whole of finding PB1.
- MUTATION: add one extra predicate call per candidate. RED: "the adjacent shape cost 10 predicate calls; want at most 8, because one operation places the authority directly below its material event". The mutated separated shape rose from 3018 to 27154 calls, which shows the counter is measuring the walk and not a constant.

PROBE 7 — PASS.
- THE TIER HELD: the store was opened with the tight test profile, whose SQLiteBusy tier is 25 ms. A SECOND connection on the same file (dbconn.OpenSharedDBWithProfile) took the write lock and held it past that tier. The hold is released by a CHANNEL the test closes after it has observed the contended write; there is no sleep and no fixed-deadline poll, and the observation and the release it justifies are ordered by that one signal.
- THE ERROR OBSERVED: the write to the throwaway pasture-owned table failed with the SQLite locked-or-busy outcome, which is the timeout the reader will map to RefusalIndexStale. It is a clean refusal, not a partial write: after the holder rolled back, the table held 0 rows.
- PROVENANCE WRITE OWNERSHIP UNDISTURBED: a later journal Apply on the same handle committed normally, and returned both of its result slots.
- MUTATION: never take the write lock. RED: "the pasture-owned write succeeded while another connection held the write lock for longer than the 25ms busy tier; want a busy timeout, because that is the error the gate maps to a stale-index refusal".
- CAVEAT, stated because it is a truth claim: the busy outcome is recognised by the driver's message text ("database is locked" / "busy"), because the pure-Go driver does not export a typed sentinel here. The probe explicitly excludes a context deadline so the two are not confused.

=========================
2. NO PROBE FAILED FOR WANT OF A PROVENANCE CHANGE
=========================
Probe 5 is the only FAIL, and its closing change is named above with its cost. It is NOT on the critical path: the plan's own torn check covers the same risk. No other probe needs a provenance release or a go.mod re-pin. Nothing was copied, vendored, or reached through a provenance internal package.

=========================
3. GATE COUNTS
=========================
INHERITED HEAD 0b33f07, archive copy, six gates, all green:
1 make build rc=0 (pastured, pasture-release, pasture, pasture-migrate-crash)
2 go vet rc=0
3 go test -race -count=1 ./... : ok=74, FAIL=0, DATA RACE=0, "no tests to run"=0, rc=0; 9 packages report "no test files"; slowest cmd/pasture 75.6 s, internal/tasks 65.5 s, internal/engine 50.5 s
4 make generate rc=0, 171 log lines (169 plus the dev-shell banner and the return-code line), git porcelain 0
5 nix flake check --no-build rc=0
6 gofmt -l . lists 0 files; NEGATIVE CONTROL: one planted unformatted file made it list exactly 1, and removing it returned it to 0
No package needed a re-run.

MY OWN SHA a393c8c, fresh archive copy, same six gates, all green:

2 go vet rc=0
3 go test -race -count=1 ./... : ok=74, FAIL=0, DATA RACE=0, "no tests to run"=0, rc=0; slowest internal/tasks 179.9 s, cmd/pasture 76.4 s, internal/engine 51.0 s
4 make generate rc=0, 171 log lines, git porcelain 0

GATE RUNNING / GATE DONE were posted around both race suites.

COST: internal/tasks under -race goes from 65.5 s to 179.9 s, plus 114 s, almost all of it probe 6b's 3017-candidate walk. Ruling wanted (already posted above): keep the 3000-event stretch in the committed guard, or lower it and keep the measured number in this report only.

=========================
4. OWNERSHIP
=========================
Commit a393c8c on slice/rp2tju-s3. git show --stat names exactly one file: internal/tasks/gate_reader_feasibility_test.go (added, 978 lines). The commit message's Ownership paragraph names that one file and no other. Working tree porcelain 0. Committed with git agent-commit. Nothing pushed, no pull request, no Beads task closed.

=========================
5. DEVIATIONS FROM THE LEAF TEXT, EACH WITH ITS REASON
=========================
D1 NINE test cases, not seven. Probe 6a needed TWO cases, because there are two write paths with two different fields, and the composed path is the one all four production writers use. Splitting them keeps one subject per case and lets each name its own mutation.
D2 Probe 6b measures THREE shapes, not one. The leaf asks for "the per-fact work"; the measurement showed there is no single number, so the probe measures the cheap production shape and the expensive shape and reports both. Reporting only one would have been a false bound.
D3 The cost measurement uses a COUNTING WALK that mirrors the production recovery's two candidate ranges and calls the SAME exported predicate, with the production method assignmentAuthorityForEvent as the ORACLE for the id. Reason: the production method exposes no call counter, and instrumenting it would change production code in a spike leaf. The walk is the instrument; the production method is the truth.
D4 Probe 5's negative half ("the predicate does not return") uses a two-second CLOCK AS A FAILURE CEILING, because a non-event cannot be waited on by a condition. The positive half, which carries the proof, is a condition wait: the predicate completes when the transaction releases the connection. This is stated in the source.
D5 Probe 7 recognises the busy outcome by message text, because the pure-Go driver exports no typed sentinel for it here. The probe excludes a context deadline explicitly.
D6 SC-1 is satisfied with no exception: no probe says "feasibility only"; every one has a performable mutation and every mutation was driven to RED.

=========================
6. STALE CITATIONS CORRECTED
=========================
S-9 is answered, not just seeded: JournalTaskEventPageV1.SnapshotMaxJournalID IS the journal maximum, it is the maximum of the WHOLE journal and not of task events, and it is 0 on an empty journal.
S-11 is answered: MaxFactPageSize (256) bounds the provenance FACT page API, not QueryTaskEvents. QueryTaskEvents.Limit has no cap and rejects only a negative value. S3 must define its own page size; lwmdw3's use of MaxFactPageSize as "the catch-up page size" is a wrong citation, not just an open question.
The leaf's own line citations were used only to FIND the code; every evidence statement above names the function and the committed path, never a line that moves. The two the leaf gives that still hold at v0.0.7: AuthorityGovernsTaskAt on the Journal interface, and its borrowed wrapper in dbos_store.go. The predicate body is in internal/sqlite/operations_helpers.go, which is a provenance INTERNAL package: it is named here as evidence only and is not reachable from pasture, which is correct.
NEW FACT NOT IN ANY LEAF, for 1sg9v6: the four production assignment writers emit NO EffectAssignmentStart. Provenance creates the child authority inside the composed allocation. The choke point therefore reads GovernedAllocationComposedResult.Closure().Children()[i].AssignmentRow.JournalID, not a result slot. 1sg9v6 currently says "Name the exact provenance.CommittedResult field", which is right for the direct-Apply shape only.

STOPPING HERE and waiting for the supervisor's next order. L2 is not started.

text: LEAD RULING 2026-09-05 on the L1 verdict (YES a393c8c) findings, plan-level parts only; supervisor-s3 owns the test design. (1) 'ONE READ TRANSACTION' IS WITHDRAWN from L5 lwmdw3 and from tradeoff T21's wording: the measurement shows a journal read leases its own pooled connection, and at the production pool size of one a journal read issued inside a held pasture transaction cannot obtain a connection and would hang a real gate for its whole budget. The Reader's consistency mechanism becomes ONE SNAPSHOT, not one transaction: take the journal snapshot id (SnapshotMaxJournalID) first; do the pasture-side reads (claim, index, phase) in ONE pasture transaction; do the journal reads through the provenance API bounded by that snapshot id; run the torn check (probe 4: any journal row for the episode tasks after the snapshot id) after the reads and refuse with the torn reason if it fires; NEVER hold a pasture transaction while issuing a journal read, and pin that with a test (a journal read inside a held pasture transaction at pool size one must be refused or impossible by construction, not hung). Recorded as S3 deviation 2 on o8z8pn. (2) The authority id for an assignment start comes from the composed allocation closure the four production writers already hold, available only after the commit; L4 and L12 take it from there, not from a CommittedResult slot; the doc states the source. (3) The backfill cost is not knowable in advance, so the ONE-SHOT OFFLINE REBUILD (L9 rebuild-index) with a bounded catch-up on the command path is the shape, as the plan reviewers preferred. supervisor-s3 rules the probe 6b stretch and every test detail; the chain worker (same Opus worker, continued) carries these three into L4, L5, L9 and L12.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROBE 5 CONSEQUENCE, SURFACED by supervisor-s3 (2026-09-05) for the LEAD's ruling, because it withdraws a sentence of the ratified plan (tradeoff T21 and this leaf: "All of steps 3 to 7 run inside ONE read transaction on the store handle"). Until the lead rules, this text is a PROPOSAL and L5 / L12 do not start on it.
MEASURED (L1 probe 5, a393c8c): pasture opens the journal with provenance.OpenBorrowedSQLite(auditDB), so the journal shares the pasture *sql.DB POOL and not a pasture TRANSACTION; the Journal interface has no transaction-scoped read; every journal read leases its OWN pooled connection. At the production pool size of one (DefaultDBPoolSize = 1, internal/tasks/pool.go) a journal read issued while a pasture transaction is open cannot obtain a connection and HANGS until the transaction ends; above one it runs under a DIFFERENT snapshot. The only pasture transaction site today is bindWellKnownAgent (well_known.go), an IMMEDIATE write transaction (_txlock=immediate).
PROPOSED RULING (one text governs once the lead confirms):
1. WITHDRAW "one read transaction spanning steps 3 to 7". The Reader NEVER holds an auditDB transaction across a journal read (a live-path hang on a production store).
2. The snapshot is pinned by snapshotJID = JournalTaskEventPageV1.SnapshotMaxJournalID taken ONCE (probe 2: the maximum over the WHOLE journal; 0 on an empty journal). Every journal-side read is bounded by it: the catch-up page (AfterJournalID = watermark, SnapshotMaxJournalID = snapshotJID), the governance predicate (beforeJID = snapshotJID), the torn probe (AfterJournalID = snapshotJID). The pasture-side reads (claim, index) run in one SHORT read of the pasture tables with no journal call inside it; if a transaction is used for them it is closed before any journal call.
3. The torn probe (finding B19, probe 4) is the mechanism that makes the composite read safe: any row above snapshotJID on the episode tasks refuses with RefusalSnapshotTorn, a FAULT, never a Deny. A phase read is a task-record read; if it is a journal-side read it is bounded by snapshotJID too, and the torn probe runs LAST.
4. The page size is an S3-OWNED constant (probe 3: provenance.MaxFactPageSize bounds the fact API only; QueryTaskEvents.Limit has no cap); name it in gateauthority with its reason (the gate budget bounds it).
5. Acceptance criterion A23 (torn -> refusal) and A-B18 (catch-up) are unchanged; the test "a write that lands between the snapshot and the phase read -> RefusalSnapshotTorn" stays and now carries the guarantee the transaction used to carry. Add one test: a Snapshot never opens an auditDB transaction while a journal read is in flight (mutation: wrap a journal read in BeginTx at pool size one, the test must fail by its bounded timeout, never hang).
6. Alternative NOT recommended: a provenance change (a transaction-scoped Journal read surface), about 8 to 16 hours plus a provenance release and a go.mod re-pin; it would also let a gate hold a connection on a live user database. This is the user's decision if the lead wants it raised.

author: David Huu Pham
text: NEW FACT for this leaf from L1 probe 6a (supervisor-s3, 2026-09-05; a393c8c): the FOUR production assignment writers emit NO EffectAssignmentStart; provenance creates the child authority inside the composed governed allocation. At the choke point the authority journal id is therefore read from GovernedAllocationComposedResult.Closure().Children()[i].AssignmentRow.JournalID (provenance.GovernedChildBinding / GovernedProducedRow, exported through reexports.go); TaskRow.JournalID is the child's task row and is NOT the authority. The direct-Apply shape yields it from CommittedResult.ResultSlots (the binding whose Slot is the caller's EffectAssignmentStart slot; ProducedJournalID; Kind JournalKindAuthority). Both are available only AFTER the commit; the index write happens after Apply. The transfer path (TransferTaskAssignment) must be checked for which shape it uses. NO scan at the choke point. BACKFILL: the measured cost is the DISTANCE of the backwards walk, not O(journal) per fact in general: adjacent 2 calls, composed-on-new-task 3 calls, separated (authority committed by an earlier operation, 3000-event stretch) 3018 calls; the bound is a property of the store's history and cannot be known in advance, so the chosen shape is the ONE-SHOT OFFLINE REBUILD through pasture gate rebuild-index (L9) with a BOUNDED catch-up on the command path; an on-command migration is NOT built. State this in the commit and in the S3 report item 6b.

pasture/worktree/rp2tju-s4--claude-coverage, branch slice/rp2tju-s4, at origin/main 0b33f07. Porcelain is empty. No commit of mine exists. I never edit this tree; workers do. I verify on archive copies.

== 3. THE 33 REGISTERED CLAUDE ROWS ==
Source: internal/lifecycle/registration/claude_2_1_261.gen.go (33 NativeName rows) and the committed hooks/pasture-activation.json (33 event rows). The two agree. The documentation citation for the same 33 names is https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, recorded by the lead on 2fyuvb.

== 4. CONTRADICTIONS, SURFACED ==

C-1 (BLOCKING for L1 and L2; I ask the lead to carry the ruling if it is plan-level). THE TRANSPORT CANNOT FIRE A HOOK FOR AN EVENT THAT IS NOT ALREADY ENABLED.
Measured: internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go emits a hooks.json row only when the activation state is Enabled ("if state.State == activation.Enabled", line 185). The committed hooks/hooks.json therefore carries exactly 8 event keys. I compared it with the installed plugin at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/aura-plugins/pasture/0.0.8/hooks/hooks.json: the two are JSON-equal, and that copy also carries exactly the same 8 keys.
Consequence: a live session that uses either transport records the 8 events we already have and nothing else. S2 never met this, because S2 recaptured events that were already enabled. S4 must capture events that are NOT enabled. The capture kit therefore needs a transport that registers the whole candidate population.
Second-order problem: activation.NewEnabled refuses an entry without a capture proof and a production proof, so "enable it first, then capture" is circular in the product. It is not circular in a THROWAWAY KIT, because the proof values are constants that the generator does not check against the filesystem.
Options for L1 to measure and report, with my recommendation:
  (a) Build the kit in a throwaway archive copy, add the candidate rows to claude_targets.go there with placeholder proof strings, run `make generate`, and use the hooks.json the real generator emits. This exercises the shipped generator and prefigures the L4 edit. RECOMMENDED.

The measured catalogue is 2.1.261 with 33 registered rows. The lead already moved the ceiling on 4gm83b at 2026-09-05 08:35, and the IMPL_PLAN carries the rule that a moved ceiling falsifies claims at a distance. RULING: the numbers 2.1.251, 20 and 30 in every S4 leaf are superseded. The target is DERIVED at L1 from the committed catalogue and the reachability of each trigger. Governing text: the lead's comment on 4gm83b of 2026-09-05 08:35, plus the derived-enumeration rule on o8z8pn.

C-3 (resolved by me; recorded). The ownership table in handoff section 5, the slice text and i2qq6b all name internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/claude_2_1_251.go. That file does not exist. S2 renamed it to claude_2_1_261.go, and the registration file is now claude_2_1_261.gen.go. RULING: read every 2_1_251 path as the file that carries the currently pinned Claude contract. The ownership intent is unchanged.

C-4 (resolved by me; recorded). The run-harness-capture skill says "Claude Code, 8 events" and "the plan default is that the user drives the sessions". Both sentences describe S2. RULING: for S4 the event list comes from L1, and AGENTS drive the sessions through tmux. Governing text: the lead's Wave-1 dispatch on 4gm83b of 2026-09-05 20:46, and the user's standing instruction recorded in the S2 campaign.

C-5 (recorded for L4, not for L1 to L3). The plan says the Elicitation pair is withheld naming pasture issue #80 by URL. The committed activation report gives those two rows the reason "missing-request-correlation" and an empty evidence cell. No #80 URL appears. L4 owns that correction.

C-6 (recorded for L1). PreModelSwitch is registered, is not a target, and ALREADY carries a host citation for exit-2 blocking, taken from the installed 2.1.261 binary. It is therefore a documented gate. L1 must find its trigger and L4 must not demote it by accident.

C-7 (recorded; the workaround is known). bm1ci8 says CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION is undocumented and is absent from a live 2.1.261 session's environment, so the shipped hook passes the literal "unknown". For the capture campaign the S2 workaround stands: export CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION from `claude --version` in the capture shell, or every captured file is named "unknown". The product-level fix belongs to L9 and is not in this dispatch.

== 5. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT ==
I post a self-check over L1 to L3, then I write the L1 recipe-list worker prompt and ask the lead to spawn it. L1 must answer C-1 with a measurement before any capture starts.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
S6 SELF-CHECK over leaves L1, L2 and L3 (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). One screen, per the standing rule: every added pin names its mutation; every named mutation is one a worker can actually perform; no text a person acts on is left unpinned; and the leaf BODY is checked against the COMMENT record that governs it. I report the nil results too, because a nil result costs one line.

## L1 ae098k (recipe list)
- Pins: NONE. The leaf writes no assertion and owns no file. Correct, and its own text says so.
- Mutations: not applicable.
- Operator text: none shipped. The recipe list is read by the user and by the capture agents, so it is a truth claim about the HOST, not about the product. It is checked by the dry run and by the sitting itself, which is the right check.
- FINDING S-1 (IMPORTANT for the prompt, not a defect in the leaf). The leaf says "for EACH of the 45 events". It does not say WHERE the 45 come from. Under the derived-enumeration rule, a hand list taken from upstream documentation would be the wrong population: it could miss a registered row or add an unregistered one, and the recipe list is what the capture campaign then works through. The prompt must require the population to be DERIVED from the tree (the 47 rows of .opencode/pasture-opencode-activation.json at contract opencode/1.18.29, minus the 2 already enabled), and the list must state that derivation. APPLIED to the L1 prompt.
- FINDING S-2 (IMPORTANT for the prompt). The leaf says the user time figure is "about 3-4 hours". That figure was written for a campaign that had not been decomposed, and D11 has since been re-scoped once already. The 32 event-bus rows and the 15 named callbacks are not the same kind of work: a bus row needs the action that publishes it, a named callback needs the host to reach that extension point. The prompt must require the estimate to be built UP from the recipe list, per sitting, and to say plainly if it exceeds the working figure. APPLIED.

## L2 rtcnpj (capture campaign)
- Pins: NONE. The leaf writes no assertion. Correct.
- Mutations: not applicable.
- Operator text: none.
- FINDING S-3 (IMPORTANT, body versus record). The body says the sessions are driven "by the worker with the user present" and that the version must equal 1.18.19. Both are superseded by the record: the user's 12:17 ruling of 2026-09-05 put the sittings in the agents' hands, and the D1 amendment makes 1.18.29 the recorded version with floor admission. SURFACED to the lead in the start record as C-5. The prompt follows the record.
- FINDING S-4 (IMPORTANT for the prompt). The leaf's gate is "the recording notice printed; the capture directory is outside the repository; the host version matched at both ends". That is necessary and not sufficient. The S2 campaign showed the failure this misses: the generated plugin never LOADED in a real host, and every proof stayed green, so a session can produce zero files with every stated gate satisfied. The prompt must add the load check as a precondition of the first sitting: the host log shows the plugin loaded, and the one-event dry run wrote a real numbered file.

## L3 djji42 (clearance)
- Pins and mutations NAMED in the leaf: "leave the pre-substitution digest on one fixture and show the corpus turns RED", and "plant a token and show the secret scan turns RED". Both are performable, and both were performed at S2 (the secret scan reach control turned RED naming the file and the byte offset). PASS.
- FINDING S-5 (IMPORTANT, the leaf is now INCOMPLETE against the tree). The leaf predates three guards that S1 and S2 landed, and it names none of them, so a worker could satisfy the leaf's own words and still turn the suite red at its first gate:
  (a) the free-text corpus assertion — a committed fixture that carries free text must list free-text-v1 in its redaction, or the corpus test is RED naming the fixture and the field;
  (b) the structural home-segment guard — over every file under every harness testdata directory, every home-path spelling must name the placeholder segment "user" and no other;
  (c) the redaction SHAPE — the committed field is ONE comma-joined string parsed by a grammar, not a list, and not a free string. Measured in the committed sidecar today.
  APPLIED to the L3 prompt as required reading with the measured shape.
- FINDING S-6 (IMPORTANT, unpinned text a person acts on). CLEARANCE.md is the record the user's ACCEPT covers, so every sentence in it is a truth claim. The leaf lists the sections but sets no standard for the "## Capture" prose. The standard exists, but it lives in the S2 order and in the S2 lead gate, not in the leaf: state the operator truthfully, use no agent name and no process word, and spell the record's own paths with a tilde. Nothing turns RED if the prose is wrong, so the check is mine and the lead's, before the user is asked. APPLIED to the L3 prompt, and I will re-run it myself on the drafts.
- FINDING S-7 (MINOR). The leaf says "Refuse outright ... raw tool-response file contents over 4 KiB". Of the 15 named callbacks, tool.execute.after and the experimental transform callbacks carry host or model text that can exceed that size. The refused-class check is therefore not a formality on this harness, as it nearly was on the S2 batch. The prompt must require the check to be reported with the measured largest value, not asserted.

## NIL RESULTS, reported because they are informative
- No leaf of L1 to L3 widens its file ownership without saying so. L1 and L2 own no repository file; L3 owns internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/testdata/** only. The Wave-1 exclusive table agrees.
- No contradiction between the three leaves themselves. The order L1 to L2 to L3 is a real dependency and the Beads edges say so.
- The private-first rule is stated in all the right places and rests on a mechanism, not on discipline: the worker has no push path.
- No pin in these three leaves has loosened, because these three leaves add no pin at all. The pin work starts at L4.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SELF-CHECK over L0 to L3, supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05. I list what each leaf must answer, what I expect to go wrong, and how I will know.

L0 1w7rkf, re-derive the Codex catalogue from the runtime profile
1. What the leaf changes. The catalogue file for the recorded host version (internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go after the S2 root move) and, if the derivation lives there, the generator. It must NOT change the enabled set, the fixtures or the transport.
2. The claim it must make true. No catalogue row labels a mode that its runtime profile row does not hold. The test drives the comparison FROM the profile, so a later demotion cannot disagree in silence.
3. The trap. The plan text says eight Codex rows were demoted by the evidence rule. That number was measured before S2 moved the catalogue from ten rows to twelve. A moved ceiling falsifies claims at a distance, so the worker DERIVES the demoted set from the source and reports the number it measures; it never copies eight from the plan. If the measured number is not eight, that is the finding, not an error.
4. The byte claim. SessionStart and PreToolUse must produce the same hook-path bytes as a binary built from 0b33f07. The worker proves it by running both binaries over the two committed fixtures and comparing standard output, standard error class and exit code, not by reasoning.
5. Identities. Rows with no capture keep NO identity and NO payload field (option A, the S2 ruling). A worker that "fills in" SessionEnd or Interrupt fields from the upstream struct breaks that ruling. The row comment may CITE the upstream shape; the row may not declare it.
6. Mutation evidence. Relabel one demoted row as blocking and show the agreement test RED, quoting the message text and naming the row, never a line number.
7. Risk I hold: the IP-1 comment retirement is a text change in a shipped file. Its replacement must claim only what the slice makes true. The slice binds no third event yet at L0, so the retirement sentence must say what ends the condition (the enabling leaf), not that it has ended. I will read that sentence myself before I accept the leaf.

L1 u6ixdm, the recipe list
8. FIRST, the kit question. Ten of twelve rows have no runner, so the sitting needs a kit whose transport wires all twelve. The worker MEASURES whether the throwaway archive copy can enable all twelve and run `make generate` (option A), and reports the generator's refusal verbatim if it refuses (option B). No recipe is written before that measurement.
9. The list. One entry per uncaptured event: the trigger (the exact command or prompt or key), the session state the trigger needs, the observable that proves it fired, and the expected file name codex_<snake_event>_0_153_0.<n>.json. The setup section follows the skill: the binary built outside the repository with its SHA-256, PASTURE_BIN, PASTURE_DB_PATH in a scratch directory, PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR absolute and pre-existing under ~/.local/share/pasture-captures/s5/, a throwaway project directory holding the kit's .codex/, trusted ONCE in the TUI, and the dry run.
10. The known Codex facts the list must carry: SessionStart is queued at session construction and runs at the start of the FIRST TURN, so no file appears before the first prompt; hooks run only after "Trust all and continue" on the hooks review; `codex exec` cannot grant trust but works after the TUI granted it.
11. The unreachable list. Any event with no trigger is RAISED to me before the sitting, with the two options, and I take it to the lead for the user. SubagentStart and SubagentStop are the first candidates. PermissionRequest needs a session state that asks for approval, so the recipe must name the sandbox or approval setting that produces one; the S2 sitting saw NO approval prompt in the read-only sandbox.
12. Sizing. The published estimate is agent time, not user time, because agents drive. It comes from the recipe list, not from D11's figure.

L2 etb9cx, the capture campaign
13. One capture agent per sitting, Sonnet, driving through tmux by the skill's five rules. `codex --version` re-checked before every session and pasted into the report. Sessions run in the throwaway project directory, never in a repository.
14. The live store /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture is never opened. PASTURE_DB_PATH points at the scratch database. The fail-open identity fault line is expected and is not a capture failure.
15. Per capture the report gives the event, the trigger used, the time, the raw digest and the byte count, plus `ls -la` of the capture directory verbatim, the pane text at each decision, and anything unexpected.
16. Risk I hold: a sitting that produces a file for an event the recipe did not target is still evidence and is reported, never deleted. A missing stem is the finding.

L3 95tfao, clearance
17. The shape is the committed one: harness and pinned version; capture (kit digests, environment, trust, the SessionStart timing fact, one line per event with raw and committed digests); inventory; rules applied in order per fixture; secret scan with a reach control; refused classes; the fixture list; the user acceptance; the pull-request line left for the integrator.
18. Every fixture names the CLEARANCE.md PATH as its clearance, never a bare identifier. The digest is recomputed over the committed bytes.
19. Nothing is committed before the user's ACCEPT reaches the leaf. I relay the ACCEPT verbatim; the worker writes it in and commits locally; the lead pushes.
20. Risk I hold: an unclearable payload. PostToolUse carries tool OUTPUT, and the refused classes forbid a raw tool response above 4096 bytes. The recipe must choose a trigger whose output is small (for example `echo hi`, not `ls -la` of a large tree), or the event becomes unclearable and needs a user decision. I will state this to L1 so the recipe avoids it by construction.
21. Second risk: UserPromptSubmit and Stop carry prompt or message text. free-text-v1 substitutes them, but a free-text field that rule 2 does not substitute is refused outright. The inventory report is what decides; the worker runs it and does not judge by eye.

ORDER AND GATES
22. L0 runs now, alone. L1 starts after the L0 SHA gates green, because the recipe cites the catalogue the L0 leaf re-derives.
23. L2 starts only after the recipe list has my verdict and the raised list has the user's answer.
24. L3 starts when the file set is complete or the withheld list is ruled.
25. Every gate is the full suite on an archive copy, under the race lock on aura-plugins-ow5zsm, with GATE RUNNING and GATE DONE posted. A filtered run says nothing about the packages it skipped.
26. I never edit the worktree, never push, never merge, never close a task, never install a Git hook.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SUPPLEMENT 1 to the START record (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05): measured state of the Codex code at 0b33f07, from a read-only survey. Three items CORRECT the leaf text, and one adds a risk to the kit question. Every claim carries a file and a line.

1. THE IP-1 COMMENT IS ALREADY RETIRED. L0's scope item 2 asks the slice to quote and retire the "Known divergence, and why it is inert" comment. S2 did it, in commit c81704b. The catalogue now carries a "Known divergence" block at internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go:36-51 that states the true numbers: 12 registered rows, 10 with no authentic capture and no declared identity, 11 rows where the two artefacts disagree on the failure mode, and 7 rows where this source declares a BLOCKING mode and the runtime profile declares none. The retired wording is now forbidden by a test: internal/lifecycle/registration/failure_divergence_test.go:315-319 fails if the file still carries "and why it is inert" or "rejects the other". L0 must therefore NOT re-retire the comment. L0 quotes the CURRENT block in its report and closes the condition the block describes.

2. THE DEMOTED-ROW COUNT IS SEVEN, NOT EIGHT. The plan and the slice text say the evidence rule demoted 8 Codex rows. The measured set is 7, and it is exactly the 7 Codex GATE rows: PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit (internal/lifecycle/registration/failure_divergence_test.go:106-109). The test comment at :63-66 states the demoted set as "11 Claude plus all 7 Codex gates". The plan's 8 was measured before S2 moved the catalogue from ten rows to twelve. A moved ceiling falsifies claims at a distance; the derived number governs. L0 re-derives and reports what it measures.

3. THE REAL L0 WORK, RESTATED FROM THE MEASUREMENT. The catalogue labels are HAND-WRITTEN by two builders, observe and gate, at codex_0_153_0.go:64-79. The runtime profile builds every Codex row with an empty FailureEvidence (internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go:116) and lets evidenceBoundFailure demote it (internal/runtime/lifecycle.go:254-267). So the catalogue says exit-2-blocks on 7 rows that the profile runs as report-and-continue. L0 must end that by MECHANISM, not by relabelling seven literals: the catalogue's failure label derives from the same evidence rule the profile uses, so a later demotion or a later citation cannot disagree in silence. That is the standing rule that an enumeration deciding a blast radius is derived, never hand-maintained.
   THE ONE ROW THAT NEEDS A RULING BEFORE THE WORKER ACTS. PostCompact is an OBSERVATION in the catalogue (codex_0_153_0.go:117) and a GATE in the runtime profile (lifecycle_profiles_codex.go:128). The two land on the same failure arm by COINCIDENCE, which is why the divergence test deliberately excludes it (failure_divergence_test.go:58-61). A derivation that reads the profile would make the catalogue call PostCompact a gate. That is a semantic change, not a label change, and it is not what "the failure labels agree" asks for. MY RULING, which I will state in the worker prompt: L0 derives the FAILURE MODE from the evidence rule and leaves the gate-or-observation SEMANTIC alone; PostCompact stays an observation in the catalogue and the coincidence is stated plainly in the report and in the doc comment. If the lead or a reviewer wants the semantic aligned too, that is a separate decision with the host emission site as its evidence.
   MOVED-CEILING SWEEP THAT L0 OWNS. The divergence test pins totals: 22 divergent rows (:160-162) and 18 over-claiming rows (:198-200), and the Codex doc-comment counts are derived and pinned by TestTheCodexDocCommentsStateTheDerivedCounts (:283-329), which reads codex_0_153_0.go and internal/lifecycle/frontend/codex/codex.go. When the Codex over-claim ends, those totals move to the Claude-only numbers and both doc comments must state the new derived counts. The commit that moves the ceiling sweeps for every claim about it.

4. A NEW RISK ON THE KIT QUESTION (option A). The generator emits a runner only for enabled rows: internal/codegen/codex_manifest.go:75 and :91-99, with the membership filter at :300-302 and the rule stated in the doc comment at :61-66. Enabling twelve rows in a throwaway copy would therefore emit twelve runners, which is what option A wants. BUT the matchers are not all proven: codexAuthenticMatchers (codex_manifest.go:168-171) holds a proven matcher only for SessionStart ("startup") and PreToolUse ("*"). Six named events would be emitted with an EMPTY matcher string, and Stop and UserPromptSubmit with no matcher key at all (:186-194). Whether the host fires a hook whose matcher is the empty string is UNMEASURED. L1 must measure it in the dry run and in the first sitting, and must not assume it. If an empty matcher fires nothing, the fallback is the hand-shaped hooks.json of option B, with each matcher taken from the upstream source (for example the PreCompact matcher pattern "manual|auto" at codex-rs/hooks/src/events/common.rs:302). author: David Huu Pham
text:
SELF-CHECK over L1, L2 and L3 (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). I read the leaf texts against the tree and against the S2 record. Nine risks follow. Each carries a ruling or a raise.

R-1 THE TRANSPORT GAP (raised as C-1 in my START record; L1 must measure it first).
The generator writes a hooks.json row only for an enabled event. The tree's hooks.json and the installed plugin 0.0.8's copy each carry exactly the 8 enabled keys and are JSON-equal. So no live session can fire a hook for any of the 23 candidate events today. L1 measures the fix and reports it BEFORE it writes a single trigger recipe, because the recipe's expected-file column is worthless without it. L1 does not start L2.

R-2 THE COMMIT-ORDER TRAP (I rule; the lead should know, because the lead pushes).
internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/authentic_2_1_261_test.go holds a CLOSED, HAND-LISTED inventory: a map of 8 fixture names plus 3 control names, closed by require.Equal over the glob of testdata/fixtures/*_2_1_261*.json. A new cleared fixture in that directory turns that test RED at once.
Consequence: L3 cannot commit a cleared fixture without also extending that inventory, and it cannot enable the event either, because enabling is L4 and L4 waits for S3.
RULING: L3 commits the accepted fixtures AND extends the closed inventory in the same commit, so the tree stays green (the user rule: a change that is green alone is committed the same hour). The fixture is then a committed, cleared, reviewed capture that is NOT YET activated. L3 says exactly that in CLEARANCE.md and in the commit message. L3 does NOT touch claude_targets.go, the profiles or hooks.json; those are L4.
OWNERSHIP WIDENING, recorded: S4 owns internal/lifecycle/ingress/claude/** , not only its testdata subtree. The whole package is Claude-only, so no other Wave-1 slice can collide. The widening goes in the slice ownership statement in the same commit that uses it.

R-3 THE CLOSED INVENTORY IS A HAND LIST, WHICH THE STANDING RULES FORBID.
C-GUARD-REACH and the derived-enumeration rule on o8z8pn both say a guard that claims to cover "every fixture" derives its population. This one types it. It is pre-existing, so it is not an S4 defect, but S4 doubles its size and must not make it worse. RULING: L3 extends the list as the smallest green step. L4 replaces it with a derivation over the activation manifest plus a declared control set, with a non-vacuity control and a named mutation. I record the derivation as L4 work now so it is not forgotten.
Also pre-existing in the same test: require.NotContains(body, "minttea") hardcodes the capturing user's name, which the S2 structural guard was written to avoid. I record it for the batch task inamu5 and I will confirm with the lead.

R-4 PAYLOAD SIZE AND FREE TEXT DECIDE WHETHER A CAPTURE IS CLEARABLE.
The refused classes are absolute: a tool response above 4096 raw bytes, an environment dump, and any unsubstituted free text on a prompt or message event. A trigger that produces a large or interesting payload creates an UNCLEARABLE capture, which costs a live session and then a user decision to withhold.
RULING for L1: design every trigger to produce a SMALL and BORING payload. Short prompts. Tiny files. No secrets, no real paths beyond the throwaway project, no personal text. The recipe's per-event line states the expected payload size class and names every free-text field the event carries, taken from AllowedFields in the registration table, not guessed.

R-5 SOME CANDIDATE EVENTS ARE PROBABLY NOT REACHABLE FROM ONE INTERACTIVE SITTING.
My reading of the registration table says the doubtful ones are Setup, TeammateIdle, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, PermissionDenied, StopFailure, MessageDisplay, UserPromptExpansion and PostModelSwitch. I do NOT rule on any of them. L1 must probe the installed 2.1.261 binary and the hooks documentation, then RAISE one list with the two options (find a trigger together, or withhold with WithheldNoReachableTrigger plus a recorded user decision) BEFORE the sitting. A withheld row without a recorded user decision is refused by the code, so the list must reach the user in time.
The Elicitation pair stays withheld by ruling and is NOT on the capture list.

R-6 PreModelSwitch ALREADY CARRIES A HOST CITATION FOR EXIT-2 BLOCKING.
S2 recorded it from the installed binary's own hook-event table. So the event is a documented gate. L1 gives it a trigger (a model change) and states that citation in its line, so L4 cannot demote it by accident.

R-7 THE HOST VERSION MUST REACH THE FILE NAME.
CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION is undocumented and is absent from a live session's environment (bm1ci8). Without the export every captured file is named "unknown" and the whole batch is wasted. RULING: the recipe exports it from `claude --version` in the capture shell, and the DRY RUN proves the stem carries 2_1_261 before any live session starts. This is a precondition, not a check at the end.

R-8 THE CAPTURE AGENT IS ITSELF A CLAUDE CODE SESSION.
It must unset CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT in the tmux launching shell, and it must NEVER export PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR or PASTURE_DB_PATH in its own shell. Only the tmux pane that runs the target session carries them. It must never touch the live store at ~/.local/share/pasture. It must never modify the installed plugin.

R-9 GATE LOCK AND WHO RUNS WHAT.
L1 and L2 run no race suite, so they take no gate lock. L3 runs the full suite and MUST take the lock on ow5zsm: read the newest comment, wait while a GATE RUNNING has no GATE DONE, post GATE RUNNING, then GATE DONE with counts. Every worker prompt carries this.
L1 is everyday work: Sonnet. L2 is everyday work driven through tmux: Sonnet, one agent per sitting. L3 is complex tooling and judgement: Opus.

EXIT for this dispatch: I post "S4 L1-L3 DONE: <sha>" and wait for the lead's word that S3 merged.

MODEL: OPUS, not Sonnet. The lead's dispatch called recipe writing an everyday leaf and allowed Opus if the trigger derivation is harder than expected. It is harder, for three measured reasons.

EVERY NEW ASSERTION WITH ITS MUTATION AND THE QUOTED RED MESSAGE. Six mutations, each driven in a throwaway archive copy.
1. The role mirror is total. MUTATION: add a role arm to the task store's own enum with no rendering of its own. RED: "enum mirror task-store AssignmentRole -> gateauthority.RoleFromToken: 1 source arm(s) have no mapping on the mirror side: [AssignmentRole(4)]; add the mapping for each named arm".
2. The import edge points one way. MUTATION: add an import of internal/tasks to types.go. RED: "this package imports the task store: [types.go imports github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/tasks]; want no such import, because the store imports this package and the edge must point one way only".
3. The phase mapping is total. MUTATION: drop one phase arm from the gate enum. RED, both checks at once: "PhaseFromProvenance(unscoped) refused a phase the task store calls valid; want a mapping, because every stored phase must be readable by the gate" and "enum mirror task-store Phase -> gateauthority.PhaseFromProvenance: 1 source arm(s) have no mapping on the mirror side: [unscoped]; add the mapping for each named arm".
4. Every enum zero is invalid. MUTATION: let the role validity predicate accept the zero. RED: "RoleUnset reports itself valid; want invalid, because a role nobody set must not pass for a real slot".
5. Index completeness is turned into a refusal in one place. MUTATION: stop looking at Complete() inside RequireComplete. RED: "RequireComplete accepted a snapshot whose index is not complete; want a refusal, because an authority built on a partial index can miss an assignment that exists".
6. An out-of-range phase is refused, not renamed. MUTATION: drop both range checks from PhaseFromProvenance. RED: "PhaseFromProvenance(-1) = (phase-unset, true); want (phase-unset, false), because a negative phase is outside the store's range" and "PhaseFromProvenance(13) = (TaskPhase(14), true); want (phase-unset, false), because a phase one above the store's top arm was written by a newer build and must be refused, not renamed".

DERIVED POPULATIONS AND THEIR NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, as the standing constraint requires.
- The task-store ROLE arms are PARSED from the store's own source with go/ast over internal/tasks, every const spec typed AssignmentRole, ordinal order, the invalid zero skipped. Controls: the parse must visit at least one file, and it must find at least two arms; either failure is a hard stop naming what was read. Parsing rather than walking String() is deliberate, and mutation 1 shows why: an arm added with NO rendering is still found, and it is exactly that arm the check exists to catch.
- The task-store PHASE arms are derived from the store's own IsValid predicate, walked from zero until it refuses, with a runaway ceiling of 1024 that is a safety stop and not the arm count, and a hard stop if fewer than two arms are found or the ceiling is reached.
- This package's own three enums publish their arms from an unexported upper sentinel, and the zero-value test asserts each derived list is non-empty and that every arm in it is valid and renders a real token rather than the numeric fallback.
- The import check parses this package's own production files, so a file added later is covered with no edit; it hard-stops if it visited no file or found no import at all, because either would pass while proving nothing.

BYTE IDENTITY FOR THE 12 ENABLED EVENTS: UNCHANGED. This unit adds one package that nothing imports yet. No handler, transport, encoder, generated artefact or fixture is touched, make generate reports drift 0, and no host byte can differ.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE TASK TEXT, WITH REASONS
D1 The test file is an EXTERNAL test package (gateauthority_test), not an internal one. Reason: it imports internal/tasks to read the source role enum, and internal/tasks will import gateauthority at L5. Only an external test package may close that loop; an internal one would become a real import cycle the day the store imports this package. The import-direction check is unaffected: it parses PRODUCTION files only, so a test-only import can never satisfy it.
D2 The role mirror bridges through the CANONICAL PAYLOAD TOKEN (RoleFromToken), not through a direct type mapping. Reason: a direct mapping would need one package to import the other, which is the cycle this package exists to break. The token is what the store actually writes into the assignment-start event, so the bridge is the real one, not a test fixture.
D3 CatchUpPageSize is declared HERE, at 64, although the catch-up itself is later work. Reason: the ruling puts the constant in gateauthority, and no later unit owns this file. Its comment states the reason the ruling gives: the journal module's fact-page bound governs the decision and evidence page API, not the task-event query the catch-up uses, whose limit has no cap and rejects only a negative value.
D4 RequireComplete and IncompleteIndexError are added beyond the listed type set. Reason: the task text asks for "a contract test that a Snapshot reporting Complete() == false is never usable to build an Authority". A test alone cannot enforce that; one production function that turns the typed fact into a refusal can, and the later Reader calls it. Without it the requirement would have been a comment.
D5 Each enum carries an unexported upper sentinel and an exported arm-list function. Reason: the standing constraint that a derived population reads the product's own source. The sentinel is the single place the arm count lives, so a new arm needs no second edit.

STALE CITATIONS CORRECTED
S-8 is confirmed and corrected: provenance.Phase is at pkg/ptypes/enums.go, not ptypes/enums.go, and its first arm PhaseRequest is 0 with 13 arms through PhaseUnscoped, so the mirror offset of one is right. The code cites no line number; it reads the store's own IsValid predicate instead, so the citation cannot go stale again.
The task text cites the source role enum at material_events.go:141-151. That is where it is today, and the parse does not depend on it: it reads every const spec of that type anywhere in internal/tasks, so the enum may move file without breaking the check.
S-11 is applied: the catch-up page size is pasture's own constant, and the reason is recorded in the source.
