author: David Huu Pham
text:
SUPPLEMENT 2 to the START record (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05): the S2 shapes this slice copies, and every Codex fact S2 measured. Distilled from aura-plugins-vwy7zt, aura-plugins-462y6n, aura-plugins-kthzht and aura-plugins-gt001f. L1, L2 and L3 follow these shapes; a worker that changes a shape says why.

1. THE RECIPE-LIST SHAPE (from vwy7zt, comment of 2026-09-05 07:40, with the kit records at 07:48 and 08:31 and the correction at 13:02)
A header promise in capitals, then a purpose line that says the list is copy-pasteable and marks what was already dry-run as PROVEN. Then:
 Section 0, state of readiness: one bullet per harness with a state token (READY NOW, READY WHEN, NOT YET) and the evidence for it.
 Section 1, setup, once: create the capture directories (pasture never creates one; a missing directory is a warning and no capture); build the binary outside the repository from a named head and check `--version` prints the development string, not an installed release; the exports for every capture shell with a paragraph that says WHY the scratch database exists and that predicts the known fail-open identity fault line; then the DRY RUN into a separate dryrun directory, with the command, an EXPECT line quoting the notice text and the expected file name, and an "if the notice does not print" list (binary version; the directory must be absolute, must exist, must be outside every repository). The dryrun directory is emptied afterwards; hand-piped bytes are never fixtures.
 Section per harness: a SETUP paragraph naming the transport, how the host version reaches the dispatch, the project directory, the `--version` line to paste, and the launch; then the event lines in ONE fixed form, "state -> command -> observable file", numbered; a deliberate-set-up sentence where the trigger needs a contrived state; then a Report line naming the exact `ls -la` command and what to expect.
 Section: version re-check before EVERY session, with the expected strings and the rule that a moved host is a STOP.
 Section: the time estimate, itemised then totalled, then compared with the plan's figure.
 Section: raised questions as lettered options with a recommendation and a reason; the worker recommends and does not choose.
 The list closes with a coverage statement that says plainly whether any event lacks a reachable trigger.
 THE KIT RECORD, five parts: RECORD (head SHA, the archive-copy method, the exact root edits); the transport diff of the copy against the head, where anything beyond version strings is a STOP; a SHA-256 per file; the exact lines to REPLACE in the recipe with a checksum the operator runs; and NOTES.
 The file-name pattern is <harness>_<snake_event>_<version_with_underscores>.<n>.json, written by internal/handlers/capture_sink.go about :171-175.
 The unreachable escape has a mechanism behind it: a test asserts every event enabled at the start is enabled again at the end or carries a closed-set withheld reason, and the enabled floor holds unless a row names WithheldNoReachableTrigger with the user's decision recorded.

2. THE SITTING-REPORT SHAPE (from 462y6n, 12:24 and 12:34)
RESULT (n of n files, per harness, with "no file is missing, no extra file is present"); KIT AND ENV (binary path and digest; the exports verified by echo in the pane before launch; the kit digests re-verified in the project directory; and the measurement that the LIVE STORE was not touched); VERSION LINES taken immediately before each session, pasted as a shell transcript; then per harness the tmux session name and the working directory, numbered steps, an UNEXPECTED entry with its diagnosis and source citation where one occurred, the prompt text verbatim with the send method, the time each file appeared after Enter, a payload check naming the fields seen, and a side note for anything that could mislead a reader; then the `ls -la` listing and one sha256 line per file; then HOUSEKEEPING (dry-run files made and deleted, kit files unmodified, the expected fault line, the tmux sessions killed).

3. THE CLEARANCE SHAPE (from 462y6n 12:35, 13:08, 13:10; the committed record is in the tree)
The clearance order has six items: choose ONE file per event and say why (default the .1 file) and name the unchosen files as captured-and-not-used with their raw digests; derive any controls; run the procedure exactly as AGENTS.md states it; state the operator truthfully with no agent names and no process words; RECORD, do not fix, anything outside the slice; and post CLEARANCE READY with full evidence, committing NOTHING until the verbatim ACCEPT arrives.
CLEARANCE READY states, per fixture, one fixed line: event | trigger | time | raw sha256 with size | committed sha256 with size | rules applied. Then the inventory counts, the secret scan with a REACH CONTROL (a planted key shape turning the scan RED, quoting the message, and the copy discarded), the refused-class checks with the measured largest tool response, the sidecar field list, and what it waits on.
THE COMMITTED FILE has nine headings in a pinned order: Harness and pinned version; Capture; Inventory; Rules applied, in order; Secret scan; Refused classes; Fixtures; User acceptance; Pull request. A template test pins the headings.
TWO CORRECTIONS S2 PAID FOR, and this slice must not repeat: the RECORD must not re-introduce what the rule removed (the first drafts carried the real home path; the record's own paths use the tilde spelling and the fixture bytes keep the /home/user placeholder), and the "no user name survives" assertion is a COMMITTED STRUCTURAL GUARD that carries no user name in it, while the check that names the real user stays a tool of the clearing run and is never committed.
home-path-v1 rewrites every spelling of the home directory: the absolute path, the relative spelling, the directory slug a host derives from a path, and any occurrence inside free text. free-text-v1 replaces each flagged free-text string by placeholder text of the same raw length. The digest is recomputed over the COMMITTED bytes, so every line carries two digests and two byte counts.

4. THE USER'S ACCEPT SHAPE (462y6n 13:13)
Three questions were put: the acceptance wording verbatim for the batch or per harness; whether the substitution rule keeps its name; and the spelling of directory paths in the record. The user answered "1. seems fine / 2. keep home-path-v1 / 3. sure, use tilde". The answers went into the record verbatim, with the date and the questions, in a fenced block. This slice asks its own questions in the same shape and never paraphrases an answer.

5. CODEX FACTS S2 MEASURED, all at tag rust-v0.153.0 (commit 41e22fe), for the recipe leaf
 - SessionStart is QUEUED at session construction (codex-rs/core/src/session/session.rs:1623) and RUNS at the start of the FIRST TURN (codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs:264). It does NOT run at process start. S2 first wrote the recipe wrongly, waited 30 s after trust and 45 s after a relaunch, and got nothing. Do not relaunch waiting for a file.
 - Hooks run only after the project is TRUSTED once in the TUI. The startup menu says "Hooks need review"; the operator types 2 to move the highlight to "Trust all and continue", then Enter. The host writes trust_level = "trusted" for the project into ~/.codex/config.toml. `codex exec` CANNOT grant trust; after the TUI granted it, `codex exec` works.
 - The trust gate is in codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs (hook_trust_status); a handler runs only when the status is Trusted or Managed.
 - The hooks feature is Stable and default-enabled at 0.153.0 (codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs about :1144-1148). hooks.json is read from the config folder (discovery.rs about :343): $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json or <project>/.codex/hooks.json.
 - Hook subprocesses inherit the environment minus Codex-internal names (codex-rs/hooks/src/registry.rs about :77), so the PASTURE_ variables reach the hook.
 - The generated runners live at .codex/hooks/events/<Event>.sh and pass --host-version 0.153.0. The stem the sink writes comes from that argument, so a stale runner writes a FALSE version into an operator-visible file name. S2 REFUSED capturing with false stems and corrected the kit instead.
 - Kit digests S2 ran, byte-identical to the committed files: hooks.json 0afc4938056274f3a3e9989d16630bb1080dfd7b8976cd6b1ae7fdae6ac79dce; SessionStart.sh e51312d01df72ac8983c89e4cd1532b0c4f102d6b2abc25e79ca6239951486db; PreToolUse.sh 18bfdd48a63ab3f45e52d677ec4be35372fd25df5291c753f0c61441a9835566.
 - The captured shapes: SessionStart carries session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, model, permission_mode, source, and NO free text. PreToolUse carries the same plus turn_id, tool_name, tool_input.command (the one free-text field), tool_use_id.
 - NO APPROVAL PROMPT appeared: the read-only sandbox ran `ls -la` without asking. THIS MATTERS FOR THIS SLICE: PermissionRequest needs a session state that actually asks for approval, so the recipe must name the sandbox or approval setting that produces one, and must prove it in the pane text.
 - Codex's own `ls -la` answer listed files the disk did not hold; that is a sandbox view, not a real directory. Do not read a host answer as a measurement of the file system.
 - Identities on unproven rows stay ABSENT (option A). The source-declared field names live in the row comment as the cited SHAPE, never as a declared identity. A guard states that a source-derived catalogue entry never implies authentic runtime proof.

6. LESSONS S2 CLOSED WITH, that bind this slice
 - Dry-run the real host before you book anyone's time. Two of three transports were broken in a way only a live host showed.
 - Never hand-edit a transport. Build the kit in a throwaway archive copy of a committed head, run the generator there, build outside the repository, and record the head, the edits, the diff and a digest per file. Anything in the diff beyond the expected token is a STOP.
 - Correct a published recipe by a NEW comment that cites the source, not by an edit.
 - Capture more than you commit; choose one file per event and say why; name the unchosen files.
 - State what the host really did, even when it is not what you asked for.
 - Turn a discipline into a gate: a promise that a test does not hold is not a control.
 - Record, do not fix, what is outside the slice. Text-only MINOR findings go to aura-plugins-inamu5.
 - A mutation that hits a comment is not a mutation.
 - The archive copy needs a git repository with an origin remote for some tests to run.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
KIT RULING APPLIED TO L1 (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). The lead ruled that the capture kit is built in a throwaway archive copy with all 47 registered OpenCode rows enabled and `make generate` (option A), and that hand-shaped callbacks in the throwaway project are the fallback if the generator refuses (option B). Nothing hand-shaped is committed. I VERIFIED THE PREMISE MYSELF BEFORE APPLYING IT, and I add four measurements that change how much work each option is.

## The premise is TRUE, and here is the mechanism
Measured in .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts at head 0b33f07, in the exported factory:
  async event(callback) { if (callback.event?.type !== "session.created") return; ... }
and the only other registered key is "tool.execute.before". So a live session with the COMMITTED transport produces exactly two files, whatever the operator triggers. The other 31 event-bus observations are dropped by that one equality test, and the other 14 named callbacks are not registered at all. A capture campaign run on the committed plugin would have produced 2 files and looked like 43 unreachable events. That is the failure the ruling prevents.

## Four measurements, for the worker and for whoever reviews the kit
M-1. OPTION A IS LIKELY TO SUCCEED, because the proof generator never verifies evidence that does not exist yet. internal/lifecycle/activation/internal/proofgen/proofgen.go parses the two proof tables with go/parser and reads exactly two fields per row, `ordinal` and `arm`. It never opens a fixture and never resolves a test name. Its refusals are: a duplicate ordinal, a duplicate arm name, an ordinal of 0, an ordinal outside the harness range (OpenCode 200-299), a missing table, and a row shape it cannot read. So 45 new arms at ordinals 202 upward, with placeholder fixture and test strings, are not refused at generation time.
M-2. THE ACTIVATION CORPUS LOADER NEVER RUNS DURING GENERATION. internal/lifecycle/activation/corpus.go LoadCorpus is test-time evidence tooling and no codegen path calls it. A fixture that does not exist yet therefore cannot fail `make generate`.
M-3. THE REAL RISK IN OPTION A IS COMPILE ORDER, NOT REFUSAL. opencode_targets.go will name CaptureProof and ProductionProof constants that do not exist until the proof generator writes them, so the package does not compile until that step has run. The worker is told to run `go generate ./internal/lifecycle/activation/...` first in the copy if `make generate` stops earlier, and to report exactly what it ran.
M-4. OPTION B IS NOT 45 HAND-SHAPED CALLBACKS. It splits in two, and the two halves cost very different amounts.
  - The 31 event-bus observations need ONE line: the `event` guard is a single equality test. Widening it is the whole change.
  - The 14 named callbacks are NOT uniform. Each Hooks key in ~/codebases/sst/opencode/packages/plugin/src/index.ts at v1.18.29 has its own parameter shape: some take one input, some take an input and an output object, and the output object differs per key. A hand-shaped callback whose signature does not match the host's call will throw inside the host. The worker must read each key's declaration before shaping it. This is the part of option B that can go wrong quietly, so it is written into the prompt.

## What changed in the L1 prompt
Section 1 (SETUP) is rewritten. It now carries the kit rule, both options in the lead's order, the refusal-quoting requirement before any fallback, the four measurements above, and a new requirement: the recipe list states the kit digests (head SHA, the enablement edit, the plugin SHA-256, the binary SHA-256) AND the number of callbacks the generated plugin carries. That number is expected to be 47, and a smaller number is a STOP before any sitting starts. My earlier sentence "no kit is needed" was true only about the version roots; it is corrected to "no ROOT MOVE is needed", and the kit is now required for a different reason.

The prompt file is unchanged in every other section. It is /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s6/prompt-worker-s6-l1.md.

text:
AMENDMENT 1 to the L1 dispatch order (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05), carrying the team lead's kit ruling. The worker prompt file /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s4/prompt-worker-s4-l1.md IS PATCHED and now carries this text. Nobody had been spawned when I patched it. Spawn from the patched file.

THE LEAD'S RULING, adopted whole:
OPTION A first. Build the capture kit in a throwaway archive copy with ALL 33 registered Claude rows enabled in claude_targets.go, then `make generate`. Expect 33 keys in the kit's hooks.json.
OPTION B is the fallback, and only if the generator REFUSES an unproven row. Quote the refusal verbatim, then hand-shape the missing hooks.json entries in the throwaway project directory, byte-identical to the generated shape except for the event name, and record every hand-shaped entry per line in the sitting report and in CLEARANCE.md. NOTHING HAND-SHAPED IS EVER COMMITTED.
THE MECHANISM. The installed plugin 0.0.8's hooks.json will NOT carry these entries. That is expected. The session must be launched so the KIT's hooks.json reaches Claude. Two acceptable paths: a project-level .claude/settings.json in the throwaway project directory, or the plugin's hooks file replaced inside a THROWAWAY COPY of the plugin. L1 states which one it used and confirms it verified it by dry run.

ONE SUPERVISOR CLARIFICATION, which changes nothing in the ruling. Enabling all 33 rows in the KIT is a generator input, not a product decision. Elicitation and ElicitationResult stay withheld in the product and stay OFF the trigger list. If a live session emits either of them, L1 records the file and does not propose it as a fixture.

TWO NUMBERS, reconciled so nobody conflates them later.
25 = registered and not enabled. That is the set the KIT transport must register. It is the number the lead used.
23 = capture candidates. That is 25 minus the Elicitation pair.
Both are correct and they answer different questions.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULINGS RECEIVED AND THE BAR I WILL HOLD THE RECIPE LIST TO (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## Rulings from the lead, recorded here so they live on Beads and not only in a message
- C-2 WITHDRAWN. The "43 rows before S2 ... S6 STOPS" note in the slice body is superseded by the comment record. The tree holds 47 rows. No worker acts on the body's STOP condition.
- C-3 RULED. Leaf u5ju80 is a NON-REGRESSION leaf. The plugin's fault-record sentence is already true at 0b33f07; the duty is to keep it true through this slice's regeneration and to pin it.
- C-5 CONFIRMED. Leaf rtcnpj is superseded on both points: agents drive the sittings, and the version is 1.18.29 under floor admission. I write the L2 prompts that way.
- The capture-kit ruling stands as the lead wrote it, and my four measurements on it are in the comment above.

## The bar. I will check the recipe list against these eight items and publish the result either way.
1. POPULATION DERIVED. The list states which artefact it read and re-measures 32 observations plus 15 named callbacks, 47 total, 2 enabled, 45 to capture. A count that differs is a STOP, not a reconciliation.
2. EVERY ROW HAS A TRIGGER OR IS RAISED OR IS UNCERTAIN. No row is silently absent. The three groups add up to 45.
3. EVERY TRIGGER IS CITED. For an observation, the upstream file and symbol that PUBLISHES the event. For a named callback, the file and symbol that CALLS the key. An uncited trigger is marked as a guess by the worker, or it is a finding by me.
4. FILE NAMES ARE RIGHT. The stem rule is read from CaptureStem and snakeCase, and the list states the one hyphenated stem, opencode_installation_update-available_1_18_29.
5. THE KIT IS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. The head SHA, the enablement edit, the plugin SHA-256, the binary SHA-256, and THE NUMBER OF CALLBACKS THE GENERATED PLUGIN CARRIES. Expected 47. A smaller number stops every sitting. If option B was used, the refusal is quoted verbatim and every hand-shaped callback is listed with the host signature it matches.
6. THE LOAD CHECK IS A PRECONDITION. The first sitting shows, from the host's own log, that the plugin loaded. The earlier campaign measured a plugin that never loaded while every proof stayed green.
7. THE ESTIMATE IS BUILT UP. Per sitting, from the list, with a total and a sitting count, and a plain statement if it exceeds the plan's working figure of about 3 to 4 hours.
8. SETUP IS COMPLETE AND SAFE. Absolute pre-existing capture directory outside every repository; a scratch database and never the live store; the dry run into its own directory with its contents deleted afterwards; the expected fail-open fault line stated so that nobody reads it as a capture failure.

An item that fails is a finding I post on the leaf with what would close it. I do not fix the list myself.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L1 DISPATCH ORDER (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). Worker worker-s5-l1, Sonnet, this leaf only. The prompt is at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s5/prompt-worker-s5-l1.md and the team lead spawns from it.
WHY SONNET: the leaf writes no production code and changes no repository file. It reads the host source, measures two host behaviours, and publishes a list in a shape that already exists. The judgement calls are raised, not taken.
WHY IT RUNS IN PARALLEL WITH L0, and not after it: this leaf owns NO file, and the catalogue re-derivation that L0 performs changes no trigger, no registered event and no enabled row. The two leaves are disjoint by construction. The capture campaign waits on host time, so the recipe is on the critical path and the catalogue work is not. The worker reads the slice worktree and never writes it; it builds only in a throwaway archive copy outside every repository.
THE TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT COME FIRST, before any list text: (1) can a kit built in a throwaway archive copy with all twelve Codex rows enabled pass `make generate`, and does the host fire a hook whose generated matcher is the empty string; (2) does the runtime emit SubagentStart and SubagentStop at 0.153.0 at all, since the upstream events directory holds no payload file for either.
RAISED, NEVER GUESSED: any event with no reachable trigger goes to me with the two options from the leaf text, and I take it to the lead for the user before a sitting is booked. PermissionRequest needs a session state that truly asks for approval; the earlier sitting saw none because the read-only sandbox did not ask. PostToolUse must use a trigger with SMALL output, because the clearance rules refuse a raw tool response above 4096 bytes whatever the substitution.
The published estimate is AGENT time, because agents drive the sittings.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROGRESS (worker-s6-l1, 2026-09-05). Derivation and kit measurement done; the recipe list follows in the next comment.

DERIVED POPULATION, re-measured, agrees with the start record: internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_opencode.go openCodeLifecycleMappings holds 32 rows built by openCodeObservationMapping and 15 rows built by openCodeNamedMapping, 47 in all; .opencode/pasture-opencode-activation.json at contract opencode/1.18.29 holds 47 rows, 2 enabled (session.created, tool.execute.before) and 45 withheld. So 45 to capture: 31 observations and 14 named callbacks. The 15 named names equal the 15 event keys of the Hooks interface in ~/codebases/sst/opencode/packages/plugin/src/index.ts at v1.18.29, exactly. The 32 observation names equal, exactly, the 32 members of the Event union in packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts at that tag; that union is the type of the plugin event hook's payload.

KIT: OPTION A FAILED, MEASURED. In a throwaway archive copy of 0b33f07 I enabled all 47 rows in internal/lifecycle/activation/opencode_targets.go and ran make generate. It returned 0 and REFUSED NOTHING. The activation report then held 47 enabled rows, but the generated plugin was BYTE-IDENTICAL to head and still carried only 2 callbacks. The plugin body is a fixed template in internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go, not a loop over the enabled set, so enablement cannot add a callback. That is a third outcome the ruling did not name: not a generated 47-callback plugin, and not a refusal. OPTION B APPLIES.

MEASURED, and it makes the campaign simpler: a hook invocation for a WITHHELD event still writes its capture. On a fresh scratch database the identity fault makes every route fail open with exit 0 and empty output, for enabled and withheld rows alike, and the capture is written first. So one binary built from head serves all 47 rows, and no named callback can throw and break a sitting.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
OPENCODE 1.18.29 TRIGGER-RECIPE LIST, 45 events (worker-s6-l1, 2026-09-05). This is the list the capture sittings work through and the list you read before they start. Copy-pasteable.

EACH SESSION RECORDS THE RAW HOST PAYLOADS TO A DIRECTORY OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY. THE BINARY PRINTS A NOTICE ON STANDARD ERROR WHILE IT RECORDS. NOTHING IS COMMITTED OR PUSHED BEFORE THE CLEARANCE STEP AND YOUR ACCEPT.

## 0. How the population was derived, and the four numbers

I derived the rows from the tree. I did not hand-list them.
- internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_opencode.go, function openCodeLifecycleMappings, is the source of truth. It holds 32 rows built by openCodeObservationMapping (surface SurfaceOpenCodeCatchAllSSE, non-blocking, observe-only) and 15 rows built by openCodeNamedMapping (surface SurfaceOpenCodeNamedOutput, blocking, throw-fail-fast). 47 rows in all.
- .opencode/pasture-opencode-activation.json publishes the same 47 rows at contract opencode/1.18.29: 2 enabled (session.created, tool.execute.before) and 45 withheld.
- Cross-check against the host: the 15 named names equal, exactly, the 15 event keys of the Hooks interface in ~/codebases/sst/opencode/packages/plugin/src/index.ts at tag v1.18.29. The 32 observation names equal, exactly, the 32 members of the Event union in packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts at that tag; that union is the declared type of the plugin event hook's payload. Neither set has a name the other lacks.

Rows derived 47. Events to capture 45. Events RAISED to you 14. Events UNCERTAIN 1 (it also has a recipe). Recipes published 31.

## 1. SETUP, once

### 1.1 The capture kit. OPTION B applies. I measured it.

The committed plugin at 0b33f07 registers callbacks for the 2 enabled events only, so a live session through it cannot capture the other 45.

I tried OPTION A first, in a THROWAWAY ARCHIVE COPY of head 0b33f07 (never the live worktree). In the copy I enabled all 47 rows in internal/lifecycle/activation/opencode_targets.go, with a capture-proof and a production-proof declaration for each, and ran make generate.

MEASURED RESULT: make generate returned 0. It REFUSED NOTHING, so there is no refusal text to quote. The activation report in the copy then held 47 enabled rows. But the generated plugin .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts was BYTE-IDENTICAL to head and still carried exactly two callbacks. The reason is in internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go: the plugin body is a fixed template string with two hand-written callbacks, sessionCreated and toolExecuteBefore. The enabled set is only checked, at GenerateOpenCodeHooksModule, to confirm those two rows carry proofs; it is never iterated. Enablement therefore cannot add a callback.

That is a third outcome the capture-kit ruling did not name: not a 47-callback generated plugin, and not a refusal. It is a silent no-change. I report it and do not smooth it over. It also tells the later generator work what it must add.

So OPTION B. The kit plugin is hand-shaped in the throwaway project directory, and nothing hand-shaped is ever committed.
- Kit plugin path: /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-plugin/pasture-lifecycle.ts
- SHA-256: 0882a8b47db0969f5824fd9b7ab811bcd51266ff0f1f9f9e5e3a37e3d693eb6f
- It parses under Bun (bun build --target=bun, 1 module, 5.35 KB).

WHAT IS HAND-SHAPED, in full. Everything above the marked line is the generated plugin at head, byte for byte: the same header, the same PASTURE_RUNTIME_CONTRACT, the same METADATA, the same invokeLifecycle, the same acceptProceed, the same sessionCreated, the same toolExecuteBefore, the same default export object. Below the line:
1. kitObservation(callback): one pass-through bus callback. It keeps the generated observation shape (try, invokeLifecycle, catch, console.error) and changes only the event name, which it reads from callback.event.type. One callback covers all 31 uncaptured observations, because the host delivers every bus event through the single event key.
2. kitNamed(event, input, output): one named callback body. It keeps the generated named shape (invokeLifecycle then acceptProceed) and changes only the event name. It sends { input, output }.
3. Fourteen one-line named callbacks in the returned object, one per uncaptured named key, each calling kitNamed with its own name: chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, permission.ask, command.execute.before, shell.env, tool.execute.after, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.provider.small_model, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition.
4. The event key now calls kitObservation instead of the session.created filter. tool.execute.before still calls the generated toolExecuteBefore, unchanged.

ONE DEVIATION, STATED. The generated toolExecuteBefore sends { input, output: { args } } and restores output.args afterwards, because that row is a mutation gate. kitNamed sends { input, output } whole and mutates nothing. tool.execute.before is already captured, so no capture uses the generic path for it.

The version string is 1.18.29 by generation, not by hand: openCodeHostVersion() reads runtime.OpenCode1_18_29().Versions().Min(). The proof is in the file: every invokeLifecycle line carries --host-version "1.18.29", and the same literal appears in the untouched generated part above the marked line.

### 1.2 The binary. ONE binary, from head, outside the repository.

Built from the worktree head 0b33f07:
  nix develop <worktree> -c env GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o <outside-path>/pasture ./cmd/pasture
- Prebuilt at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/bin/pasture-head
- SHA-256: 0411482772b75caff4a5dab869c590475dfb0b8df721e8da049281a50044920b
- "$PASTURE_BIN" --version must print: pasture version devel. An installed release binary records nothing.

NO SECOND BINARY IS NEEDED, and this is measured, not assumed. I piped a payload for the withheld event session.idle through this binary and it wrote opencode_session_idle_1_18_29.1.json and exited 0. On a fresh scratch database the identity-bootstrap fault makes EVERY route fail open with exit 0 and EMPTY output, for enabled and withheld rows alike, and the capture is written before that step. Two consequences: a withheld row captures normally, and acceptProceed sees an empty body and returns, so no named callback can throw and break a sitting.

### 1.3 The three environment variables, exported in EVERY capture shell

  export PASTURE_BIN=/home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/bin/pasture-head
  export PASTURE_DB_PATH=/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/scratch/pasture.db
  export PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR=/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/<sitting>

PASTURE_DB_PATH must be a scratch database outside the repository. NEVER the live store at ~/.local/share/pasture. PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR must be ABSOLUTE, must ALREADY EXIST, and must be outside every git repository; pasture never creates it and refuses with one warning naming the rule it refused on. Create the directories first:
  mkdir -p /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/{scratch,dryrun,s1,s2,s3,s4,s5,s6,s7,s8,project}

### 1.4 The throwaway project directory

  mkdir -p /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project/.opencode/plugins
  cp /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-plugin/pasture-lifecycle.ts /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project/.opencode/plugins/
  sha256sum /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project/.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts
The digest must equal 0882a8b47db0969f5824fd9b7ab811bcd51266ff0f1f9f9e5e3a37e3d693eb6f there, in the project, not only in the kit.
The project also needs, for later sittings: git init and one commit; README.md and NOTES.md; a Program.cs and a probe.csproj; a .opencode/command/probe.md.

### 1.5 The one-event dry run, into a SEPARATE directory

  printf '%s' '{"event":{"type":"session.idle","properties":{"sessionID":"dry-run"}}}' | PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR=/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/dryrun "$PASTURE_BIN" hook lifecycle --harness opencode --event session.idle --host-version 1.18.29
  ls /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/dryrun

EXPECT on standard error, once: pasture: capture mode is recording this session to /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/dryrun
EXPECT one file: opencode_session_idle_1_18_29.1.json
IF THE NOTICE DOES NOT PRINT: check that "$PASTURE_BIN" --version says devel; check that PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR is absolute, exists, and is outside every git repository. The binary prints one warning that names the rule it refused on. Correct it and repeat. This step is PROVEN: I ran it.
DELETE the dryrun directory's contents afterwards. Hand-piped bytes are never fixtures.

### 1.6 The expected fault line

On a fresh scratch database each hook prints one long fail-open fault that ends in: Lifecycle ingress cannot resolve Pasture's persisted system identity. The host proceeds and the capture is written before that step. It is NOT a capture failure. The plugin's child process inherits the screen's standard error, so this line and the capture notice are drawn inside the OpenCode screen until the next redraw. That is cosmetic and the capture is not affected.

### 1.7 A SAFETY WARNING YOU MUST READ BEFORE SITTING 2

Four named callbacks carry the host's PROVIDER CONTEXT in their input, and that context can hold a live credential.
- Measured: packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts passes input.provider to chat.params (line 115) and to chat.headers (line 135). packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts passes a provider object to experimental.compaction.autocontinue (line 500). packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts passes toPublicInfo(provider) to experimental.provider.small_model (line 1949).
- Measured: the provider Info schema at packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:1091 declares options: Record<String, Any> and an optional key field, and provider.ts:931 builds options as { baseURL, apiKey: token }. toPublicInfo at line 1117 removes functions and symbols only; it does NOT remove a key.
So a sitting run against a provider that authenticates with an API key in configuration can write that key into the captured bytes.
GOOD NEWS on one of them: the chat.headers OUTPUT starts as an empty object, so the output side carries no secret. The risk is on the INPUT side only.
This is question Q3 below. It is a decision for you, not for me.

## 2. THE 45 RECIPES, grouped by sitting

Read every row as: native name, kind, state before the trigger, trigger, expected file, evidence.
KIND is OBSERVATION (event bus, non-blocking) or NAMED (blocking callback).
EVIDENCE names the upstream file and symbol I read at ~/codebases/sst/opencode, tag v1.18.29.
The stem rule is measured, and section 2.0 states it.

### 2.0 THE FILE-NAME RULE, measured

I read internal/handlers/capture_sink.go, function CaptureStem (line 171) and function snakeCase (line 182). The stem is opencode_<snake_event>_1_18_29. snakeCase replaces each dot with an underscore and lowers the name. IT DOES NOT TOUCH A HYPHEN, and the coordinate pattern at line 50, ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, admits one. So installation.update-available produces:
  opencode_installation_update-available_1_18_29.1.json
That is the ONLY hyphen in the corpus. I verified it on the built binary: the file appeared with that exact name. NOBODY MAY LATER "CORRECT" IT.
The number before .json is one above the highest already present for that stem, so repeats arrive as .2, .3 and so on. Extra numbered files are expected; a MISSING STEM is the finding.

### SITTING 1. THE PLUGIN MUST LOAD. About 10 minutes.

This sitting captures nothing. It exists because the generated plugin never loaded in a real host before the fix at https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/issues/142, while every offline proof stayed green. A sitting that starts without this check can produce zero files and look correct.

State: the project directory of 1.4, with the kit plugin in place and its digest verified there.
Steps:
1. opencode --version. It must print 1.18.29. Anything else is a STOP.
2. Note the current size of the host log: wc -c ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log (it was 404 MB on 2026-09-05, so always read the TAIL, never the whole file).
3. Start opencode in the project directory. The FIRST start installs the plugin npm package into the project's .opencode directory. That takes a moment. It is the host's own behaviour.
4. Send one short prompt.
5. Read the tail of the log and require BOTH:
   - a line msg="loading plugin" that names pasture-lifecycle, and
   - NO line message="failed to load plugin" for pasture-lifecycle.
   Expect to see an unrelated failed-to-load line for opencode-claude-auth; that is a different plugin and is not this campaign's concern.
6. Require at least one file in the sitting's capture directory.
If the TUI shows no prompt after about ninety seconds, quit and start again in the same directory. Two non-interactive dry runs stalled at init during the earlier campaign and a relaunch recovered. In the same shell, opencode run '<prompt>' is a proven fallback.
IF THE PLUGIN DID NOT LOAD: STOP and report. Do not run sitting 2.

### SITTING 2. ONE ORDINARY TURN. 15 events. About 15 minutes.

This is the largest sitting by far. One prompt that makes one tool call produces fifteen of the forty-five.

State: a fresh session, in the project directory. The project's opencode.json must NOT set small_model (see row 6). Capture directory .../s6/s2.
Trigger, in order:
  T1. Start opencode (or run opencode run) and send: Read the file README.md in this directory and tell me its first line.
  T2. Wait for the answer to finish and for the session to go idle.
Files that arrive together from that one turn:

 1. chat.message — NAMED. Fires once per user message, before the parts are resolved. -> opencode_chat_message_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/prompt.ts:999 plugin.trigger("chat.message", ...).
 2. chat.params — NAMED. Fires once per LLM request. -> opencode_chat_params_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/llm/request.ts:114.
 3. chat.headers — NAMED. Fires once per LLM request, straight after chat.params. -> opencode_chat_headers_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/llm/request.ts:134. READ THE SAFETY WARNING IN 1.7.
 4. experimental.chat.system.transform — NAMED. Fires once per LLM request, before chat.params. -> opencode_experimental_chat_system_transform_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/llm/request.ts:69.
 5. experimental.chat.messages.transform — NAMED. Fires once per step of the turn. -> opencode_experimental_chat_messages_transform_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/prompt.ts:1255. WARNING: the output carries every message of the session. On a long session this file is large. Keep the session short.
 6. experimental.provider.small_model — NAMED, CONDITIONAL. Fires while the host generates the session TITLE from the first user message, and only when the configuration does not set small_model and the title agent declares no model of its own. -> opencode_experimental_provider_small_model_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: provider/provider.ts:1935 getSmallModel returns early when cfg.small_model is set, and triggers the hook at line 1949; session/prompt.ts:220 calls getSmallModel on the title path. STATE REQUIREMENT: no small_model in the project or global configuration, and the session must be NEW (title generation runs on the first real user message only, prompt.ts:206).
 7. tool.definition — NAMED. Fires ONCE PER VISIBLE TOOL, each time the tool list is built for the model. Expect MANY numbered files, one per tool. -> opencode_tool_definition_1_18_29.1.json, .2, .3, ... Evidence: tool/registry.ts:318.
 8. experimental.text.complete — NAMED. Fires when an assistant text part ends. -> opencode_experimental_text_complete_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/processor.ts:530, case "text-end".
 9. tool.execute.after — NAMED. Fires after each tool call returns. -> opencode_tool_execute_after_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/tools.ts:121 to :123 and session/prompt.ts:389. WARNING: the output carries the tool's title, output text and metadata. A read of a large file makes a large capture. README.md must be SHORT (a few lines).
10. session.status — OBSERVATION. Fires on every status change, so at least twice: busy, then idle. -> opencode_session_status_1_18_29.1.json, .2. Evidence: session/status.ts:41.
11. session.idle — OBSERVATION. Fires when the status is set to idle, right after session.status. -> opencode_session_idle_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/status.ts:43.
12. session.updated — OBSERVATION. Fires on every session patch, and touch patches the session on activity. -> opencode_session_updated_1_18_29.1.json (expect several). Evidence: session/session.ts:746.
13. message.updated — OBSERVATION. Fires on every message write. -> opencode_message_updated_1_18_29.1.json (expect several). Evidence: session/session.ts:631.
14. message.part.updated — OBSERVATION. Fires on every part write. -> opencode_message_part_updated_1_18_29.1.json (expect many). Evidence: session/session.ts:637.
15. session.diff — OBSERVATION. Fires at step 1 of every turn, from the forked summarize call. -> opencode_session_diff_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/summary.ts:114, reached from session/prompt.ts:1253.

Verification for this sitting: 15 distinct stems present, every name carrying 1_18_29. If row 6 is absent, check the configuration for small_model and repeat with a NEW session; if it is still absent, it moves to the raised list and I want to know.

### SITTING 3. SHELL AND PERMISSION. 2 events. About 15 minutes.

State: the project directory, plus a project opencode.json that asks for permission on the shell tool:
  { "permission": { "bash": "ask" } }
Evidence for the key: packages/core/src/v1/config/config.ts:128 declares permission, and packages/core/src/v1/config/permission.ts declares the per-tool actions ask, allow and deny with a bash key.
Capture directory .../s6/s3.
Trigger:
  T1. Start opencode and send: Run the shell command ls -la and tell me what you see.
  T2. The host asks for permission. ANSWER IT (choose once).

16. shell.env — NAMED. Fires when the shell tool builds its environment, before the command runs. -> opencode_shell_env_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: tool/shell.ts:417 to :420, and session/prompt.ts:554 to :557 for a shell part inside a prompt.
17. permission.replied — OBSERVATION. Fires when the reply is recorded. -> opencode_permission_replied_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: permission/index.ts:115 events.publish(Event.Replied, ...), where Event is PermissionV1.Event (permission/index.ts:10).

NOTE, and it matters for the raised list: the request side of this pair publishes permission.asked, NOT permission.updated. Evidence: packages/schema/src/v1/permission.ts:61. See raised row R4.

### SITTING 4. FILES, WATCHER, BRANCH AND LANGUAGE SERVER. 4 events. About 20 minutes.

State: the project directory MUST BE A GIT REPOSITORY with at least one commit and a branch. It must also hold Program.cs and probe.csproj for row 21. Capture directory .../s6/s4.
Trigger, in order:

18. file.edited — OBSERVATION. Fires when the edit, write or patch tool changes a file. -> opencode_file_edited_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: tool/edit.ts:115 and :159, tool/write.ts:68, tool/apply_patch.ts:256, all events.publish(FileSystem.Event.Edited, ...).

Evidence: packages/core/src/filesystem/watcher.ts:88 to :90 (add, change, unlink), and tool/edit.ts:116, tool/write.ts:69, tool/apply_patch.ts:262.
20. vcs.branch.updated — OBSERVATION. Fires when the watcher sees a change to a file whose name ends in HEAD and the branch value has changed. -> opencode_vcs_branch_updated_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: project/vcs.ts:319 to :329: the listener filters on Watcher.Event.Updated and on the file ending in HEAD, then publishes Event.BranchUpdated only when the new branch differs. MEASURED on this machine: gopls, typescript-language-server, pyright and the json server are NOT on PATH, but ~/.local/share/opencode/bin already holds csharp-ls and vscode-eslint. Hence probe.csproj and Program.cs. The Go route (lsp/server.ts:358) would work too, but only by downloading gopls from the network, which I do not recommend inside a capture sitting.

### SITTING 5. COMPACTION. 3 new events. About 15 minutes.

State: a session that already holds at least one completed turn (reuse the sitting-2 session, or send one prompt first). Capture directory .../s6/s5.

Fires after compaction succeeds and before the synthetic continue message, on the non-replay path. -> opencode_experimental_compaction_autocontinue_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/compaction.ts:500, guarded by if (!replay) at line 497. READ THE SAFETY WARNING IN 1.7: its input carries the provider object.

(experimental.chat.messages.transform fires again here, at session/compaction.ts:379. That is expected and arrives as a further numbered file.)

### SITTING 6. A PROJECT COMMAND AND A TODO LIST. 3 events. About 20 minutes.

State: the project must hold a command file. The host scans the glob {command,commands}/**/*.md (config/command.ts:14), so create .opencode/command/probe.md with a short template, for example: Say the word probe and stop.
BEFORE USING IT, verify the command appears in the TUI's slash-command list. That check costs nothing and it protects the sitting.

26. command.executed — OBSERVATION. Fires after the command's prompt returns. -> opencode_command_executed_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/prompt.ts:1474 events.publish(Command.Event.Executed, ...); the definition is packages/schema/src/v1/legacy-event.ts:8 CommandExecuted.

Evidence: session/todo.ts:50 and packages/core/src/session/todo.ts:56; the definition is packages/schema/src/session-todo.ts:19. STATE REQUIREMENT: the todowrite tool must be available to the agent.

### SITTING 7. UNDO, THEN A NEW PROMPT, THEN DELETE. 3 events. About 20 minutes.

The two removal events do NOT fire on the undo itself. They fire on the NEXT prompt, when the host cleans up the reverted range. That ordering is the whole recipe; without it the sitting produces nothing.
State: a session with at least two completed turns. Capture directory .../s6/s7.
Trigger, in order:
  T1. Press the leader key then u (keybind messages_undo is "<leader>u", keybind.ts:147; the leader is ctrl+x, keybind.ts:41). session.diff fires again here (revert.ts:78).
  T2. Send any new short prompt. THIS is what fires the two removals.
  T3. Press the leader key then l to open the session list (keybind session_list is "<leader>l", keybind.ts:90), select a session you do not need, and press ctrl+d (keybind session_delete, keybind.ts:94).

28. message.removed — OBSERVATION. -> opencode_message_removed_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/session.ts:857 removeMessage, called from session/revert.ts:110 cleanup, which is called from session/prompt.ts:1056 at the start of a prompt.

STATE REQUIREMENT: it fires only when the revert point is a PART, not a whole message (revert.ts:112, if session.revert.partID && target). Undo from inside an assistant message rather than at a message boundary.
30. session.deleted — OBSERVATION. -> opencode_session_deleted_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/session.ts:622 events.publish(SessionV1.Event.Deleted, ...); the TUI reaches it at packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-list.tsx:307 sdk.client.session.delete.

### SITTING 8. AN ERROR TURN. 1 event. About 10 minutes.

State: the project directory. This one is easiest non-interactively. Capture directory .../s6/s8.
Trigger:
  opencode run --agent this-agent-does-not-exist 'hello'

31. session.error — OBSERVATION. -> opencode_session_error_1_18_29.1.json. Evidence: session/prompt.ts:642 publishes Session.Event.Error with the message "Agent not found" before throwing, inside createUserMessage. A second, equally good trigger: opencode run --model no-such-provider/no-such-model 'hello', which reaches session/prompt.ts:604 with the message "Model not found". Both flags exist on the run command (cli/cmd/run.ts:165 model, :170 agent).

## 3. THE RAISED LIST. 14 events with no trigger reachable from an interactive session or from opencode run. YOU DECIDE.

I do not choose. For each row I give what I read that shows it is not reachable, and your options. Beside the two options the leaf names, several rows have a THIRD, measured option, and I state it where it exists.

The standing two options for every row below are:
 (a) find a trigger together, or
 (b) withhold the event with WithheldNoReachableTrigger and your decision recorded in the clearance record.

### Group R-A. THE HOST DOES NOT DEFINE THESE TWO EVENTS AT 1.18.29. This is a catalogue finding, not only a trigger gap.

R1. lsp.client.diagnostics — OBSERVATION. At tag v1.18.29 the ONLY occurrence of this string in the whole checkout is the auto-generated SDK type file packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts:25 (EventLspClientDiagnostics). There is NO Event.define for it: packages/schema/src/lsp-event.ts defines lsp.updated and nothing else, and its Definitions inventory holds Updated alone. There is no publish site anywhere in packages/opencode/src or packages/core/src. Expected file, if it ever arrives: opencode_lsp_client_diagnostics_1_18_29.1.json.
R2. permission.updated — OBSERVATION. Same shape. The only occurrence is packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts:440 (EventPermissionUpdated). The permission events the host actually defines and publishes are permission.asked and permission.replied (packages/schema/src/v1/permission.ts:61 and :62), and the v2 pair permission.v2.asked and permission.v2.replied (packages/schema/src/permission.ts:43 and :44). Expected file, if it ever arrives: opencode_permission_updated_1_18_29.1.json.
WHY THEY ARE IN OUR CATALOGUE: our 32 observations were taken from the SDK Event union, and that union is the declared payload type of the plugin event hook. The two names are members of that union but have no producer at this tag. THIRD OPTION for R1 and R2: treat them as a catalogue defect at 1.18.29 and record a withholding reason that says the host declares the name but never emits it, rather than one that says we could not find a trigger. That is a truer sentence, and it is your call whether the vocabulary should carry it.

### Group R-B. THE HOST EMITS THESE, BUT NOT ON THE BUS THE PLUGIN LISTENS TO.

The plugin's event hook is fed by events.listen inside packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:255 to :262, and it drops any event whose location directory is not the plugin's own directory. That listener is the EventV2 bus. The rows below are emitted on the raw GlobalBus, or synthesised inside an HTTP route, and never enter EventV2. No plugin can see them.

R3. installation.updated — OBSERVATION. Evidence: cli/upgrade.ts:43 GlobalBus.emit("event", { directory: "global", payload: { type: Installation.Event.Updated.type, ... } }). Raw GlobalBus, and the directory is the literal string "global", which can never equal a project directory. -> opencode_installation_updated_1_18_29.1.json.
R4. installation.update-available — OBSERVATION. Evidence: cli/upgrade.ts:16 and :31, the same raw GlobalBus emit with directory "global". -> opencode_installation_update-available_1_18_29.1.json. THIS IS THE ONE HYPHENATED NAME IN THE CORPUS.
R5. server.connected — OBSERVATION. Evidence: it is not published at all. It is the synthetic FIRST FRAME of the server's event stream, written at server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/event.ts:70 as Stream.make({ ..., type: "server.connected", ... }), and again at handlers/global.ts:41. It exists only for a reader of that HTTP stream. -> opencode_server_connected_1_18_29.1.json.
R6. server.instance.disposed — OBSERVATION. Evidence: project/instance-store.ts:79 to :91, emitDisposed uses GlobalBus.emit directly; the HTTP route re-injects it into the stream at handlers/event.ts:47 to :57. It never enters EventV2. -> opencode_server_instance_disposed_1_18_29.1.json.
THIRD OPTION for R5 and R6: capture them from the host's own event stream instead of from the plugin, by reading the server's /event stream while a session runs. That is authentic host output, but it is a DIFFERENT TRANSPORT from every other row, and our surface constant for observations is named SurfaceOpenCodeCatchAllSSE, which suggests the design once expected exactly that. This is a design question, not a capture question, and it belongs to you and to the plan.

### Group R-C. REACHABLE ONLY BY CALLING THE HOST'S OWN LOCAL HTTP API.

These five rows ARE published on the EventV2 bus with a project location, so a plugin WOULD see them. Nothing in the interactive session and nothing in opencode run makes them fire. Their only producer is an HTTP route on the instance server, which a desktop or editor client calls.

R7. tui.prompt.append — OBSERVATION. Evidence: server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/tui.ts:37 and :88, publishing TuiEvent.PromptAppend from the POST route /tui/append-prompt (groups/tui.ts:37). -> opencode_tui_prompt_append_1_18_29.1.json.
R8. tui.command.execute — OBSERVATION. Evidence: handlers/tui.ts:32 and :90, from POST /tui/execute-command (groups/tui.ts:44). -> opencode_tui_command_execute_1_18_29.1.json.
R9. pty.created — OBSERVATION. Evidence: packages/core/src/pty.ts:242, reached from the POST /pty create route (handlers/pty.ts:69). MEASURED: the TUI never opens a pty; there is no pty caller anywhere in packages/tui/src. -> opencode_pty_created_1_18_29.1.json.
R10. pty.updated — OBSERVATION. Evidence: packages/core/src/pty.ts:250, from the update route. -> opencode_pty_updated_1_18_29.1.json.
R11. pty.exited — OBSERVATION. Evidence: packages/core/src/pty.ts:232, when the pty process exits. -> opencode_pty_exited_1_18_29.1.json.
R12. pty.deleted — OBSERVATION. Evidence: packages/core/src/pty.ts:149, from the delete route. -> opencode_pty_deleted_1_18_29.1.json.
THIRD OPTION for R7 to R12: drive the host's own local HTTP API from the capture shell while a session runs. The payload bytes would still come from the host and would still travel through the plugin, so the capture is authentic; only the ACTION is an API call rather than a keystroke. I estimate about one hour of agent time for all five plus a pty life cycle, mostly in finding the instance port and the exact request bodies. I DO NOT CHOOSE. If you rule this in, it is one more sitting.

### Group R-D. ONE ROW WITH TWO PRODUCERS, NEITHER OF WHICH I CAN GUARANTEE.

R13. tui.toast.show — OBSERVATION. -> opencode_tui_toast_show_1_18_29.1.json. It has exactly two producers at this tag. The first is the same HTTP route family as group R-C: handlers/tui.ts:82 and :92, POST /tui/show-toast. The second IS reachable from a session, but only with a particular set-up: mcp/index.ts:304 and :315 publish TuiEvent.ToastShow when a configured MCP server answers with an authentication or client-registration error. That needs a real remote MCP endpoint that demands OAuth, which I cannot verify offline and which reaches the network from a capture sitting. Options: the two standing ones, the HTTP-API option of R-C, or configure an OAuth-demanding MCP server for one sitting.

### Group R-E. A REGISTERED NAMED GATE THAT THE HOST NEVER CALLS.

R14. permission.ask — NAMED, BLOCKING. -> opencode_permission_ask_1_18_29.1.json. The key is declared in the host's own plugin contract at packages/plugin/src/index.ts:261, with the signature (input: Permission, output: { status: "ask" | "deny" | "allow" }). MEASURED: NOTHING IN THE HOST CALLS IT. There is no plugin.trigger("permission.ask", ...) anywhere in packages/opencode/src or packages/core/src, and every trigger call site in the tree passes a literal name (I read all of them). The permission flow at permission/index.ts:100 publishes the bus event permission.asked and waits on a deferred; it consults no plugin.
WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MOST. Our catalogue gives this row Blocking, SemanticGateConsultation and FailureThrowFailFast. That is a claim that the host asks us for a decision and honours a refusal. At 1.18.29 the host never asks. Options: the two standing ones, or a third: record it as a declared-but-uncalled extension point, so the withholding sentence says what is true instead of saying we could not find a trigger.

## 4. THE UNCERTAIN GROUP. 1 event.

U1. lsp.updated — OBSERVATION. I am sure of the mechanism and unsure of this machine. The publish site is exact (lsp/lsp.ts:293, once per newly spawned client). What I cannot promise is that a language server will actually start here. MEASURED: gopls, typescript-language-server, pyright and the json server are not on PATH; ~/.local/share/opencode/bin already holds csharp-ls and vscode-eslint. So sitting 4 tries the C-sharp route, which needs no download. WHAT I WOULD NEED IN ORDER TO DECIDE: run sitting 4 row 21 and look. If a client spawns, the row is an ordinary capture. If none spawns, the row joins the raised list with the evidence that no admissible server exists on this machine, and you get the same two options.
I put this row in its own group on purpose. An event wrongly called unreachable buys a withheld row that a five-minute action could have captured; an event wrongly called reachable buys a failed sitting. This one is neither yet.

## 5. VERSION RE-CHECK

Run opencode --version IMMEDIATELY BEFORE EVERY SESSION and paste the line into the sitting report. The expected answer is 1.18.29. I measured 1.18.29 on this machine today. A host that has moved is a STOP AND A REPORT, not a capture.

## 6. THE AGENT-TIME ESTIMATE, built up from this list

Agents drive the sittings, so this is AGENT time. No step below needs you, except the decisions in section 7.

  Setup, kit copy, digests, directories, dry run          45 min  (DONE; the kit and the binary already exist)
  Sitting 1, plugin-load proof                            10 min
  Sitting 2, one ordinary turn, 15 events                 15 min
  Sitting 3, shell and permission, 2 events               15 min
  Sitting 4, files, watcher, branch, language server, 4   20 min
  Sitting 5, compaction, 3 events                         15 min
  Sitting 6, project command and todo, 3 events           20 min
  Sitting 7, undo then prompt then delete, 3 events       20 min
  Sitting 8, an error turn, 1 event                       10 min
  Inventory, per-file check, sitting reports              30 min
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                                                 3 h 20 min, in 8 sittings after the setup

IS THE PLAN'S 3-TO-4-HOUR FIGURE WRONG? NOT FOR WHAT IT COVERS, AND YES FOR WHAT IT PROMISES. The figure holds for the 31 events that have a recipe. It does NOT buy 45 events, because 14 of the 45 have no trigger reachable from a session and one more is uncertain. Stated plainly:
  - 31 events, this list, about 3 h 20 min of agent time. The plan's figure is right.
  - If you rule that the 6 HTTP-API rows (R7 to R12, plus R13 by the same route) are captured through the host's own local API, add about 1 hour and one more sitting. About 4 h 20 min.
  - The remaining 7 rows (R1 to R6 and R14) cannot be bought with more time at this host version. They need a decision, not hours.
So the honest number is 3 h 20 min for the reachable set, and the plan's figure should no longer be read as buying 45 of 45.

## 7. RAISED QUESTIONS. Options only. I do not choose.

Q1. THE 14 RAISED EVENTS (section 3). For each group: (i) find a trigger together; (ii) withhold with WithheldNoReachableTrigger and your decision in the clearance record; (iii) for R5 to R13, capture through the host's own event stream or local HTTP API, which costs about one more hour and uses a different transport from every other row; (iv) for R1, R2 and R14, record a withholding reason that states the measured truth (the host declares the name and never emits it, or declares the gate and never calls it) rather than one that says we could not find a trigger.

Q2. THE 47-OF-47 TARGET. The slice target is 47 of 47. This list shows that at most 33 of 47 can be captured from a plugin at this host version, and 39 of 47 if the HTTP-API route is ruled in. Options: (i) keep the target at 47 and treat the raised rows as withheld-with-decision, which still counts them as classified but not as captured; (ii) restate the target as 33 of 47 captured plus 14 withheld with recorded decisions; (iii) something else you name. This is a plan-level question and it should reach the plan, not only this slice.

Q3. THE PROVIDER CREDENTIAL (section 1.7). Four named callbacks can carry a live provider credential in their input: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.compaction.autocontinue and experimental.provider.small_model. Options: (i) run those sittings against a provider whose credential is NOT an API key in configuration, so the bytes never hold one; (ii) run them as they are and let the clearance step refuse them, which makes four rows WithheldUnclearablePayload; (iii) capture them and clear them by value substitution, which the clearance rules allow only for home paths and free text today, so it would need a new rule and a new decision. I recommend nothing. I record that option (ii) turns four capturable rows into withheld rows, and that option (i) costs only the choice of provider for one sitting.

Q4. THE GENERATOR (section 1.1). Enabling all 47 rows and regenerating produced a plugin BYTE-IDENTICAL to head. That is a silent no-change: the plugin template does not iterate the enabled set. The later generator work in this slice must add that loop, or the enablement it produces will be a claim with no callback behind it. Options: (i) treat this as an input to that work and record it now; (ii) raise it as a defect in its own right. Either way I want it written down before the generator is touched.

text:
RECIPE LIST READY: aura-plugins-ae098k (worker-s6-l1, 2026-09-05). The full list is the newest comment on that leaf. Four numbers, then the two things that need a ruling before L2 starts.

FOUR NUMBERS. Rows derived 47 (32 observations from openCodeObservationMapping, 15 named callbacks from openCodeNamedMapping; the activation report agrees, 2 enabled and 45 withheld). Events to capture 45. Events RAISED 14. Events UNCERTAIN 1 (lsp.updated; it also has a recipe). Recipes published 31, in 8 sittings, about 3 h 20 min of agent time after the setup.

KIT OPTION: B. Option A was MEASURED and it failed in a third way the ruling did not name. In a throwaway archive copy of 0b33f07 I enabled all 47 rows in internal/lifecycle/activation/opencode_targets.go and ran make generate. It returned 0, refused NOTHING, produced a 47-enabled activation report, and produced a plugin BYTE-IDENTICAL to head with the same 2 callbacks. The plugin body in internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go is a fixed template with two hand-written callbacks; the enabled set is only checked for those two and is never iterated. So there is no refusal text to quote, and enablement cannot add a callback. The kit plugin is hand-shaped: one pass-through bus callback that carries callback.event.type, one generic named body, and 14 one-line named callbacks. SHA-256 0882a8b47db0969f5824fd9b7ab811bcd51266ff0f1f9f9e5e3a37e3d693eb6f, at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-plugin/pasture-lifecycle.ts. Nothing hand-shaped is committed.

ONE BINARY IS ENOUGH, measured: a withheld event still writes its capture. On a fresh scratch database the identity fault makes every route fail open with exit 0 and empty output, enabled or withheld, and the capture is written first. Binary at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/bin/pasture-head, SHA-256 0411482772b75caff4a5dab869c590475dfb0b8df721e8da049281a50044920b, --version prints "pasture version devel". A second consequence: acceptProceed sees an empty body and returns, so no named callback can throw and break a sitting.

TWO ITEMS THAT NEED A RULING BEFORE L2 (both are in the list as Q2 and Q3).
1. THE TARGET. At most 33 of 47 can be captured through a plugin at this host version (2 enabled plus 31 recipes), or 39 of 47 if the local HTTP API route is ruled in. Seven rows cannot be bought with time at all. The slice target of 47 of 47 needs restating or an explicit withheld-with-decision reading.
2. THE PROVIDER CREDENTIAL. Four named callbacks carry the host's provider context in their INPUT, and that context can hold a live API key: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.provider.small_model. Measured at provider.ts:1091 (options is Record<String, Any>, plus an optional key field), provider.ts:931 (options built as { baseURL, apiKey }) and provider.ts:1117 (toPublicInfo removes functions and symbols only). Running sitting 2 against an API-key provider writes that key into the capture directory. The chat.headers OUTPUT is empty at trigger time, so the risk is on the input side only.

ALSO WORTH THE SLICE RECORD, for L4 and L5. The 14 raised rows split into five measured groups, and three of them are catalogue findings, not trigger gaps: lsp.client.diagnostics and permission.updated have NO Event.define and NO publish site at v1.18.29 (they exist only in the generated SDK type union, which is where our 32 observations came from); installation.updated, installation.update-available and server.instance.disposed are emitted on the raw GlobalBus and server.connected is synthesised inside the HTTP event route, so none of them enters the EventV2 bus the plugin listens to (plugin/index.ts:255-262); and permission.ask is declared in the host's plugin contract (packages/plugin/src/index.ts:261) but is NEVER CALLED anywhere in the host, while our catalogue gives it Blocking, SemanticGateConsultation and FailureThrowFailFast. The five pty and tui rows are on the EventV2 bus with a project location but have no producer other than an HTTP route.

I edited no repository file and committed nothing. The raised list is a user item and goes to the lead.

text:
L1 VERDICT (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05): ACCEPTED, with three findings that must close BEFORE sitting 1, and two items escalated to the lead for the user. The list meets seven of my eight published items and exceeds the bar on the first three. I re-measured the load-bearing claims myself rather than taking them; the results are below.

## What I verified myself, and what I found
V-1. OPTION A CANNOT ADD A CALLBACK. CONFIRMED, and this is the most valuable thing in the report. internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go builds the plugin from a FIXED template string (`const module = ...`) with two hand-written callbacks. The enabled set is read once, only to refuse when the two selected handlers lack proof: `if !enabled[sessionEvent.Kind] || !enabled[toolEvent.Kind]`. The enabled set is never iterated. So enabling 47 rows produces 47 enabled rows in the activation report and a byte-identical plugin with 2 callbacks. THE RULING'S OPTION A WAS SOUND AS AN INSTRUCTION AND FALSE AS A PREMISE, and neither the lead nor I caught it. My own M-1 and M-2 were correct about the generator refusing nothing and wrong in the conclusion I drew from them: I checked what would REFUSE and never checked what would EMIT. The worker checked the output. That is the lesson, and it is the same one this plan already records: a gate that passes because it ran nothing is worse than a red one.
V-2. R14 permission.ask IS DECLARED AND NEVER CALLED. CONFIRMED. `trigger("permission.ask"` has ZERO occurrences in the whole checkout at v1.18.29. The only occurrences of the name are the interface declaration at packages/plugin/src/index.ts:261 and one documentation file. The `permission.ask(` at session/processor.ts:372 is the Permission module's own method and not a plugin trigger. Our catalogue gives that row Blocking, SemanticGateConsultation and FailureThrowFailFast, so it claims the host asks us for a decision that the host never asks for. That is a host-contract truth finding for L5 and L7, not only a trigger gap.
V-3. THE CREDENTIAL PATH IS REAL. CONFIRMED. session/llm/request.ts:114 passes `provider: input.provider` into the chat.params trigger input, and :134 does the same for chat.headers. provider/provider.ts builds provider options as `{ baseURL, apiKey: token }`, and toPublicInfo (provider.ts:1117) strips only functions, symbols, undefined and bigint. Nothing removes a key from options.
V-4. AND THE CLEARANCE BACKSTOP DOES NOT COVER IT. This is mine to add, and it changes the severity. internal/lifecycle/ingress/inventory.go commits NINE secret shapes: a private key block, two AWS shapes, two GCP shapes, two GitHub shapes, the Anthropic `sk-ant-` shape, and a JSON web token. There is NO generic `apiKey` assignment shape and no bare `sk-` shape. So a provider key that is not one of those nine passes the secret scan SILENTLY, and the recorded model on this machine at the earlier sitting was not an Anthropic one. The scan cannot be relied on as the safety net here. The decision must be taken BEFORE the bytes are written, not after.

## THREE FINDINGS. Each must close before sitting 1.
F-1 THE KIT CALLBACK COUNT IS NOT STATED. The report gives the kit plugin's SHA-256 and the binary's SHA-256, which is right, but not the kit path and not the number of callbacks the hand-shaped plugin carries. That count is the gate I published in advance, and it exists for one reason: a kit that silently carries 2 callbacks is indistinguishable from a good one until a sitting produces nothing. STATE the kit path, the callback count, and the list of hand-shaped callbacks with the host signature each one matches.
F-2 THE KIT PLUGIN IS NOT YET PROVEN TO LOAD. Hand-shaping is exactly the change that can break the host's loader rule, which is the defect this epic already paid for once: the loader reads the default export first and refuses a module whose exports it cannot accept, and the earlier Bun proofs never crossed the loader. Before sitting 1, prove from the HOST'S OWN LOG that the hand-shaped plugin loaded, and prove that at least ONE hand-shaped callback actually fired by producing its file. A digest proves the bytes; only the host proves the plugin.
F-3 DO NOT REST THE SITTING DESIGN ON A DEFECT. The claim "one binary serves all 47" is TRUE, and the reason given is the wrong one. The report rests it on the identity-bootstrap fault making every route fail open. The DURABLE reason is that the sink records the payload BEFORE anything is evaluated, which is stated in AGENTS.md and which the activation substrate work made true for withheld events on purpose. Rest it on that. A scratch database that later resolves an identity would change the fault line and not the capture, and a sitting designed around the fault would then look broken when it is not. Restate the sentence in the list.

## The five items that PASS, recorded so the record is complete
Population derived and cross-checked in BOTH directions against the host at v1.18.29 (the 15 named names against the Hooks keys, the 32 observation names against the SDK Event union) — that is stronger than I asked for. The three groups sum to 45. The triggers carry file and symbol citations; I spot-checked two and both held. The one hyphenated stem is named. The estimate is built up per sitting and says plainly what it does and does not buy.

## ESCALATED TO THE LEAD, for the user. I do not choose either.
E-1 THE 47-OF-47 TARGET CANNOT BE MET THROUGH A PLUGIN AT THIS HOST VERSION. At most 33 of 47 through the plugin, 39 of 47 if the local HTTP API route is ruled in, and seven rows cannot be bought with time at all. Two of those seven are catalogue rows the host does not define at 1.18.29.
E-2 A PROVIDER CREDENTIAL CAN REACH THE CAPTURE BYTES on four named callbacks, and the committed secret scan does not cover it.

text:
ACK (worker-s6-l1, 2026-09-05). I read the two comments in full: the kit ruling with M-1 to M-4, and the eight-item bar. The recipe list was already published before they arrived, so I am now re-running option A exactly as M-3 prescribes, checking my kit against M-4 key by key, and I will post the result either way. Three things I can already answer.

M-3, COMPILE ORDER: it did not bite, and here is why. The Makefile target already runs the proof generator BEFORE the codegen step. Makefile lines 20 to 27, in order: go generate ./internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract; go generate ./internal/lifecycle/activation/...; go generate ./internal/codegen/...; then the three target packages and the metamodel. So the activation proof generator writes the missing CaptureProof and ProductionProof constants before anything needs the package to compile. My run returned 0 and stopped nowhere. I am repeating it from a fresh archive copy with the two steps run SEPARATELY, so that the record states exactly what I ran, and I will post both command lines and both return codes.

M-1 AND M-2 HELD, MEASURED, and that is the point: the generator did NOT refuse. It accepted 47 enabled rows with placeholder fixture and test strings, wrote a 47-enabled activation report, and then produced a plugin BYTE-IDENTICAL to head. So the outcome is not "refusal" and not "47 callbacks". It is a third one: acceptance with no effect. The cause is in internal/codegen/opencode_hooks.go, where the plugin body is a fixed template string holding two hand-written callbacks, and the enabled set is read only to check that those two carry proofs (GenerateOpenCodeHooksModule). Nothing iterates the enabled set. I will restate this with the fresh command record.

BAR ITEM 5, AND A CORRECTION I RAISE RATHER THAN DECIDE. The gate says the list states the number of callbacks the generated plugin carries, expects 47, and stops every sitting on fewer. I measure 2, so by that gate the sittings STOP. But I do not think 47 is a reachable number for ANY correct OpenCode plugin at v1.18.29, and the reason is in the host contract, not in our generator: the host delivers all 32 event-bus observations through ONE key, "event", whose payload carries the native type (packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:259, hook["event"]?.({ event: { id, type, properties } })). There is no per-event key for an observation, so 32 of the 47 rows can never have a callback of their own. The measurable quantities are two, and I will state both: REGISTERED KEYS and ROWS COVERED. The committed plugin carries 2 registered keys and covers 2 rows. My kit plugin carries 16 registered keys (one "event", one "tool.execute.before", and 14 named) and covers 47 rows. I ask you to rule whether the gate reads on registered keys, on rows covered, or on something else. I do not change the gate myself.
