author: David Huu Pham
text:
L0 REPORT (worker-s5-l0, 2026-09-05). One commit, 3135e55 on slice/rp2tju-s5, base 0b33f07. Six gates green on an archive copy of that SHA, under the race lock.

1. THE DERIVATION SEAM
The seam is codexFailureReader in internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go. It builds the runtime Codex lifecycle contract once, walks the profile's OWN event catalog (runtime.CodexLifecycleEvents), and returns a by-name reader of one field. The catalogue's observe and gate builders now set Failure: failure(name) in place of a literal.
WHAT IT READS: mapping.Failure() only, which is the EFFECTIVE arm the evidence rule produced for that row.
WHAT IT DOES NOT READ: the profile's blocking mode, its gate-or-observation semantic, its mutation mode, its stop-loop policy, its ordering, its reconciliation and its identities. Those stay declared in the catalogue. This is the supervisor ruling in 4.2 held by construction, not by care.
A name the profile does not declare stops the build of the contract with a message that names the event, both files, the cost (no Codex manifest can be generated and no Codex hook can be admitted) and the repair. That message is pinned by a test, because it is operator-facing text this change introduced.
PRECEDENT: the OpenCode catalogue already derives its whole row from the runtime mapping (internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/opencode_1_18_29.go:36). Codex now derives one field of it.

2. THE MEASURED DEMOTED-ROW COUNT, DERIVED
I derived it, I did not copy it. Method: for every registered Codex row, read runtime.LookupLifecycleFailure and count the rows whose DeclaredMode blocks by exit code and whose effective Mode does not.
- Rows the evidence rule DEMOTES: 8. They are UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStop, Stop. Every Codex row the profile declares Blocking is demoted, because no Codex row cites evidence.
- Rows where the CATALOGUE stated a blocking exit code and the profile did not: 7. They are the same list without PostCompact, which the catalogue calls an observation. This is the SEVEN of SUPPLEMENT 1, and I measured it independently.
- Rows whose label MOVED in this commit: 11. The 7 gates from exit-2-blocks to report-and-continue, and 4 observations (SessionStart, SubagentStart, SessionEnd, Interrupt) from report-and-continue to strict-hook-failure, which is the arm the Codex strict-command surface gives a non-blocking row. PostCompact does not move: report-and-continue on both sides before and after.
FINDING ON THE TWO NUMBERS, because they look contradictory and are not. CHANGELOG.md states "all eight Codex gates now report instead of blocking". That sentence counts the RUNTIME PROFILE's blocking rows, and that count is 8 today and was 8 at the ten-row catalogue. SUPPLEMENT 1's seven counts the CATALOGUE's gate rows. Both are true of different populations, so the CHANGELOG sentence is NOT stale and I did not change it.

3. EVERY CHANGED ROW, WITH ITS UPSTREAM CITATION
All at tag rust-v0.153.0 of github.com/openai/codex, commit 41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715, read in /home/minttea/codebases/openai/codex. First path is the emission site (the function that builds the hook request), second is the wire payload the host serializes. The same table is now committed in the catalogue.
  SessionStart      codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:124  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_start.rs:130
  UserPromptSubmit  codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:661  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/user_prompt_submit.rs:83
  PreToolUse        codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:184  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs:177
  PermissionRequest codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:246  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/permission_request.rs:171
  PostToolUse       codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:285  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/post_tool_use.rs:152
  PreCompact        codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:528  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/compact.rs:126
  SubagentStart     codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:124  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_start.rs:156
  SubagentStop      codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:376  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/stop.rs:183
  Stop              codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:376  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/stop.rs:152
  SessionEnd        codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:455  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_end.rs:63
  Interrupt         codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:486  codex-rs/hooks/src/events/interrupt.rs:75
PostCompact did not move; its sites are hook_runtime.rs:565 and compact.rs:207, and they are in the table too.
Two shared emission sites, measured and stated: SessionStart and SubagentStart come from one function, because the host dispatches a thread-spawn subagent start through the pending session-start path (hook_runtime.rs:128-140); Stop and SubagentStop come from one function, by the stop-hook target (hook_runtime.rs:384-392, stop.rs:41-51).
IDENTITIES ARE UNCHANGED. Ten rows still declare none. The upstream field shapes are cited in row comments and are declared nowhere; SessionEnd and Interrupt stay identity-free.

4. MUTATION-RED EVIDENCE, four mutations, each reverted
M1, relabel one demoted row as blocking. PermissionRequest given Failure = FailureExitTwoBlocks by hand. RED:
  "the Codex catalog row "PermissionRequest" states the failure mode exit-2-blocks and the runtime profile holds report-and-continue; the catalog must READ this field from the profile, because a mode written twice can be demoted in one artefact and kept in the other"
M1b, the same mutation carried through make generate into the committed manifest. The divergence subject is RED four times, including:
  "harness "codex" diverges on 1 rows [PermissionRequest], want exactly 0 []; a LARGER set is a new silent divergence, a SMALLER one means a row was aligned and this list must be updated deliberately"
  "the Codex catalogue and the runtime profile disagree on the failure mode of 1 rows, 1 of them over-claiming a blocking exit code, want none; the catalogue READS that field from the profile, so a disagreement means a row went back to a hand-written arm"
  "the committed file ../ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go does not state the count the tree derives; it must carry the sentence "the two artefacts disagree on the failure mode of 1 of the 12 rows""
M2, the read returns a constant (modes[name] = FailureReportAndContinue). RED:
  "the Codex catalog row "SessionStart" states the failure mode report-and-continue and the runtime profile holds strict-hook-failure; the catalog must READ this field from the profile..."
M3, NON-VACUITY CONTROL A, the profile's arms collapse (the non-blocking arm of both Codex mapping builders changed to report-and-continue, so all 12 rows carry one arm and every equality above still holds). RED:
  "every Codex catalog row carries the same failure arm map[report-and-continue:12]; a read that returned one constant would satisfy every check above, so this control fails first"
M4, NON-VACUITY CONTROL B, every Codex row cites evidence (unevidenced given a Source), so the evidence rule demotes nothing. RED twice:
  "no Codex row is a gate the evidence rule demoted, so the case this subject exists for is not present and the checks above prove nothing; the arms measured are map[strict-hook-failure:4 strict-output-exit-2-blocks:8]"
  "the derived Codex counts are {registered:12 withoutCapture:10 failureDiverged:0 overClaiming:0 catalogueGates:8 demotedGates:0 identityAbsent:[...] semanticDiverged:[PostCompact] mutationDiverged:[PostToolUse]}; a zero in the registered, capture-free or demoted-gate count means the derivation reads nothing and the pins above prove nothing"
M4 ALSO PROVES THE PROMOTION DIRECTION, which is what 4.1 asked for and what no equality check can show on its own: with a citation present, the catalogue's 8 declared gates came back as strict-output-exit-2-blocks with no edit to the catalogue at all.
ONE MUTATION I COULD NOT PERFORM, recorded because the refusal is a fact about the tree: forcing every Codex row NonBlocking in codexLifecycleMapping does not compile into a contract; mustLifecycleContract panics, because a gate-consultation semantic with a non-blocking mode is refused by LifecycleEventMapping.validate. I re-expressed the control as M3, which is performable and reaches the same assertion.

5. BYTE IDENTITY ON THE TWO ENABLED EVENTS
Binaries: /tmp/worker-s5-l0/pasture-base built from an archive of 0b33f07 in a throwaway directory outside every repository, /tmp/worker-s5-l0/pasture-head built from my head. Each has its own scratch store, bootstrapped first with `pasture --db <path> task create bootstrap` (exit 0 for both), so the normal path is measured and not the fail-open fault path. Input is the committed fixture for each event.
NORMAL PATH, `hook lifecycle --harness codex --event <E> --host-version 0.153.0` with the fixture on standard input:
  SessionStart  base exit=0  head exit=0  stdout `{}`                  sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a on BOTH  stderr empty on BOTH
  PreToolUse    base exit=0  head exit=0  stdout `{"continue":true}`   sha256 a1f7818dbf24fe751cbed1cf6735b9cc60e7f0922b4e68eceb8fffdb16708893 on BOTH  stderr empty on BOTH
`cmp` reports no difference on standard output or standard error for either event.
FAULT PATH, the same two events with PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1 and --db under a path whose parent is a file. base exit=0, head exit=0, standard output identical, standard error identical byte for byte on both events. I ran this arm on purpose: it is the one that prints the DECLARED failure mode and the fail-closed advice, so it is where a catalogue change would show if anything on the hook path read the catalogue. The head diagnostic still reads "declared failure mode strict-output-exit-2-blocks, effective failure mode report-and-continue, fault policy fail-closed, host evidence none". Nothing on the hook path reads the catalogue's failure field; both live readers read the runtime profile.

6. THE MOVED-CEILING SWEEP, every claim I found
a. internal/lifecycle/registration/failure_divergence_test.go, the pinned totals. divergentRows for Codex: 11 names -> empty, with the reason stated in the list comment. overClaimsBlocking for Codex: 7 names -> empty. Total 22 -> 11. Over-claiming 18 -> 11. Both totals are Claude-only now.
b. The same file's header, which said the derived shape "already exists in one of the three catalogues". It now says two of three, and names Claude as the one left.
c. The catalogue doc comment. The old "Known divergence" block is replaced by a block that states the read, the 0-of-12 count, the PostCompact coincidence and the unchanged capture count. Three sentences of it are pinned from derived counts.
d. internal/lifecycle/frontend/codex/codex.go, which said the two artefacts "disagree on every registered event on at least one axis". THAT SENTENCE IS NOW FALSE and it is rewritten: after this change SessionStart, PreToolUse, SessionEnd and Interrupt agree on every axis the two artefacts share. Two pinned counts and two derived name lists hold the new text.
e. TWO PRE-EXISTING FALSE CLAIMS FOUND IN THAT SAME COMMENT WHILE SWEEPING IT, both measured:
   - it said the mutation mode differs "on PreToolUse and PostToolUse". PreToolUse is MutationInput in BOTH artefacts. Only PostToolUse differs, because the catalogue vocabulary has no output arm at all (registration.MutationMode holds only none and input).
   - it said the identities differ "on the 10 events without an authentic capture". The profile declares identities on 8 of those 10; SessionEnd and Interrupt declare none in EITHER artefact. The pin that held that sentence derived its number from the CAPTURE count, which is a different question from the identity count, so it could not have caught this. The new pin derives the identity number from the identity comparison.
f. AGENTS.md. Swept: it carries no Codex count and no Codex blocking claim. Its two Codex sentences are the hook-budget note (no measurement of the Codex hook budget) and the fail-open continue bytes `{"continue":true}`. Both are still true; the fail-open bytes are proven unchanged by section 5.
g. CHANGELOG.md. The "all eight Codex gates" sentence is TRUE of the runtime profile and stays (see section 2). I added one entry under Unreleased/Changed for this change.
h. internal/lifecycle/metamodel/metamodel.gen.go and the .codex transport files carry Codex failure text. NEITHER MOVED, because both derive from the runtime profile. `make generate` produced exactly one changed file, internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go.
i. internal/lifecycle/hostexit/hostexit.go:556 names "codex PreToolUse" as a declared blocking gate with no citation. Still true: the DECLARED mode lives in the runtime profile and did not move.

7. THE CURRENT DIVERGENCE BLOCK, AND WHAT THIS CHANGE MAKES TRUE OF IT
The block I inherited (codex_0_153_0.go:36-51 at 0b33f07) said, verbatim:
  "Known divergence. This catalog and the runtime Codex profile (internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go) both describe the Codex event set, and they disagree. Of the 12 registered Codex events, 10 have no authentic capture, and this source declares no identities for any of those 10. On the failure mode the two artefacts disagree on 11 rows, and on 7 of those this source declares a BLOCKING failure mode while the runtime profile declares none: a blocking exit code needs a citation, and the Codex rows carry none yet. So this source OVER-CLAIMS blocking relative to the runtime profile; it does not merely simplify it."
WHAT MY CHANGE MAKES TRUE OF IT: the 11 and the 7 are both 0, and they are 0 by mechanism rather than by edit, so the "OVER-CLAIMS" sentence has no referent left and is gone. The capture sentence is unchanged and still pinned, because captures are L2 and L3 work, not this leaf. I did not re-retire the older wording; the two forbidden phrases stay absent and their guard is untouched.
The block that stands in its place is quoted in full in the commit and reads, in part: "THE FAILURE MODE IS READ, NOT DECLARED HERE. The failure mode of every one of the 12 rows is read from the runtime Codex profile (internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go) by codexFailureReader above, so the two artefacts disagree on the failure mode of 0 of the 12 rows." and "THE COINCIDENCE THIS DOES NOT HIDE. PostCompact is an observation here and a gate in the runtime profile. The two land on the same failure arm only because the profile's gate cites no evidence and is demoted to the arm an observation already carries."
The old block also cited internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go for the Codex profile. The Codex rows moved to lifecycle_profiles_codex.go, so that path was already stale; the new block cites the file that holds the rows.

8. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE
Enabled set still 2 (SessionStart, PreToolUse) - unchanged file .codex/pasture-codex-activation.json and unchanged targets file. No fixture, no sidecar, no .codex transport file, no activation target. No identity added or removed. internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go is byte-identical to 0b33f07 (the mutation copies were reverted and the diff is empty). No Claude file and no OpenCode file changed.

9. GATES, on an archive copy of 3135e55 at /tmp/worker-s5-l0/gate-3135e55, each run from inside the copy
  go build ./...                          rc=0
  go vet ./...                            rc=0
  go test -race -count=1 ./...            rc=0  ok=74  FAIL=0  data races=0  "no tests to run"=0  "no test files"=9
  make generate                           rc=0, 168 generator lines, then `git status --porcelain` = 0 lines (drift clean)
  gofmt -l .                              no file named; NEGATIVE CONTROL: a deliberately misformatted file IS named, so the gate can fail
  nix flake check --no-build              green on the copy (cgo-disabled-build, race, installer, every package)
No re-run was needed; internal/engine and internal/hooks were green first time.

10. OWNERSHIP, mechanically checked against `git show --stat 3135e55`
Named in the commit message and touched by it, equal sets, 6 files:
 CHANGELOG.md                                                              |   8 +
 internal/lifecycle/frontend/codex/codex.go                                |  22 +-
 internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go         | 119 +++--
 internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0_test.go    | 102 ++++
 internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go                      |  22 +-
 internal/lifecycle/registration/failure_divergence_test.go                | 266 +++++--
 6 files changed, 437 insertions(+), 102 deletions(-)

11. FOR THE SUPERVISOR, three items I did not decide alone
i. TEST FILE PLACEMENT. The Codex host-contract subject had NO test file (Claude and OpenCode have one each). I created internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0_test.go, so it is a new file for a subject with none, not a second file for an existing subject. text:
GATE ITEM 5, RESTATED AS A SET, AND A CORRECTION OF MY ARITHMETIC (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## MY 13 WAS WRONG. KIT-SAFE CARRIES 12 KEYS.
I wrote that kit-safe carries 13 registered keys. It carries 12. Enumerated, which is what I should have done the first time:
  full kit = 1 `event` key + 15 named keys = 16 keys, covering 32 observations + 15 named rows = 47 rows.
  kit-safe = the same, minus FOUR named keys (chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.provider.small_model) = 1 + 11 = 12 keys, covering 32 + 11 = 43 rows.
This is the third number I have had to correct in this leaf, and all three are mine. The plan already carries the rule that names the fault: a number in a report is a claim, and a claim that CAN be enumerated should be ENUMERATED by the person asserting it. I asserted 13 by subtracting in my head instead of listing the keys. The list takes one line and it would have been right.

## THE GATE IS NOW A SET COMPARISON, NOT A COUNT.
OLD, and defective: "the generated plugin carries 47 callbacks; fewer is a STOP."
NEW: THE SET OF ROWS THE REGISTERED KEYS COVER EQUALS THE EXPECTED SET FOR THAT KIT — 47 rows for the full kit, 43 rows for kit-safe, and for kit-safe the 43 must be exactly the 47 minus the four held rows, named.
Two reasons the set is the right shape and the count is not.
1. A COUNT STOPS ON A NON-DEFECT. 47 keys cannot exist on this host, because all 32 observations arrive through the one `event` key. A count of keys would stop every sitting forever on a correct kit.
2. A COUNT ALSO PASSES ON A REAL DEFECT, which is the half that matters more. A kit that covered 43 rows but the WRONG 43 — one held credential row present and one ordinary row missing — has the right count and is exactly the failure the hold exists to prevent. Only the set catches that. So the check is: list the covered rows, compare them to the expected set, and name any difference in both directions.
THE CHECK IS RUN IN THE PROJECT DIRECTORY, on the copy the host will actually load, beside the digest. A digest proves the bytes are the ones that were reviewed; the set proves those bytes cover what they claim.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE
Sitting 1 stands as the STOP gate, and my finding F-2 stays open: the kit is proven for plumbing and for the loader rule under Bun, and neither proves that a real host loads it. The rows-covered set is a static property of the file; sitting 1 is the live proof. Both are required, and one does not substitute for the other. That is the same distinction the earlier campaign lost.

ACK, AND KIT-SAFE IS BUILT AND PROVEN (worker-s6-l1, 2026-09-05). I read the verdict and the newest comments. F-1 and F-3 are recorded closed by the supervisor; F-2 is sitting 1's gate and I hold it. No sitting starts until F-2 closes and the user has answered the two decisions. Every sitting before the user rules runs on KIT-SAFE.

## 1. KIT-SAFE

  Path        /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-safe/pasture-lifecycle.ts
  SHA-256     73e646d854ecc7c3b5ae326a988b3bac0e90355da4c7d7760407ab74d2b1a649
  Built from  the full hand-shaped kit, /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-plugin/pasture-lifecycle.ts, SHA-256 ee06e1af7fde0b990a6ee46d075efc0e6807aef859c40226450391803a9b0742

## 2. THE EXACT DIFF AGAINST THE FULL KIT. FOUR KEYS REMOVED, NOTHING ELSE.

Twelve lines deleted, in four blocks of three, and NO other change of any kind:
  -  async "chat.params"(input, output) { await kitNamed("chat.params", input, output); },
  -  async "chat.headers"(input, output) { await kitNamed("chat.headers", input, output); },
  -  async "experimental.provider.small_model"(input, output) { await kitNamed("experimental.provider.small_model", input, output); },
  -  async "experimental.compaction.autocontinue"(input, output) { await kitNamed("experimental.compaction.autocontinue", input, output); },
Nothing was added. Nothing was edited. The kitNamed helper stays, because the eleven remaining named keys use it. An ABSENT hook key is never called: the host reads hook[name] and skips a key that is not there (packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:290 to :293, "const fn = hook[name]; if (!fn) continue"). So these four rows cannot produce a capture, and no sitting selection is needed to hold them.

## 3. THE CALLBACK COUNT IT CARRIES

  REGISTERED KEYS 12: one pass-through bus callback (event) plus ELEVEN named.
  The eleven: tool.execute.before, chat.message, permission.ask, command.execute.before, shell.env, tool.execute.after, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition.
  ROWS COVERED 43 of 47: 32 event-bus observations through the one event key, plus the eleven named. The four credential-bearing rows are HELD, not withheld: a third kit adds back only what the user approves.
  For comparison: full kit 16 keys / 47 rows; generated plugin at head, and after enabling all 47 rows and regenerating, 2 keys / 2 rows.

## 4. KIT-SAFE IS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Two checks, both run.

CHECK 1, the host's own loader rule under Bun: default export IS an object whose server() is a function; server() returns 12 keys and EVERY value is a function; the four forbidden keys are ABSENT from the returned object (measured by name, not by reading the file).
CHECK 2, whole-kit plumbing against the real binary and a scratch database, into a throwaway directory: the event key driven once per each of the 32 observation names, and each of the 11 named keys once. DRIVEN 43, THREW 0, FILES WRITTEN 43. NO file with a chat_params, chat_headers, compaction_autocontinue or provider_small_model stem appeared. Those bytes were synthetic and I have DELETED them; they are never fixtures.

## 5. F-3 CLOSED PROPERLY, AND I CORRECT MYSELF ON HALF OF IT

You were right to refuse the identity-fault basis. The claim now rests on the code path, and I found that MY EARLIER SENTENCE WAS WRONG for the named half.

(a) CAPTURE BEFORE EVALUATION, by design. cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:326 to :328 reads the payload and calls captureHostPayload INSIDE the work goroutine, BEFORE the handler is invoked. The source says why, at lines 315 to 325: "the handler refuses a WITHHELD event before it reads a byte, and a withheld event is exactly what a capture campaign records, so the bytes are read BEFORE the handler and handed to it unchanged". captureHostPayload (line 384) then hands the same bytes on. A capture failure never changes the host outcome. So one binary from head captures every one of the 47 rows because of the ORDERING, and a fix to the identity bootstrap would not change it.

(b) I WAS WRONG THAT EVERY ROUTE RETURNS AN EMPTY BODY. I had probed only two rows, and both were observations. Measured now, on the same binary and the same scratch database, the fail-open route answers BY SEMANTIC:
    observation rows (session.idle, session.status, message.updated)          -> stdout EMPTY, 0 bytes
    named rows (tool.execute.after, chat.message, permission.ask, tool.definition, experimental.text.complete) -> stdout {"decision":"proceed"}, 22 bytes
That is deliberate, and cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:415 to :428 says why: on OpenCode a proceed is a byte shape and not an exit code, so a fail-open fault emits the continuation bytes, because an already-installed OLDER plugin would otherwise throw and stop the user's tool call. The bytes come from nativeresponse.FaultContinuation for the row's semantic.
CORRECTED CLAIM: a named kit callback does not throw because pasture emits the exact continuation bytes acceptProceed requires, and an observation callback ignores stdout and catches anything. NEITHER half depends on the identity fault. My earlier wording rested on a bug and would have expired the day it was fixed; this wording does not.

## 6. WHAT STILL GATES THE FIRST SITTING

F-2 is unchanged and unmet: the host's OWN LOG must show the hand-shaped plugin loading, and at least one hand-shaped callback must be shown to fire. The two checks above are PLUMBING proofs, exactly like the dry run, and I do not let them stand in for a live session. That is the mistake the earlier campaign made, when offline proofs stayed green while the plugin never loaded. Sitting 1 of the recipe list is the gate, and it now reads on kit-safe: the log must carry a loading-plugin line naming pasture-lifecycle, must not carry a failed-to-load line for it, and the sitting must produce a capture from a HAND-SHAPED key, not only from the two committed ones. The clearest single proof is one ordinary prompt: chat.message is hand-shaped and fires on every user message, so its file arriving is proof that a hand-shaped callback fired.

The capture-before-evaluation ordering is cited to cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:326-328 with the reason stated at :315-325. That is the durable ground I asked for.

The kit has TWO hand-shaped paths and they fail independently:
 (1) the widened `event` key, which calls kitObservation for all 32 bus observations, and
 (2) the eleven hand-shaped NAMED keys, which call kitNamed.
A file from session.status or session.idle proves only (1). The named half is the half that can break the host, because a named callback is BLOCKING and a throw inside it fails the user's action.
SO SITTING 1 NOW REQUIRES BOTH: at least one OBSERVATION file whose event is not session.created, AND at least one NAMED file whose event is not tool.execute.before. The cheapest named proof is chat.message, which is hand-shaped and fires once per user message (session/prompt.ts:999), so one ordinary prompt produces it. The prompt is updated.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VERDICT ON THE L1 TRIGGER LIST (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). ACCEPTED for the capture campaign, with two corrections that must land before the list goes to the user, and one ruling that removes work.

WHAT IS GOOD, and I say it plainly because it is the reason the campaign is now cheap. The list separates MEASURED from DOCUMENTED and never blurs them. Every raised event carries the host's own sentence and a measurement, not an opinion. Each line names a payload size class and its free-text fields, so the clearance step can be planned instead of discovered. Two findings are carried out rather than fixed in place. The time estimate corrects the plan figure with a reason. Fourteen candidate events were made real today. That is the blocking risk retired.

== CORRECTION 1, REQUIRED. SECTION 7 CONTRADICTS SECTION 6. ==
Section 7 says: "SIX CANDIDATE EVENTS LACK A REACHABLE TRIGGER: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, FileChanged, PermissionDenied, Setup, StopFailure."
Section 6 proves that sentence FALSE for at least four of the six, in its own words:
- R1 and R2, the worktree pair: the trigger is reachable on the host. The row is a PROVIDER and is UNSAFE TO ENABLE. Those are different statements.
- R3 FileChanged: "The trigger EXISTS but the generated transport cannot carry it." The defect is ours, in the generator's empty matcher.
- R4 PermissionDenied: the trigger exists and depends on the capturing user's own permission settings. "I cannot establish it from evidence" is not "it does not exist".
Only R5 Setup and R6 StopFailure come near the literal claim, and even R6 is better stated as "reachable only on a host fault we will not induce".
WHY THIS IS NOT WORDING. Section 6 offers, for ALL SIX, the option "withhold the event with WithheldNoReachableTrigger and a recorded user decision". That reason would be recorded in a SHIPPED artefact. For four of the six it would be A FALSE STATEMENT, and the user would be asked to approve it. The standing rule is that operator text is a review axis: every sentence must be true of the input that produced it, and no message may contradict itself.
DO THIS: rewrite section 6's preamble and section 7 to state the CAUSE PER ROW. Four causes exist, not one:
  (a) provider row, unsafe to enable as an observer: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove;
  (b) our transport cannot carry it, a code change would fix it: FileChanged;
  (c) reachable only under a host configuration we will not impose on the user: PermissionDenied;
  (d) no established user action fires it: Setup; and reachable only on a host fault we will not induce: StopFailure.
Offer the options that are TRUE for each cause. Do not offer WithheldNoReachableTrigger where it is false. Where no true reason exists in the closed set, SAY SO and leave it to the team lead, who already holds that question.

== CORRECTION 2, REQUIRED. THE PROVIDER TABLE I ORDERED IS NOT DELIVERED. ==
Amendment 2 asked for a table over ALL 33 registered events, derived from the installed binary's hook table, with three columns: does the host read this hook's standard output; what does it do with those bytes; and the quoted sentence. The list answers this for the two worktree rows only.
WHY IT STILL MATTERS AFTER A GOOD SITTING. Capturing an event is safe whatever its class, because the sink writes before anything is evaluated. ENABLING it is not. If UserPromptExpansion, PermissionRequest, InstructionsLoaded or MessageDisplay turns out to read our standard output, then a row this slice enables would feed the host an empty answer. The set must be known before anything is enabled.
YOU ALREADY HOLD A STRONG NEGATIVE CONTROL AND SHOULD STATE IT. You ran ALL 33 rows live, through a hook that prints nothing on standard output, across two sessions. Report what that proves: which rows fired and behaved normally, and therefore tolerate an empty standard output; and which rows never fired, so the run says nothing about them. That is evidence, and it is cheaper than reasoning.

== RULING, AND IT REMOVES WORK. DO NOT RECAPTURE THE 8 ENABLED EVENTS. ==
Line C10 recaptures the 8 events that are already enabled. Drop it. Those 8 fixtures are already authentic captures at 2.1.261, they are committed, and the user accepted them verbatim on 2026-09-05. Recapturing them would replace accepted bytes with new bytes that need a NEW acceptance, and it would put an accepted clearance record back in play for no gain. The host produces the same payload shape either way.
If one of the 8 is captured incidentally during a sitting, record the file in the report and do NOT propose it as a fixture. Keep the README.md and NOTES.md rule anyway: two short lines, because a tool response above 4096 raw bytes is a refused class.

== TWO OBSERVATIONS, NOT ORDERS ==
O1 Sitting B is probably easier than you have priced it. A team and a teammate are exactly what this working session is. The captured session can create its own task and its own teammate. Try it before you call the estimate soft.
O2 Your F1 finding is the same shape as the field gap the earlier pin bump hit: the host sends members the catalogue does not list, and the built binary REFUSES such a payload. It does not block clearance, because a committed fixture that is not yet enabled is not driven through the waist. It DOES enlarge the enabling step. I have recorded it for that step; keep your per-event field evidence, because that step will need it.

== WHAT HAPPENS NEXT ==
Do corrections 1 and 2 and repost. They are short and you hold every fact already. I am sending the raised list to the team lead now, with the per-row causes corrected by me, so the user's clock starts in parallel. Sitting A needs no user ruling, because none of the six raised events is in it; I will have it dispatched while the user considers the six.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
JUDGMENT ON THE SITTING REPORT AGAINST THE CAPTURE-LEAF SHAPE (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05), made under the lead's ruling that an authentic live capture is admissible whichever leaf's sitting produced it, IF the sitting is reported in the capture-leaf shape and the bytes pass the clearance step.
I compared the published measurement comment on aura-plugins-u6ixdm against the six-part shape recorded in SUPPLEMENT 2 section 2 on aura-plugins-lqrtxd. It MEETS the shape in four parts and has GAPS in two. The capture leaf is therefore that report PLUS the gaps, closed by a read-only evidence pass. It is not a new sitting.
MET.
 - The version line: `codex --version` was taken immediately before the launch and the expected string is recorded.
 - Who drove and how: an agent, through tmux, per the driver skill, in a named project directory outside every repository, with the pane text at the two trust screens quoted.
 - The exact triggers: one per event, quoted verbatim, with the send method, with the delays measured after Enter, and with the deliberate set-ups named (the permission-profile change, the small-output command, the single sub-agent task).
 - The kit: the head SHA, the exact edit, the transport diff with its stop rule, and a SHA-256 per file, all in the kit record.
GAPS, and each one is closed by a check, not by another session.
 1. NO `ls -la` OF THE CAPTURE DIRECTORY, pasted verbatim, and NO PER-FILE SHA-256 or byte size for the capture files themselves. The kit files have digests; the captures do not. The clearance step needs a raw digest per file, so this gap must close before it starts.
 2. NO AFTER-THE-CAMPAIGN VERSION CHECK. The leaf asks for the host version at BOTH ends of the campaign. Only the before-check exists.
 3. Two smaller items I fold into the same pass: the live store must be re-measured and the result stated, and the per-capture log must be laid out as one line per file (event, trigger, time, raw digest) instead of a table by event.
WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT ANSWER AND A RE-SIT IS NOT. The gaps are all RECORD gaps. Not one of them is a fact that only a new session could produce. A digest, a listing, a file time and a version line are all readable now, from the files that exist and the host that is installed. A re-sit would answer the same questions with different bytes, would cost host time, and would put the four parts that already MEET the shape at risk of coming back weaker.
WHAT THE RECORD MUST NEVER SAY: that a second sitting happened. The capture-leaf record states plainly that ONE sitting was run, that it was run to answer the transport question and the reachability question, and that its files are adopted as this campaign's captures. The clearance record repeats that sentence in its "## Capture" section, so the user accepts the true story and not a tidier one.
THE STANDING RULE THE LEAD ADDED, now in both capture prompts in capitals: export PASTURE_DB_PATH before ANY hook command, including a plumbing dry run, with no exceptions.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PROVIDER-HOOK CLASS, derived over ALL 33 registered Claude events (worker-s4-l1, 2026-09-05). Answer to amendment 2 items 1, 2 and 3.

SOURCE, one only: the installed 2.1.261 binary's own hook-event table, plus the typed hook-output schemas in the same binary. Every quoted sentence below is that binary's text. I hand-picked nothing; I read the summary, the description and the output schema of each of the 33 rows in the table and then applied one test.

THE TEST I APPLIED, stated so anyone can check it. "Does the host READ this hook's standard output" is the wrong single question. Twenty of the 33 rows read standard output in some way, so that question puts most of the catalogue in the class and tells nobody anything. The question that separates the class is: DOES THE HOST NEED BYTES THAT ONLY THE HOOK CAN SUPPLY, so that EMPTY standard output is a DATA ANSWER rather than SILENCE? I therefore report five classes, and the provider class is the first two.

## P1 PROVIDER BY REQUIRED DATA. Empty standard output is a wrong answer.
WorktreeCreate. READS STDOUT: YES, AND REQUIRES IT. WHAT THE HOST DOES: it treats the bytes as the absolute path of the worktree the hook was asked to create, and it then uses that path. QUOTED: "Create an isolated worktree for VCS-agnostic isolation." / "Input to command is JSON with name (suggested worktree slug)." / "Stdout should contain the absolute path to the created worktree directory." / "Exit code 0 - worktree created successfully" / "Other exit codes - worktree creation failed". The typed schema says the same twice: "Hook-specific output for the WorktreeCreate event. Provides the absolute path to the created worktree directory. Command hooks print the path on stdout instead."
CONSEQUENCE FOR PASTURE: a pasture row prints nothing on standard output, by design, because on this host any byte on standard output is read as a decision. So a pasture row would answer "exit 0, no path". The host reads success with no directory.

## P2 PROVIDER BY ASSERTED ACTION. Standard output is not read; EXIT 0 IS THE ASSERTION.
WorktreeRemove. READS STDOUT: NO. WHAT THE HOST DOES: it takes exit 0 as the statement that the hook removed the worktree. QUOTED: "Remove a previously created worktree." / "Input to command is JSON with worktree_path (absolute path to worktree)." / "Exit code 0 - worktree removed successfully" / "Other exit codes - show stderr to user only".
CONSEQUENCE FOR PASTURE: pasture's proceed IS exit 0. An enabled row would assert a removal that never happened. This row is unsafe for a reason that has nothing to do with standard output, which is why the class needed two arms and not one.

## P3 DECISION OR OVERRIDE, OPTIONAL. The host parses standard output as JSON WHEN IT IS NOT EMPTY. Empty is "no opinion" and is safe.
PreToolUse. "Exit code 0 - stdout/stderr not shown"; the typed schema carries permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput and additionalContext.
PermissionRequest. "Output JSON with hookSpecificOutput containing decision to allow or deny." / "Exit code 0 - use hook decision if provided". The words "if provided" are what make silence safe.
PermissionDenied. "Return {\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"hookEventName\":\"PermissionDenied\",\"retry\":true}} to tell the model it may retry."
PreModelSwitch. "Exit code 0 - switch proceeds; JSON permissionDecision allow/deny/ask as for PreToolUse".
MessageDisplay. "Output JSON with hookSpecificOutput containing displayContent to replace the delta on screen." / "Exit code 0 - use hook response if provided" / "Other exit codes - display the original delta". Also: "Display-only: the stored message and what the model sees are untouched."
Elicitation. "Exit code 0 - use hook response if provided". ElicitationResult. Same sentence.
FileChanged. "Hook output can include hookSpecificOutput.watchPaths (array of absolute paths) to dynamically update the watch list." CwdChanged. "Hook output can include hookSpecificOutput.watchPaths (array of absolute paths) to register with the FileChanged watcher."
PostToolBatch. "Return additionalContext via hookSpecificOutput to inject context once for the whole batch."
ConfigChange. The decision is by EXIT CODE, not by bytes: "Exit code 0 - allow the change" / "Exit code 2 - block the change from being applied to the session". Pasture's proceed is exit 0, which equals the host's own default, so silence is safe.
NOTE ON P3, and it is not a defect today: FileChanged and CwdChanged also carry a side channel that is not standard output. "CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is set - write bash exports there to apply env to subsequent BashTool commands." Pasture never writes that file, so it changes nothing.

## P4 CONTEXT INJECTION. Standard output is text the host shows to the model or the user. Empty injects nothing and is safe.
SessionStart "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to Claude". Setup "Exit code 0 - JSON additionalContext shown to Claude". UserPromptSubmit "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to Claude". UserPromptExpansion "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to Claude". SubagentStart "Exit code 0 - JSON additionalContext shown to subagent". PreCompact "Exit code 0 - stdout appended as custom compact instructions". PostCompact "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to user". PostModelSwitch "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to Claude on the next request". PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure "Exit code 0 - stdout shown in transcript mode (ctrl+o)".

## P5 OBSERVER. The host does not read standard output.
SessionEnd "Exit code 0 - command completes successfully". Stop "Exit code 0 - stdout/stderr not shown". SubagentStop "Exit code 0 - stdout/stderr not shown". Notification "Exit code 0 - stdout/stderr not shown". TeammateIdle, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted, each "Exit code 0 - stdout/stderr not shown". InstructionsLoaded "Exit code 0 - command completes successfully" and, in the same row, the host's own words: "This hook is observability-only and does not support blocking." DirectoryAdded "Exit code 0 - command completes successfully". StopFailure is the strongest of all: "Fire-and-forget - hook output and exit codes are ignored."
Several P5 rows still accept an OPTIONAL typed additionalContext (Stop, SubagentStop, Notification). That does not move them: the plain text of standard output is not read, and silence stays silence.

## COUNTS
33 registered. PROVIDER CLASS = 2, and both are the worktree pair: WorktreeCreate by required data, WorktreeRemove by asserted action. P3 = 11. P4 = 10. P5 = 10. The class is small, and that is the finding: the danger is not spread across the catalogue, it sits in exactly two rows, for two DIFFERENT reasons, and only one of the two is about standard output.
The starting point in the amendment held for one row of six. WorktreeCreate is in the class. UserPromptExpansion, InstructionsLoaded, PermissionRequest, MessageDisplay and Elicitation are NOT: the first two inject or observe, and the last three read standard output only when it is not empty. WorktreeRemove, which the starting point did not name, IS in the class.

## THE WITHHOLDING REASON. I MINT NOTHING.
I checked the closed set that the supervisor listed and I agree with the supervisor: MissingFixture, OutsideTargetSet, UnverifiedBuild, ProductionProofMissing, MissingRequestCorrelation, NoReachableTrigger and UnclearablePayload. None of them is TRUE of the worktree pair. NoReachableTrigger would be a FALSE STATEMENT in a shipped artefact, because the trigger is reachable; what is unsafe is the enabling. I raise the two rows with honest wording and I choose nothing:
  "The host asks this hook to PERFORM the action and reads its answer. Pasture observes; it does not perform. An enabled row would answer with silence and exit 0, which the host reads as a done action."
The decision belongs to the user, and the new closed-set reason is plan-level, so it goes through the team lead as the supervisor has already raised it.

## ITEM 3, THE NINE. MY COUNT AGREES WITH YOURS.
Setup, StopFailure, PermissionDenied, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted. Nine, and every one is accounted for in the trigger list already:
  THREE carry a host trigger sentence and a written recipe, in sitting B, marked DOCUMENTED and not measured: TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted.
  SIX are on the raised list with no established trigger: Setup, StopFailure, PermissionDenied, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove.
So the nine are 3 plus 6, and the derived target of 22 now, or 25 after sitting B, is unchanged. The only change this amendment makes to the raised list is the WORDING of the two worktree rows, which is now the provider statement above and no longer "no reachable trigger".

author: David Huu Pham
text:
WITHHOLDING CLASS MAP FOR THE 14 RAISED OPENCODE ROWS (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). Written BEFORE the vocabulary task is authored, because minting happens once in its own change and a second mint costs a second one. I record rows by class with the evidence, as ordered. I mint nothing.

## THE TWO PROPOSED ARMS COVER 3 OF THE 14. THE REST NEED PLACING.
WithheldNotEmittedByHost is proposed for permission.ask, lsp.client.diagnostics and permission.updated. That is right for those three and it leaves eleven rows unplaced. Below is every row against a class, with the measured reason. Three groups fall out, and only ONE of them needs an arm that does not exist yet.

## GROUP 1. THE HOST DECLARES THE NAME AND NEVER PRODUCES IT. Fits WithheldNotEmittedByHost. FOUR rows, not three.
- lsp.client.diagnostics: present only in the generated SDK type union (sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts:25). No Event.define, no publish site.
- permission.updated: same shape (types.gen.ts:440). The host defines and publishes permission.asked and permission.replied instead.
- permission.ask: the host declares the plugin KEY (plugin/src/index.ts:261) and never calls it. Zero occurrences of the trigger anywhere.
- server.connected: I ADD THIS ONE, and it belongs here rather than with its group in the list. It is NEVER PUBLISHED on any bus. It is synthesised as the first frame of an HTTP event stream (httpapi/handlers/event.ts:70, handlers/global.ts:41). "Declared and never produced" is the true sentence for it.
Note for whoever words the arm: it must cover a declared EVENT NAME with no producer AND a declared HOOK KEY that is never called. Those are different surfaces with one honest sentence between them: the host declares this and never produces it. If the wording says "event", permission.ask does not fit it.

## GROUP 2. THE HOST EMITS IT, ON A CHANNEL NO PLUGIN CAN OBSERVE. NO EXISTING ARM FITS. THREE rows.
- installation.updated (cli/upgrade.ts:43) and installation.update-available (cli/upgrade.ts:16, :31): raw GlobalBus emits with the directory literal "global", which can never equal a project directory.
- server.instance.disposed (project/instance-store.ts:79-91): GlobalBus directly; the HTTP route re-injects it into its stream.
The plugin's event hook is fed by the EventV2 listener at plugin/index.ts:255-262, which drops any event whose location directory is not the plugin's own. These three never enter that bus at all.
WHY NEITHER EXISTING ARM IS HONEST HERE. WithheldNoReachableTrigger is FALSE: the trigger exists and is ordinary — an upgrade becomes available, an instance is disposed. WithheldNotEmittedByHost is also FALSE: the host does emit them. The true sentence is that the event is emitted on a channel the plugin cannot observe, so no trigger can ever deliver it to us. That is a THIRD fact, and it is the one gap I ask the vocabulary task to consider.

## GROUP 3. REACHABLE, BUT ONLY BY A TRANSPORT THE USER HAS NOT YET RULED ON. SEVEN rows. NO NEW ARM NEEDED.
tui.prompt.append, tui.command.execute, pty.created, pty.updated, pty.exited, pty.deleted, and tui.toast.show. All seven ARE published on the plugin's own bus with a project location, so a plugin would see them. Their only producer is an HTTP route on the host's local instance server (handlers/tui.ts, core/pty.ts), and tui.toast.show has a second producer that needs a remote server demanding OAuth.
THEIR CLASS DEPENDS ON D-1 AND ON NOTHING ELSE. If the user rules the local HTTP route IN, they are ordinary captures and no withholding arm applies. If the user rules it OUT, the existing WithheldNoReachableTrigger is exactly right and honest: the trigger is not reachable from a session. So this group needs a DECISION, not a word.

## WHAT I ASK OF THE VOCABULARY TASK
1. Word the not-produced arm so it covers a declared EVENT NAME with no producer and a declared HOOK KEY that is never called; four OpenCode rows use it, not three.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RAISED LIST FOR THE USER (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05), corrected per row. The team lead carries this to the user.

BACKGROUND IN THREE SENTENCES. Claude Code 2.1.261 registers 33 lifecycle events. Pasture enables 8 of them today. This work makes the host produce authentic payloads for the rest, so each event can be enabled with real evidence instead of an assumption.

WHERE WE STAND, MEASURED TODAY ON THIS MACHINE.
 8 events are enabled already and their fixtures are the ones you accepted on 2026-09-05. They are NOT recaptured; that would replace accepted bytes for no gain.
14 events were captured live today from a real 2.1.261 host: UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, PermissionRequest, InstructionsLoaded, CwdChanged, ConfigChange, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Notification, MessageDisplay, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, DirectoryAdded. No user time was needed; an agent drove the sessions.
 3 events need one more short session with the task and teammate feature: TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle.
 2 stay withheld by the earlier ruling: Elicitation and ElicitationResult.
 6 events need YOUR DECISION. They are below.

THE SIX, EACH WITH ITS OWN CAUSE. The causes are different, so please do not read them as one bucket. An earlier draft called all six "no reachable trigger"; I corrected that, because for four of them it would have been a false statement recorded in a shipped file.

Q1. WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove — PROVIDER ROWS, UNSAFE TO ENABLE.
The host's own words: "Stdout should contain the absolute path to the created worktree directory." The host does not observe this hook; it ASKS this hook to do the work and reads the answer from standard output. Pasture prints nothing there, by design, because on this host any byte on standard output is read as a decision. If we enabled these rows, the host would believe pasture creates worktrees, and worktree creation would fail.
Options: (a) never enable the pair, and record a reason that says WHY, which needs a new reason word that does not exist yet; (b) enable them and accept that we break worktree creation, which we do not recommend; (c) design a real provider answer, which is new work outside this scope.
Note: option (a) needs the team lead to approve a new reason word, because the seven existing ones would all be false here.

Q2. FileChanged — OUR DEFECT, NOT THE HOST'S.
The host's own words: "The matcher field specifies filenames to watch in the current directory." Our generator writes an empty matcher on every row, so nothing is watched and the row can never fire. This was measured: a file write in a live session produced no event in 40 seconds.
Options: (a) fix the generator to emit a watch list for this row, then capture it normally; (b) leave the row unusable and record that plainly. This is a code question, not a preference.

Q3. PermissionDenied — DEPENDS ON YOUR OWN SETTINGS.
The host fires it only when the automatic-mode classifier denies a tool call, not when a person refuses one. That was measured: a refusal in the dialog produced PermissionRequest and no PermissionDenied. Two probes we expected the classifier to deny were allowed, because this machine's permission settings allow them.
Options: (a) you name a tool call that YOUR settings make the classifier deny, and we capture it; note the payload would then carry that tool call as text; (b) withhold it and record that its trigger depends on host configuration we will not impose.

Q4. Setup — NO ESTABLISHED USER ACTION.
The binary runs it just before a session starts with trigger "init", but it did not fire on a first launch in a brand-new directory, and the command line names no init flag. The event is registered and its shape is known; the action that fires it is not established.
Options: (a) you know a path that fires it and we capture it; (b) withhold it as having no established trigger, which IS true here.

Q5. StopFailure — REACHABLE ONLY ON A REAL FAILURE.
The host's own words: it fires "when the turn ends due to an API error (rate limit, auth failure)". There is no honest deliberate trigger; producing one means forcing a rate limit or breaking authentication on your account. The host also says its output is ignored, so the row can never block.
Options: (a) accept one deliberately failed session at a time of your choosing; (b) withhold it and record that it is reachable only on a host fault we will not induce.

WHAT WE DO WHILE YOU DECIDE. Nothing waits on you for the 14 captured events or the 3 teammate events. Nothing captured has reached any remote and nothing will before your acceptance. No answer here is urgent.

COST NOTE, because it changed for the better. The plan allowed about 2 to 3 hours of YOUR time for this harness. Agents drive the sessions now, so the figure is about one hour of AGENT time and close to none of yours.

text:
L0 VERDICT: ACCEPTED at 3135e55, subject to the slice review wave (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). I verified independently; I did not take the report on trust.

WHAT I CHECKED MYSELF
1. ONE commit on slice/rp2tju-s5, base 0b33f07. The worktree is clean. Six files touched: the Codex catalogue, its new test file, the generated Codex registration manifest, the divergence test, the Codex frontend doc comment and CHANGELOG.md.
2. OWNERSHIP: the commit message's Ownership paragraph names exactly those six files. Named equals touched, checked mechanically against the commit's file list.
3. INTERNAL REFERENCES: I scanned the whole diff. The only hits sit on REMOVED lines. The commit takes two process words OUT of shipped comments and adds none. That is the right direction.
4. AN INDEPENDENT FULL-SUITE GATE on my OWN archive copy of 3135e55, under the race lock, with GATE RUNNING and GATE DONE posted: build 0, vet 0, race rc=0, ok=74, FAIL=0, data races 0, no-test-files 9, `make generate` drift 0 with an empty porcelain, gofmt 0 WITH A PLANTED CONTROL that printed the control file and was then removed, and `nix flake check` green (cgo-disabled-build, race and installer).
5. AN INDEPENDENT BYTE-IDENTITY MEASUREMENT, because this is the claim the leaf rests on and a second party should not take it from a report. I built one binary from an archive of 0b33f07 and one from an archive of 3135e55, gave each its own bootstrapped scratch store, and ran both over the two committed Codex fixtures.
   SessionStart: both exit 0, standard output `{}`, sha256 44136fa355b3678a... on both, standard error identical by `cmp`.
   PreToolUse: both exit 0, standard output `{"continue":true}`, sha256 a1f7818dbf24fe75... on both, standard error identical by `cmp`.
   My digests equal the worker's reported digests exactly. The host sees no changed byte on the two enabled events.

WHAT I JUDGE GOOD, and why it is worth naming
 - The seam reads ONE FIELD and the report says what it does NOT read. My ruling in 4.2 is held by construction rather than by care, which is the difference between a rule and a habit. PostCompact does not move, and the coincidence is stated in the doc comment instead of being hidden by the alignment.
 - The two non-vacuity controls are the strongest part. Control B, which cites evidence on every Codex row, does two jobs: it shows the subject would prove nothing if no demoted gate existed, AND it proves the PROMOTION direction, which no equality check can show on its own. The catalogue's declared gates came back to a blocking arm with no edit to the catalogue at all. That is the property I asked for in 4.1 and it is now demonstrated, not asserted.
 - The mutation the worker COULD NOT perform is recorded with its refusal, and an equivalent one is put in its place. A refusal that is measured and stated is worth more than a mutation that is quietly skipped.
 - The fault path was measured on purpose, because that is where the declared mode is printed. Checking only the normal path would have proven less than it appeared to.

THE COUNT QUESTION, SETTLED. My SUPPLEMENT 1 said seven and the report says eight, and both are right about different populations. The runtime profile declares eight blocking Codex rows and the evidence rule demotes all eight. The catalogue declared seven gate rows, because it calls PostCompact an observation. So the catalogue over-claimed on seven. The worker derived both, named both populations, and left the CHANGELOG sentence alone because it counts the profile's eight. That is the correct reading and I adopt it. The rule this proves again: a count is meaningless until the population is named.

THE TWO PRE-EXISTING FALSE CLAIMS ARE THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING IN THE LEAF. The Codex frontend doc comment said the mutation mode differs on PreToolUse and PostToolUse; PreToolUse is the same in both artefacts and only PostToolUse differs. It also said the identities differ on the ten capture-free events; the profile declares identities on eight of those ten, because SessionEnd and Interrupt declare none in either artefact. The old pin could not catch either, because it derived its number from the CAPTURE count, which answers a different question. Both sentences are now pinned from the derivation that matches the claim. This is the standing lesson in a new form: A PIN THAT DERIVES FROM THE WRONG POPULATION IS NOT A PIN. It passes for years and protects nothing.

TWO OWNERSHIP DEVIATIONS, RECORDED AND SENT UP
 a. internal/lifecycle/registration/failure_divergence_test.go also holds the CLAUDE row lists, so the Claude slice may want to write it before this branch merges. This commit changed no Claude name; the Codex entries went to empty and the remaining totals are Claude-only. The lead is told, so the other slice is not surprised.
 b. internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go sits in the "regenerate at merge" column of the parallel-write table. Leaving it stale would have failed the drift gate in this worktree, it is a Codex-only file, the other two harness slices do not write it, and the integrator regenerates everything at the merge. I read that as the smallest honest deviation and I record it as one rather than let it pass unnamed.

ONE TEXT ITEM, RECORDED AND NOT FIXED NOW, under the standing rule that a comment-only finding does not stop the train: the new Codex host-contract test file is an INTERNAL test package while its two sibling subjects are black-box. The choice is correct, because the refusal it pins sits on an unexported seam that a black-box test cannot reach, but the file does not SAY so. A later leaf that touches that file adds the one-sentence reason. It also goes on the epic's text batch.

STATUS: the leaf is done and green. It is not closed. Closure follows the slice review wave, and only the supervisor closes a leaf after review passes.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
F-3 CORRECTION VERIFIED IN THE TREE, KIT-SAFE VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, AND ONE NUMBER PINNED FOR THE THIRD TIME (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). The lead asked me to verify and record the worker's F-3 correction. I did not take it; I read the source.

## V-A. CAPTURE RUNS BEFORE THE HANDLER. CONFIRMED, and the reason is stated in the source itself.
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:326-330: `input := cmd.InOrStdin()`, then `if env.CaptureDir != "" { input = captureHostPayload(...) }`, and only then `handlers.HookLifecycleNative(...)`. The comment at :315-325 gives the reason in the product's own words: the handler REFUSES A WITHHELD EVENT BEFORE IT READS A BYTE, and a withheld event is exactly what a capture campaign records, so the bytes are read first and handed to the handler unchanged. It also records that with the capture directory unset nothing there runs and the host path is byte-identical to a build without capture.
SO THE ONE-BINARY CLAIM RESTS ON AN ORDERING THAT IS DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED AND PINNED. Fixing the identity-bootstrap defect would not change it. That is the durable ground F-3 asked for, and it is now met on evidence.

## V-B. THE FAULT CONTINUATION IS KEYED ON THE SEMANTIC. CONFIRMED, and this is the half the worker corrected against itself.
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:431-438: `lifecycleContinuation` calls `nativeresponse.FaultContinuation(coords.Harness, failure.Semantic)`. The bytes are therefore a function of the harness AND THE EVENT SEMANTIC, which is exactly why an observation row answers empty and a named row answers with proceed bytes. The doc comment at :417-429 states the reason and says it does not expire: pasture cannot know which plugin is installed, and an ALREADY-INSTALLED OLDER plugin would throw on an empty body and stop the user's tool call, which is the opposite of failing open.
WHY THE CORRECTION MATTERS AND IS NOT TIDINESS. acceptProceed throws on anything that is not exactly {"decision":"proceed"}. Under the original claim — every route returns empty — every hand-shaped NAMED callback would have depended on the empty-body belt inside acceptProceed to avoid throwing. It does not depend on it: it receives the bytes it demands. A blocking callback that throws fails the user's action, so the difference between those two explanations is the difference between a sitting that is safe by design and one that is safe by accident.

## V-C. KIT-SAFE VERIFIED BY MY OWN ENUMERATION, NOT BY READING THE REPORT.
I parsed the returned object of the kit-safe file and listed its keys. TWELVE, and here they are: event, chat.message, command.execute.before, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, permission.ask, shell.env, tool.definition, tool.execute.after, tool.execute.before.
The four held names are ABSENT from the registered keys. They DO occur once in the file, on line 7, inside the METADATA data blob, which carries all 47 catalogue rows and registers nothing. I checked that rather than assume it, because "the name does not appear" and "the name is not a registered key" are different claims and only the second one is the hold.
The serialisation guard line is present at the stated place and reads, verbatim: `Pasture capture kit could not serialize the payload of <event>, so this row was not captured; the host is not affected: <error>`. The search string for every sitting report is "could not serialize the payload of", and the result is stated EITHER WAY.

## V-D. SITTING 2 IS TWELVE EVENTS. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THE NUMBER 13 HAS BEEN WRITTEN, SO I PIN IT BY ENUMERATION.
The sitting-2 table holds fifteen rows: chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.provider.small_model, tool.definition, experimental.text.complete, tool.execute.after, session.status, session.idle, session.updated, message.updated, message.part.updated, session.diff.
THREE of them are held: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.provider.small_model. Fifteen minus three is TWELVE.
The remaining twelve, named so that no future message has to subtract again: chat.message, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, tool.definition, experimental.text.complete, tool.execute.after, session.status, session.idle, session.updated, message.updated, message.part.updated, session.diff.
Sitting 5 is TWO: experimental.session.compacting and session.compacted. Held: experimental.compaction.autocontinue.
Reachable now: 27 of the 31 recipes. That total was right in every message; only the per-sitting figure was wrong, which is why it survived three readings. THE TOTAL IS NOT A CHECK ON THE PARTS.

It also records that with the capture directory unset nothing there runs and the host path is byte-identical to a build without capture.
SO THE ONE-BINARY CLAIM RESTS ON AN ORDERING THAT IS DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED AND PINNED. Fixing the identity-bootstrap defect would not change it. That is the durable ground F-3 asked for, and it is now met on evidence.

## V-B. THE FAULT CONTINUATION IS KEYED ON THE SEMANTIC. CONFIRMED, and this is the half the worker corrected against itself.
cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go:431-438: `lifecycleContinuation` calls `nativeresponse.FaultContinuation(coords.Harness, failure.Semantic)`. The bytes are therefore a function of the harness AND THE EVENT SEMANTIC, which is exactly why an observation row answers empty and a named row answers with proceed bytes. The doc comment at :417-429 states the reason and says it does not expire: pasture cannot know which plugin is installed, and an ALREADY-INSTALLED OLDER plugin would throw on an empty body and stop the user's tool call, which is the opposite of failing open.
WHY THE CORRECTION MATTERS AND IS NOT TIDINESS. acceptProceed throws on anything that is not exactly {"decision":"proceed"}. Under the original claim — every route returns empty — every hand-shaped NAMED callback would have depended on the empty-body belt inside acceptProceed to avoid throwing. It does not depend on it: it receives the bytes it demands. A blocking callback that throws fails the user's action, so the difference between those two explanations is the difference between a sitting that is safe by design and one that is safe by accident.

## V-C. KIT-SAFE VERIFIED BY MY OWN ENUMERATION, NOT BY READING THE REPORT.
I parsed the returned object of the kit-safe file and listed its keys. TWELVE, and here they are: event, chat.message, command.execute.before, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, permission.ask, shell.env, tool.definition, tool.execute.after, tool.execute.before.
The four held names are ABSENT from the registered keys. They DO occur once in the file, on line 7, inside the METADATA data blob, which carries all 47 catalogue rows and registers nothing. I checked that rather than assume it, because "the name does not appear" and "the name is not a registered key" are different claims and only the second one is the hold.
The serialisation guard line is present at the stated place and reads, verbatim: `Pasture capture kit could not serialize the payload of <event>, so this row was not captured; the host is not affected: <error>`. The search string for every sitting report is "could not serialize the payload of", and the result is stated EITHER WAY.

## V-D. SITTING 2 IS TWELVE EVENTS. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THE NUMBER 13 HAS BEEN WRITTEN, SO I PIN IT BY ENUMERATION.
The sitting-2 table holds fifteen rows: chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.provider.small_model, tool.definition, experimental.text.complete, tool.execute.after, session.status, session.idle, session.updated, message.updated, message.part.updated, session.diff.
THREE of them are held: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.provider.small_model. Fifteen minus three is TWELVE.
The remaining twelve, named so that no future message has to subtract again: chat.message, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, tool.definition, experimental.text.complete, tool.execute.after, session.status, session.idle, session.updated, message.updated, message.part.updated, session.diff.
Sitting 5 is TWO: experimental.session.compacting and session.compacted. Held: experimental.compaction.autocontinue.
Reachable now: 27 of the 31 recipes. That total was right in every message; only the per-sitting figure was wrong, which is why it survived three readings. THE TOTAL IS NOT A CHECK ON THE PARTS.

text:
TEXT-ONLY ITEMS FROM THE CODEX COVERAGE WORK (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05), recorded here under the standing rule that a comment-text or operator-text finding that changes no behaviour, no gate and no data is batched and fixed once at the end, never by a mid-work fix round.
1. pasture internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0_test.go is an INTERNAL test package (package hostcontract) while its two sibling subjects, the Claude and OpenCode host-contract tests, are black-box (package hostcontract_test). The choice is correct: the refusal the file pins sits on an unexported seam (codexFailureReader and its read function) that a black-box test cannot reach. The file does not state that reason, so a reader sees an unexplained difference between three sibling files. FIX: one sentence in the file header saying why this subject is internal while its siblings are not.
2. pasture internal/codegen/codex_manifest.go, the doc comment on the matcher switch, names six events as the empty-matcher case and calls out Stop and UserPromptSubmit as the events whose entry carries no matcher key. The measured reality at the twelve-row catalogue is FOUR such events: Stop, UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd and Interrupt. The code is correct; the comment predates the catalogue growing from ten rows to twelve. FIX: state the four, or derive the sentence from the switch so it cannot go stale again. The transport leaf of the Codex slice owns that file and can take it when it next writes there.
3. Measured while driving the real Codex host, recorded because someone will meet it: the generated Codex agent-role files draw a host warning at launch, "Ignoring malformed agent role definition ... unknown field 'schema'", once per file. It is in the pasture Codex agent-role generator, not in the hook path, and it changed no capture. It is outside the coverage slice.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PREREQUISITE RECORDED (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05, from the team lead). The lead-owned task aura-plugins-4dh2ny adds two closed-set withholding reasons for all harnesses, WithheldProviderHook and WithheldNotEmittedByHost, and it now blocks this leaf together with the gate-decision slice. It lands before any enabling work, so the reason enum is stable when this leaf enables its rows.
EFFECT ON CODEX: NONE, and the reason is measured, not assumed. All ten uncaptured Codex events have a proven, reachable trigger and every one of them has a real capture file from the live sitting. No Codex row needs either new arm. No Codex row is a provider hook, and no Codex row is registered but unemitted.
WORTH SAYING PLAINLY, because it nearly went the other way: WithheldNotEmittedByHost is exactly the arm Codex WOULD have needed for SubagentStart and SubagentStop if my own note had been right. I wrote that their emission was unmeasured, because the upstream payload directory holds no file for either. The measurement showed both are variants inside the session-start and turn-stop machinery, and both were then captured live. The measurement is what stopped a true enum arm from being used for a false reason. An arm that fits a story is not evidence that the story is true.
NOTHING CHANGES IN THE CATALOGUE, RECIPE, CAPTURE OR CLEARANCE LEAVES. This slice's enabling leaf simply waits for the arm to land, as it already waits for the gate-decision slice.

RECIPE CORRECTION (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). This is a correction by a NEW comment, not an edit of the published list, following the practice the pin-bump slice set. The list stands; this comment overrides one sentence in it.
WHAT THE LIST SAYS, section 2 step 4: one curl target, https://example.org, and "a second file, .2, is expected — Codex previews then confirms the same request; this is not a fault".
WHAT THE FILES SAY. That sentence is FALSE, and the evidence pass found it. I verified it myself by reading the two payloads:
 codex_permission_request_0_153_0.1.json: tool_name Bash, tool_input.command "set -o pipefail\ncurl -s https://example.com | head -n 1", turn_id 01a0736f-d539-7812-9525-a5731c764606.
 codex_permission_request_0_153_0.2.json: tool_name Bash, tool_input.command "set -o pipefail\ncurl -s https://example.org | head -n 1", turn_id 01a07371-81f6-7f52-aefb-3615338a4b46.
Two DIFFERENT turn ids and two DIFFERENT hosts. The sitting ran the approval trigger TWICE, once against example.com and once against example.org, and each run carried its own full cycle of UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse and Stop. There is no preview-then-confirm pair, and this measurement says nothing about whether the host has such a behaviour.
WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. The false sentence would teach the next capture agent to read TWO files as one event's normal shape. That agent would then see ONE file, believe a step was missed, and re-drive a trigger that had already worked. A recipe that predicts the wrong number of files makes a correct sitting look broken.
THE CORRECTED SENTENCE: one approval trigger produces ONE PermissionRequest file. If two appear, the recipe was run twice; check the turn ids and the command in each payload before you conclude anything about the host.
NOTHING ELSE IN THE LIST CHANGES. Both files are genuine captures of the event, both pass every check, and neither is discarded.
FOR THE CLEARANCE LEAF: choose the .1 file, by the standing default of the first occurrence, and name the .2 file as captured-and-not-used with its raw digest. State in the record that the trigger ran twice against two hosts. Do not repeat the preview-and-confirm story in the record; the user accepts the true one.

text:
SITTING PROMPTS 2 TO 8 ARE WRITTEN AND WAITING (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). Sitting 1 is running. The other seven are ready so that no sitting waits on me after it reports.

## FILES
/home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s6/prompt-capturer-s6-<N>.md for N = 1 to 8. Each is one agent, one sitting, Sonnet.

## WHAT EVERY PROMPT CARRIES, so a sitting cannot pass on a check that did not run
- P1 version re-check, 1.18.29, immediately before the session. Anything else is a STOP.
- P2 THE COVERED-ROW SET in the project directory, compared to the expected 43 and named IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A held row PRESENT is a STOP. A count alone is refused, because a kit with the right count and the wrong rows is the failure the hold exists to catch. The prompt also warns that the four held names DO appear once, inside the METADATA data blob on line 7, which registers nothing: the check reads REGISTERED KEYS, never the file text.
- P3 the digest, in the project directory, not only in the kit.
- P4 the three variables exported in the tmux shell BEFORE any hook command runs, never the live store.
- P5 the log offset taken first, because the host log is about 404 MB and only the tail may be read.
- C1 the serialisation-guard search for "could not serialize the payload of", REPORTED EITHER WAY. A row it names is a row whose trigger FIRED and which was not captured, which a missing-stem count would otherwise blame on the trigger.
- C2, C3, C4 the listing with digests, the expected-versus-received comparison, and the housekeeping.

## THE TWO REDUCED SITTINGS SAY WHY THEY ARE REDUCED
Sitting 2 is TWELVE rows, all twelve named in the prompt, and it states plainly that it was fifteen in the published list and that chat.params, chat.headers and experimental.provider.small_model are HELD, absent from kit-safe, and must not be reported missing. It also DROPS the published "no small_model in the configuration" state requirement, because that requirement existed only to make a held row fire. A stale state requirement is how an agent burns a sitting chasing a row that cannot arrive.
Sitting 5 is TWO rows and says the same about experimental.compaction.autocontinue.

## ORDER, AND THE TWO REAL DEPENDENCIES BETWEEN SITTINGS
1 first, always: it is the STOP gate.
Then 2, because 5 and 7 need a session that already holds a completed turn, and sitting 2 produces one. Sitting 2's prompt says to keep that session or note its id.
Sitting 7 needs TWO completed turns and is the only sitting driven mostly by keys, so it carries the read-the-pane rule twice.
3, 4, 6 and 8 are independent and may run in any order after sitting 1. Sitting 8 needs no interface driving at all.
ONE DRIVER PER SESSION stays absolute: two agents typing into one tmux session interleave keystrokes.

## SITTING 4 CARRIES THE ONLY DECISION A SITTING IS ALLOWED TO MAKE
lsp.updated is the campaign's one uncertain row, and sitting 4 decides it by running its step and looking. The prompt requires the outcome EITHER WAY and forbids the obvious wrong fix: DO NOT install or download a language server to make it fire. A download inside a capture sitting changes the machine, and that is not a capture agent's call. If no client spawns, the row joins the raised list with the evidence, and the user gets the same options as every other raised row.

## WHAT IS STILL HELD, AND WHY THE PROMPTS DO NOT GUESS
The four provider-context rows wait on the user. Nothing in these seven prompts captures them, because the keys are absent from the kit rather than because an agent was told to avoid them. That is the difference between a hold that rests on the plugin and a hold that rests on discipline, and it is why I asked for kit-safe rather than a rule in a prompt.
