text:
CORRECTED LIST, corrections 1, 2 and 3 in one repost (worker-s4-l1, 2026-09-05). Sections 6 and 7 below REPLACE the sections of the same number in my trigger list. Section 1.2, sections 2 to 5 and section 8 stand, with one change: LINE C10 IS DROPPED under the supervisor's ruling. I do not recapture the 8 already-enabled events. If one is captured while another trigger runs, I record it and never propose it as a fixture. README.md and NOTES.md stay at two short lines whatever else changes.

=====================================================================
# CORRECTION 1. SECTION 6 AND SECTION 7, REWRITTEN WITH THE CAUSE PER ROW
=====================================================================
The supervisor is right and my section 7 was false for four of six rows. "No reachable trigger" was a summary word that my own section 6 contradicts. A withholding reason is recorded in a shipped artefact and the user is asked to approve it, so it must be true of the row it names. The nine remaining events now carry a CAUSE, and each cause carries only the options that are TRUE for it.

## 6. RAISED, BY CAUSE
There are four causes. No row is filed under a cause that is not its own.

### CAUSE (a). PROVIDER ROW. The trigger is reachable. ENABLING is unsafe.
The host asks this hook to PERFORM the action and reads its answer. Pasture observes; it does not perform. An enabled row would answer with silence and exit 0, which the host reads as a done action.
a1 WorktreeCreate. The host reads standard output as the path of the worktree the hook was asked to create. "Stdout should contain the absolute path to the created worktree directory." / "Other exit codes - worktree creation failed."
a2 WorktreeRemove. The host reads NO standard output; exit 0 IS the assertion that the removal happened. "Exit code 0 - worktree removed successfully."
TRUE OPTIONS, and I choose none: (i) capture and commit the bytes but never enable the row, which is safe because the sink writes before anything is evaluated; (ii) neither capture nor enable, and record why. WHAT IS NOT TRUE HERE: WithheldNoReachableTrigger. The trigger is reachable. No reason in the closed set states "the host expects this hook to perform the action". That gap is plan-level and belongs to the team lead.

### CAUSE (b). OUR TRANSPORT CANNOT CARRY IT. A CODE CHANGE WOULD FIX IT.
b1 FileChanged. The trigger exists on the host and is ordinary: a watched file changes. The generated Claude transport gives every row the empty matcher, and this one row uses the matcher AS ITS WATCH LIST. "The matcher field specifies filenames to watch in the current directory (e.g. \".envrc|.env\")." With an empty matcher nothing is watched, so the row never fires. MEASURED: I approved a file write in a live session and waited 40 seconds; the file was created and no capture appeared.
TRUE OPTIONS: (i) change the Claude hooks generator to emit a watch matcher for this one row, then capture it normally; (ii) leave the row unenabled and record that the transport does not carry it. WHAT IS NOT TRUE HERE: WithheldNoReachableTrigger, and also WithheldUnclearablePayload. Nothing about the payload is the problem.

### CAUSE (c). REACHABLE ONLY UNDER A HOST CONFIGURATION WE WILL NOT IMPOSE.
c1 PermissionDenied. "After auto mode classifier denies a tool call." The trigger EXISTS. It is not a user refusal: MEASURED, I refused a write in a permission dialog and only PermissionRequest appeared. It needs the auto-mode classifier itself to deny, and what the classifier denies depends on the capturing user's own permission settings. MEASURED: two probes I expected to be denied, a write under /etc and "sudo id", were both ALLOWED by this machine's settings and simply failed at the operating system.
TRUE OPTIONS: (i) the user names one tool call that THEIR settings make the classifier deny, and we capture it, accepting that the payload carries that tool call as free text; (ii) leave the row unenabled and record that its trigger depends on user configuration. WHAT IS NOT TRUE HERE: WithheldNoReachableTrigger. The trigger exists and somebody else's machine reaches it every day.

### CAUSE (d). NO ACTION WE CAN TAKE FIRES IT.
d1 Setup. Registered, payload shape known, and I could not find the user action. The binary runs it with kind "setup" and trigger "init" immediately before session start, but it did NOT fire on a first launch in a brand-new directory, and `claude --help` names no init or setup flag. So: no ESTABLISHED user action fires it. This is the only row of the nine where "no reachable trigger" is close to true, and even here the honest wording is "no established trigger", because absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
d2 StopFailure. Reachable only on a host fault we will not induce. "Fires instead of Stop when an API error (rate limit, auth failure, etc.) ended the turn. Fire-and-forget - hook output and exit codes are ignored." Firing it deliberately means forcing a rate limit or breaking authentication on the user's own account.
TRUE OPTIONS for d1: (i) find the action together; (ii) leave it unenabled and record that no established action fires it. For d2: (i) accept one deliberately failed session at a cost the user names; (ii) leave it unenabled and record that its only trigger is a host fault. For d2 note also, in the host's own words, that the row can never block.

### THE THREE THAT ARE NOT RAISED
TaskCreated, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle are NOT on this list. Each has a host trigger sentence and a written recipe in sitting B. They are DOCUMENTED and not measured, which is a different statement from raised.

## 7. CLOSING LINE, CORRECTED
NO CANDIDATE EVENT IS KNOWN TO LACK A REACHABLE TRIGGER. Two rows are reachable and UNSAFE TO ENABLE (WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove). One is reachable on the host but not through our transport (FileChanged). One is reachable only under a permission configuration we will not impose (PermissionDenied). One has NO ESTABLISHED ACTION that fires it (Setup). One is reachable only on a host fault we will not induce (StopFailure). Three carry a documented trigger and a written recipe but no measurement (TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle). The remaining fourteen candidates I made a real 2.1.261 host produce today.

=====================================================================
# CORRECTION 2. THE THREE-COLUMN TABLE OVER ALL 33, WITH THE LIVE NEGATIVE CONTROL
=====================================================================
Columns: READS = does the host read THIS hook's standard output. DOES = what the host does with those bytes. QUOTE = the installed 2.1.261 binary's own sentence. LIVE = did the row fire in my two sessions through a hook that prints NOTHING on standard output, and did the host behave normally.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, stated first because it is the strongest evidence here. My two sessions ran ALL 33 rows registered, through a hook that prints nothing on standard output. TWENTY of the 33 rows FIRED. In every one of those twenty cases the host behaved normally: the model answered, the tools ran, the permission dialog appeared and my answer decided it, the directory was added, the model switched, the subagent ran and finished, the configuration change applied, the sessions ended cleanly. So those twenty rows TOLERATE AN EMPTY STANDARD OUTPUT, by measurement and not by reasoning. THIRTEEN rows never fired, so the run says NOTHING about them, and I say nothing about them either.
FIRED (20): SessionStart, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, PermissionRequest, Notification, MessageDisplay, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, SubagentStart, SubagentStop.
NEVER FIRED (13): Setup, StopFailure, PermissionDenied, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, PreCompact, PostCompact, Elicitation, ElicitationResult. PreCompact and PostCompact are already enabled and simply had no trigger in these sessions.
THE FOUR ROWS THE AMENDMENT NAMED ARE ALL IN THE FIRED SET, so none of them is a provider row and the control proves it directly: UserPromptExpansion (the command expanded and the model answered), PermissionRequest (the dialog appeared and my answer decided it), InstructionsLoaded (nothing changed), MessageDisplay (the text displayed unchanged).

 1 SessionStart        READS yes, as text.        DOES injects it as context for the model. QUOTE "Exit code 0 - stdout shown to Claude". LIVE fired, normal.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CAPTURE LEAF VERDICT: THE CAMPAIGN IS COMPLETE (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). The evidence pass closes both record gaps I named, and the leaf's own acceptance criterion is met with more coverage than the criterion asks for.
THE CRITERION AND THE RESULT. The leaf asks for eight authentic captures outside the repository at the pinned version. The campaign holds 39 files covering ALL TWELVE registered Codex events, at Codex 0.153.0, in /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s5/codex, which is outside every repository. Ten of those events are this slice's targets; the other two are the events already enabled, recaptured by the same sitting and available if the clearance leaf wants them.
WHAT I CHECKED MYSELF, beyond the pass. I read both PermissionRequest payloads and confirmed the surprise the pass reported. I confirmed the file count, the event coverage, the size ceiling and the event-name agreement in my own earlier read. I measured the live store before the pass and the pass measured it again; the two measurements agree on the only number that matters.
GAP 1 IS CLOSED: a verbatim listing, a SHA-256 and a byte size for every one of the 39 files, and a per-capture log of one line per file with the event, the trigger, the time and the digest. The pass states that the log is a REBUILD from the file bytes and the file times, not a copy of an earlier log. That sentence is what makes the log evidence rather than a restatement.
GAP 2 IS CLOSED: `codex --version` re-checked at the end of the campaign, `codex-cli 0.153.0`, unchanged from the check taken before the sitting. The version held at both ends.
THE LIVE STORE, RE-MEASURED: 11,340 lines in the fault journal, up from the 11,065 I counted, and STILL EXACTLY ONE line naming harness codex. The pass drew the right conclusion from the growth: because the codex count did not move, every new line belongs to another harness, so the growth is this session's own hooks and not a second incident. That is the correct way to read a moving number, by holding the population fixed rather than by trusting the total.
THE SURPRISE IS THE MOST VALUABLE PART OF THE PASS. The recipe said the two PermissionRequest files are a preview-then-confirm pair for one request. The payloads carry two different turn ids and two different hosts, so the trigger simply ran twice. I verified it and published the correction as a new comment on the recipe leaf. The lesson for this team: A RECIPE THAT PREDICTS THE WRONG NUMBER OF FILES MAKES A CORRECT SITTING LOOK BROKEN. The next agent would have seen one file, believed a step failed, and re-driven a trigger that had already worked. An evidence pass that only counted files and matched names would have passed this. It was caught because the pass read the payloads and compared them with the story the recipe told.
WHAT THE PASS DID NOT DO, correctly: it did not choose which file the clearance step commits, it did not edit a capture, it did not open the database, it repaired nothing and it deleted nothing.
THE FREE-TEXT FIELD LIST for the clearance step, reported as field names only: prompt on UserPromptSubmit; last_assistant_message on Stop and on SubagentStop; tool_input on PreToolUse, PostToolUse and PermissionRequest; tool_response on PostToolUse. The clearance inventory, not this pass, is the authority; the pass says so itself.
THE LEAF IS DONE. It is NOT closed; closure follows the slice review wave. The clearance leaf starts now.

text:
L1 ACCEPTED AND CLOSED OUT (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). All three corrections are delivered. I verified the two findings myself, read-only, and one of them is bigger than reported.

== WHAT I VERIFIED, NOT TOOK ON TRUST ==
V1 THE EXACT-PAIRS FINDING IS TRUE, and it holds precisely. I counted files and unique digests per stem in the capture directory.
  Already-enabled stems: session_start 4 files / 2 digests. pre_tool_use 14 / 7. post_tool_use 8 / 4. Exactly two to one.
  Candidate stems: user_prompt_submit 11 / 11. stop 10 / 10. message_display 13 / 13. notification 4 / 4. All unique.
  So the cause is confirmed: the installed plugin registers exactly the 8 enabled events and runs the same command with the same binary, so each of those firings is recorded twice. IT IS NOT A DOUBLE-FIRING HOST DEFECT. Whoever selects fixtures must not read it as one.
V2 THE LIVE STORE WAS NOT TOUCHED. ~/.local/share/pasture/pasture.db carries an mtime of 2026-09-05T14:13, hours before the sittings. The scratch database took the writes, as ordered.
V3 THE MODEL-SWITCH FINDING IS TRUE AND IT IS BIGGER THAN REPORTED. I read all three PreModelSwitch and all four PostModelSwitch payloads.
  PreModelSwitch, all three with source "picker": fable to haiku; fable to sonnet; haiku to sonnet.
  PostModelSwitch, four firings with TWO DIFFERENT SOURCES: fable to haiku, source "picker"; haiku to sonnet, source "auto"; sonnet to haiku, source "auto"; haiku to sonnet, source "picker".
  TWO CONCLUSIONS FOLLOW, AND THE SECOND IS A COVERAGE FACT NOBODY HAD.
  First, the candidate reading is confirmed with evidence: the Pre firing "fable to sonnet" has no matching Post, so the host consulted the hook for a model the user only highlighted and never chose.
  Second, and this is the one that matters: THE TWO "auto" SWITCHES HAVE NO PreModelSwitch AT ALL. The host fires the Pre gate only for a picker-driven switch. So a gate on PreModelSwitch CANNOT BLOCK AN AUTOMATIC MODEL SWITCH. PreModelSwitch already carries a host citation for exit-2 blocking, so the row will read as an enforceable gate; it is enforceable only over one of the two ways this host changes model. That must be stated where the row is enabled and where its capability is claimed, or the product will overstate what the gate does.
  FIXTURE GUIDANCE, from the same reading: take the matched picker pair, PreModelSwitch "fable to haiku" with PostModelSwitch "fable to haiku". Do not pair a picker Pre with an auto Post.

== WHAT L1 GOT RIGHT THAT I GOT WRONG ==
I gave the worker the test "does the host read this hook's standard output". That test is WRONG: 20 of the 33 rows read it in some way, so the class would have swallowed the catalogue. The worker replaced it with "does the host NEED bytes only the hook can supply, so that empty standard output is a DATA ANSWER rather than silence". That test found WorktreeRemove, which my starting list did not name and which reads NO standard output at all: our proceed IS exit 0, and the host reads exit 0 as "removed successfully", so an enabled row would assert an action that never happened. One arm was not enough, and that is why the reason-minting task carries two.
The worker also stated the negative control first, which is the right ordering: 20 of the 33 rows fired live through a hook that prints nothing on standard output and the host behaved normally, so those 20 tolerate an empty standard output BY MEASUREMENT; 13 never fired, so the run says nothing about them and the worker said nothing about them either.

== RECORDED FOR THE ENABLING STEP, so it is not lost ==
E1 PreModelSwitch is enforceable only over picker-driven switches. Automatic switches never consult it. Do not claim a full gate.
E2 TaskCreated and TaskCompleted are BLOCKING rows: "Exit code 2 - show stderr to model and prevent task creation".
E3 The registered field lists are incomplete against real payloads for at least seven events. It does not block clearance, because a committed fixture that is not yet enabled is not driven through the waist. It does enlarge the enabling step.
E4 The generated Claude transport gives every row the empty matcher. That is right for most rows and wrong for FileChanged, which uses the matcher as its watch list.
E5 The kit needs TWO generate passes. A compile error on undefined proof constants is NOT a generator refusal. Fewer than 33 keys in the kit transport is a STOP before any sitting.

== L1 IS COMPLETE ==
The trigger list, the provider table, the raised list and the per-file attribution log are all posted. I release worker-s4-l1 with thanks: it captured fourteen events when I asked for one, and that removed a whole sitting from the plan.
I DECLINE ITS OFFER TO RUN SITTING B, for one reason only: the standing rule is that a worker is released when its work is accepted, and a long-running agent making live-session decisions is exactly where context rot bites. Sitting B belongs to the capture leaf and its own worker, which must read this context anyway.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SUPERVISOR GUIDANCE ON THE ONE CONTRADICTION THIS LEAF IS MOST LIKELY TO MEET (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05), added to the lead's instruction to read the Claude corpus before deciding and to surface a contradiction rather than resolve it.
THE SITUATION. This leaf commits cleared fixtures for TEN Codex events that are NOT yet enabled. Enabling is a later leaf and it waits on the gate-decision slice and on the new withholding arms. So for a while the tree will hold an authentic, cleared fixture for an event the activation table still withholds.
WHAT TO MEASURE BEFORE YOU DECIDE ANYTHING. Read the committed Claude corpus and its guards, and answer three questions with file and line: (1) does any guard require a fixture to belong to an ENABLED event, or is the relation one-way, so that an enabled event needs a capture proof but a capture does not need an enabled event; (2) does the per-harness fixture-digest subject accept a new row by a deliberate edit, which is what its own comment says it wants; (3) does anything treat the PRESENCE of a fixture as proof and enable a row by side effect. The third question is the dangerous one. A fixture that enables a row by its presence would turn this leaf into an enabling leaf, and enabling is blocked.
THE ORDER OF PREFERENCE, if the tree allows a choice. FIRST, commit the fixtures and their sidecars and grow the digest table deliberately, and leave the activation table untouched, so the capture work lands and the enabling stays where the plan put it. SECOND, if a guard refuses a cleared fixture for a withheld event, STOP AND SURFACE IT to me. Do not weaken the guard, do not add an exemption, and do not enable a row to make a test pass. A guard that refuses this case may be right, and the answer would then be that the fixtures wait for the enabling leaf.
WHY I SAY IT THIS WAY. The standing rule is to commit what is green and true the same hour. That rule does not license making a claim the tree is not ready to make. A cleared fixture is a true artefact on its own; an enabled row is a claim that the product binds the event. Land the first without the second, or land neither and say why.

ADDENDUM 1 to the L2 order (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). Three facts were measured AFTER the L2 prompt was written. worker-s4-l2 must read them before it selects any fixture. Two of them would cause a wrong action if it did not.

A-1 WHERE THE ATTRIBUTION LOG IS. It is the THIRD section of the worker-s4-l1 comment on aura-plugins-k9xfts timestamped 21:37, under the heading "CORRECTION 3. PER-FILE ATTRIBUTION LOG". It is intact; it was read back out of Beads to confirm it did not arrive as a dash. Stage B is UNBLOCKED.

A-2 THE ALREADY-ENABLED STEMS ARRIVE IN EXACT DIGEST PAIRS. DO NOT FILE A BUG.
I measured this myself, read-only, by counting files against unique digests in the capture directory. Already-enabled stems: session_start 4 files and 2 digests; pre_tool_use 14 and 7; post_tool_use 8 and 4. Exactly two to one. Not-yet-enabled stems: user_prompt_submit 11 and 11; stop 10 and 10; message_display 13 and 13; notification 4 and 4. All unique.
THE CAUSE: the installed plugin registers exactly those 8 events and runs the same command with the same binary, so each firing is recorded twice, once by the project transport and once by the plugin. IT IS NOT A DOUBLE-FIRING HOST DEFECT. A reader who does not know this will file a bug that does not exist.
This affects nothing you select, because those 8 events are not recaptured by my ruling. It affects what you WRITE in the report, and it must not be reported as an anomaly.
Also recorded: pre_compact and post_compact are ABSENT from the directory, because no compaction was run. That is expected and is not a gap, because those two are already enabled and are not recaptured.

A-3 THE MODEL-SWITCH PAIR NEEDS CARE, AND THE REASON IS BIGGER THAN A SELECTION RULE.
I read all three PreModelSwitch and all four PostModelSwitch payloads.
PreModelSwitch fired THREE times, every one with source "picker": fable to haiku, fable to sonnet, haiku to sonnet. One of those switches never happened, so the host consults this hook for a model the user only HIGHLIGHTED.
PostModelSwitch fired FOUR times with TWO sources: fable to haiku (picker), haiku to sonnet (auto), sonnet to haiku (auto), haiku to sonnet (picker).
THE TWO "auto" SWITCHES HAVE NO PreModelSwitch AT ALL.
SELECTION RULE, binding: take the MATCHED PICKER PAIR, PreModelSwitch "fable to haiku" with PostModelSwitch "fable to haiku". NEVER pair a picker Pre with an auto Post; the two describe different host paths and a mismatched pair would put a false story in the clearance record.
WHY IT IS MORE THAN A SELECTION RULE, and this belongs in your report: PreModelSwitch carries a host citation for exit-2 blocking, so the row will read as an enforceable gate when it is enabled. It is enforceable over only ONE of the two ways this host changes model. Say so in the capture report, because the step that enables the row reads your report.

A-4 A REMINDER THAT COSTS NOTHING. Copy, never move. The 102 files in the capture directory are evidence and they are the only record of two live sittings. The kit, the throwaway project with its .claude/settings.json and .claude/commands/probe.md, the scratch database and the capture directory are ALL needed to repeat a sitting. None of them belongs to another team. Delete nothing.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
S4 ROW-TO-ARM MAPPING for the withholding-reason task (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). I post this while the arms are still being written, because the definitions are cheap to get right now and expensive later. Six Claude rows need a reason. Here is what each one is TRUE of, from the measured evidence, and which arm I believe fits.

CLEAN FITS, no question from me:
- WorktreeCreate -> ProviderHook, required-data limb. The host asks the hook to perform the action and reads the answer on standard output: "Stdout should contain the absolute path to the created worktree directory."
- WorktreeRemove -> ProviderHook, asserted-action limb. The host reads NO standard output here. Our proceed IS exit 0, and the host reads exit 0 as "worktree removed successfully", so an enabled row asserts an action that never happened.

ONE QUESTION, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE I HAVE:
- FileChanged. Does EmittedOutsideTransport cover it? The host WOULD emit this event, and it does not, because OUR generator writes an empty matcher on every Claude row while this row uses the matcher as its watch list. So the host is willing and our transport does not subscribe. If EmittedOutsideTransport means "the host emits it, but not through the transport we generate", the fit is exact. If it means something narrower, then FileChanged has no true arm and it should stay unenabled with the cause recorded in prose rather than forced into a near-miss.
  Measured: a file write in a live session produced no event in 40 seconds.

S4 IS NOT A CONSUMER OF NotEmittedByHost, and I say so because it may narrow the definition usefully. All six of my rows ARE emitted by the host, or would be. None of them needs a cited absence of an emission site. So the Codex caution on that arm does not have to accommodate any Claude case.

THE OTHER THREE STAY ON THE EXISTING ARM, and I think that is correct rather than a compromise:
- PermissionDenied, Setup and StopFailure all take WithheldNoReachableTrigger WITH A RECORDED USER DECISION. That arm already requires a clearance path, so the TRUE cause is written in CLEARANCE.md where a reader can find it: for PermissionDenied, that it is reachable only under a permission configuration we will not impose; for Setup, that no user action is established; for StopFailure, that it is reachable only on a host fault we will not induce.
  The arm is honest for these three in a way it was NOT honest for the other three, because here the trigger genuinely is not reachable for us, and the clearance record carries the reason it is not. That is the distinction my earlier correction was about, and it holds.

WHAT I AM NOT ASKING FOR. I am not asking for a fourth arm. Three arms plus the existing NoReachableTrigger cover all six Claude rows, on the condition that the FileChanged question above is answered.

text:
SITTING 1, THE PLUGIN LOAD PROOF. Result: PASSED. The kit-safe plugin loaded and a hand-shaped callback fired.

1. VERSION. `opencode --version` immediately before the session printed: 1.18.29.

2. WHO DROVE. This agent (capturer-s6-1) drove through tmux, session name s6cap, in a shell started for that session only. No non-interactive fallback was needed; the TUI showed a prompt in the normal time and never stalled.

3. THE KIT.
   - Plugin SHA-256, kit-safe, verified in the throwaway source: 73e646d854ecc7c3b5ae326a988b3bac0e90355da4c7d7760407ab74d2b1a649.
   - Plugin SHA-256, verified again in the project directory (/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project/.opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts): same digest, matched.
   - Binary SHA-256 (/home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/bin/pasture-head): 0411482772b75caff4a5dab869c590475dfb0b8df721e8da049281a50044920b, matched the order.
   - COVERED-ROW SET (2a). I read the plugin's returned object. It registers 12 keys: one pass-through `event` key (dispatches every native bus event dynamically through kitObservation, so it covers all 32 catalogued observation rows) plus 11 named keys: tool.execute.before, chat.message, permission.ask, command.execute.before, shell.env, tool.execute.after, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition. The 4 named keys NOT registered are exactly the 4 the order named as held back: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.provider.small_model, experimental.compaction.autocontinue. Coverage: 32 observation rows + 11 named rows = 43, matching the order's expected 43 for kit-safe. NO held row is present. NO ordinary row is missing.
   - Project directory: /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project (holds .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts, copied from kit-safe before the session).

4. PLUGIN LOAD EVIDENCE. The host's log at this version (1.18.29) has NO success-path log line for a loaded plugin — I read packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts at the pinned checkout and confirmed the only plugin-load log call is `Effect.logError("failed to load plugin", ...)` on the FAILURE path; there is no corresponding success message anywhere in that file. So the recipe's expectation of a `msg="loading plugin"` line naming pasture-lifecycle does NOT exist at this host version; that expectation is stale documentation, not a defect in this sitting. Reported as an anomaly below.
   What the log DOES show, read from the exact byte offset noted before the session (baseline 404518397, delta captured to /tmp/s1-log-delta.txt): one `failed to load plugin` ERROR line, naming path=file:///home/minttea/.config/opencode/plugins/bd-prime.ts, error "must default export an object with server()". This is a DIFFERENT global plugin (bd-prime.ts, not the predicted opencode-claude-auth, but still not pasture-lifecycle).    Positive proof pasture-lifecycle loaded: files from MANY distinct native events (catalog.updated, plugin.added x90, integration.updated, reference.updated) were written to the capture directory during host bootstrap, BEFORE any prompt was sent. This can only happen if the plugin's default export was accepted by the loader and its `event` hook was registered on the EventV2 bus (packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:255-262, `for (const hook of hooks) void hook["event"]?.(...)`). A plugin that failed to load would have produced zero of these files.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SITTING 1 ACCEPTED. F-2 IS CLOSED. AND ITS SECOND ANOMALY IS A COVERAGE FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT 47 OF 47 MEANS (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). I verified both anomalies in the upstream source. Both hold, and the second is bigger than it was flagged as.

## F-2 CLOSED
The version matched, both digests were verified in the project directory, the covered-row set was 12 keys over 43 rows with no held row present and no ordinary row missing, and files arrived for chat.message, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.text.complete and tool.definition. NONE of those five exists in the generated plugin at head, so a hand-shaped NAMED key fired in a real host. That is what F-2 asked for.

## ANOMALY 1: MY GATE CONDITION WAS UNSATISFIABLE. THE AGENT WAS RIGHT TO SUBSTITUTE, AND RIGHT TO SAY SO.
I required a host log line `msg="loading plugin"` naming pasture-lifecycle. MEASURED: at v1.18.29 the host logs plugin loading ONLY on the failure branch — packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:231, `Effect.tapError((error) => Effect.logError("failed to load plugin", ...))`. There is no success log anywhere in that file. So NO CORRECT PLUGIN COULD EVER SATISFY THE CONDITION I WROTE, and a literal reading would have stopped the campaign on a working kit.
THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS MY BAR ITEM 5, TWICE IN ONE DAY: a gate whose expected value the system cannot produce. Both came from writing an expectation without measuring the thing that would satisfy it. The rule I keep re-learning: A GATE MUST NAME AN OBSERVABLE THAT SOMETHING IN THE SYSTEM ACTUALLY PRODUCES, and the way to know is to produce it once before publishing the gate.
THE SUBSTITUTE IS STRONGER THAN WHAT I ASKED FOR, and I accept it. Files arrived from the widened `event` hook DURING HOST BOOTSTRAP, before any prompt. That is only possible if the plugin registered, which is what "loaded" means; a log line would have been a report of that fact, while the files ARE the fact. Together with no failure line naming pasture-lifecycle, the load is proven. The agent reported the substitution loudly instead of quietly passing my check, which is the behaviour the rules ask for.
Correction for the record: the predicted unrelated failure was for bd-prime.ts, not opencode-claude-auth. The recipe's prediction was stale.

## ANOMALY 2: OUR OBSERVATION POPULATION IS DERIVED FROM THE WRONG SOURCE. THIS IS A COVERAGE CLAIM PROBLEM.
The widened pass-through captured native events that ARE NOT IN OUR 47-ROW CATALOGUE: catalog.updated, plugin.added (about 90 files), integration.updated, reference.updated and message.part.delta.
I MEASURED ALL FIVE, AND THE RESULT IS DECISIVE:
 - Every one is a REAL HOST EVENT, defined with `define({ type: ... })` in packages/schema/src — catalog.ts:5, plugin.ts:10, integration.ts:80, reference.ts:8, v1/session.ts:633.
 - Every one is ABSENT from packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts, which is the SDK Event union our 32 observations were derived from. Measured count of occurrences in that file: 0, for all five.
 - Every one WAS DELIVERED to the plugin's `event` hook in a live session.
SO THE SDK EVENT UNION IS NOT THE SET OF EVENTS THE PLUGIN RECEIVES. Our observation population was taken from a type file that does not describe the bus. A live host delivered at least five events our catalogue does not carry.
WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING ROW: the epic's claim is that EVERY REGISTERED NATIVE EVENT lowers to the waist IR, and the number 47 is what makes that claim checkable. If the registered set is smaller than the set the host delivers, then 47 of 47 is a true statement about our own table and a FALSE statement about the host. A later reader cannot tell those apart from the report. This is the plan's own "derive the population" rule biting at the level above the guard: the guard derived its population faithfully FROM THE WRONG SOURCE, and every internal check stayed green.
IT TOOK A LIVE SESSION TO SEE IT. My published bar asked for the population to be derived from OUR tree, which is the right check for internal consistency and CANNOT catch a wrong upstream source. The capture campaign found what no static check in this slice was looking for.

## WHAT I RULE, AND WHAT I ESCALATE
I RULE, slice-internal: the sittings CONTINUE. Nothing here stops the capture of rows we do have. From now on every sitting report LISTS OUT-OF-CATALOGUE STEMS SEPARATELY, as evidence toward the true population, at no extra cost. They are NOT findings against the sitting and NOT fixtures for any row. I am adding that to prompts 2 to 8.
I RULE, for L3: an out-of-catalogue capture is NEVER committed as a fixture. It has no row, no target, no proof arm and no clearance basis. It is evidence in a report, and nothing more.
I ESCALATE, plan-level, because it changes a published number and a user decision that is already in flight: the observation population needs re-deriving from the host's own event definitions rather than from the SDK type union, and the 47 in D-1 is now a floor and not a total. The five names above are the measured start of that list and I do NOT claim they are all of it: nobody has enumerated the schema definitions yet, and after today I am not going to assert a count I have not listed.

text:
CAPTURE REPORT for the leaf (worker-s4-l2, 2026-09-05).

## 1. VERSION, BEFORE AND AFTER STAGE A
`claude --version` immediately before the sitting: "2.1.261 (Claude Code)".
`claude --version` immediately after the sitting: "2.1.261 (Claude Code)".
The host did not move. No STOP.

## 2. WHO DROVE, AND HOW
I drove one live session through tmux (session name s4l2b), per the tmux-capture-driver skill.
Launch: `tmux new-session -d -s s4l2b -c <project dir>`, then in the launching shell:
`unset CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `export PASTURE_BIN=<kit binary>`,
`export PASTURE_DB_PATH=<scratch>/pasture-b.db` (a fresh scratch database, separate file from
sitting A's), `export PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR=<base>/sitting-b`,
`export CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION="$(claude --version | cut -d' ' -f1)"`, then `claude`.
The project directory had already been trusted in an earlier sitting, so no folder-trust prompt
appeared this time.

Two prompts were sent, text and Enter as two calls each:
1. "Use the Team tool to create one teammate named prober with the single task \"Reply with the
   word ok.\" Wait for it to finish and go idle, then tell me it is done."

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CATALOGUE COMPLETENESS AT OPENCODE 1.18.29, MEASURED (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). The lead asked how many distinct bus event types the host publishes versus the 47 we register, with citations. Here is what I measured, what it means, and the number I REFUSE to publish because I have not enumerated it properly.

## 1. THE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE IS THE HOST'S OWN EVENT MANIFEST, AND IT IS NOT WHAT WE USED
The plugin's `event` hook is fed by one listener: packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:255-262. It takes EVERY event from `events.listen` whose `location.directory` equals the plugin's own directory, and hands it to `hook["event"]` with the native type. There is no per-event filter and no allow-list.
The set of events that bus can carry is composed in packages/schema/src/event-manifest.ts:63-84, `EventManifest.Definitions`, which unions about twenty definition modules (session, filesystem, permission, plugin, pty, question, tui, lsp, mcp, vcs, workspace, worktree, installation, integration, catalog, reference, project and more).
OUR 32 OBSERVATIONS WERE DERIVED FROM packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts, the generated SDK type union. THAT IS A DIFFERENT SET. The manifest is the population; the SDK union is a type file that does not describe the bus.

## 2. WHAT I MEASURED, WITH ITS LIMITS STATED
I extracted every `define({ ... type: "..." ... })` declaration under packages/schema/src. RESULT: 86 distinct event type strings.
THAT 86 IS A FLOOR, NOT A TOTAL, AND I CAN PROVE IT IS INCOMPLETE. My extraction did not find tui.command.execute, which IS declared, at packages/schema/src/tui-event.ts:14. A text extraction that misses one declaration misses others I have not identified. So the honest statement is AT LEAST 86.
Set difference against our 47 catalogue rows: 58 declared types are absent from our catalogue. Of those, 30 are the `session.next.*` family declared in packages/schema/src/session-event.ts, and that module IS inside the manifest, through `coreDefinitions` at event-manifest.ts:37. So they are not a separate generation sitting outside the bus.
Four of our observation rows did not appear in my extraction. TWO of those are extraction misses (tui.command.execute at tui-event.ts:14, and server.instance.disposed, which has a cited emit site). THE OTHER TWO ARE THE GENUINE CATALOGUE DEFECTS ALREADY RAISED: lsp.client.diagnostics and permission.updated, which have no declaration and no publish site at this version.

## 3. THE EVIDENCE THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON MY ANALYSIS AT ALL
FIVE events reached the plugin IN A LIVE SESSION and are absent from our 47: catalog.updated, plugin.added (about 90 files), integration.updated, reference.updated, message.part.delta. Each is declared in packages/schema/src (catalog.ts:5, plugin.ts:10, integration.ts:80, reference.ts:8, v1/session.ts:633) and each occurs ZERO times in packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts.
THIS IS THE DECISIVE PART OF THE FINDING. It needs no manifest reading and no set arithmetic: a real host delivered events to a real plugin, and our table does not carry them. Everything in section 2 explains that fact; section 3 IS the fact.

## 4. WHAT I WILL NOT SAY
I will not publish "the host has N bus events" or "we are missing 58 rows" as a number to act on. My extraction is provably incomplete, and the 58 mixes three different things: types certainly on the plugin's bus, types whose bus I have not checked one by one, and artefacts of my own regex. The correct derivation walks `EventManifest.Definitions` itself rather than grepping for a literal, and nobody has done that yet.
I make this refusal explicit because the plan records three counts in this epic that were wrong and every one of them was enumerable and described instead. I have added three more today. THE NUMBER TO ACT ON MUST BE PRODUCED BY WALKING THE MANIFEST, and that is L5 work with a test behind it, not a supervisor's grep.

## 5. WHAT THIS COSTS THE SLICE, STATED PLAINLY
The claim "47 of 47" is a true statement about OUR TABLE and an unproven statement about the host. That is exactly the shape the plan warns about: a guard that derives its population faithfully from the wrong source passes every internal check while covering a fraction of the real population. Our derivation was faithful; our source was wrong.
A second consequence, and it is a live one: the capture directories now hold files for events with no catalogue row. They are captured-and-not-in-catalogue. They are NOT fixtures, they get no row, no target, no proof arm and no clearance basis, and L3 never commits them.

## 6. WHAT I RULE AND WHAT I ESCALATE
RULED, slice-internal: sittings continue; every report lists out-of-catalogue stems separately as population evidence; those files never enter the batch.
ESCALATED: whether S6 widens the catalogue at L5 or records a follow-up is the lead's call, and it interacts with D-1, which is with the user now. D-1 asks the user to choose between 33 of 47 and 39 of 47. THE DENOMINATOR IN THAT QUESTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Whichever way the lead rules on the catalogue, the user should not be asked to approve a coverage fraction whose bottom number is now known to be a floor.

text:
THE THREE TEAMMATE EVENTS DID NOT FIRE. CLASSIFIED WITH EVIDENCE (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). This amends the final reason table posted earlier today.

WHAT HAPPENED. The capture worker made two genuine attempts in a live session: it spawned a NAMED teammate with an inline one-line task, and it then asked the session to create a task with a subject and a description for that same teammate. A real named teammate was created, given work, replied and went idle, TWICE, visible in the transcript and the status panel. TaskCreated, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle produced NO capture file, while ten other stems fired normally in the same session.

I DID NOT ACCEPT "RAISE THEM" WITHOUT RULING OUT OUR OWN GAP FIRST, because that is exactly the shape FileChanged turned out to have.

TEST 1, IS IT OUR TRANSPORT? NO. I read the session's own settings file. It carries 33 hook keys. TaskCreated, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle are ALL PRESENT, each with the correct command line and the version argument. Our side subscribed and the host did not deliver. This is NOT the FileChanged shape.

TEST 2, IS THE HOST SIMPLY NOT EMITTING THEM IN THIS BUILD? NOT SUPPORTED. The new NotEmittedByHost arm requires a CITED ABSENCE OF AN EMISSION SITE. I counted the names in the installed 2.1.261 binary: TaskCreated 19 occurrences, TaskCompleted 27, TeammateIdle 23. Compare the events that DO fire: SubagentStart 29, DirectoryAdded 29. The density is comparable, so there is no absence to cite. The evidence the arm demands does not exist, and I will not claim it.

CONCLUSION, and it is the honest one: THE EVENTS ARE EMITTED BY THIS BUILD UNDER A CONDITION WE DID NOT REACH. That is the same class as Setup. The reason is NoReachableTrigger WITH A RECORDED USER DECISION, and the true cause goes in CLEARANCE.md in words: two genuine attempts with a real named teammate did not produce them, and the condition that does is not established.

THIS DOES NOT REVERSE WHAT I TOLD THE TEAM LEAD. S4 STILL CONSUMES TWO ARMS ONLY, ProviderHook and NoReachableTrigger. NotEmittedByHost still has no Claude consumer. No fourth arm is needed.

== AMENDED FINAL TABLE. 33 rows. ==
ENABLE-ABLE: 22. The 8 already enabled, plus the 14 captured and cleared.
WITHHELD: 11, across four reasons.
  MissingRequestCorrelation, 2: Elicitation, ElicitationResult.
  ProviderHook, 2: WorktreeCreate (required-data), WorktreeRemove (asserted-action).
  OutsideTargetSet, 1: FileChanged, cause in prose, our matcher gap, follow-up filed.
  NoReachableTrigger with a recorded user decision, 6: PermissionDenied, Setup, StopFailure, and now TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle.
22 plus 11 is 33. The user-decision rows move from three to six.
THE DERIVED TARGET IS 22 OF 33, not the 25 the trigger list projected. Sitting B was run and it did not deliver its three.

MY RECOMMENDATION, and the user decides. DO NOT SPEND A THIRD SITTING BLINDLY. Two genuine attempts failed and we cannot name what would make the third different. If the user knows the team or task topology that fires these three, one short sitting captures them and the target returns to 25. If not, withhold the three with the decision recorded.

== TWO NOTES ON THE CAPTURE REPORT ITSELF ==
N1 CORRECT A COUNT. The report says sitting B produced 48 files. I counted 47 files, all of them .json. A count in a record the user reads must be right, and the standing rule is that a count states its range. Fix it to 47.
N2 THE BINDING SELECTION RULE WAS FOLLOWED EXACTLY, and I checked rather than assumed. The batch carries PreModelSwitch "fable to haiku, picker" with PostModelSwitch "fable to haiku, picker". That is the matched picker pair, not a picker Pre with an auto Post.
Also verified: the batch holds 14 files over 14 distinct stems, exactly the 14 candidates; the 102 originals are intact; nothing was moved.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
L2 ACCEPTED AND CLOSED OUT (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). Both corrections are posted and I verified them read-only. worker-s4-l2 is released.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF, not on trust.
V1 The batch holds 14 files over 14 distinct stems, exactly the 14 candidates. The 102 originals are intact in the capture directory. Nothing was moved. Copy, never cut, was obeyed.
V2 THE MATCHED-PAIR CLAIM IS TRUE AND THE WORKER FOUND BETTER EVIDENCE THAN MY RULE ASKED FOR. My binding rule said to match on source and on the model pair. The worker also checked prompt_id, and I confirmed it: both committed model-switch payloads carry the SAME prompt_id, b00aa439-bb17-4596-9f84-3ef106a968e4, with source "picker" and the same from and to models. A shared prompt_id proves the two events belong to ONE host operation. That is stronger than matching on the fields I named, because two separate picker operations could have carried the same model pair. I adopt prompt_id as the pairing test for any paired event from now on.
V3 The count correction landed and is right: 47 files, all .json. The earlier prose said 48 in two sentences; the listing was always correct. The correction says to read 47 wherever the report says 48, which also covers the one remaining "48" in the acknowledgement comment.

A FIELD-GAP DATUM FOR THE ENABLING STEP, which I noticed while checking the pairing. PreModelSwitch's registered field list allows prompt_id, and the real payload also carries from_model, to_model and source, none of which the catalogue lists. That is finding F1 made concrete on a specific row with specific field names, rather than as a general warning. The built binary refuses a payload carrying a member the registration does not allow, so this row cannot be enabled until its field list grows. The same is true for the other six rows F1 named.

WHAT L2 DID WELL, recorded because it is the behaviour I want repeated.
It reported a NEGATIVE RESULT plainly. Three events did not fire after two genuine attempts, and it said so instead of presenting a thin success. That negative result, plus the fact that the subscription was live and carried throughout, is the whole evidence base for classifying the teammate trio. A worker that had quietly dropped them would have left the slice claiming a target it could not reach.
It also added the right sentence to its report without being told twice: that a sitting producing zero new fixtures is still useful, because it independently confirms the transport delivers all 33 subscribed hooks.

THE CAPTURE LEAF'S OUTPUT IS FINAL: 14 cleared-ready captures, one per event, each with its trigger, time and raw digest. The clearance step starts from it.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PAIRING RULE, ADDED TO THIS LEAF'S ORDER (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05), from a harness-independent rule the Claude slice measured, then refined against the Codex bytes.
THE RULE. When a fixture set holds PAIRED events, a pre and a post of one host operation, or two files a recipe says belong together, the pairing test is the HOST'S PER-OPERATION IDENTIFIER, not the field values and not the source. Two separate operations can carry identical field pairs and pass a value-only test. On Codex the identifiers are turn_id and tool_use_id; on Claude it is prompt_id; on OpenCode it is the session or call id.
THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE IS IN THIS BATCH. The two PermissionRequest files carry two different turn ids and two different hosts. A value-only reading would have called them a preview and a confirmation of one request, and the recipe did exactly that. The record must pair by identifier and must say plainly that the two files are TWO OPERATIONS.
WHAT I MEASURED IN THE BATCH, so this leaf does not have to guess. All 39 files carry ONE session_id. Seven distinct turn ids exist. Two files carry no turn id at all.
CODEX HAS TWO GRANULARITIES AND THE RIGHT ONE DEPENDS ON THE EVENT:
 - TOOL-CALL SCOPE, the finest: PreToolUse and PostToolUse both carry tool_use_id. The chosen pair proves it: codex_pre_tool_use_0_153_0.1.json and codex_post_tool_use_0_153_0.1.json share BOTH the turn id and the tool_use_id, so they are one tool call, not two that look alike.
 - TURN SCOPE: PermissionRequest carries turn_id and NO tool_use_id, so it can be paired to a turn but never to a specific tool call by identifier alone. Say that limit in the record rather than implying a tighter link than the bytes support.
 - SESSION SCOPE, and this is the trap: the two files with no turn id pair only by session_id, and this batch holds ONE session. A session-level pairing claim therefore carries NO INFORMATION here, because every file in the batch would satisfy it. AN IDENTIFIER THAT EVERY MEMBER SHARES DOES NOT PAIR ANYTHING. Do not state a session-level match as if it were evidence of a pair.
WHAT THE RECORD MUST DO. For every pair it asserts, name the identifier and its scope, and give the value. For every file it does NOT pair, say so plainly rather than leaving the reader to assume a link. State the PermissionRequest case as two operations against two hosts, with both turn ids.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
THE PLUGIN-BUS EVENT POPULATION AT 1.18.29, ENUMERATED FROM THE HOST'S OWN MANIFEST (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). This replaces my earlier grep, which I refused to publish a total from. This one is derived from the manifest composition, module by module, and it validates itself.

## THE DERIVATION, AND WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE
The plugin's `event` hook receives every event from `events.listen` whose `location.directory` equals the plugin's directory, with no filter (packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts:255-262). The set that bus can carry is `EventManifest.Definitions`, composed at packages/schema/src/event-manifest.ts:63-84, from `foundationDefinitions` (:36-44), `coreDefinitions` (:37) and `featureDefinitions` (:46-55). I walked that composition and took the declared event types of each module it names.

## THE 28 MODULES AND THEIR DECLARED TYPE COUNTS, with the file for each
catalog 1 (catalog.ts) · filesystem 1 · filesystem-watcher 1 · installation-event 2 · integration 2 ·
legacy-event 1 (v1/legacy-event.ts) · lsp-event 1 · mcp-event 2 · models-dev 1 · permission 2 ·
permission-v1 2 (v1/permission.ts) · plugin 1 · project 1 · project-directories 1 · pty 4 ·
question 3 · question-v1 3 (v1/question.ts) · reference 1 · server-event 2 ·
session-compaction-event 1 · session-event 32 · session-status-event 2 · session-todo 1 ·
session-v1 10 (v1/session.ts) · tui-event 4 · vcs-event 1 · workspace-event 3 · worktree-event 2.
All files are under packages/schema/src.

## THE COUNT
88 DISTINCT EVENT TYPES across those 28 modules. NO MODULE COUNTS ZERO.
That last clause is the check, not decoration. My FIRST run of this same enumeration returned 72 and showed FOUR modules at zero: session-v1, permission-v1, legacy-event and question-v1. Four empty modules is implausible, and it was: those four files are one-line re-exports of packages/schema/src/v1/*.ts, so the declarations live one directory down and my extraction read the wrong file. A TOTAL WOULD HAVE HIDDEN THAT. The per-module breakdown is what exposed it, and it is why this report prints every module rather than a number.

## HOW OUR CATALOGUE COMPARES
Our catalogue carries 32 observation rows. 29 of them are in the 88. THREE ARE NOT, and every one is already explained, which is the strongest validation this enumeration has:
- lsp.client.diagnostics and permission.updated: the two rows measured earlier as declared nowhere at this version. They fit WithheldNotEmittedByHost.
- server.instance.disposed: emitted on the raw GlobalBus (project/instance-store.ts), never on this manifest. It fits the third arm, emitted outside the plugin's transport.
So the enumeration independently reproduces three findings that were reached by a different route. That is why I am willing to publish this count and was not willing to publish the last one.
59 OF THE 88 ARE NOT IN OUR CATALOGUE AT ALL.

## THE LIMIT ON THAT 59, STATED BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT
59 IS AN UPPER BOUND ON WHAT A PLUGIN CAN SEE, NOT A COUNT OF MISSING ROWS. The listener drops any event whose location directory is not the plugin's own, so a type that is only ever emitted with a global scope never reaches a plugin however well it is declared. Candidates in the 59 on their names alone are global.disposed, models-dev.refreshed and ide.installed, and I have NOT checked them one by one. The number of rows we are actually missing is somewhere between 5 and 59, and closing that gap means checking the emit site of each type for its location scope.
FIVE ARE PROVEN, and they need no argument: catalog.updated, plugin.added, integration.updated, reference.updated and message.part.delta reached a real plugin in a live session on this machine.

## WHAT I HAND TO L5
The derivation above is the mechanism L5 should implement as a test, not a number to copy: walk the manifest composition, take the declared types, and compare against the registered set. A test shaped that way covers a type added upstream with no test edit. A hand-list of 88 would pass its own mutations today and be wrong at the next host release, which is the exact defect the plan's derive-the-population rule exists to stop.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PRE-VERIFICATION FOR THE CLEARANCE STEP (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). Two read-only checks I ran on the batch before the clearance worker started. One is a specific hazard; the other corroborates the commit ruling.

H-1 THE SLUG SPELLING IS PRESENT IN TEN OF THE FOURTEEN FILES. This is the spelling that gets missed.
home-path-v1 has three spellings: the absolute /home/<user>, the relative home/<user>/, and the directory SLUG a host derives from a path, -home-<user>-. I grepped the batch. At least TEN files carry the slug spelling: directory_added, instructions_loaded, cwd_changed, config_change, message_display, user_prompt_submit, notification, permission_request, user_prompt_expansion and post_model_switch.
CONSEQUENCE IF IT IS MISSED: the capturing user's name survives clearance in ten committed files. The structural home-path guard exists precisely to catch this, so the likely outcome is a red gate rather than a leak; but the cost of finding out that way is a wasted round, and the cost of the guard not covering a spelling is a leak. The clearance worker is told to handle all three and to prove it.
CHECKED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO: all 14 files carry a home path, so after substitution every one satisfies the corpus assertion that the body contains the placeholder. No fixture will fail that check for want of a path.

C-1 THE COMMIT RULING IS CORROBORATED, AND THE WORKER STILL MEASURES IT ITSELF.
The team lead ordered the clearance worker to measure the cleared-but-not-enabled facts and to STOP if any is false. That is the right instruction and it stands. I ran the same read independently and I get the same answer:
- The production-waist test iterates a HAND LIST, authenticClaudeEnabledFixtures, holding exactly the 8 enabled fixtures. A new fixture is not in it and is not driven through the waist.
- The frontend test and the codegen test reference fixtures by EXACT PATH, and only for enabled events. Neither globs.
- The only globber over the directory is the closed inventory in authentic_2_1_261_test.go. The secret scan and the home-path guard walk all files and SHOULD see the new ones.
So a committed-but-not-enabled fixture is legal and green, and my ruling that the clearance step commits the bytes and extends the closed inventory in the same commit holds. IF THE WORKER'S MEASUREMENT DISAGREES WITH MINE, THE WORKER'S WINS AND IT STOPS. I would rather be corrected before the commit than have a wrong ruling ship.

ONE PRACTICAL NOTE RECORDED FOR THE COMMIT: the closed inventory maps fixture name to event name and then validates each fixture's sidecar against that event. The 14 new entries must carry the correct event name, or the extension fails for a reason that looks like a clearance defect and is not.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PAIRING RULE RECORDED FOR L3, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IT HAS ALREADY CREATED IN THIS HARNESS (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## THE RULE, as ruled by the lead from S4 and binding on my L3 order
A PAIRED EVENT — a before and after pair of ONE host operation — is matched by the host's PER-OPERATION IDENTIFIER, never by field values and never by the source alone. Two operations can carry identical fields. On OpenCode the identifiers are sessionID plus callID for tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after, and the message identifier for the message events.
WHY FIELD VALUES ARE NOT ENOUGH, in this harness specifically: two `ls -la` calls in one session produce two tool.execute.before payloads whose `output.args.command` is the same string, and after free-text substitution BOTH become the same placeholder of the same length. At that point nothing but the callID distinguishes them, and the substitution has erased the only other difference.

## THE CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE TREE
The committed OpenCode corpus holds two fixtures from the earlier campaign, and I read their identifiers:
- session_created_1_18_29.json carries sessionID ses_f8e723e13ffeUWnfE2vlRBO1xN.
- tool_execute_before_1_18_29.json carries the SAME sessionID and callID call_4zMdLgUBV12aE7yHvuYQolSx.
Sitting 2 will capture tool.execute.after. IT WILL COME FROM A DIFFERENT SESSION AND A DIFFERENT OPERATION, because it is a new sitting on a new day. So the committed `before` and the new `after` would be two halves of a pair THAT NEVER HAPPENED. Any test, IR assertion or report that reads them as one operation would be asserting something the host never produced, and every gate would stay green, because each fixture is individually authentic.

## THE FIX IS FREE, AND I RULE IT NOW
KIT-SAFE REGISTERS tool.execute.before — it is one of its twelve keys. So every sitting that runs a tool call captures a NEW before ALONGSIDE the after, from the SAME operation, at no extra cost and with no extra sitting.
L3 THEREFORE SELECTS THE PAIR FROM ONE OPERATION: choose the tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after whose sessionID AND callID match, from the same sitting, and state both identifiers in the clearance record beside the two file names.
WHETHER THAT NEW `before` REPLACES THE COMMITTED ONE is a question I do not settle alone, because the committed fixture is covered by a user acceptance already given. I record both options for the lead: replace it, so the corpus holds one coherent operation and the batch acceptance covers both halves; or keep it and accept that the corpus holds a before from one operation and an after from another, with that fact written in the clearance record so no later reader pairs them. I recommend nothing here; I note only that the second option must be WRITTEN DOWN if it is chosen, because an unstated mismatch is the version of this that hurts.

## WHAT L3 MUST DO WITH IT, in the order it will run
1. For every paired family, group the captures by per-operation identifier BEFORE choosing which file to commit.
2. Choose the pair, not the file. The earlier default was "take the .1 file per stem". THAT DEFAULT IS UNSAFE FOR A PAIR: the .1 before and the .1 after can be different operations whenever a sitting made more than one call.
3. State the identifiers in the clearance record, so a reader can verify the pairing without re-reading the bytes.
4. The same rule governs the message family: message.updated, message.part.updated, message.removed and message.part.removed are grouped by the message and part identifiers, not by arrival order.

NOTHING IS LOST BY THE SITTINGS ALREADY RUNNING. The identifiers are IN THE CAPTURED BYTES, so L3 can group them after the fact. A sitting report that also says which turn produced which file makes that grouping cheaper, but it is not required and I am not interrupting five running sittings to add it.

text:
ROUND-1 REVIEW (reviewer-s5-r1, 2026-09-05). Target 3135e55 on slice/rp2tju-s5, base 0b33f07. VERDICT: REVISE. 0 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT, 3 MINOR. I never touched the live worktree; every measurement is on my own archive copy at /tmp/reviewer-s5-r1.

WHAT HELD, AND HOW I PROVED IT
1. THE MECHANISM IS RIGHT. The catalogue reads one field, mapping.Failure(), the effective arm the evidence rule produced. It reads nothing else. The gate-or-observation semantic, the mutation mode, the stop-loop policy and the identities stay declared, and each of the three remaining axes is now pinned BY NAME from a derivation. The seam is smaller than the OpenCode precedent, which derives its whole row, and it is the right size for a catalogue that still holds hand-declared identities.
2. ALL 24 CITATIONS ARE CORRECT, checked one by one in the read-only clone at tag rust-v0.153.0 (41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715). Every emission site names the function that builds the hook request; every payload site names the serde_json::to_string of the command input for that event.
3. BOTH SHARED-EMISSION CLAIMS ARE TRUE, and I refuted nothing. SessionStart and SubagentStart come out of run_pending_session_start_hooks at :124, which picks StartHookTarget::SubagentStart for a thread-spawn subagent at :128-140 and StartHookTarget::SessionStart otherwise. Stop and SubagentStop come out of run_turn_stop_hooks at :376, which picks the target at :385-392. The two payload sites differ inside one file, session_start.rs:130 against :156 and stop.rs:152 against :183, which is what the table says.
4. ALL FOUR WORKER MUTATIONS RE-DRIVE RED, with the message text the worker quoted.
   M1 hand-written arm on one row: "the Codex catalog row "PermissionRequest" states the failure mode exit-2-blocks and the runtime profile holds report-and-continue; the catalog must READ this field from the profile, because a mode written twice can be demoted in one artefact and kept in the other".
   M2 the read returns a constant: same subject, RED on SessionStart, "states the failure mode report-and-continue and the runtime profile holds strict-hook-failure".
   M3 control A, the profile's arms collapsed: "every Codex catalog row carries the same failure arm map[report-and-continue:12]; a read that returned one constant would satisfy every check above, so this control fails first", and the registration subject RED four ways beside it.
   M4 control B, every Codex row cites evidence: "no Codex row is a gate the evidence rule demoted, so the case this subject exists for is not present and the checks above prove nothing; the arms measured are map[strict-hook-failure:4 strict-output-exit-2-blocks:8]", plus the derived-counts fatal and the runtime evidence pin.
5. THE BYTE IDENTITY HOLDS, measured by me, not taken from the report. One binary from an archive of 0b33f07 and one from 3135e55, each with its OWN bootstrapped scratch store ("pasture --db <path> task create bootstrap", exit 0 on both), over the two committed Codex fixtures.
   NORMAL PATH: SessionStart exit 0 on both, stdout {} , sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16... on both; PreToolUse exit 0 on both, stdout {"continue":true}, sha256 a1f7818dbf24fe751cbed1cf... on both. cmp reports no difference on stdout or stderr for either event.
   FAIL-CLOSED FAULT PATH, --db under a path whose parent is a file, PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1: both events, both binaries, exit 0, stdout identical, stderr identical byte for byte by cmp. The PreToolUse diagnostic still reads "declared failure mode strict-output-exit-2-blocks, effective failure mode report-and-continue" on BOTH binaries. One correction to the worker report: the SessionStart fault diagnostic reads "declared failure mode strict-hook-failure, effective failure mode strict-hook-failure", not the exit-2 pair; the pair the report quotes is the PreToolUse one. The conclusion is unchanged, and it is the important one: nothing on the hook path reads the catalogue.
6. THE THIRD KIND OF VACUITY IS NOT PRESENT AT TREE LEVEL. I asked whether the derivation could read an empty or narrower population and still pass. An EMPTY profile population cannot hide: codexFailureReader builds its map from the profile's own event catalog and then looks up by name, so a missing name stops the build loudly. A NARROWER CATALOGUE cannot hide either: I deleted one catalogue row, ran make generate and the suites, and the tree turned RED in three independent places, including "the registration manifests declare 91 events and the lifecycle profiles declare 92 rows" and a build failure in internal/lifecycle/activation. The gap is only in the NEW subject, which stayed green on that mutation; that is MINOR aura-plugins-1fpx1p.
7. OWNERSHIP IS EXACT AND BOTH DEVIATIONS ARE THE SMALLEST AVAILABLE. Named equals touched, six files, checked against git show --stat. failure_divergence_test.go could not stay true without this edit, and moving the Codex lists to a second file would break the one-file-per-subject rule, so the deviation is minimal; it also holds the Claude lists, so it is a merge point for S4 and no Claude name moved. The generated Codex manifest is a table row assigned to the merge, and the drift gate cannot be green without regenerating it; my own make generate on my copy reproduced the committed bytes exactly, so the integrator's authoritative regeneration will too.
8. NO INTERNAL REFERENCE IS ADDED. I scanned every changed line and the commit message for task ids, proposal or slice names, phase numbers, round or finding ids and process words. The only hits are on REMOVED lines: "harness slices should prefer" and "harness slice fixed a row", both replaced by prose with no process word. Two out, none in, as claimed.
9. SIX GATES GREEN ON MY OWN ARCHIVE COPY, under the race lock, with GATE RUNNING and GATE DONE posted on aura-plugins-ow5zsm. go build 0, go vet 0, go test -race -count=1 ./... rc=0 ok=74 FAIL=0 data races 0 no-test-files 9 no-tests-to-run 0, make generate with an EMPTY porcelain after 168 generator lines, gofmt -l . naming nothing and then NAMING MY PLANTED CONTROL FILE, which I removed, and nix flake check --no-build green on cgo-disabled-build, race and installer. No re-run was needed.
10. THE MOVED-CEILING SWEEP IS REAL, not a claim. AGENTS.md carries no Codex count and no Codex blocking claim; its two Codex sentences are the hook-budget note and the fail-open bytes {"continue":true}, and section 5 above proves those bytes unmoved. CHANGELOG "all eight Codex gates" counts the runtime profile's eight blocking rows and is true; the new entry's "seven Codex events" counts the catalogue's seven gate rows and is true; I measured both populations. metamodel.gen.go and the .codex transport files derive from the runtime profile and did not move, and make generate produced exactly one changed file. hostexit.go still calls "codex PreToolUse" a declared blocking gate with no citation, which is still true because the DECLARED mode did not move.

WHAT DID NOT HOLD: FOUR IMPORTANT FINDINGS
None is a BLOCKER. The mechanism is sound and nothing a host sees moves. All four are false or unwatched CLAIMS, which is what this axis exists for.
aura-plugins-kq5497 THE ZERO-GATE PIN REFUSES THE FIRST REAL CODEX CITATION AND MISDIAGNOSES IT. I gave exactly ONE Codex row a real citation, changed no catalogue line, ran make generate and the suites. The new check turned RED with "the Codex catalogue states a blocking exit code on 1 rows while the runtime profile cites no Codex evidence for one; a reader of the catalogue would learn a refusal the product cannot perform". Both clauses are then false. The commit message promises that a later citation "moves both artefacts together"; this pin is the one thing that stops that promise, and the next leaf of this slice exists to record Codex deny-contract evidence.
aura-plugins-nd601m THE NEW REFUSAL MESSAGE OVERSTATES ITS COST, AND A TEST PINS THE FALSE PHRASE. It says "no Codex manifest can be generated and no Codex hook can be admitted". The second half is false: the hostcontract package is not imported by any non-test, non-generator package, and Parse in internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/capture.go admits with the COMMITTED generated manifest. A maintainer who meets this panic is told the product is down for Codex when only regeneration stops.
aura-plugins-lcs8q7 "THE COUNTS ABOVE ARE READ BACK FROM THE TREE" IS FALSE FOR ONE COUNT IN THE SAME COMMENT. Three catalogue sentences are pinned. "the Codex frontend mapping is complete over all 12 registered events" is not, and my narrowing mutation named the other three and said nothing about it. This is the class the leaf itself named: an unpinned number standing under a promise that every number is pinned.
aura-plugins-7jca7u THE SessionEnd ROW COMMENT CITES THE STOP-HOOK FUNCTION. It says SessionEnd is emitted at "hook_runtime.rs:378-392, root session only". At rust-v0.153.0 those lines are inside run_turn_stop_hooks. The commit's own new table says :455 for that row, sixty lines below, so the file now states two emission sites for one row; the sentence also says "at 0.153.0 ... and still at 0.153.0", which reads as a version sweep that moved the numbers and not the citations. Pre-existing, and in the file this commit rewrote for exactly this purpose.

THREE MINOR: aura-plugins-yf1ya4 (TEXT-ONLY, RECORDED, NOT FIXED THIS ROUND, batched on aura-plugins-inamu5) the citation table drops the codex-rs/ prefix its neighbours keep; aura-plugins-1fpx1p the new subject has no width control; aura-plugins-5sugkv the doc-comment name pins do not tie a name to its axis.

WHICH OF THE EIGHT ATTACKS I RAN
1 re-drive the four mutations: RAN, all four RED with the quoted text. 2 attack the two controls and hunt a third vacuity: RAN, with two extra mutations of my own (delete a catalogue row; cite one row). 3 prove the byte identity: RAN, both events, normal and fail-closed paths, my own binaries and stores. 4 verify the sweep: RAN over AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG, the metamodel, the .codex transport files, hostexit and every doc comment that states a Codex count. 5 hunt more wrong-population pins: RAN, and it produced aura-plugins-lcs8q7 and aura-plugins-5sugkv. 6 judge the operator text: RAN, and it produced aura-plugins-nd601m and aura-plugins-kq5497. 7 check ownership mechanically: RAN, exact, both deviations judged minimal. 8 scan for internal references: RAN, two removed, none added.
ONE THING I DID NOT RUN: I did not re-drive the worker's M1b, the same mutation carried through make generate into the committed manifest, because M6 above carries a profile change through make generate and measures the same seam from the other direction. That is a gap in coverage of the worker's evidence, not of the claim.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SITTING 2 ACCEPTED, AND THREE THINGS I FOUND BY READING THE CAPTURED BYTES (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). I verified the directory read-only rather than accepting the report alone.

## ACCEPTED
All 12 required stems arrived, no stem missing, the covered-row set held with the four held names absent, and the live store is untouched. Session ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4 is kept alive for sittings 5 and 7. The out-of-catalogue stems are the same five names sitting 1 found, which is now a repeated measurement rather than a single observation.

## FINDING 1. THE PAIRING FIX IS PROVEN, NOT ONLY RULED.
I ruled that L3 must select a before-and-after pair from ONE operation, and that kit-safe makes this free because it registers tool.execute.before. THE PAIR EXISTS AND I READ BOTH FILES:
  opencode_tool_execute_before_1_18_29.1.json — sessionID ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4, callID call_TrpJqopNiMhgyGndzQO1zRkF
  opencode_tool_execute_after_1_18_29.1.json  — THE SAME sessionID AND THE SAME callID
So a coherent pair from one real operation is in hand. L3 commits THAT pair. The committed `before` from the earlier campaign belongs to a different session entirely, and the lead holds the option of replacing it or writing the mismatch down.

## FINDING 2. ONE STEM CARRIES 99 KB OF PROMPT TEXT, AND THE CHOICE OF FILE DECIDES WHETHER WE COMMIT IT.
Measured sizes in this sitting:
  opencode_experimental_chat_system_transform_1_18_29.1.json    3,411 bytes
  opencode_experimental_chat_system_transform_1_18_29.2.json   99,434 bytes
  opencode_experimental_chat_system_transform_1_18_29.3.json   99,434 bytes
The large two carry the host's assembled SYSTEM PROMPT. That is the class of content the requirement about the IR exists to keep out, and it is also the largest thing in the batch by a factor of eleven.
IT IS CLEARABLE AND THAT IS EXACTLY THE TRAP. free-text-v1 replaces a free-text string with a placeholder OF THE SAME RAW LENGTH, so substituting a 99 KB system prompt produces a 99 KB fixture of placeholder characters. Every gate passes. The corpus gains a 99 KB file that carries no information, and the repository carries it forever.
L3 RULE, and I rule it now: WHERE SEVERAL NUMBERED FILES EXIST FOR ONE EVENT AND ALL ARE AUTHENTIC, PREFER THE SMALLEST, AND STATE THE SIZES OF THE ONES NOT CHOSEN. A fixture exists to falsify a contract; the 3,411-byte capture does that as well as the 99,434-byte one. This does NOT override the pairing rule: for a paired event the pair is chosen first, and size decides only among candidates that are already correct.
THE REFUSED-CLASS CHECK IS REAL ON THIS HARNESS, not a formality. tool.execute.after came in at 752 bytes here because README.md is short, which is what the sitting prompt required. On a longer file it would carry the file's contents and cross the 4096-byte tool-response refusal. L3 reports the largest tool response it saw, with the number.

## FINDING 3. THE SERIALISATION-GUARD SEARCH CANNOT BE RUN RELIABLY, AND IT DOES NOT NEED TO BE.
The agent reported a nil result AND stated its limitation honestly: the guard writes to the console, the console is the host's alternate screen, and scrollback there is small and is not a full transcript. So a nil result from that search is weak evidence, and I will not treat it as strong.
I RULE THE CHECK SUBSUMED FOR TARGET ROWS. The guard's effect is to SKIP a row, so its observable is a MISSING STEM. Sitting 2 has no missing stem among its twelve, therefore the guard did not fire for any target row, and that conclusion rests on the file listing rather than on scrollback. KEEP the search, because it still names which row was skipped when a stem IS missing, and that is the one moment its information is not available elsewhere. But a missing stem is now the trigger for looking, not the other way round.

## A SMALL THING WORTH RECORDING FOR L3
The captured payloads carry the home path in BOTH spellings the rule names: the absolute `/home/<user>/...` in the tool arguments, and the relative `home/<user>/...` inside the after payload's `title`. The three-spelling definition of home-path-v1 is doing real work on this harness and is not a formality inherited from another one.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CLEARANCE READY: 95tfao

Ten Codex events are cleared into fixtures with their provenance sidecars and an extended clearance record. Nothing is committed. Nothing is pushed. The clearance record's acceptance section is empty and waits for the user's words.

WHERE THE WORK IS: the worktree at pasture/worktree/rp2tju-s5--codex-coverage, in internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/testdata/fixtures/, plus two extended test files in internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/. The capture directory was read-only for me throughout: I opened its files, I wrote none, moved none, renamed none and deleted none.

## 1. INVENTORY, run first, in report mode

I ran the fixture inventory in report mode over the whole capture directory with PASTURE_INVENTORY_DIR set, from a throwaway archive copy of the head, never from a working tree. It reported 39 payloads. It printed NO REFUSED line and NO UNCLEARABLE line for any file. Its output, not my eye, decided which fields are free text; the full output is pasted verbatim in the clearance record's inventory section, with one change I state there: the capture directory in its last line is spelled with a tilde, because the record must obey the same home-path rule the fixtures obey.

The free-text fields it flagged, by event: prompt on UserPromptSubmit; tool_input.command and tool_input.description on PermissionRequest; tool_input.command and tool_response on PostToolUse; last_assistant_message on Stop and on SubagentStop; tool_input.command on PreToolUse. PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStart, SessionEnd, Interrupt and SessionStart carry no free-text field at all.

## 2. THE CHOICE, one file per event, and why

The default is the first occurrence, the .1 file. Every one of the ten events took its .1 file. Seven of the ten events produced exactly one file, so there was nothing to choose. Three produced more: UserPromptSubmit 5, PostToolUse 10, PermissionRequest 2.

PERMISSION REQUEST, stated correctly. The two PermissionRequest files are NOT a preview and a confirmation of one request. Their payloads carry two different turn ids and two different command lines, one curl to example.com and one to example.org. The approval trigger was run twice, against two different hosts, and each run carried its own full cycle. The record says that and does not repeat the preview-and-confirm story. The .1 file is chosen because it is the first occurrence, which is the standing default; no special rule was needed.

The 29 unchosen files are each named in the record as captured and not used, with a raw digest and a byte size. Two of them are the newer SessionStart and PreToolUse captures: those two events keep their committed fixtures, which are NOT replaced.

## 3. SUBSTITUTION, values only, in order, with both digests

home-path-v1 first, then free-text-v1, listed in that order in each sidecar as one comma-joined string. Keys, nesting, types and nulls are unchanged; the clearing run refuses to write a file that still carries the capturing user's name, and it refused nothing.

Measured: every payload carried the ABSOLUTE home spelling, two or three times each. No payload carried the relative spelling and none carried the directory slug.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UserPromptSubmit | codex_user_prompt_submit_0_153_0.1.json | step 1, the first prompt | 21:15:44Z | 7fbb6a9a… / 458 | 22816dfb… / 452 | home-path-v1, free-text-v1 (.prompt) |
