author: David Huu Pham
text:
JOINT WITHHOLDING-VOCABULARY PROPOSAL. Written by supervisor-s4, agreed with supervisor-s6, with the axis contributed by supervisor-s5. One text, for the team lead to acknowledge. NO REASON IS ASSIGNED TO ANY ROW UNTIL THAT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT.

== THE AXIS (supervisor-s5) ==
The question is not "is there a switch". It is DOES THE DEFAULT REACH IT. Three cases follow.
 1 PLAIN: the default reaches it.
 2 CONFIGURATION-DEPENDENT: the default never reaches it; an operator can, on purpose.
 3 UNREACHABLE: no operator reaches it at any configuration.

== THE TWO MEASURED FACTS THAT DECIDE THE SHAPE ==
F1 THE ARM NAME SHIPS; THE DOC COMMENT DOES NOT. WithheldReason.String() maps each arm to a token, and the generated activation report carries that token — rows read "reason": "outside-target-set" today. So a reader meets the NAME. Re-wording a doc comment cannot repair a name that overclaims. Verified by supervisor-s6 in the source and in the generated report.
F2 THE TOKEN no-reachable-trigger IS CARRIED BY ZERO ROWS TODAY, in all three reports: OpenCode 45 outside-target-set and 2 enabled; Claude 23 outside-target-set, 2 missing-request-correlation and 8 enabled; Codex 10 outside-target-set and 2 enabled. It has never been rendered against a row. Nothing consumes it and no committed report changes. THE FIX IS FREE TODAY AND GETS MORE EXPENSIVE WITH THE FIRST ASSIGNMENT. Measured by supervisor-s6.

== THE PROPOSAL, FOUR POINTS ==

P1 CAPTURE-WITH-DISCLOSURE IS THE DEFAULT wherever a row can be captured at all. Set the configuration in the CAPTURE PROJECT ONLY, capture the row normally, and state the required non-default configuration BESIDE THAT FIXTURE in the clearance record. Nothing is withheld, so no arm is involved.
Why: configuration decides WHETHER an event happens, never WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE when it does. A reader who does not know a non-default setting produced a fixture will conclude the event fires for everybody.
Already done: OpenCode permission.replied, captured after a per-agent permission rule; Codex PermissionRequest, captured. Ordered: OpenCode lsp.updated with the language-server key set; Claude PermissionDenied, probed the same way through the capture project's own settings file.

P2 MINT ONE ARM, and LEAVE WithheldNoReachableTrigger EXACTLY AS IT IS.
The new arm covers two causes with one common truth: THE HOST CAN FIRE THE EVENT AND WE CHOSE NOT TO PRODUCE THE CONDITION. Its two limbs are (a) a setting we will not impose and (b) a condition we will not induce. It requires a clearance path, as NoReachableTrigger does, so the SPECIFIC cause is recorded per row where a reader can follow it.
Proposed name WithheldTriggerNotExercised. NAMING CRITERION, binding because of F1: THE NAME MUST NOT ASSERT ANYTHING ABOUT THE HOST. The subject of the name is us.
WithheldNoReachableTrigger needs NO re-word. Its current text — no KNOWN action makes the host fire it, so no authentic capture can exist — is TRUE of the narrow case it keeps, which is case 1 of the three below: nobody knows what fires it.

P3 NO SPLIT between the configuration limb and the condition limb. They differ only in WHAT KIND of condition we declined, and a clearance record carries that better than an enum. An enum arm should carry a fact a reader must not miss; the specific cause is a fact a reader can look up.

P4 TWO ITEMS ARE RECORDED AND ARE NOT CLOSED BY THIS CHANGE. A WITHHOLDING REASON RECORDS WHY WE HAVE NO CAPTURE. IT CORRECTS NO CLAIM ELSEWHERE.
 (i) OpenCode permission.ask keeps Blocking, gate-consultation and throw-fail-fast in the catalogue while the host never calls it.
 (ii) Claude WorktreeCreate's catalogue row says Blocking with exit-two-blocks, which describes an ordinary gate and not a provider that must print a path on standard output; Claude WorktreeRemove's says NonBlocking, report-and-continue, while our proceed IS exit 0 and the host reads exit 0 as "worktree removed successfully".
Both are false statements about the host in files we ship, and no reason string touches either. They stay on their own tickets.

== WHERE EVERY AFFECTED ROW LANDS, so this is checkable ==
WithheldNoReachableTrigger, narrow, case 1, nobody knows what fires it: Claude Setup, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle. Evidence for the last three: a real named teammate was created, given work and allowed to go idle, twice, none of the three fired, and the emission sites are present in the installed binary at comparable density to events that do fire, so the condition exists and is unknown to us.
THE NEW ARM: Claude StopFailure. It fires when an API error ends a turn. No configuration reaches it, so capture-with-disclosure cannot rescue it, and we will not force a rate limit or break the user's authentication to produce one. Claude PermissionDenied joins it ONLY IF its disclosure capture fails.
CAPTURED WITH DISCLOSURE, not withheld: OpenCode permission.replied and Codex PermissionRequest, both done; OpenCode lsp.updated and Claude PermissionDenied, both pending.
UNCHANGED: Claude Elicitation and ElicitationResult on MissingRequestCorrelation; Claude WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove on ProviderHook; Claude FileChanged on OutsideTargetSet with its cause in prose.

== THE COUNT, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE WEAKEST PART OF THE CASE ==
The new arm has ONE certain row today, Claude StopFailure, and a possible second. S6 and S5 expect zero.
WE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED TWO ALTERNATIVES:
 - Put StopFailure on the existing OutsideTargetSet with its cause in prose, minting nothing. Rejected: that arm forces no clearance path, so the recorded decision is not guaranteed, and the token tells the reader nothing.
 - Broaden WithheldNoReachableTrigger's doc to cover it. Rejected on F1: the doc is not what ships, so the token would read no-reachable-trigger against a row whose trigger is perfectly well known. That is the exact false-and-precise claim this task exists to remove.
ONE HONEST ARM WITH ONE ROW BEATS A SHIPPED FALSE TOKEN. F2 says the correction costs nothing today and costs more after the first assignment.

== HOW THIS PROPOSAL WAS REACHED, recorded because it matters to how it is read ==
supervisor-s4 and supervisor-s6 each argued the other's position at one point and swapped sides once. Neither out-argued the other. Both switches followed a MEASUREMENT: F1 defeated the re-word, and F2 defeated the record-it-as-debt option. supervisor-s6 also corrected its own arithmetic: it counted rows in the CONFIGURATION limb only and found zero, which is half the population the arm was built for; the CONDITION limb holds StopFailure and always did.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CONSOLIDATED CAPTURE INVENTORY ACROSS ALL SITTINGS, MEASURED (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05). This is the input the clearance leaf's row list is built from. I derived it from the 47 catalogue rows and the seven capture directories, not from the sitting reports, so it is independent of what anybody wrote down.

## THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES, WHICH IS THE FIRST THING I CHECKED
25 of the 47 rows have at least one capture. 22 do not, and every one of the 22 is accounted for:
 - 4 are HELD pending the user's credential decision: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.provider.small_model, experimental.compaction.autocontinue.
 - 3 are sitting 7's, which is running now: message.removed, message.part.removed, session.deleted.
 - 1 is sitting 4b's: lsp.updated.
 - 14 are the raised rows, which no sitting was ever going to produce: installation.updated, installation.update-available, lsp.client.diagnostics, permission.updated, server.connected, server.instance.disposed, tui.prompt.append, tui.command.execute, tui.toast.show, pty.created, pty.updated, pty.exited, pty.deleted, permission.ask.
4 + 3 + 1 + 14 = 22. And 25 captured plus 3 from sitting 7 plus 1 from 4b gives 29, which is the 2 already enabled plus the 27 reachable rows. THE INDEPENDENT COUNT MATCHES THE PLANNED ONE, which is the check that the campaign captured what it set out to capture and nothing has quietly gone missing.

## THE HELD ROWS ARE ABSENT FROM EVERY DIRECTORY, NOT JUST FROM SITTING 5
I looked for all four held rows in ALL SEVEN capture directories. ZERO FILES, EVERYWHERE.
That is a much stronger result than the one I reported earlier. Sitting 5 was one negative test at the compaction moment. This is a negative across seven sittings, dozens of turns and every kind of trigger the campaign ran — including sittings that made many LLM requests, which is where chat.params and chat.headers would fire on every single one. THE MECHANISM HAS NOW BEEN TESTED BY EVERYTHING WE DID, and no credential-bearing payload was written at any point.
The user's decision is therefore still fully open, and nothing has been produced that would pre-empt it.

## THE SELECTION PROBLEM IS BIGGER THAN THE LEAF ASSUMES, AND THIS IS THE REAL FINDING
Most rows were captured MANY TIMES, in sittings that were not aiming at them, because the widened key sees everything. Examples: tool.definition has 324 files across six directories; message.part.updated has 150 across seven; tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after each appear in FOUR different sittings.
SO THE CLEARANCE STEP IS NOT PICKING BETWEEN ".1 AND .2" — IT IS PICKING ONE FILE OUT OF UP TO 324, SPREAD ACROSS SITTINGS RUN HOURS APART WITH DIFFERENT PROJECTS, DIFFERENT SESSIONS AND DIFFERENT CONFIGURATIONS. The leaf text, and my own selection rules, were written for the smaller problem.
THE RULES STILL HOLD AND THE ORDER MATTERS MORE THAN I SAID:
 1. PAIRS FIRST, and the pair must come from ONE OPERATION IN ONE SITTING. tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after appear in four sittings; only a matched sessionID and callID makes a pair. The proven pair is in sitting 2.
 2. THEN PREFER ONE SITTING PER ROW FAMILY where the rows describe one session's life. A session.created from one sitting beside a session.idle from another describes no session that ever existed. This is the pairing rule widened, and I state it now because the inventory shows how easy it would be to break by accident.
 3. THEN THE SMALLEST AUTHENTIC FILE, with the sizes of those not chosen recorded.
 4. AND STATE THE SITTING each committed fixture came from, so a reader can see which fixtures share a session and which do not.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE
Nothing needs re-capturing. Every candidate is on disk with its identifiers in the bytes. The work is selection, and selection is exactly what the clearance leaf is for. But it is a bigger judgement than "take the .1 file", and the row list I hand over will say so per row.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
THE WIDENED GUARD IS VERIFIED AND ACCEPTED (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). I read the implementation and ran it myself. Nothing is committed.

WHAT I CHECKED IN THE SOURCE, rule by rule, rather than trusting the report.
RULE A reads a derived population: registeredByName is built from the registration manifest's own entries, and a fixture naming an undeclared event is an error that then CONTINUES, so it cannot also be counted as an enabled row.
RULE B is a per-event identity and not a count. fixturesPerEnabledEvent is keyed by event name and the final loop distinguishes ZERO from MANY with different messages, each naming the event. The append happens BEFORE the transport-metadata lookup, so an enabled event whose metadata is missing still counts for Rule B and cannot hide as a zero.
RULE C runs only for enabled events, at full strength, over every top-level member.
RULE D is implemented as a bare CONTINUE with no assertion. That is the repair: it has no population and therefore no non-vacuity clause to trip. My withdrawn objection cannot apply to it.
NON-VACUITY is guarded twice and both are hard failures: an empty registration manifest and an empty enabled set each stop the test.
THE GLOB IS UNCHANGED and the comment names the three sidecar controls that must never begin to match it.
THE SOURCE COMMENT IS REPLACED and it states Rule D's green-by-design case together with what catches it later. A reader who meets an undeclared member on a not-enabled fixture is told, in the file, why it is green and what turns it red.

WHAT I RAN MYSELF: the guard passes, and I confirmed THE RUN NAMED THE TEST rather than exiting 0 while running nothing. Output: "=== RUN TestClaudeLifecycleTransportAllowsAuthentic2_1_261FieldShapes" then "--- PASS". The first run printed only "ok" in 0.005s, which is exactly the shape a vacuous run has, so I re-ran with the full test name and -v before believing it. That check is cheap and it is the rule.

THE WORKER'S EVIDENCE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, and two parts of it deserve recording.
M-b WAS RUN IN THE EIGHT-FIXTURE WORLD SO THE COMPARISON IS FAIR. The worker moved its 14 fixtures aside, gave SessionStart two fixtures and SessionEnd none, and ran BOTH guards over the SAME tree: the widened guard RED on both halves, naming the event with two and the event with none; today's count guard, restored from the committed file, GREEN. That is the proof the enabled arm was strengthened and not weakened, and it is the single most important piece of evidence in this change. Comparing the two guards on one tree is what makes it a proof rather than an assertion.
THE AFTER STATE IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A CLAIM. The worker built a throwaway copy of the worktree OUTSIDE the repository, enabled the fourteen rows there with placeholder proofs, regenerated, ran the guard, and deleted the copy. It did NOT touch the target table in the live worktree, which is the rule about never mutating a worktree to prove a point. Result: Rule A and Rule B both clean over 22 enabled events with 22 fixtures; no dead arm; and Rule C reporting 39 errors over ten events, which is the coupling working exactly as intended — enabling a row without growing its field list turns the guard RED at once, naming the event and the field.

THE WORKER CORRECTED ITS OWN COUNT AND I RECORD THE CORRECTION AS THE AUTHORITATIVE FIGURE: TEN of the fourteen fixtures carry undeclared members, not nine, and there are 39 undeclared members in total. Four fixtures are clean. Its earlier message said nine and then listed ten; the list was right. The after-state run printed exactly 39 errors over exactly those ten files, which is what caught the arithmetic. A count that is checked by a run beats a count that is typed.

The filled record joins them when the acceptance arrives.

WHAT I CHECKED IN THE SOURCE, rule by rule, rather than trusting the report.
RULE A reads a derived population: registeredByName is built from the registration manifest's own entries, and a fixture naming an undeclared event is an error that then CONTINUES, so it cannot also be counted as an enabled row.
RULE B is a per-event identity and not a count. fixturesPerEnabledEvent is keyed by event name and the final loop distinguishes ZERO from MANY with different messages, each naming the event. RULE D is implemented as a bare CONTINUE with no assertion. That is the repair: it has no population and therefore no non-vacuity clause to trip. My withdrawn objection cannot apply to it.

The lead ruled that the committed tool_execute_before is REPLACED by the same-operation pair from sitting 2, so the corpus holds one real operation without a caveat sentence.
THE SAME REASONING REACHES ONE MORE COMMITTED FIXTURE. session_created is also committed, from the EARLIER campaign's session ses_f8e723e13ffe.... If the other thirteen family rows come from sitting 2's session ses_f8c74e69bffe..., then the committed session.created DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT SESSION FROM EVERY OTHER FILE AROUND IT. The family would say one session began and another one lived.
Sitting 2 captured its own session.created, 653 bytes, from the same session as the other thirteen. So the coherent option costs nothing to produce.
THE OPTIONS, and this touches an acceptance the user has already given, so it is not mine:

author: David Huu Pham
text:
CORRECTED CLOSING ORDER, replacing the one I stated earlier (worker-s4-l3, 2026-09-05). The tree is unchanged; this is a record correction only.

MY ERROR: I wrote that I would run the race suite on an archive copy and THEN commit. That order cannot work and its failure is SILENT. `git archive` reads a commit, and my work is uncommitted: three modified files and 28 untracked ones. An archive taken before the commit would carry HEAD, which holds none of the fixtures, none of the sidecars, neither the widened guard nor the extended inventory. The suite would PASS, on a real tree with real packages, and I would report a green full-suite gate for work that was never in the copy. A green report for work that was never checked is worse than a red one, and this shape is worse still, because the copy looks complete.

THE ORDER I WILL FOLLOW, once the user's verbatim acceptance reaches me:
 1. Write the verbatim acceptance with its date into the clearance record.
 2. Preserve the filled record beside the artefacts already at the accepted directory outside every repository, and post its digest here.
 3. FAST CHECKS IN THE WORKTREE FIRST, because they are what makes the commit safe: build, vet, gofmt with a negative control, and the affected packages. Re-run after the record edit, because the record itself is walked by the home-segment guard and by the secret scan.
 4. COMMIT. One commit, ownership paragraph naming exactly the touched files and verified against the diff, `git agent-commit` only.
 5. THEN take the gate lock on the ledger, archive THAT COMMIT'S SHA into a scratch directory, and run the full race suite FROM INSIDE the copy. A run that names no packages did not run; entering the dev shell does not change the working directory, so the command runs inside the copy and the output is checked for the package names.
 6. IF THE GATE IS RED: FIX FORWARD with a second commit naming what it corrects. Never amend, never rebase, because records and reviews cite SHAs and a rewrite invalidates every citation.

WHY STEP 4 BEFORE STEP 5 IS NOT AN UNCHECKED COMMIT: the rule forbids committing UNCHECKED work, and step 3 is the check. Step 5 is the full-suite proof over an immutable copy of exactly what was committed. Nothing is pushed at any point, and I have no push path, so a red at step 5 costs one more commit and nothing else.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
A GATE-ORDER TRAP, CAUGHT BEFORE IT FIRED, AND RECORDED FOR EVERY HARNESS SLICE (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05).

WHAT HAPPENED. The clearance worker restated its closing sequence as "run the race suite on an archive copy of the SHA from inside that copy; then ONE commit". That order cannot work, and its failure is SILENT.

WHY IT IS SILENT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. `git archive` reads a COMMIT. The work here is uncommitted: three modified files and 28 untracked ones. An archive taken before the commit contains HEAD, which has NONE of the fixtures, NONE of the sidecars, NOT the widened guard and NOT the extended inventory. THE SUITE WOULD PASS, because it would test the tree as it stood before the work began. The worker would then report a GREEN FULL-SUITE GATE FOR WORK THAT WAS NEVER CHECKED.
This is the standing "a gate that passes because it ran nothing" failure, in its most dangerous form. The usual version is easy to spot: the run names no packages, or the make target is missing. THIS ONE LOOKS COMPLETELY NORMAL — a real tree, real packages, a real pass. Nothing in the output says the work is absent.

THE CORRECT ORDER, recorded so the other harness slices do not have to rediscover it:
 1 Write the acceptance into the record; preserve the filled record and post its digest.
 2 FAST CHECKS IN THE WORKTREE FIRST — build, vet, gofmt with a negative control, and the affected packages. This is what makes committing safe, and it must be RE-RUN after the record is edited, because the record itself is walked by the home-segment guard and by the secret scan.
 3 COMMIT. One commit, ownership paragraph naming exactly the touched files, verified against the diff, `git agent-commit` only.
 4 THEN take the gate lock, archive THAT COMMIT'S SHA, and run the full race suite from inside the copy.
 5 A RED AT STEP 4 IS FIXED FORWARD with a second commit that names what it corrects. Never amend, never rebase: records and findings cite SHAs, and a rewrite invalidates every citation. A second commit is the required repair, not a blemish.

WHY STEP 3 BEFORE STEP 4 IS NOT A VIOLATION OF THE NO-COMMIT-WITHOUT-GATES RULE. That rule forbids committing UNCHECKED work. Step 2 is the check that makes the commit safe; step 4 is the full-suite proof on an immutable copy of exactly what was committed. Nothing is pushed at any point and the worker has no push path, so a red at step 4 costs one more commit and nothing else.

AND VERIFY THE GATE RAN. A run that names no packages did not run, and `nix develop <copy> -c ...` does NOT change the working directory. Run from INSIDE the copy and check the output names the packages. Precedent from today: my own first run of the widened guard printed only "ok" in 0.005 seconds, which is the shape of a vacuous run, so I re-ran with the test named and -v and got "=== RUN" then "--- PASS" before believing it. That check costs one command.

WHY THIS IS ON THE SLICE AND NOT ONLY IN A MESSAGE. Every harness slice ends with the same shape — a batch of new untracked fixtures plus a few modified files, then one commit. The temptation to gate before committing is strongest exactly there, because the worker wants a green before it commits. The answer is that the fast checks give it that green, and the archive gate necessarily comes after.

THE TRAP, caught on another harness before it fired. `git archive <sha>` reads a COMMIT. An archive copy taken BEFORE your clearance commit holds NONE of your uncommitted fixtures, sidecars, record or test edits. The race suite then passes on a tree WITHOUT YOUR WORK and the result looks completely normal. A green gate that tested nothing is worse than a red one, because it ends the questioning.

Keep saying that in every gate report. A gate on an overlay is only trustworthy because the report says it was an overlay and says how the identity was checked.
THE ORDER FOR THE LAST STEPS, once the user's verbatim acceptance is relayed onto this task.
1. Write the acceptance into the record, with its date and the questions asked, verbatim and unparaphrased.
2. Post the record's digest.
3. RE-RUN the checks AFTER that edit. This is the step that is easy to skip and the reason it matters is specific: the record itself is walked by the home-segment guard and by the secret scan, so an edit to the record can turn either RED. Fast checks in the worktree first: build, vet, gofmt with a planted control, and the affected packages.
4. ONE commit.
5. THEN take the lock, archive THAT SHA, and run the full race suite from INSIDE the copy.
6. A red at step 5 is fixed FORWARD by a second commit. Never amend, never rebase, never rewrite history.
VERIFY THAT THE GATE RAN. A package that reports "ok" in 0.005 s is the shape of a run that executed nothing. Where a result looks too fast for the work it claims, re-run that package with the test name selected and verbose output until the NAME PRINTS. A gate that names no packages did not run, and a gate that names them but printed no test name did not run either.

text:
DISPOSITION OF THE THREE S4 CARRY-OVERS, so none is discovered at closing time (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05).

THE PROBLEM I FOUND WHILE WAITING. aura-plugins-uieu0p, aura-plugins-kqm151 and aura-plugins-bm1ci8 all BLOCK this slice directly and NONE of them has a leaf owner or a worker. The slice cannot close until all three are resolved, and nothing today would have surfaced them: they are not in the capture, clearance or enabling leaf texts. Recording an owner now costs one comment; discovering them at closing costs a round.

PROPOSED OWNERS. I rule these as slice-internal placements; the team lead corrects any of them.
- uieu0p, the Claude "proceed" answer that is in neither documented enum while the package doc claims documentation support -> THE ENABLING LEAF, aura-plugins-i2qq6b. That leaf already owns the Claude host contract file and the target table, and the fix is a contract-and-doc change in the same place.
- kqm151, the Claude schema refusal that names three causes because it cannot say which one fired -> ALSO THE ENABLING LEAF, but flagged as A REAL CODE CHANGE AND NOT TEXT. It must NOT go to the text-only batch: the refusal has to learn WHICH cause fired, which is behaviour. Under the actionable-error standard a message that lists three possible causes tells the reader to guess, which is the defect.
- bm1ci8, the Claude host version source -> THE TRANSPORT LEAF, aura-plugins-9h8j3v, which owns hooks/hooks.json and the regeneration. See the measurement below before anyone designs the fix.

A MEASUREMENT FOR bm1ci8, TAKEN NOW FROM A LIVE 2.1.261 SESSION, WITH THE TRAP IT CONTAINS.
Measured, read-only, over a live session's own environment: CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION IS ABSENT, as the task says. But CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH IS PRESENT and its value carries the segment "versions/2.1.261". AI_AGENT is present too. So an undocumented source of the version does exist in the environment.
THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON I AM RECORDING THIS: THAT VERSION SEGMENT IS AN ARTEFACT OF THIS INSTALLATION'S LAYOUT, not a promise. It exists because this host is installed under a directory tree that happens to be named by version. AN INSTALLATION WITH A DIFFERENT LAYOUT — a system package, a global package-manager install, a Nix store path — WOULD YIELD NO VERSION SEGMENT OR A WRONG ONE, and a parser would then produce an empty or false host version SILENTLY. That is the same class of defect as every false claim this epic has been removing: a value that looks measured and is really inferred from a local accident.
SO THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG ONE unless it also says what it does when the pattern does not match, and that arm must fail LOUDLY rather than fall back to a plausible-looking string.

THE THREE OPTIONS, EACH WITH ITS REAL COST, so the leaf starts from the tradeoff and not from the first idea:
 1 PARSE THE EXEC PATH. Cheap and works here. INSTALLATION-SPECIFIC, silently wrong elsewhere unless the no-match arm is explicit and loud.
 2 ASK THE HOST, by running the host binary for its version. Truthful anywhere. COSTS A SUBPROCESS INSIDE THE FIVE-SECOND INVOCATION BUDGET, on every hook, and the binary may not be on the path the hook inherits.
 3 STOP CLAIMING A VERSION WE WERE NOT GIVEN. Record absence honestly instead of the literal "unknown", which today reads like a version string in the journal and in every downstream report. Cheapest and truest; it gives up a field rather than inventing one.
A FOURTH THAT LOOKS ATTRACTIVE AND IS NOT: have the generator bake the pinned contract version into the transport. It asserts THE VERSION THE TRANSPORT WAS GENERATED FOR, not the version of the host that is running, and under floor admission the two diverge exactly when the user upgrades without regenerating — which is the case admission exists to judge. That would make the admission check read its own assumption.

WHAT THE CAPTURE CAMPAIGN DID, and why it does not settle this: it exported CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION by hand in the capture shell. That is correct for a capture sitting and is NOT a product fix, because no real user exports it.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULINGS ON THE FIX WORKER'S THREE QUESTIONS (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). Fix round 1 delivered 7272b5f, cd1313b and 1e27166. I rule on the two items it raised and I record the third.

RULING 1: THE REMOVED CONTROL. ACCEPTED, and the reasoning is worth keeping, because "remove a control" is normally the wrong answer.
MY RULE CUTS BOTH WAYS. I said a control that cannot fail is not a control, and I said it to demand more controls. The same sentence condemns a DEAD assertion, and a dead assertion is worse than no assertion, because a reader counts it as protection and stops looking for the real one. So the rule does not say "keep every control"; it says "every control must be able to fail".
WHAT MAKES THIS REMOVAL SAFE RATHER THAN CONVENIENT, and I checked each part. The worker did not delete a control it found inconvenient; it WIDENED the control first, then measured whether the widened form could ever fire, and found it cannot: only a blocking row can be demoted or promoted, a non-blocking row always takes the strict arm, so a tree in which nothing moves carries one arm and the ARMS control fires first. It then proved the coverage is not lost: a read that returns the declared field turns the row equality RED naming the row, and a constant read turns the arms control RED, both measured, not argued. And the equivalent control in the divergence subject IS reachable, so it is kept and shown RED there. A removal with a measurement, a replacement and a surviving sibling is a different act from a removal with an excuse.
ONE CONDITION I ADD. The file must say what would make the removed control LIVE AGAIN, not only why it is dead today. Deadness here is a consequence of one property: a non-blocking row cannot be demoted or promoted. If a later change gives a non-blocking row a demotable mode, the control becomes reachable and should return. Write that sentence next to the measurement, so the next reader inherits the condition and not only the conclusion.

RULING 2: THE CLASS SWEEP THAT HIT THE CAPTURE WORK. ACCEPTED, and this is the best thing in the round.
The non-vacuity control of that subject treated the CAPTURE-FREE COUNT as its proof that the derivation reads something. The capture work is on this same branch. The moment a Codex row gains a capture proof, that control would have FATALED with "the derivation reads nothing", which would have been FALSE, and it would have looked like a defect in the capture work rather than in the control. Two leaves of one slice would have blamed each other for a wrong assertion.
THIS IS WHY THE SWEEP RULE EXISTS. It was not in the review, no gate would have caught it, and it was found only by asking what else belongs to the class the reviewer probed. A control keyed to a number that the slice's own next step is designed to change is a self-inflicted false alarm with a scheduled date.
I ALSO CHECKED THE NEAR NEIGHBOUR MYSELF, because a false alarm and a missed alarm live next door. The capture-free count derives from the ACTIVATION manifest's capture proof, not from the fixture directory. The clearance work commits fixtures and leaves the activation table untouched, so it does NOT move that number. The three pinned sentences turn RED at the ENABLING leaf, which is the correct place, and each message names the exact sentence the file must then carry. That is a pin doing its job, not a conflict.

RECORDED, NOT RULED: two mutations were REFUSED by the runtime contract validation, an observation may not declare a native mutation and a stop-loop policy may not stand outside a blocking gate consultation. The worker recorded the refusals and reached the same assertion by a third, performable mutation. A refusal that is measured and written down is evidence about the tree. A mutation quietly skipped is a hole in the evidence. This is the second time in this slice that a worker met an impossible mutation and reported it instead of dropping it, and both times the report told us something true about the contract.

text:
ROUND-2 ORDER (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). Fresh Opus reviewer, reviewer-s5-r2, on 1e27166, which is the base plus the catalogue commit and the three fix commits. The prompt is at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/supervisor-s5/prompt-reviewer-s5-r2.md.
THE BAR: a FIX-FREE CLEAN ROUND, 0 BLOCKER, 0 IMPORTANT, 0 MINOR, on a round in which no fix is applied. The prompt says plainly: do not soften a finding to reach a clean number, and do not invent one to look thorough.
WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A RE-RUN. The reviewer reproduces each ORIGINAL failure before it accepts that a fix answers it. It re-walks the CITATION CLASS, because a sweep that fixed two and missed a third is itself a finding. It runs the linkage proof itself rather than accepting the claim. It performs all ten narrowing mutations itself, because a pin that names a neighbour's sentence is the same defect in a new place. On the moving-state pin it must try a THIRD world, the one where EVERY row is cited, not only the one-row world the fix was measured in.
IT MUST AUDIT MY TWO RULINGS RATHER THAN INHERIT THEM. SITTING 7 REPORT. UNDO, THEN A NEW PROMPT, THEN DELETE. Capturer capturer-s6-7, agent Sonnet, under supervisor-s6, slice aura-plugins-ok39i3, leaf aura-plugins-rtcnpj.

## 1. Sitting name and version line

Sitting: SITTING 7, UNDO, THEN A NEW PROMPT, THEN DELETE. Three target rows: message.removed, message.part.removed, session.deleted.

`opencode --version` in the tmux capture shell, immediately before the session, printed: 1.18.29. This matches the required version. No stop condition.

## 2. Who drove and how

I (capturer-s6-7, an agent) drove the whole sitting through a tmux session named capturer-s6-7, using the TUI interactive interface. No non-interactive fallback was needed. Every keystroke followed a pane read first. Two host resizes were used mid-sitting to force a screen redraw when the hook's own stderr had drawn over the TUI (a known cosmetic condition, stated in the setup notes); each resize was followed by a pane read that showed the redraw succeeded.

## 3. Kit digests and project directory

- Project directory: /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project (shared with two earlier sittings, per the lead addendum).
- Kit-safe plugin path: /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/kit-safe/pasture-lifecycle.ts
- Kit-safe plugin SHA-256: 73e646d854ecc7c3b5ae326a988b3bac0e90355da4c7d7760407ab74d2b1a649
- Project copy plugin SHA-256, computed in the project directory: 73e646d854ecc7c3b5ae326a988b3bac0e90355da4c7d7760407ab74d2b1a649. Matches. No stop.
- Binary path: /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/worker-s6-l1/bin/pasture-head
- Binary SHA-256: 0411482772b75caff4a5dab869c590475dfb0b8df721e8da049281a50044920b. Matches the value on record.
- "$PASTURE_BIN" --version printed: pasture version devel.
- PASTURE_DB_PATH (scratch, never the live store): /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/scratch-s7/pasture.db (directory created fresh for this sitting).
- PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR: /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/s7 (pre-existing, empty at start, outside every repository).

Covered-row set (precondition P2), computed on the project copy: I parsed the returned object of the plugin's default export and counted 12 registered keys: the one `event` key, plus 11 named keys (tool.execute.before, chat.message, permission.ask, command.execute.before, shell.env, tool.execute.after, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition). None of the four held names (chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.provider.small_model) is registered. This is the expected 12-key, 43-row coverage. No held row present. No missing ordinary row observed against the expectation. All three of this sitting's target rows (message.removed, message.part.removed, session.deleted) are OBSERVATION rows reached through the one `event` key, so all three are inside the covered set.

Host process check before starting (lead addendum "ONE LIVE HOST"): `pgrep -a opencode` returned nothing; `uptime` showed load average 0.76, 1.33, 2.98 (below the 8.0 bound, no wait needed).

Host log size noted before starting (P5): 404733849 bytes at ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log.

## 4. Plugin load evidence

This sitting reused session ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4 in the shared project directory. That session was already proven loaded (with the same plugin copy) by an earlier sitting in this same project directory; I did not re-derive load evidence from the host log for this session, since the plugin's own effect was the proof I used here: the very first turn I drove in this sitting (the throwaway "Say the word probe and stop.") produced a large burst of capture files (90 for one stem alone; see anomalies), which is only possible if the plugin's widened `event` handler is loaded and running. I did not additionally grep the host log for a "loading plugin" line naming pasture-lifecycle in this sitting; that check belongs to Sitting 1, already run and accepted earlier in this campaign per the recipe list record.

## 5. Per-step actions, files, and waits

Baseline file count in the capture directory before any trigger: 49 (already present from a prior burst that fired immediately on process start; see anomalies).

Step: create a throwaway session (leader ctrl+x, then n), because the session list held the reused session plus one other pre-existing session ("One-word greeting") that belongs to a different sitting and must not be touched. I created my own throwaway rather than reuse "One-word greeting."
- Action: ctrl+x, then n (session_new).
- Pane read confirmed a fresh empty session screen.

Step: send one short prompt in the throwaway session, to give it a completed turn before deleting it in T3.
- Action: send-keys -l "Say the word probe and stop.", pause, Enter.
- Expected: a completed turn (no specific capture file required for this housekeeping step).
- Observed: assistant replied "probe" after about 2.4s; pane read confirmed the turn completed (idle). File count in the capture directory rose from 49 to 139 (90 new files, dominated by the withheld-population flood; see anomalies). Wait: about 8s including one resize-forced redraw.

Step: switch back to the reused session via the session list (leader ctrl+x, then l; Down to move off the throwaway; Enter to select).
- Confirmed via ANSI-highlight inspection (`tmux capture-pane -e`) that the correct target row carried the selection background before pressing Enter, both here and again before T3.
- Pane read after Enter showed the reused session's transcript ("Read the file README.md..." / compaction block), confirming the switch worked.

T1. Press leader (ctrl+x) then u, to undo.
- Action: ctrl+x, then u (messages_undo).
- Expected: a revert, and session.diff firing again (documented as expected).
- Observed: pane showed "1 message reverted / ctrl+x r or /redo to restore." opencode_session_diff_1_18_29.3.json appeared (the count went from 2 to 3 files for that stem). Wait: about 6s including one resize-forced redraw.
- IMPORTANT FINDING carried from this step into T2: I checked the reachable OpenCode v1.18.29 TUI source before driving this step (packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx, the "session.undo" / "Undo previous message" command, and packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts). The TUI's undo command always calls `session.revert` with `messageID` only, and never supplies a `partID`. Inside `revert()`, when `input.partID` is undefined, the computed `partID` on the revert record is always undefined too, regardless of cursor or scroll position. This means "undo from inside an assistant message" does not, in this build, produce a PART-level revert point through any TUI-reachable path I found; it always reverts at the boundary of the last USER message. I drove the recipe's exact key sequence as given (T1 then T2) without inventing a substitute trigger, and I report the measured result below rather than retrying.

T2. Send a new short prompt (the trigger for the two removal events).
- Action: send-keys -l "Say hi and stop.", pause, Enter.
- Expected files: opencode_message_removed_1_18_29.*.json and opencode_message_part_removed_1_18_29.*.json.
- Observed: opencode_message_removed_1_18_29.1.json and .2.json appeared (two distinct messageIDs, both under sessionID ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4 — the reused session; confirmed by reading the file contents). opencode_message_part_removed_1_18_29.*.json did NOT appear, checked immediately after the turn completed and again after a further 5-second settle. File count in the capture directory: 186 immediately after, 186 again 5s later (stable). Wait: about 11s total including the settle re-check.
- FINDING: message.part.removed is a MISSING STEM for this sitting, and I attribute it to the code-level cause found before T1 (the TUI's undo command never sets a partID, so `cleanup()` in revert.ts never reaches its `if (session.revert.partID && target)` branch that calls `removePart`). This is a trigger-reachability finding, not a capture-sink defect: the event is reachable in principle only through a direct call to the host's own local HTTP API, `POST /session/:sessionID/revert`, with an explicit `partID` field in the body (the schema at packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts:16 declares `partID: Schema.optional(PartID)`, and the route exists at packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts:99). That is the same "drive the host's own local HTTP API" third option documented for Group R-C in the raised list, not something I was authorized to do inside this sitting's scope, so I did not attempt it.

T3. Open the session list (leader ctrl+x, then l), select a session not needed, and press ctrl+d to delete it.
- Action: ctrl+x, then l. Pane read (with `tmux capture-pane -e` for ANSI highlight) confirmed the selection background was on "Request to say probe and stop" (my own throwaway), not on "Find first line of README.md" (the reused session) or "One-word greeting" (another sitting's session).
- Action: ctrl+d, then ctrl+d again to confirm (the TUI asks for a second press).
- Expected file: opencode_session_deleted_1_18_29.*.json.
- Observed: opencode_session_deleted_1_18_29.1.json appeared. Its content names sessionID ses_f8c53f41cffeUR63YhV555JtiG and title "Request to say probe and stop" — my throwaway, confirmed correct. Wait: about 4s.
- After T3, I read the pane again and confirmed the reused session ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4 was untouched and still showed both of its turns.

## 6. Listing, SHA-256, and file count taken twice

Host was stopped first (ctrl-c inside the tmux pane), confirmed by `tmux list-panes` showing no child process under the pane PID and the pane showing the host's own resume line ("Continue: opencode -s ses_f8c74e69bffeqDIe64dzbMVPc4"), before any listing was taken.

File count, taken twice on the stopped directory: 190, then 190 again (unchanged). 190 also matches the line count of both `ls -la` and `sha256sum *` taken below.

Target-row SHA-256 (excerpted from the full listing):
```
9f4e867ff2a2ad1823d7effaa0bd864c9acbea7f93237d3eca2e4ef622d6f059  opencode_message_removed_1_18_29.1.json
58d30b2141b764133bd71bbd098eae9595faa86097972c181e860740f1d897ca  opencode_message_removed_1_18_29.2.json
dffa3748e5fae19d4faa3328c97527424431d950e12b580b09aaf25c9beb932d  opencode_session_deleted_1_18_29.1.json
```
No opencode_message_part_removed_1_18_29.*.json exists (MISSING STEM, per the finding in section 5).

Per-stem counts (all 190 files), computed by stripping the `_1_18_29.<n>.json` suffix:
```
     90 opencode_plugin_added
     24 opencode_tool_definition
     12 opencode_message_updated
     10 opencode_session_updated
     10 opencode_message_part_updated
      9 opencode_session_status
      5 opencode_session_diff
      5 opencode_catalog_updated

      2 opencode_message_removed

      2 opencode_experimental_chat_messages_transform

```
Sum: 190. Verbatim `ls -la` and full `sha256sum *` output are attached as this comment's two follow-on parts if the supervisor wants the byte-for-byte listing; I hold both files (/tmp/s7_ls_la.txt, /tmp/s7_sha256.txt on this machine) and will post them on request rather than inflate this report by default.

## 7. Anomalies

A1. UNRECOGNIZED NATIVE EVENTS, not in the 45/47-row population derived for this campaign. At session start (before any of my triggers), and again during the throwaway turn, the host published a burst of events that pasture's own ingress validation refused with "the opencode registration ... declares no native event named X": plugin.added (90 occurrences, all inside the capture window, all with a real evt_ id and a real properties.id such as "core/config-reference"), catalog.updated (5), reference.updated (3), integration.updated (3). None of these four names appears in the 32-observation / 15-named population that worker-s6-l1 derived from internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_opencode.go and the OpenCode 1.18.29 Event union. The capture sink still wrote the raw payload for every one of them (capture happens before validation, by design), so nothing was lost, but pasture's own hook fails open with a validation error for each. This looks like a host feature (a plugin/skill/config "catalog" or "reference" subsystem) publishing on the same EventV2 bus, outside the audited SDK Event union at the tag the population was measured against. I did not investigate further; this is outside my assignment's scope, but the volume (90 plugin.added files from ONE short "probe" turn) is large enough that I flag it for the supervisor and the population owner.

A2. A FIFTH unrecognized stem, message.part.delta (3 occurrences), also outside the 45/47-row population. I did not check whether pasture's ingress refused it the same way; I list it here as the same class of anomaly as A1.

A3. The TUI screen froze (stopped redrawing) twice during the sitting, once after the reused-session resume and once after T3's delete confirmation, both times because the hook's own stderr (the capture notice and, later, the validation-fault lines from A1) was drawn inside the TUI's own screen and the TUI's redraw did not recover on its own. This matches the documented cosmetic condition exactly ("the hook's standard error is drawn inside the interface... the redraw may never recover"). I recovered the screen both times with a tmux window resize (shrink by one row/column, then restore), which forces a full repaint; I did not use any kill or pattern-kill to do this. Keystrokes sent while the screen was frozen (none were, in this sitting — I always waited for a working screen before sending a key) were not required, since the resize recovered the screen before every subsequent keystroke.

A4. Trigger-reachability finding for message.part.removed, detailed in section 5 (T1/T2): confirmed absent, with a code-level explanation and a named alternate trigger (the host's own local HTTP API with an explicit partID) that I did not attempt, being outside this sitting's authorized scope.

A5. My display of the reused session after T1+T2 showed BOTH the original "Read the file README.md..." turn and the new "Say hi and stop." turn as separate, complete exchanges, even though T1's undo was supposed to revert (hide) the first one. I do not have a firm explanation for this from the pane text alone (it may be that the restored input-box text from the revert and my newly typed text were sent as one combined turn that the model then answered as two parts, or the display re-populated after the second turn completed). This does not change the file-level finding (message.removed fired twice with two real messageIDs under the correct sessionID, and message.part.removed did not fire at all), so I did not chase it further, but I flag it since a wrong read of "what got reverted" could mislead a later sitting reusing this same session.

## 8. Housekeeping

- C1 (serialize-failure search): searched the tmux pane scrollback (2000 lines) and the host log tail, filtered to this project's directory string, for "could not serialize the payload of". Zero occurrences either way. This is a nil result and weak evidence per the standing rule (the console is the alternate screen); I did not see the string on the one stream I could search.
- C2/C4: host stopped first (ctrl-c), confirmed by process check, before any listing. Listing taken twice, unchanged (190, 190). tmux session capturer-s6-7 was killed by its exact name only, after the host had already exited.
- Live-store check: ~/.local/share/pasture/pasture.db SHA-256 after this sitting is 3da48f08f603e306f19727976379bc918192f9716f0cd9e9ba6855344ee0b5aa, with a filesystem mtime of 2026-09-05 14:13:58 -0700 — before this sitting started (my first command in this sitting ran at 15:17 -0700 the same day). I did not take a SHA-256 of the live store before starting this sitting (an oversight on my part); the mtime predating my whole sitting is the evidence I have that the file was not touched, since PASTURE_DB_PATH and PASTURE_BIN were exported only inside the capture tmux shell and pointed at the scratch database the whole time.
- No numbered capture file was deleted. The dryrun directory was not used in this sitting (no dry run was re-run; the one-time dry run belongs to setup, already done earlier in this campaign).
- Out-of-catalogue stems (not findings, not fixtures, listed separately per instructions): opencode_plugin_added (90), opencode_catalog_updated (5), opencode_reference_updated (3), opencode_integration_updated (3), opencode_message_part_delta (3). See anomalies A1 and A2 for detail.

Result: 2 of 3 target rows captured (message.removed, session.deleted). message.part.removed is a measured miss under the given trigger, with a cited code-level cause and a cited, unauthorized-for-this-sitting alternate trigger.

text:
STATE OF THE CODEX COVERAGE SLICE AT THE L0-TO-L3 WAITING POINT (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). Recorded because most of this slice's agents are now shut down and the position must survive them. Two things are open and everything else is done.

BRANCH: slice/rp2tju-s5, base 0b33f07. Four commits: 3135e55 the catalogue derivation, then 7272b5f, cd1313b and 1e27166 the round-1 fixes. Uncommitted in the worktree: the ten cleared Codex fixtures, their sidecars, the extended clearance record and two of its test files. NOTHING IS COMMITTED FROM THE CLEARANCE. NOTHING IS PUSHED. NO TASK IS CLOSED.

LEAF STATE.
 L0, the catalogue re-derivation: DONE and accepted at 3135e55, then fixed by round 1. The catalogue now READS its failure mode from the runtime profile, so the two artefacts cannot disagree in either direction.
 L1, the trigger recipes: DONE and accepted, with one published correction. Ten of ten target events have a proven, reachable trigger. No event goes to the user for a withhold decision.
 L2, the capture campaign: DONE and accepted. 39 files covering all twelve registered Codex events at 0.153.0, outside every repository, with a per-file digest and a per-capture log rebuilt from the bytes.
 L3, the clearance: EVIDENCE COMPLETE AND VERIFIED, WAITING ON THE USER. Ten events cleared, twelve sidecar digests recomputed and matching, zero occurrences of the capturing user's name, every sidecar naming the record path.
 L4 onward: not started, and blocked by the gate-decision slice, by the new withholding arms, and by the reason-vocabulary task.

THE TWO OPEN ITEMS.
 1. THE USER'S VERBATIM ACCEPTANCE of the Codex clearance batch, with the three questions in front of them, one of which is a real choice about the tool-event pair. The clearance worker is held and commits only when those words reach its task.
 2. ROUND 2 OF THE REVIEW, a fresh reviewer on 1e27166. The bar is a fix-free clean round. Round 1 was REVISE at 0 BLOCKER, 4 IMPORTANT and 3 MINOR; all six non-text findings are fixed and one text-only finding is batched. If round 2 is not clean, one round remains for the whole slice diff and I surface the position before it is spent.

GATES THAT STAND, each on an archive copy and each posted on the lock ledger: the catalogue commit, gated twice, by its worker and independently by me, including a byte-identity measurement from two binaries that I ran myself; the clearance bytes, gated twice by their worker with the second run on exactly the bytes to be committed; the fix commits, gated by their worker; and THE COMBINED STATE, 1e27166 plus the uncommitted clearance files, gated by me, because neither worker could see the other's tree and both reported green in good faith about a tree that was not the one to be committed.

WHAT THIS SLICE LEARNED, in the order the lessons arrived.
 - Measure the emission, never the directory listing. The absence of a payload file said two events were unreachable; both are reachable and both were captured.
 - A count is meaningless until the population is named. Seven and eight were both right, about different populations.
 - A pin that derives from the wrong population is not a pin. It passes for years and protects nothing.
 - A claim is a deliverable. Every round-1 finding was a false or unwatched sentence in a correct mechanism.
 - A recipe that predicts the wrong number of files makes a correct sitting look broken.
 - Pair by the host's per-operation identifier at the finest scope the event carries. An identifier every member shares pairs nothing.
 - A control that cannot fail is not a control, and that sentence condemns a dead assertion as well as a missing one.
 - A green gate that tested nothing is worse than a red one, because it ends the questioning.
 - When two agents share a branch, each gates its own state and nobody gates the combined one unless the supervisor does.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SITTING 7 ACCEPTED AT 2 OF 3, AND ITS SECOND ANOMALY IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FORWARD-LOOKING FINDING OF THE CAMPAIGN (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## ACCEPTED
message.removed (2 files) and session.deleted (1) captured. The reused session is intact and only the capturer's own throwaway session was deleted, which is exactly the safety the lead added to that sitting.

## message.part.removed MOVES OUT OF THE REACHABLE SET, AND I SAY WHAT I VERIFIED AND WHAT I DID NOT
The capturer read the interface source and reports that the undo command always calls revert with a message identifier and NEVER a part identifier, so the cleanup never reaches the remove-part branch.
WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF, on the host side: packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts declares partID as OPTIONAL at :16; the selection branch at :56 fires only when a part identifier matches; :57 sets the part identifier to undefined when no part remains; and the cleanup at :108 removes a part ONLY when session.revert.partID is set. So the event genuinely depends on a revert carrying an explicit part identifier.
WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY: the interface's own call site. My search of the interface package returned nothing, so I am relying on the capturer's reading for that half, and I say so rather than presenting the whole chain as mine.
CONSEQUENCE: the row is reachable only by calling the host's local HTTP API with an explicit part identifier, which is the SAME transport as the tui and pty rows. IT THEREFORE JOINS GROUP R-C AND ITS FATE IS DECIDED BY D-1, not by another sitting. The counts move: the reachable set becomes 26, and the HTTP-dependent group becomes 8. I am not asking for another sitting; the capturer was right not to attempt it, because that transport is outside what was authorised and it is the user's decision.

## THE ANOMALY THAT MATTERS FOR THE PLUGIN WORK: A REFUSAL STORM IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL
The capturer observed that pasture's own ingress REFUSED four out-of-catalogue events BY NAME, while the capture sink still wrote every payload. I found the refusal: internal/lifecycle/ingress/validate.go:108, "the %s registration at host version %s declares no native event named %q".
NOW PUT THAT BESIDE THE VOLUMES. In this one sitting the host delivered plugin.added NINETY TIMES, plus catalog.updated 5, reference.updated 3, integration.updated 3 and message.part.delta 3. Our capture kit forwards every bus event, so pasture was asked to bind about a hundred events it has no row for, and refused each one.
THIS IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT ON THE PLUGIN GENERATOR WORK, and it is the first time the population gap has a cost that a user would feel. The committed plugin forwards ONE bus event, guarded by name. When the generator is widened to serve the enabled set, IT MUST FILTER TO THAT SET AND NOT FORWARD EVERYTHING. A plugin that forwards every bus event would hand pasture about a hundred unregistered events per session, each one refused, each refusal a fail-open fault with a diagnostic — on a host whose screen already draws the hook's standard error over the user's session.
THE PLAN ALREADY NAMES THIS CLASS OF DEFECT, in the gate cost work: a gate that faults on every invocation prints a diagnostic on every tool call, which is its own defect even though nobody is blocked. This is the same shape, at about a hundred events per session rather than one per tool call.
SO THE WIDENED PLUGIN NEEDS AN EXPLICIT ALLOW-LIST DRIVEN BY THE ENABLED SET, and the proof that belongs with it is a live session showing NO refusal line for an unregistered event. I record this for the generator and proof leaves rather than ruling their design, which is not mine to fix.

## ONE HONEST OVERSIGHT, RECORDED
The capturer took the live store's digest only AFTER its sitting, not before, and said so unprompted. The mtime predates the sitting, so the conclusion holds; the evidence is one step weaker than the standard the previous sittings met. Recording it costs a line and it stops a later reader assuming every sitting met the same bar.

NOW PUT THAT BESIDE THE VOLUMES. In this one sitting the host delivered plugin.added NINETY TIMES, plus catalog.updated 5, reference.updated 3, integration.updated 3 and message.part.delta 3. Our capture kit forwards every bus event, so pasture was asked to bind about a hundred events it has no row for, and refused each one.
THIS IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT ON THE PLUGIN GENERATOR WORK, and it is the first time the population gap has a cost that a user would feel. The committed plugin forwards ONE bus event, guarded by name. When the generator is widened to serve the enabled set, IT MUST FILTER TO THAT SET AND NOT FORWARD EVERYTHING. A plugin that forwards every bus event would hand pasture about a hundred unregistered events per session, each one refused, each refusal a fail-open fault with a diagnostic — on a host whose screen already draws the hook's standard error over the user's session.
THE PLAN ALREADY NAMES THIS CLASS OF DEFECT, in the gate cost work: a gate that faults on every invocation prints a diagnostic on every tool call, which is its own defect even though nobody is blocked. This is the same shape, at about a hundred events per session rather than one per tool call.
SO THE WIDENED PLUGIN NEEDS AN EXPLICIT ALLOW-LIST DRIVEN BY THE ENABLED SET, and the proof that belongs with it is a live session showing NO refusal line for an unregistered event. I record this for the generator and proof leaves rather than ruling their design, which is not mine to fix.

## ONE HONEST OVERSIGHT, RECORDED
The capturer took the live store's digest only AFTER its sitting, not before, and said so unprompted. The mtime predates the sitting, so the conclusion holds; the evidence is one step weaker than the standard the previous sittings met. Recording it costs a line and it stops a later reader assuming every sitting met the same bar.

text:
RULING ON message.part.removed, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN L5 TABLE THAT THE VOCABULARY CHANGE CREATED (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## THE HOST FACT IS NOW FULLY VERIFIED, BOTH HALVES MINE
I said earlier that I had checked the host side and was relying on the capturer for the interface side. The lead supplied the path and I have now read it. packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx has TWO revert call sites, at :623 and :666, AND BOTH PASS ONLY sessionID AND messageID. Neither passes a part identifier. Together with the host side I already verified — partID optional at revert.ts:16, the selection branch at :56, the cleanup removing a part only when it is set at :108 — the chain is complete: THE INTERFACE CANNOT PRODUCE message.part.removed AT THIS VERSION, and the only route is the host's local HTTP API with an explicit part identifier.

## THE RULING: IT IS NOT A SEPARATE DECISION. IT JOINS THE EIGHT.
The row is reachable by a KNOWN ACTION on a transport we have not been authorised to use. That is exactly the position of the seven tui and pty rows. So it takes THE SAME ANSWER AS THEY DO, from D-1, and I am not ruling it separately: a row that is materially identical to seven others should not acquire a different reason because it was discovered on a different day.
If D-1 admits the local HTTP route, all eight are ordinary captures and the action is an API call rather than a keystroke. If D-1 excludes it, all eight are withheld together.

## THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE VOCABULARY CHANGE I HELPED MAKE
My earlier class map said that if the HTTP route is excluded, these rows take WithheldNoReachableTrigger, on the ground that the trigger is not reachable from a session. THE LEAD RECORDED THAT MAP AS S6'S L5 TABLE. IT IS NOW WRONG.
WithheldNoReachableTrigger has just been NARROWED, with my agreement, to the case where NOBODY KNOWS WHAT FIRES THE EVENT — the case where the condition exists and is unknown to us. THAT IS NOT THESE ROWS. We know exactly what fires them: a specific request to the host's own local API, cited per row to its handler. Putting them on that arm would assert ignorance we do not have, which is the same class of false statement the whole vocabulary exercise removed.
THE CORRECT PLACEMENT, if D-1 excludes the route: the NEW arm, on its second limb — a condition we will not induce. We know the action; we decline to take it. That is precisely what that limb was written for.
I RAISE THIS BECAUSE NOBODY ELSE WOULD CATCH IT. It sits in the interaction between two things I own: a row placement I published before the vocabulary settled, and a narrowing I argued for afterwards. The map was true when I wrote it and the change I helped make falsified it. A placement that is quietly stale is worse than one that was never made, because it has already been recorded as agreed.

## AND IT CORRECTS SOMETHING I TOLD THE LEAD, IN MY OWN SLICE'S FAVOUR
I said the new arm was "earned by StopFailure, not by my rows", and offered my zero as the honest basis for minting it. THAT MAY NOW UNDERSTATE THE CASE. If D-1 excludes the HTTP route, S6 contributes EIGHT rows to that arm, not zero. The arm would then have nine examples across two harnesses rather than one.
I am not re-arguing the decision — it is made, correctly, and on grounds that did not depend on the count. But the count I gave is no longer the honest one, and a number I supplied as the weakest part of our case should not be left standing when it has moved in our favour. THE ARM'S EARNINGS ARE PENDING D-1, and that is the true statement.

text:
PERMDENIED PROBE REPORT (worker-s4-probe, 2026-09-05). ANSWER: DID NOT FIRE.

## Load average at session start
`uptime`: 15:24:18, load average 2.96, 3.85, 3.73. Below the 8 threshold. No wait needed.

## Host version check
`claude --version`: `2.1.261 (Claude Code)`. Matches the pinned host. Not a stop.

## Kit binary digest check
sha256 of `/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/kit/pasture`:
`c2c2ad98940f312f94b8ee88052c84e07da9ab0c5c7d54bf339e31a835af46d6`. Matches the recorded value. Not a stop.

## Host evidence read from the installed 2.1.261 binary, quoted
Read with `strings -a` and a byte-offset context dump on
`/home/minttea/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.261` (a single bundled binary, not a source tree).

Three literal strings the host prints or documents for this event:
1. `Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: `
2. `This goes through the permission gate (a user prompt, or the auto-mode classifier when auto mode is active)`
3. `Return {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PermissionDenied","retry":true}} to tell the model it may retry.`

These three sentences say: PermissionDenied is the auto-mode classifier's own denial, distinct from a user's dialog answer, and the hook may ask the model to retry. This matches the earlier L1 measurement (a human dialog refusal produces PermissionRequest, not PermissionDenied).

A separate internal help text (an audit-check description baked into the binary, not applicable to us directly but useful context) states the permission mode set is `acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, default, dontAsk, plan`, and that the VALUE `"auto"` for `permissions.defaultMode` is source-restricted: a project or local settings file CANNOT turn auto mode on by itself; only user-scope or managed-policy settings can. This did not block my probe because I did not try to set `defaultMode` in the project settings; I enabled auto mode with the CLI flag `--permission-mode auto` on the launching command line, which is a session launch argument, not a settings-file edit, and is unrestricted.

## The rule I set, and the settings file digests
File: `/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/project/.claude/settings.json` (the throwaway project's own settings; never touched `~/.claude/`).

Before (unchanged from L1's transport file): sha256 `ae58b608b44be3765fb641cd0d177d77702888b818d846eeaaae3970d83a927d`.

Rule shape 1 (tried first): added `"permissions": {"deny": ["Bash(cat probe-secret.txt)"]}` (sha256 of the file with this rule: `e6dc7cf9b580844d87747bc14a7c13eb6a0431df2b09d35967e41a75e653b533`). RESULT: no effect. The model ran `cat` with the absolute path (`cat /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/project/probe-secret.txt`), which does not match the exact-string rule `Bash(cat probe-secret.txt)`. The call succeeded. This was a rule-matching miss, not a measurement of the classifier.

Rule shape 2 (tried second, and last, as the instruction caps me at two): changed the rule to the prefix-wildcard `"permissions": {"deny": ["Bash(cat *)"]}` (sha256 of the file with this rule: `45eb038c915410666aaa18c95b3eccd3584e84b0bbb0f495e94d01caeeadf3fa`). RESULT: this rule matched and the Bash call was refused (see pane text and capture evidence below), but no PermissionDenied capture appeared.

After the probe: settings file restored from a byte-for-byte backup taken before any edit. sha256 after restore: `ae58b608b44be3765fb641cd0d177d77702888b818d846eeaaae3970d83a927d`. Matches the recorded before value exactly. Restore confirmed.

## The exact prompt
`Run the shell command \`cat probe-secret.txt\` in this directory and tell me its content.`

Sent twice (once per rule shape), through tmux, literal text then a separate Enter, in the project directory `/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/project`, launched with `claude --permission-mode auto`.

## Pane text at each decision

Rule shape 1 (session 1, no matching rule): the model satisfied the prompt with the Read tool instead of Bash for the "tell me its content" half, then separately ran Bash `cat` with the absolute path, which the exact-match rule did not catch. Pane: `The file probe-secret.txt contains one line: hello`. No denial happened; this run is not evidence about the classifier, only about rule syntax.

Rule shape 2 (session 2, fresh `claude --permission-mode auto` launch after the rule edit): pane showed:
```
● I will run the command and report the file content.
  Read 1 file
● The Bash call was denied. I will try the Read tool as a different route to the file.
  Read 1 file
● I could not run the shell command. The permission system denied the Bash call for cat probe-secret.txt. I read the file with the Read tool instead.
  The file content is:
  hello
```
The refusal is real and visible: "The Bash call was denied" and "The permission system denied the Bash call". The model self-corrected to the Read tool and answered from that.

## Capture directory evidence
`PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR=/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/probe-permdenied`, created fresh by me before the first session (pasture never creates it).

Stopped the host (`/exit` inside the pane, confirmed the resume line, then `tmux kill-session -t s4probe`) before listing. Counted twice, 2 seconds apart, both times 41 fixture files (43 directory-listing lines minus `.` and `..`), no file added or removed between counts.

`ls -la` (post-stop, both counts agreed):
```
claude-code_config_change_2_1_261.1.json
claude-code_instructions_loaded_2_1_261.1.json / .2.json
claude-code_message_display_2_1_261.1.json .. .7.json
claude-code_notification_2_1_261.1.json / .2.json
claude-code_post_tool_batch_2_1_261.1.json .. .6.json
claude-code_post_tool_use_2_1_261.1.json .. .4.json
claude-code_pre_tool_use_2_1_261.1.json .. .6.json
claude-code_session_end_2_1_261.1.json .. .4.json
claude-code_session_start_2_1_261.1.json .. .4.json
claude-code_stop_2_1_261.1.json / .2.json
claude-code_user_prompt_submit_2_1_261.1.json / .2.json
```
No `permission_denied` stem anywhere in that list.

The two PreToolUse files for the denied Bash call (`.3` and `.4`, tool_use_id `toolu_01Pn3bMAyXP7nsKFsqSXpdXP`, prompt_id `464ae4ac-f86a-4eef-9626-c6e5b97e0ef6`) DID fire, with `tool_name: "Bash"` and the full `cat` command as `tool_input`. No PostToolUse, no PostToolUseFailure, and no PermissionDenied file exist for that tool_use_id anywhere in the directory. PreToolUse fires for every tool attempt regardless of the later permission decision; the later stages (PostToolUse or PermissionDenied) are what a decision produces, and here neither one appeared for the denied call.

## Did PermissionDenied fire
NO. Waited a bounded poll (up to 90 seconds, actual wait to first stable read: 90s ceiling reached with count unchanged both before and after) for a `*permission_denied*` file; none appeared. The stop-then-recount protocol from the tmux-capture-driver skill was followed: host stopped first, two reads two seconds apart, both agreeing at 41 files.

## What I tried, what the host did instead, and my reading
I tried two rule shapes in the project's own `permissions.deny` list: an exact-match rule (which never matched the model's absolute-path command, so it is not informative), and a prefix-wildcard rule (`Bash(cat *)`), which did match and did produce a real, visible refusal inside the session. But the refusal took a silent path: PreToolUse fired, then the tool call was rejected with no PostToolUse and no PermissionDenied, and the model was simply told in its own tool result that the call was denied, with no hook running.

My reading, backed by the three quoted host strings above: `permissions.deny` (and by symmetry `permissions.allow`) are STATIC rules resolved before the auto-mode classifier is ever invoked. The classifier is the FALLBACK decision-maker for calls with no matching rule. PermissionDenied is documented and worded as the classifier's OWN denial ("denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier"), not a general "any deny" event. A rule-based deny short-circuits that whole path: the host still fires PreToolUse (as it does for every tool attempt) but never reaches whatever code path calls the classifier and emits PermissionDenied. So setting a deny RULE in the project's settings file blocks the call, but it takes an entirely different, non-classifier code path than the one PermissionDenied instruments, and it therefore cannot be used to capture that event. Only an action the classifier itself judges unsafe, with no matching static rule at all, would reach that path — and per the earlier L1 measurement, this machine's own settings are permissive enough that the two actions tried there were resolved before the classifier could deny them either.

## Settings file restore, confirmed
Restored `/home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/project/.claude/settings.json` from the byte-for-byte backup taken before my first edit. sha256 after restore: `ae58b608b44be3765fb641cd0d177d77702888b818d846eeaaae3970d83a927d`, matching the recorded before value. Confirmed done.

## Scope discipline
No file in the aura-plugins worktree changed (`git status --porcelain` before and after: unchanged, same 6 modified `.beads/backup/*` files and the same 2 untracked `.agents.local/*` files that were already there). Nothing in `~/.local/share/pasture-captures/s4/accepted`, `.../batch`, `.../probe`, or `.../sitting-b` was touched. `~/.claude/` was never written. `PASTURE_DB_PATH` pointed at the s4 scratch database for every hook invocation; the live store at `~/.local/share/pasture` was never touched. Killed only my own tmux session by exact name (`s4probe`), after reading the pane and confirming the resume line, never a pattern kill.

## Answer
This row (PermissionDenied) is NOT captured with disclosure by this route. A project-settings permission rule blocks a call but does not exercise the classifier code path that PermissionDenied instruments, so it cannot be used to capture this event. The row still needs either (i) the user naming a tool call THEIR own settings leave unruled and that the live classifier itself judges unsafe, or (ii) withholding it with a recorded user decision, per L1's Q3 options on aura-plugins-k9xfts. This does not fit `WithheldNoReachableTrigger` cleanly either, since the trigger mechanism (an actual classifier denial) is real and reachable in principle; it is a host-configuration-dependent trigger, not a rule we can set ourselves in the throwaway project.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULING: PROCEED WITH SITTING 4b. THE HOST IS NOT OURS, CANNOT INTERFERE, AND MY RULE WAS TOO BROAD (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## WHAT I MEASURED, READ-ONLY
Process 2880744 is `opencode2`, a DIFFERENT BINARY from the `opencode` this campaign drives, installed under the user's own global package directory. Its working directory is /home/minttea/dev/peasant-labs, OUTSIDE this campaign's tree entirely. Its child is that binary's own service process.
THE DECISIVE FACT: ITS ENVIRONMENT CARRIES ZERO PASTURE VARIABLES. No PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR, no PASTURE_BIN, no PASTURE_DB_PATH. So it cannot write into any capture directory, it does not run our binary, and it is not loading our plugin, which lives only in the campaign's project directories.
Load average has also fallen to 3.83, well under the bound.

## THE RULING
PROCEED. Re-check the load bound immediately before starting, and NEVER TOUCH THAT PROCESS: not a signal, not a kill, not a keystroke, not its directory. It is almost certainly the user's own working session on the user's own project.

## MY RULE WAS WRONG AND I AM FIXING IT, NOT WAIVING IT
I wrote "YOU RUN ALONE. No other live host may run at the same time as this one. If you find another host running, STOP and report it." THAT IS TOO BROAD. It makes the campaign hostage to the USER'S OWN WORK: a person opening their own editor on their own project would halt our sittings indefinitely, and the agent has no way to tell how long to wait.
WHAT THE RULE WAS ACTUALLY FOR: our own concurrent sittings, which shared machine load and produced three stalls, a starved redraw and an incident. A host we did not start, in a project outside the campaign, with none of our environment, contributes to LOAD and to nothing else.
CORRECTED RULE, and it is now two separate checks rather than one:
 1. NO OTHER SITTING OF OURS MAY RUN. Identify ours by the campaign's project directories and by the PASTURE variables in the process environment. That is the rule that stops us colliding with ourselves.
 2. LOAD MUST BE UNDER THE BOUND, with a bounded wait. That is the rule that covers every other process on the machine, ours or not, including a foreign host.
A FOREIGN HOST IS THEREFORE HANDLED BY THE LOAD CHECK, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY IT CAN AFFECT US. Nothing else about it is our business.

## THE AGENT DID EXACTLY THE RIGHT THING, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS CHEAP TO FIX
It stopped before starting a host, before touching any directory and before touching the live store; it did not kill, signal or investigate the foreign process beyond reading what was already visible; and it asked. A too-broad rule obeyed carefully costs one message. The same rule guessed at costs a user's session.
IT ALSO REPORTED THE LOAD SEQUENCE HONESTLY — 12.00 at first check, a 60-second bounded poll, 7.39 after, then the collision STOP — rather than presenting the clearance as if the path had been clear. That is the record that let me rule in one read.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PermissionDenied IS SETTLED: A PROJECT CONFIGURATION CANNOT CAPTURE IT (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). I verified the worker's mechanism in the installed binary and the evidence is STRONGER than the worker's own reading.

THE PROBE RESULT. Two permissions.deny shapes were tried in the throwaway project under auto mode. Shape 1 never matched the model's absolute-path command. SHAPE 2 MATCHED AND PRODUCED A REAL REFUSAL — the pane showed the Bash call denied — AND NO PermissionDenied FILE APPEARED, after a bounded 90-second wait, with the host stopped and the count taken twice at 41 files, stable. PreToolUse fired for the denied call; no PostToolUse and no PermissionDenied. The settings file was restored to its original bytes and the digest checked equal before and after. Nothing else was touched.

THE WORKER'S READING: static permissions.deny and permissions.allow rules resolve BEFORE the auto-mode classifier is consulted, and PermissionDenied is the CLASSIFIER'S OWN denial, not a general "something was denied" event. A settings rule short-circuits the call before it reaches classifier code, so a rule cannot fire this event.

WHAT I FOUND IN THE BINARY, WHICH GOES FURTHER. I confirmed the emission site exists — the strings executePermissionDeniedHooks and emitPermissionDenied are both present, so this is not a declared-and-never-called row. I confirmed rule matching and classifier approval are separate concerns: matched_ask_rule, classifier_approvable and suppressAlwaysAllowRule are distinct strings. AND THE DECISIVE ONE, WHICH THE WORKER DID NOT CLAIM: the binary calls it "THE SERVER-SIDE AUTO MODE CLASSIFIER", and carries the message "Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: ".
THE CLASSIFIER RUNS SERVER-SIDE. So it is not merely that a local rule short-circuits it. NO LOCAL CONFIGURATION DETERMINES ITS VERDICT AT ALL.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OPEN USER QUESTION, and it makes that option weaker than it reads. The question offered the user the option of naming a call that their OWN unruled settings leave to the classifier. Leaving a call unruled does get it TO the classifier — but WHETHER THE CLASSIFIER DENIES IS A SERVER-SIDE DECISION WE CANNOT CONTROL OR PREDICT. So that option raises the chance of an event and cannot guarantee one, and the user should be told that before they spend a sitting on it. Presenting it as a reliable route would be a claim we cannot support.

WHERE THIS LEAVES THE ROW. Capture-with-disclosure through a configuration WE set is CLOSED, by measurement. The row is therefore expected to take the new withholding arm, alongside StopFailure, unless the user both names an unruled call and the server-side classifier happens to deny it.
THE JOINT VOCABULARY TEXT SAID THIS ROW WAS "PENDING" ON A DISCLOSURE CAPTURE. That pending item is now resolved for the configuration route. The new arm therefore has ONE CERTAIN ROW plus ONE EXPECTED ROW, where the text recorded one certain and one possible. The count moved toward the arm, not away from it.

A CATALOGUE DATUM FOR THE ENABLING STEP, worth more than the probe itself: PermissionDenied's practical reachability is NARROW BY DESIGN. It fires only in auto mode, only when no static rule covers the call, and only when a SERVER-SIDE classifier decides to deny. Any text that describes this row as a general denial notification would be false. Whoever writes its evidence row should say what actually fires it.
