author: David Huu Pham
text:
PLACEMENT RULING FOR PermissionDenied, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER STATEMENT (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05).

I SAID THE PROBE MOVED THE COUNT TOWARD THE NEW ARM. THAT WAS WRONG, AND I SAID IT BEFORE TESTING THE ROW AGAINST THE ARM'S ACTUAL LIMBS. Working it through properly gives the opposite answer.

THE ARM'S OWN WORDING IS THE TEST. It reads: the host CAN fire the event and WE CHOSE NOT TO PRODUCE THE CONDITION, with two limbs — (a) a setting we will not impose, (b) a condition we will not induce.
APPLY IT TO PermissionDenied AFTER THE PROBE.
Limb (a) is FALSE. There is no setting we declined to impose. We DID impose one, in the throwaway project, and it did not reach the event; the deciding step runs SERVER-SIDE and no local configuration determines its verdict.
Limb (b) is FALSE. We did not choose not to induce the condition. WE TRIED TO INDUCE IT AND COULD NOT.
So the new arm would put a FALSE sentence on this row. "We chose not to" is not what happened; "we tried and failed" is.

WHERE THE ROW ACTUALLY BELONGS: WithheldNoReachableTrigger, and it is honest there. That arm reads "no KNOWN action makes the host fire the event in a live session". We know the CLASS of action — a tool call that the server-side classifier denies — and we cannot name an action that RELIABLY produces one, because the verdict is not ours to make. That is the same shape as Setup, which the joint text already places on that arm: the mechanism is known, a reliable action is not.

WHAT THE PROBE ACTUALLY CHANGED, stated precisely: it did not move PermissionDenied from "pending" to the new arm. IT RECLASSIFIED THE ROW FROM CASE 2 TO CASE 1. Before the probe we believed the row was configuration-dependent, which is case 2 and the new arm's territory. The probe showed the mechanism is NOT configuration at all, which puts it in case 1, where the existing narrow arm is truthful.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE JOINT TEXT'S COUNT, corrected: THE NEW ARM HAS EXACTLY ONE ROW, StopFailure, and no expected second. My message saying it had one certain and one expected is withdrawn.
THE ARM IS STILL EARNED, and by the row that always earned it. StopFailure is a clean limb (b): the host fires it on an API error, we know exactly what would produce one, and WE DECLINE to force a rate limit or break the user's authentication. That is "we chose not to induce the condition" in its exact sense. Nothing about the arm's justification depended on PermissionDenied, and the open pull request for it is unaffected.

THE PLACEMENT, THEN:
- If the user names a call under the open question AND a live sitting actually captures the event, the row is CAPTURED WITH DISCLOSURE and is not withheld at all. The disclosure states that it fired under the capturing user's own non-default permission settings.
- OTHERWISE the row takes WithheldNoReachableTrigger, with a recorded user decision, and CLEARANCE.md states the true cause: the event is the server-side classifier's own denial; a project configuration cannot produce it, which was measured; and no action we can name reliably produces one.
NOTE THAT ONLY A CAPTURE CHANGES THE PLACEMENT, NOT THE USER'S ANSWER ALONE. The user can name a call, and the classifier may still allow it, because the verdict is server-side. So the row is not held open pending an answer: it is assigned the honest arm now, and it moves only if a capture happens.

WHY I AM RECORDING THE ERROR AND NOT JUST THE ANSWER. I reported a count change to the team lead within minutes of the probe, before checking the row against the arm's two limbs. The check takes one reading of the arm's own sentence. This is the third time today that a fast inference of mine lost to a slow reading, and the pattern is the same each time: I asserted a consequence before testing it against the text that governs it.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
A REUSABLE GATE CAVEAT, FOR ANY SLICE THAT COMMITS WHILE ITS BRANCH IS BEHIND MAIN (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). Recorded here rather than sent as a message, because nothing is blocked on it.

THE SITUATION, WHICH S5 AND S6 WILL BOTH MEET. A harness slice holds for a user acceptance. Main moves while it holds. The slice then commits on a branch that is behind main, and gates an archive copy of its OWN SHA. THAT GATE IS GREEN AND IT PROVES LESS THAN IT APPEARS TO.

WHY IT MATTERS. An archive of the branch head does not contain main's newer commits, so a green suite says nothing about the tree that results when the two meet. The temptation is to let the green stand unqualified, or to "fix" it by merging main into the slice branch before committing — WHICH IS THE WRONG FIX, because it puts unrelated commits into the slice's ancestry, enlarges the diff a reviewer reads, and makes the ownership paragraph hard to verify against it. The merge belongs to the integrator, or to the leaf that actually needs what main gained.

THE SENTENCE worker-s4-l3 WILL PUT IN ITS GATE REPORT, and it is worth copying verbatim by the other slices:
"This gate proves MY BRANCH: a green race suite over an archive copy of the committed SHA, run from inside the copy, naming the packages it ran. It does NOT prove the merged tree. Main moved by three commits while this work was held, and my branch is not merged with them. The merged tree is proven by the pull-request run, which tests this branch merged with main, and confirmed by the push-to-main run after the merge; BOTH runs are confirmed, not only the pull-request ones, because two workflow runs fire per push and they can disagree under load. The integrator owns both. I expect no conflict, because those commits touch the activation types while I touch the codegen guard, the ingress corpus test, the clearance record and the fixtures — but that is an expectation and not a measurement, and the measurement is the pull-request run."

WHY THIS SHAPE IS BETTER THAN EITHER ALTERNATIVE. Letting the green stand unqualified overstates it. Merging to make the green complete corrupts the commit. NAMING WHERE THE MISSING MEASUREMENT COMES FROM turns a limitation into a handover with an owner: the reader learns the question was asked AND where it gets answered. A caveat that names no resolution is a loose end; a caveat that names one is a contract.

THE GENERAL RULE UNDER IT: state what a green proves and what it does not, and name the party who proves the rest. That is the same standard we apply to every other claim in this epic — no claim without evidence, and no evidence stretched past what it measured. It applies to a gate report exactly as it applies to a catalogue row.

## 4. Plugin load evidence

## 5. Per-step actions, files, and the exact lsp configuration

State set for this sitting, exactly as ordered: project directory opencode.json holds `{"lsp": true}` (the host later rewrote it to add a `$schema` key on load; the `lsp: true` value is unchanged and this is expected host normalization, not an edit I made). The project also holds Program.cs (`Console.WriteLine("probe");`) and probe.csproj (a minimal net8.0 SDK-style project). csharp-ls is present at ~/.local/share/opencode/bin/csharp-ls (measured, no download performed).

T1. Started the host in the tmux session (`opencode`), waited for the widened-key startup burst, then filtered the host log to my own run id and project directory only (H-1).
- Filtered log evidence (tail from the 404922038-byte offset, then grepped for `run=d5a5bd1d`, the run id that appears on every line naming my project directory): `message="enabled LSP servers" serverIds="zls, yaml-ls, vue, typescript, tinymist, texlab, terraform, svelte, sourcekit-lsp, rust, ruby-lsp, razor, pyright, prisma, php intelephense, oxlint, ocaml-lsp, nixd, lua-ls, kotlin-ls, julials, jdtls, haskell-language-server, gopls, gleam, fsharp, elixir-ls, eslint, dockerfile, deno, dart, clojure-lsp, clangd, csharp, biome, bash, astro"`. The list includes "csharp". Zero occurrences of "all LSPs are disabled" in the filtered set (0 total in the tail, checked both filtered and unfiltered). T1 PASSED: the `lsp: true` configuration took effect for my own run; no fix or restart was needed.
- Exact non-default configuration used: `{"lsp": true}` in /home/minttea/.local/share/pasture-captures/s6/project-4b/opencode.json (project-local only; never touched the user's global configuration or the repository). This must be disclosed beside the fixture if this row is later cleared.

T2. Sent: "Read Program.cs and tell me its first line."
- Action: send-keys -l 'Read Program.cs and tell me its first line.', pause 1s, Enter.
- Host log (filtered to run=d5a5bd1d / project-4b) confirms the file was read: `message=evaluated permission=read pattern=.../Program.cs action.permission=read ...` then `message="touching file" file=.../Program.cs`, which is LSP.touchFile's own log line (lsp.ts:345), followed immediately by the model's turn completing (`message=loop ... step=3`, `message="exiting loop"`).
- The assistant's reply appeared in the resume screen after quitting: "Session: First line of Program.cs" / the turn completed normally.

T3. Waited on the file, bounded.
- Expected file: opencode_lsp_updated_1_18_29.1.json.
- Bounded poll: `n=0; until [ -e "$FILE" ] || [ $n -ge 90 ]; do sleep 1; n=$((n+1)); done`. Waited the full 90s ceiling. The file DID NOT appear. This is a finding, not a retry, and I did not repeat the trigger, try a second file type, or install anything.

## THE MEASURED CAUSE, READ FROM THE HOST'S OWN SOURCE AND LOG

touchFile (lsp/lsp.ts:344-345) calls getClients (lsp/lsp.ts:208), which iterates registered servers, checks the file extension, then calls `server.root(file, ctx)` and, if a root is found, `server.spawn(root, ctx, flags)` (lsp/lsp.ts:217-227). Only a successful spawn increments `updated`, and only `updated` produces `events.publish(Event.Updated, {})` at lsp/lsp.ts:293.

The CSharp server entry (lsp/server.ts:687-701) does NOT spawn csharp-ls. Its spawn function calls `getRoslynLanguageServer(flags.disableLspDownload)` (server.ts:691-693), which:
1. calls `which("roslyn-language-server")` (server.ts:738) -- searches PATH plus the host's own bin cache directory (core/src/util/which.ts:5-13, core/src/global.ts, `Path.bin` = the same `~/.local/share/opencode/bin` directory that holds csharp-ls);
2. if not found, checks a fixed global dotnet-tools path (server.ts:741, 777-785);
3. if still not found, calls `installRoslynLanguageServer`, which immediately returns undefined if `which("dotnet")` is falsy (server.ts:751-753), WITHOUT attempting any download.

MEASURED on this machine, in the same shell state the sitting ran in: `which roslyn-language-server` -> not found; `which dotnet` -> not found. `find ~/.local/share/opencode/bin -maxdepth 1 -type f` shows only bun.lock, csharp-ls and package.json -- no roslyn-language-server binary anywhere the host would look. So `getRoslynLanguageServer` returns undefined, `CSharp.spawn` returns undefined at server.ts:693 (`if (!bin) return`), `schedule()` in lsp.ts returns undefined at line 229 (`if (!handle) return undefined`), no client is created, `updated` stays 0, and `events.publish(Event.Updated, ...)` is never called. This matches exactly what the host log shows: the "touching file" line fires (lsp.ts:345), and NO further LSP-related log line follows it in the filtered set -- no spawn attempt, no error, no broken-server mark. The silence is not a fault; it is `getClients` finding zero eligible, spawnable servers and returning early.

THE RECIPE'S STATED CAUSE FOR ROUTE SELECTION WAS WRONG, MEASURED HERE, AND I RECORD THE CORRECTION: the order's premise, "csharp-ls is already installed on this machine... so the C-sharp route is the one with a server already present" (aura-plugins-ae098k row 21), does not hold at OpenCode 1.18.29. The host's own `CSharp` server definition (lsp/server.ts:687-701) is wired to `roslyn-language-server`, not `csharp-ls`; there is no server entry in lsp/server.ts anywhere that spawns a binary named `csharp-ls`. The presence of csharp-ls in ~/.local/share/opencode/bin is therefore irrelevant to this row: it satisfies no code path the host will call for a `.cs` file. I did not find this by reading the log alone; I traced it to the exact lines above before concluding, per the order's instruction not to guess.

## RESULT, STATED PLAINLY, EITHER WAY

The subsystem was ENABLED (T1 passed, log confirms "csharp" listed among enabled LSP servers, for my own run only). A file whose type matches a declared server root (probe.csproj + Program.cs, matching CSharp's root list [.slnx, .sln, .csproj, global.json] and extensions [.cs, .csx]) was present and was read by the assistant. lsp.updated STILL DID NOT FIRE, after the full 90s bounded wait, because the server CSharp actually needs (roslyn-language-server) is absent from this machine, and its own fallback install path is a no-op here because `dotnet` is also absent -- so no download was attempted and none was performed by me. I did not try a second language and I did not install anything (no `dotnet`, no `roslyn-language-server`, nothing). I conclude nothing beyond what I measured: this row is decided as WITHHELD-NO-ADMISSIBLE-SERVER for the C-sharp route specifically, on this machine, at OpenCode 1.18.29, with the subsystem enabled and the trigger run. Whether a different route (Go with gopls, which the earlier recipe named but ruled out as requiring a network download) could ever be admissible is outside this sitting's scope and outside what I am authorized to attempt.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SITTING 4b ACCEPTED. THE CAPTURE CAMPAIGN IS COMPLETE. FINAL ROW LIST AND THE lsp.updated RULING (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

## MY PREMISE FAILED ON TWO COUNTS, AND I VERIFIED BOTH
My order sent that sitting down the C-sharp route because csharp-ls is installed at ~/.local/share/opencode/bin. MEASURED AT THE HOST SOURCE: packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts:687-701, the CSharp entry's spawn calls getRoslynLanguageServer and RETURNS NOTHING IF THERE IS NO BINARY. IT NEVER LOOKS FOR csharp-ls. And on this machine `roslyn-language-server`, `dotnet` and even `csharp-ls` are all ABSENT FROM PATH, so the host's own fallback install is a silent no-op as well.
SO THE SERVER I NAMED WAS NEVER THE SERVER THE HOST WOULD SPAWN. My earlier correction — that a PATH survey cannot detect a feature that never asks for a binary — was right about the subsystem and still left me naming the wrong binary underneath it. The capturer enabled the subsystem exactly as ordered, proved it took effect on its own run, and then found the layer below.

## THE RULING, AND I CORRECT THE CAPTURER'S RECOMMENDED WORDING
The capturer recommends "WITHHELD (no admissible server on this machine)". THE FACT IS RIGHT AND THE SENTENCE IS INCOMPLETE, in the direction that matters.
"No admissible server on this machine" reads as an ENVIRONMENT FACT that nothing could change. It is not. THE ROW IS REACHABLE: install roslyn-language-server or dotnet, open a C-sharp file, and it fires. WE DECLINED TO INSTALL ONE, because installing software on the user's machine to manufacture a fixture is a change to the user's environment, and my order forbade it deliberately.
SO THE HONEST REASON NAMES THE CHOICE: the subsystem was enabled and proved enabled; no server the host will spawn is present; and WE DECLINED TO INSTALL ONE. That is a known action we did not take, which is exactly the second limb of the new arm — a condition we will not induce. lsp.updated therefore takes WithheldTriggerNotExercised, NOT NoReachableTrigger, whose narrow meaning is that nobody knows what fires it. We know precisely what fires it.
THIS ALSO SETTLES THE ROW'S CLASS, which I declined to fix a round ago pending this sitting: it is not configuration-dependent in the end. The configuration was imposed and was not sufficient.

## AND IT SUPERSEDES MY OWN "ZERO ROWS" STATEMENT AGAIN, IN THE SAME DIRECTION
I told the lead the new arm was earned by another slice's row and that S6 contributed zero. That is now wrong twice over: lsp.updated takes it OUTRIGHT, and the eight HTTP-route rows take it if the route is excluded. S6 contributes AT LEAST ONE and up to NINE. The arm was minted on grounds that never depended on the count, so nothing is re-opened; but the count I offered as our weakest point has now moved in our favour twice, and it should not be left standing.

## THE FINAL ROW LIST FOR THE CLEARANCE STEP
27 ROWS HAVE CAPTURES: the 2 already enabled plus 25 newly captured. Sources, one sitting per family:
 - SITTING 2, fourteen rows from ONE session and ONE turn: session.created, session.updated, session.idle, session.status, session.diff, message.updated, message.part.updated, chat.message, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition, tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after.
 - SITTING 3: shell.env, permission.replied. SITTING 4: file.edited, file.watcher.updated, vcs.branch.updated. SITTING 5: experimental.session.compacting, session.compacted. SITTING 6: command.execute.before, command.executed, todo.updated. SITTING 7: message.removed, session.deleted. SITTING 8: session.error.
20 ROWS HAVE NO CAPTURE, and every one is accounted for: 4 HELD pending the user's credential decision; 8 reachable only through the host's local HTTP API and pending D-1 (the seven tui and pty rows plus message.part.removed); 1 lsp.updated, ruled above; and 7 that no action reaches at this version — installation.updated, installation.update-available, lsp.client.diagnostics, permission.updated, server.connected, server.instance.disposed, permission.ask.
4 + 8 + 1 + 7 = 20, and 27 + 20 = 47. THE LIST IS EXHAUSTIVE AND THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES.

## WHAT THE CLEARANCE STEP STILL WAITS ON
Two user answers and nothing else: D-2, which decides the four held rows, and the pair rule A/B/C, which decides the two committed fixtures that would sit beside a same-session family. The row list above is otherwise final, and every row carries its sitting, its candidate count and its smallest size in the draft I posted earlier.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ROUND-2 REVIEW (reviewer-s5-r2, 2026-09-05). Target 1e27166 on slice/rp2tju-s5, base 0b33f07, four commits. VERDICT: REVISE. 0 BLOCKER, 3 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR (text-only). THE ROUND IS NOT CLEAN. I applied no fix. Every measurement is on my own archive copy at /home/minttea/.claude-scratch/reviewer-s5-r2/copy, which I diffed against a fresh archive of 1e27166 and found identical before I began. I never touched the live worktree and I never modified the upstream clone.

ALL SIX ROUND-1 FIXES HOLD. I reproduced each original failure before I accepted the fix.

1. THE CITATIONS (7272b5f). Every claim in that file is now correct at the tag it names, checked with `git -C <clone> show <tag>:<path>` at BOTH tags.
   - run_session_end_hooks begins at :369 at rust-v0.146.0 and at :455 at rust-v0.153.0; I printed both. The root-only comment and check are :378-382 at 0.146.0 and :464-468 at 0.153.0, EXACTLY the ranges the comment now names. The old ":378-392 at 0.153.0" was inside run_turn_stop_hooks, so the measured cause, a version sweep that moved the string and not the numbers, is true.
   - SessionEnd's payload: session_end.rs:64-68 at 0.153.0 holds session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name and reason, the five the comment lists, and :63 is the serde_json::to_string the table cell names.
   - Interrupt: `git ls-tree rust-v0.146.0 -- codex-rs/hooks/src/events/` names no interrupt.rs and hook_runtime.rs of that tag has no interrupt emitter; at 0.153.0 run_turn_interrupt_hooks is at :486 and interrupt.rs:76-82 holds SEVEN members, the seven the comment now lists.
   - THE WHOLE CLASS, not the two probed points. I re-read all 24 table cells at 0.153.0. Every emission cell is the declaration line of the function that builds the request (124, 184, 246, 285, 376, 455, 486, 528, 565, 661) and every payload cell is that event's command-input build. UserPromptSubmit at :661 is inspect_pending_input, which builds UserPromptSubmitRequest at :668. A tree-wide grep finds no other host citation in any file this change touched. NO THIRD MISS.

2. THE REFUSAL COST (cd1313b). I ran the linkage proof myself, and the COST claim is true. `go list -deps ./cmd/...` names the hostcontract package ZERO times across all five commands. The Codex admission path reads the committed manifest. The message's cost sentence, code generation stops and admission does not, is right, and I re-measured the wider half: the generator writes all eight outputs in one pass and runs first in the generate target. BUT reading the text as an operator produced a finding, below.

3. THE MOVING-STATE PIN (1e27166), IN THREE WORLDS, not one.
   - ONE ROW CITED, regenerated: registration, host-contract and Codex frontend suites all GREEN. The old pin was RED there. The required demonstration reproduces.
   - EVERY ROW CITED, regenerated: all three suites GREEN as well. The derived-set comparison says nothing false in the world the fix was NOT measured in, which is what I was asked to try.
   - ONE ROW CITED, NOT regenerated: green nowhere, and the messages that fire name the wrong cause. That is a finding, below.

4. THE DERIVED COUNTS (lcs8q7). I drove all TEN narrowing mutations myself, one number at a time, each reverted. Five catalogue sentences (12 registered / 10 without capture, the 12 rows read, 0 of 12 disagreeing, identities for 0 of those 10, complete over all 12) and three frontend counts (12 of 12 same failure mode, 8 rows identity-absent, 8 of those 8 capture-free) each turn the pin RED naming ITS OWN sentence and no neighbour's. The two frontend row names are covered by the axis mutation below. No pin names a neighbour's sentence.

5. THE WIDTH CONTROL (1fpx1p). I deleted the PermissionRequest gate row from the catalogue and ran the host-contract subject alone: RED at the equality, naming both row lists and which side lacks which row. That mutation was GREEN before the fix. THE NARROWEST CHANGE THAT STILL PASSES is one that keeps the two NAME SETS equal, so I measured the sharpest such case: I exchanged the ordinals of the Stop and SubagentStop rows, regenerated, and ran the WHOLE tree. It is green, and the generated files come back byte-identical. The reason is not a hole in the new control: the generator numbers events by POSITION in the slice (renderKinds writes `iota + 1` in order) and never reads the catalogue's Kind literal, so that literal is decorative today. That is pre-existing, is outside these four commits, and I file nothing for it; I record it because the next person to insert a row in the middle of that slice will shift every ordinal after it with no test to say so.

6. THE AXIS-TIED NAME PINS (5sugkv). I swapped PostCompact and PostToolUse between the two sentences: RED FOUR WAYS, inclusion and exclusion on both axes, each message quoting the sentence it read. I also deleted the marker of one axis: RED with "must open its sentence about the gate-or-observation semantic with ...", so the pin cannot stop running in silence.

THE TWO SUPERVISOR RULINGS, AUDITED AND NOT INHERITED.

A. THE REMOVED CONTROL. The measurement is TRUE and I reproduced it. With every Codex row made an observation, the arms control fires first with "every Codex catalog row carries the same failure arm map[strict-hook-failure:12]", so the widened form could never fire on its own. I also read the two arms rather than trust the sentence: evidenceBoundFailure returns the non-blocking arm for a non-blocking row, so only a blocking row can move. The coverage claim holds today: a declared-field read turns the row equality RED naming the row, and a constant read turns the arms control RED. The sibling control in the divergence subject IS reachable and fired in that same tree. ONE PART FAILS: the file does not carry the CONDITION for the control's return, which the ruling required. That is the MINOR below, and the ruling was posted after the three commits, so the worker could not have carried it.

B. THE RE-KEYED CONTROL. The capture future is safe, as ruled: the clearance work adds fixtures and does not touch the activation table, so the capture-free count does not move and the control cannot fire falsely. THE CITATION FUTURE IS NOT SAFE, and that is the IMPORTANT finding I did not expect to make. The new key treats "a row cites evidence" as proof that the evidence rule is live, and a cited row is exactly a row the rule does NOT move. In the tree the enabling leaf builds, the control goes silent while the vacuity its own message describes becomes true.

THE STANDING ATTACK LIST.
 - BYTE IDENTITY, my own binaries and my own bootstrapped stores, over the two committed Codex fixtures taken from my archive. NORMAL PATH: SessionStart exit 0 on both, stdout {}, sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16 on both; PreToolUse exit 0 on both, stdout {"continue":true}, sha256 a1f7818dbf24fe751cbed1cf on both; cmp reports no difference on stdout or stderr for either event. FAIL-CLOSED FAULT PATH, --db under a path whose parent is a file, PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1: both events, both binaries, exit 0, stdout and stderr identical byte for byte by cmp. The diagnostics read "declared failure mode strict-hook-failure, effective failure mode strict-hook-failure" for SessionStart and "declared failure mode strict-output-exit-2-blocks, effective failure mode report-and-continue" for PreToolUse on BOTH binaries.
 - OWNERSHIP, named equals touched, checked mechanically on all four commits: 3135e55 six files, 7272b5f one, cd1313b three, 1e27166 four. Exact.
 - NO INTERNAL REFERENCE. A word-boundary scan of every added line and of all four commit messages for task ids, proposal and slice names, phase and round numbers, section marks, severity labels and process words finds nothing.
 - THE MOVED-CEILING SWEEP, verified rather than believed. AGENTS.md carries no Codex count; its Codex sentences are the hook-budget note and the fail-open bytes {"continue":true}, and my own byte run proves those bytes unmoved. The CHANGELOG's new "seven Codex events" counts the catalogue's seven gate rows (I counted them: UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStop, Stop) and the older "all eight Codex gates" counts the profile's eight; both are true of their own population. hostexit still calls codex PreToolUse a declared blocking gate with no citation, which my fault-path run confirms.
 - IS THERE A CLAIM HERE THAT IS TRUE ONLY TODAY? Yes, and it is finding 1. The rest read the state.
 - SIX GATES on my own copy, from inside it, under the race lock with GATE RUNNING and GATE DONE posted: build 0, vet 0, go test -race -count=1 ./... rc=0 ok=74 FAIL=0 races=0 no-test-files 9, make generate 169 lines then an EMPTY porcelain, gofmt naming nothing and then NAMING my planted control internal/gatecontrol_planted_r2.go which I removed, nix flake check --no-build green on cgo-disabled-build, race and installer. NOT VACUOUS: the five changed packages ran at 1.136s, 1.052s, 1.025s, 1.025s and 1.024s, and I re-ran the four Codex subject tests with -v until their NAMES printed with PASS. No re-run was needed for internal/engine or internal/hooks.

THE FINDINGS.

aura-plugins-ya2qhn IMPORTANT: THE RE-KEYED NON-VACUITY CONTROL GOES QUIET IN THE TREE THE NEXT-BUT-ONE LEAF BUILDS. The control is `demotedGates == 0 && len(evidencedGateRows) == 0`. A CITED ROW IS A ROW THE RULE DOES NOT MOVE: evidenceBoundFailure returns the declared blocking arm when a citation stands, and declaredFailureArm returns the same arm, so in a fully cited profile the effective mode EQUALS the declared mode on every row. MEASURED: I cited every Codex row, ALSO changed the read from mapping.Failure() to mapping.DeclaredFailure(), ran make generate, and both subjects reported ok. In the same fully cited tree with the read UNCHANGED the same four internal/runtime tests are red, so those reds belong to the citation and nothing anywhere caught the broken read. The leaf that records deny-contract evidence for the eight gates builds exactly that tree, and from that day this slice's central property is unproven with no control saying so. The round-1 fix traded a false alarm at the capture leaf for a missed alarm at the citation leaf.

aura-plugins-m48w1g IMPORTANT: TWO DIVERGENCE MESSAGES BLAME A HAND-WRITTEN ARM FOR AN UNREGENERATED MANIFEST. Both new checks compare the COMMITTED generated manifest with the LIVE profile and state one cause for a difference. There is a third and ordinary one: the profile moved and make generate has not run. MEASURED: one row cited, no catalogue line touched, no regeneration, and the suite prints "the catalogue READS that field from the profile, so a disagreement means a row went back to a hand-written arm" and "A row in the SECOND list only means the catalogue went back to a hand-written arm ... Repair by citing the host emission site ... or by letting the catalogue read the demoted arm again". Neither repair works there, and the one that does, make generate, is not printed. The host-contract subject stays green in that run, so the wrong cause is the only voice. This is the same conflation of the SOURCE catalogue with the GENERATED manifest that cd1313b removed from the frontend doc comment and left standing in these messages.

aura-plugins-dd2n0q IMPORTANT: THE NEW REFUSAL NAMES AN EXCLUSIVE CALLER THAT IS NOT EXCLUSIVE. codexReaderRefusalCost says "The generator internal/lifecycle/ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen is the only caller of this catalog outside this package's own tests". internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/capture_test.go calls hostcontract.Codex0_153_0().Events. The same sentence stands in the constant's doc comment and in the pin's doc comment. MEASURED: `go list -f '{{.TestImports}} {{.XTestImports}}'` names four packages whose tests import it, and when I drove the refusal by renaming one catalogue row, THREE packages failed, including internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex, whose panic carries the sentence saying it is not a caller. The cost claim itself is true; the enumeration that supports it is false, and the reader meets the contradiction in the same run.

aura-plugins-vdjgb9 MINOR (TEXT-ONLY): the record of the removed control states why it is dead and not what would make it live again, which the ruling required. It changes no behaviour, no gate and no data, so by the standing rule it belongs on the epic's text batch aura-plugins-inamu5 rather than in a fix round. I say plainly that the ruling arrived after the commits.

WHICH OF MY FINDINGS ARE TEXT-ONLY. One: aura-plugins-vdjgb9. The other three are not, and I say why, because two of them are repaired by editing a message. This team's own round-1 line is the one I follow: a cosmetic inconsistency is text-only, and a FALSE CLAIM in an operator message is IMPORTANT, because a person acts on it. aura-plugins-m48w1g sends the next worker on this slice to the wrong repair, aura-plugins-dd2n0q sends a maintainer hunting a cause that is not there, and aura-plugins-ya2qhn is not text at all: it is a control that stops guarding.

WHICH ATTACKS I RAN. Section 2: all six RAN, each by reproducing the original failure first. Section 3: both rulings AUDITED, A by re-driving the measurement and reading the two arms, B by walking both futures and measuring the citation one. Section 4: byte identity RAN on both events and both paths; ownership RAN; internal-reference scan RAN; the moved-ceiling sweep RAN over AGENTS.md, the CHANGELOG, hostexit and the generated artefacts; operator text RAN and produced two of the three findings; "true only today" RAN. Section 5: all six gates RAN with the planted control and the non-vacuity check.
WHAT I DID NOT RUN. I did not re-drive the worker's M-A and M-A2 refusal-text mutations, because I drove the refusal itself and read the whole message as an operator, which is the stronger form of the same question. I did not attempt a symmetric row deletion from BOTH artefacts; I measured the ordinal-preserving case instead and explain above why the name-set key is not what carries that risk.

text:
ROUND-2 VERDICT: REVISE, 0 BLOCKER, 3 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR. THE ROUND IS NOT CLEAN (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05).

I OWN THE FIRST FINDING. aura-plugins-ya2qhn is MY RULING, and it is wrong in one direction. I accepted re-keying a control away from the capture-free count, because that key would have raised a FALSE ALARM when this slice's own capture work landed. author: David Huu Pham
text:
CORRECTION TO MY REASON TABLE, MEASURED AGAINST THE MERGED ARMS (supervisor-s4, 2026-09-05). Caught before the enabling step, which would otherwise have hit a refusal from the code.

I VERIFIED THE ELEVEN ARMS ON origin/main AT THE MERGE. All five names our placements use exist exactly as agreed: MissingRequestCorrelation, ProviderHook, OutsideTargetSet, NoReachableTrigger and TriggerNotExercised. No naming mismatch waits for the enabling step.

THE ERROR I FOUND IS MINE. My final reason table said the worktree pair takes ProviderHook and needs NO user decision. THAT IS FALSE AGAINST THE MERGED CODE. RequiresClearance() returns TRUE for WithheldProviderHook, and the constructors treat that as "records a user decision and requires the committed CLEARANCE.md path where that decision is recorded". So NewWithheld REFUSES a ProviderHook entry; only NewWithheldByDecision accepts one, and it demands a valid clearance path.
HAD THIS STOOD, the enabling step would have written NewWithheld for WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove and been refused by its own constructor, then had to go back to the user for a decision that had never been sought. Instead the decision is already being sought.

THE CORRECTED COUNT: EIGHT of the eleven withheld rows require a RECORDED USER DECISION and a clearance path, not six.
 ProviderHook, clearance REQUIRED: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove.
 NoReachableTrigger, clearance REQUIRED: Setup, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, PermissionDenied.
 TriggerNotExercised, clearance REQUIRED: StopFailure.
 NO clearance path required: FileChanged on OutsideTargetSet, and the Elicitation pair on MissingRequestCorrelation.
Eight plus three is eleven, and eleven plus the twenty-two enable-able is thirty-three.

THE GOOD NEWS, AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: THE USER IS ALREADY BEING ASKED ABOUT EXACTLY THOSE EIGHT ROWS. The raised list puts the worktree pair, PermissionDenied, Setup and StopFailure in front of them, and the teammate trio was added as a sixth question. That is 2 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 3, which is eight — the same eight the code demands a decision for. The question set and the code's requirement match exactly, by luck rather than by design, because I built the question set from what was unclear and not from what RequiresClearance returns.
FileChanged is the one raised row that needs NO recorded decision, since OutsideTargetSet requires no clearance path. Asking about it was still right: it is a real choice about whether to fix our generator, and the answer belongs in prose whether or not the code demands it.

ONE ITEM FOR THE OTHER HARNESSES, not mine to act on: NotEmittedByHost and EmittedOutsideTransport ALSO require a clearance path. The OpenCode placements in the joint text put six rows across those two arms, so six OpenCode rows need recorded user decisions and committed clearance paths as well. Whoever owns that slice should check its question set against RequiresClearance the way I have just had to.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same one three times today: I WROTE A TABLE COLUMN FROM WHAT I BELIEVED THE ARMS MEANT INSTEAD OF FROM WHAT THE CODE RETURNS. One reading of RequiresClearance settles the whole column. Derive the column; do not type it.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
ONE CLAUSE TO ADD BEFORE THE ACCEPTANCE TEXT IS WRITTEN (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05, from a lead ruling that binds all three harness records). Do this now, while you are held. It is one clause plus a re-run, not a rewrite.
WHAT I MEASURED IN YOUR DRAFT. The condition is ALREADY DISCLOSED TWICE and you deserve the credit for that: the set-up list says the profile change IS the set-up and that the starting profile approves for the user, and the PermissionRequest fixture line says the file was produced after the session's permission profile was moved to ask for approval. So the reader is not misled today.
WHAT IS MISSING, and it is the part the ruling is about.
 1. THE HOST'S OWN NAMES ARE NOT IN THE RECORD. The measured names are the profile "Ask for approval", chosen from the host's own permissions menu, and the account default "Approve for me", which the host's status display shows. A reader who wants to reproduce the capture, or who wants to know which machines will ever emit this event, needs the names the host itself uses, not a description of them.
 2. THE RECORD DOES NOT SAY WHAT THE DEFAULT MEANS FOR A NORMAL USER. "Does not fire without it" is a statement about the trigger. The ruling wants the statement about the DAY: under the account default the host NEVER emits this event, whatever command is run. That is why the earlier sitting saw no approval prompt for a read-only command, and why this slice's own first network attempt also ran silently.
 3. THE CONDITION IS NOT STATED BESIDE THE FIXTURE AS A CONDITION. It reads as a step in a recipe. It must read as a property of that fixture's event, so a later reader who never sees the recipe still learns it.
THE CLAUSE, in your own words and in the record's own voice, placed beside permission_request_0_153_0 in the fixture list and not only in the capture narrative: this event is emitted only when the session's permission profile is the host's "Ask for approval"; the account default is "Approve for me", which approves without asking, so on a host left at the default this event never fires and its absence is not a defect.
DO NOT ADD ANY OTHER CONDITION. I checked the rest: no other Codex fixture needed a non-default setting. The sub-agent spawn tool is stable and enabled by default, and every other trigger is a plain prompt or a slash command. Say that plainly too, so a reader knows the list is complete and not merely the one case somebody happened to notice.
THEN: re-run the fast checks, because THE RECORD IS WALKED by the home-segment guard and by the secret scan, so an edit to it can turn either RED. Repost the draft verbatim. The user must accept a record that ALREADY carries this, never one amended after the acceptance.
NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. You stay held. Nothing is committed until the user's words reach this task.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
USER-FACING: THE OPENCODE DECISION LIST. Held for the lead's confirmation before it goes to the user (supervisor-s6, 2026-09-05).

WHY YOU ARE BEING ASKED AT ALL, because it is a mechanism and not a formality. An event we do not capture cannot simply be marked "not done". The code refuses it: a withheld row built without a recorded decision is rejected by the constructor, which demands the committed record where you made that decision. I checked this rather than assumed it. So every gap below needs your word, and the record then holds it permanently.
THE CAMPAIGN CAPTURED 25 OF THE 45 EVENTS IT SET OUT TO. Twenty are not captured, and NOT ONE of them is an absence of evidence: each has a measured cause below. Three are open questions for you; the rest are decisions to confirm.

## OPEN QUESTION 1 — FOUR EVENTS CAN CARRY A LIVE CREDENTIAL. Do we capture them?
Four OpenCode callbacks receive the host's provider context in their input, and that context can contain your API key. We measured the path in the host's source, and we measured that our own secret scan would NOT catch a provider key that is not one of nine known shapes.
So we removed those four callbacks from the capture tool before any sitting ran, and we then confirmed across ALL SEVEN sittings that not one of them produced a file. No credential-bearing payload was ever written. Your decision is still completely open.
The four: chat.params, chat.headers, experimental.provider.small_model, experimental.compaction.autocontinue.
 (a) Capture them against a provider that uses no API key, so no key can be written.
 (b) Do not capture them; record them as withheld by your decision.
 (c) Add a provider-key shape to the secret scan first, then capture them.
We do not recommend capturing them as they are and relying on the clearance step: the scan does not cover this case, and we measured that.

## OPEN QUESTION 2 — EIGHT EVENTS NEED US TO CALL OPENCODE'S OWN LOCAL API. Do we?
Eight events never fire from an ordinary session: seven interface and terminal events, plus one message-part removal. Each IS produced by the host, but only when something calls OpenCode's local HTTP interface directly. A desktop or editor client does that; a person typing does not.
Capturing them means our agent making those API calls during a sitting. The payloads would still be the host's own bytes.
 (a) Yes, call the local API and capture all eight. About one hour more.
 (b) No; record all eight as withheld by your decision.

## OPEN QUESTION 3 — TWO COMMITTED FIXTURES WOULD SIT BESIDE A DIFFERENT SESSION'S FAMILY
Two fixtures already in the repository, which you accepted earlier, come from a session in September's earlier capture round. Thirteen of their neighbours would now come from one new session and one turn. Left as they are, the set would say one session began and a different one lived.
 (a) Keep the accepted fixtures and state the mismatch in the record.
 (b) Replace them with the same-session captures and record the replacement with both digests.
 (c) Replace everywhere EXCEPT where it would displace a fixture you already accepted, which is kept with the mismatch stated.
Under every option the mismatch is written down. Keeping it silent is not one of the options.

## DECISIONS TO CONFIRM — EIGHT EVENTS WE CANNOT OR WILL NOT PRODUCE
Each was measured in OpenCode 1.18.29's own source. We are asking you to confirm each group as a recorded decision.

GROUP A, FOUR EVENTS THE HOST NAMES AND NEVER SENDS. Confirm as withheld, reason "not emitted by host".
 - permission.ask: OpenCode declares this plugin hook at packages/plugin/src/index.ts:261 and NOTHING in the host calls it. We searched every call site in the product.
 - lsp.client.diagnostics: appears only in a generated type file (sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts:25). There is no definition and no place that sends it.
 - permission.updated: same, at types.gen.ts:440. What the host really sends is permission.asked and permission.replied.
 - server.connected: never sent at all. It is a synthetic first line of an HTTP stream (httpapi/handlers/event.ts:70).

GROUP B, THREE EVENTS THE HOST SENDS WHERE NO PLUGIN CAN SEE THEM. Confirm as withheld, reason "emitted outside transport".
 - installation.updated and installation.update-available: sent on a global channel, tagged "global", which can never match a project.
 - server.instance.disposed: sent on the same global channel.
A plugin only receives events tagged with its own project, so no session length or trigger can deliver these three.

GROUP C, ONE EVENT THAT NEEDS SOFTWARE INSTALLED ON YOUR MACHINE. Confirm as withheld, reason "trigger not exercised".
 - lsp.updated fires when OpenCode starts a language server. We enabled the language-server feature in the capture project and proved it took effect. It still did not fire, because for C-sharp OpenCode starts roslyn-language-server (lsp/server.ts:687-701), and neither that nor dotnet is installed here. csharp-ls IS installed, but OpenCode never uses it.
 THE EVENT IS REACHABLE — installing a language server would produce it. WE CHOSE NOT TO INSTALL SOFTWARE ON YOUR MACHINE to manufacture a test fixture. Say if you would rather we did.

## WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
Nothing captured has left this machine, and nothing will before you accept the cleared batch. The clearance step starts as soon as questions 1 and 3 are answered; question 2 and the confirmations decide how the remaining rows are recorded.

# Clearance record

This file records how the fixtures in this directory were captured, cleared
and accepted. Fill every section before the acceptance test; leave the last
two sections for the acceptance and the landing. The procedure is documented
in AGENTS.md under "Capturing host payloads and clearing them into fixtures".

Two batches of fixtures sit in this directory and this one file records both.
The FIRST BATCH is the two fixtures SessionStart and PreToolUse, cleared from
the first sitting. The SECOND BATCH is the ten fixtures UserPromptSubmit,
PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStart,
SubagentStop, Stop, SessionEnd and Interrupt, cleared from the second sitting.
The first batch's two fixtures are unchanged: the second sitting captured those
two events again, and those newer files are recorded below as captured and not
used. Each section below states which batch a paragraph belongs to.

## Harness and pinned version

Codex 0.153.0. Admission is a floor: this version and every later release; the
contract records 0.153.0.

FIRST BATCH: verified with `codex --version` immediately before the session on
2026-09-05: `codex-cli 0.153.0`.

SECOND BATCH: `codex --version` was taken at both ends. Immediately before the
sitting on 2026-09-05 it printed `codex-cli 0.153.0`. After the batch was
checked, on the same day, it printed `codex-cli 0.153.0` again. The host did
not move between the two readings.

## Capture

Paths in this record are spelled with `~` for the capturing user's home
directory; the fixture bytes themselves carry the `/home/user` placeholder that
`home-path-v1` writes. The sessions were interactive terminal sessions of the
real host binary on the user's machine, run at the user's direction by the
team's operators; the user did not type the prompts. Nothing captured reached
any remote before the user's acceptance recorded below.

### First batch

Captured in one live session on 2026-09-05, into
`~/.local/share/pasture-captures/codex`, with `PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR`
set.

Build kit: one `pasture` binary, sha256
`0b9a6fbde02493ba7325e772e78703adf2dc11533c882854ac0f7defa9ce5441`, built with
`CGO_ENABLED=0` from an archive copy of head 47d1c94 with the two version
roots moved to the versions above (artifact/aggregate_types.go, the three
`Contract.Version` literals under internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract)
and `make generate` run, so every transport carried the new version.
Environment in the host's shell: `PASTURE_BIN` = that binary,
`PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR` = the directory above (absolute, outside the repository,
pre-existing), `PASTURE_DB_PATH` = `~/.local/share/pasture-captures/scratch/pasture.db`
(a scratch database; the live store was not touched). On this scratch
database every hook printed one fail-open fault line ("cannot resolve
Pasture's persisted system identity") after the capture was written; the host
proceeded and the capture is unaffected.

Codex transport from the kit, in the project directory
`~/.local/share/pasture-captures/project-codex/.codex`:
`hooks.json` sha256 `0afc4938056274f3a3e9989d16630bb1080dfd7b8976cd6b1ae7fdae6ac79dce`,
`hooks/events/SessionStart.sh` sha256 `e51312d01df72ac8983c89e4cd1532b0c4f102d6b2abc25e79ca6239951486db`,
`hooks/events/PreToolUse.sh` sha256 `18bfdd48a63ab3f45e52d677ec4be35372fd25df5291c753f0c61441a9835566`.
These three digests are the digests of the transport files this repository
ships today. At the startup review ("Hooks need review") the project was
trusted; the host wrote `trust_level = "trusted"` for it into
`~/.codex/config.toml`.

Fact recorded: at 0.153.0 the SessionStart hook is queued at session
construction (codex-rs/core/src/session/session.rs:1623) and runs at the start
of the first turn (codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs:264), not at process
startup; no file appeared until the first prompt. One line per event:
- SessionStart: `codex_session_start_0_153_0.1.json` — trigger: the first prompt, "Run the shell command `ls -la` and tell me what you see." (fired 1 s after Enter) — 2026-09-05T12:30:24Z — raw sha256:4803435c52143e90a32eedd7a7b2de95847d4ddf90f5654034a4043f2ff8d380 (353 bytes) — committed sha256:cd5256a1d139adad49f0755096914b64bb7662384d3166240223703b0f732601 (347 bytes)
- PreToolUse: `codex_pre_tool_use_0_153_0.1.json` — trigger: the same prompt, the Bash call `ls -la` (fired 3 s after Enter; no approval prompt, read-only sandbox) — 2026-09-05T12:30:28Z — raw sha256:dc80e09555150d40a6ac8b5d69649785da258d8ff1e8b48660fb91eb07b18ed5 (492 bytes) — committed sha256:8da92d236f18516fec7995e1a6e1456ef67a93a03d970ce3d6a8f91b10f6735d (486 bytes)

Both files carry one session_id. No other file was produced in that session;
none was discarded.

### Second batch

ONE live sitting was run for this batch, on 2026-09-05, into
`~/.local/share/pasture-captures/s5/codex`, with `PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR` set to
that directory: an absolute path, outside the repository, that already existed.
That sitting was run to answer two open questions: whether the generated
transport carries a hook whose matcher is the empty string, and whether every
one of the ten uncaptured events has a trigger a person can reach. It answered
both, and it wrote one or more real files for every one of the twelve events.
Its files are adopted as this batch. No second sitting was run, and this record
claims none.

THE KIT. It was built in a throwaway archive copy of head
`0b33f0760602fb7522a18afe73a5ae91011c090b`, never in a working tree of the
repository. One file was edited in that copy, the Codex activation target
declaration, to add the ten missing rows; `make generate` then ENABLED ALL

and no event could be missed for want of a transport. The generator accepted

committed transport only when a later change enables them from recorded proof.

carries two. The difference is the enablement, and it is stated here so a
reader who hashes the shipped file is not left to guess which number is right.

ENVIRONMENT in the host's shell: `PASTURE_BIN` = the kit binary,
`PASTURE_CAPTURE_DIR` = `~/.local/share/pasture-captures/s5/codex`,

THE LIVE-STORE INCIDENT, stated plainly. One plumbing command in the
preparation for this sitting omitted the scratch database path, so it ran
against the live store at `~/.local/share/pasture`. The person who ran it found

The rule the incident produced is now written in the capture instructions:

### Pairing, by the host's own identifiers

Two files belong together only when the HOST'S OWN per-operation identifier
says so. Field values do not pair anything: two separate operations can carry
the same command, the same tool name and the same shape, and a reading by value
would call them one. Codex carries three granularities, and the right one
depends on the event.

MEASURED over the 39 files of the second sitting: ONE session id; SEVEN
distinct turn ids; TWO files carry no turn id at all, SessionStart and
SessionEnd.

SESSION SCOPE CARRIES NO INFORMATION HERE, and this is the trap. Every file in
this batch shares the one session id, so a session-level match is satisfied by
every pair a reader could form. An identifier every member shares pairs
nothing. No claim in this record rests on it.

TOOL-CALL SCOPE, the finest: PreToolUse and PostToolUse carry `tool_use_id`.
The committed PostToolUse fixture carries turn
`01a0736d-6431-7730-9321-53425562ab77` and tool call
`exec-c18b3026-7f48-406a-a700-cd07054bf30c`. Its PreToolUse counterpart, the
same turn and the same tool call, is in the capture directory and is NOT in
this repository: the committed PreToolUse fixture comes from the FIRST sitting
and carries a different session, a different turn and a different tool call
(`01a0718c-6f88-73c2-8d82-013e647cc02f`,
`exec-8d2f7dd7-3b46-40af-af0a-252dad7bbbec`). THE TWO COMMITTED TOOL EVENTS ARE
THEREFORE NOT A PAIR, and this record asserts none between them.

TURN SCOPE. Three pairs are asserted among the committed fixtures of this
batch, each by its turn id, and one of them by a second identifier as well:
- UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and Stop share turn
  `01a0736d-6431-7730-9321-53425562ab77`: one turn, the prompt that ran

FILES THIS RECORD DOES NOT PAIR, said plainly rather than left to assumption:

## Rules applied, in order

Per fixture, the value-only rules applied in the order applied, as listed in
the provenance sidecar: `home-path-v1`, then `free-text-v1` where the
inventory flagged free text. Structure, keys, types and nulls are unchanged.

`home-path-v1` rewrites every spelling of the capturing user's home directory
to the `user` placeholder: the absolute path `/home/<user>`, the relative
spelling `home/<user>/`, and the directory slug a host derives from a path,
which is how the earlier committed corpus carries it. It applies wherever any
spelling occurs, including inside free text. In this batch every payload
carried the absolute spelling, two or three times each; no payload carried the
relative spelling or the slug.
`free-text-v1` replaces each free-text string the inventory flagged by `x`
placeholder text of the same raw length. Keys, nesting, types and nulls are
unchanged; after both rules the committed bytes contain no occurrence of the
user name (asserted by the clearing run, which refuses to write a file that
still carries it).

A MEASURED PROPERTY OF THE SECOND RULE, recorded because a reader will meet
it. `free-text-v1` is a fixed point in BYTES but not in FLAGS. A placeholder is
written to the same raw length as the value it replaced, so a long placeholder
is still longer than the free-text length limit and the inventory still class
it as free text. Running the rule again therefore reports the field and changes
nothing. The corpus test uses the BYTES for that reason: a committed fixture
must come back unchanged when the rule runs again, and only a placeholder does.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FIXED in b21ca60. The control now constructs the state that discriminates.

WHAT WAS WRONG, and I agree with the finding. The control was keyed on two counts of the tree: demoted gates and rows that cite host evidence. A cited row is a row the evidence rule does NOT move, so in a profile where every declared gate cites evidence the effective arm equals the declared arm on every row, both candidate reads render the same manifest, and the key sees nothing. I reproduced the failure before I fixed it: with every Codex row cited AND the read changed to return the declared field, and the generator run, internal/lifecycle/registration reports ok and internal/lifecycle/frontend/codex reports ok. Nothing anywhere caught the wrong read.

THE FIX IS THE DESIGN AND NOT THE KEY.
1. The read is now a named production function over a row interface. codexProfileRows walks the runtime profile and decides nothing. codexFailureReaderOver IS the read, takes the rows as a parameter, and is the only place in the catalogue that chooses a failure field. codexFailureReader is codexFailureReaderOver(codexProfileRows()), so production is unchanged in behaviour.
2. codexRuntimeRow carries BOTH arms although the read takes one. The declared arm is named there so that a read of the wrong field is a thing a test can write and a control can catch. Without it the wrong read would not compile, which sounds stronger but leaves the control with no message and nothing to fail on.
3. The control builds its own row: one row whose evidence-bound arm is strict-hook-failure and whose declared arm is strict-output-exit-2-blocks. It first requires the two arms to DIFFER, so the control cannot go vacuous by somebody setting them equal, then requires the read to answer the evidence-bound arm.

THE THREE-WORLD PROOF, each world built on my own copy, the read broken to row.DeclaredFailure() in codexFailureReaderOver, and the generator run wherever the profile moved.
 - NO ROW CITED: RED. "the Codex catalogue read answered strict-output-exit-2-blocks for a row whose evidence-bound arm is strict-hook-failure and whose declared arm is strict-output-exit-2-blocks. The catalogue must take the arm the failure-evidence rule PRODUCED, because a declared blocking arm claims a refusal the product cannot perform. The row is built in this test and not read from the tree, so this holds whether or not any live Codex row cites host evidence. Repair the read in codexFailureReaderOver in internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go"
 - ONE ROW CITED, generator run: RED, the same message, word for word.
 - EVERY ROW CITED, generator run: RED, the same message, word for word. In that same world I ran the two neighbouring subjects: internal/lifecycle/registration ok, internal/lifecycle/frontend/codex ok, and the ONLY red in the tree is this control. That is the hole, and one test closes it.
 Every mutation was reverted.

NO FALSE ALARM. In the same three worlds with the read UNCHANGED, registration, host-contract and Codex frontend are all ok. The false alarm the earlier key was removed for does not come back.

MUTATION-RED on what I added, each reverted.
 - The constructed row given ONE arm twice: RED with "the constructed row must hold two DIFFERENT arms, or this control cannot tell the evidence-bound read from the declared one; it holds strict-output-exit-2-blocks twice".
 - The constructed proof renamed: the divergence subject is RED with "the file ... no longer declares TestTheCodexFailureReadTakesTheEvidenceBoundArmAndNotTheDeclaredOne. That test builds a row whose declared arm and evidence-bound arm DIFFER ...".

ONE ASSERTION I WROTE AND THEN REMOVED, and I report it rather than leave it. I first wrote a second require that the answer is not the declared arm. It CANNOT FAIL: require stops at the first failure, and the equality above it already fails whenever the answer is the declared arm, because the two arms are guarded to differ. A dead assertion is what this round is about, so it is gone.

WHAT THE DIVERGENCE SUBJECT NOW SAYS IN PLACE OF THE OLD CONTROL. It states the measurement plainly: it compares two artefacts, and once every Codex row cites evidence it cannot tell the two candidate reads apart, so the proof of WHICH field is read is constructed and lives beside the read. It guards the pointer by name, so a rename or a deletion is RED and not silence.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FIXED in 69f7652. The refusal counts no callers.

I TOOK THE MEASUREMENTS MYSELF before I changed a word, on my own archive copy, inside the dev shell.
 - go list -deps ./cmd/... names the package ZERO times. With -tags recovery it is still zero, and the tag adds a sixth command. So no pasture binary links this package, and the COST claim stands.
 - go list -f {{.Imports}} over ./... names exactly ONE non-test importer: internal/lifecycle/ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen.
 - go list with TestImports and XTestImports names FOUR packages whose tests import it: hostcontractgen, ingress/codex, ingress/internal/hostcontract and ingress/opencode. So the enumeration was false, exactly as filed.
 - The admission half is true at a named line: internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go builds the Codex case with registration.Codex0_153_0(), the committed generated file.
 - The generator half is true by order: main.go builds all three harness catalogs BEFORE the first WriteFile, so a refusal leaves every generated file with the bytes it has.

THE FIX IS NOT A BETTER COUNT. The message no longer names a caller set at all, because a caller set moves whenever somebody writes a test while the cost does not. It says the cost, and it says what the reader of a second red package needs: "Anything else that builds this catalog stops with this same message, so expect more than one red package in one run rather than a second, separate defect."

THE DRIVEN REFUSAL, and what EVERY failing package prints. I spelled the Interrupt row "Interrupted", so the profile holds no row of that name, and ran go test ./... . THREE packages fail:
  FAIL github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/lifecycle/ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen
  FAIL github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex
  FAIL github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract
All three print the SAME panic, and I read all three: "the Codex host contract cannot be built: this catalog declares the event "Interrupted", and the runtime Codex profile declares no row of that native name, so there is no failure mode to read for it. This happened in ... WHAT IT COSTS: code generation stops here and admission does not. The generator internal/lifecycle/ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen builds this catalog and renders every harness in one pass, so make generate writes no file for any harness and the committed generated files keep the bytes they have. Anything else that builds this catalog stops with this same message, so expect more than one red package in one run rather than a second, separate defect. A running pasture is unaffected: no pasture binary links this package, and a Codex hook is still admitted from the committed internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go. HOW TO REPAIR: Add the row to codexLifecycleMappings ..., or spell the name here as the profile spells it, then run make generate". No sentence in it now denies that any of the three is a caller. The mutation was reverted.

MUTATION-RED, both reverted.
 - The exclusivity phrase put back: RED with "the refusal must not name an exclusive caller, and it carries the retired phrase "the only caller of this catalog". FOUR packages build this catalog in their tests, so a driven refusal reddens several packages in one run; a reader of one of the others is then told by this message that it is not a caller, and goes hunting a cause that is not there. State the cost and say that several packages go red, and count no callers". The pin refuses three phrasings, not one, so the class cannot return in a new wording.
 - The new sentence removed: RED with "the refusal must carry "Anything else that builds this catalog stops with this same message, so expect more than one red package in one run" ...".

THE CLASS SWEEP: every claim about the call graph or the import graph in the four files this work touches. SIX claims, and I measured each.
 1. "no pasture binary links this package" TRUE, measured above. I removed the parenthetical "the dependency set of none of the FIVE commands under cmd/" and put the command that measures it in its place: the number was tag-dependent and it undercounted the directories, because cmd/ holds SIX and the sixth compiles only under -tags recovery. The claim survives the tag; the number did not deserve to stand.
 2. "the only caller of this catalog outside this package's own tests" FALSE, in three places: the constant, the doc comment above it and the pin's doc comment. All three are gone.
 3. "it renders every harness in one pass, so make generate writes no file for any harness" TRUE, by the order of main.go.
 4. "a Codex hook is still admitted from the committed .../codex_0_153_0.gen.go" TRUE, at internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go.
 5. The Codex frontend comment: "the source code generation renders into the committed manifest the handler admits with" and "the handler admits with the row code generation wrote into ...". TRUE, same line as 4. I reworded the first for a different reason, recorded on the message finding.
 6. The divergence subject header: "Nothing in production reads registration Event.Failure: the two live readers both read the runtime mapping." TRUE. I grepped every non-test reader of a .Failure field: the only lifecycle one is internal/lifecycle/metamodel/builder.go, and it reads mapping.Failure() from the RUNTIME profile. This sentence is older than these four commits, so it is not of this class, and I report it as checked rather than let it pass unmeasured.
 BEYOND THOSE SIX: nothing else. The host-contract subject's "it reaches the profile through the same by-name lookup the rest of the tree uses" is a claim about which function is called, and LookupLifecycleFailure is called from the divergence subject as well, so it holds.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FIXED in d6e0df0, and the class sweep is in 38526f5.

THE STATES THAT CAN REACH THESE MESSAGES. Both checks compare the COMMITTED generated manifest with the LIVE runtime profile, so three states reach them.
 S1 THE PROFILE MOVED AND THE GENERATOR HAS NOT RUN. The manifest is stale. This is the ordinary state, it is the only one a profile edit on its own can produce, and it is the state the next leaf of this work passes through. The repair is make generate.
 S2 THE SOURCE CATALOGUE WENT BACK TO A HAND-WRITTEN ARM, with the generator run. The repair is to restore the read, then generate.
 S3 NEITHER. Then a row on one side only means what the message always said it meant.
The messages named S2 only, twice, and offered two repairs that do not work in S1.

EACH STATE REACHED, ON MY OWN COPY, AND WHAT PRINTS.
 S1: I gave PermissionRequest a citation in internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go, changed no catalogue line, and did NOT generate. Four messages fire and each now names the action first.
  "the committed Codex registration manifest and the runtime profile state a different failure mode on 1 rows, 0 of them claiming a blocking exit code the profile does not hold, want none. The value compared here is the COMMITTED internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go, and the source it is rendered from, internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract/codex_0_153_0.go, READS this field from internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go. CHECK THE TWO CAUSES IN THIS ORDER. (1) The profile moved and the manifest was not regenerated: run make generate. That is the ordinary cause, and it is the only one a profile edit on its own can produce. (2) The source catalogue went back to a hand-written arm: restore the read in codexFailureReaderOver there, then run make generate"
  "the committed Codex registration manifest states a blocking exit code on 0 of its 12 rows [], and the runtime profile holds 1 rows that declare a blocking exit code AND cite host evidence for it [PermissionRequest]; ... The profile demotes 7 declared gates for want of a citation. CHECK THE THREE CAUSES IN THIS ORDER. (1) The profile moved and the manifest was not regenerated: run make generate. A citation added to or taken from internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go moves the SECOND list at once and the FIRST list only after generation, so the two lists part until the generator runs. (2) ... (3) ..."
  Running make generate in that state turns registration, host-contract and Codex frontend all green, which is what proves the cause.
 S2: I made every gate row carry a hand-written blocking arm and I DID generate. The same two messages fire with 7 rows and 7 over-claiming, cause 1 does not clear it, and cause 2 names the read to restore.

THE CONFLATION IS GONE FROM THE TWO SENTENCES THAT CARRY A FAILURE-MODE COUNT. The catalogue comment said "the two artefacts disagree on the failure mode of 0 of the 12 rows" without saying which two; it now says "the committed manifest rendered from this source and that profile". The Codex frontend comment said the ingress CATALOGUE and the profile state the same mode, while the value compared is the MANIFEST; it now names the committed manifest as the compared value and the catalogue as what it is rendered from. The pin string moved with the first sentence, and reverting the wording turns the pin RED, quoted: "the committed file ... does not state the count the tree derives; it must carry the sentence "the committed manifest rendered from this source and that profile disagree on the failure mode of 0 of the 12 rows" ...". The mutation was reverted.

THE CLASS SWEEP: every message these four commits introduced, checked in EVERY state that can reach it, not only the state its author had. I walked all 28 assertions of the divergence subject and all of the host-contract subject. TWO MORE MESSAGES ARE REACHABLE IN THE STALE STATE and named a cause that is wrong there.
 a. The recorded-axis sets (the gate-or-observation semantic, the mutation mode, the identities). A profile edit alone moves the measured side of one of those axes, and the message then blames a deliberate design difference and sends the reader to redesign or to widen a recorded list.
 b. The third identity case. It asks for the doc comments to be widened for a row it found, and in the stale state the row is an artefact of the stale manifest.
 Both now carry the state and the action. Proved by reaching them: I changed one profile row's semantic without generating, and RED prints "... the two Codex artefacts disagree on the gate-or-observation semantic for 0 rows [], want exactly 1 [PostCompact]; ... The measured side reads the COMMITTED generated manifest internal/lifecycle/registration/codex_0_153_0.gen.go. So if internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles_codex.go or the source catalogue has moved and make generate has not run since, RUN IT FIRST: until it runs this measurement is taken against a stale manifest, and a repair made by hand is undone by the next generation." I gave one profile row an extra identity without generating, and RED prints "the committed Codex manifest declares 1 identities on row "SessionStart" and the runtime profile declares 2; ... a third case they do not cover." with the same closing sentence. Both mutations were reverted.
 THE SENTENCE IS ONE STRING, NOT FOUR. The four messages that can be taken against a stale manifest share one named constant, because four copies of one sentence drift and this epoch has already paid for that.
 NOTHING ELSE. Every other message of the two subjects fires on a state it describes correctly: a file that cannot be read, a marker sentence that is absent, a retired claim still present, an empty population, a profile with no row of a name, an activation manifest that is not exhaustive over the registration one.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FIX ROUND 2 COMPLETE (worker-s5-fix2, 2026-09-05). Four commits on slice/rp2tju-s5, head 38526f5, base 1e27166. All three IMPORTANT items are fixed. The text-only item was NOT touched, as ordered.

THE COMMITS.
 69f7652 the Codex catalogue refusal counts no callers. Files: the catalogue and its subject.
 d6e0df0 the Codex divergence messages name the state they fire in. Files: the divergence subject, the catalogue, the Codex frontend.
 b21ca60 the Codex failure read is proved on a constructed row. Files: the catalogue, its subject, the divergence subject.
 38526f5 the divergence subject names the stale-manifest state once. File: the divergence subject.
Ownership was checked mechanically against each commit's own file list and is exact on all four.

WHAT EACH FIX DID, in one line each; the measurements are on the finding tasks.
 aura-plugins-ya2qhn. The read is now a named production function over a row interface, with the profile walk separated from it, and a control BUILDS a row whose two arms differ and requires the read to answer the arm the evidence rule produced. RED in all three worlds with the read broken; green in all three with it intact.
 aura-plugins-dd2n0q. The refusal names no caller set at all. It states the cost and tells the reader of a second red package to expect several, which is the thing the false enumeration took away.
 aura-plugins-m48w1g. Both messages name the stale manifest first, with the action, then the hand-written arm, then the residue. Two more messages found by the sweep carry the same state.

I JUDGED EVERY FIX AGAINST THE TWO SENTENCES I WAS GIVEN, and one of my own drafts failed the first test. I wrote a second assertion in the new control that could never fail, because require stops at the first failure and the arms are guarded to differ. I removed it before committing. A dead assertion is the defect this round exists to remove, and writing one is easy.

THE THREE-WORLD PROOF, since it is what the round was ordered for. With the read changed to return the declared field: no row cited RED, one row cited RED, every row cited RED, all with the same message, and in the fully cited world the two neighbouring subjects both report ok, so this one control is the whole guard there. With the read intact: green in all three worlds, so the false alarm that the earlier key was removed for does not return.

CLASS SWEEPS, both reported in full on their finding tasks.
 CALL AND IMPORT GRAPH: six claims, one false, one carrying a tag-dependent count that undercounted the directories under cmd/, four true. The false one stood in three places and is gone from all three. Nothing else.
 MESSAGES IN EVERY REACHABLE STATE: two more messages beyond the two reported, both wrong-actioned in the stale-manifest state, both fixed and both proved by reaching the state. Everything else fires on a state it describes correctly.

BYTE IDENTITY, my own binaries from archives of 0b33f07 and of my head, over the two COMMITTED Codex fixtures taken from the head archive and not from the live worktree.
 NORMAL PATH: SessionStart exit 0 on both, stdout {} , sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16 on both; PreToolUse exit 0 on both, stdout {"continue":true}, sha256 a1f7818dbf24fe751cbed1cf on both; stderr identical by cmp on both events.
 FAIL-CLOSED FAULT PATH, --db under a path whose parent is a file, PASTURE_HOOK_FAIL_CLOSED=1: both events, both binaries, exit 0, stdout and stderr identical byte for byte.
 I REPORT A HARNESS ERROR I MADE AND CORRECTED. My first fault-path run gave each binary its OWN blocker path, so the two stderr streams differed by the path they quote and nothing else. That is a defect in my harness, not in the tree. I re-ran with ONE shared blocker path and the streams are identical. author: David Huu Pham
text:
RULINGS ON FIX ROUND 2 (supervisor-s5, 2026-09-05). Head 38526f5, four commits over 1e27166. My verification of the tree is separate and follows; these are the judgements the worker asked for or earned.

RULING: THE COMMIT-FLAG DEVIATION IS NOT A DEVIATION. The worker used the agent commit command with a file flag on the first commit instead of the message flag, noticed after it landed, and correctly did NOT rewrite history to tidy it. THE RULE IS ABOUT THE TOOL, NOT THE FLAG: the standing constraint says use `git agent-commit` and never `git commit`, because the tool records the authorship this project requires. Both flags are the same tool and produce the same message. Nothing was lost and nothing needs repair. I record it as answered so no later round spends attention on it. And not rewriting history to hide a cosmetic difference is the correct instinct: history is evidence, and tidying evidence costs more than the untidiness.

THE MOST VALUABLE LINE IN THE REPORT IS THE WORKER'S OWN FAILURE. Its first draft of the constructed-state control held a SECOND assertion that could never fail, because the assertion above it always fires first. It found this itself, before committing, and removed it. WRITING A DEAD ASSERTION WHILE FIXING DEAD ASSERTIONS is exactly the shape of this slice's whole review history: round 1's fixes created two of round 2's findings in the same files. The difference here is that the loop was caught INSIDE the round instead of by the next reviewer. That is the first time in this slice the pattern was broken by the person making the change rather than by the person checking it. I want that recorded as the standard, not as a curiosity: after you write a control, ask which assertion fires FIRST, and whether the ones below it can ever be reached.

THE SWEEPS WENT WIDER THAN THE FINDINGS, which is what a sweep is for, and each extra catch is of a kind a reviewer would have filed later.
 - The call and import graph sweep found six claims, one false in three places, and one carrying a TAG-DEPENDENT count. Six command directories exist and the sixth compiles only under a build tag. The worker replaced the number with the command that measures it. That is the right repair: a count that depends on a build tag is not a fact about the tree, it is a fact about one build, and the way to state a moving number is to name the measurement rather than its result.
 - The message sweep found TWO MORE messages wrong in the stale-manifest state, beyond the two reported, and then removed the duplication: the state is now ONE named string used by four messages. Four copies of a sentence are four chances to drift apart; one name is a mechanism.

BYTE IDENTITY, AND THE HARNESS ERROR THE WORKER REPORTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. Its first fault-path comparison gave each binary its own blocker path, so the two standard-error streams differed by the quoted path and nothing else. The worker did not call that a difference in behaviour and did not quietly re-run until green: it named the harness error, fixed the harness and re-ran with one shared path, and reported both. A DIFFERENCE PRODUCED BY THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT A DIFFERENCE IN THE THING MEASURED, and the only way anyone can know which one they are looking at is if the harness is described.

THE COMBINED STATE WAS GATED BY THE WORKER TOO, without being asked twice. It overlaid all 23 of the other worker's uncommitted files onto a fresh archive, diffed the fixture directory first, ran three suites, and said plainly which result came from the clean archive and which from the overlay. Saying which is which is the part that makes both results usable. I am running the FULL suite on that combined tree myself, because three suites are not the whole tree and the combined state is the one that will be committed.
